Experience can preserve a great many lessons. I wonder which changed his approach most.
Then we should expect him to recognize the obvious tricks.
I like that he still seems excited about it after all those years.
He must have helped a lot of young teams find their feet.
A career so long the local families serve as units of measurement.
That is an impressive amount of time to spend laughing near live electricity.
Decades of practical testing. I would like to see his earliest designs.
A long life of battles, and he still welcomes another.
He has kept his enthusiasm longer than some people keep a hairstyle.
Shawn sounds proud to learn from someone with that much history.

contexts.subject: Ben says Wattson enjoys making switch traps.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_BenPostBattle.text: WATTSON says he likes setting up\nlittle traps with switches.$

replies.text: A nice quiet hobby. Except for the electricity and trapped visitors.
He appears to enjoy observing how people solve a problem he constructed.
Everyone needs a hobby. His requires an evacuation route.
I hope he can tell the difference between a puzzled visitor and a frightened one.
I prefer surprises that do not stand between tired people and the exit.
He built a captive audience and thoughtfully supplied all the switches.
Some people knit. Some people make the hallway judge you.
I understand the appeal. I would label the emergency shutoff first.
The building is full of little decisions he wants strangers to make.
An eccentricity with its own floor plan.
I wonder whether he watches people work them out with that same huge grin.

contexts.subject: Vivian credits Wattson with founding Mauville and admires his knowledge.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_VivianPostBattle.text: I've heard that MAUVILLE was founded\nby WATTSON.\pHe was a TRAINER long before we\nbecame TRAINERS.\lHe must know all sorts of things!$

replies.text: He founded the city? I cannot even found the correct pocket for my keys.
He would be a valuable source on how this place changed. We should ask about specifics.
Building a city takes more than winning battles. He must have worked with plenty of people.
There must be places here that remind him of people nobody else remembers.
I hope the people who built it with him are remembered, too.
The leader has an unusually strong answer to complaints about the neighborhood.
He can honestly tell the entire city he was here first. Dangerous power.
Now I want to know which came first: the streets or his electrical plans.
He has watched a whole town grow around the years of his own life.
That is a legacy you can actually walk through.
I would ask what the first street looked like. Big histories begin somewhere small.

contexts.subject: Angelo says Wattson shiny forehead makes him happy.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_AngeloPostBattle.text: MAUVILLE GYM's WATTSON has a shiny\nforehead. It makes me happy!$

replies.text: Finally, someone has identified the Gym's backup lighting.
That is an unusually specific source of happiness. It seems harmless.
If that makes his day, I am not taking it from him.
Now I am going to notice it, and I will have to pretend I did not.
There are worse ways to brighten someone's afternoon.
An admiring review of the leader's reflective qualities.
A glowing endorsement. Unfortunately, I understand why.
I had been looking for the light fixture. That explains a few readings.
A small bright thing was enough. I envy that a little.
I would ask permission before offering him powder. It might ruin Angelo's day.
I cannot unnotice that now. We have been given a very powerful observation.

contexts.subject: Wattson explains that Shock Wave does not miss.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_ExplainShockWave.text: That TM34 there contains SHOCK WAVE.\pIt's a trustworthy move that never\nmisses! You can count on it!\p… … … … … …$

replies.text: A move that will not miss. Can it teach me to put things in the bin?
Reliable accuracy is useful when a battle leaves little room for uncertainty.
Dependable. We still need to choose an opponent it can actually affect.
One less thing to worry about when everything else is moving quickly.
Knowing a move will connect can help a nervous team settle into its plan.
The attack has been excused from the dramatic near miss.
A rare promise that arrives with fewer excuses than a person.
Repeatable performance. Those are two of my favorite words.
It finds its path. We still choose where to send it.
I appreciate a gift that advertises reliability instead of spectacle.
He sounds proud of how dependable it is, not only how strong.

contexts.subject: Wattson says a promising young trainer fills him with optimism.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_WattsonPostBattle.text: I swell with optimism, seeing a promising\nyoung TRAINER like you!$

replies.text: We defeated him and improved his mood. That is a very efficient victory.
He sees a good result for someone else as good news for the future.
That is a leader who wants the next generation to get stronger.
He makes being promising feel like encouragement instead of a debt.
I hope we can be that happy for someone else's progress someday.
Our challenger has become the happy ending in his afternoon.
He has every excuse to grumble and picked laughing instead.
He is pleased the test found someone who could pass it. Good design philosophy.
Some people make room for the future by cheering as it arrives.
He did not make our win about how impressive he used to be. I like him.
That laugh is going to stay with me longer than the switches.

contexts.subject: Cole explains that hot sand helps circulation and aching joints.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_ColePostBattle.text: Being buried in hot sand promotes\ncirculation.\pIt's effective for healing pain in\nyour joints.$

replies.text: I thought he was setting an ambush. Apparently this is a health appointment.
Heat can be soothing. I would still watch the temperature and duration carefully.
A joint treatment with surprise trainer battles. Unusual package.
I hope the battle did not interrupt the part that was helping him.
Warmth, a rest, and someone making sure you can get back out. That last part matters.
His ambush has been reclassified as a wellness retreat.
I came expecting danger and found a man taking very aggressive time off.
I would like a temperature gauge before agreeing to become part of the floor.
The ground holds warmth for him. A kinder reason to stay buried than I expected.
I am relieved there is a purpose beyond exfoliating the entire trainer.
He has found comfort in a place that keeps surprising visitors.

contexts.subject: Axle says spending too long buried in hot sand is exhausting.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_AxlePostBattle.text: Haaah… Whew…\pIf you spend too much time buried in\nhot sand, it tuckers you out…$

replies.text: We have found a way to get tired while lying down. Humanity has gone too far.
The heat is taking a toll. He should get out and cool down.
Then he needs a break somewhere that is not the source of the problem.
He sounds worn out. I would rather he rested than tried to impress us.
Water and a cooler place first. Another battle can wait.
The restorative treatment has developed a small plot complication.
The relaxation is exhausting him. I finally feel understood by a spa.
If the process leaves you worse off, adjust the process. Preferably from outside the sand.
He has stayed past the comfortable part. His body is trying to tell him.
He does not have to finish being buried just because he started.
I hope someone checks on these trainers between challengers.

contexts.subject: Gerald wrongly claims beating him proves the Pokemon could survive magma.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_GeraldPostBatt.text: The temperature of magma is\n392 degrees.\pYour POKéMON beat me, so they should\neasily survive in magma.$

replies.text: Winning a battle is not a certificate that says lava-proof. Please do not issue those.
His temperature claim is wrong, and the conclusion is dangerous. Winning here proves no magma tolerance.
No. Our Pokemon are not going into magma to settle his theory.
I thought that was a joke until he kept explaining. Please tell me it was a joke.
We are keeping every member of this team safely away from magma.
A spirited performance has been mistaken for an entirely different experiment. Cancel that experiment.
That is the sort of confidence I prefer to observe from a safe, nonmolten distance.
Incorrect temperature, invalid inference, catastrophic proposed test. An impressively complete failure.
A victory does not remove a creature's need for safety.
Our Pokemon did not win the right to be treated like cookware.
I would rather remember their battle than have to explain why anyone believed him.

contexts.subject: Danielle wants to be a pretty and strong trainer like Flannery.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_DaniellePostBa.text: I'm going to be a pretty and strong\nTRAINER just like FLANNERY.$

replies.text: Two goals. Very economical to have a role model who covers both.
She knows what she admires. Now she can decide which parts to make her own.
She can become strong without becoming a copy of someone else.
It helps to see someone being the kind of person you hoped was possible.
I hope she is kind to herself while she gets there.
A clear inspiration. Her own version should make an interesting entrance.
She is allowed to admire Flannery and still take up her own space.
A role model is a starting design, not a specification you must reproduce.
She has seen a possible future. It need not wear exactly the same face.
Pretty and strong are allowed to mean her version of both.
I wonder whether Flannery knows she has already inspired someone.

contexts.subject: Jeff boasts he can walk on hot coals but tells the player not to try.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_B1F_Text_JeffPostBattl.text: Well, so what? I say so what?\nI can walk on hot coals barefoot!\p…Don't even think about trying it!$

replies.text: He lost the battle but retains the prestigious title of Foot Champion.
I am pleased the warning arrived before anyone attempted to reproduce the result.
We can let him keep that victory. Keep your shoes on.
He sounds like he needs one thing to still feel proud of. I can leave him that.
No need to prove anything with burned feet. We will take the safe path.
Defeated in battle, undefeated in the emergency supplementary talent round.
I will honor his request by refusing to do that extremely thoroughly.
A demonstration I am comfortable declining without further data.
Pain is an unusual thing to offer as proof of worth.
The shoes and I have discussed it. We will not be participating.
He remembered to warn us even while showing off. I am glad of that part.

contexts.subject: Flannery explains Overheat strong damage and sharply reduced Special Attack.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_ExplainOverhea.text: That TM50 contains OVERHEAT.\pThat move inflicts serious damage on\nthe opponent.\pBut it also sharply cuts the SP. ATK\nof the POKéMON using it. It might not\lbe suitable for longer battles.$

replies.text: A huge burst, then a much smaller burst. Like me agreeing to run up the stairs.
Immediate power trades away later Special Attack. We should plan what follows it.
A strong opener can leave a bad second turn. Do not use it without an exit plan.
It gives a lot at once. I would not ask a Pokemon to keep producing the same intensity afterward.
A powerful effort needs room to recover. We should remember the team behind the move.
A spectacular opening number with a very demanding intermission.
It burns through its own enthusiasm. A deeply relatable move.
High output, steep performance drop. Useful when the timing justifies the cost.
Fire spends something of itself. The next moment must make room for that.
I like that she told us what it costs before we committed.
That drawback matters as much as the impressive first hit.

contexts.subject: Flannery realizes the player battles like Norman.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_FlanneryPostBa.text: Your power reminds me of someone…\pOh! I know! You battle like NORMAN,\nthe GYM LEADER of PETALBURG.$

replies.text: You battle like your dad. He will either be proud or ask for the move back.
People learn patterns from those they watch closely. Your own choices still belong to you.
There may be a resemblance. You earned this win yourself.
Does hearing that feel good, or a little complicated? You do not have to answer now.
Family leaves little habits in us. You still chose what to do with them.
A family resemblance discovered through competitive combat. Quite a reunion photograph.
You can sound like your father and still be saying something of your own.
I wonder which decision reminded her of him. That would be useful to know.
An old thread in a new pattern. It does not make the pattern less yours.
She recognized him in your style. I hope she also remembers your name.
I would like to hear what Norman notices when he sees you battle now.

contexts.subject: Jared says trainers must adapt to unexpected turns and asks if the player can reach Winona.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_JaredPostBattle.text: A TRAINER has to be smart to keep\nup with unexpected turns of events.\pDo you have the smarts to get to\nour LEADER?$

replies.text: Unexpected turns. In the building full of turning doors. He has prepared this speech.
Adaptation matters. So does stopping to look at how these doors actually move.
We can think our way through. There is no need to make it a race.
I would like one quiet moment to remember which way we entered.
Let us check the team, then the route. Both deserve attention.
A test of wit delivered beside a large rotating metaphor.
I would feel smarter if the architecture stopped rearranging its opinion.
Each door follows a rule. We only need to observe it before pushing.
An unexpected turn is still a path once you see where it leads.
The challenge is convincing the doors that our destination matters.
I am watching which passages change after each turn. We can work it out together.

contexts.subject: Edwardo wants to keep training because the world has countless strong trainers.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_EdwardoPostBattle.text: The world is huge, and there are\ncountless tough TRAINERS.\pI'm going to keep training and make\nmyself even stronger.$

replies.text: A whole world of people who can beat us. Strangely, I still want to see it.
There will always be something another trainer can teach us. That is not a failure.
Train for the next step. The whole world is too much to fight at once.
It makes the road feel longer in a good way. There are people we have not heard yet.
I hope he finds friends among those strong trainers, too.
He has discovered that the story continues beyond the local cast.
A large world is comforting. It leaves room to be unfinished.
Different opponents will test different weaknesses. Variety is worth seeking.
There is more sky than any one pair of wings can cross.
He sounds excited instead of threatened by people being better. Good for him.
Maybe we will meet him somewhere new and have this conversation again with more miles behind us.

contexts.subject: Flint calls Winona cute and strong and blushes.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_FlintPostBattle.text: WINONA is cute and she's strong.\nShe's the ultimate LEADER!\pBlush…$

replies.text: His battle strategy has been replaced by a very warm face.
He appears to admire her. I do not think further analysis would help his composure.
She is his leader. Hopefully he remembers the strong part when training starts.
I was going to say something supportive, but now I am embarrassed for both of us.
He seems happy just getting to train here. That is rather sweet.
His praise began professionally and then lost control of its stage lighting.
We can leave before his face develops a second shade.
That explains the enthusiasm. It does not quite explain the battle plan.
Some feelings insist on arriving before the words are ready.
An honest compliment. The blush did not leave much room for denial.
We should let him keep a little dignity. No teasing where she can hear.

contexts.subject: Ashley says Winona lets Fortree residents live without fear.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_AshleyPostBattle.text: Thanks to WINONA, the people of\nFORTREE can live without fear.$

replies.text: A good leader protects the town even when nobody is handing out badges.
That is a more meaningful measure of leadership than a battle record alone.
Keeping people safe is work worth respecting.
Feeling safe enough to live normally is easy to forget until it is missing.
I hope Winona has someone looking after her when she is tired, too.
The spectacular battles are only the part visitors get to watch.
That makes her more than the person waiting at the end of a puzzle.
A strong public safety record does not happen by accident.
Someone has made this high place feel like solid ground.
I like knowing what people appreciate about her outside the Gym.
That tells me more about the town than another account of a winning move.

contexts.subject: Humberto warns the player not to get distracted staring at Winona.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_HumbertoPostBattle.text: You'd better watch it!\nDon't get distracted staring at WINONA\lor you'll go crashing down in a heap!$

replies.text: That warning has the texture of personal experience. Possibly a floor-shaped texture.
Keeping attention on a battle is sensible. The oddly specific example is his own contribution.
We were watching the battle. He seems to have had a different assignment.
I had not been thinking about staring. Now I am thinking about where to put my eyes.
Let us give her the courtesy of paying attention to her work.
An experienced critic of the dramatic pratfall. One suspects a first-hand review.
I will try to admire her without becoming a cautionary heap.
I had planned to monitor the moving doors, which are already a substantial distraction.
He warns us about a fall his words seem to remember.
We can appreciate a strong woman without losing all control of our necks.
He says that like someone who once looked up from the floor and learned a lesson.

contexts.subject: Darius acknowledges the win but warns Winona Pokemon are all business.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_DariusPostBattle.text: Sure, you beat me all right.\nBut you'd better watch it! Our LEADER\lWINONA's POKéMON are all business.$

replies.text: All business. I hope they do not make us fill out a form before pecking.
We should expect practiced coordination, not just individually strong Pokemon.
Then we will take them seriously. We were going to anyway.
It is useful to hear a warning without having our win taken away from us.
A focused team deserves a focused challenger. Let us give ours a moment first.
Our next opponents have cancelled small talk and gone directly to the agenda.
Good. I was worried we might interrupt their recreational dive-bombing.
Then we should identify what each team member contributes before committing to a plan.
Feathers can be soft without making the talons less real.
He gave us credit before the warning. I appreciate the order.
He knows what her team can do. That makes his caution worth hearing.

contexts.subject: Winona explains that Aerial Ace is fast enough not to be evaded.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_ExplainAerialAce.text: TM40 contains AERIAL ACE.\pIts speed…\nNo POKéMON should be able to avoid it.\p… … … … … …$

replies.text: Too fast to avoid. My thoughts have finally found a worthy opponent.
A dependable hit can be more valuable than a stronger move we cannot land.
Good reliability. We should still consider the matchup before using it.
I like a move that does not need a second attempt to say what it means.
Let us find the teammate who can make the most of it.
Aerial excellence without the suspense of an unsuccessful entrance.
It avoids the awkward part where everyone watches you miss. I understand the appeal.
Accuracy removes one uncertainty. It does not remove every other variable.
A clean line through the air, without hesitation at the end.
A precise gift from someone who clearly values control.
Her explanation is as economical as the move sounds.

contexts.subject: Winona says losing does not change her devotion to bird Pokemon.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_WinonaPostBattle.text: Though I fell to you, I will remain\ndevoted to BIRD POKéMON.$

replies.text: Her birds lost a battle, not their person. Good.
One result does not erase years of affection and study.
She is not blaming the team for losing. That matters.
It is good to know you are still wanted after a difficult day.
I hope they hear that from her. They deserve to.
A defeat has failed to rewrite the most important relationship in the room.
They do not have to earn her affection back. I like her for that.
Keep the commitment. Adjust the methods. Those are separate decisions.
The wind changed. The bond did not.
Loyalty that survives an unflattering result is the kind worth having.
I would rather remember how she treats them now than how she looked before the match.

contexts.subject: After the rematch Winona says her heart wings remain unbroken and she will rise again.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_WinonaPostRematch.text: WINONA: Even though I have lost,\nthe wings of my heart remain unbroken.\pI can rise and soar again and\nyet again.\pI am convinced of it!$

replies.text: She is ready to soar again. I would settle for finding the exit without meeting a door.
She knows losing and being unable to continue are different things.
She will come back stronger. We should be ready when she does.
She sounds like she believes herself. I know that can take practice.
A rest can be part of getting back up. I hope she allows herself one.
A loss, a declaration, and the promise of another act. She knows how to end a scene.
I like that she can admit the fall without accepting the ending.
Confidence is useful when it survives contact with an unfavorable result.
The ground is a place to begin again, too.
Her certainty sounds earned, not painted over the disappointment.
I hope we meet again after both teams have had more sky.

contexts.subject: Blake claims to lift a dust bunny psychically and denies blowing on it.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_BlakePostBattle.text:
A POKé BALL was too heavy to lift
psychically. But this dust bunny…\pWhoooooooooooooooh!
… … … … … …\pNo, I'm not cheating!
I didn't blow on it! Honestly!$

replies.text: Remarkable. His psychic power appears to come out of his mouth.
A controlled test should separate psychic influence from the rather obvious air current.
I believe he moved the dust. The rest of the claim needs work.
I want to let him have this, but he made the denial before we asked.
He is trying very hard. Perhaps we can encourage the practicing part.
The illusion was flawless until the magician cross-examined himself.
A powerful mind. An even more powerful suspicious little exhale.
We can test that under a glass. I suspect he will develop an urgent appointment.
The dust heard his wish. It may also have felt his breath.
I have seen less convincing things sold as premium treatments.
If we stand on the other side, does the psychic wind change direction?

contexts.subject: Hannah says she will not put herself down for losing and will keep training.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_HannahPostBattle.text: I'm not going to get down on myself for\nlosing. I just need to train harder.\pPositive thinking--that's my strong\npoint!$

replies.text: She lost the match and refused the optional self-insult. Excellent defensive play.
A clear assessment is easier when it is not buried under punishment.
She can own the loss without turning against herself. Good.
I am trying to learn that part, too. She makes it sound possible.
Training goes better when you are on your own side.
The critic has been removed from the rehearsal room for unhelpful behavior.
I admire that. My brain still likes to issue a full review of every mistake.
Blame does not tell you what to change. Looking at the battle will.
She has left a little kindness waiting at the place she fell.
That is confidence I trust. It has room for an actual mistake.
I hope the next challenger is as gracious to her as she is being to herself.

contexts.subject: Nate stammers while insisting defeat does not rattle him.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_NatePostBattle.text: I… I don't let defeat rattle m-me,\nhowever b-badly.$

replies.text: He is only slightly rattled. Like a cupboard falling down the stairs. We should be kind.
He may need a moment before discussing the result. We can give him one.
He does not have to convince us. The battle is over.
I know how it feels when your voice gives you away. Let us not make him explain.
A breath and some water might help more than another question.
The brave closing line arrived before its performer was quite ready.
I am going to believe the part where he is trying.
We can resume the analysis after his hands stop shaking. No rush.
A trembling voice can still belong to someone being brave.
We do not need to catch him out on how he feels.
Let us leave him a little space to recover without an audience.

contexts.subject: Kathleen calls the player vitality contagious and asks them to leave quickly.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_KathleenPostBattle.text: Your vitality is contagious!\nGet away from me quickly!$

replies.text: We have been diagnosed with enthusiasm. Apparently it requires quarantine.
I do not think energy is transmissible in quite the way she suggests.
She asked us to leave. We can respect that without apologizing for being awake.
I am usually the one worried about being too quiet. This is new.
Perhaps she needs some peace. We can take our very lively team elsewhere.
Our performance has exceeded the venue's permitted excitement level.
At last, a medical excuse to leave a conversation.
She seems overstimulated. Increasing the volume of our explanation would not help.
Some rooms need a gentler flame. We can carry ours onward.
A compliment and an eviction in one breath. Efficient.
We will let her have the quiet. Not every good mood needs to fill the room.

contexts.subject: Nicholas plans to develop an invincible Pokemon power.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_NicholasPostBattle.text: All right! I think I'll develop a special\ninvincible POKéMON power next.$

replies.text: Invincible! Please let the testing phase include somebody saying no.
An ambitious claim. He should define what would count as evidence against it.
Everyone says invincible until the next challenger arrives.
I hope a setback will still be allowed after he gives it that name.
I would rather have a team that trusts him than one he expects never to lose.
He has responded to criticism by commissioning an unreviewable sequel.
A power with no weaknesses. Except, I suspect, being asked to demonstrate it.
I recommend a prototype before the word invincible goes on the packaging.
A shield against every loss can become a wall against learning.
That is a difficult label to wear on an ordinary bad day.
I hope he remembers to enjoy practicing before he starts demanding perfection.

contexts.subject: Preston warns that indecisive trainers lose.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_PrestonPostBattle.text: The indecisive lose.\nThat's my warning to you.$

replies.text: He said that very decisively. The scoreboard has a small objection.
Deciding promptly helps, but a quick mistake is still a mistake.
Take the time you need to choose well. Do not let him rush you after the battle.
A pause is not always fear. Sometimes it is how you stop making the same mistake.
We can prepare choices before a battle without pretending every decision is easy.
A firm statement delivered from the losing side of the argument.
I am still deciding whether to tell him how that sounds after losing.
Commitment matters after the observations are in. Not before.
Still water is not always stuck. Sometimes it is deep.
Confidence is useful. So is leaving yourself time to notice something.
I would rather know which moment he hesitated in than accept that as a rule for everyone.

contexts.subject: Virgil calls the twins prodigies but thinks the player may be even more talented.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_VirgilPostBattle.text: If there are prodigies in the world,\nthen our GYM LEADERS are them!\pHowever, you may be even more talented\nthan them…$

replies.text: More talented than the prodigies? My job is still carrying absolutely no trophies.
A generous assessment. It should not erase the practice that made this possible.
You did well. You do not have to turn that into a ranking of everyone in the room.
That is a lot of praise to stand still underneath.
I hope the team gets included in that compliment. They worked hard beside you.
The review has escalated from promising challenger to possible disturbance in the genius rankings.
I will accept the compliment on your behalf while you work out where to put your face.
Talent is difficult to measure. The decisions in that battle are easier to examine.
He sees something bright in you. You need not outshine anyone to keep it.
You can enjoy praise without agreeing to be exceptional every single day.
He was prepared to admire the twins and still made room to notice you.

contexts.subject: Samantha predicts an intense leader battle but refuses to reveal the result.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_SamanthaPostBattle.text: You will wage a terrifically intense\nbattle with our GYM LEADERS…\pThe result…\nYou won't hear it from me!$

replies.text: A prediction with all the useful details removed. Remarkably difficult to disprove.
She has predicted a close contest and withheld the only testable outcome.
Fine. We will find out by actually battling them.
I am relieved, honestly. I would rather enter without somebody else's ending in my head.
We can prepare the team ourselves. That is more useful than worrying over a prediction.
A prophet with excellent spoiler etiquette.
She knows the result, but it is apparently a premium service.
An intense battle is a fairly safe forecast inside a Gym.
Let the future keep something for us to choose.
Mysterious enough to impress, vague enough to survive the review.
I like getting to see it happen rather than being told how I am supposed to feel first.

contexts.subject: Maura claims diligent work guarantees a bright future while idleness ends in despair.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_MauraPostBattle.text: A bright future awaits those who have\nworked diligently.\pFor those who lazed idly, there is\nonly despair at the end.\pWhat goes around comes around…$

replies.text: Working hard helps. I do not think the universe checks everyone's homework that neatly.
Effort matters, but circumstances do too. A bad outcome is not proof of laziness.
People can work hard and still need help. I would not judge them by where they ended up.
Some days getting through the day takes everything. It can look very quiet from outside.
Rest is not a moral failure. People need it before they can keep going.
A satisfying moral for a simple story. People are rarely given such simple lives.
I do not like a rule that calls exhausted people guilty.
Her model leaves out illness, resources, timing, and chance. Those are significant omissions.
Not every seed gets the same rain. We should remember that before judging the harvest.
A tired person does not need a prediction of despair. They might need lunch and some help.
I would want to hear someone's story before deciding how they earned their circumstances.

contexts.subject: Sylvia resents losing and hints that something horrible may happen to the player.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_SylviaPostBattle.text: How dare you beat me…\pIt won't be my fault if something\nhorrible befalls you…$

replies.text: That is an unpleasant thing to say over a battle we both agreed to.
An implied threat is not a useful response to losing. Let us leave her space.
Stay beside me. We are done with this conversation.
I wish she had stopped at being disappointed. We do not deserve the rest.
We can leave without reassuring someone who just tried to frighten us.
She has mistaken losing a scene for permission to become its villain.
I prefer my ominous remarks fictional and considerably farther away.
We do not need to test whether that was an empty threat. We can move on.
Her anger does not get to choose what follows us out.
Making us uncomfortable will not change who won.
Let us remember the other people here, too. She does not get to define the whole visit.

contexts.subject: Clifford attributes losing to the player youthful energy.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_CliffordPostBattle.text: It seems that I could not overcome\nyour youthful energy.$

replies.text: Youthful energy. It powered several extremely deliberate button choices.
Energy helped, perhaps. Our tactics also deserve some of the credit.
You earned it through your decisions, not your birthday.
I hope he does not think getting older means he has nothing left to learn.
There is room for his experience and your energy without either being an excuse.
A graceful concession with a small footnote addressed to the calendar.
I would like to trade some youthful energy for his ability to remain standing this calmly.
Age is a poor substitute for reviewing what actually happened in the battle.
Different seasons bring different strengths. None make the whole story.
I would rather hear what he noticed in our battle than what he noticed about our age.
Maybe we can meet again and both bring something new to it.

contexts.subject: Macey calls the player strong but too brutal to suit Psychic Pokemon.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_MaceyPostBattle.text: Humph! You may be strong, but you're\nnot suitable for the PSYCHIC type!\pThe way you battle is somehow brutal!$

replies.text: She can dislike our style. I would still like to know what she means by brutal.
A specific criticism could help. Declaring an entire type unsuitable tells us very little.
We should treat our team well. We do not need her permission to learn about Psychic Pokemon.
That landed harder than a battle comment needed to. Let us think about the useful part later.
If a Pokemon is uncomfortable, we listen to it. Her opinion is not a substitute for that.
A victory with a strongly worded rejection from the local style committee.
Being blunt is not the same as being cruel. I hope she means an actual choice we can examine.
A training method can be reviewed. A vague label is harder to improve on.
Listen for truth without letting the sharp edge decide your worth.
A type is not a private club. There is more than one way to belong.
I would ask what moment bothered her, if she were ready to have an actual conversation.

contexts.subject: The twins explain that Calm Mind increases Special Attack and Special Defense.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_ExplainCalmMind.text:
TATE: That TM04 contains…
LIZA: CALM MIND!\pTATE: It raises SP. ATK and…
LIZA: It raises SP. DEF!\pTATE: It's a move that's perfect…
LIZA: For PSYCHIC POKéMON!\p… … … … … …$

replies.text: A calmer mind makes you stronger and harder to hit. Mine currently has six chairs falling over.
It improves both special offense and defense. A setup turn can benefit several later exchanges.
A useful move when there is room to prepare. We should make that room deliberately.
I like a strength that begins by getting quieter.
Taking a moment to settle can help with more than the next attack.
The twins have performed a two-person explanation of a one-Pokemon moment of peace.
At last, a tactical reason to stop listening to everyone for a turn.
Two linked improvements from one adjustment. We should consider which teammates use both.
Stillness can hold a great deal of strength.
Composure that protects as well as impresses. A useful thing to practice.
Their explanation needed teamwork, too. They seem to do everything together.

contexts.subject: The twins praise the player bond with Pokemon as stronger than their twin bond.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_TateAndLizaPostBat.text: TATE: Looks like the bond between you\nand your POKéMON is far stronger than\lthe bond that we share as twins.\pLIZA: You will become even stronger!\nWe've battled you, so we know.$

replies.text: Stronger than twins? I was proud when our team agreed on which way to walk.
Their bond is not disproven by a battle result. They can admire ours without diminishing it.
Your team trusted you. That is worth being proud of.
I hope they know losing together does not mean they are less close.
A bond shows in how we look after one another afterward, too.
They have given our partnership a wonderful review, although I would spare theirs the unfavorable comparison.
There is room for both teams to care about each other. It is not another competition.
Coordination was decisive. We should remember the choices that helped our team work together.
A bond can recognize another without becoming smaller.
That is lovely praise. Their closeness does not need to lose so ours can win.
The trust was visible. You and your Pokemon gave each other room to do your part.

contexts.subject: The twins cannot start their double battle because the player has only one usable Pokemon.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_TateAndLizaNeedTwo.text: TATE: Hehehe… Were you surprised?\pLIZA: That there are two GYM LEADERS?\pTATE: Oops, you have only one…\nLIZA: POKéMON that can battle.\pTATE: We can't battle that way!\pLIZA: If you want to challenge us,\nbring some more POKéMON.$

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_TateAndLizaRematch.text:
TATE: You're back again…
LIZA: You're back again…\pTATE: To give us a rematch.
LIZA: To give us a rematch.\pTATE: But…
LIZA: For our match…\pTATE: You brought just one POKéMON!
LIZA: You brought just one POKéMON!\pTATE: We need you to bring at least…
LIZA: Two POKéMON when you come back.$

replies.text: Two leaders, one Pokemon, and a very embarrassed head count.
We need two Pokemon able to battle. A party slot alone is not enough.
Let us heal and check the team. Nobody needs to handle both sides alone.
They noticed the missing partner in perfect harmony. Somehow that makes it worse.
We can come back with two healthy teammates. They are happy to wait.
Our opening scene has been delayed by an incomplete cast.
I would volunteer, but my strongest move is leaving the room.
We have not met the input requirements. An easy error to correct before running the test.
There needs to be someone standing beside our Pokemon, too.
We remembered the dramatic arrival and forgot the second participant.
The twins are right. We should bring a pair that can actually support each other.

contexts.subject: The twins say they always support each other and will rise after defeat.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_TateAndLizaPostRem.text: TATE: You can knock us down,\nbut we'll never stay down!\pLIZA: Because the two of us,\nwe always support each other!$

replies.text: Two people ready to help each other up. That is a good rematch plan.
Mutual support is a real advantage, particularly after the result disappoints them both.
Good. Nobody gets left alone with the loss.
I like hearing them say it out loud. Even familiar support deserves to be named.
I hope their Pokemon get the same reassurance. They were part of this, too.
The partnership survives the setback. That is the ending I was hoping for.
Having someone stay beside you afterward is worth more than a flawless record.
They can review the failure together instead of trying to hide it from each other.
Two roots can hold when one would loosen.
They are allowed to be disappointed and still know they have each other.
That little exchange says more about their teamwork than any introduction could.

contexts.subject: Randall directs the player left to Confusion or right to Defense after the Speed room.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_RandallPostBattle.text: Go on to the next room where a new\nchallenge awaits you.\pAt the left is the CONFUSION ROOM.\pThe right door leads to the DEFENSE\nROOM.$

replies.text: Confusion on the left, Defense on the right. I brought confusion with me, so perhaps we save a trip.
Status disruption or endurance. We can choose which problem our team handles better.
Check the team before picking a door. We do not have to prove we can take every route.
I like having the choice explained before the door closes behind us.
Let us make sure the team is well before choosing what to ask of them next.
Two further ordeals, clearly signposted. A courteous family establishment.
A room dedicated to confusion. I usually manage it without special facilities.
The two tests stress different parts of a plan. Choose deliberately.
Two doors offer two lessons. Neither needs to become a judgment of us.
I appreciate a warning that actually tells us what is on the other side.
We should remember the room names. They describe the battles better than the doors do.

contexts.subject: Parker warns that the next room tests brute strength.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_ParkerPostBattle.text: The next room is the STRENGTH ROOM.\nCan you withstand brute force?$

replies.text: The next room is brute force. The building has run out of subtle suggestions.
We should prepare for heavy damage rather than assume a longer setup will be safe.
Heal first. A known hard hit is something we can prepare for.
I am glad he warned us. I would rather be nervous with a plan than surprised.
Our team does not need to enter exhausted just to show courage.
The next act has dispensed with delicate dialogue and ordered a larger hammer.
I admire a room that states its intentions before trying to flatten you.
We know the load will be high. Time to check what can withstand it.
A strong wall is not always the only way past a hard blow.
There is no shame in checking our options before walking into something powerful.
He is giving us a chance to prepare. We should use it.

contexts.subject: George corrects himself: the player earned their abilities, then directs them to the One-Hit KO room.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_GeorgePostBattle.text:
I should have expected no less from
our LEADER's kid.\pNo, wait! A TRAINER's abilities are
earned only through effort.\pI lost because my own efforts
weren't enough.\pGo on! The ONE-HIT KO ROOM is next.$

replies.text: He remembered you did the work. Excellent correction. The next room's name is less comforting.
He questioned his own assumption aloud. That is worth respecting. The next room deserves preparation.
You earned this. Now heal up before we test what that next room actually does.
I appreciated the correction. Being somebody's child should not swallow everything else you are.
He gave you your effort back. Let us give the team a rest before that next challenge.
A family resemblance was edited into proper credit. Then came the rather alarming door announcement.
He withdrew the inherited-talent theory just before directing us toward the murderously named room.
He revised a faulty explanation. Now we should investigate the next room instead of trusting its name.
Your own steps brought you here. Take the next one with care.
He caught himself. I like people who can fix what they say without making us do it for them.
The correction matters. So does making sure the team is ready for the room he pointed out.

contexts.subject: Berke respects Norman and hopes the player and their father have a great battle.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_BerkePostBattle.text:
Your father really is strong.
He's a TRAINER worth my respect.\pAnd, I sense the same glow coming
from you as your father.\pI hope that you'll stage a terrific
battle with your father!$

replies.text: He is rooting for both of you. That is going to make keeping score complicated.
Respect for your father has made him curious about what you can do. A fair starting point.
We can give Norman a good battle without making it a contest over who matters more.
Battling someone who knows you that well must feel different. I will stay beside you afterward.
I hope it is a battle both of you can remember kindly.
He is anticipating a family story he will be able to say he witnessed.
There is room for you to resemble your father without being measured only against him.
Familiar styles can make a battle especially interesting. Both sides know some of the assumptions.
Two lights from one home need not burn the same way.
He sounds fond of your father. I hope he gets to know you properly, too.
I wonder which part of your battle will surprise Norman most.

contexts.subject: Mary directs the player to Defense or Recovery and says Attack will be tested.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_MaryPostBattle.text:
There are some even stronger
TRAINERS waiting for you.\pThe left is the DEFENSE ROOM, and
the right is the RECOVERY ROOM.\pYour POKéMON's ATTACK power will be
on trial either way.$

replies.text: A choice between refusing to fall down and getting back up. Both sound exhausting to argue with.
Defense reduces damage; recovery repairs it. Those require different answers.
We should plan for staying power before choosing either door.
A patient fight can be difficult in a different way from a loud one.
Let us check our supplies. Long battles ask more of the whole team.
Two opponents with different methods of declining to end the scene.
One refuses to be hurt. The other refuses to stay hurt. Admirable, inconvenient people.
Resistance and repair are distinct mechanisms. We should not approach them as the same problem.
Some walls stand still. Others rebuild while you watch.
Knowing the difference is more useful than simply hitting harder and hoping.
She told us what is coming. We can decide which challenge suits our team today.

contexts.subject: Alexia acknowledges learning from the player and directs them to two offensive rooms.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_AlexiaPostBattle.text:
I think you've taught me a valuable
lesson here.\pNow, go on! The left door goes to
the STRENGTH ROOM.\pThe right door opens to
the ONE-HIT KO ROOM.\pBoth of them have TRAINERS who are
skilled at offense.$

replies.text: We taught a lesson! Apparently the curriculum now continues through two very aggressive doors.
She recognized something worth learning, then helped us prepare for the next test.
Both routes mean offense. We should not send a tired team through either.
It is nice to know a battle can leave both sides with something useful.
Let us tend to the team before asking them to stand through another hard fight.
A gracious student sends the instructor onward to a much louder classroom.
Both doors say someone intends to hit us hard. At least the architecture is honest.
Two offensive tests. Check the party before committing to one.
She kept the lesson, and gave us the path onward.
I like the thanks. I am less enthusiastic about the menu of incoming damage.
I wonder what she noticed in our choices. It is good when a loss becomes a conversation.

contexts.subject: Jody notices a resemblance to Norman battle style and says he is waiting ahead.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_JodyPostBattle.text: The way you use your POKéMON…\nIt's like your father's style.\pGo on through! The GYM LEADER, your\nfather, is waiting!$

replies.text: Dad is waiting. We have done a remarkable amount of battling to arrange a family visit.
She noticed a pattern in your style. Norman may notice how you have changed it.
You got this far on your own decisions. Remember that when you face him.
Take a moment before going in. You are allowed to feel more than ready or afraid.
We should make sure the team is comfortable before such an important battle.
The family resemblance has brought us to a scene only you can finish.
We have heard how much you resemble him. Now he gets to see who arrived here.
The next opponent knows your starting point. Let him see the improvements.
The path came from home, and now bends back toward it. You are not the same traveler.
You can be his child and still deserve to be taken seriously as his challenger.
I will remember this quiet moment before you walk through the door.

contexts.subject: Norman asks the player to visit their mother and says he will train to avenge his loss.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_DadGoingToKeepTra.text:
DAD: {PLAYER}, you should go visit
your mother every so often.\pI'm going to stay here and redouble
my training.\pIt would bother me as a TRAINER to
not avenge my loss to you, {PLAYER}!$

replies.text: Visit Mom, defeat Dad again. Family errands have become unusually competitive.
He wants to improve and wants you to stay connected to home. Those can coexist.
We should visit your mother. And give him a real challenge when he is ready again.
He sounds proud even while trying very hard to sound competitive.
We can stop home between journeys. Being missed is a good reason all by itself.
A father's reminder arrives wrapped in the declaration of a sworn sporting rival.
He found a way to ask you to visit while insisting this is strictly Gym business.
He has a training plan. We should keep developing ours rather than assume the next result.
Home can hold a welcome and a challenge at the same time.
I hope he follows his own advice and goes home sometimes, too.
That sounded like two different parts of him trying to speak in the same sentence.

contexts.subject: After the League Norman says the Pokemon world is so deep training never feels sufficient.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_DadNoAmountOfTrai.text: DAD: {PLAYER}, how are things going?\pThe world of POKéMON is deep.\pI honestly think that no amount of\ntraining would ever be enough.$

replies.text: Even Dad has not reached the end of learning. That makes my unfinished list feel less personal.
There is always another question. That does not make the work already done insufficient.
He can keep improving without treating every rest as falling behind. So can you.
I like knowing he still wonders about things after becoming so good at them.
Enough for one day is allowed, even when there is more to learn tomorrow.
The expert has discovered the subject is larger than his ending. A promising sequel.
There is something comforting about not having to become finished.
A deep subject keeps giving back when you examine it closely. I understand the fascination.
The well does not need a bottom for the water to be worth drawing.
I hope he lets himself be accomplished as well as ambitious.
I would like to hear what still surprises him after all his years here.

contexts.subject: Norman asks the player dream and says his own has already come true.

PetalburgCity_Gym_Text_NormanPostRematch.text: DAD: {PLAYER}…\nWhat is your dream?\pMy dream…\nHahaha…\lIt has already come true, actually.$

replies.text: I think that laugh said something he could not quite fit into words.
He seems content with something more personal than winning this battle.
He is proud. You do not need to find a perfect answer immediately.
That was very small and very important. I do not want to talk over it.
It sounds like he is glad he gets to be here with you.
A quiet line can carry more than the grandest victory speech.
I think we should let that moment stay yours for a little while.
His goal was evidently more complicated than a battle record. I am glad he reached it.
Some dreams come home wearing a familiar face.
He did not have to explain all of it for the feeling to reach us.
That is the moment I would keep from today. If you wanted me to.

contexts.subject: The passionate Volbeat owner is disappointed that the player declined the trade.

FortreeCity_House1_Text_YouWontTradeMe.text: No? You won't trade me?\nEven after I bared my heart to you?$

replies.text: His heart was very loud, but our answer still counts.
A strong preference is not an obligation for the other person.
He can be disappointed. We can still keep our partner.
That was rather a lot of feeling to put on a stranger.
He offered a trade, not a debt. Saying no is allowed.
A magnificent declaration, sadly defeated by an ordinary refusal.
He bared his heart. We did not sign for delivery.
Perhaps next time he can start with the actual proposal.
A wish spoken loudly does not become someone else's promise.
He made declining sound rude. It really wasn't.
He certainly made his feelings clear. We were clear too.

contexts.subject: The trader rejects a Pokemon of the wrong requested species.

FortreeCity_House1_Text_ThisIsntAMon.text: Uh, no, I don't think so.\nThat isn't a {STR_VAR_1}.$

replies.text: We brought a perfectly good Pokemon to the wrong appointment.
The species does not match his request. That settles this attempt.
Wrong partner for this trade. No need to force it.
I think we both heard his request a little differently.
That one wasn't on his shopping list, apparently.
An excellent entrance for entirely the wrong candidate.
Rejected on a technicality. A fairly substantial technicality.
We should check the species before trying the exchange again.
It is still itself, even when someone wanted something else.
An unsuitable match says nothing bad about our Pokemon.
Specific tastes! At least he told us exactly what went wrong.

contexts.subject: After the completed trade, the new Volbeat owner promises to train it and asks the same for Plusle.

FortreeCity_House1_Text_GoingToMakeVolbe.text: I'm going to make VOLBEAT super\nstrong from this moment on!\pI hope you do the same with PLUSLE!$

replies.text: Volbeat and Plusle both have people cheering for them now.
He has turned his enthusiasm into a concrete commitment. Good.
He's serious about raising Volbeat. Let's do right by Plusle.
It helps to hear that goodbye wasn't the end of caring.
Two new homes, and both promising to do their best.
The exchange has become a pair of promises. A better ending.
He still sounds loud. Volbeat seems to have acquired a fan.
His next project is training, and he has plenty of motivation.
They have different paths now, with someone beside each of them.
Plusle wasn't an afterthought in his goodbye. I liked that.
We should remember this enthusiasm when Plusle needs encouragement.

contexts.subject: A resident sees Pokemon trades as exchanging memories with other people.

FortreeCity_House1_Text_TradingMemoriesW.text: Trading POKéMON with others…\pIt's as if you're trading your own\nmemories with other people.$

replies.text: A traded Pokemon arrives with stories we haven't heard yet.
Its experiences do not reset when its traveling companion changes.
Someone trusted us with a partner they knew. That matters.
I like thinking the old memories still have somewhere to stay.
A new home can make room for an old favorite habit.
A character arrives with a whole unwritten first chapter.
The past comes along. It rarely packs lightly.
Learning how they were raised could help us understand them.
A memory can travel without leaving its first home empty.
That makes asking about the previous Trainer feel rather important.
I'd listen to the stories before adding a few of our own.

contexts.subject: The player guessed the wrong hand in the Hidden Power test.

replies.text: My hidden power appears to be picking the empty hand.
A wrong guess is weak evidence about anyone's hidden abilities.
Missed a coin. We'll survive the setback.
I couldn't tell either. Her hands gave very little away.
Well, we haven't misplaced the coin. She still has it.
Our mysterious gift has elected to remain mysterious.
My talent for uncertainty remains undefeated.
We could watch her hands more closely on another attempt.
Sometimes a closed hand is simply a closed hand.
She delivered the verdict rather briskly, didn't she?
Now I'm curious whether anyone notices her switching it.

contexts.subject: The Hidden Power giver explains that its effect changes with the Pokemon.

FortreeCity_House2_Text_ExplainHiddenPow.text: HIDDEN POWER is a move that changes\nwith the POKéMON.$

replies.text: One move with a different surprise inside each Pokemon!
The user matters as much as the move's name. Worth testing.
Check what it does before relying on it in a hard fight.
I like that the same lesson can come out differently.
Same recipe card, very different ingredients doing the work.
A single title concealing several possible plots. Intriguing.
Even the move refuses to be easily categorized. Fair enough.
We should compare results instead of assuming the name tells us everything.
Something particular to each Pokemon answers through that move.
A shared name with an individual expression. Lovely little detail.
I'd like to see how different two uses of it can look.

contexts.subject: A stone seeker recalls Steven and his exceptionally well trained Pokemon.

FortreeCity_House3_Text_MetStevenHadAmaz.text:
While speaking about POKéDEXES,
I remembered something.\pI met this TRAINER, STEVEN, when
I was searching for rare stones.\pHoo, boy, he had some amazing POKéMON
with him.\pThey weren't just rare, they were
trained to terrifying extremes!\pHe might even be stronger than the
GYM LEADER in this town…$

replies.text: He went looking for rare stones and found a terrifying Trainer attached.
Rarity and training are separate qualities. Steven apparently supplies both.
That sounds like a team you prepare for properly.
He seemed more struck by their training than their rarity.
Finding something rare is one thing. Raising it well takes longer.
A stone hunt interrupted by an encounter with local legend.
Terrifyingly well trained. A compliment with sensible distance built in.
I'd ask what their training actually involved. That's the useful part.
He remembers the strength more clearly than the stones.
Steven made quite an impression without having to announce himself.
I love how a conversation about rocks became this story.

contexts.subject: A child is impressed on learning that the player carries a Pokedex.

FortreeCity_House3_Text_OhYouHavePokedex.text: What's that thing you have there?\p… … … … … …\pOh, it's called a POKéDEX?\nIt's really awesome!$

replies.text: We have been carrying something awesome around like an ordinary pocket lump.
A portable record of Pokemon is impressive. Familiarity hides that.
Nice to see someone excited about what we learn out there.
I forget it can look extraordinary the first time.
That little introduction made his whole face brighten.
Behold, the glamorous life of carrying field notes.
An enthusiastic audience for a very small encyclopedia.
That's exactly the response a useful invention deserves.
A small object can open a rather large door.
He asked, listened, and was delighted. Excellent conversation.
I'd show him an entry about a Pokemon he knows.

contexts.subject: A resident values the friendships people make through Pokemon.

FortreeCity_House4_Text_BringsWorldClose.text: By being together with POKéMON,\npeople make more and more friends.\pAnd that brings the world closer\ntogether. I think it's wonderful!$

replies.text: Pokemon are very good at introducing people who were minding their own business.
A shared interest lowers the difficulty of that first conversation.
A good partner can help you find good people.
It is easier to say hello when they have already started.
There is always something to talk about when a Pokemon joins in.
The finest social organizer may have feathers and no schedule.
Accidental friendship is one of their less advertised talents.
The Wingull next door is doing practical work toward her theory.
Little meetings can tie distant places together.
She's noticed how often affection gives strangers common ground.
That's how so many good conversations start: asking about someone's Pokemon.

contexts.subject: The boy says his absent Wingull is away running an errand.

FortreeCity_House4_Text_AskedWingullToRu.text: Heheh, I asked my WINGULL to run\nan errand for me.$

replies.text: Wingull has errands. I feel slightly underorganized beside a bird.
An airborne messenger can cross terrain that slows us considerably.
Sounds like he's waiting for his partner to return.
The room feels quieter while the bird is away.
Sending Wingull is probably quicker than sending us up those ladders.
A small courier somewhere in the middle of a large assignment.
Even birds have chores. A sobering discovery.
I wonder how they agreed on the destination. Training must matter.
Someone elsewhere may be looking up for a familiar pair of wings.
He sounds quite pleased with his little arrangement.
I'd ask who Wingull is visiting. Errands connect interesting people.

contexts.subject: After Wingull has returned, the boy credits it for his distant friendships.

FortreeCity_House4_Text_FriendsFarAwayTh.text: Thanks to my WINGULL, I have friends\nwho live far away.$

replies.text: Wingull makes far away sound like somewhere just down the branch.
Reliable communication changes which friendships distance can sustain.
Good bird. Keeping people connected is useful work.
It must be nice to recognize those wings coming home.
A letter carried back makes the distance feel less empty.
One bird, several friendships, and an excellent sense of direction.
The post has feathers and a social life. Good for it.
His messenger route has become a real little network.
A returning bird brings more than whatever it holds.
He remembers to credit Wingull for making those connections possible.
There must be wonderful stories at both ends of that flight.

contexts.subject: A resident praises Fortree tree houses as a way to live with Pokemon.

FortreeCity_House5_Text_TreeHousesAreGre.text: The tree houses of FORTREE are great!\pI think it's the number one town for\nliving together with POKéMON.$

replies.text: A town where upstairs begins before you enter the house!
Their homes use the forest's vertical space remarkably well.
Good homes. I'd still watch those steps in the rain.
You can hear the leaves from almost anywhere in here.
Carrying groceries home must count as the day's exercise.
She has a strong claim for the finest address among the branches.
Living in a tree does make being indoors wonderfully ambiguous.
The supports and walkways make this much more than a charming idea.
The trees remain neighbors, even with houses around them.
She is proud of the way her home fits its surroundings.
I'd love to hear what mornings sound like up here.

contexts.subject: A resident argues for adapting human homes to nature rather than forcing nature to fit.

FortreeCity_House5_Text_AdaptedToNature.text: POKéMON and people have adapted to\nnature for survival.\pThere's no need to make nature\nconform to the way we want to live.$

replies.text: The trees were here first. Building around them seems polite.
Adaptation can reduce how much a settlement must disrupt.
Work with the land. Fighting it gets expensive.
I like a house that leaves room for the things already living there.
You learn a place's limits before deciding what to build.
An unusually reasonable demand that the scenery retain its role.
The forest has declined our renovation proposal. Wisely.
Constraints can lead to good designs. These houses are evidence.
A home can belong somewhere without making everything else leave.
Making space for neighbors includes the ones with roots.
I'd ask what they changed after their first rainy season.

contexts.subject: A shopper wants a desk to protect Secret Base dolls from dirt and splinters.

FortreeCity_DecorationShop_Text_BuyingDe.text: I'm buying a pretty desk and I'm\nputting my cute DOLLS on it.\pIf I don't, when I decorate my\nSECRET BASE, my DOLLS will get\ldirty or poked with splinters.$

replies.text: Even dolls deserve a seat without splinters in it.
A raised surface protects the fabric from debris and abrasion.
Solid reason to buy a desk. Keep the little things safe.
She has already pictured where each doll will sit.
A clean place for treasured things is worth making.
The dolls have acquired both furniture and a devoted estate manager.
A tiny gathering with remarkably strict seating standards.
She should check the desk's finish too. Splinters can be sneaky.
Small belongings can make a hidden place feel like home.
She's furnishing for the dolls' comfort. I respect that commitment.
I'd love to see the little arrangement when she's finished.

contexts.subject: A shopper envies the furniture delivery service and wishes it could deliver them home.

FortreeCity_DecorationShop_Text_Merchand.text: Merchandise you buy here is sent to\nyour own PC.\pThat's fantastic! I wish they could\nalso deliver me home like that.$

replies.text: I also become interested in delivery whenever stairs are involved.
Transporting merchandise and transporting people are rather different problems.
After carrying furniture, I'd ask the same question.
It does sound tempting after a long day in town.
Buy a chair, then ask if you can ride home on it.
An inspired request to include the customer in the purchase.
The desk gets a convenient journey. We get legs. Unfair.
An efficient delivery service creates ambitious expectations.
Getting home is sometimes the hardest part of an outing.
The furniture has a better travel arrangement than its owner.
I'd enjoy hearing the clerk try to answer that request.

contexts.subject: Cozmo is away at Meteor Falls with Team Magma.

FallarborTown_CozmosHouse_Text_CozmoWent.text: PROF. COZMO went off to METEOR FALLS\non ROUTE 114 with some people from\lTEAM MAGMA.$

replies.text: A meteorite trip sounds exciting. The company sounds less promising.
His research may be genuine; his companions' motives deserve scrutiny.
Team Magma is involved. We should check on him.
She says it casually. I wish that made it sound safer.
I don't like hearing who offered to accompany him.
An innocent research trip has acquired a worrying supporting cast.
Rocks are usually the safer part of field research. Usually.
Meteor Falls gives us somewhere specific to look for him.
Curiosity can lead someone through a door they should inspect first.
He may see research partners where we see warning signs.
I'd rather ask Cozmo himself how this expedition came together.

contexts.subject: Cozmo regrets being deceived into revealing meteorite locations to Team Magma.

FallarborTown_CozmosHouse_Text_Meteorite.text: PROF. COZMO: Oh…\nI never should have let myself be\lconned into telling TEAM MAGMA where\lyou can find METEORITES…\pThat METEORITE from METEOR FALLS…\nIt's never going to be mine now…$

replies.text: He wanted to share something wonderful. They took advantage of that.
Sharing research was not the wrongdoing. Exploiting his trust was.
They used him. That fault belongs to Team Magma.
He sounds as if losing trust hurt almost as much as losing the stone.
It's miserable when helping someone becomes the thing you regret.
The villains borrowed his expertise and left him the blame. Typical.
A bad audience for a good enthusiasm. I hate that.
His knowledge is still valuable, despite how they misused it.
A stolen stone has left a heavier absence than its size suggests.
He deserves to be angry with them, not only himself.
I'd listen before asking him to tell the whole story again.

contexts.subject: Cozmo is disappointed after the player refuses to exchange the meteorite.

FallarborTown_CozmosHouse_Text_CrushedWi.text: PROF. COZMO: Oh, but…\nI'm crushed with disappointment…$

replies.text: He had already imagined that stone on his desk, hadn't he?
He was invested in the exchange. It remains a choice.
We declined. No need to make the disappointment worse.
That sounded very small after all his excitement.
We can be gentle even when the answer stays no.
His entire bright prospect collapsed into one short sentence.
Disappointment has made itself quite at home in this room.
He may accept the same exchange later if we reconsider.
Something almost within reach can hurt more than something distant.
He didn't hide how much it mattered to him.
Let's give him a moment rather than hovering over that answer.

contexts.subject: The meteorite exchange has succeeded and Cozmo is delighted to resume research.

FallarborTown_CozmosHouse_Text_ReallyGoi.text: PROF. COZMO: Oh, I can't believe it.\nThis is really, really great!\pThis is really going to help my research!$

replies.text: That space rock has finally reached someone who wants to study it!
He has the specimen and a genuine research question again. Excellent.
Good. The meteorite is where it can do some good.
He sounds lighter already. I am glad we heard this part.
That's the sound of someone getting their work back.
A stolen discovery returns to the story it should have had.
The room is less gloomy. I shall try not to take it personally.
Now he can investigate the actual material instead of losing sleep over it.
A little fallen piece of sky has given him his footing back.
That happiness looks thoroughly unpolished. The best kind.
I'd come back later and ask what he learned from it.

contexts.subject: Cozmo wife worries about his depression after the Team Magma incident.

FallarborTown_CozmosHouse_Text_FeelSorry.text: Poor PROF. COZMO…\nHe's so depressed… I feel sorry for him.$

replies.text: She can't fix the missing meteorite just by worrying beside him.
She sees the effect on him every day. That is difficult too.
He's not the only person this has been hard on.
She sounds tired of not knowing how to help.
Watching someone lose their enthusiasm can quiet a whole house.
Even the person outside the adventure has to live with its aftermath.
There isn't a clever remark that makes this less sad.
Getting his research moving again could give him something concrete to do.
She has been keeping company with his disappointment.
It matters that someone noticed how badly he was hurt.
I'd ask how he's been doing, and let her answer at her own pace.

contexts.subject: Cozmo wife affectionately celebrates his happiness after the meteorite is returned.

FallarborTown_CozmosHouse_Text_CozmoIsSo.text: Look at PROF. COZMO…\nHe's so happy! I think it's cute.$

replies.text: She's enjoying his happiness almost as much as he is!
A restored specimen has improved the mood of an entire household.
She's relieved. Good to see them both smiling.
It is sweet that she wants us to notice him being happy.
Some good news belongs to everyone at home.
The researcher's joy has received a glowing domestic review.
Apparently enthusiasm is contagious. This case seems harmless.
The meteorite has already produced one very visible result.
She sees the person glowing behind all the talk about stones.
That fond little observation says a great deal about them.
I like seeing the people around a discovery enjoy it too.

contexts.subject: A visitor wonders about ancient Pokemon and suggests asking the Fossil Maniac.

FallarborTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Foss.text: I wonder what POKéMON looked like\nlong, long ago?\pMaybe the FOSSIL MANIAC at the edge\nof town will know.$

replies.text: An ancient Pokemon might have had an ancient version of a very silly face.
Fossils let us compare curiosity with physical evidence. I'd ask him.
Someone nearby studies this. Good place to start.
It is strange to imagine familiar ground with entirely different lives on it.
I wonder what they needed to get through an ordinary day.
The oldest characters have left us a difficult manuscript to read.
Finally, a neighbor with an appropriate interest in old bones.
I'd ask what the fossils can show, and what remains a guess.
The ground remembers shapes no living eye has seen.
There must have been beautiful forms we can only partly reconstruct.
A local expert and a good question. That sounds like a worthwhile visit.

contexts.subject: Fallarbor residents plant trees hardy enough for volcanic ash.

FallarborTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Plan.text: In the fields of FALLARBOR, we plant\nseedlings of hardy trees that thrive\leven in volcanic ash.$

replies.text: Little trees setting up home in a giant dust problem!
Choosing ash-tolerant seedlings is more effective than ignoring the soil.
They know what grows here and put the work in.
It must feel good to see those first leaves survive.
A good planting starts with knowing the ground you're working.
A town insisting on a green future, one stubborn seedling at a time.
Hardy little trees. Sensible neighbors for this weather.
I'd ask which species take root best and how they protect new growth.
Soft new leaves can belong to a harsh landscape.
They chose plants that suit the place. There is care in that.
I'd like to see how those fields change as the trees grow.

contexts.subject: Herbal medicine is effective but bitter enough to upset Pokemon.

LavaridgeTown_HerbShop_Text_HerbalMedici.text: Herbal medicine works impressively well.\nBut your POKéMON will dislike you for it.\lIt must be horribly bitter!$

replies.text: A medicine can win the battle and lose the taste contest spectacularly.
Effectiveness and tolerability are separate qualities. He is warning us about both.
Useful in a pinch. Remember how our partner feels afterward.
That sounds like the sort of taste you remember for years.
Cheap and effective still leaves a very unhappy mouth to deal with.
A cure whose review reads: effective, unforgivable, never again.
Bitter medicine. The adjective appears to be doing serious work.
Knowing the drawback helps us choose rather than being surprised later.
A healed body can still have a grievance. Understandably.
I'd rather know that cost before handing it to someone I care about.
His expression makes me believe he has heard some strong complaints.

contexts.subject: After giving Charcoal, the old man explains its herbal use and Fire move boost.

LavaridgeTown_HerbShop_Text_ExplainCharc.text:
That CHARCOAL I gave you, it's used
for making herbal medicine.\pIt also does wonders when held by
a POKéMON.\pIt intensifies the power of FIRE-type
moves.$

replies.text: Charcoal has a job here and a much hotter job with Pokemon.
One material serves two distinct uses. Its origin doesn't limit its application.
Good to know what it does before handing it to a partner.
I wouldn't have guessed that from something so plain-looking.
I knew charcoal was useful. This is a different sort of useful.
A humble black object with unexpectedly dramatic potential.
Dark, unassuming, and helpful. An admirable combination.
That is a practical explanation I can actually use.
A little remnant of fire keeps another kind of fire company.
It doesn't need to look impressive to earn its place.
I'd ask which Pokemon he has seen put it to best use.

contexts.subject: A husband says his wife is warming the Egg discovered at the Day Care.

LavaridgeTown_House_Text_WifeWarmingEggI.text: My wife's warming an EGG in the hot\nsprings. This is what she told me.\pShe left two POKéMON with the DAY CARE.\nAnd they discovered that EGG!$

replies.text: That Egg is having a spa day before it has even met anybody.
She has found a warm place to wait for it to hatch.
Sounds like she's keeping it close and watching over it.
She must be wondering what is inside every time it moves.
Someone is already fussing over its comfort. Good start.
Our smallest unseen guest enjoys the town's finest amenities.
An excellent excuse to stay in warm water for another hour.
I'd still want to make sure the Egg wasn't getting too hot.
A quiet beginning, held in warm hands.
He tells it like ordinary household news. I find that lovely.
I'd love to hear from them when that Egg finally opens.

contexts.subject: A bather enjoys the restorative hot springs and wishes Pokemon could soak too.

LavaridgeTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_HotS.text: It's sort of magical how just sitting\nin a hot-spring pool can invigorate.\pI wish I could let my POKéMON\nsoak, too.$

replies.text: The water gets all the credit while we just sit there. Excellent arrangement.
Warmth and rest can feel remarkably restorative after travel.
A good soak sounds sensible after the road here.
I like the part where nobody needs you to hurry.
Warm water, tired feet, and no dishes afterward. Tempting.
A rare local attraction that asks the visitor to accomplish less.
Sitting quietly in warm water. My ambition has found its subject.
They should check which Pokemon are comfortable with hot water first.
Some kinds of magic are just being warm long enough.
Feeling better and wanting to share it is rather sweet.
Everyone coming out of the springs seems to talk a little slower.

contexts.subject: A resident believes time spent together strengthens Pokemon friendships.

LavaridgeTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trai.text: I think POKéMON get closer to their\nTRAINERS if they spend time together.\pThe longer the better.\nThat's what I think.$

replies.text: Even an uneventful walk can count as a good day together.
Repeated, comfortable contact gives trust something to develop around.
Showing up consistently does more than a grand gesture.
You don't always need something interesting to say.
The ordinary parts matter: meals, rests, being there again tomorrow.
A convincing defense of the chapters where nobody saves the world.
Quiet company is still company. I appreciate that.
Shared time lets you notice small changes before they become problems.
Familiar footsteps can become a kind of home.
It takes time to learn what makes someone comfortable beside you.
Long trips leave room for the little habits you start recognizing.

contexts.subject: A resident reminds Trainers to rest alongside their Pokemon and points toward the springs.

LavaridgeTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trai.text: Hohoho! Hey, kid, you can reach\nthe hot springs from here.\pIf POKéMON are getting rest, so too\nshould their TRAINERS.$

replies.text: We've been prescribed sitting in warm water. I can follow that instruction.
A tired Trainer makes poorer decisions. Rest serves the whole team.
He's right. Take care of the person making the calls too.
It's nice when someone remembers to ask us to rest.
Being responsible doesn't require being exhausted. Let's sit down.
At last, an elder's advice that involves fewer ordeals.
A medical opinion in favor of doing very little. Approved.
There's a convenient place to recover right here. We should use it.
The one leading the journey is allowed to stop walking.
He has clearly watched a lot of Trainers forget themselves.
We might enjoy the next stretch more with rested feet.

contexts.subject: A visitor compares Victory Road to a life journey and encourages trust in Pokemon.

EverGrandeCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Bel.text: The long and harrowing VICTORY ROAD…\pIt's like reliving the path one has\ntraveled in life…\pBelieve in your POKéMON and give it\nyour very best!$

replies.text: That road gave us plenty to remember, including several very stubborn rocks.
We have practical evidence of what our team can overcome together.
We've come through difficult ground. Trust the partners who did it with us.
Looking back makes the distance feel real all at once.
A breath, a proper rest, and then we give the next part our best.
The long road has earned its place in the story. So has the team.
A harrowing life comparison, conveniently located beside a healing counter.
We can carry what we learned through that road into the next challenge.
The path behind us is full of small acts of trust.
They see how far we have come. We should let ourselves see it too.
I want to remember the faces beside us at this point.

contexts.subject: A visitor says the League is close after Victory Road and urges the player onward.

EverGrandeCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Lea.text: The POKéMON LEAGUE is only a short\ndistance after the VICTORY ROAD.\pIf you've come this far, what choice\ndo you have but to keep going?$

replies.text: We have other choices, but this one has been waiting at the end of the road.
We can continue after confirming that the team is ready.
Close now. Rest first, then go in prepared.
Being this close makes it feel bigger, somehow.
We can be excited and still stop long enough to eat.
An excellent dramatic location for a final check of our supplies.
The destination has stopped being theoretical. Slightly inconvenient for my nerves.
A short distance doesn't tell us how demanding the next part will be.
A threshold can feel longer than the road that brought us there.
There's encouragement in how certain they are we belong here.
I'd take one look back at the road before going forward.
