contexts.subject: Scott celebrates the player reaching the League and promises contact if they become Champion.

EverGrandeCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Sco.text:
SCOTT: {PLAYER}{KUN}, you've clawed your
way up to face the POKéMON LEAGUE!\pI'm happy for you!
You made my cheering worthwhile!\p{PLAYER}{KUN}, if you were to become
the POKéMON LEAGUE CHAMPION…\pI'll get in touch with you then.\pOkay, {PLAYER}{KUN}.
Go for greatness!$

replies.text: Scott has saved up a whole League's worth of cheering for us.
His promised contact is conditional. For now, we have a challenge ahead.
He kept an eye on our progress. Let's make a solid attempt.
That is quite a lot of confidence to receive just before going in.
A familiar face cheering here takes some of the chill out of it.
Scott offers a tantalizing sequel. We must finish this chapter first.
He sounds delighted. Apparently our difficult walk had a spectator.
Whatever he has planned can wait until we've handled the League.
Someone has been hoping we would reach this door.
He made his pride in us quite clear. That's generous.
I'd like to tell him how it goes after we've actually tried.

contexts.subject: The League attendant denies entry because the player lacks all required badges.

EverGrandeCity_PokemonLeague_1F_Text_Hav.text: You haven't obtained all the BADGES.\pIf you're bound for the POKéMON\nLEAGUE, you must return with them.$

replies.text: We reached the door before we finished collecting the keys.
The entry requirement remains unmet. Traveling here doesn't replace it.
We know what is missing. Let's finish that work.
A long trip to hear a short answer. At least it is clear.
Better to find out here than walk into something we're not ready for.
The grand entrance has been postponed by the admissions office.
The door is unmoved by our impressive arrival. Understandable.
Let's check the badge case and plan the remaining stops.
A closed door can still tell you which path to take next.
He was firm without making it personal. That's fair.
We can return with a different answer in our badge case.

contexts.subject: After checking all badges, the League attendant admits the player and encourages the team.

EverGrandeCity_PokemonLeague_1F_Text_GoF.text: TRAINER! Believe in yourself and your\nPOKéMON, and go forth!$

replies.text: The door says yes! My stomach appears to be saying several things.
All requirements are satisfied. The rest depends on our decisions together.
We're cleared to enter. One battle at a time.
I knew the door would open. Hearing it still feels enormous.
We've prepared what we can. Let's look after one another in there.
Our introduction is complete. Now comes the part worth remembering.
An open door. A surprisingly effective source of nerves.
Final checks are done. We can focus on the challenge itself now.
Carry the trust that brought us here across that threshold.
A simple welcome, earned one badge at a time.
Take a breath. This is a moment we'll want to remember clearly.

contexts.subject: A child proudly recalls their father helping clear trees for Rustboro expansion.

RustboroCity_CuttersHouse_Text_DadHelped.text: When they were expanding the city of\nRUSTBORO, my dad helped out.\pHe made his POKéMON use CUT to clear\nthe land of trees.$

replies.text: His dad helped make room for the city. That's a big thing to point at.
Pokemon labor was part of the city's growth. I'd ask what stood here before.
He's proud of his father doing useful work. I get that.
It must be odd to remember trees where there are houses now.
A child can see a whole town and think of their dad.
A family's little story fits inside the city's larger one.
The city's history has stumps beneath the paving.
Clearing land changes drainage too. Expansion takes more than cutting.
A growing town leaves memories of the forest it replaced.
He knows a piece of the city through someone he loves.
I'd ask which part his father helped build room for.

contexts.subject: The Cutter explains reusable Cut HM and the Stone Badge needed to use it in the field.

RustboroCity_CuttersHouse_Text_ExplainCu.text:
That HIDDEN MACHINE, or HM for
short, is CUT.\pAn HM move is one that can be used
by POKéMON outside of battle.\pAny POKéMON that's learned CUT can
chop down thin trees if the TRAINER\lhas earned the STONE BADGE.\pAnd, unlike a TM, an HM can be used
more than once.$

replies.text: A useful lesson that doesn't disappear after one Pokemon learns it!
Learning the move and having permission to use it outside battle are separate.
Useful for a blocked path. Check the badge requirement first.
I like having the explanation after the excitement settles down.
One tool we can keep teaching from. That's generous.
An obstacle-removal lesson with surprisingly durable teaching material.
A thin tree is about to have an inconvenient afternoon.
Reusable instructions make it easier to train the right partner.
A path can open, but the choice to cut still belongs to us.
He made the limits clear along with the possibilities.
I would check which paths it opens around the city.

contexts.subject: A Devon employee is pleased to see the player wearing their Running Shoes.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_1F_Text_ThoseShoe.text: Hey, those RUNNING SHOES!\nThey're one of our products!\pIt makes me happy when I see someone\nusing something we made.$

replies.text: Our muddy feet just gave somebody a professional compliment.
Seeing a product used is a satisfying form of feedback.
They work. We've put enough distance on them to know.
He looks happy to know they made it out into the world.
Something he helped make is making our day easier. Nice.
Our shoes have become traveling ambassadors with terrible manners.
A touching reunion between an employee and some very worn footwear.
Actual use tells you things a demonstration never will.
He sees a little of his work in our journey.
A well-made everyday thing deserves that kind of pride.
I'd tell him which part of the journey they've helped with most.

contexts.subject: A Devon attendant refuses entry to unauthorized visitors.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_1F_Text_OnlyAutho.text: I'm sorry, only authorized people\nare allowed to enter here.$

replies.text: Our enthusiastic face doesn't seem to count as authorization.
A research workplace has reasonable reasons to restrict access.
Private area. We can ask who handles visitors.
I think we have reached the end of this particular hallway.
Fair enough. People are trying to work back there.
Curiosity meets the employee responsible for saying no.
The boundary is admirably clear. I can respect a closed door.
We need permission from someone responsible for the site.
Some thresholds are kept for ordinary reasons.
A polite refusal is still a refusal. We can move along.
I'd ask if there is a public area where visitors can learn more.

contexts.subject: An employee has heard that the stolen Devon Goods were recovered.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_1F_Text_SoundsLik.text: It sounds like they've recovered\nthe ripped-off DEVON GOODS.$

replies.text: Good news is finally making its way around the building.
The report has reached the staff. Recovery eases more than one concern.
The parcel's back. One less thing for them to worry about.
Even secondhand relief sounds different from the worry before.
Work probably feels a little more normal with that settled.
The building's rumor network has received a welcome update.
At last, office gossip with a tolerable conclusion.
Now they can check the goods and resume the interrupted work.
Something missing has returned to the shape of their day.
A small sentence carrying quite a lot of relief.
I'd be curious how quickly that news reached every floor.

contexts.subject: An employee says the stolen specialist parcel would be useless to an ordinary thief.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_1F_Text_RobberWas.text: That stolen parcel…\pWell, sure it's important, but it's not\nanything that anyone can use.\pIn my estimation, that robber must not\nhave been very bright.$

replies.text: Stealing a thing before knowing what it does is a very crooked shopping plan.
It may require specialized knowledge. That does not make the theft harmless.
Useless to the thief still means missing from the people who need it.
He sounds more insulted by the thief's judgment than anything else.
An important parcel doesn't have to be useful to everybody.
A theft whose research phase appears to have been omitted.
A specialized disappointment for an unspecialized criminal.
Unless the thief was acting for someone else. I'd avoid assuming too much.
They carried away a purpose they did not understand.
I wouldn't mistake their ignorance for a reason to relax.
I'd ask who actually knows how those goods are used.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that each Pokemon has a special ability.

RustboroCity_Flat1_1F_Text_EveryPokemonH.text: Every POKéMON has a special ability\nthat it can use.$

replies.text: Every Pokemon comes with its own little surprise clause.
Abilities can matter even when no move is being selected.
Know your partner's ability. Know the opponent may have one too.
Some of the important things aren't obvious at first glance.
It's worth learning what helps each partner do well.
Every character arrives with something absent from the move list.
An unseen advantage. Naturally, that also means unseen trouble.
I'd examine the ability before planning how to use a move.
What a creature is can change what happens around it.
Two similar-looking Pokemon can still bring different strengths.
I'd ask which ability first made them notice this.

contexts.subject: A resident simply marvels at the strangeness of Pokemon.

replies.text: Some of them are tiny, some are enormous, and all of them get hungry.
Familiarity has not made them any less worthy of investigation.
Strange, yes. Reliable company all the same.
I still notice something unexpected when I think I know one.
They can astonish you and steal your lunch in the same minute.
A concise review of a very complicated subject.
A world full of odd creatures. I feel appropriately at home.
The more you learn, the better your questions get.
A familiar face can still hold a little mystery.
That is a perfectly fair reaction to looking around here.
I'd love to know which Pokemon started that thought.

contexts.subject: A resident travels to meet the varied people and Pokemon of different places.

RustboroCity_House1_Text_AllSortsOfPlace.text: In all sorts of places, there are all\nsorts of POKéMON and people.\pI find that fascinating, so I go to all\nsorts of places.$

replies.text: That's a good reason to travel. The snacks can be a second reason.
Different environments offer different encounters. A fine incentive for fieldwork.
Travel with open eyes. Plenty worth meeting out there.
I like hearing a place described through who lives there.
You learn a town quickly when someone invites you to their table.
A sensible objection to spending one's entire story in one room.
A compelling argument, despite the unfortunate amount of walking.
I'd ask what surprised them most between two neighboring towns.
Some places become dear because of who met us there.
They seem interested in differences without judging them. I like that.
That is exactly the kind of travel story I want to hear.

contexts.subject: After trading, the owner says care and kindness can make any Pokemon cute.

RustboroCity_House1_Text_AnyPokemonCanBe.text: Any POKéMON can be cute if you raise\nit with care and kindness.$

replies.text: Even a very grumpy face gets cuter when you know who's making it.
Affection changes what details an observer notices.
Treat them well. You start seeing the little things.
Knowing someone can make a plain moment feel lovely.
A familiar appetite can become surprisingly endearing.
A persuasive defense of the charm hidden outside the usual casting choices.
Some of us require a generous interpretation of cute. Appreciated.
Care lets their comfortable habits show. That's useful to remember.
Kindness gives small, guarded things room to unfold.
Cute is often a relationship before it is a look.
I'd ask what habit made them first feel that way.

contexts.subject: The Rustboro trader accepts a refusal while remaining proud of their Pokemon.

RustboroCity_House1_Text_YouDontWantToTh.text: Oh, if you don't want to, that's okay.\nBut my POKéMON is cute, you know…$

replies.text: No trade, and the Pokemon still gets a compliment. Good result.
They accept our decision without withdrawing their affection.
That is a fair way to take no for an answer.
I'm glad nobody had to feel awkward for very long.
They like their partner either way. That's reassuring.
The proposal ends gracefully, with one final advertisement for cuteness.
A refusal survived without catastrophe. Refreshing.
No exchange needed if the arrangement doesn't suit both Trainers.
Their affection hasn't depended on our answer.
A little pride, without trying to make us feel guilty.
I like how easily we can keep talking after that.

contexts.subject: The Rustboro trader rejects the offered Pokemon because it is not the requested species.

RustboroCity_House1_Text_DoesntLookLikeM.text: Huh? That doesn't look anything like\na {STR_VAR_1} to me.$

replies.text: The Pokemon is here. The correct Pokemon is apparently elsewhere.
A species mismatch prevents the proposed exchange.
Wrong species for this trade. Simple enough to correct.
That was a very understandable bit of confusion.

contexts.subject: The trader asks the player to care well for their Pokemon after a successful trade.

contexts.subject: A resident questions whether naming Pikachu Pekachu is meaningfully original.

contexts.subject: A resident proudly claims perfectly suited Pokemon nicknames as an expression of originality.

RustboroCity_House3_Text_IGivePerfectlyS.text: For my own POKéMON, I give them\nperfectly suited nicknames!\pIt's my expression of, uh…\noriginality, yes, that's it!$

contexts.subject: A child admires Roxanne knowledge as well as her strength.

contexts.subject: A resident praises the Trainer School as a possible beginning for future Gym Leaders.

RustboroCity_House2_Text_TrainerSchoolEx.text: The TRAINER'S SCHOOL is excellent.\pIf you study there, you could even\nbecome a GYM LEADER.$

contexts.subject: A Trainer compares their naive Pokemon with a friend jolly Pokemon.

Every familiar kind of creature can hold an unfamiliar someone.

contexts.subject: A student struggles to record the many held items after learning about berries.

contexts.subject: The teacher explains Quick Claw occasional priority and the breadth of held item study.

contexts.subject: Rydel invites the player to return if they want to exchange bicycle types.

MauvilleCity_BikeShop_Text_ComeBackToSwi.text: RYDEL: If you get the urge to switch\nBIKES, just come see me!$

WALLY: Please watch me, {PLAYER}.\nI'm going to get stronger than you.\pWhen I do, I'm going to challenge you\nto another battle.$

What cannot be seen may still change the path of a thing.
Appearances alone won't tell us what a move can accomplish.
I'd ask for an example they've actually run into.

contexts.subject: A resident retells a childhood story of three cave-hidden Pokemon representing rock, ice, and steel.

PacifidlogTown_House1_Text_RegiStory.text:
In the HOENN region, there are three
POKéMON that represent the power of\lrock, ice, and steel.\pEach of them is said to hide away deep
inside caves.\pThat's the story I heard when I was
just a little kid.$

replies.text: Three kinds of power, each with a cave to call home. That's a sturdy old story.
An oral account gives us leads, though not confirmation of each detail.
Old cave stories deserve respect and a little caution.
He has carried that story since childhood. It must have stayed vivid.
I like hearing what people remember being told when they were small.
Three hidden figures and three materials. A story built to survive retelling.
Ancient cave residents. I trust nobody plans to knock carelessly.
I'd compare that account with any ruins or inscriptions we find.
Stone, frost, metal. Three different ways for time to hold still.
The way he remembers it matters, even before we know what's true.
I'd ask who first told him, and whether they named the caves.

contexts.subject: A resident remembers her grandfather cryptic saying about six dots and three doors.

PacifidlogTown_House1_Text_SixDotsOpenTh.text: “Six dots open three doors.”\pGrandpa used to say that, but I don't\nknow what he meant.$

replies.text: A door that wants dots instead of a key. I would have packed incorrectly.
A repeated pattern of six dots may carry information rather than decoration.
Keep the wording in mind. It may mean something somewhere else.
A small sentence can outlast the person who explained it.
I would write that down before the numbers get muddled.
An inherited riddle, waiting for the right page of the story.
Grandpa left an interestingly unhelpful set of instructions.
I'd look for grouped marks near any unusual doors. Carefully.
An old voice can leave a question open for another generation.
She remembers the exact words even without understanding them.
I'd ask whether he said it while showing her something.

contexts.subject: The boy interprets the player yes answer as the name of their hometown.

PacifidlogTown_House4_Text_YesTown.text: Yes?\nYES TOWN?\pI've never heard of a place like that.$

replies.text: Yes Town! Convenient place for people who agree on everything.
He interpreted an answer category as a location. A reasonable confusion here.
We should try that introduction again with an actual place name.
I don't think either of us answered the question we thought we heard.
I'd hate to give directions from Yes Town to Maybe Village.
A new settlement has been founded by conversational accident.
Yes Town sounds exhausting. No quiet dissent anywhere.
The question and the available answer clearly didn't fit each other.
A place invented in the little gap between two meanings.
He is being perfectly sincere, which makes it rather sweet.
Now I want to hear what he thinks Yes Town looks like.

contexts.subject: The boy is confused by the player no answer and jokes about a seafloor birthplace.

PacifidlogTown_House4_Text_YouHaveToCome.text: No? That doesn't make any sense.\nYou have to come from somewhere.\pOh! Wait! You're not going to say you\nwere born at the bottom of the sea?$

replies.text: Born under the sea would make the first walk to school quite ambitious.
He has correctly rejected nowhere, then selected a rather unusual alternative.
Let's give the kid a straight answer before this gets stranger.
I think he is doing his best with a very unhelpful answer.
An underwater birthday party would complicate the cake considerably.
Our mysterious origin has acquired gills through a clerical misunderstanding.
From nowhere to the seafloor. An impressively rapid escalation.
We should clarify the town name rather than extend this faulty premise.
Every path begins somewhere, even one arriving over water.
I admire how hard he is trying to make the answer work.
I'd tell him about home before he invents anything deeper.

contexts.subject: The watcher cannot see Mirage Island today.

PacifidlogTown_House5_Text_CantSeeMirage.text: I can't see MIRAGE ISLAND today…$

replies.text: No island today. The horizon is keeping its special guest list private.
Today's observation is negative. It does not settle whether visibility can change.
Nothing to see from here today. We can check another time.
He sounds as if he has spent a long time looking.
A patient job, staring at water that usually stays water.
The elusive island has declined another appearance.
An absence with a very dedicated audience.
I would keep a record of when he checks and what he sees.
Some mornings the sea offers only distance.
That little disappointment sounds very familiar to him.
I'd ask what it looked like the last time he saw it.

contexts.subject: The watcher excitedly reports that Mirage Island is visible today.

PacifidlogTown_House5_Text_CanSeeMirageI.text: Oh! Oh my!\nI can see MIRAGE ISLAND today!$

replies.text: Today is an island day! I didn't know days could have that category.
A positive observation. We should note where he is looking.
If we plan to investigate, check the route while it is visible.
All that watching finally found something. Listen to his voice.
That is a good reason to put everything down and look.
The absent guest has arrived, to the delight of its faithful host.
An island has chosen to be conspicuous. How unlike it.
We should record the conditions before they change.
A hidden place has entered the ordinary daylight.
He's earned the right to be that excited about a horizon.
Show me where! I want to see what he has waited for.

contexts.subject: A resident considers weather and a genuinely appearing island as competing explanations.

PacifidlogTown_House5_Text_MirageIslandA.text: MIRAGE ISLAND…\pIt must become visible and invisible\ndepending on the weather conditions\lthat make mirages appear.\pOr is it really appearing and\ndisappearing?$

replies.text: Either the air is playing tricks or the island has very unusual manners.
Those are different hypotheses. Repeated observations could help distinguish them.
Interesting question. Best not treat either answer as settled.
I like that he leaves room for not knowing.
I'd listen to the people who spend every day watching this water.
An optical explanation competes with a much more dramatic island.
Weather is strange enough without land developing a schedule.
Comparing sightings with weather records would be a useful start.
Seeing a thing and understanding its arrival are separate mysteries.
He lets his neat explanation stay a question. Sensible.
I'd gather a few different accounts before choosing a story.

contexts.subject: The old woman finds the paired orbs at Mt Pyre soothing.

SootopolisCity_House2_Text_YesTwoOrbsSid.text: Yes, two orbs side by side…\pThe sight of them together…\nIt is somehow soothing…$

replies.text: Two little circles making a whole mountain feel a bit calmer.
The paired arrangement has an emotional significance for her.
Some sights make people feel things they can't easily explain.
I understand remembering how a place feels more than what it looks like.
A quiet place can leave you with something peaceful to carry home.
She offers a feeling rather than an explanation. Sometimes that is enough.
An appreciation of still objects in a quiet place. Understandable.
I'd be interested in how the orbs were placed there originally.
Two shapes keeping each other company at the summit.
Something about them together matters more to her than either alone.
I'd ask what else she remembers about that visit.

contexts.subject: The old woman recommends visiting Mt Pyre to see its two orbs.

SootopolisCity_House2_Text_OughtToVisitA.text: Is that so?\nPerhaps you ought to visit and see…$

replies.text: Some things don't quite fit into a description from a living room.
A visit would let us observe the setting she is describing.
Worth seeing respectfully if our route takes us there.
She sounds like she wants us to understand the place for ourselves.
I'd leave time for a quiet visit instead of rushing through.
A recommendation to let the location tell its own part of the story.
A mountaintop visit. Quiet, probably, though less convenient than this chair.
We can look without disturbing what people have placed there.
Some meanings wait where the stones stand.
I'd remember that it is a place other people visit for serious reasons.
I'd ask what a first-time visitor should be mindful of.

contexts.subject: A resident speculates that local underwater ruins may contain ancient treasure.

SootopolisCity_House4_Text_AncientTreasu.text:
Listen up, and I'll tell you something
good.\pThere's supposed to be an ancient
ruin in the sea around here.\pThere could be treasures just waiting
to be discovered down there.$

replies.text: Old ruins under the sea! Even finding the front door sounds exciting.
The ruins and the treasure are claims with different levels of certainty.
Plan the dive before getting carried away by treasure talk.
I wonder who last walked there when it was dry.
A fascinating trip still needs enough supplies to come home.
A rumor has supplied us with both a setting and a temptation.
Ancient rooms underwater. At least the dust problem is solved.
We should learn the currents and exits before exploring a ruin.
A place beneath water may hold more history than gold.
I would be curious about what people left, not only what it is worth.
I'd ask who first found the ruins and what they actually saw.

contexts.subject: A resident values an underwater walk with Pokemon even without finding treasure.

SootopolisCity_House4_Text_StrollUnderwa.text: Ancient treasures…\pIt would be nice if they existed, but\neven if they didn't, it would be so\lbeautiful to take an underwater\lstroll with my POKéMON.$

replies.text: A beautiful walk counts as finding something good, even if it doesn't fit in a bag.
The environment itself can make exploration worthwhile.
A good partner and a safe route. Plenty of reason to go.
That sounds like a quiet memory I'd keep for a long time.
An outing doesn't need a prize at the end to be a good one.
A satisfying expedition that refuses to require a treasure chest.
A walk where nobody can insist on conversation. Intriguing.
I'd still check where we can surface before choosing a path.
Light moving through water can be worth the journey alone.
She has a lovely idea of what makes time well spent.
I'd want to know what caught her eye first down there.

contexts.subject: An elder explains how an emerged volcanic crater filled with rainwater to form Sootopolis.

SootopolisCity_House7_Text_CityFromErupt.text:
An underwater volcano erupted and
forced itself up from the depths.\pIts crater emerged from the sea and
became filled with rainwater.\pThat's how SOOTOPOLIS CITY came into
being.$

replies.text: The sea got a mountain, the mountain got a bowl, and the bowl got a town!
Volcanic uplift created a basin that could collect rainwater. Remarkable setting.
Good to know what we're standing on. This town has strong walls for a reason.
It makes the quiet water look different when you imagine what came before.
People found a place to live inside the remains of something enormous.
A city occupying the peaceful aftermath of an astonishing entrance.
A volcanic crater becomes a neighborhood. People are persistent.
I'd ask how they manage water levels inside a basin like this.
Violence made the hollow; rain taught it another life.
The shape of the town tells a story much older than its buildings.
I'd love to hear what the earliest settlers found here.

contexts.subject: Dock says calculations alone are insufficient and wants an experienced sailor advice.

SlateportCity_SternsShipyard_1F_Text_Cou.text: DOCK: Shipbuilding is an art.\pA lot of things can't be figured out\njust by calculating.\pI really could use advice from a veteran\nwho knows the seas…$

replies.text: A ship should listen to someone who has actually been tossed around in one.
Calculations benefit from observations gathered under real operating conditions.
Ask the people who will trust it with their lives.
It's good that he can say what he doesn't know yet.
You learn things doing the work that no neat page quite explains.
The designer seeks a reader who has survived the sea's harsher edits.
The sea is unlikely to honor a convincing diagram.
Exactly. Design needs feedback from the people using the finished machine.
Experience remembers the wave that arrived unlike all the others.
Knowing when to ask for help makes his confidence more credible.
I'd ask which part of the ferry he most wants a sailor to inspect.

contexts.subject: Dock reports steady ferry construction after experienced sailor Briney joins the project.

SlateportCity_SternsShipyard_1F_Text_Bri.text: DOCK: Hi! MR. BRINEY's joined us to\nlend us his help.\pThanks to the veteran sailor, the\nferry is steadily coming together.$

replies.text: They found the missing part of the plan, and it wears a sailor's hat.
Practical experience is helping convert the design into a working vessel.
Good team. One knows the build, the other knows the water.
Dock sounds less alone with the problem now.
Sometimes the best help is somebody who knows what to look for.
The stalled project has acquired exactly the supporting character it needed.
The ferry progresses. The doohickeys may finally have names.
That's a useful collaboration: design knowledge and experience in service.
Two kinds of knowing have found a common task.
He gives Briney credit openly. That makes a good partnership.
I'd love to hear what changed after Briney first looked it over.

contexts.subject: The S.S. Tidal is completed and Dock is already considering further improvements.

SlateportCity_SternsShipyard_1F_Text_Fer.text:
DOCK: The ferry is finally ready!\pThe new S.S. TIDAL is truly a marvel
of technology!\pBut, I get the feeling that we can
make something even better.\pYou know, there's never an end to
technology's march.$

replies.text: The ferry is ready, and his next idea is already trying to climb aboard.
A completed design can still suggest the questions for its successor.
Finish well, celebrate it, then think about the next one.
I hope he gives himself a moment to see what he has made.
Get everyone a good meal before beginning the next enormous project.
The triumphant ending has immediately sprouted a sequel.
The boat is finished. The engineer is apparently not.
I'd love to ask what he wants to improve and what this version taught him.
A finished thing can become the beginning of another thought.
He's proud without becoming too comfortable. That's a useful balance.
I'd like to see his face when the first passengers come aboard.

contexts.subject: Briney credits meeting the player for renewed energy and joins Dock ferry project.

SlateportCity_SternsShipyard_1F_Text_Dec.text:
MR. BRINEY: Ah, {PLAYER}{KUN}!
It's been too long!\pAye, since I met you, this old sea dog's
been feeling frisky!\pSo I've decided to help DOCK make
a ferry.\pAye, after all, a ferry would be able
to carry a lot of people.\pBut, you know, that DOCK is really
something special.\pWith his knack for technology and
my experience, I'm sure that we can\lbuild one great ship, aye!$

replies.text: Briney's next adventure is helping build everybody else's ride.
He recognizes how his experience complements Dock's technical skills.
Glad he's found good work with someone who values him.
He sounds excited about having something new to be part of.
Putting old experience toward a new purpose can feel wonderful.
A veteran returns with renewed vigor and an excellent collaborator.
Retirement appears to have lost its argument with a ferry.
He is thinking about the passengers as well as the machine. I like that.
A little renewed spirit can carry work toward a distant shore.
His praise for Dock is as warm as his pride in his own experience.
I'd love to hear the stories those two tell while working.

contexts.subject: A shipyard worker gets seasick and contributes from land instead.

SlateportCity_SternsShipyard_1F_Text_Get.text: I get seasick real easily.\nSo I get to help out here instead.$

replies.text: Helping the boat from a floor that stays put. An excellent compromise.
He has found a role that uses his effort without triggering the problem.
Still useful work. No need to suffer to prove he belongs.
I'm glad there is a place for him here too.
The people on the water need plenty done by people on land.
A sensible character who has negotiated with his principal weakness.
An admirable commitment to boats at a medically respectful distance.
A working ship depends on far more than its crew.
You can help a journey without taking the same path.
He adjusted the role instead of giving up something he cares about.
I'd ask what part he most enjoys working on here.

contexts.subject: A shipyard worker describes sea conditions changing with weather, seasons, and moon.

SlateportCity_SternsShipyard_1F_Text_Sea.text:
The seasons, the weather, where
the moon sits in the sky…\pThese and other conditions make
the sea change its expression.\pThat's right!
The sea is like a living thing!$

replies.text: The sea has moods, and none of them agree to our timetable.
Several interacting conditions make a single description insufficient.
Check today's water. Yesterday's crossing isn't a guarantee.
It can look familiar and sound different the next morning.
The people who work here must learn to notice tiny changes.
An immense, unpredictable presence with no obligation to explain itself.
A living thing that is mostly water. We should get along famously.
A vessel needs to handle changing conditions, not just a calm demonstration.
The moon moves far away, and the water answers here.
He knows the sea through changes most visitors might miss.
I'd ask which change he notices before anyone else does.

contexts.subject: The motel owner says Team Aqua presence has driven away tourists.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_1F_Text_NoGue.text: Oh, sorry, sorry!\nI was too involved in watching TV!\pSince that TEAM AQUA came to town,\nthe tourists have been staying away.$

replies.text: Empty rooms are another kind of mess Team Aqua has left behind.
Perceived danger can damage a town's livelihood without a direct attack.
People don't take holidays where they feel unsafe.
A quiet motel sounds different when nobody chose the quiet.
Buying food for guests who never come must be a difficult gamble.
The villains have disrupted even the stories that aren't about them.
Empty rooms are peaceful only when the owner can afford them.
Removing the danger is the first step toward getting visitors back.
A town can feel absence long before anything is broken.
He's trying to watch television while worrying about the business.
I'd ask how long the regular visitors have been staying away.

contexts.subject: After the hideout is cleared, the motel receives a large company reservation.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_1F_Text_Heard.text:
Oh, sorry, sorry!
I was too involved in watching TV!\pI heard that someone busted
the TEAM AQUA HIDEOUT.\pThanks to that, we just booked
a reservation from a big group.\pIt was a company called… Uh…
GAME something…$

replies.text: One big booking sounds like fresh air coming into an empty building.
Improved safety is already producing a visible local benefit.
Good. The town can start getting back to ordinary business.
He sounds distracted, but relieved underneath it.
Time to check the pantry before that big group arrives.
A defeated hideout produces a remarkably practical happy ending.
The villains depart; a reservation arrives. Good exchange.
He should write the company name down before the next distraction.
Doors that stayed empty are expecting footsteps again.
The name can wait a second. The relief is the real news.
I'd like to hear how the town feels when visitors return.

contexts.subject: The motel owner remembers the arrived Game Freak group needs dinner after watching television.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_1F_Text_Bette.text:
Oh, sorry, sorry!
I was too involved in watching TV.\pOh, yes. A big group of guests arrived
a little while ago.\pThey booked in as GAME FREAK,
so I guess they must make games.\pUh-oh, I'd better get working on
their dinner!$

replies.text: The television won't make dinner, even if the program has excellent snacks.
His attention needs to return to the guests' immediate needs.
We should let him work. A big group won't feed itself.
I think he remembered the kitchen at exactly the right moment.
First count the guests, then check what can be cooked in time.
A room full of game makers faces its greatest challenge: a distracted host.
The dinner has yet to become more than a concept. Concerning.
A reminder by the television might prevent this particular scheduling problem.
Hungry people have a way of bringing wandering thoughts home.
Enthusiasm is lovely. Hospitality also needs something on the table.
I'd leave him to it before our conversation becomes another delay.

contexts.subject: The motel owner complains when the player blocks his television and moves them aside.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_1F_Text_CantS.text: Hey, down in front!\nI can't see the TV!$

replies.text: We have accidentally become the least popular show on television.
We obstructed his view. The remedy seems straightforward.
Let's move aside. No need to make a thing of it.
I would rather not become the center of attention this way.
Fair enough. I wouldn't stand between someone and their dinner either.
Our unexpected appearance has received a brisk cancellation.
My talent for blocking light has finally found an audience.
A small change of position fixes the whole problem.
We stood in the path of someone else's little escape.
He has made his seating priorities extremely clear.
I'd rather ask what he's watching from somewhere beside the screen.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor reports the lowest possible Pokemon friendship.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: This is a little hard for me to say…\pYour POKéMON simply detests you.\nDoesn't that make you uncomfortable?$

replies.text: That is hard to hear. Our partner is having an even harder time feeling it.
The assessment points to a serious trust problem. Our routine needs to change.
Take this seriously. Start treating that partner differently today.
I don't want us to look away just because the answer hurts.
A gentler routine matters more than finding a quick way to erase this.
A painful review, and one that calls for action instead of excuses.
That is a bleak result. A clever reply would not improve it.
Let's identify what has been hurting trust and stop doing it.
An open hand means little until it stops bringing hurt.
This is information about how our partner feels, not an insult to dodge.
We should watch their reactions and start earning something better.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor reports that the Pokemon remains deeply wary of its Trainer.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: It's very wary.\nIt has scary viciousness in its eyes.\lIt doesn't like you much at all.$

replies.text: That wary look isn't a challenge. It is a sign we've got work to do.
Defensive behavior is consistent with low trust. Give it safer experiences.
Don't crowd it. Show it that being with us can be safe.
I wouldn't try to demand affection from that expression.
Consistent care will mean more than one elaborate treat.
Our next chapter needs fewer demands and better reasons to trust us.
Wary eyes are entitled to keep their distance.
We should review the routine and remove avoidable stress.
A guarded creature needs reasons to lower its guard.
Calling it vicious won't tell us why it feels this way.
I'd give it space and pay attention to what makes it tense.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor says the Pokemon is unfamiliar with the Trainer and neutral.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: It's not very used to you yet.\nIt neither loves nor hates you.$

replies.text: We are still in the learning-each-other's-weird-habits part.
Neutral familiarity is a beginning, not evidence of rejection.
Give it time. Trust isn't owed on the first day.
It can be quiet between people who don't know each other yet.
A steady routine is a good way to become familiar.
We have been introduced. The relationship still needs to be written.
A perfectly respectable initial opinion: undecided.
Learn its signals instead of expecting it to know ours immediately.
Roots do not appear the instant a seed meets soil.
No need to force a closeness that hasn't had time to grow.
We can start by noticing one small thing it likes.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor sees the Pokemon beginning to trust the Trainer.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: It's getting used to you.\nIt seems to believe in you.$

replies.text: We're becoming a familiar face in the good way.
Repeated contact is beginning to produce a trusting response.
Good start. Keep giving it reasons to believe in us.
A little trust can be a very big change.
The small, ordinary things are starting to add up.
A tentative friendship has found its first convincing lines.
We have been promoted from stranger to probable ally.
Consistency is working. We should keep the routine dependable.
A cautious leaf has turned toward the light.
It is beginning to expect good things from being with us.
I'd pay attention to what it is comfortable doing beside us now.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor says the Pokemon is fond of the Trainer and wants extra affection.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: It likes you quite a lot.\nIt seems to want to be babied a little.$

replies.text: A formal request for a little extra fussing. I support the petition.
It is comfortable enough to seek attention from us.
We can spare a moment for our partner.
It is nice when someone feels safe enough to ask for closeness.
Some affection doesn't need to wait for a special occasion.
Our devoted companion has submitted a modest demand for indulgence.
A little pampering. A surprisingly reasonable ambition.
Let's notice how it asks, so we recognize the signal next time.
Being wanted can be as simple as staying a moment longer.
There's confidence in asking to be treated tenderly.
I'd put the next errand off for a small moment together.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor reports a very happy Pokemon with strong affection.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: It seems to be very happy.\nIt obviously likes you a whole lot.$

replies.text: Our partner has given us a very good review without needing any words.
A strongly positive assessment. Our day-to-day care appears to be working.
Good. That's worth more than a lot of battle praise.
I like knowing the happiness we see isn't just our imagination.
A happy partner makes the ordinary parts of the trip better too.
An excellent report from the one critic whose comfort matters most.
Contentment. Quietly impressive, and much harder to fake than a pose.
Let's keep doing what gives it that confidence and comfort.
Something warm has settled into being together.
That's the kind of praise you earn while nobody is watching.
I'd like us to remember how it looks when it feels this safe.

contexts.subject: The friendship assessor reports the highest affection and is delighted to witness it.

VerdanturfTown_FriendshipRatersHouse_Tex.text: It adores you.\nIt can't possibly love you any more.\lI even feel happy seeing it.$

replies.text: So much fondness it spilled over and made the rater happy too!
The strongest possible assessment. That reflects a well-established bond.
Our partner feels at home with us. Let's keep deserving that.
It is a little overwhelming to hear something so kind said plainly.
All those ordinary days have become something wonderful.
A love story with no need for a more dramatic witness.
Even I have run out of gloomy qualifications for that result.
The best outcome still needs everyday care. We're doing well.
Some closeness becomes so steady it warms the room around it.
The happiness on the rater's face says how clear it is to see.
I'd treasure this moment without making our partner perform for it.

contexts.subject: A researcher says their device for talking to Pokemon has had little success.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F_Text_DeviceFor.text: We're developing a device for talking\nwith POKéMON.\pBut we haven't had much success…$

replies.text: A machine for asking Pokemon questions. First question: was that really my lunch?
Communication research needs a way to distinguish meaning from coincidence.
Big goal. Keep listening to what Pokemon already tell us too.
Even if it never works, I like that someone wants to understand.
I'd be delighted to ask a partner what they actually want for dinner.
Imagine interviewing a Pokemon and discovering it has notes about us.
A device that could confirm exactly how unimpressed a Pokemon is. Dangerous.
I'd ask what response they count as evidence of progress.
A voice may be present long before we learn how to hear it.
I wonder whether the hardest part is translation or paying attention.
I'd want to hear what question made the researcher begin this project.

contexts.subject: A researcher is struggling to develop new kinds of Poke Balls.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F_Text_Developin.text: I'm developing new kinds of\nPOKé BALLS…\pBut I haven't made much headway…$

replies.text: A small round invention can contain a very large pile of failed ideas.
A lack of visible progress is common when several constraints interact.
Hard work takes time. Better to get it right.
It sounds discouraging when the result won't show what you've tried.
Some days you only learn what doesn't work yet.
The brilliant invention has reached its unglamorous middle chapter.
The prototypes are refusing to become achievements on demand.
I'd ask which part is holding them up: materials, function, or reliability.
An unfinished thing can still carry a great deal of thought.
They sound tired of explaining the distance still left to go.
I'd ask about the latest attempt, not just the finished result.

contexts.subject: The researcher celebrates working Repeat and Timer Balls with different capture uses.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F_Text_WeFinally.text:
We finally made new kinds of
POKé BALLS!\pThe REPEAT BALL makes it easier to
catch POKéMON you've caught before.\pThe TIMER BALL gets better at catching
POKéMON the longer a battle runs.\pBoth are proudly developed by
the DEVON CORPORATION.\pPlease give them a try!$

replies.text: One remembers who we've met; the other appreciates a long battle. Clever little spheres!
Two designs for different conditions. Their value depends on the encounter.
Know which one fits the situation before you throw it.
They finally get to say it works. That must feel good.
A long wait made into a tool for a different long wait.
The prototypes have graduated to named, useful inventions.
Patience has become a product. An unusually tidy development.
They solved distinct problems with distinct designs. I'd love the details.
Familiarity and passing time can each alter an encounter.
The excitement sounds earned after hearing how hard it was before.
I'd ask which successful test finally convinced the team.

contexts.subject: A researcher is struggling with a machine to show Pokemon dreams.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F_Text_DeviceToV.text: I'm trying to develop a device that\nvisually reproduces the dreams of\lPOKéMON…\pBut it's not going well.$

replies.text: I wonder whether a Pokemon dreams about us dreaming about its dreams.
Producing an image and verifying that it represents a dream are separate problems.
Interesting work. Make sure the Pokemon can rest comfortably.
Some dreams might be very quiet things to show another person.
I'd love to know whether their favorite meals turn up there too.
A machine proposing to publish a very private kind of story.
I am uncertain any of us need our dreams presented without editing.
I'd ask how they can test accuracy without asking the dreamer directly.
The sleeping mind keeps a country no one else can walk into.
A lovely idea, if the dreamer is comfortable with the looking.
I'd want to hear what first made them curious about those dreams.

contexts.subject: The PokeNav inventor is proud and grateful to have made a useful invention.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F_Text_IMadePoke.text: I made the POKéNAV!\pAs an engineer, I feel blessed to have\nmade something so great!$

replies.text: He made a thing that helps people get un-lost. That's worth smiling about.
He can connect a finished invention to a clear benefit for its users.
Useful work. He has earned some pride in it.
He sounds happy just knowing it exists because of his work.
Making something people carry on their journey must feel special.
A creator allowing himself an entirely deserved moment of satisfaction.
A successful project. I hear those exist occasionally.
I understand that feeling: an idea finally becoming something someone can use.
Something he imagined now travels farther than this room.
He credits his good fortune as well as his skill. I like that.
I'd ask which part he remembers finally getting right.

contexts.subject: The fossil scientist asks for patience while the regeneration machine works.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F_Text_FossilReg.text:
The FOSSIL REGENERATOR, which I made,
is incredible.\pBut it has one drawback--it takes
a long time to work.\pSo, uh… How about you go for a stroll
and look around for a while?$

replies.text: Bringing back an ancient Pokemon probably deserves more time than boiling an Egg.
A substantial process can be impressive without being fast.
Let it work. We can use the time for something else.
I would rather wait than ask him to rush something this delicate.
Some important things simply aren't improved by standing over them.
Prehistory has waited this long. We can manage a short interval.
The ancient past is experiencing a minor delay.
Speed isn't the only design goal. Reliability matters much more here.
A very old beginning is taking its time to return.
He is proud enough of the machine to admit its drawback.
I'd ask when we should check back, then give him room to work.

contexts.subject: The move relearner ends the visit with a reminder that teaching costs a Heart Scale.

FallarborTown_MoveRelearnersHouse_Text_C.text: If your POKéMON need to learn a move,\ncome back with a HEART SCALE.$

replies.text: A Heart Scale is his lesson fee. I should stop thinking of them as shiny pocket clutter.
He has specified the resource required for another lesson.
Keep a scale handy if a partner needs an old move back.
It's good to know there is a way to revisit something forgotten.
We'll know what to save when we find another one.
A specialist whose tuition policy fits in one small sentence.
A tiny object purchases a second chance at remembering. Reasonable.
We should decide what move we need before spending the scale.
A lost skill may be closer than it feels.
I like that the door stays open for another visit.
I'd keep track of which partners might benefit from coming back.

contexts.subject: Lanette introduces herself as the Pokemon Storage System developer and invites a home visit.

FallarborTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Lane.text:
Oh, hello.
You are?\pOkay, your name's {PLAYER}{KUN}.
I can see that you're a TRAINER.\pSo that means you use the POKéMON
Storage System I developed.\pHow I arrived at that conclusion is
a simple deductive process.\pYou spoke to me because you wanted
to access something on this PC.\pOh, I'm sorry. I'm LANETTE.\pHonestly, I'm glad to meet you--it's
great you're using the Storage System.\pIf you could, please visit me at home.
My house is on ROUTE 114.$

replies.text: We met the person behind the PC, and she nearly forgot the person part.
Her deduction was plausible. Her introduction arrived a little later.
Useful system, friendly person. Good to put a face to the work.
I understand getting caught up explaining something before saying your name.
She's glad people use her work. That makes the invitation feel warm.
An introduction that takes the scenic route through a proof.
Social preliminaries have survived a brief encounter with deductive reasoning.
I'd love to ask how she made the system manageable for so many Trainers.
A familiar convenience has turned out to have a face and a home.
She noticed the awkwardness and softened it herself. I like her.
A visit to Route 114 might give us more time to hear her story.

contexts.subject: A Trainer enthusiastically explains PokeNav calls and rematch notices.

FortreeCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_DoYouK.text:
Oh, wow, you have a POKéNAV!
And it's just like mine!\pDo you know about POKéNAV's
MATCH CALL system?\pAccess it, and you can chat with
registered TRAINERS anytime.\pIt also shows you which TRAINERS
want a rematch with you.\pIt's really nifty! Those DEVON guys
sure know what they're doing!$

replies.text: A map, a conversation, and a way to learn who wants to battle us again. Busy little thing!
Communication and rematch information are useful features in one portable tool.
Good way to check in before walking all the way back.
It's nice to talk to someone when the road has taken you far away.
A quick call can save a long trip made on a guess.
Our earlier opponents now have a convenient way to request an encore.
A pocket full of people. Fortunately, they can be put away.
Clear rematch notices solve a very practical travel problem.
A familiar voice can find you between unfamiliar places.
He likes the convenience, but he sounds happiest about staying connected.
I'd ask who was the first person he called with it.

contexts.subject: A visitor recommends the Safari Zone for Pokedex research.

FortreeCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_GoToSa.text: Listen, kid, are you working\non a POKéDEX?\pHmm… Go to the SAFARI ZONE.\nThat's my suggestion.$

replies.text: A place full of Pokemon we might not have met. That is a strong recommendation.
A designated habitat can be useful for broadening our recorded observations.
Worth checking the rules before heading inside.
I'd enjoy looking around without rushing to the next town.
We should find out what to bring before making the trip.
A remarkably concise travel guide: go where the interesting creatures are.
A destination with an admirably honest name.
I'd ask which species made that visit worthwhile for him.
A different stretch of land may answer different questions.
His advice is specific enough to be useful.
I'd love to hear what surprised him most when he visited.

contexts.subject: A Trainer enjoys mixing records while admitting not understanding the technical process.

FortreeCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Record.text:
Have you done anything at
the RECORD CORNER?\pIt's pretty neat. It mixes and matches
the records of TRAINERS.\pI don't know quite how it works,
but it's cool. It's exciting, even!$

replies.text: He doesn't know how it works, but he knows he had fun. Respectable review.
Enjoying a system and understanding its implementation are separate things.
Fair enough. You can use something without taking it apart.
It's nice hearing someone sound excited without pretending to know everything.
You don't need the whole recipe to know you enjoyed the dish.
An unusually candid enthusiast. The mystery has not impaired the applause.
A user who admits uncertainty. We should treasure this one.
I'd ask what changed afterward. That tells us about the useful part.
An exchange can leave a trace even when its workings remain hidden.
He knows what he liked and where his explanation stops.
I'd ask which part he would show a first-time visitor.

contexts.subject: A woman tells the player to work harder to acquire fans.

SootopolisCity_House3_Text_LonesomeTryWo.text: Oh, dear…\nThat's a little lonesome.\pTry working a little harder to get\na fan following.$

replies.text: We can have a good journey without appointing an official cheering section.
A fan count is not a reliable measure of skill or companionship.
We have people who matter to us. That is enough.
I don't think I would be comfortable with a crowd following us anyway.
A few good friends beat a room full of hungry expectations.
The publicity department has mistaken obscurity for loneliness.
A small audience sounds like a feature, personally.
Training well is a better goal than trying to control who admires us.
A quiet life can be full of people who care.
Being liked and being watched are different kinds of attention.
I'd rather know who she enjoys spending time with than count fans.

contexts.subject: A woman assumes the player must be strong because they have fans.

SootopolisCity_House3_Text_YouMustBePret.text: Oh, then you must be pretty strong.$

replies.text: People cheering is lovely. They still can't do the hard part for us.
Popularity can follow strength, though it isn't proof of it.
We'll let the battles answer that question.
Being noticed does make every mistake feel a little louder.
It's kind that people are interested in how we're doing.
The audience has been accepted as evidence of the performance. Bold.
A flattering inference with a few missing steps.
Skill is something we can practice. Popularity is less predictable.
Other people's attention does not change the weight of the next step.
She means it as praise. We can receive it without making it a rule.
I'd ask what makes her choose a Trainer to cheer for.

contexts.subject: A girl describes the passionate international fan crowd at Lilycove Trainer Fan Club.

SootopolisCity_House3_Text_TrainerFanClu.text: Dedicated fans come over from even\noutside of HOENN.\pIt was really wild when I went to the\nTRAINER FAN CLUB in LILYCOVE.$

replies.text: People cross the sea to argue about their favorite Trainer? That's committed arguing.
A common interest can bring together people from a considerable distance.
Sounds lively. I'd stay near a door if it got crowded.
I might enjoy hearing about it more than standing in the middle.
That many visitors probably keep the nearby cafes busy.
A room where every spectator apparently brings a leading character.
An international gathering of extremely certain opinions. Daunting.
I'd be curious how they settle disagreements over different battle styles.
Admiration can travel a very long way to find company.
She enjoyed the energy. That is part of what makes a gathering work.
I'd ask who she met there, as well as who they cheered for.

contexts.subject: A visitor wonders whether the claim that Pokemon originated in space is true.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_DidPoke.text: Some people claim that POKéMON came\nfrom space. Could it be true?$

replies.text: If Pokemon came from space, that is the longest trip to meet a friend I've heard of.
A compelling question needs evidence beyond the fact that someone proposed it.
Interesting theory. I'd ask what makes people think so.
Looking up makes the things we don't know feel very large.
Wherever they began, I am glad we get to know them here.
A grand opening chapter in search of reliable witnesses.
An extraterrestrial origin would explain some things. It would raise rather more.
We'd need observations that distinguish it from other explanations.
The sky is a tempting place to put an unanswered beginning.
I like that she asks instead of presenting a rumor as certainty.
I'd ask the researchers what evidence they find most interesting.

contexts.subject: An elder marvels that a huge metal rocket can reach space.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Rockets.text: A giant chunk of metal bursts through\nthe skies and flies into space…\pIt boggles my mind!$

replies.text: A giant metal thing gets to leave the sky. My little legs have no such ambition.
The scale is striking, but controlled thrust can overcome its weight.
Takes a lot of careful work to make that look possible.
I don't think understanding it completely would make it less wonderful.
All that effort lifts something no person could carry.
An improbable sight becomes ordinary through a vast amount of extraordinary work.
An enormous metal object refusing to remain sensibly on the ground.
Every system has to work together. That's what makes the whole thing amazing.
Something made from the earth reaches beyond the clouds.
His amazement feels fresh, however many times he has watched.
I'd ask what he remembers about seeing his first launch.

contexts.subject: The rocket enthusiast resents Team Magma threatening the spaceflight dream.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_MagmaWa.text: A giant chunk of metal bursts through\nthe skies and flies into space…\pBut TEAM MAGMA wants to spoil\nthat dream of mine!\pI'm not having any of that!$

replies.text: Team Magma has picked a very large dream to kick over.
Stealing fuel threatens the work and aspirations of the people here.
He's right to be angry. They have no claim to this place.
Something that made him happy has become something to worry about.
There are real people behind the supplies they're trying to steal.
A thief sees fuel where an entire room sees a future.
A remarkably efficient way to become unwelcome on an island.
That fuel belongs in a controlled launch, not in their hands.
A dream does not become disposable because someone else wants its materials.
He isn't merely protecting an attraction. It means something to him.
I'd like to hear him talk about a launch again when this is safe.

contexts.subject: A visitor realizes using Team Aqua against Magma could embolden another criminal team.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_AquaSho.text: TEAM AQUA should take care of\nTEAM MAGMA!\pBut if they did that, TEAM AQUA will\nbecome bold and brazen, won't they?$

replies.text: Replacing one enormous problem with another enormous problem seems like poor tidying.
She has recognized the flaw in relying on a competing threat.
Neither team needs more power over this town.
I am glad she stopped to think through what would follow.
You don't fix a spoiled meal by handing the kitchen to another troublemaker.
A proposed rescue acquires a suspiciously similar second act.
Two disasters do not reliably cancel each other out.
The useful goal is securing the center, not helping either group win.
One shadow is not sunlight simply because it covers another.
She wants help badly enough to consider it, then sees the cost.
I'd ask what support the center has from people it can actually trust.

contexts.subject: The launch counter staff reports that a rocket launch is imminent.

replies.text: A launch soon! I would like to stand where the ground is least surprised by it.
The preparations are nearing their final stage. A good time to observe carefully.
Let's stay clear of the staff and follow their instructions.
Knowing it is almost time makes this room feel different.
I'd hate to be the person who picked this moment to wander off.
A short announcement with a truly extravagant event attached.
The sky is about to receive a very noisy visitor.
Final checks must be intense. I'll leave the team room to work.
A thousand careful tasks are approaching one bright moment.
That is an announcement worth putting other plans aside for.
I'd ask where visitors can watch without getting in the way.

contexts.subject: The launch counter staff confirms a safe launch and records its numbered success.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Success.text: The rocket launched safely!\nThat's successful launch no. {STR_VAR_1}!$

replies.text: Another safe launch! The number sounds small beside all the work inside it.
A recorded success is the result of many systems working within their requirements.
Safely done. That's the word that matters.
I wonder how the room felt in the first quiet moment afterward.
Someone ought to make that crew a proper celebration meal.
An entire ascent compressed into one number and a very good piece of news.
A safe departure into space. I find that reassuringly improbable.
Every successful launch is still worth checking and learning from.
A light has gone beyond sight, and a roomful of people can breathe again.
That plain report must carry enormous relief for the people who built it.
I'd ask how the team marks a successful launch afterward.

contexts.subject: During the weather crisis, a resident explains that townspeople are sheltering inside.

SootopolisCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Eve.text: Everyone in town has taken refuge\nand won't come out of their homes.\pEven I would rather not venture\noutside.$

replies.text: People are staying inside for good reason. Let's not give them another worry.
Sheltering reduces exposure while conditions remain dangerous.
Stay indoors if you can. We shouldn't urge anyone out into this.
A whole town listening to the weather from behind closed doors.
We should check that people have what they need without sending them outside.
The grand catastrophe is also a hundred interrupted ordinary days.
Today, remaining indoors is less a preference than a strategy.
A safe building and reliable information matter most right now.
A familiar street can become somewhere frightening to step into.
There is no shame in choosing shelter while the danger lasts.
I'd ask whether anyone nearby still needs help getting somewhere safe.

contexts.subject: During the crisis, a woman is distressed that Pokemon could cause such destruction.

SootopolisCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Are.text: Aren't POKéMON our friends?\pWhy are they going wild this way?$

replies.text: She knows Pokemon as friends. This must feel impossible to fit beside that.
Pokemon friendship doesn't mean every creature is harmless in every situation.
Being afraid right now doesn't erase the good she knows.
I don't think she is asking for a clever explanation. She sounds hurt.
Her own friends are still her friends, even with this happening outside.
An enormous conflict has shaken a very personal certainty.
Something trusted has become frightening. That is a hard thing to hold.
We need to respond to the actual danger without blaming every Pokemon for it.
A kind memory can remain true beside a terrible present.
She is trying to understand the crisis through the relationships she knows.
I'd stay with the question for a moment instead of dismissing it.

contexts.subject: Outside the crisis, a woman affirms lasting friendship with Pokemon because they are good company.

SootopolisCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Alw.text: Whenever, wherever, and whatever\nhappens, I will always be friends with\lPOKéMON.\pBecause it's fun to be with POKéMON!$

replies.text: Being together is a perfectly good reason to keep being together.
She values the relationship itself, beyond any practical advantage.
Good company is worth staying loyal to.
I like how simple she lets that feeling be.
You don't need a grand reason to enjoy someone beside you.
A lifelong declaration grounded in the radical pleasure of liking your friends.
Enjoyable company. A rare quality, and a sensible basis for loyalty.
A relationship can be valuable without solving a particular problem.
Some promises begin with the quiet fact of being glad someone is here.
She sounds comfortable in that affection. It suits her.
I'd ask which ordinary thing she most enjoys doing with them.

contexts.subject: The guide volunteers to help us become Champion and explains Roxanne Rock weaknesses.

RustboroCity_Gym_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Yo, how's it going?\pListen, my friend!
Would you like to become the CHAMPION?\pI'm no TRAINER, not me, but I can
sure give you winning advice.\pThat's settled, then! We'll aim for the
POKéMON CHAMPIONSHIP together!\pIt's your job as a TRAINER to collect
GYM BADGES, am I right?\pBut GYM LEADERS aren't pushovers!\pAnd that's where I come in!
I'm here to provide expert advice!\pROXANNE, the GYM LEADER, is a user
of ROCK-type POKéMON.\pThe ROCK type is very durable, but
it can't stand WATER-type and\lGRASS-type moves.\pCome see me afterwards, if you beat
the GYM LEADER.\pWell, go for it!$

replies.text: We have acquired a very enthusiastic unpaid coach. He even came with useful advice.
Water and Grass attacks are worth considering. Check our actual moves before choosing a lead.
Useful information. You still get to decide how to use it.
He believes in us very loudly for someone we just met.
A stranger has decided to cheer us on. That is a nice welcome.
He cast himself as our trusted adviser before we could hold auditions.
I was not prepared to become a group project this morning.
He identified the specialty and two weaknesses. A practical briefing under all the shouting.
A long road begins with somebody insisting you can walk it.
He gives advice freely. That is a good first impression.
I wonder how many first-time challengers he has helped through that door.

contexts.subject: The guide credits his cheering and tells us to check our first badge on the Trainer Card.

RustboroCity_Gym_Text_GymGuidePostVictor.text:
Whoa! What a breathtaking victory!
My cheering must've worked!\pGreat!
Check your TRAINER CARD.\pThe STONE BADGE you got should be
properly recorded on it.\pIn other words…\pYou've climbed the first step on
the stairs to the CHAMPIONSHIP!\pThat's got to feel awesome!$

replies.text: His cheering won the battle! Our Pokemon would like a brief word about that.
Checking the recorded badge is sensible. His causal explanation is more enthusiastic than rigorous.
You and the team earned it. He can have a little credit for the encouragement.
Seeing it on the card might make the whole thing feel real.
Let us check the badge, then thank the team properly.
The supporting cast has submitted a modest claim to authorship of the finale.
I am happy he enjoyed his contribution from the very safe part of the room.
Confirm the result is recorded. Celebrate after the paperwork. Then celebrate properly.
A little mark on a card can hold the weight of a long first step.
You should look at it for a moment. You only get a first badge once.
I want to remember your face when you see it recorded there.

contexts.subject: The guide warns about Fighting attacks and says winning battles brightens the dark Gym.

DewfordTown_Gym_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Hey, how's it going, CHAMPION-
bound {PLAYER}?\pDEWFORD's GYM LEADER BRAWLY commands
FIGHTING-type POKéMON.\pGoing against him with NORMAL-type
POKéMON is asking for trouble.\pFIGHTING POKéMON will lay a serious
smack down on NORMAL POKéMON,\lso be careful!\pWhat's worse, the GYM is as dark as
the ocean floor.\pBut it will get brighter after defeating
the TRAINERS in your way.\pHey, okay, go for it!$

replies.text: Defeat trainers to turn on the lights. I have been paying an electricity bill like a fool.
Keep Normal Pokemon away from unfavorable matchups. The changing visibility is a separate puzzle.
Watch the team and the path. It is easy to lose track of either in here.
I like the dimness. I like knowing where the exits are even more.
Let us make sure everyone is comfortable before starting through the dark.
The lighting designer has delegated the entire production to our battle record.
A Gym where victory lets you see the person you just fought. Thoughtful.
Performance-controlled lighting. I would prefer a normal switch for emergencies.
Each challenge leaves a little more of the room visible.
I appreciate the advice. I would also appreciate a railing.
We should keep track of where we came from before the room changes around us.

contexts.subject: The guide jokes that both the Gym and player future are bright after victory.

DewfordTown_Gym_Text_GymGuidePostVictory.text: Whoah! It's turned too bright in here!\pYour future is bright, too!$

replies.text: The future is bright. So is the room. My eyes would like both to adjust gradually.
He is pleased for us. The room is also considerably easier to navigate now.
Good win. Now we can find the exit without guessing.
I forgot how visible we would all be at the end.
A badge and a clear way home. Both good results.
Our victory has received the full lighting budget.
The future looks promising. The present is making me squint.
The brightness change is decisive. At last I can see what the floor has been doing.
The room kept a little sunrise for the end of the battle.
He has been waiting for an excuse to say that. Let him enjoy it.
I would like to remember this room with everyone finally visible.

contexts.subject: The guide warns Water Pokemon about Electric attacks and describes Wattson switch doors.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Hey, how's it going, CHAMPION-
bound {PLAYER}?\pWATTSON, the LEADER of MAUVILLE
GYM, uses ELECTRIC-type POKéMON.\pIf you challenge him with WATER-type
POKéMON, he'll zap them! Bzzt!\pAnd, he's put in switch-controlled
doors all over his GYM! Eccentric!\pHey, go for it!$

replies.text: Water and electricity are a bad introduction. So are visitors and unmarked switches.
An Electric specialty and a switching puzzle. We should prepare for both independently.
Choose the lead carefully. Then look before stepping on anything.
The explanation helps. I would rather know what can happen before it happens.
We can take our time. The team does not need to rush through a place this unfamiliar.
The eccentric host has supplied danger, doors, and a man to shout the instructions.
A cheerful warning that the building may zap us. Very welcoming.
Switch-controlled doors! I have concerns, but I am listening.
The bright room has a pattern beneath its noise. We can find it.
I am keeping both feet well away from anything that looks decorative and electrified.
His impression of the electricity was vivid enough. I would rather not hear the original.

contexts.subject: The guide celebrates our electric victory and opened doors.

MauvilleCity_Gym_Text_GymGuidePostVictor.text: Whoa, you're electrifying!\nYou've powered the door open!$

replies.text: We powered the door open! Please do not make us the building's permanent generator.
The path is clear and the badge is earned. A satisfying pair of results.
We are through. Give the team their due before the next stop.
I am glad the room feels less threatening now.
A good battle, and no need to solve another door on the way out.
The building has accepted our performance and released its doors for the curtain call.
Electrifying. I am choosing to treat that as figurative while standing very still.
A successful test and an accessible exit. Both important acceptance criteria.
The path opens after the noise. A good moment to breathe.
We can enjoy being impressive once we are clear of the wiring.
He sounds almost as pleased as Wattson. This Gym knows how to welcome a winner.

contexts.subject: The guide praises Flannery passion and recommends Water attacks with overheated metaphors.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Hey, how's it going, CHAMPION-
bound {PLAYER}?\pLAVARIDGE's GYM LEADER FLANNERY
uses FIRE-type POKéMON.\pHer passion for POKéMON burns stronger
and hotter than a volcano.\pDon't get too close to her--you'll burn!
Hose her down with water and then\lgo for it!$

replies.text: I assume he means Water moves. I would like that confirmed before anyone buys a hose.
Fire matchups are useful information. The rest of his temperature forecast seems figurative.
We can use the advice without underestimating her.
I hope she is easier to talk to than that introduction makes her sound.
A Water teammate may help. So will keeping everyone rested in this heat.
The adviser has mistaken a tactical briefing for a municipal fire warning.
I will admire her passion from the recommended nonflammable distance.
A type recommendation, several alarming metaphors, and no explanation of the floor vents.
Fire is more than heat. We should see how she actually tends hers.
I would rather meet her than keep hearing how dramatically she burns.
She must have made quite an impression on him. I wonder what she thinks of his version.

contexts.subject: The guide calls the victorious battle scorching hot.

LavaridgeTown_Gym_1F_Text_GymGuidePostVi.text: Yow! That was a scorching-hot battle!$

replies.text: Scorching! I am going to recover with an extremely ordinary temperature of water.
A demanding battle. The team has earned a cooler place to recover.
Good fight. Let us get everyone out of the heat for a while.
I can feel my shoulders relaxing now that it is over.
Water, shade, and some rest before the next journey.
An enthusiastic review from a critic whose vocabulary has been thoroughly preheated.
I am happy with the win and ready to stop marinating in the atmosphere.
Successful, but we should still let everything cool before the next test.
The flame has settled. We can set down the effort for a moment.
A victory looks better on a team that has had a chance to recover.
He felt the energy of it, too. I am glad somebody was cheering.

contexts.subject: The guide introduces Winona Flying team and rotating doors.

FortreeCity_Gym_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Yo, how's it going, CHAMPION-
bound {PLAYER}?\pFORTREE GYM LEADER WINONA is
a master of FLYING-type POKéMON.\pShe's waiting at the back of this GYM,
behind the rotating doors.\pShe's waiting for new challengers
who are trying to take wing!\pOkay, go for it!$

replies.text: She waits behind rotating doors. A surprisingly complicated way to discourage drafty visitors.
We know her specialty. The doors are a spatial problem, not a test of our Pokemon.
Watch where each door sends us. We can work through it without rushing.
I would rather take a little longer than pretend I know where I am going.
Let us keep track of the way back in case the team needs a break.
The leader awaits behind a moving set. A very committed entrance design.
Trying to take wing. I am still trying to take the correct hallway.
Rotating barriers! I want to see how the pivot clearance works. After we find the route.
The door moves. The destination stays where it is.
I am prepared for the Flying team. The building has been less forthcoming.
We should look at the door positions before changing them. It will make the path easier to remember.

contexts.subject: The guide celebrates the win as achieving liftoff.

replies.text: Liftoff! I hope this does not mean the stairs are now optional.
He has found a concise way to celebrate a difficult result.
We did it. Let us give the team a rest before going anywhere.
I still feel very much on the floor, but a little lighter.
A good flight deserves a safe landing and something to eat.
A triumphant launch, followed by the less celebrated task of finding the exit.
We have achieved liftoff. My feet have chosen to remain professionally skeptical.
A successful ascent through both the team and the door mechanism.
Sometimes a victory is simply feeling able to go a little further.
We can enjoy the height without immediately looking for a higher one.
That is a fine moment to remember before the next part of the road.

contexts.subject: The guide warns about Psychic matchups and the twins coordinated double attacks.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_GymGuideAdvice.text:
Yo, how's it going, CHAMPION-bound
{PLAYER}?\pThe GYM LEADERS here use
PSYCHIC-type POKéMON.\pIf you go up against them with
FIGHTING- or POISON-type POKéMON,\lthey'll inflict horrible damage!\pPlus, they'll come at you with
outstanding combination attacks.\pIf you want to win, you'll need to show
them how tight you are with your\lPOKéMON. Go for it!$

replies.text: Two leaders with a shared plan. We should bring something more organized than two separate ideas.
Avoid the unfavorable matchups and consider how our two Pokemon support each other.
Pick a pair that works together. Individual strength is only part of this fight.
It helps to know who is watching which part when everything happens at once.
The team should feel like partners, not two strangers we put in the same room.
A double act requires more than two performers arriving at the same address.
Outstanding combinations. I hope ours include a plan and the ability to remember it.
Check the interactions between our moves before discovering them during the battle.
Two lives can make a third kind of strength when they move together.
Coordination makes a pair look effortless. It is usually the part someone practiced hardest.
I will watch for the moments one Pokemon makes room for the other.

contexts.subject: The guide calls us an astounding trainer after beating the twins.

MossdeepCity_Gym_Text_GymGuidePostVictor.text: Wow, you're astounding!\nYou're one great TRAINER!$

replies.text: Astounding! We should tell the team before the compliment develops a queue.
That was good coordination. Everyone involved deserves the credit.
You led them well. Make sure they know you noticed their work.
I am glad he said it. You should hear something kind after working that hard.
A good trainer and a good team. We should celebrate both.
