An invitation to witness the next draft rather than only the polished legend.
A social plan that lets someone else fill the silence. Promising.
He might keep a few earlier versions to hear what changes.
A feeling given time can find a clearer voice.
He sounds excited to have someone notice the next improvement.
I'd enjoy hearing what he changed, then hearing what stayed his.

contexts.subject: Rose claims she can smell our PokeNav and demands registration.

Route118_Text_RoseRegister.text: Sniff… That odor--it's a POKéNAV!\nWe must register each other!$

replies.text: Our contact information apparently has an aroma.
That is an unusual identification method. I'd want to test it.
Sharp nose. Direct invitation. Hard to miss.
I wasn't expecting our things to introduce us by smell.
I wonder what scent she associates with it.
A detective has sniffed out a remarkably sociable conclusion.
I sincerely hope our other belongings don't have equally clear signatures.
The source might be the casing or something stored beside it.
An unseen detail has led her toward a new acquaintance.
That is the most unusual accessory compliment I've heard today.
She notices a whole layer of a scene I might never think to check.

contexts.subject: Catherine notices we have a PokeNav and suggests keeping in touch.

Route119_Text_CatherineRegister.text: Do you have a POKéNAV?\nIt's a must-have tool for any TRAINER.\pOh, you do have one!\nLet's register each other, then!$

replies.text: The equipment check has turned into a friendly introduction.
A shared tool makes future coordination straightforward.
Useful gear. Better when there's someone worth calling.
It's nice when practical talk becomes a friendly invitation.
Keeping in touch can make the route feel less isolated.
A practical recommendation followed by an excellent use for it.
Our preparedness has unexpectedly produced a social obligation.
A tool earns its place through what we can actually do with it.
A journey can gather familiar voices as well as familiar places.
She noticed the useful detail and made it personal.
We could compare notes the next time one of us travels this way.

contexts.subject: Jackson asks for a rematch without being mocked for what he does not know.

Route119_Text_JacksonRegister.text: I hope you'll give me a rematch without\nmocking my lack of knowledge.$

replies.text: A rematch doesn't need a side order of humiliation.
A gap in knowledge is a reason to learn, not to ridicule someone.
No mocking. We'll give him a fair match.
I know how hard it can be to ask that plainly.
He should be able to learn without bracing for a joke.
A rival deserves a contest, not an audience for his embarrassment.
Ignorance is temporary more often than cruelty is useful.
We can share the missing information before testing it again.
An honest question should find room to breathe.
Confidence grows better without someone picking at every loose thread.
I'd rather remember what he learned than keep a record of his awkward moment.

contexts.subject: A Team Aqua grunt claims that the organization exists for everyone benefit.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Aqua.text: We, TEAM AQUA, exist for the good\nof all!$

replies.text: Everyone is a very large group to speak for without asking.
A stated intention does not establish a beneficial result.
Then they should stop making trouble for the people here.
I don't think saying it confidently answers the doubts.
People generally notice when help keeps making their day worse.
A sweeping claim delivered without any troublesome supporting evidence.
How convenient that everyone apparently appointed him their spokesman.
I'd judge the work by what it actually does for this town.
A kind word can be placed over an unkind purpose.
He assumes we are included in his definition of good.
I'd ask which local people he has actually helped.

contexts.subject: A Team Aqua grunt complains that their ordered gathering lacks its leader.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_OurB.text: We were told to assemble here,\nso we did, but…\pOur BOSS, the linchpin, isn't here.$

replies.text: They assembled all the parts except the person with the instructions.
A group relying on one coordinator becomes inefficient when that person is absent.
Not our job to organize them. Let them wait.
They don't seem to know what to do without being told.
A meeting without the person who called it is a familiar nuisance.
The assembled villains are missing their principal source of direction.
A leaderless collection of matching outfits. Very educational.
You'd think they would agree on a time and a backup plan.
An instruction can bring people together without giving them purpose.
The uniforms create a stronger impression of organization than the meeting does.
I'd rather hear the museum guide than help them find their boss.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt wonders whether stealing museum exhibits would make them rich.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Woul.text: If I ripped off the stuff here,\nwould it make me rich?$

replies.text: They came to a museum and only noticed the imaginary price tags.
Public research value is not equivalent to resale value.
Leave the exhibits where people can learn from them.
It is a sad way to look at something meant to be shared.
There are people working hard to keep this place open.
An exhibition reviewed by someone with a catastrophically narrow interest.
He appears to have mistaken public education for a shopping opportunity.
Those instruments belong to the work they support. Keep them here.
Taking a thing can rob others of more than the thing itself.
He didn't even pretend to be interested in why it matters.
I'd rather point that plan out to a member of staff.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt plans to use museum knowledge for wrongdoing.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_CanL.text: What I learn here, I can put to use on\nnefarious deeds…$

replies.text: The information is free, and somehow they still found a way to misuse it.
Education supplies capability. It does not determine how someone applies it.
Learning something doesn't give you the right to hurt people with it.
That makes his interest in the displays feel unpleasant.
A useful skill can still end up in very inconsiderate hands.
The museum has acquired an admirer with an unfortunate proposed application.
At least he has spared us the effort of doubting his intentions.
Knowing how something works should make you more careful with it.
A clear window can be used to choose where to throw a stone.
He says that as though we are going to appreciate the ambition.
I'd remember his face if he starts asking about restricted equipment.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt blames fellow members Rustboro failures for the current assignment.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Rust.text: If our goons didn't bungle things\nin RUSTBORO, we wouldn't be here!$

replies.text: Their team spirit seems to consist mostly of pointing at another team member.
Blame has arrived more quickly than an analysis of what went wrong.
Their bad planning isn't our concern. Their actions are.
I doubt the people he's blaming are enjoying the story either.
A group goes sour quickly when nobody owns their part.
An organization rich in villains and poor in favorable references.
A charming workplace. All the menace, none of the mutual respect.
Even their complaints tell us they haven't coordinated very well.
People can stand together and still leave each other alone.
He wants us to know he is better than the absent members.
I'd listen to what he reveals rather than joining in the blame.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt admits being delayed because they could not afford the museum fee.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Didn.text: I didn't have ¥50, so it took a long\ntime getting by the receptionist.$

replies.text: The museum's smallest obstacle has defeated a very official-looking criminal budget.
The entrance fee appears to have been omitted from their preparations.
The attendant shouldn't have to argue just to collect the fee.
I feel for the person who had to handle that conversation.
If you're going somewhere, bring enough for the entrance. Basic planning.
A grand operation, stalled at the ticket counter.
The revolution has forgotten its spending money.
A tiny predictable cost should not become a staff member's problem.
A large purpose can trip over a very small threshold.
He seems more annoyed by the delay than embarrassed by his preparation.
I'd like to hear the attendant's version of that exchange.

contexts.subject: After giving Thief, the familiar Aqua grunt hurriedly wishes never to meet the player again.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Hope.text: That TM, it suits you more than it\ndoes me.\pHope I never see you again!\nWahahaha!$

replies.text: A gift and a request to disappear from his life. Very mixed manners.
He is eager to end the encounter now that the exchange is complete.
Good. Let him leave without making more trouble.
I don't think that laugh was quite as relaxed as he intended.
At least he has found a way to finish this without another fight.
A farewell attempting to sound triumphant while backing rapidly toward the door.
Our company has inspired both generosity and a desperate exit.
His nerves are clearer than his attempt at confidence.
He leaves a small gift where he would rather leave no memory.
He wants to keep a little dignity on the way out. Fine.
That will be a very different story when he tells his friends.

contexts.subject: With no bag space for Thief, the frightened grunt insists the player accept before he can leave.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_YouH.text: Awww, come on!\nYou have to take this and let me go!$

replies.text: His escape plan depends on our packing skills. That's unfortunate for both of us.
The transfer failed for lack of space. Nothing has changed hands yet.
He can wait while we sort the bag. No need for panic.
He looks trapped by the favor he is trying to give us.
A gift needs somewhere to go. We can't solve that by insisting.
A daring getaway defeated by an overfull bag.
An unusually literal case of baggage delaying a farewell.
We need to clear space before this particular exchange can finish.
He cannot put down his fear until we can put away the item.
He's trying very hard to hurry a problem that needs a quiet moment.
I'd give him room while we decide what can leave the bag.

contexts.subject: A museum patron wants to apply knowledge of the sea to Pokemon battles.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Lear.text: I want to learn about the sea and\nuse that knowledge for battling.$

replies.text: Homework that comes with fish and eventually helps win a battle!
Understanding a habitat may reveal useful context for the Pokemon found there.
Good. Learn what you're working with before testing it in a fight.
I like that they're looking for more than a list of moves.
Knowing where a partner lives can help you understand what it needs.
A challenger has found a training ground with exceptionally informative walls.
A museum as battle preparation. Quietly more alarming than shouting.
Useful ideas often turn up outside the place where you plan to use them.
A creature carries traces of its home into every encounter.
They are taking their interest far enough to study it.
I'd ask which display changed the way they think about battling.

contexts.subject: A sea enthusiast admires Captain Stern as their foremost role model.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Ster.text: I get all giddy and gooey when\nI see the sea!\pFor me, CAPT. STERN is the number\none role model!$

replies.text: They love the sea so much the sentence went a little wobbly.
Stern gives that enthusiasm a person and a body of work to follow.
Good choice to admire someone who does the hard work too.
It's sweet to hear somebody so openly delighted by their interest.
The sea makes them happy, and Stern gives them something to aim for.
An admirer in danger of becoming entirely liquid with enthusiasm.
A passionate endorsement delivered with minimal structural stability.
I'd ask which of Stern's projects first caught their attention.
The sea has given them wonder, and someone to look up to.
No embarrassment about caring this much. I find that refreshing.
I'd ask whether they have had a chance to meet him yet.

contexts.subject: A patron imagines unknown Pokemon in the immense unexplored sea.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Must.text: The sea is vast without end, and\ninfinitely deep…\pThere must be many POKéMON that\nwe don't know about.$

replies.text: There could be a Pokemon down there that has never seen a person either.
The ocean's scale makes incomplete knowledge entirely unsurprising.
Good reason to explore carefully. Unknown doesn't mean harmless.
It is strange to think how much life can go unseen beneath us.
Whole kinds of ordinary days might be happening where we can't look.
An enormous unwritten cast beneath a surface we mistake for the whole scene.
The depths retain excellent privacy. I can understand the appeal.
Better equipment could let researchers investigate without guessing so much.
Dark water need not be empty water.
There is room for wonder without pretending we already know what waits.
I'd like to hear what the explorers saw that they couldn't identify.

contexts.subject: A patron wants a sea Pokemon because it seems pleasantly cool to hug.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Want.text: I want a sea POKéMON.\pI think it would feel cool and nice\nto hug.$

replies.text: A cool hug sounds lovely. We should check whether the Pokemon agrees.
Sea Pokemon vary substantially in texture, temperature, and comfort with handling.
Meet the Pokemon first. Some are less cuddly than the idea.
I understand wanting that sort of gentle company.
A lovely plan, provided the chosen partner doesn't have sharp edges.
An affectionate casting decision that still needs the candidate's approval.
A cooling embrace. Species selection seems crucial.
I'd learn how to handle that species before trying a hug.
A creature of the sea may still enjoy being close on its own terms.
The fondness is sweet. A little knowledge would make it sweeter.
I'd ask which sea Pokemon they've actually spent time with.

contexts.subject: The museum attendant cannot admit the player because they cannot afford the fee.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_NotE.text: Oh? I'm sorry, but you don't seem to\nhave enough money.$

replies.text: We have arrived with curiosity and slightly insufficient coins.
The admission requirement is clear. We can return once it is met.
No argument needed. We'll come back prepared.
I always feel as if everyone can hear the coins I don't have.
Let's check the purse before making another trip to the counter.
Our cultural outing has encountered a modest financial obstacle.
The budget has delivered a concise critique of our plans.
We can set aside the entrance fee before buying other things.
A closed visit today need not be a closed door forever.
The attendant kept it polite. Let's do the same.
I'd find out the opening hours so the return trip is easy.

contexts.subject: The attendant mistakes the player for part of the earlier group and waives the fee.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_Catc.text: Oh? You're with that group that\nwent in earlier?\pYou're the only one who's late.\nYou'd better go catch up to them!$

replies.text: We have been admitted by a very unfortunate assumption about our company.
She inferred an affiliation that we have not actually claimed.
We're here to find Stern. Let's stick to that.
I don't especially want people thinking we came with them.
A helpful gesture, attached to the wrong explanation.
An accidental disguise supplied entirely by the ticket counter.
We have acquired an affiliation without the inconvenience of joining.
The assumption explains her decision, even though the premise is wrong.
A mistaken resemblance can open an unexpected door.
She sees a late visitor, not what we actually came to do.
I'd be careful not to turn her mistake into more trouble for her.

contexts.subject: A Trainer recommends developing varied Pokemon rather than relying on one strong partner.

SlateportCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Rais.text:
Want a tip for battling?\pI'd say it's raising different kinds
of POKéMON in a balanced manner.\pIt's no good to make just one
POKéMON strong.\pIf it has a type disadvantage,
it might not stand a chance.$

replies.text: One star Pokemon shouldn't have to carry the whole sky.
A varied team can cover weaknesses that raw strength alone cannot remove.
Have a second plan and a partner ready to carry it out.
It's kinder when one Pokemon doesn't have to handle everything.
Spread the work around. Everybody needs a chance to learn.
An ensemble gives the adventure more than one solution to a difficult scene.
A single excellent answer eventually meets the wrong question.
Different capabilities give us options when a familiar approach fails.
Several kinds of strength can share one road.
A team needs room for each member to contribute.
I'd ask what encounter first taught that Trainer this lesson.

contexts.subject: A Trainer especially enjoys a friend traded Pokemon arriving with a held item.

SlateportCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trad.text: I trade POKéMON with my friends.\pIf a traded POKéMON is holding an\nitem, it makes me twice as happy!$

replies.text: A new Pokemon arrives carrying a little extra hello from a friend.
The held item adds practical value and evidence of an extra thoughtful choice.
Nice touch. Someone remembered to send it with something useful.
Small surprises can make a happy meeting even warmer.
It's like sending someone home with a little packed lunch.
The introduction comes with a thoughtful footnote from its previous companion.
A gift carrying a gift. Efficiently pleasant.
I'd check what the item does before changing it. They may have chosen carefully.
A small object can carry another person's attention with it.
They enjoyed the thought behind it as much as the thing itself.
I'd ask about the friend who made that exchange special.

contexts.subject: A resident assumes any visiting Trainer must be going to the Battle Tent.

SlateportCity_House_Text_MustBeGoingToBa.text: You're a TRAINER, aren't you?\pSince you came to SLATEPORT CITY,\nyou must be going to the BATTLE TENT.$

replies.text: We apparently look like people with very specific plans.
It is a plausible destination, though being a Trainer does not establish our itinerary.
Could be. Plenty else worth visiting in this town too.
I might just have wanted to look around quietly.
A port city surely has room for an errand and a good lunch as well.
The local attraction has become the only approved explanation for our presence.
An itinerary supplied by a stranger. Saves thinking, I suppose.
We can ask what the Tent offers before deciding whether to visit.
A person may arrive with a purpose that isn't visible.
They are proud of the attraction, even if the guess is narrow.
I'd ask what they enjoy watching there themselves.

contexts.subject: A Trainer connects a hasty Pokemon nature to its unusually high Speed.

SlateportCity_House_Text_NatureToDoWithS.text: My POKéMON has a HASTY nature.\pIt has higher SPEED compared to\nmy other POKéMON.\pMaybe their nature has something to\ndo with the stat gains of POKéMON.$

replies.text: Its personality may be doing a little of the running too.
That observation is a useful lead. Controlled comparisons would strengthen it.
Worth understanding your partner's strengths before planning training.
It's interesting when a habit and an ability seem to line up.
They noticed a difference by paying attention to their own team.
An everyday observation has opened the door to a serious question.
Hasty in temperament, swift in practice. An unusually consistent individual.
We should compare similar Pokemon before assuming nature is the only cause.
The way a creature meets the day may leave a trace in its strength.
I like that they're curious instead of treating every difference as a flaw.
I'd ask what else they have noticed when raising them side by side.

contexts.subject: After awarding a Red Scarf, the chairman explains that it emphasizes Pokemon coolness.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Explai.text: Let a POKéMON hold that RED SCARF.\pEveryone will recognize the coolness\nof that POKéMON!$

replies.text: The scarf says cool while also being a perfectly sensible neck blanket.
An accessory can emphasize the contest quality it was designed to support.
It suits a purpose. Make sure the partner is comfortable wearing it.
A small detail can make a confident pose easier to notice.
A bright little finishing touch after all that raising.
Our distinguished contestant has acquired an appropriately dramatic accent.
A formal certificate of coolness, issued in wearable form.
Now we know which contest category to pair it with.
A warm color can frame a very composed presence.
Red draws attention. Let the Pokemon's own confidence do the rest.
I'd like to see how the Pokemon carries itself wearing that.

contexts.subject: After awarding a Blue Scarf, the chairman explains that it enhances beauty.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Explai.text: Let a POKéMON hold that BLUE SCARF.\pIts beauty will be accentuated much\nmore than now!$

replies.text: A little blue frame around an already lovely Pokemon.
The scarf is intended to accentuate beauty rather than change the underlying work.
Good reward. It should complement the partner, not get in its way.
Blue can make the little changes in the light easier to notice.
They've put care into raising it. This gives that care a nice finish.
The contestant receives a finishing flourish in the color of a clear day.
Beauty has been provided with a pleasantly restrained accessory.
A small item with a clear specialized use. Easy to remember.
A soft color can draw the eye without demanding it.
Let it sit comfortably. A lovely accessory shouldn't compete with its wearer.
I'd enjoy seeing the difference in how it looks when it moves.

contexts.subject: After awarding a Pink Scarf, the chairman explains that it emphasizes cuteness.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Explai.text: Let a POKéMON hold that PINK SCARF.\pIt will draw out the cuteness of\nthe POKéMON some more!$

replies.text: The Pokemon was cute already, and now the scarf is enthusiastically agreeing.
It supports a specific contest quality. The intended use is clear.
Cute is fine. Just keep it comfortable and out of the way.
A little pink detail can make a familiar face look unexpectedly sweet.
A cheerful reward for the work that brought us here.
Our contender has received official assistance in being adorable.
A strategic deployment of pink. The opposition has been warned.
We can keep it with the items meant for that contest category.
A small bright thing can invite a gentler sort of attention.
Pink works best when it feels like part of the Pokemon's own charm.
I'd watch for the little expression it makes when everyone notices.

contexts.subject: After awarding a Green Scarf, the chairman explains that it enhances smartness.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Explai.text: Let a POKéMON hold that GREEN SCARF.\pThat will enhance the\nsmartness of POKéMON!$

replies.text: A smart scarf! I hope it doesn't start judging my decisions.
The accessory supports smartness in contests. It is not a substitute for preparation.
Useful for that category. Keep the plan as sharp as the outfit.
It's a quiet color for drawing attention to something clever.
The right finishing touch can show the work off nicely.
An intellectual flourish, delivered in fabric rather than footnotes.
At last, a scarf with a promising academic record.
A clear visual cue helps us remember which quality it supports.
Green suits the thought of something carefully growing.
A smart look should feel deliberate. This gives us a place to start.
I'd ask what clever performance the chairman remembers best.

contexts.subject: After awarding a Yellow Scarf, the chairman explains that it emphasizes toughness.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Explai.text: Let a POKéMON hold that YELLOW SCARF.\pIt will bolster your POKéMON's\ntoughness so much more!$

replies.text: Toughness in a scarf! I have clearly underestimated laundry.
Its contest function is specific. Yellow marks it as the toughness accessory.
Good. Let the Pokemon do the hard part; the scarf can help present it.
A bright detail can make a steady stance look even surer.
There's a cheerful reward for a very sturdy partner.
The rugged contender gains a surprisingly sunny finishing touch.
Toughness, with a color that refuses to brood. An interesting choice.
We should match it to the appropriate contest rather than its color alone.
Strength does not always need to dress in dark colors.
Bright yellow can make confidence look open instead of threatening.
I'd like to see the Pokemon show that toughness in its own way.

contexts.subject: The chairman finds contest condition moderate and recommends additional Pokeblocks.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_GiveMo.text:
Hmmm… It's not bad, but it's not
good, either…\pYou, the TRAINER, must put more
effort into raising this POKéMON!\pFor instance, may I suggest that
you give it more {POKEBLOCK}S?$

replies.text: He has advice, though he wraps it in a rather large frown.
He is assessing contest condition, which is narrower than overall welfare.
We can improve condition without treating the partner like a failed project.
That is a rather stern way to say there is room to grow.
We should check which flavors suit it before making more treats.
The critic has requested revisions and suggested an edible method.
A lukewarm review accompanied by practical snack advice. Could be worse.
Let's identify the quality we're trying to improve before choosing Pokeblocks.
A measure can point to work ahead without defining the whole creature.
He could offer the useful suggestion without making it sound like a scolding.
I'd ask what change he would look for at our next visit.

contexts.subject: The Pokemon qualifies for a scarf reward, but the full bag prevents receiving it.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_NoSpac.text: Oh, my…\pYour POKéMON is growing quite well,\nso you deserve a reward.\pUnfortunately, you have no space for\nthis in your BAG.$

replies.text: Our Pokemon passed the assessment. Our packing failed its own little exam.
The condition qualifies; storage capacity is the only obstacle identified.
Make some space. No need to redo the training.
I'd rather not have our partner think the delay is its fault.
A good result still needs somewhere to put the reward.
A promising award ceremony interrupted by a bag's unreasonable completeness.
Merit has encountered luggage. Luggage appears to be winning.
Let's organize the bag before returning for that specialized item.
The praise has arrived even if the object must wait.
We can enjoy the compliment while fixing the practical problem.
I'd thank him for recognizing the work, then sort our things.

contexts.subject: After all scarf rewards are awarded, the chairman says he has nothing further to give.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Nothin.text: I'm sorry, but I've nothing else to\ngive you! None at all!\pAfter all, you're blessed with the gift\nof raising POKéMON without resorting\lto any items!$

replies.text: We have exhausted the scarf supply. An unexpectedly fashionable achievement.
His available rewards are exhausted. The work he praised remains accomplished.
We've had plenty from him. A thank-you is enough now.
It's nice to visit without needing the visit to end in a gift.
We can still show him how the team is doing.
The critic has run out of accessories before running out of admiration.
A finite stock of fabric has met a persistent visitor.
We should keep track of what each scarf helps with. The set is useful.
A completed collection can leave room for an ordinary conversation.
That's quite a range of looks to work with now.
I'd ask which part of our Pokemon's growth he enjoyed seeing most.

contexts.subject: The chairman hopes to see Pokemon raised by a Trainer who has entered a contest.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_LikeTo.text: The POKéMON of a TRAINER who has\nentered a POKéMON CONTEST…\lThat, I would like to see.$

replies.text: He wants to meet a contestant almost as much as he wants to talk about one.
He is particularly interested in how contest participation affects training.
We can show him when we have something relevant to share.
His curiosity sounds a little more personal than a list of results.
People who raise Pokemon enjoy comparing the little things they learn.
The chairman is waiting for a story with a qualified leading Pokemon.
An enthusiast hoping for a visitor who shares his particular obsession.
I'd ask which changes he expects to notice in a contest-trained partner.
Care takes different shapes around different shared pursuits.
He wants to see the Pokemon behind the performance. That's good.
I'd listen to the questions he asks when he finally meets one.

contexts.subject: The chairman boasts about his position and explains the club informal Pokemon showcases.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_MeetCh.text:
Er-hem! I am the CHAIRMAN of the
POKéMON FAN CLUB!\pBeing the CHAIRMAN, I am naturally
the most important!\pNo one can best me when it comes
to raising POKéMON. No one!\pWell, let me tell you about
POKéMON CONTESTS.\pThey're events where one can show off
POKéMON for the world to see!\pHowever, they're held in far-off towns,
so I cannot participate often enough.\pThat is why we gather here to show
off our POKéMON, and have others\lshow us theirs.$

replies.text: He is very important, and fortunately still has room to admire everyone else's Pokemon.
The club provides a local exchange when distant contest venues are inconvenient.
A place to meet and compare training is useful. The boasting is optional.
That introduction had quite a lot of chairman in it.
He can be proud of his team and still enjoy what other people bring.
A grand introduction to the modest pleasure of showing friends your Pokemon.
The chairmanship appears to come with excellent self-esteem.
They have found a practical local substitute for traveling to every contest.
A shared room can hold many kinds of fondness.
He makes himself sound grand, but the gathering itself sounds welcoming.
I'd ask to meet his Pokemon after hearing such an introduction.

contexts.subject: A club member warns that repeated fainting damages Pokemon trust.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Pokemo.text:
If you keep letting a POKéMON faint
in battle, it'll come to resent it.\pSoon, it will become less trusting
of the TRAINER.\pIn other words, it certainly won't
like you very much.$

replies.text: Our partners remember the hard parts, even after the battle is over.
Repeated adverse experiences can weaken trust. Prevention matters more than repair.
Pull a struggling partner back before making it take more hits.
I wouldn't want one to expect that every outing ends badly.
Getting them healed doesn't erase the need to change the routine.
A battle record leaves things out that the participant still remembers.
Repeated collapse is a poor foundation for any working relationship.
We should adjust our plan before the same failure happens again.
A creature can learn to fear the hand that keeps sending it forward.
They need to see us respond when something is hurting them.
I'd watch for fatigue before a number tells us it's already too much.

contexts.subject: A member noticed their Pokemon seeming happy when given Protein.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_MonEnj.text: Do POKéMON enjoy having items used\non them?\pMine acted really happy when I gave\nit some PROTEIN.$

replies.text: A pleased Pokemon is very persuasive feedback, even without a review card.
A positive reaction is worth observing, though it may not reveal the exact cause.
Good that they're paying attention to how their partner responds.
It's nice when you can tell something you offered was welcome.
I love the small happy reactions that make you want to remember a favorite.
The recipient has supplied a favorable review without writing a word.
A supplement with an unexpectedly enthusiastic audience.

She doesn't have to belong to our fan club to see something good in us.
I'd ask what she admires about each Trainer rather than demand a winner.

contexts.subject: An elder sees strength but judges that the player has unrealized potential.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: Yes, I see strength in your eyes.\pBut!\pYou still haven't realized your\npotential.$

replies.text: Potential is a very large room with surprisingly few directions on the walls.
The judgment would be more useful with a specific area for improvement.
There's always more to learn. Give us something concrete to work on.
Encouragement can feel rather heavy when it sounds like disappointment.
I'd rather know the next useful step than the size of an imagined future.
A reviewer praises the draft while declining to identify the missing chapter.
An unfinished destiny. Apparently those are diagnosed by looking at eyes.
I'd ask which decisions suggest room to improve and how to practice them.
An unopened bud still needs ordinary rain, not merely prediction.
She means we can grow. I would keep that part and ask for details.
I'd ask what she thinks we haven't tried yet.

contexts.subject: An elder fan gives the player brief, direct praise.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: You…\pImpressive!$

replies.text: Two words, and somehow they arrived wearing a whole medal.
A concise positive assessment. The approval is unmistakable.
Thanks. Sometimes that's all that needs saying.
I appreciate praise that leaves a little quiet around it.
A short compliment can feel more generous than a long speech.
A complete favorable review with no unnecessary preface.
Excellent editorial restraint. The sentiment survives intact.
A clear response is helpful. We don't have to decode it.
A small sentence can hold a warm weight.
She let the compliment stand on its own. Elegant.
I'd smile and make sure she knows it was heard.

contexts.subject: The player sole elder fan claims exclusive insight into their hidden worth.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: Your true worth, it is fine if only\nI recognized it.\pThe others I doubt will understand\nthe hidden power that beats within.$

replies.text: I'm glad she sees something good. I don't think it needs to be a secret club of one.
Her support is welcome; exclusivity is not evidence of greater accuracy.
We can appreciate her without deciding nobody else understands us.
It feels strange when a compliment tries to put a wall around you.
Kindness doesn't need to tell us all the other people are wrong.
A flattering review has reserved all interpretation rights for its author.
Our true worth has apparently appointed a sole distributor.
I'd ask what specific strength she noticed rather than accept a mysterious verdict.
Being seen by one person need not make the rest of the world blind.
The affection can stay. The claim to understand us best needs room to breathe.
I'd welcome the conversation without making it our only source of support.

contexts.subject: An elder questions the player true strength before admitting she cannot define it herself.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text:
It is true that you are tremendously
powerful.\pBut!
I can tell…\pThat strength cannot be considered
true strength yet!\pTrue strength is…!
… …\pActually, I have no idea, either.$

replies.text: She climbed onto a very serious sentence and discovered the ladder was missing.
A distinction without a definition is difficult to evaluate meaningfully.
If she figures out what she means, we can talk about it.
At least she told us when she ran out of an answer.
I like the honesty more than the speech she almost gave.
A grand philosophical reveal has encountered a blank final page.
A devastating critique, narrowly defeated by its own missing content.
We can ask useful questions about strength without pretending to have a complete theory.
A word can sound deep before anyone looks inside it.
She let the confident pose fall away. That's better than bluffing.
I'd ask for an example and see whether we can work it out together.

contexts.subject: A fan enthusiastically names the player as the Trainer they want to succeed.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: Yo, {PLAYER}!\nYou're the one we want to win!$

replies.text: A cheer addressed straight to us. No guessing who they're talking about now.
They are expressing support, not predicting a guaranteed result.
Appreciated. We'll put in the work.
Being wanted here feels different from being judged here.
It's nice to hear good wishes without a comparison attached.
The audience has selected its favorite ending for our next appearance.
A plainly stated preference. How mercifully easy to understand.
We can carry the encouragement into preparation rather than rush because of it.
A warm voice has joined the road ahead of us.
They sound happy simply to have someone to cheer for.
I'd make a point of saying thanks before we leave.

contexts.subject: The player sole male fan urges them to prove the rest of the club wrong.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: The others, they don't know that\nyou're the best of the best!\pIsn't that right, {PLAYER}?\nShow them you've got guts!$

replies.text: I'd rather make our partner proud than win an argument we didn't start.
His support is encouraging, but the room's disagreement is not our obligation to resolve.
We'll fight our own battles. No need to add his argument to them.
It feels heavy when believing in you becomes another thing to prove.
A good wish is easier to carry than somebody else's grudge.
Our next battle has been volunteered as evidence in a private dispute.
An unsolicited feud. I was hoping for a quieter membership benefit.
We can focus on controllable choices instead of everyone else's conclusions.
The loudest challenge in the room may not be one we need to answer.
I'd thank him for caring and quietly decline the pressure.
I'd ask what he enjoys about our battles when there is no argument to settle.

contexts.subject: A lone supporter complains that nobody listens to his praise of another Trainer.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: Darn it… I've been telling people\nthat {STR_VAR_1} is the best now…\pBut no one wants to listen…$

replies.text: Maybe everyone could take turns before this room runs out of hearing.
Repeating a conclusion is different from sharing the observations behind it.
He can keep his favorite. He can't make the whole room agree.
Not being heard can sting, even when the argument is small.
A conversation works better when everybody gets a little space.
A passionate review has found itself without a willing readership.
A shortage of listeners in a room overflowing with speakers. Predictable.
I'd ask him to describe one battle instead of repeat the ranking.
A voice can be lonely even in company.
He may want someone to enjoy the story more than someone to surrender.
I'd listen once, provided he is willing to listen in return.

contexts.subject: A fan says another Trainer is the extraordinary competitor everyone is discussing.

LilycoveCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_.text: I hate to say this, but the TRAINER\neverybody's talking about is\l{STR_VAR_1}, no question about it!\pThat TRAINER's power…\nIt's out of the ordinary.$

replies.text: Extraordinary strength sounds useful to learn from, even when it isn't ours.
A reputation is a lead for inquiry, not a substitute for watching decisions.
Strong opponents give us something to prepare for.
I would like to hear the actual battle instead of only the impressive summary.
Admiring someone's skill can give you ideas without making your own work smaller.
A formidable character has arrived in the story through enthusiastic hearsay.
A notably strong Trainer. The adjective budget has clearly been approved.
I'd ask which tactic made the difference and whether it could be countered.
Some names cast a long ripple before the person arrives.
He needn't feel reluctant to praise somebody else while we're here.
I'd ask who first told him and whether they watched the battle themselves.

contexts.subject: A local has heard reports of Pokemon theft and stolen meteorites.

LilycoveCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Heard.text: I've been hearing about some rotten\nscoundrels who steal POKéMON and rip\loff METEORITES.$

replies.text: That's a nasty pair of things to hear about while you're trying to enjoy town.
The reports involve distinct thefts, possibly linked. Details would help.
Keep partners close and report anything specific.
Rumors like that can make an ordinary outing feel less safe.
People shouldn't have to wonder if their partner is safe in a busy town.
The trouble has traveled here in the form of an unpleasant story.
A very specialized collection of crimes. None of them charming.
I'd separate what he actually saw from what someone told him.
A stolen companion leaves a different kind of emptiness from a stolen stone.
The unease is real even if the details are still secondhand.
I'd ask where he heard it so useful information can reach the right people.

contexts.subject: After the hideout events, a local has not seen the thieves recently.

LilycoveCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Haven.text: Those rotten scoundrels who steal\nPOKéMON and rip off METEORITES…\pI haven't seen them around recently.$

replies.text: It's good when the news is that the trouble hasn't come back.
A period without sightings is encouraging, though not proof of permanent absence.
Good. People deserve a quieter time here.
I imagine it feels better to walk around without looking for them.
Ordinary business can settle back into the space the worry took up.
The unwelcome cast has stopped appearing in the local daily story.
A pleasantly uneventful report. One of my favorite kinds.
A calmer town is a good result. We can still stay observant.
Sometimes relief arrives as another unremarkable afternoon.
He noticed their absence. That tells you how much their presence mattered.
I'd ask what has started feeling normal again around town.

contexts.subject: A boy wonders about worldwide Pokemon diversity and wants to trade across the seas.

LilycoveCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_HowMa.text: I wonder how many kinds of POKéMON\nthere are in the world.\pIt'd be great to cross seas and\ntrade POKéMON with people far away.$

replies.text: Somebody far away might think our most ordinary Pokemon is an amazing visitor.
Geographic differences give both travel and trading genuine research value.
Plenty out there to meet. Start by learning the ones beside you.
I like imagining someone elsewhere asking the very same question.
A trade can come with stories about a place we've never eaten breakfast in.
An enormous cast, and a young reader eager for the next introduction.
The world remains inconveniently larger than our list. Interesting, though.
I'd compare records with visiting Trainers before trying to count the whole world.
A distant shore can hold a familiar friendship in an unfamiliar shape.
He wants to meet people as well as collect new entries. Lovely.
I'd ask which place he would choose for his first crossing.

contexts.subject: The curator asks the player to secure artists permission to exhibit lively modern Pokemon paintings.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Plea.text:
I beg your pardon. I didn't intend
to monopolize the conversation.\pNow, as you are young, and yet
obviously well traveled…\pYou must encounter lively POKéMON
and works of art depicting them.\pIf you were to come across such
a painting, may we ask you to obtain\lthe artist's permission to exhibit\lit here?$

replies.text: A new job for our eyes: notice lovely paintings and ask before borrowing them.
He explicitly asks for the artist's permission. That distinction matters.
We can look while traveling. No promises about what we'll find.
I like the idea of helping a painting find people who will enjoy it.
A shared wall can give someone's careful work a whole new audience.
A curatorial quest with the vital requirement that the author actually agrees.
An adventure involving art and permission. Mercifully more civilized than theft.
We should find out how the museum wants artists to submit work.
A lively creature can leave another kind of life on a wall.
He values new work enough to make room for it beside the established collection.
I'd ask what makes a painting feel alive to him.

contexts.subject: With no paintings contributed, the curator hopes to fill the hall with modern Pokemon art.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Wish.text: I wish to fill this exhibit hall with\nmodern and vibrant paintings of\lPOKéMON.$

replies.text: Empty walls are apparently a very large collection of possibilities.
He has a clear direction for the collection, even before it has works.
A good space. Now it needs people willing to put work into it.
I can almost see the room he is imagining.
A room feels different when someone has plans for welcoming things into it.
The gallery exists first in its curator's stubbornly vivid imagination.
A blank room with standards. I can respect that.
He should make the submission process clear to potential artists.
An empty frame can wait without being finished.
Modern work needs somebody willing to believe it belongs in a museum.
I'd ask whose paintings he has been looking at recently.

contexts.subject: The curator thanks the player for a new painting depicting their Pokemon.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Than.text: Thanks to you, we've added a new\npainting to our collection!\pI've heard it depicts your POKéMON.\nTruly magnificent!\pThank you so very, very much!$

replies.text: Our partner has become somebody's reason to stop and look at a wall.
A particular Pokemon's image is now part of a public collection.
Good to see our partner recognized in a different way.
A little piece of our journey can stay here after we leave.
People will enjoy meeting it through the painting, even when we're far away.
Our traveling companion has acquired a permanent supporting role in a gallery.
A portrait that won't need feeding while we are away. Convenient.
The artist's work and our partner's presence are doing something useful together.
A moment has found a place where strangers can return to it.
I'd want the Pokemon to see the attention its portrait receives.
I'd watch which detail makes visitors lean a little closer.

contexts.subject: With no decoration space, the curator keeps the Glass Ornament reward for another visit.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Keep.text: I will keep this for you until we\nmeet again.$

replies.text: He'll keep the thank-you safe while we find a place to put it.
The reward remains uncollected. The completed collection is unaffected.
No rush. We can return when there's room.
I'm glad he didn't make the delay feel like a problem.
A thoughtful gift can wait for a proper place.
The award ceremony has arranged a perfectly gracious postponement.
A fragile object spared the company of our present clutter. Wise.
We should organize our decoration storage before the next visit.
A kindness can be held for us without being taken away.
He kept the gratitude warm while sorting out the practical detail.
I'd thank him for holding it and make a note to return.

contexts.subject: After the completed collection reward, the curator welcomes the player to enjoy the museum.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Hono.text: Ah, so good to see you, {PLAYER}!\pIt's an honor to have you visit us\non your busy journeys.\pPlease, relax and do enjoy your\nvisit with us.$

replies.text: A visit where we can simply look around. No painting errands attached.
The invitation now centers on enjoying the collection rather than expanding it.
Good. We've earned a quiet look at the work.
I like being welcome without needing to accomplish something first.
Let's take the time to enjoy what everyone helped bring together.
The contributor is invited to become a visitor again. A lovely courtesy.
An official request to relax. I intend to honor it.
We can see how the finished collection works as a whole now.
A familiar room has kept a place for an unhurried return.
He's made us feel like guests rather than useful hands.
I'd spend a little longer with the painting we rushed past before.

contexts.subject: A returning visitor admires the new portraits and wishes her Pokemon could be painted as beautifully.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_NewP.text: I've been away awhile, so the new\npaintings up here surprised me.\pI wish someone would paint my POKéMON\nthis pretty.$

replies.text: She came back to familiar walls and found a new wish hanging on them.
A changed collection gives returning visitors a reason to look again.
Good art makes people think about the partners they know.
I wonder which little expression she would want the painter to catch.
Her own Pokemon is probably already lovely to her. She wants others to see it.
A gallery visit has produced a prospective commission. Excellent work by the paintings.
The portraits have inspired envy of a fairly harmless variety.
I'd ask what detail made the Pokemon in the paintings feel so vivid.
A painted stranger can remind us of someone waiting at home.
She wants her fondness translated into something other people can see.
I'd ask her to describe the Pokemon she'd put in the portrait.

contexts.subject: An older visitor is pleasantly interested in the topical modern Pokemon paintings.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_NewP.text: Well… So this is where they show\nthe topical POKéMON paintings.\pI see, these new paintings are indeed\nrather amusing.$

replies.text: He gave the new paintings a proper look before deciding what to think.
New subject matter can engage an audience familiar with older work.
Good to see him open to something different.
The little surprise in his voice is nice.
It's good when trying something unfamiliar turns out pleasantly.
A traditional visitor has encountered a new style and survived with enjoyment intact.
An unfamiliar painting has escaped immediate condemnation. Progress.
I'd ask what feels different from the work he usually enjoys.
A familiar eye can still find a fresh doorway.
He doesn't have to abandon old favorites to enjoy these.
I'd ask which painting held him there longest.

contexts.subject: A visitor is delighted to learn that the displayed paintings depict the player Pokemon.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Thes.text: Wow, is that right?\nThese paintings are of your POKéMON.\pIsn't that just the ultimate joy for\na TRAINER?$

replies.text: The gallery has accidentally been hosting a very polite family album.
The subject's identity gives the work an additional connection for this visitor.
Proud of the team. They deserve the attention.
It feels strange to stand beside something that makes a familiar face so grand.
I'd be happy knowing people enjoy a partner we've raised with care.
The painted protagonist's traveling household has arrived to inspect the reviews.
An impressive family resemblance, preserved in pigment.
It is satisfying to see everyday work become something people can appreciate.
Something dear to us has found a welcome in another person's eyes.
It's a lovely kind of recognition when affection and skill meet.
I'd tell him one small thing about the Pokemon the portrait doesn't show.

contexts.subject: Walda mother is worn down by choosing what meals to make every day.

RustboroCity_Flat1_2F_Text_ComingUpWithM.text:
Oh, it's so hard every day…\pWhat's hard?
You need to ask?\pIt's trying to figure out what to
make for meals every day.\pIt really isn't easy coming up with
meals every day.$

replies.text: Cooking happens once. Deciding what to cook somehow happens for the rest of your life.
A repeated planning task can be exhausting even when each individual choice is small.
The family could help make the choices, not just wait to be served.
It sounds like she wants somebody to notice the thinking behind the meal.
I'd make a short list of meals everyone likes, then let them take turns choosing.
The daily menu is a serial work whose readers expect an endless supply of endings.
An eternal question with hungry critics. A grim occupation.
A simple rotating plan could remove some decisions without repeating every day.
The work begins long before anyone sees something on a plate.
She is carrying the invisible part as well as the shopping and cooking.
I'd ask what the rest of the household could take off her hands.

contexts.subject: The player declines to suggest a funny phrase, and Walda father remains open to future ideas.

RustboroCity_Flat1_2F_Text_OhIsThatRight.text: Oh, is that right?\pWell, if you come up with a good\nsuggestion, I'm all ears.$

replies.text: He'll keep a little space ready for a joke we haven't thought of yet.
He accepts that we don't currently have a useful suggestion.
No harm in admitting we don't have an answer.
Thinking of something funny gets harder when someone waits for it.
We can bring an idea back if one arrives over lunch.
The household comedy department has kindly extended its submission window.
A joke may arrive once it has stopped being mandatory.
A few ordinary observations of what makes Walda smile might help him more.
A little laughter can be invited without being caught.
He lets us leave the question open instead of forcing an answer.
I'd remember what she reacts to if we spend more time in the room.

contexts.subject: After the phrase entry is canceled, Walda father returns to his previous saying.

RustboroCity_Flat1_2F_Text_OhYouDontKnow.text: Oh, so you don't know any good words.\nI guess I'll try to amuse her with\lthe saying I used before.\pAnyways, if you have a good suggestion,\ndon't hesitate in telling me, okay?$

replies.text: The old joke has been called back for another performance. Brave little joke.
He retains a familiar approach when no new suggestion is supplied.
He can keep trying, but he shouldn't turn smiling into a test.
Walda doesn't have to laugh every time to enjoy him being nearby.
Sometimes children enjoy the familiar thing more than the clever new thing.
The previous material has survived another round of proposed revisions.
An established joke has received an alarming renewal.
He could watch for other things she enjoys rather than repeat one phrase indefinitely.
A quiet child may have a rich day behind a still face.
I would give both father and daughter a little room to be unpolished.
I'd ask when she seems most relaxed, not only when she laughs.

contexts.subject: The player suggested phrase fails to make Walda laugh.

RustboroCity_Flat1_2F_Text_ShesNotSmilin.text: {STR_VAR_1}.\n{STR_VAR_1}.\pHmmm… She's not smiling at all.\nMaybe WALDA is one serious child…$

replies.text: Our joke has encountered an audience with exceptionally firm standards.
One unsuccessful stimulus tells us little about a child's overall temperament.
Didn't land. No need to put that on Walda.
I think I would blush more than the joke deserved.
A laugh isn't something you can insist on serving at a particular time.
The youngest critic in Rustboro has declined to issue a favorable review.
My material has found its natural audience: silence.
We can try something different, or simply let her be comfortable.
A serious face may be listening more closely than we know.
I wouldn't label her serious just because one suggestion missed.
I'd smile, let the moment go, and notice what interests her next.

contexts.subject: After the player cancels a first phrase, Walda father own attempt fails to make her smile.

RustboroCity_Flat1_2F_Text_ShesNotSmilin.text: {STR_VAR_1}.\n{STR_VAR_1}.\pHmmm… She's not smiling at all.\nMaybe WALDA is one serious child…$

replies.text: Dad supplied the joke himself. Walda supplied an extremely honest pause.
He tried his own idea and observed no smile. That is not a verdict on either of them.
He tried. Now let the kid have a quiet moment.
Sometimes trying so hard makes everyone a little nervous.
He might get a better laugh when he forgets he is trying to get one.
The author has performed his own material before an unpersuaded household critic.
A brave joke, laid gently to rest by a child.
Watching what she already enjoys could guide his next attempt.
Affection does not always return in the shape we request.
He wants to connect with her. The connection can be quieter than laughter.
I'd ask whether she likes faces, sounds, or a favorite little game.

contexts.subject: Walda laughs at the player phrase, and her researcher father unlocks Friends box wallpapers as thanks.

RustboroCity_Flat1_2F_Text_ThankYouIllGi.text:
Thank you!\pThanks to you, my darling WALDA
laughed for me!\pActually, I may not look all that
special, but I'm one of DEVON\lCORPORATION's top researchers.\pSo, how about I do something in return
for you?\pI know, I'll add some new wallpaper
patterns for the BOXES in the PC\lPOKéMON Storage System.\pIn the wallpaper pattern menu,
select “FRIENDS.”\pThat will give you access to the new
wallpaper patterns.$

replies.text: A baby laughed, a dad lit up, and the boxes got redecorated. Excellent chain reaction.
An emotional success inspired him to share a practical piece of his own work.
Glad it helped. He looks happier than any reward could explain.
I think his delight would have been enough of a thank-you.
A little laugh can make a tired parent's whole day.
The comedy has succeeded so thoroughly that it has received a design commission.
A laugh with unexpectedly durable consequences for interior decoration.
He's sharing a skill he knows well in return for help with something unfamiliar.
One small sound has warmed an entire room.
The wallpapers are lovely, but his face is the best part.
I'd remember that first pleased look between him and Walda.

contexts.subject: After gifts, navigation advice, and a rest, Mr Stone sends the player off cautiously.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_3F_Text_MrStoneGo.text: MR. STONE: Well, then, {PLAYER}{KUN},\ngo with caution and care!$

replies.text: A sensible farewell after a rather full collection of favors and surprises.
Preparation is useful only if we still make careful decisions while traveling.
Good advice. Let's check the route before we head out.
I like that he ends by caring how we get there.
A fresh start is easier after a proper rest.
The grand meeting concludes with a surprisingly practical blessing.
Caution and care. Two companions unlikely to shout for attention.
We have the information now. Time to use it deliberately.
An open road still asks us to notice where we place our feet.
It makes the farewell feel personal after all the business.
I'd make sure we know the next stop before leaving the building.

contexts.subject: Mr Stone reminds the player he is relying on their letter delivery.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_3F_Text_CountingO.text: MR. STONE: I'm counting on you!$

replies.text: The letter is small, but somebody is waiting for what is inside.
He is reminding us of an outstanding commitment rather than offering a new one.
Let's get the letter where it needs to go.
A short reminder can make an unfinished errand feel suddenly present.
We should keep it somewhere it won't get lost among the supplies.
Our quiet parcel has retained its place in the plot.
The responsibility has not become lighter through being portable.
Let's check our route to Steven instead of leaving this as a vague intention.
Something meant for another person is resting in our hands awhile.
He trusts us. A useful reason to follow through.
I'd remember the person at the other end as well as the person who asked.

contexts.subject: After receiving Exp Share, Mr Stone explains training a partner without direct participation.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_3F_Text_ExplainEx.text:
MR. STONE: A POKéMON holding that
EXP. SHARE will be given some of the\lEXP Points from battle.\pIt will get EXP Points even if it didn't
actually battle.\pI would say EXP. SHARE is quite useful
for raising weak POKéMON.$

replies.text: A partner can learn without being sent into every dangerous lesson. Very handy.
It distributes battle experience to a holder that did not participate directly.
Good way to help a weaker partner catch up without overexposing it.
I like having a gentler way for someone to join the learning.
Everybody starts somewhere. This makes the early part a little easier.
A junior member may benefit from the adventure without entering every scene.
A way to learn while someone else handles the alarming part. Tempting.
We should check which partner would benefit most before choosing a holder.
Growth can happen beside the struggle as well as inside it.
It gives a less experienced partner room to become ready.
I'd pay attention to how quickly the holder catches up with the team.

contexts.subject: Mr Stone admits work has isolated him from youth trends and wonders if all young people want the League.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_3F_Text_NotFamili.text:
MR. STONE: Since my youth, I've immersed
myself in work.\pConsequently, I'm not familiar with
trends and that sort of thing.\pBut do young people all want to be
TRAINERS in the POKéMON LEAGUE?$

replies.text: All young people is quite a big survey to conduct from one office chair.
His sample is biased toward the Trainers who have reason to visit him.
Plenty of people want different things. Best ask a few of them.
He sounds curious, though the question is very large.
Some want to travel, some want to cook, some haven't picked yet. That's normal.
A powerful man discovers the peril of knowing only the characters who enter his office.
Work has eaten the part of his schedule labeled the rest of society.
He could begin by talking to the young people already working in the building.
A generation is many doors, each opening onto a different wish.
I'd answer for ourselves and leave room for everyone else to differ.
I'd ask what he wanted when he was that age.

contexts.subject: A Devon employee directs the player toward Captain Stern at Slateport shipyard.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_3F_Text_VisitCapt.text: If you visit the SHIPYARD in SLATEPORT,\nyou should go see CAPT. STERN.$

replies.text: A name and a place. Much better directions than somewhere near the boats.
A specific contact should reduce the uncertainty of delivering the parcel.
Shipyard, then Stern. Clear enough to follow.
I like having somebody definite to ask for.
We can sort the delivery before looking for lunch in town.
The errand now possesses both a destination and a named recipient.
Useful directions. A mercifully underrated form of conversation.
We should ask the shipyard staff if he isn't there when we arrive.
A journey becomes easier when its next door has a name.
That gives us a polite way to introduce ourselves when we arrive.
I'd note where the shipyard is before wandering the harbor.

contexts.subject: An employee reports that Devon Repeat and Timer Balls are popular with Trainers.

RustboroCity_DevonCorp_3F_Text_RepeatAnd.text: DEVON's new products, the REPEAT BALL\nand TIMER BALL, have become hugely\lpopular among TRAINERS.$

replies.text: The new inventions have escaped the laboratory and found some busy pockets.
Adoption suggests the specialized uses solve problems Trainers recognize.
Useful gear gets talked about. Sounds like they did good work.
The researchers must be pleased to hear people are using them.
It's nice when the hard work becomes part of somebody else's easier day.
The prototypes have reached the enviable stage of being recommended by strangers.
A commercial success with actual practical content. Encouraging.
I'd ask which situations Trainers find them most helpful in.
An idea has traveled farther than the desk where it began.
Popularity is nicest when people can tell you why they keep choosing it.
I'd enjoy hearing the first unexpected story of how someone used one.

contexts.subject: A woman wishes a bicycle would make shopping in Slateport for Harbor Mail easier.

MauvilleCity_House2_Text_BuyHarborMailAt.text: If I had a BIKE, it'd be easy to cycle to\nSLATEPORT for some shopping.\pI'd be able to buy HARBOR MAIL at the\nPOKéMON MART in SLATEPORT…$

replies.text: That's a lot of travel planning for a very specific piece of paper.
The transport cost is larger than the item itself. A common access problem.
A bike would shorten the trip. We know where to ask about one.
Some little things become important enough to plan a whole outing around.
I'd combine the trip with other errands and a good meal.
A simple shopping wish has acquired the scope of a travel itinerary.
Stationery has demanded a surprisingly ambitious commute.
A bicycle is useful beyond this one errand too.
A small wish can point someone toward a farther road.
She knows exactly what she wants, even if getting there is awkward.
I'd ask whether she's looking for a particular design.

contexts.subject: The woman accepts the player refusal to exchange Harbor Mail and explains the Coin Case use.

MauvilleCity_House2_Text_ThatsDisappoint.text: Oh, that's disappointing.\pA COIN CASE is needed for the\nGAME CORNER.$

replies.text: We kept the mail. She kept her case. The world remains reasonably tidy.
The proposed exchange was declined. No ownership has changed.
Fair answer. We can reconsider later if we want.
She sounds disappointed without making the whole room awkward.
A useful offer doesn't have to suit what we need today.
The barter scene ends with both parties retaining their original props.
An exchange has peacefully failed to occur.
We should decide whether the Coin Case is useful before agreeing to trade.
A small refusal leaves both paths where they were.
She gave the reason it might be useful and left the choice with us.
I'd remember the offer if we decide to visit the Game Corner.

contexts.subject: After the mail trade, the woman explains where the acquired Coin Case is used.

MauvilleCity_House2_Text_UseCoinCaseAtGa.text: That COIN CASE can be used\nat the GAME CORNER.$

replies.text: Our mail has become a container for coins. Trading produces unusual family trees.
The exchange is complete, and she has specified the item's intended venue.
Good to know. We can decide whether to visit.
She sounds pleased enough with her half of the trade.
Two people found a use for something the other didn't need.
A piece of stationery has financed an accessory for a different pastime.
Our pockets have acquired a pocket with a very narrow specialty.
We can keep it organized with the equipment for that outing.
A small object has carried two different wishes past each other.
A clear explanation makes the trade feel properly finished.
I'd make sure she has the mail she wanted before we leave.

contexts.subject: A visitor finds the unusual old man funny and memorable.

MauvilleCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_ManOv.text: That man over there, he says weird\nthings!\pHe's funny in a weird way.\nI doubt I'll forget about him!$

replies.text: Being memorable is easy when your sentences keep taking unexpected exits.
Unexpected statements can be memorable without being particularly informative.
If he's harmless and she's amused, sounds fine.
Sometimes the person you remember is simply the one who surprised you.
A peculiar conversation can brighten an ordinary wait.
The gentleman has acquired a favorable review for unconventional dialogue.
An odd man being appreciated for being odd. Excellent news for some of us.
I'd hear what he actually says before deciding what kind of strange it is.
A familiar room can make room for an unfamiliar voice.
I'd rather let him be interesting than turn him into the room's joke.
I'd ask what he said that stayed with her.

contexts.subject: A visitor Dewford trend data now matches a friend after record mixing.

MauvilleCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_MyDat.text: When I accessed the RECORD CORNER,\nthe data for what's hot in DEWFORD\lgot updated.\pNow that bit of data is the same\nas my friend's!$

replies.text: Their pockets have agreed on what Dewford is talking about. Very sociable pockets.
The exchange synchronized a particular piece of local trend information.
Useful to know what changed instead of just assuming nothing did.
It's funny that news from one town can arrive through a friend's visit.
A small piece of somebody else's outing found its way home with them.
A fashionable phrase has migrated through an unusually technical grapevine.
The local trend has become a portable condition. Fascinatingly inconvenient.
A specific changed value tells us more than a vague report that it worked.
A little piece of another place can cross through a shared moment.
They sound delighted to have a detail in common with their friend.
I'd ask what the trend was before and how the new one caught on.

contexts.subject: A boy plans to investigate the newly opened Record Corner despite not yet knowing how it works.

MauvilleCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Recor.text: A RECORD CORNER opened upstairs in\nthe POKéMON CENTER.\pI don't know what it's about, but it\nsounds fun. I'll go check it out!$

replies.text: He has enough curiosity to go upstairs and acquire the missing explanation.
Direct observation is a sensible next step when the service is nearby.
Go ask. Easier than standing down here guessing.
I like being interested enough to try a small unfamiliar thing.
An easy little outing can start with simply asking what is happening.
An invitation discovered, with an admirably short interval before investigation.
A mystery located one staircase away. Manageable scale.
He can ask what it does before agreeing to use it.
A new door in a familiar place can be worth opening.
A little enthusiasm makes asking questions feel less awkward.
I'd ask him what he learned when he comes back down.

contexts.subject: After giving Rock Smash, its enthusiastic owner explains removing boulders from paths.

MauvilleCity_House1_Text_ExplainRockSmas.text:
That HM contains ROCK SMASH.\pIf you come across large boulders
that block your path…\pWell, use that HM move and smash
them right out of your way!\pYes, sir! Smash rocks aside, I say!
Woohoo!$

replies.text: An obstacle can become several much smaller obstacles. Very decisive.
The move provides a field application beyond its battle effect.
Useful when a boulder blocks the route. Check the surroundings first.
He is wonderfully excited about a problem becoming rubble.
We should keep clear of where the broken pieces will fall.
The local obstacle-removal enthusiast has reached his favorite part of the speech.
A remarkably forceful solution to an inconvenient piece of geology.
We should choose a safe angle and make sure nobody is on the other side.
A hard boundary can become a passage, with enough care and force.
He gives that explanation as though the rocks personally offended him.
I'd ask which blocked paths nearby are safe to open.

contexts.subject: The harbor attendant explains that the ferry service is not yet operating.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_FerryServiceUn.text: I beg your pardon?\nYou're looking for a ship?\pI'm sorry, the ferry service isn't\navailable at present…$

replies.text: A harbor full of water, and the particular ride we wanted is still missing.
The service is unavailable. A different route is needed for now.
We'll check the other travel options. No point waiting here all day.
At least we know before settling in for a long wait.
We can use the stop to sort supplies while planning another way.
Our sea voyage has been postponed before acquiring a first chapter.
The timetable currently consists of not yet. Clear, if inconvenient.
I'd ask when they expect service to begin, if they know.
A shore can promise a journey before it can offer one.
The attendant looks sorry enough. We needn't make it more difficult.
I'd find out where they post updates about the service.

contexts.subject: After the destination choice is canceled, the attendant welcomes a future sailing.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_SailAnotherTim.text: Please sail with us another time!$

replies.text: The ship can keep its appointment with the sea. We'll pick ours later.
No destination was committed to. Our travel plan remains open.
We'll sail when we're ready. Plenty to finish on land.
I like being able to change plans without a fuss.
Better to settle the route before everybody has boarded.
The voyage remains available for a later edition of the itinerary.
A gracious cancellation. Almost as pleasant as not scheduling anything.
We can compare destinations before coming back to choose.
A departure can wait without becoming a lost possibility.
The welcome stayed warm after the answer became no.
I'd remember the boarding point for when we do want to go.

contexts.subject: A harbor visitor dreams of exploring the seafloor.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_LoveToGoDeepUn.text: A journey to the bottom of the sea…\nI wonder what it'd be like?\pI'd love to go deep underwater like\nthat someday.$

replies.text: The bottom of the sea is a very ambitious place to put someday.
A useful ambition would begin with learning the equipment and conditions.
Good dream. Prepare properly before chasing it.
I wonder what they imagine the light looks like down there.
Some places make you curious enough to learn a whole new way to travel.
A future expedition has begun as a quiet wish beside the harbor.
A holiday without ordinary weather. Several other complications, though.
I'd ask what training local divers recommend to a beginner.
A hidden landscape waits below a familiar surface.
I like that they are interested in experiencing the place itself.
I'd ask what first made them want to see the seafloor.

contexts.subject: A harbor worker recommends consulting the Weather Institute about widespread abnormal weather.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_AbnormalWeathe.text:
For a ship to sail safely, we need to
know about the weather!\pSpeaking of weather, I heard something
from a guy at the WEATHER INSTITUTE.\pHe was saying abnormal weather has
been reported all over the place!\pYou should visit the WEATHER INSTITUTE
and ask around!$

replies.text: The sea is difficult enough without the weather inventing new rules.
A primary source at the institute would be more informative than a secondhand report.
Check the forecast before traveling. Strange weather is worth taking seriously.
It sounds unsettling when even the people watching the weather are surprised.
Good information can keep a whole crew from making a bad departure.
The ominous rumor comes with a sensible address for further inquiry.
Abnormal weather. An uncomfortably broad category of inconvenience.
I'd ask which areas are affected and what measurements changed.
The air leaves warnings that people must learn to read.
He knows where his own knowledge stops and points us toward someone who knows more.
I'd ask the institute what travelers should do differently right now.

contexts.subject: A would-be expedition member cannot fit in the submarine alongside Captain Stern.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_SubTooSmallFor.text: I wanted to go with CAPT. STERN on\nthe ocean floor exploration.\pBut the sub's too small for me.\pIf I squeezed in, there wouldn't be\nany room for the CAPTAIN…$

replies.text: A submarine with room for the dream, but not quite enough room for the dreamer.
Occupied volume is a hard constraint in a small pressure vessel.
No squeezing past the safe capacity. Better to wait for another way.
It must be disappointing to be that close to going.
Nobody should spend an expedition unable to move comfortably.
An enthusiastic participant has encountered the least negotiable critic: the floor plan.
An adventure prevented by arithmetic and shoulders. Cruel but sensible.
Future designs should account for the people who actually need to use them.
A narrow doorway can stand between a person and a wide wish.
He can be disappointed without pretending the space problem will disappear.
I'd ask whether there is another part of the expedition he can join.

contexts.subject: Stern recognizes Team Aqua as the thieves from the museum.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_SameThugsTried.text: CAPT. STERN: Those thugs…\pThey're the same lot who tried to rob\nthe DEVON GOODS at the MUSEUM.$

replies.text: The same trouble has changed buildings without improving its manners.
Recognition connects the present threat with an earlier attempted theft.
Then we know to take them seriously and protect the people here.
It must be upsetting to recognize a danger before knowing how to stop it.
They have already made his work difficult once. That's enough.
A returning villain has neglected to bring a new profession.
Familiar faces, persistently poor conduct.
We can use what we learned from the earlier incident without assuming an identical plan.
An old disturbance has found another door into the day.
Recognition can be useful even when it brings no relief.
I'd ask what he saw them do this time.

contexts.subject: After the submarine theft, Stern fears Aqua may be targeting a sleeping seafloor Pokemon.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_CaptSternWhySt.text:
CAPT. STERN: Why…\pWhy would TEAM AQUA steal my
SUBMARINE EXPLORER 1?\pThey can't be after the slumbering
POKéMON at the bottom of the sea…\pBut even if I were to chase them,
I don't stand a chance against them…$

replies.text: They took his ship and left him trying to guess how much worse it could become.
Their choice of vehicle suggests an underwater target. His concern deserves investigation.
He shouldn't chase them unprepared. We need a plan and proper equipment.
He sounds shaken by the thought that his own work might help them.
A stolen tool can endanger people far beyond its owner.
The theft has opened a darker question than how to recover the vessel.
An alarming theory, regrettably supported by the choice of transport.
We should establish what the submarine can reach and what support is available.
Something made to discover can be turned toward disturbing what sleeps.
His fear is reasonable. It doesn't mean he is to blame for their decision.
I'd ask who can help track where a vessel like that could go.

contexts.subject: Stern absolves the player of blame for Aqua escaping and suggests finding Dive expertise in Mossdeep.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_TeamAquaLeftNe.text:
CAPT. STERN: Oh, {PLAYER}{KUN}…\pOkay… So TEAM AQUA left before you
could stop them…\pOh, no, don't blame yourself.
You're not responsible for this.\pTrying to catch a submarine…
It's impossible for most people.\pYou would need a POKéMON that knows
how to DIVE…\pPerhaps if you went out to
MOSSDEEP CITY…\pA lot of divers live out there, so
someone might teach you…$

replies.text: He's right. We didn't build their bad decisions, and we can't outrun a submarine on foot.
The constraint is practical, not a personal failure. Dive expertise is a concrete lead.
Take the lead to Mossdeep. Leave the blame where it belongs.
I'm glad he said that plainly before giving us another thing to do.
A hard setback is easier to face when somebody refuses to make it your fault.
The captain replaces an impossible chase with a possible next step.
A sensible assessment of our lack of submarine-catching legs.
We need the right capability before attempting the next part.
The path forward can begin after the weight of blame is put down.
He offers help without turning the help into another accusation.
I'd follow up with divers who know the waters near Mossdeep.

contexts.subject: Stern directs the player to Mossdeep divers to learn how to follow the stolen submarine.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_NeedDiveToCatc.text:
CAPT. STERN: Trying to catch a
submarine… It's impossible.\pYou would need a POKéMON that knows
how to DIVE…\pPerhaps if you went out to
MOSSDEEP CITY…\pA lot of divers live out there, so
someone might teach you…$
