replies.text: We need a way down, not a faster way to wave at the water.
The proposed pursuit requires a capability we should secure before attempting it.
Mossdeep is the lead. We'll ask people who know the depth.
A definite next step makes the whole problem feel less impossible.
We should learn how to come back up as well as how to go down.
The chase pauses for the acquisition of a very necessary skill.
At last, a plan acknowledging the inconvenient volume of water involved.
Local divers can explain hazards as well as the move itself.
An unseen path still needs a safe way home.
He's sharing the useful part instead of pretending the task will be simple.
I'd ask the divers what they know about that particular stretch of sea.

contexts.subject: Stern credits Briney arrival with bringing the ferry near completion.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_WontBeLongBefo.text: CAPT. STERN: Oh, yes.\nMR. BRINEY came to our SHIPYARD.\pIt won't be long now before we finish\nmaking the ferry!$

replies.text: Briney's experience has turned not yet into nearly. That's a useful kind of magic.
The additional expertise has improved the project's progress.
Good. More people will have a reliable way to travel soon.
He sounds pleased to have someone he trusts helping.
A good pair of hands can change the mood of a whole job.
The long-awaited voyage is approaching the end of its construction chapter.
Nearly finished. A phrase with considerably more hope than the earlier version.
I'd ask which remaining checks they need before passengers can board.
A careful craft can bring distant homes a little closer.
He made sure Briney's contribution didn't disappear behind the finished product.
I'd like to hear how the two of them first started working together.

contexts.subject: Stern celebrates the completed S.S. Tidal, credits Briney, and invites the player aboard.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_FinishedMaking.text: CAPT. STERN: {PLAYER}{KUN}!\pWe finally finished making the ferry\nS.S. TIDAL!\pWe couldn't have done it without\nyour friend MR. BRINEY.\pPlease go for a short cruise on it!$

replies.text: The ferry is real now! All those plans have finally become a very large ride.
A completed vessel turns their collaboration into a useful public service.
Well done to the crew. Worth taking a trip when we're ready.
I like that he wants us to enjoy the thing they made.
A launch deserves a celebration, and so do the people who did the work.
The project's finale includes an invitation to become part of the next story.
A boat with a name, a purpose, and apparently sufficient room. Excellent.
I'd love to see what they learned from Briney reflected in the finished design.
Something built on land is ready to belong to the water.
Giving Briney credit makes the invitation feel warmer.
I'd want to hear what the crew felt as the first passengers boarded.

contexts.subject: Stern accepts a declined Scanner exchange while leaving his offer open.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_IfYouWantToTra.text: CAPT. STERN: Are you certain?\nIt's useless to you, {PLAYER}{KUN}…\pWell, okay, then. If you want to trade\nyour SCANNER, let me know.$

replies.text: He can't use our answer yet, but he can leave us room to change it.
The exchange is optional, and the equipment remains with us.
No trade for now. He knows where he stands.
I'm glad disappointment didn't become an argument.
We can decide what is useful without being rushed by someone else's need.
The bargain remains open, with its final page mercifully unsigned.
A device of no use to us has acquired a surprisingly complicated farewell.
We should compare the offered items before choosing.
A wish can remain open without becoming a demand.
He pressed a little, then respected the answer. That matters.
I'd remember what he offered if we come back to reconsider.

contexts.subject: The Scanner exchange is complete and Stern thanks the player for helping research.

SlateportCity_Harbor_Text_ThisWillHelpRe.text: CAPT. STERN: Thanks, {PLAYER}{KUN}!\nThis will help our research a lot!$

replies.text: The Scanner has finally reached the person with a sea-sized use for it.
The transfer is complete. Specialized equipment can now support the intended research.
Good. He'll put it to proper use.
He sounds relieved to have the missing piece in hand.
Something we carried around is going to make somebody's work easier.
The wandering instrument has reached the chapter where its purpose begins.
A technical object reunited with someone qualified to be excited about it.
I'd ask what new observations the Scanner will let them make.
A small tool can open a larger hidden place to understanding.
His thanks feel tied to the work it will help, which I like.
I'd come back later to hear what they discovered with it.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater politely ends a canceled or declined naming session.

replies.text: Our Pokemon's name has survived the consultation unruffled.
No naming change was committed to during this visit.
We're fine with it for now. Good to leave the choice open.
I'm glad declining didn't need a speech.
A familiar name doesn't have to change just because someone offers.
The editorial consultation concludes without revisions.
A perfectly satisfactory result: no unnecessary alterations.
We can come back when we have a deliberate change in mind.
A name can rest where it has already found a home.
He let the decision stay ours. A good way to end the visit.
I'd say thanks and keep the introduction we already know.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater refuses to assess a Pokemon Egg nickname.

SlateportCity_NameRatersHouse_Text_ThatI.text: Now, now.\nThat is merely an EGG!$

replies.text: The Egg has not yet submitted a name for critical consideration.
There is no hatched Pokemon's nickname for him to assess yet.
Let it hatch first. No hurry on the naming.
It might be easier to find a name once we meet the one inside.
We can wait until there's a face to go with the idea.
The candidate has arrived before the character introduction.
The critic has rejected our most quietly mysterious applicant.
We need a hatched partner before this service applies.
A little life can begin before its name does.
There is time to choose something that feels right later.
I'd rather meet the Pokemon than decide everything from the shell.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater declines to change another Trainer Pokemon name and praises the existing one.

SlateportCity_NameRatersHouse_Text_Magni.text: Hmmm… {STR_VAR_1} it is!\pThis is a magnificent nickname!\nIt is impeccably beyond reproach!\pYou'll do well to cherish your\n{STR_VAR_1} now and beyond.$

replies.text: Somebody else chose that name with a little thought we weren't here to see.
He preserves a name assigned by the previous Trainer.
Keep the name it arrived with. We can learn the partner behind it.
A familiar name may be one comfortable thing on a new journey.
It comes with a bit of its old home attached.
The previous author retains the title, with an enthusiastic endorsement from the editor.
An impeccable name. Conveniently beyond the critic's jurisdiction.
Continuity can help us remember the Pokemon's history beyond our own team.
An old voice can remain folded inside the sound we use now.
A name carries a relationship as well as a style choice.
I'd ask the previous Trainer how they came to choose it if we get the chance.

contexts.subject: After the player chooses a different nickname, the Name Rater declares the new name superior.

SlateportCity_NameRatersHouse_Text_MonSh.text: Done! From now on, this POKéMON\nshall be known as {STR_VAR_1}!\pIt is a better name than before!\nHow fortunate for you!$

replies.text: A new name! Our Pokemon may need a moment to update its who-is-being-called list.
The nickname has changed. We should use it consistently so the partner recognizes it.
If it fits, good. Let's say it kindly.
A name feels different once you speak it to the Pokemon itself.
I'd try it gently and see how the partner responds.
The revised title has been published with extravagant editorial approval.
A new name, declared superior by the man responsible for approving new names.
A useful change should be something we actually want to keep calling it.
A familiar companion can meet us through a different sound.
The best test is how naturally it feels when we say it together.
I'd remember the first time it turns toward that new name.

contexts.subject: The unchanged nickname is nevertheless declared superior by the Name Rater.

SlateportCity_NameRatersHouse_Text_NameN.text: Done! From now on, this POKéMON\nshall be known as {STR_VAR_1}!\pIt looks no different from before,\nand yet, this is vastly superior!\pHow fortunate for you!$

replies.text: The name has improved so much it has become exactly the same name. Remarkable.
The output is unchanged. His evaluation has altered without a change in the subject.
Same name. Saved us learning a new one.
I suppose being certain about the old choice can feel like a new choice.
The familiar name is still a perfectly good thing to enjoy.
A masterful revision whose restraint includes making no revision whatsoever.
An invisible improvement. The most convenient kind to maintain.
There is no functional change, but we have confirmed our preference.
Sometimes returning to a name makes it feel chosen again.
He gave the old name a fresh bit of confidence. I can live with that.
I'd laugh with him and see whether our Pokemon noticed any difference.

contexts.subject: The Move Deleter ends a canceled or declined session and invites another visit.

LilycoveCity_MoveDeletersHouse_Text_Come.text: Come again if there are moves that\nneed to be forgotten.$

replies.text: The moves are staying where they are today. Their tiny eviction notices are canceled.
No deletion occurred. The current move set remains available.
Better to wait if we aren't sure.
It's a relief that asking doesn't commit us to forgetting anything.
We can think it over without holding up the room.
The editor puts down the eraser until a clear decision arrives.
Forgetting has been postponed. An oddly memorable outcome.
We should choose what replaces a move before removing it.
A skill can stay with us until letting it go has a purpose.
A calm ending makes it easier to return when the choice is clearer.
I'd revisit the team's needs before making another appointment.

contexts.subject: The Move Deleter refuses to remove a Pokemon only known move.

LilycoveCity_MoveDeletersHouse_Text_MonO.text: {STR_VAR_1} knows only one move\nso it can't be forgotten…$

replies.text: Taking its only move would leave a rather awkward hole in the instructions.
The last remaining move is protected so the Pokemon retains an action.
Keep it. Our partner needs something it can do.
I'm glad that limit is there before anyone tries to remove everything.
We should give it another option before taking this one away.
The editor has declined to erase the book's only sentence.
An empty move list seems like a particularly bleak syllabus.
The minimum capability needs to stay intact. Sensible safeguard.
Even letting go needs somewhere left to stand.
A change should leave the partner with more room, not none.
I'd look at what it can learn next before returning.

contexts.subject: The Move Deleter refuses to perform the service on an Egg.

LilycoveCity_MoveDeletersHouse_Text_EggC.text: What?\nNo EGG should know any moves.$

replies.text: We have asked the Egg to forget something before it has introduced itself.
The service cannot operate on an unhatched Pokemon.
Leave the Egg be. We can talk about moves after it hatches.
There is plenty of time to meet the one inside before changing anything.
Let the little one arrive before we start rearranging its day.
A premature revision request has reached a still-sealed manuscript.
The Egg has wisely arrived without an editable curriculum.
We need a hatched Pokemon for this selection to make sense.
A beginning should be allowed to begin first.
I'd rather learn who is inside than plan what it should leave behind.
We can return after we've had time to know the Pokemon.

contexts.subject: The last available Surf user cannot have Surf removed.

LilycoveCity_MoveDeletersHouse_Text_Cant.text: Hm!\pYour {STR_VAR_1} doesn't seem willing\nto forget SURF.$

replies.text: Our way across the water is requesting continued employment. Sensible move.
Surf is retained because this is our last available user. It preserves travel access.
Keep it until another partner can get us across safely.
I would rather not discover the missing ride while standing on an island.
Some useful things need to stay until another arrangement is ready.
The plot has declined an edit that would strand its entire cast.
A vital transport service has successfully resisted deletion.
Redundancy first, removal second. A practical order of operations.
The path home should not be the thing we choose to forget.
A safety limit is welcome when a small menu choice can have a large effect.
I'd check who else can learn it before trying to change this partner.

contexts.subject: The selected Pokemon has successfully forgotten the selected move.

LilycoveCity_MoveDeletersHouse_Text_MonH.text: It worked to perfection!\p{STR_VAR_1} has forgotten\n{STR_VAR_2} completely.$

replies.text: One move has left the list. I hope we have something useful ready for that room.
The deletion is complete. The available move set has genuinely changed.
Done. Let's make sure the remaining moves cover what we need.
It is a strange thing to hear a forgetting announced so neatly.
There's room for something new now. We should choose it with care.
A deliberate edit has been made; the next lesson can take its place.
A very successful absence. Unusual work to congratulate someone on.
We should review the result rather than assume one removed move solves the whole plan.
An empty space can be a choice rather than a loss.
The change is settled. Now the partner needs a clear direction for what comes next.
I'd check how the new arrangement feels before making another change.

contexts.subject: Brock praises our talent and recommends challenging Cerulean Gym.

PewterCity_Gym_Text_BrockPostBattle.text:
There are all kinds of TRAINERS in
this huge world of ours.\pYou appear to be very gifted as a
POKéMON TRAINER.\pSo let me make a suggestion.\pGo to the GYM in CERULEAN and test
your abilities.$

replies.text: A compliment and directions. Much easier to carry than another boulder.
A new Gym means a different test. We can take confidence without assuming the same plan will work.
Good win. Check the team before the next road.
He is sending us onward like he expects to hear good things.
We should celebrate with the team before turning this into the next errand.
The formidable first obstacle has become a generous guide to the next chapter.
I appreciate an opponent who gives us something useful besides bruises.
Cerulean is a concrete next objective. Time to check the route and our supplies.
A stone can mark the beginning of a road rather than block it.
He sounds sincerely impressed. You are allowed to enjoy that.
I wonder what he hopes challengers remember about meeting him here.

contexts.subject: Liam calls us good but insists Brock is even better.

PewterCity_Gym_Text_LiamPostBattle.text: You're pretty hot.\n…But not as hot as BROCK!$

replies.text: We are hot, but Brock is hotter. The Rock Gym has developed a temperature scale.
He recognizes our strength while warning about his leader. Both observations can be useful.
We will take Brock seriously. He does not need to diminish our win to arrange that.
I think that was a compliment trying not to disappoint his favorite person.
We can be proud of this battle and still prepare for the next one.
A favorable review carefully approved by the Brock appreciation committee.
A compliment with a larger compliment standing directly behind it.
Then the next test will need its own plan. This result does not predict all the others.
One stone is not the mountain. We still earned our footing.
I appreciate his loyalty. The comparison is doing a lot of work.
He admires Brock enough to put him into every part of this conversation.

contexts.subject: Brock explains the single-use Rock Tomb TM and its Speed reduction.

PewterCity_Gym_Text_ExplainTM39.text:
A TM, Technical Machine, contains a
technique for POKéMON.\pUsing a TM teaches the move it
contains to a POKéMON.\pA TM is good for only one use.\pSo, when you use one, pick the
POKéMON carefully.\pAnyways…
TM39 contains ROCK TOMB.\pIt hurls boulders at the foe and
lowers its SPEED.$

replies.text: The rocks hurt and make you slower. I had a similar experience carrying groceries.
Reduced Speed can influence later turns. The single-use TM makes choosing its recipient important.
Check who can learn it before deciding. We cannot take the lesson back afterward.
I like moves that leave the next moment a little easier to handle.
Let us choose a teammate it really suits, rather than use a gift just because it is new.
A lesson in momentum, taught by a rather unaccommodating pile of stones.
A permanent educational decision disguised as a small disc. No pressure.
Damage plus speed control. Its second effect may be more useful than the first.
The falling stone changes the rhythm after the impact.
He explained the limitations clearly. We should give the choice the same care.
It is a useful reminder to watch what a move changes beyond the visible hit.

contexts.subject: The guide explains the lead Pokemon and recommends changing party order for opponents.

PewterCity_Gym_Text_TryDifferentPartyOrd.text:
The first POKéMON out in a match is
at the left of the POKéMON LIST.\pBy changing the order of POKéMON,
you may gain an advantage.\pTry different orders to suit your
opponent's party.$

replies.text: We can change the plan by moving a name up a list. Finally, tactics that respect my knees.
The opening matchup can shape the whole battle. Party order is worth reviewing deliberately.
Put the right partner first. Do not make the lead position somebody's permanent chore.
It is nice to have one useful thing we can decide before the noise starts.
Different teammates deserve chances to begin when the situation suits them.
The cast order can change the opening scene more than a louder entrance.
A rearrangement that accomplishes more than most of my rearranging.
A low-cost adjustment with a potentially large effect. Good advice.
Who takes the first step changes how the others can follow.
A fitting order depends on where we are going. It need not stay the same forever.
I will watch how each teammate handles getting the first turn.

contexts.subject: The guide says the victory proves we are Champion material.

PewterCity_Gym_Text_YoureChampMaterial.text: Just as I thought!\nYou're POKéMON champ material!$

replies.text: Champion material! I hope it is comfortable and does not shrink in the wash.
A promising result. Becoming Champion will involve many more, not merely repeating this one.
Take the encouragement. Keep doing the work.
He sounds very certain. I hope the feeling reaches you without turning into pressure.
We can enjoy this step without asking the team to carry the whole future today.
Our enthusiastic adviser has upgraded the forecast to a possible championship finale.
You do not have to be perfect tomorrow to deserve his happiness today.
The first test is passed. The next ones will supply more information.
A bright possibility does not need to become a demand.
That confidence is a gift. You get to choose how to carry it.
I would remember how it felt to hear that before the title became anything more than a possibility.

contexts.subject: Diana says battling other trainers reveals how good one really is.

CeruleanCity_Gym_Text_DianaPostBattle.text: You have to face other TRAINERS\nto see how good you really are.$

replies.text: Other people are an inconvenient but effective test of my excellent imaginary plans.
An unfamiliar opponent can expose weaknesses a familiar routine never tests.
A real battle teaches something. It does not need to decide your entire worth.
It is easier to learn when losing is allowed to mean more than being bad.
Different partners bring different lessons. So do different opponents.
A private rehearsal has encountered the very useful inconvenience of another actor.
Reality is an annoyingly thorough editor.
Test the plan against behavior you did not design yourself. That is where the surprises are.
A mirror shows one side. Another traveler shows a different one.
Feedback helps when it is specific. A single result still leaves plenty unknown.
She seems to have learned something about us and herself from the same match.

contexts.subject: Luis insists Misty keeps improving and cannot lose to someone like us.

CeruleanCity_Gym_Text_LuisPostBattle.text: MISTY is a TRAINER who's going to\nkeep improving.\pShe won't lose to someone like you!$

replies.text: Misty is improving. We are apparently expected to remain politely where he last estimated us.
Her progress is a reason to prepare, not evidence that ours must stop.
We can respect her without accepting his opinion of us.
I would rather meet her than keep hearing who we supposedly are.
Let us check our team instead of arguing over his prediction.
The local fan has declared our role in advance. We are free to improvise.
Someone like us. He has known us for an impressively brief time.
Both teams can improve. His forecast leaves out one moving variable.
A person's certainty does not narrow the road under our feet.
Admiring her does not require being rude to everyone else.
I wonder what Misty would think of him dismissing her challengers before she meets them.

contexts.subject: Misty gives Water Pulse and suggests an aquatic Pokemon learn it.

CeruleanCity_Gym_Text_ExplainTM03.text: TM03 teaches WATER PULSE.\pUse it on an aquatic POKéMON!$

replies.text: A water move for a water-loving teammate. Finally, a lesson that comes with its own splash zone.
We should check compatibility rather than choose purely by appearance.
See who can learn it and who benefits. Then choose.
I would like to see a teammate enjoy learning something that suits them.
Let us make sure the recipient actually needs another Water move first.
An aquatic part is available. We should cast it for ability rather than costume alone.
I support teaching it to someone who enjoys being damp more than I do.
The suggested category is a start. The actual movepool is the specification.
Let the lesson find a creature it belongs with.
A thoughtful match is better than giving it to the first blue Pokemon we see.
She sounds pleased to share a move she likes with somebody new.

contexts.subject: The guide recommends Grass or Electric Pokemon against Misty Water team.

CeruleanCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyAdvice.text:
Yo!
Champ in the making!\pLet me give you some advice!\pThe LEADER, MISTY, is a pro who
uses WATER-type POKéMON.\pYou can drain all their water with
GRASS-type POKéMON.\pOr, you might use ELECTRIC-type
POKéMON and zap them!$

replies.text: Drain them or zap them. His tactical vocabulary has a very practical little sound department.
Grass and Electric attacks offer useful matchups. We still need to consider individual opponents.
Good starting advice. Check our actual team before assuming a type alone will win.
Having a plan makes the pool feel a little less enormous.
The right matchup helps the team avoid taking unnecessary damage.
Our adviser has supplied two possible approaches and one enthusiastic nickname for us.
Champ in the making. I would settle for challenger with dry socks.
Two counter-options. Choose based on the moves and resources we actually have.
There is more than one way through the water.
We can use the advice without making our own team feel like the wrong choice.
I would like to see how Misty responds when someone arrives with that very common plan.

contexts.subject: The guide claims we make a great team after we beat Misty.

CeruleanCity_Gym_Text_WeMakePrettyGoodTe.text: You beat MISTY!\nSee, what'd I tell ya?\pYou and me, kid, we make a pretty\ndarn-good team!$

replies.text: You, me, and the Pokemon who did all the splashing. A very large team, selectively remembered.
The advice helped. The team still had to carry out the battle.
He can share the celebration. Make sure our Pokemon get the credit.
I like that he feels involved. It is nice to have someone waiting to be happy for us.
A little encouragement can matter. So can thanking the ones who actually battled.
The adviser has awarded himself a supporting credit in our successful production.
I admire his confidence in a partnership conducted entirely from the dry side of the room.
Useful input, successful execution. Different contributions, both easy to acknowledge.
A few kind words can travel alongside a team without entering the battle.
I am happy he is celebrating. Let us widen the thanks to everyone involved.
He was waiting to see how we did. That is a small kindness worth noticing.

contexts.subject: Surge warns that Electric attacks do not affect Ground Pokemon.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_LtSurgePostBattle.text: A little word of advice, kid!\pElectricity is sure powerful!\pBut, it's useless against GROUND-\ntype POKéMON!$

replies.text: Powerful electricity, stopped by dirt. Nature has a very dry sense of humor.
Immunity matters more than raw power in that matchup. We should remember the type, not the appearance.
A strong move still needs the right target. Good lesson.
It helps to know there is something a frightening attack simply cannot do.
Knowing our team's limits is part of keeping them safe.
The grand electrical spectacle meets a remarkably firm objection from the ground.
I appreciate a weakness that can be explained without making me touch a wire.
Increasing output will not solve an immunity. Change the approach.
The earth has its own answer to a storm.
A confident fighter admitting a clear limit. I respect that.
I wonder how often he has watched challengers learn that the hard way.

contexts.subject: Tucker connects the difficult door with Surge cautious military habits.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_TuckerPostBattle.text: It's not easy opening that door.\pLT. SURGE was always famous for\nhis cautious nature in the Army.$

replies.text: Caution is one thing. Hiding the entrance behind the rubbish is a very personal interpretation.
He has carried a security habit into the Gym design. It certainly slows visitors.
A cautious leader can still make the exit obvious. I hope he did.
It makes meeting him sound like something we need clearance for.
I hope the staff can get through quickly when somebody needs help.
An audience with the commander requires defeating both his team and his housekeeping.
Cautious enough to make strangers inspect his bins. A remarkable defensive doctrine.
Security should account for usability. I would like to see the emergency procedure.
Some old habits become walls long after the danger changes.
The story explains the locks. It does not make them less irritating.
I wonder which part of this place feels reassuring to him rather than inconvenient.

contexts.subject: Baily gives the vague hint that door switches are hidden inside something.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_BailyPostBattle.text: Okay, I'll talk!\pLT. SURGE said he hid door\nswitches inside something.$

replies.text: Inside something. Our search has narrowed to the entire concept of containers.
Technically information. Only slightly more specific than saying they exist.
He could have saved us a little more time than that.
I think he wants the secret to survive the explanation.
We can look carefully without turning the room upside down.
A witness has revealed that the concealed objects are, indeed, concealed.
A generous serving of almost an answer.
I shall record that under insufficiently specified location data.
The secret has moved from nowhere to somewhere. Progress, of a kind.
A hint so discreet it can barely be distinguished from withholding one.
I will watch where people glance when the switches come up. It may be more useful than that answer.

contexts.subject: Dwayne says Surge built the double locks and the second switch neighbors the first.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_DwaynePostBattle.text:
LT. SURGE installed the traps in
the GYM himself.\pHe set up double locks everywhere.
Let me give you a hint.\pWhen you open the first lock, the
second lock is right next to it.$

replies.text: The second switch is next door to the first. Finally, a neighbor with useful information.
Adjacent to the first switch. That substantially reduces the search space.
Remember the first location before checking its neighbors.
An actual clue. I can feel the room becoming less confusing.
We should slow down once we find the first one, not rush past the useful detail.
The mystery has acquired a rule instead of merely a personality.
A secret explained by someone apparently willing to explain it. Refreshing.
A local adjacency constraint! Much better than searching randomly.
The second answer waits close to the first. Keep track of where we began.
That is a hint I can use without pretending to understand the leader's entire life.
I would remember which bin started the sequence before looking anywhere else.

contexts.subject: Erika admires our cataloguing but says she would collect only attractive Pokemon.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_ErikaPostBattle.text: You are cataloging POKéMON?\nI must say I'm impressed.\pI would never collect POKéMON if\nthey were unattractive.$

replies.text: Some of my favorite faces look like a dropped sandwich. They still deserve an entry.
A catalogue is most useful when it includes what the observer would not personally choose.
She can have favorites. The others still matter.
I like the strange ones that take a little longer to understand.
Sometimes a creature becomes beautiful because you know how it greets you.
An excellent personal collection and a complete account are different projects.
Fortunately, attractiveness has never required unanimous approval. I checked.
Research that selects only appealing examples produces a distorted record.
There are flowers that look like weeds until someone kneels close enough.
Her taste is her own. I would rather keep mine curious.
A less obvious subject can become the picture you remember longest.

contexts.subject: Kay hopes Erika defeats us after losing.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_KayPostBattle.text: Bleaah!\nI hope ERIKA wipes you out!$

replies.text: We have lost the local cheering section. Fortunately, it was already cheering for someone else.
She is disappointed. Her wish tells us little about the battle ahead.
Let us move on. Winning does not require getting her approval.
I hope she feels better after we leave. We do not have to wait for it.
We can be kind without standing here to receive more anger.
The defeated supporting character has handed the revenge subplot to management.
A hostile review from a very recently defeated critic.
That is an emotional response, not additional tactical information.
Her sharp words can stay in this room.
We are allowed to enjoy the win without convincing her to enjoy it with us.
I would rather remember the team working together than the last thing she said.

contexts.subject: Bridget explains Grass advantages against Water, Rock and Ground.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_BridgetPostBattle.text: GRASS-type POKéMON are tough\nagainst the WATER type.\pThey also have an edge on ROCK-\nand GROUND-type POKéMON.$

replies.text: A leaf has a surprisingly ambitious list of things it can defeat.
Three useful matchups. We should still check the opponent's other type and moves.
Good advantages to know. They are a start, not permission to stop thinking.
Something that looks delicate can have a very firm answer.
It helps to know when a teammate will feel at home in the battle.
The greenery has arrived with a rather assertive list of professional references.
I admire a plant that can make a rock regret its choices.
An effective range of targets. Coverage gaps still matter when building the rest of a team.
Roots know how to enter both stone and soil.
A gentle appearance is not the same thing as a weak position.
I like watching an unassuming teammate reveal exactly what it can do.

contexts.subject: Tina realizes the attention she noticed was directed at Erika.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_TinaPostBattle.text: Oh, you were looking at ERIKA…\nYou weren't looking at me…$

replies.text: The misunderstanding has left the conversation very carefully through a side door.
We should not turn an awkward realization into a public investigation.
No need to make her feel worse. We can leave it there.
I would like everyone to look somewhere neutral until this feeling passes.
A little kindness will do more than trying to explain every glance.
An imagined subplot has been cancelled in front of its hopeful author.
I am going to study this completely unremarkable patch of floor.
A mistaken observation. No need to make her defend it.
Some small hopes arrive before anyone has invited them.
We can spare her the little laugh she is probably expecting.
Not every awkward moment needs to become a story we keep telling.

contexts.subject: Tamia says Grass Pokemon also help the Gym make flower arrangements.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_TamiaPostBattle.text: We only use GRASS-type POKéMON at\nour GYM.\pWhy? We also use them for making\nflower arrangements!$

replies.text: The team does battles and centerpieces. I have been dramatically underusing my hobbies.
A shared interest connects their training with something creative outside it.
Good to know the team gets to do more together than fight.
I like imagining the room after practice, when everyone makes something quiet.
Growing things and arranging them together sounds like a pleasant afternoon.
The ensemble handles both combat and the set decoration.
A Gym with a peaceful use for all that enthusiasm. I approve.
I would be interested in how the different Pokemon contribute to the work.
The garden is allowed to be both strong and beautiful.
Finally, someone understands that an arrangement can have a personality.
I would like to see an unfinished one, with the team deciding what belongs where.

contexts.subject: Lisa says Erika is quiet but well known locally.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_LisaPostBattle.text: Our LEADER ERIKA might be quiet,\nbut she's famous around here.$

replies.text: Quiet and famous. An excellent strategy for making everybody else handle the announcements.
Public influence does not require speaking more than everyone around you.
She lets her work establish who she is. Nothing wrong with that.
I like knowing a quiet person does not have to become louder to be taken seriously.
People remember how you make a place feel, too.
A leading role need not be played at maximum volume.
A comforting career possibility for those of us suspicious of introductions.
A reputation is a result of sustained work, not merely the noise around it.
A soft voice can still be the one a room listens for.
She has a presence that does not need to keep asking for attention.
I would rather catch an ordinary moment with her than make her perform being famous.

contexts.subject: Lori wants to improve her manners before a blind date, including if it involves battling.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_LoriPostBattle.text: I have a blind date coming up.\nI have to learn to be polite,\lespecially if I have to battle.$

replies.text: Battle etiquette for a date. I had only prepared how to share the bread basket.
Courtesy under competition is useful. I hope the date is not primarily an examination.
Treat them well whether you win or lose. That is a good place to start.
If the date requires battling, I would like to know before choosing what to wear.
Listening and being kind are easier to remember than an elaborate performance.
The romantic subplot comes with a contingency plan for competitive combat.
I had not considered bringing a battle strategy. My social anxiety is taking notes.
A little preparation helps. Trying to script the entire meeting probably will not.
A stranger may become familiar faster over kindness than victory.
Manners help. So does arriving as someone you can keep being after the first hour.
I hope she gets to enjoy meeting them instead of only checking how she is doing.

contexts.subject: Mary says she did not bring her best Pokemon and promises a stronger next battle.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_MaryPostBattle.text: I didn't bring my best POKéMON.\nWait until next time!$

replies.text: The best team was unavailable. A very popular explanation among today's defeated teams.
A different team may change the next result. It does not change this one.
We will take the next challenge seriously when she brings it.
I hope the Pokemon beside her do not hear that as being the disappointing ones.
This team did its best today. They deserve care before comparisons.
An unfavorable premiere has prompted a promise to replace the cast.
The invisible better team remains undefeated. Impressive record.
Then the next test will involve different conditions. We should prepare rather than argue.
The creatures who came with her are still the ones waiting for kindness now.
A better team begins with treating the current one as worth her attention.
I would like to see what she learns before the next meeting, not only who she brings.

contexts.subject: Kayden praises our combination of strength and thought but is surprised by a young trainer.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_KaydenPostBattle.text: So, you mix brawn with brains?\nGood strategy!\pThat's remarkable for a trainer\nTRAINER.$

replies.text: Brawn and brains. I contribute a third quality: standing somewhere inconvenient.
He noticed the decisions behind the power. The surprise about age is less useful.
You used what the team could do well. That is worth recognizing.
I like being noticed for thinking, even when somebody sounds surprised we can.
A good plan gives the team room to use its strengths.
The reviewer has noticed both the action and the rather important work behind it.
A compliment that almost made it to the end without expressing surprise at our existence.
Force and planning are complementary. Neither excuses ignoring the other.
A strong arm still needs to know what it is reaching for.
Keep the useful praise. The surprised tone can stay with him.
I would like to know which choice made him stop and reconsider us.

contexts.subject: Kirk will keep training under Koga teachings after losing.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_KirkPostBattle.text: Even though I've lost, I will keep\ntraining according to the teachings\lof KOGA, my ninja master.$

replies.text: He still has a teacher and tomorrow. Losing has not cancelled either.
A consistent method can help, provided he reviews what this battle exposed.
Keep training. Just leave room to change what did not work.
It helps to have somewhere to return with the mistakes you want to understand.
I hope the next lesson includes giving the team a proper rest.
A loyal student has placed the defeat inside a longer course of study.
Devotion is useful when it leaves room for an inconvenient question.
Test the method against the result. Loyalty does not require ignoring data.
A teaching can be a path without becoming a cage.
It is nice to have a practice you still believe in on a bad day.
I wonder what Koga will ask him about this battle when he describes it.

contexts.subject: Nate likes poison and sleep because their effects outlast the battle.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_NatePostBattle.text: I like poison and sleep techniques,\nas they linger after battle!$

replies.text: An attack that follows you home. A particularly unwelcome souvenir.
Persistent effects make recovery supplies important beyond the immediate battle.
Check the team afterward. Winning does not automatically make everyone well.
I dislike the part where the fight can be over and someone is still hurting.
We should tend to any lingering condition before continuing.
The antagonist enjoys an effect that ignores the closing curtain.
A memorable impression. Unfortunately, the medical sort.
Post-battle state matters. We should inspect it instead of assuming the reset is complete.
Some harms remain after the noise stops. Notice them.
I prefer a battle that ends when both sides agree it has ended.
I will watch how the team is moving afterward, not only whether we won.

contexts.subject: Phil compliments the win and advises looking closely for gaps in the invisible walls.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_PhilPostBattle.text: You impressed me!\nHere's a hint!\pLook very closely for gaps in the\ninvisible walls!$

replies.text: Look closely at the invisible thing. A hint with an ambitious relationship to eyesight.
The gaps are the useful detail. We can test the route systematically.
Slow down and follow the boundary. Guessing wildly will take longer.
I would like to draw the path as we learn it. It is easy to forget what we cannot see.
Let us avoid sending a teammate into each wall just to find the way.
The scenery is concealed, but the exit apparently has visible intentions.
I will stare at the air with renewed purpose.
Map the obstruction, then identify the breaks. Unseen does not mean unmeasurable.
Even a hidden wall must leave room for a path.
A patient look costs less than another bruised shoulder.
I am watching where people actually walk. That may tell us more than the empty-looking room.

contexts.subject: Edgar admits he still has a great deal to learn.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_EdgarPostBattle.text: I still have much to learn.$

replies.text: A short sentence with a whole useful future inside it.
Recognizing what is unknown is a good beginning, not an embarrassment.
He can start with this battle. One thing to change is enough for today.
It is good when you can say that without having to sound ashamed.
I hope he is as patient with himself as he would be with a new Pokemon.
An honest closing line leaves the next chapter open.
I trust that more than a speech explaining why the result does not count.
Now identify the first question. A vague gap becomes manageable when it is specific.
An open hand can receive more than a clenched one.
He did not turn the admission into an excuse or an insult. I like that.
I would ask what surprised him most. That is often where the next lesson begins.

contexts.subject: Shawn asks whether we choose light or shadow.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_ShawnPostBattle.text: Where there is light, there is\nshadow!\pLight and shadow!\nWhich do you choose?$

replies.text: I choose whichever contains the exit and preferably a chair.
Those are not independent options. A shadow depends on a light source.
Depends what we need. Shade is useful on a hot day.
A little shade can feel kind. I do not think it needs to become a declaration.
I choose a place where the team can rest comfortably.
A dramatic either-or has encountered the practical appeal of sitting under a tree.
Shadow, if this is about where I have to stand for the rest of the conversation.
Could he specify the task? The correct lighting depends on what we are trying to do.
I prefer the place they meet. Edges reveal things.
Both belong in a good room. One makes the other interesting.
Light shows the face. Shadow gives it shape. I would not want to lose either.

contexts.subject: Blaine recommends teaching Fire Blast to a Fire Pokemon such as Vulpix or Charmeleon.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_BlainePostBattle.text: TM38 contains FIRE BLAST.\nTeach it to FIRE-type POKéMON.\pVULPIX or CHARMELEON would be\nideal for that move.$

replies.text: Fire Blast. A name that has not wasted anybody's time wondering what it does.
His examples are sensible. We should still check the recipient's current moves before teaching it.
Choose someone who can use it well. A strong move is not automatically the right replacement.
I would like to admire the demonstration from somewhere with very little dry grass.
Let us decide with the whole team's needs in mind.
The gift arrives with casting suggestions and a distinctly unsubtle stage effect.
I appreciate being told the fire is going to be a blast before meeting it personally.
A high-output option. Compatibility and the rest of the moveset still matter.
A fierce flame asks for a hand that knows how to guide it.
A dramatic move deserves a thoughtful choice of who gets it.
I would want to see how the chosen teammate makes that power its own.

contexts.subject: Erik begins explaining oxygen and combustion before trailing into blah blah.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_ErikPostBattle.text: Fire, or to be more precise,\ncombustion…\p…Oxygen in the air…\nBlah, blah, blah, blah…$

replies.text: The fire needed oxygen. The explanation eventually needed an ending.
He had a real explanation before abandoning it to sound effects. I would have listened.
If there is a useful point, he can make it without holding us here all afternoon.
I feel bad when someone stops expecting people to listen halfway through a thought.
A shorter explanation might give the interesting part room to land.
A promising opening paragraph has been swallowed by its own placeholder text.
He reached the scientific term for the moment my attention left the room.
Oxygen was relevant. I was waiting for the rest of the mechanism.
A fire needs air. A thought needs someone willing to finish tending it.
Editing is an act of kindness to the person standing in front of you.
I would ask one specific question. It might help him find the part he actually wants to tell us.

contexts.subject: Quinn admits wanting to steal other people Pokemon.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_QuinnPostBattle.text: I get this uncontrollable urge to\nsteal other people's POKéMON.$

replies.text: Wanting a Pokemon is not a permission slip to take somebody else's partner.
An urge is something he is responsible for managing, not an instruction the rest of us must accept.
Keep the team close. We do not owe him a chance to prove he means it.
I do not like hearing someone talk about another person's companion that way.
A Pokemon is not a prize he gets to take because he wants one.
A troubling confession has arrived with rather too little concern for its intended victims.
I am suddenly more interested in keeping our belongings and partners beside us.
He needs a way to interrupt that behavior before anyone is harmed.
Desire does not undo another creature's home.
There are ordinary ways to meet a Pokemon. Theft does not become charming because he admits it.
I would rather leave than give him more details about our team.

contexts.subject: Avery claims his theories are too complicated for us to understand.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_AveryPostBattle.text: My theories are too complicated\nfor you to understand.$

replies.text: An impressive theory. Apparently its greatest defense is refusing to explain it.
An explanation is part of the work. Complexity alone does not establish correctness.
If he will not explain, we are allowed to stop asking.
Not understanding a bad explanation does not make us incapable of learning.
He could start with one small part if he actually wanted to share it.
A grand manuscript has been protected from criticism by withholding every page.
I have never met such carefully guarded evidence of being clever.
Then identify the prerequisite and begin there. Otherwise this is only a claim about us.
A locked box can hold a treasure or nothing. The lock does not tell us which.
A little mystery can be stylish. Condescension is harder to accessorize.
I would rather hear him explain one thing well than tell us how much we cannot know.

contexts.subject: Ramon wishes for a thief Pokemon he could use.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_RamonPostBattle.text: I wish there were a thief POKéMON.\nI'd use that!$

replies.text: A Pokemon is not a way to outsource being responsible for stealing.
Training another creature to carry out the act would not remove his responsibility for it.
A partner deserves a better ambition than becoming his excuse.
I hope he finds something kinder to be excited about teaching.
A good teammate is somebody you care for, not somebody you send to take things for you.
He would like an accomplice written as a convenient special ability.
A career plan that becomes worse when he starts recruiting.
The tool does not change the purpose of the task. He is still describing theft.
A creature follows the path we teach. That is a reason to choose the path carefully.
Wanting a partner should begin with what he can offer it, too.
I wonder whether he has ever pictured the person waiting for the stolen Pokemon to come home.

contexts.subject: Derek tells how a fiery bird helped the lost Blaine descend a mountain at night.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_DerekPostBattle.text:
Our LEADER, BLAINE, became lost
in the mountains but good.\pNight fell when a fiery bird
POKéMON appeared.\pIts light allowed BLAINE to find
his way down safely.$

replies.text: A bird became the emergency lantern. I hope Blaine sent a very large thank-you.
That is an extraordinary account. I would like to hear which details Blaine remembers directly.
Something helped him find a safe way down. That is the important part.
Seeing a light when you thought you were alone must have stayed with him.
I hope he has given other lost people that same feeling of relief since then.
A life-changing encounter arrived as a light in a scene that had nearly lost its way.
A quiet reason to care about a fierce kind of Pokemon. I like that.
I would ask about the route, the conditions, and what the light revealed.
A flame on the mountain became a path home.
I can see why that story would matter more than any ordinary winning battle.
I would rather hear him remember it than try to turn it into a spectacle for us.

contexts.subject: Dusty names Ponyta and Ninetales as popular Fire Pokemon.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_DustyPostBattle.text: PONYTA, NINETALES…\nThose are popular FIRE POKéMON.$

replies.text: Popular and warm. A dangerous combination when everyone wants to hug you.
Both are memorable examples. Their individual needs differ considerably.
Popularity is not a care guide. Learn about the partner before choosing one.
I can understand why people notice them. I would still want to know their quieter habits.
A beautiful Pokemon also needs somebody who likes the everyday work of looking after it.
Two impressive candidates with excellent silhouettes and a rather demanding heating department.
I admire them from the distance recommended for clothing that is not fireproof.
Their appearance is familiar. Housing and handling would require a more detailed plan.
A flame can be admired without being asked to belong to us.
They are striking. I hope people admire the actual creatures, not only the idea of looking impressive beside one.
I would love to see the way their fire moves when they are relaxed.

contexts.subject: Zac explains Water beats Fire while Fire beats Ice.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_ZacPostBattle.text: Water beats fire, of course.\pBut fire melts ice, so the FIRE\ntype beats ICE-type POKéMON.$

replies.text: Every dramatic element has somebody else arriving with a very practical objection.
A favorable matchup in one direction does not remove a weakness in another.
Know both sides of the matchup. Nobody gets to be strong against everything.
It helps to think about who needs support rather than only who looks strongest.
A teammate can be brilliant at one job and need help with the next.
The cast of elements has developed an admirably balanced schedule of rivalries.
Even fire has situations where it would rather not be the center of attention.
Matchups are relationships, not a single ranking from best to worst.
What melts one barrier can be quieted by another.
A weakness does not erase a strength. It tells us where a partner might help.
I like seeing how different teammates make room for each other's difficult matchups.

contexts.subject: Amanda says equal opponents are separated by will and urges focus against Sabrina.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_AmandaPostBattle.text: In a battle of equals, the one\nwith the stronger will wins.\pIf you wish to beat SABRINA, focus\nand will yourself to victory.$

replies.text: Focus helps. I would still like a plan that works even when my eyebrows stop looking determined.
Concentration matters, but equal strength does not make every other variable disappear.
Keep your attention on the battle. You do not need to turn losing into a failure of character.
I hope she means staying present, not being angry at yourself for feeling afraid.
Determination works better when the team is rested and trusts the plan.
A forceful inner monologue still needs an actual next move.
I have been willing myself to win for years. It occasionally requires supplementary practice.
Focus is useful. Preparation and information remain useful even when motivation is high.
A steady flame still needs fuel. Will alone is not everything.
You can want it fiercely and still deserve kindness if it goes badly.
I would watch the decisions that focus makes possible, rather than try to measure the feeling itself.

contexts.subject: Johan claims Psychic Pokemon fear only Ghosts and Bugs.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_JohanPostBattle.text: PSYCHIC POKéMON fear only ghosts\nand bugs!$

replies.text: Only ghosts and bugs? His list sounds rather more confident than complete.
That advice leaves out the Dark matchup. We should use the current type chart, not his certainty.
Remember Dark moves, too. Do not build a team from one trainer's incomplete list.
A frightening reputation can make people stop checking the details.
There are more options than he mentioned. We can choose what suits our own team.
The declaration has omitted an entire dark corner of the cast.
His explanation seems to have a weakness of its own.
An incomplete specification can still sound authoritative. Verify the matchups.
He has named two shadows and missed the darkness between them.
Confidence is not a substitute for remembering the rest of the list.
I would rather check what our teammates can actually do than let that narrow our choices.

contexts.subject: Stacy wants to master Psychic and teach it to her Pokemon.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_StacyPostBattle.text: I have much to learn still…\pI must master PSYCHIC and teach it\nto my POKéMON…$

replies.text: A learning project for the whole team. I hope she does not assign them all the same homework.
Understanding a move and choosing which partner benefits from it are separate tasks.
Keep learning. Make sure the move suits the Pokemon, too.
I like hearing a next step that sounds possible instead of just promising never to lose again.
The team can learn with her, at a pace that leaves room for mistakes.
The lesson continues after the scene ends. A useful kind of unfinished business.
A concrete goal is easier to live with than the instruction to become generally perfect.
One specific technique gives her something measurable to practice.
A thought becomes a path when it names the next step.
I hope she notices what each partner brings to the lesson, too.
I would be interested to see what changes when she tries it again.

contexts.subject: Tyron says Sabrina decisively defeated the neighboring Karate Master.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_TyronPostBattle.text: SABRINA just wiped out the KARATE\nMASTER next door.$

replies.text: The neighbor lost very thoroughly. I hope that is not how every conversation between the buildings begins.
That matchup favors her specialty. It is not a complete judgment on his training.
He lost a battle. No need to keep making it a public humiliation.
I wonder whether the neighbors can still speak without somebody bringing up the result.
A strong community needs more than the winner feeling important.
A local rivalry has acquired a narrator who greatly prefers one ending.
A victory with apparently unlimited retelling rights.
The result is useful matchup information. The contempt is not.
Two doors can remain beside each other long after the contest ends.
I would rather know what each place teaches than hear which one is allowed to feel superior.
I wonder what the same afternoon looked like from the other doorway.

contexts.subject: Tasha claims she knew the defeat would happen.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_TashaPostBattle.text: I knew that this was going to take\nplace.$

replies.text: She predicted it. I am impressed by how reliably predictions arrive after the event.
A prediction recorded beforehand would be easier to evaluate.
Then she could have warned her team a little more usefully.
Maybe knowing would not make a difficult moment feel any easier.
I hope the team still gets comfort instead of being told it was inevitable.
The defeated prophet has added a retrospective footnote to the script.
An undefeated record of explaining losses after they happen.
That claim does not tell us what she expected or when.
Even an expected rain can leave someone wet.
I would like to see the prediction before accepting the excellent timing.
I wonder whether that is certainty or a way of feeling less caught off guard.

contexts.subject: Cameron boasts the Psychic Gym defeated the dojo and removed its Gym status.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_CameronPostBattle.text:
There used to be two POKéMON GYMS
in SAFFRON.\pThe FIGHTING DOJO next door lost
its GYM status, though.\pWe simply creamed them when we
decided to have just one GYM.$

replies.text: Two schools became one official Gym and one very long-running brag.
Winning a contest determined the title. It did not erase the dojo's ability to teach.
They can be proud without treating the neighbors as worthless.
I hope the people next door still feel they belong in their own town.
There ought to be room for both groups to care about their Pokemon.
An institutional rivalry has been edited into an unnecessarily triumphant anecdote.
An official title is useful. It is not the only proof that a place matters.
Different training methods can remain valuable after an administrative decision.
A sign was taken down. The lives behind the door remained.
I would rather see what survives in both schools than join a victory lap over the loss.
I want to hear the dojo's version before letting that become the whole history.

contexts.subject: Preston says he used telepathy to read our mind.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_PrestonPostBattle.text: That's right! I used telepathy to\nread your mind!$

replies.text: Then he knows where I left the thought I was having. Please ask.
A claim about private information needs more than an announcement.
He can keep out of our heads. The conversation works fine out here.
I would prefer he asked before looking, if that is something he can do.
Being able to learn something does not make it kind to take it.
An intrusive narrator announces access to the unpublished draft.
My condolences to him. I have been living in there for years.
I would propose a blinded test before accepting that result.
A mind is still someone's room, even if the door is easy to open.
I would like my private thoughts to remain an invitation, not an open service.
Did he notice what we were thinking, or only what he expected us to think?

contexts.subject: Yuji warns that keeping up with his leader requires power.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_YujiPostBattle.text: You'll need power to keep up with\nour GYM LEADER.$

replies.text: We brought power. I would like to bring a little planning along as well.
Power is one requirement. A good matchup may change how much of it we need.
We will prepare. We do not have to rush because he sounds certain.
I would rather hear what makes the leader difficult than another warning about strength.
Let us make sure the team is well enough to use the strength it has.
The penultimate opponent has issued the traditional warning about the main attraction.
I will add power to the list, immediately beneath not panicking.
Then check our resources and matchups. A warning should lead to a practical response.
A heavy door still opens on the right hinge.
We can take him seriously without accepting that only brute force will work.
I wonder what he has seen challengers do wrong against the leader.

contexts.subject: Atsushi calls himself unworthy after losing.

replies.text: He lost a battle. That is a result, not a certificate about his entire existence.
Worth is not a statistic this contest can measure. The battle can still teach him something.
He needs a correction to the plan, not a reason to hate himself.
I know how quickly a mistake can grow into that word. It still is not the truth.
I hope he speaks to his team more kindly than he is speaking to himself.
One unfavorable scene has been mistaken for the verdict on the whole character.
A cruel narrator lives in that sentence. He need not keep giving it the pen.
Review the failure specifically. A vague judgment cannot be repaired.
A bowed branch is not a worthless tree.
He deserves a next attempt without having to earn the right to matter first.
I would ask what he wants to improve when he is ready to say something gentler.

contexts.subject: Jason asks whether we know the Gym Leader identity.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_JasonPostBattle.text: Do you know the identity of our\nGYM LEADER?$

replies.text: An identity quiz inside a Gym. Most places settle for a sign.
He has a specific person in mind. We should see who is actually here rather than speculate.
We will find out. Keep your attention on the room.
The way he asked makes the answer feel less ordinary than it should.
I would rather know how the leader treats people than only learn a name.
A mysterious final entrance is being promoted by its own supporting cast.
I dislike a workplace that treats the manager's name as a dramatic reveal.
The room contains a testable answer. We do not need a theory yet.
A hidden name still belongs to a real person. Soon we will meet them.
An introduction should not require this much suspense.
I am watching how people react when they mention him. That may tell us more than the name.

contexts.subject: Kiyo wishes his Pokemon were as good at karate as he is.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_KiyoPostBattle.text: If my POKéMON were as good at\nkarate as I…$

replies.text: His Pokemon have been asked to explain a result their trainer has already excused himself from.
Teaching requires adapting the method to the learner, not comparing them unfavorably with oneself.
Then he should help them learn. Blaming the team will not do it.
I hope they know he still values what they can do in their own way.
A good teacher notices the student's needs before admiring his own skill.
The instructor has written an excellent review of himself and a poor one of his entire cast.
A shame his own technique did not include a way to teach it.
A skill is not transferred merely by demonstrating how pleased you are with having it.
Their bodies have their own ways of finding strength. He should learn those, too.
The team deserves more than being the place he puts his disappointment.
I would rather see what he changes in the next practice than hear another comparison.

contexts.subject: Warren worries his leader will scold him for losing.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_WarrenPostBattle.text: The LEADER will scold me for\nlosing this way…$

replies.text: I hope the lesson is about the battle, not about making him afraid to return.
Fear of reporting failure makes accurate learning harder. That is poor leadership.
He should be able to discuss a loss without expecting humiliation.
The way he said that makes this room feel smaller.
I hope his team gets comfort rather than having the fear passed down to them.
An ordinary defeat has become a scene he is afraid to take back to his own director.
That is a miserable thing to be thinking about while your team needs you.
A useful review identifies what to change. Scolding alone does not.
A place of learning should not make the path back feel dangerous.
He sounds worried about more than a lost match. I do not like that.
I wonder what he would say about the battle if he were not afraid of the listener.

contexts.subject: Takashi mocks our intention to challenge the League.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_TakashiPostBattle.text: The POKéMON LEAGUE?\nYou? Don't get cocky!$

replies.text: The League has not rejected us. Its unofficial grumbling department has concerns.
His disbelief is not part of the entrance requirements.
We know what we are working toward. He does not need to approve.
A dream can be spoken quietly and still be serious.
We can keep preparing without making the whole journey an answer to him.
An unsuccessful obstacle would like editorial control over the ending.
He has mistaken the right to comment for the power to stop us.
Check the actual requirements. His prediction is not a substitute for them.
A dismissive voice is not a gate.
Ambition is not automatically arrogance just because he dislikes hearing it.
I would rather remember who helped us get there than who said we could not.

contexts.subject: Cole insists his loss was only carelessness.

replies.text: Carelessness is apparently a separate trainer who arrived and lost on his behalf.
If he can identify the careless decision, he has something concrete to improve.
Then learn from it. The result still stands.
I hope he finds the useful part instead of getting stuck defending himself.
The team needs care now, not another explanation of why the loss should not count.
An unfavorable review has been attributed to a temporary lapse in the production.
A popular explanation with very little practical advice attached.
A specific error can be corrected. The label alone is not a correction.
A loose step is still a step that happened. We can choose the next more carefully.
He can keep his pride and still admit we did something well.
I would ask which moment he would change. That answer might actually tell us something.

contexts.subject: Samuel says beating the leader is required to reach the League.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_SamuelPostBattle.text: You can go on to the POKéMON\nLEAGUE only by defeating our GYM\lLEADER!$

replies.text: One more leader between us and the League. A very serious item on the to-do list.
We should confirm the badge requirement and prepare for the actual opponent ahead.
Then we finish this properly. Check the team first.
It feels different hearing the last step described as something in the next room.
Let us take the time the team needs. The goal will still be there after a rest.
The final local gate has a name and a battle waiting behind it.
Almost there is still a place where we are allowed to breathe.
A clear remaining condition. We should not mistake closeness for completion.
The last door deserves the same care as the first.
We have come too far to treat preparation as an inconvenience now.
I want to remember who we are before the next door opens.

contexts.subject: Giovanni promises to disband Rocket, says he will train again, and leaves.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_GiovanniPostBattle.text:
Having lost in this fashion, 
I can't face my followers.\lI have betrayed their trust.\pAs of today, TEAM ROCKET is
finished forever!\pAs for myself, I shall dedicate
my life to training again.\pLet us meet again someday!
Farewell!$

replies.text: I hope he means the part about leaving people alone. They have earned some ordinary, boring days.
He has made a significant promise. What follows will matter more than the declaration.
Let him leave. The people he hurt deserve safety, not another speech.
I keep thinking about everyone who can finally stop watching the door.
I hope the people and Pokemon he harmed get time to recover.
A powerful man has given himself an ending. The people behind him still have lives to rebuild.
I would like his next ambition to involve considerably fewer stolen companions.
A stated shutdown is not the same as every part stopping. We should stay observant.
A shadow moving away leaves things visible that still need tending.
He can choose a new life. The people he hurt should get that freedom, too.
I would rather remember the people who stood up to him than turn his exit into the whole story.

contexts.subject: Sabrina says everyone has psychic power without realizing it.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_SabrinaPostBattle.text: Psychic power isn't something that\nonly a few people have.\pEveryone has psychic power.\nPeople just don't realize it.$

replies.text: Then mine has been hiding with the thought I forgot on the way into this room.
An interesting claim. I would like to know how she distinguishes unused power from no measurable power.
Maybe. I would still rather do the work than wait for a hidden talent to solve everything.
I wonder what it feels like before you know how to name it.
I hope people hear a possibility, not another thing they are supposed to prove about themselves.
The audience has unexpectedly been invited to audition for the impossible.
Mine has shown remarkable restraint during every embarrassing conversation of my life.
I would ask what a beginner can actually observe and repeat. That gives the claim somewhere to start.
Some quiet abilities do wait a long time for a name.
It is a lovely possibility. I do not want anyone feeling ordinary as a result to feel defective.
I would ask her about the first moment she realized something unusual was happening.

contexts.subject: Koga introduces Toxic as a secret technique passed down for centuries.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_KogaExplainTM06.text: Sealed within that TM06 lies\nTOXIC!\pIt is a secret technique dating\nback some four hundred years.$

replies.text: Four hundred years of practice making somebody have a worse afternoon. An impressive, troubling tradition.
A long history can preserve expertise. We should still understand the technique before using it.
Old does not mean harmless. Learn what it does and how to treat it.
I wonder how a secret feels after being handed to a stranger in a disc.
We should keep remedies ready for effects we choose to bring into a battle.
A centuries-old secret has reached the convenient gift-counter stage of its career.
An ancient legacy of being deeply unpleasant to the opposing team.
I am curious which parts of the method changed over those centuries.
A long-kept secret still asks us what we will do with it now.
A tradition deserves thought, not automatic admiration for its age.
I would like to hear who taught him, and what they wanted him to remember besides winning.

contexts.subject: Koga explains that Toxic poison damage worsens as a battle continues.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_KogaPostBattle.text: When afflicted by TOXIC, a POKéMON\nsuffers more and more.\pIt suffers worsening damage as the\nbattle wears on!\pIt will surely terrorize foes!$

replies.text: That is a very unpleasant clock to leave running. We should know where the antidotes are.
Its pressure increases with time. A slow plan needs a way to address that.
Do not ignore a poisoned teammate while waiting for the perfect move.
It makes every extra moment feel expensive. I understand why people find him frightening.
We will look after the team promptly. Nobody should be left hurting because the battle is exciting.
The technique makes delay into an opponent of its own.
A steadily worsening situation. I prefer those in fiction, where I can close the book.
The cost is cumulative. Planning only around the first tick will underestimate it.
A small harm can become a large one when nobody tends it.
I would rather remember the remedy as clearly as the threat.
I will keep watching the team after a battle with that kind of pressure.

contexts.subject: Erika explains Giga Drain heals the user for half the damage inflicted.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_ExplainTM19.text: TM19 contains GIGA DRAIN.\pHalf the damage it inflicts is\ndrained to heal your POKéMON.\pWouldn't you agree that it's a\nwonderful move?$

replies.text: Hit them and feel better. I have been trying that with pillows and getting much poorer results.
Damage and recovery are linked, so the target and the actual damage both affect the benefit.
Useful staying power. Do not assume it replaces proper healing.
It changes the feeling of an attack when it also gives our teammate a little room to recover.
A helpful move, though the team should still get rest between battles.
The action scene contributes directly to the performer's recovery budget.
An efficient move with a considerably less charming description from the other side.
Recovery scales with output. It will not provide the same return in every matchup.
Taking and restoring meet in one motion. We should use that strength thoughtfully.
I can see why she likes it. It gives a team more than one useful result.
I would watch how much breathing room it actually gives the teammate using it.

contexts.subject: Surge gives Shock Wave and recommends an Electric Pokemon.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_ExplainTM34.text: TM34 contains SHOCK WAVE!\pTeach it to an ELECTRIC POKéMON!$

replies.text: A little bottled thunder, with considerably less bottle than I expected.
Check who can learn Shock Wave and whether it improves their present options.
Pick the right teammate before using the TM.
I would like the first demonstration to happen somewhere less full of metal bins.
A useful gift. We should choose who needs it rather than simply who is nearest.
The loud commander has sent us away with a compact version of his favorite noise.
I support keeping the thunder on the team list and out of my pockets.
The recommendation narrows the candidates. Compatibility still needs checking.
A storm can become a lesson when somebody knows how to guide it.
A strong signature move should suit the Pokemon learning it, too.
I like seeing which part of a leader's style they choose to pass on.

contexts.subject: Sabrina explains Calm Mind raises Special Attack and Special Defense.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_ExplainTM04.text: TM04 is CALM MIND.\pIt makes the POKéMON concentrate\nto raise both SP. ATK and SP. DEF.$

replies.text: A calmer mind becomes stronger. I would like mine to stop organizing imaginary emergencies first.
The same preparation improves both special offense and special defense. Timing remains important.
Give it a safe turn to prepare. Calm is easier when the plan makes room for it.
I like a move that treats quiet as something powerful.
Taking time to settle can be part of caring for the team, too.
A moment of stillness changes both what the performer can give and what they can withstand.
A battle move that rewards not immediately doing the loudest thing available. Promising.
Two useful properties improve together. Choose someone who benefits from both.
Still water can hold more than the surface suggests.
Composure can protect someone as much as it impresses the room.
I would watch the difference in the next few turns, not only the quiet moment itself.

contexts.subject: Giovanni gives Earthquake and recalls making it during his earlier time at the Gym.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_ExplainTM26.text: TM26 contains EARTHQUAKE.\pIt is a powerful attack that causes\na massive tremor.\pI made it when I ran the GYM here,\nfar too long ago… $

replies.text: He made a move that shakes the ground. An unusually literal way to leave a mark on a place.
A powerful technique from an earlier part of his life. We should understand its reach before using it.
A strong gift does not erase what we know about him. Use our own judgment with it.
It is strange hearing him remember a quieter part of his life.
The move is ours to use responsibly now. That choice belongs to us.
An old chapter has survived inside the object he is handing us.
People leave complicated things behind. We do not need to inherit the rest of his choices.
I would check the targeting before a double battle. A broad effect needs careful planning.
The earth carries an old lesson without choosing the person who learns it next.
A gift can be useful without buying forgiveness.
I wonder what he remembers when he thinks of this room before everything else happened.

contexts.subject: The guide warns about Electric matchups, paralysis and Surge locked door.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyAdvice.text:
Yo!
Champ in the making!\pLT. SURGE has a nickname.\pPeople refer to him as the
Lightning American!\pHe's an expert on electric
POKéMON.\pBIRD/WATER-type POKéMON match
poorly against the ELECTRIC type.\pBeware of paralysis, too.\pLT. SURGE is very cautious.\pHe's locked himself in, so it won't
be easy getting to him.$

replies.text: Strong electricity, paralysis, and a locked door. The welcome brochure has become a threat assessment.
Avoid the poor matchups, prepare for paralysis, and solve access separately from the battle.
Check the team's condition and our remedies before starting.
Knowing what can go wrong is better than being surprised by every part of it.
I would like everyone comfortable before we go searching the bins.
A tactical briefing has doubled as a warning about the building's hostility to visitors.
I came prepared for a battle. The rubbish puzzle was an unexpected social obligation.
Type disadvantage, status risk, physical barrier. Three separate problems to prepare for.
A storm and a locked gate ask for different kinds of patience.
The advice helps. I still wish the door were less interested in proving a point.
I would watch how the staff pass through the room before assuming every barrier is obvious.

contexts.subject: The guide calls the victory electric.

replies.text: Electric! I am choosing to celebrate from a respectful distance from the wiring.
A good result. Let us check the team before enjoying it too loudly.
We did it. Time to get everyone healed.
I can finally stop thinking about where all the electricity might be going.
A win feels better once we know everyone is all right.
The critic has summarized an entire battle in the building's preferred adjective.
A charged review. I am carefully resisting the rest of that joke.
The team passed the test. The doors are somebody else's problem for a while.
The thunder has passed. We can hear ourselves again.
You earned the moment. Let yourself enjoy it before packing for the next one.
His excitement makes it feel like someone was waiting for our good news.

contexts.subject: The guide explains invisible walls and the need to find gaps to reach Koga.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyAdvice.text:
Yo!
Champ in the making!\pFUCHSIA GYM is a tricked-up place.
It's riddled with invisible walls!\pKOGA might appear close, but he's
blocked off.\pYou have to find gaps in the walls
to reach him.$

replies.text: The walls are invisible. I was prepared to be lost, but not aesthetically.
The apparent distance is misleading. We need to map the actual accessible path.
Move slowly and remember what blocks us. Do not keep testing the same wall.
I would like to sketch the route once we understand it.
We can take our time. Nobody needs a bruised nose as part of the challenge.
The leader is visible, the scenery is not, and the audience is expected to applaud the distinction.
A room designed by someone who enjoys watching people apologize to empty air.
Treat the collisions as boundary data. Then trace the gaps.
What we cannot see still changes where we can go.
I prefer a visible obstacle. At least it has the courtesy to announce itself.
I am looking at people's routes rather than the empty-looking spaces.

contexts.subject: The guide remarks that ninjas remain terrifying even now.

FuchsiaCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyPostVictory.text: It's amazing how ninja can terrify,\neven now!$

replies.text: Terrifying, yes. Also surprisingly committed to inconvenient interior design.
Preparation and concealed information can create an intimidating advantage.
He is skilled. We still found a way through.
I would like the next quiet room to be quiet for less tactical reasons.
Let us make sure the team is well after all those lingering effects.
The ninja has impressed the audience and given the cleaning staff a difficult floor plan.
The frightening part is over. I would now like to discover a chair that is visible.
