Good concealment makes the unfamiliar feel more dangerous. Understanding it helped.
A hidden path becomes less frightening once our feet know it.
I can respect the skill while preferring a more straightforward welcome.
I would remember the little signs that helped us find our way despite the fear.

contexts.subject: The guide warns Fighting Pokemon about Sabrina Psychic team.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyAdvice.text:
Yo!
Champ in the making!\pSABRINA's POKéMON use psychic
power instead of force.\pFIGHTING POKéMON are especially
weak against PSYCHIC POKéMON.\pThey'll get destroyed before they
can even aim a punch!$

replies.text: The warning is vivid. Our Fighting teammates would prefer a plan to becoming the example.
That is a poor matchup. We should choose a lead suited to the actual opponent.
Keep the vulnerable teammate out of that situation. There are other ways to use their strength.
I am glad we heard it before somebody had to learn by getting hurt.
A partner can sit out a bad matchup without being less valuable to the team.
A promising action scene has been correctly rejected at the planning stage.
I appreciate advice that arrives before the dramatic mistake rather than after it.
Do not test a known vulnerability just because a teammate is strong in other situations.
A fist need not answer every question.
A good team lets different partners handle the rooms that suit them.
I will watch for what changes when we choose a different kind of approach.

contexts.subject: The guide imagines using psychic powers to win money at slot machines.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyPostVictory.text: Psychic power, huh?\pIf I had that, I'd make a bundle\nat the slots!$

replies.text: A miracle of the mind, immediately assigned to improving the coin case.
He has jumped from an untested ability to a projected income. Several steps are missing.
Good thing that is still an imaginary budget.
I wonder whether he would still enjoy the game if the uncertainty disappeared.
I would rather he kept money for the journey than trusted a sudden winning theory.
Human potential has reached the grand vision of a very profitable afternoon indoors.
The future of the mind, apparently managed by the nearest slot machine.
I would not fund the plan until the claimed ability passes a test outside the casino.
A glimpse of possibility does not always tell us what is worth wanting.
It is impressive how quickly wonder can become a shopping list.
I would ask what he would do with that power when there was nobody counting coins.

contexts.subject: The guide recommends Water attacks and Burn Heals against Blaine.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_GymGuyAdvice.text:
Yo!
Champ in the making!\pThe hotheaded BLAINE is a FIRE
POKéMON pro.\pDouse his spirits with water!\pYou'd better take some
BURN HEALS, too.$

replies.text: Water for the battle, Burn Heals for the mistakes. A reasonably complete weather forecast.
A useful matchup and a status remedy. We should check quantities before proceeding.
Good advice. Make sure we actually have the remedies he mentioned.
I would rather carry something we never need than wish we had it afterward.
Keeping the team comfortable matters as much as finding a strong attack.
The briefing includes both the action plan and the rather important aftercare.
I have a great deal of respect for advice that includes treating the consequences.
Counter the main hazard and prepare for residual damage. Sensible checklist.
Bring something to soothe the flame as well as something to challenge it.
I like a warning that ends with an actual thing we can do.
We should look after the team between battles instead of letting the excitement rush us onward.

contexts.subject: The guide celebrates defeating Blaine.

replies.text: The firebrand has been beaten. I would like to celebrate somewhere the air is less enthusiastic.
A successful challenge. Check for lingering burns before we leave.
Good fight. The team has earned recovery, not another immediate test.
It is nice to hear the win said plainly after all that heat.
Let us get everyone comfortable, then find something good to eat.
The fiery main attraction has received its final bow for today.
I am pleased with the victory and ready to stop feeling gently toasted.
The objective is complete. Now inspect the team rather than assuming the damage ended with the match.
The fierce part is over. We can let the warmth become gentle again.
You can enjoy this without immediately searching for a harder thing to prove.
I would keep the team together for a moment before we leave this room behind.

contexts.subject: The guide does not know the leader identity but warns about difficulty and Ground Pokemon.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyAdvice.text:
Yo!
Champ in the making!\pEven I don't know the VIRIDIAN
LEADER's identity.\pBut one thing's certain.
This will be the toughest of all\lthe GYM LEADERS.\pAlso, I heard that the TRAINERS
here like GROUND-type POKéMON.$

replies.text: He knows the department, the danger level, and absolutely none of the management.
He separated his uncertainty about the identity from his information about the team. Useful distinction.
Ground Pokemon. Start there, and keep watching what is actually in the room.
I would feel better with an ordinary introduction, but we can prepare without it.
Let us make sure the team is well before meeting someone everyone describes as difficult.
The final local mystery has a tactical briefing but no cast announcement.
Even the adviser has not met the person he is advising us about. Reassuring.
Known specialty, uncertain personnel. Build a flexible plan.
A hidden name still leaves footprints. We can attend to what is here.
I appreciate him saying what he does not know instead of inventing the rest.
I am watching the staff. Their reactions may tell us what the missing name does not.

contexts.subject: The guide is astonished to learn Giovanni was the leader.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_GymGuyPostVictory.text: Blow me away! GIOVANNI was the\nGYM LEADER of VIRIDIAN?$

replies.text: The workplace mystery has become a workplace problem.
That is a significant gap in local oversight. I hope the town learns what happened here.
People deserve to know who had that authority over the Gym.
I wonder how many ordinary days happened in this room without anyone knowing.
I hope the people who trusted this place are given clear answers.
The secret identity has escaped the dramatic scene and entered the staff meeting.
I would have several questions for whoever handles hiring.
We should find out how that information remained hidden from the person greeting every challenger.
The room looks the same. Knowing its story makes it different.
Surprise is understandable. Someone still needs to explain what happens next.
I would rather hear what the town needs now than keep replaying the reveal.

contexts.subject: Brock cannot give the TM because we lack bag space.

PewterCity_Gym_Text_DontHaveRoomForThis.text: You don't have room for this.$

replies.text: We defeated the rocks and were stopped by the contents of a pocket.
The TM has not transferred. We need space before returning.
Sort the bag somewhere safe. We can collect it afterward.
I am glad he is willing to wait while we sort this out.
No need to discard something useful in a hurry. Check the options first.
The victory gift awaits the less celebrated triumph of inventory management.
A whole badge earned, and no room for a very small lesson.
Capacity failed. The reward itself is still available here.
Even a small gift asks for a place to rest.
We can make room thoughtfully instead of abandoning something valuable.
Let us remember to return. It would be easy to leave the gift behind in the excitement.

contexts.subject: Misty asks us to make bag room for her TM.

CeruleanCity_Gym_Text_BetterMakeRoomForT.text: You better make room for this!$

replies.text: Our bag has resisted Water Pulse without even being a type.
We have not received the TM. Clearing a slot is the next practical step.
We will come back. Check what can be stored or used first.
She sounds certain the gift is worth returning for. I do want to remember it.
Let us find a quiet place to sort things instead of spreading them around the pool.
A promising aquatic lesson has been delayed by a rather terrestrial bag problem.
The real final opponent was the thing I packed just in case.
A capacity limit is not a refusal. The transfer can be retried.
A crowded bag can still be rearranged without losing its journey.
I would rather reorganize properly than throw away the wrong thing to be quick.
We should keep a little space for the next unexpected kindness, too.

contexts.subject: Surge tells us to clear space before he can give the TM.

VermilionCity_Gym_Text_MakeRoomInYourBag.text: Yo, kid, make room in your BAG!$

replies.text: The commander has discovered our most vulnerable position: packing.
The gift remains here until the bag has capacity for it.
Clear a slot sensibly. Do not turn a small delay into a wasted item.
I would like to sort the bag without everyone watching, please.
Let us step somewhere comfortable and see what actually needs carrying.
A military triumph has encountered a failure in the baggage division.
I fear the inspection of our bag will reveal an alarming quantity of optimism.
An obvious storage constraint. No electrical intervention required.
A full pocket can delay a gift without losing the welcome behind it.
We can return prepared. The bag does not need a dramatic solution.
I would remember where he is waiting before we start the next errand.

contexts.subject: Erika asks us to make room before receiving her TM.

CeladonCity_Gym_Text_ShouldMakeRoomForTh.text: You should make room for this.$

replies.text: A garden full of flowers, and somehow the most overgrown thing here is our bag.
The reward has not been received. We should clear space and return.
No hurry. Decide what belongs in storage before removing anything.
She made the correction gently. I appreciate that.
Let us sort what we carry without making a mess of her floor.
The gift waits patiently while our supporting luggage undergoes a much-needed edit.
An elegant refusal from a very inelegantly packed problem.
A little reorganization should resolve the blocked transfer.
We can make a place for something new without casting away something dear.
I knew we needed a better arrangement in that pocket.
It is nice that the offer remains open while we work it out.

contexts.subject: Koga cannot hand over the TM until we have bag space.

replies.text: The secret technique has been defeated by an openly visible packing problem.
The centuries-old technique can wait while we resolve the current storage limit.
Make space, then return. The team deserves care before we sort souvenirs.
I am relieved this obstacle does not require another invisible corridor.
We can handle the bag after checking everyone is well.
The ancient inheritance is briefly suspended pending a mundane administrative correction.
A ninja can hide many things. Apparently not the state of our bag.
The transfer failed cleanly. No need to guess whether we received it.
A secret is still here, waiting for a little room.
I would sort things in good light. We have had enough invisible complications.
Let us remember the unfinished exchange before leaving the town.

contexts.subject: Sabrina cannot give her TM because our bag is full.

SaffronCity_Gym_Text_BagFullOfOtherItems.text: Your BAG is full of other items.$

replies.text: Can the bag become larger if we concentrate? No? Back to ordinary tidying.
Psychic ability has not removed the capacity constraint. We need a free slot.
Sort the bag. Thinking very hard about it is not the same task.
I hope she cannot also see everything I thought would be useful to pack.
We can make space without rushing. She is still offering the gift.
The mental discipline prize has met the physical consequences of our packing decisions.
My mind is full of possibilities. So, regrettably, is the bag.
We can solve this with ordinary storage. A useful baseline method.
A quiet mind may help us choose what to carry. The choosing still matters.
I would like to reorganize before someone describes the contents out loud.
Let us come back rather than allow a small inconvenience to become a forgotten gift.

contexts.subject: Blaine asks for bag space before giving his TM.

replies.text: No room for Fire Blast. Probably the safest sentence our bag has ever produced.
The TM remains with Blaine. We should make space before attempting the transfer again.
We can collect it after sorting the bag. Heal the team first.
I would prefer to unpack somewhere cooler than this room.
Let us take care of everyone before turning the bag inside out.
The explosive final gift has been postponed by the luggage department.
An entirely nonflammable obstacle. I am almost grateful.
A capacity issue rather than a failed reward. Easy to correct deliberately.
The flame can wait while we find a safe place for its lesson.
A little room and a little order. We can manage that.
We should return before the next destination pulls all our attention away.

contexts.subject: Giovanni cannot give the TM because we have no bag space.

ViridianCity_Gym_Text_YouDoNotHaveSpace.text: You do not have space for this!$

replies.text: A dramatic victory, followed by the extremely ordinary problem of too much stuff.
We have not received the TM. Its availability and the badge result are separate.
Sort the bag carefully. Do not let the pressure of the room rush the choice.
I would rather think about the bag once we have a quieter place to stand.
The team comes first. We can return for an item after everyone is cared for.
The grand scene has paused for a small but unavoidable logistical fact.
I am relieved to have one problem in this room that can be solved by tidying.
The transfer was blocked before the item changed hands. Keep that distinction clear.
Not every unfinished thing asks to be settled in the same breath.
We can make room without treating any old possession as suddenly worthless.
Let us remember what is unfinished here without forgetting everything we have already done.

contexts.subject: The Game Corner clerk directs coin holders to the prize room next door.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_CanExchangeC.text: Welcome!\pYou can exchange your COINS for\nfabulous prizes next door.$

replies.text: Coins here, prizes next door. The building has divided temptation into departments.
The exchange counter is separate from the games. Useful to know before wandering.
Check what a prize costs before spending anything.
A clear direction is helpful in a place this busy.
Worth knowing what the coins are for before buying them.
The first act sells the coins; the neighboring stage displays the rewards.
The little metal circles have their own destination.
Separate service counters. Follow the signs before queuing.
One door offers chances, the next gives those chances a price.
They have made browsing the prizes a separate little trip.
I wonder how often visitors check the prize list first.

contexts.subject: The coin clerk politely closes the conversation when we decline to buy coins.

replies.text: We can leave with exactly the same number of coins and fewer decisions.
Declining the purchase ended the transaction without complication.
Good. No need to buy just because we asked.
They accepted the answer without making it uncomfortable.
We can save the money for something we actually planned to get.
A commercial invitation survives our polite refusal.
A small no, allowed to remain small. Appreciated.
Purchase canceled. No unnecessary steps afterward.
The door remains open without pulling us through it.
A courteous response to a customer deciding against something.
I wonder how many people come in just to look around.

contexts.subject: The attempted coin transaction cannot proceed without a Coin Case.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_SorryDontHav.text: Oh, I'm sorry.\nYou don't have a COIN CASE.$

replies.text: The coins require their own luggage. Ordinary pockets have apparently not qualified.
A missing Coin Case prevents the transfer. No coins were received through this branch.
No case, no coins. We can move on.
At least they explained what was missing instead of leaving us guessing.
Another thing to settle before deciding whether to play.
The proposed transaction has failed its container inspection.
Small pieces of metal have surprisingly specific housing requirements.
Required container missing. Clear, recoverable error.
The little things need their own place to gather.
A useful limit to learn before handing over money.
I wonder where visitors usually get their first Coin Case.

contexts.subject: The coin clerk cannot sell coins because the Coin Case is full.

replies.text: The case is full. A rare moment when the container firmly ends the shopping.
The purchase exceeded available capacity and did not proceed.
We already have enough to fill the case. Stop there.
That makes the decision rather simple for now.
No reason to spend more while the existing coins have nowhere else to go.
The final authority on the purchase turns out to be a very small box.
A useful refusal from an inanimate accomplice.
Capacity reached. Adding more is not currently an option.
Even a little box can say quite a firm no.
The case has reached its limit. We can respect ours too.
I wonder how long it took to fill that much space.

contexts.subject: The coin clerk refuses the purchase because we cannot afford it.

replies.text: The money has voted against this particular plan.
The purchase did not occur because the funds were insufficient.
Leave it. We have other things to spend money on.
An awkward answer, but a clear ending.
Better to keep what we have for the team's needs.
The budget has exercised its veto over the evening's entertainment.
A closed purse can be an unexpectedly sensible adviser.
Insufficient funds. Changing priorities is easier than changing arithmetic.
A little less money can make the next choice clearer.
No need to turn a declined purchase into a personal challenge.
I wonder how often people spend more here than they meant to.

contexts.subject: The clerk confirms the paid coin purchase has completed.

replies.text: Coins acquired. A budget is still a useful companion to bring along.
That was a paid exchange, not a gift. The coins are now available.
Bought what we asked for. Keep track of what we spend from here.
The transaction is settled. We can take a moment before doing anything else.
A planned limit is easier to keep when we remember it at the start.
Our money has changed costume and become local currency.
Different little circles, same reason to be careful with them.
Exchange complete. Useful to record the actual cost, not just the coin count.
The numbers have moved from one place to another.
A clear handoff. The important part is remembering what those coins cost.
I wonder which purchase option most visitors choose.

contexts.subject: A player whispers a rumor that Team Rocket operates the Game Corner.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_RumoredTeamR.text: Keep this quiet.\pIt's rumored that this place is run\nby TEAM ROCKET.$

replies.text: That rumor makes the cheerful lights feel considerably less cheerful.
A serious claim, though still presented as a rumor. We should distinguish evidence from gossip.
Keep alert. A rumor is not proof, but it is worth hearing.
The way they lowered their voice makes the room feel different.
We can be careful without making a scene.
The bright establishment has acquired a rather darker alleged proprietor.
A whisper can change the color of an entire room.
Unverified ownership claim. Useful lead, not a final conclusion.
Something unpleasant may be keeping time beneath all this noise.
People whisper differently when they worry the subject might hear.
I wonder what made them believe the connection.

contexts.subject: A player suspects the slot machines have different odds.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_ThinkMachine.text: I think these machines have\ndifferent odds.$

replies.text: A theory made of many little hopeful pulls, I suspect.
Distinguishing different odds from random variation would require considerable evidence.
Do not spend more just to prove a hunch.
It must be tempting to think one seat has a better answer.
A feeling is not a good reason to keep spending.
The room has produced a hypothesis that is expensive to investigate badly.
Chance is very good at wearing the face of a pattern.
I would need records, not a streak and a suspicious glance.
People find signs in spinning things when they want an answer.
A different machine can still make the same promise without keeping it.
I wonder whether she has tracked results or simply noticed a few runs.

contexts.subject: A player says wins are intermittent and nothing is guaranteed.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_WinsComeAndG.text: Wins seem to come and go.\nNothing's a sure thing.$

replies.text: The machine has no appointment for the next happy outcome.
An uncertain result remains uncertain after either a win or a loss.
Good to remember before chasing a result.
That sounds like something learned over several uneven afternoons.
Knowing when to leave matters more than waiting for certainty.
A remarkably honest review of an establishment full of promises.
Nothing certain, except how quietly the time disappears.
Unreliable output. Do not build an essential plan around it.
A turning reel is not a promise moving toward you.
A useful reminder, especially after a lucky moment.
I wonder whether he finds it easy to follow his own advice.

contexts.subject: A player attributes slot outcomes to luck.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_WinOrLoseIts.text: These slot games…\nWin or lose, it's only by luck.$

replies.text: The reels are not impressed by our heroic posture. Probably for the best.
Chance does not become more favorable because the player feels more determined.
Then do not treat losing like a challenge to push harder.
It is worth remembering this is not a judgment of anyone's ability.
A quiet limit matters more than trying to outwork the machine.
The grand drama has no obliging author behind the next spin.
The machine does not know whether you deserve a nicer afternoon.
More confidence does not change a random process.
Some doors open by chance, not because you knock more bravely.
Good to separate the result from how clever or worthy someone feels.
I wonder whether that makes the game easier for her to leave.

contexts.subject: An older player worries about how easily games become compulsive.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_SoEasyToGetH.text: Games are scary!\nIt's so easy to get hooked!$

replies.text: A little fun can grow elbows and take over the whole afternoon.
Repeated rewards can make stopping difficult even when enjoyment is fading.
If it stops feeling like a choice, step away.
He sounds less amused than the room around him.
A break outside might make the next choice feel clearer.
The warning comes from inside the spectacle, which gives it a certain weight.
A bright room can hold you more tightly than a dark one.
A stopping rule set in advance is more reliable than willpower mid-loop.
Some invitations keep taking little pieces of your evening.
He is noticing the feeling. I hope he gives himself permission to leave.
I wonder whether he meant that as advice or an admission.

contexts.subject: A player declines to give more coins because our existing Coin Case is too full.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_YouveGotPlen.text: You've got plenty of your own\nCOINS!$

replies.text: They inspected our supply and decided the tiny metal population was large enough.
The intended transfer did not occur because existing holdings were already near capacity.
We have plenty already. No need to ask for more.
A reasonable answer. Their coins can stay where they are.
We can be grateful for the thought without needing another handful.
The patronage application has been rejected on the grounds of visible abundance.
An unusually practical limit to roadside generosity.
No remaining capacity. Avoid promising a transfer the container cannot accept.
A full little case has settled the question for everyone.
They have a point. More is not automatically better.
I wonder whether many visitors already have that much when they ask.

contexts.subject: A player says he still lacks enough coins for the Pokemon he wants.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_NeedMoreCoin.text: Darn! I need more COINS for the\nPOKéMON I want!$

replies.text: A living prize can make one more try sound far too persuasive.
A desired reward can encourage repeated spending beyond the original plan.
Wanting the Pokemon does not make every extra spin worth it.
He sounds close enough to hope and far enough to be frustrated.
I hope he keeps enough aside for caring for the partner afterward.
The promised arrival waits beyond a counter that keeps asking for another coin.
It is unsettling to hear a companion described as a reason not to stop.
Compare total cost with the goal. Sunk effort is not a discount.
A wanted companion should not become a hole in the day.
The prize is doing a lot of work to keep him in that seat.
I wonder how long he has been saving toward that particular Pokemon.

contexts.subject: A player claims close attention to the reels is the trick to winning.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_WatchReelsCl.text: The trick is to watch the reels\nclosely.$

replies.text: My eyes can stare very hard. The reels have yet to be intimidated.
Attention alone does not establish control over the outcome.
A claimed trick is still a claim. Keep the spending limit.
I would rather not turn this into a test of how intensely I can look.
No trick is worth spending the team's supply money to verify.
The oracle recommends a stern gaze at the spinning symbols.
A machine can invite concentration without rewarding it.
Need evidence that the input changes the result before optimizing the stare.
Looking closely and seeing a path are not always the same thing.
Confidence in advice does not tell us whether it works.
I wonder what made him settle on that explanation.

contexts.subject: A visitor wants Porygon but finds winning enough coins difficult.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_PrizeRoom_Text_Fa.text: I sure do fancy that PORYGON!\nBut, it's hard to win at slots!$

replies.text: Porygon has certainly caught their eye. The path to it sounds frustrating.
The desired Pokemon is clear; the uncertain acquisition cost is the difficulty.
Wanting one does not mean spending without a limit.
It is hard when something fascinating is tied to an unreliable game.
I hope they think about the partner's care as well as getting it.
An unusual creature holds the spotlight while the coin counter delays the entrance.
A strange little being behind an unusually ordinary barrier: enough money.
Porygon is fascinating. The slots are a much less interesting engineering proposition.
An unlikely creature can make a person linger a long time.
A distinctive choice. I hope admiration does not become an endless bill.
I wonder what first made Porygon stand out to them.

contexts.subject: A winner celebrates today's winnings and wishes every day were as lucky.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_PrizeRoom_Text_Ra.text: Gahaha! I raked it in today!\nIf only every day were like this…$

replies.text: A lucky day can stay a lucky day without becoming tomorrow's business plan.
One favorable session does not predict repeated returns.
Good day to leave with what he has.
He sounds delighted. I hope the memory can be enough without repeating it immediately.
Enjoy the good result without spending it all trying to make it happen again.
Today's applause has inspired ambitious plans for a permanent residency.
A bright afternoon is not a promise the next one signed.
Do not extrapolate from one unusually favorable test run.
Good fortune is a visitor, not a tenant you can charge rent.
The first half sounds happy. The second half is where expectations get expensive.
I wonder whether he has decided what to do with the winnings.

contexts.subject: A developer introduces himself as the programmer.

replies.text: A short introduction from somebody who probably spends all day fixing long problems.
A demanding profession. The brief introduction may conceal a great many late nights.
Sounds like careful work. Hope he gets breaks.
He seems comfortable letting the job speak for itself.
Every workplace has someone quietly keeping things running.
The programmer enters, establishes his role, and wastes no dialogue.
A wonderfully economical biography. I could learn from it.
Excellent! I have questions about how he solves difficult bugs. Several questions.
A person who teaches small rules to do large amounts of work.
Clear introduction. He has probably spent his patience on less clear problems.
I wonder what part of the work he enjoys most.

contexts.subject: The graphic artist jokingly claims to have drawn us.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_3F_Text_ImTheGr.text: I'm the graphic artist!\nI drew you!$

replies.text: I hope he remembered my good side. It keeps moving around.
An unusually personal way to introduce a visual arts specialty.
Bold claim. At least he seems pleased with the work.
I would be rather nervous about someone studying me that closely.
He sounds proud of making something people recognize.
An artist stakes a claim on our likeness with magnificent confidence.
I would ask for a more rested version of me, given the opportunity.
That is quite an introduction. I wonder how he handles the tiny details.
An artist sees outlines the rest of us merely live inside.
I trust he has given the hair the attention it deserves.
I would be curious to see the sketches behind that claim.

contexts.subject: The writer introduces his role and enthusiastically praises Erika, Misty, and Sabrina.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_3F_Text_IWroteT.text: I wrote the story!\nIsn't ERIKA cute?\pI like MISTY a lot, too!\nOh, and SABRINA, I like her!$

replies.text: He began with his job and ended with a very well-attended favorites list.
His professional introduction has become a personal account of the characters he likes.
He knows what he likes. Quite a lot of it, apparently.
His enthusiasm runs ahead of the introduction. It is rather endearing.
It is nice when somebody still enjoys the people they write about.
A fellow writer whose discerning favorites list is rapidly becoming the entire cast.
A brief biography with several enthusiastic footnotes.
Personal investment in the work! A little unfocused, but unmistakable.
He keeps finding one more name worth speaking warmly.
Several favorites is perfectly acceptable. The rushed defense makes it funnier.
I wonder what he most enjoys about writing them.

contexts.subject: The designer encourages us to finish the Pokedex and return.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_3F_Text_ImGameD.text: Is that right?\pI'm the game designer!\pFilling up your POKéDEX is tough,\nbut don't quit!\pWhen you finish, come tell me!$

replies.text: He has volunteered to be our very patient finishing-line audience.
A long collection project benefits from encouragement that acknowledges the difficulty.
We can keep at it at our own pace. The work is real.
It helps when somebody recognizes the effort before it is finished.
One encounter at a time is a more manageable plan than staring at the total.
A future celebration has been penciled in, with considerable work between here and there.
An unfinished thing is allowed to keep becoming.
Large task, clear completion condition. Break it into smaller outings.
A long book of names fills one meeting at a time.
He wants us to come back with good news. A nice invitation.
I wonder how many completed Pokedexes he has been shown.

contexts.subject: The designer congratulates us on completing the Kanto Pokedex before the diploma display.

replies.text: Every one of those meetings adds up to this! That is a lot of hello.
A completed regional record represents a substantial body of travel and observation.
The team helped make that happen. They deserve the credit too.
It is lovely to have the long effort recognized so plainly.
That took patience. A proper celebration seems deserved.
The sprawling collection finally receives its satisfying final full stop.
A long trail of small discoveries has reached a whole shape.
Complete! All those separate observations finally closing the checklist.
So many little lives, each leaving a name in the same book.
An achievement that carries much more work than the neat certificate can show.
I wonder which encounter comes back to mind first at a moment like this.

contexts.subject: A resident boasts about profits from the slot machines.

CeladonCity_House1_Text_SlotsReelInTheDo.text: Hehehe!\pThe slots just reel in the dough,\nbig-time!$

replies.text: Somebody is very happy about where the missing coins end up.
The operator's revenue and the player's outcome are quite different perspectives.
That money came from people on the other side of the machines.
His delight makes the room feel rather cold.
I keep thinking of the people who leave with less than they meant to spend.
A candid review from the profitable side of the counter.
A cheerful voice can make an unpleasant truth sound even worse.
Reliable income for the operator does not imply reliable returns for customers.
The spinning things always seem to know which house they belong to.
That laugh tells us more about the business than the bright signs do.
I wonder how many players hear this side of the story.

contexts.subject: A worker reports shipping two thousand Pokemon as slot prizes.

CeladonCity_House1_Text_ShippedMonsAsSlo.text: CHIEF!\pWe just shipped two thousand\nmore POKéMON as slot prizes\lagain today!$

replies.text: Two thousand living creatures, reported like boxes of spare buttons. That feels awful.
The scale is alarming, especially when the animals are discussed only as merchandise.
Those are Pokemon. Not inventory to boast about moving.
There is no warmth at all in how he says it.
That many partners need care, not a cheerful shipping tally.
An enormous number delivered with the emotional weight of an office invoice.
A crowd of lives reduced to one tidy line in a report.
At that scale, welfare cannot be an afterthought. His language gives me no reassurance.
Thousands of small journeys, and nobody here names a single traveler.
He sounds proud of the volume. I wish he sounded concerned about the Pokemon.
I wonder where they came from and who is looking after them.

contexts.subject: A resident suspiciously denies that the Game Corner poster hides a switch.

CeladonCity_House1_Text_DontTouchGameCor.text: Don't touch the poster at the GAME\nCORNER!\pThere's no secret switch behind it!$

replies.text: A secret switch? We had not asked. Fascinating choice of detail.
The unsolicited denial supplies a suspiciously specific lead.
He has given us a reason to remember that poster.
That sounded rehearsed in exactly the wrong way.
An ordinary warning usually needs fewer details about the thing it denies.
A magnificent failure of discretion. The secret has received directions to its own entrance.
Nothing suspicious, delivered with several suspicious extras.
Information leak through over-specific denial. Very poor security design.
A hidden thing sometimes points at itself through the person guarding it.
He has made the poster the most interesting object in the building.
I wonder how many people were curious before he mentioned it.

contexts.subject: A visitor says the Poke Flute wakes Pokemon through a sound only they hear.

CeladonCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_PokeFl.text: A POKé FLUTE awakens sleeping\nPOKéMON. You know that.\pIt does so with a sound that only\nthey can hear.$

replies.text: A concert with an audience we cannot quite join. Clever instrument.
A sound beyond ordinary human hearing could explain a selective response.
Useful to know. Wake a partner gently when there is time.
An instrument that reaches a different kind of listener. That fascinates me.
A practical way to help a sleeping partner when the team needs it.
A melody reserved for an audience with rather different ears.
A song can be present without being ours to hear.
Selective acoustic response! I have several questions about the mechanism.
Some notes enter rooms our ears never find.
An unusual instrument with a very specific purpose.
I wonder what its sound is like from a Pokemon's side.

contexts.subject: A cyclist is exhausted after riding uphill from Fuchsia.

CeladonCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_RodeHe.text: I rode here from FUCHSIA.\pIt's an uphill ride on CYCLING\nROAD, so I'm exhausted.$

replies.text: The hill spent the entire journey arguing with their legs. They earned a sit.
An uphill route explains the increased effort over the same distance.
Rest before riding again. No prize for falling off tired.
They sound relieved to have reached somewhere they can stop.
A drink and a good seat must feel wonderful after that climb.
The scenic route has delivered its bill in muscle fatigue.
A road can feel much longer when it refuses to lie flat.
Elevation gain is real work. Recovery belongs in the itinerary.
The hill is behind them now. That is its own comfort.
They made it. No need to make the recovery look glamorous.
I wonder whether the view made any part of the climb feel easier.

contexts.subject: A visitor wishes for a bike so they could visit Cycling Road.

CeladonCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_GoToCy.text: If I had a BIKE, I would go to\nCYCLING ROAD!$

replies.text: A bicycle and a ready-made first outing. Half the dream is planned.
A required piece of equipment is the current barrier to their preferred route.
Good to have a place you want to go when the chance comes.
I like how clearly they can imagine the day they want.
A simple ride can be a very good thing to look forward to.
The itinerary waits patiently for its missing pair of wheels.
A small wish with a long road tucked inside it.
Specific goal, specific prerequisite. A very workable plan.
The road is already calling before there are wheels to answer.
Knowing what you would actually do with a purchase is a good sign.
I wonder whether they would start from the easy end or tackle the climb.

contexts.subject: A diner gossips about another customer losing all his money at slots.

CeladonCity_Restaurant_Text_ManLostItAll.text: Munch…\pThe man at that table lost it all\nat the slots.$

replies.text: That sounds like somebody's bad day being served as table talk.
The information may be accurate, but discussing him this way adds no help.
He can probably hear. Let him eat without an audience.
It feels unkind to hear his trouble discussed over a meal.
A little privacy would be a better thing to offer than gossip.
A stranger's misfortune has become the dining room's incidental entertainment.
An ordinary meal is not improved by making somebody else's regret the centerpiece.
Observation without compassion is not automatically useful information.
Some sad stories travel too easily between nearby tables.
People deserve a little dignity when their day has gone badly.
I would rather hear from the man himself if he chooses to talk.

contexts.subject: The attendant explains the four zones, limited time, Safari Balls, and bait or rock tradeoffs.

FuchsiaCity_SafariZone_Entrance_Text_Exp.text:
The SAFARI ZONE actually has
four zones in it.\pEach zone has different kinds of
POKéMON, even some rare ones.\pUse the supplied SAFARI BALLS to
catch them.\pYou can also throw BAIT or ROCKS
besides the SAFARI BALLS.\pIf you throw BAIT, the POKéMON
becomes less likely to flee, but\lharder to catch.\pIf you throw ROCKS, the POKéMON
becomes more likely to flee, but\leasier to catch.\pWhen you run out of time or SAFARI
BALLS, it's game over for you!$

replies.text: Four zones, a time limit, and thirty chances. My wandering needs a little supervision.
The limited resources and different habitats make planning important.
Know the limits. Do not take frustration out on the Pokemon.
There is a lot to remember. I would rather move gently and pay attention.
A calm visit sounds better than turning every encounter into a scramble.
An elaborate set of rules for an afternoon that still depends on wild creatures cooperating.
A place full of life should be more than a race against a counter.
Resource limits noted. Map the zones before spending the whole allowance wandering.
Four places, many shy lives, and a clock that does not stop to watch them.
Clear rules help. A little restraint is still our own responsibility.
I wonder which zone most visitors overlook in their rush.

contexts.subject: The attendant apologizes for offering an introduction to someone already familiar with the Safari Zone.

replies.text: We have graduated from explanation to familiar face. Very official.
They adjusted the conversation once they understood we knew the rules.
No harm done. A refresher is better than assuming everyone knows.
A little awkwardness, kindly corrected.
It is nice when a place starts feeling familiar enough for that mistake.
Our credentials as repeat visitors have been accepted without an examination.
A small recognition at the edge of a large reserve.
Experience level clarified. Good to avoid redundant instructions.
A doorway feels different when someone thinks you know the way.
They corrected themselves politely. Easily forgiven.
I wonder how many regular visitors they come to recognize.

contexts.subject: A thirsty Saffron gate guard says the road is closed.

Route5_SouthEntrance_Text_ThirstyOnGuard.text: I'm on guard duty.\nGee, I'm thirsty, though!\pOh, wait there, the road's closed.$

Route6_NorthEntrance_Text_ThirstyOnGuard.text: I'm on guard duty.\nGee, I'm thirsty, though!\pOh, wait there, the road's closed.$

Route7_EastEntrance_Text_ThirstyOnGuardD.text: I'm on guard duty.\nGee, I'm thirsty, though!\pOh, wait there, the road's closed.$

Route8_WestEntrance_Text_ThirstyOnGuardD.text: I'm on guard duty.\nGee, I'm thirsty, though!\pOh, wait there, the road's closed.$

replies.text: A closed road and an open thirst complaint. We have learned both priorities.
The guard is refusing passage while mentioning a personal discomfort.
Road is closed. No need to argue at the gate.
It is frustrating to get so close and still have to stop.
Standing guard all day must be tiring. Being turned back is tiring too.
The city's entry policy has acquired an oddly beverage-shaped footnote.
A small dry throat beside a much larger closed door.
Access denied. The reason and the complaint seem poorly connected.
The road ends for now in a person wishing for a drink.
He sounds uncomfortable, but the directions are still no more helpful.
I wonder what explanation the waiting travelers have been given.

contexts.subject: After accepting Tea, the guard allows entry to Saffron and promises to share it with the other guards.

Route5_SouthEntrance_Text_ThanksIllShare.text: Huh? I can have this drink?\nGee, thanks!\l… …\lGlug, glug…\l… …\lGulp…\lIf you want to go to SAFFRON\lCITY…\l… …\lYou can go on through.\pI'll share this TEA with the other\nguards!$

Route6_NorthEntrance_Text_ThanksIllShare.text: Huh? I can have this drink?\nGee, thanks!\l… …\lGlug, glug…\l… …\lGulp…\lIf you want to go to SAFFRON\lCITY…\l… …\lYou can go on through.\pI'll share this TEA with the other\nguards!$

Route7_EastEntrance_Text_ThanksIllShareT.text: Huh? I can have this drink?\nGee, thanks!\l… …\lGlug, glug…\l… …\lGulp…\lIf you want to go to SAFFRON\lCITY…\l… …\lYou can go on through.\pI'll share this TEA with the other\nguards!$

Route8_WestEntrance_Text_ThanksIllShareT.text: Huh? I can have this drink?\nGee, thanks!\l… …\lGlug, glug…\l… …\lGulp…\lIf you want to go to SAFFRON\lCITY…\l… …\lYou can go on through.\pI'll share this TEA with the other\nguards!$

replies.text: The tea has achieved impressive diplomatic reach. And he is sharing it.
The guard accepted the tea, opened passage, and intends to distribute it to colleagues.
We can pass now. Glad the other guards get a share.
That sounded like genuine relief. The welcome feels warmer now.
A gift passed along can improve more than one person's shift.
A teacup has accomplished what a travel itinerary could not.
One warm drink has found several people on long quiet shifts.
A remarkably small intervention with a large route-planning effect.
The closed way has opened with a little warmth between strangers.
He remembered the others before the conversation even ended. Nice.
I wonder whether the guards often share small comforts through the day.

contexts.subject: Once access is allowed, the Saffron guard greets us casually.

replies.text: A much friendlier checkpoint. My feet appreciate the shorter conversation.
The interaction has become an ordinary greeting instead of an access dispute.
All clear. Nice to hear a normal hello.
It is easier to feel welcome when the first words are friendly.
A simple greeting makes a familiar route feel a little more human.
The former obstacle now contributes a pleasant line to the passing scene.
The same doorway, a much gentler voice around it.
Routine access restored. Friendly acknowledgment is a welcome extra.
A familiar face at the gate, without the closed road between us.
Casual suits him better than refusing people entry.
I wonder how his shift has been going since the tea arrived.

contexts.subject: After giving the Super Rod, the enthusiast asks to see especially large Magikarp.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_IfYouCatchBigM.text:
Fishing is a way of life!
It is like the finest poetry.\pFrom the seas to rivers, go out
and land the big one, my friend.\pNow, I have a request.\pIf you catch a big MAGIKARP 
with that ROD, I want to see it.\pAs much as I love to fish, I also
love seeing gigantic MAGIKARP.$

replies.text: A splendid rod, with one very fish-shaped request attached.
He has given us equipment and a specific observation he hopes we will bring back.
Generous gift. Showing him an interesting catch seems fair.
He sounds eager to share the excitement, not just hear a thank-you.
A good gift can open the door to more conversations later.
The new fishing partnership includes a standing invitation for outsized guest stars.
He has a particular joy, and there is something charming about its size requirement.
Useful equipment plus a measurable field challenge. Nicely defined.
The river has been asked to send its largest little surprise.
He knows exactly what would make his afternoon. Refreshingly specific.
I wonder what his first enormous Magikarp looked like.

contexts.subject: The younger fishing brother is disappointed when we decline his fishing interest.

replies.text: Another future fishing companion has failed the enthusiasm interview.
He hoped for shared interest, but the question allowed an honest negative answer.
We do not have to like it to be polite.
Disappointing someone that enthusiastic always feels more difficult than it should.
He can still enjoy the water without recruiting every visitor.
The proposed angling alliance has dissolved before its first expedition.
A small disappointment can remain small if nobody insists on fixing it.
Interest mismatch. No need to force compatibility.
The river will still be there for the people who want its company.
An honest answer is better than promising to enjoy a hobby for his sake.
I wonder how long it takes before he asks the next visitor.

contexts.subject: The fishing enthusiast recommends trying different waters and repeats his request for giant Magikarp.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_TryFishingBrin.text:
Hello there, {PLAYER}!
Have you been fishing?\pTry fishing with the SUPER ROD in
any body of water.\pYou'll find different POKéMON in
different places.\pOh, and don't forget to bring me
gigantic MAGIKARP.$

replies.text: New water, new surprises. He still has one preferred surprise.
Different habitats can change the available catches. His request remains quite specific.
Try the rod where it makes sense. No need to rush a record.
I like that he has more advice ready when we return.
A little exploring can be worthwhile even without a record fish.
The field assignment expands geographically while remaining firmly Magikarp-shaped.
A familiar greeting, followed by the world's least concealed obsession.
Sampling different habitats should give more varied results. Good advice.
Each body of water keeps a different answer beneath its surface.
He is persistent, but at least his directions are useful.
I wonder which nearby water has produced his favorite catches.

contexts.subject: After rewarding a record Magikarp, the enthusiast invites us to break the record again.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_LookForwardToG.text: I'll look forward to seeing greater\nrecords from you!$

replies.text: He is delighted, and already imagining an even more alarming fish.
The new record has been recognized and rewarded; further observations are optional.
Good catch. No need to turn every outing into another record attempt.
It is lovely when something we found makes another person that happy.
We can enjoy this result before planning the next one.
A record falls, the applause rises, and the sequel is immediately commissioned.
The quiet water keeps producing reasons for his very loud joy.
Benchmark updated. Future improvements should be measured against the new value.
A little mark on the wall has moved farther than he expected.
He knows how to make a shared hobby feel like an event.
I wonder whether he tells everyone about the new record.

contexts.subject: The presented Magikarp ties the previous size record.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_HuhXSizeSameSi.text: Huh?\n{STR_VAR_2}?\pThis is the same size as the one\nI saw before.$

replies.text: A perfect tie. The fish have agreed on a standard edition.
The measurement equals the existing record rather than exceeding it.
Still a good-sized catch. The record can wait.
Matching something impressive is not a disappointing thing in itself.
No need to make the fish larger to make the trip worthwhile.
The reigning champion has acquired an identically proportioned rival.
Two small lives have happened to arrive at the same little number.
No improvement, but useful confirmation that the measurement is repeatable.
A familiar mark has found a second visitor.
A tie can still be interesting, even without a new prize.
I wonder whether the two fish look as similar as their measurements.

contexts.subject: The presented Magikarp is smaller than the recorded best.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_HmmXSizeDoesnt.text: Hmm…\nThis one is {STR_VAR_2} long.\pIt doesn't measure up to the\n{STR_VAR_3} one you brought before.$

replies.text: A smaller fish is still a complete fish. The ruler is not its whole biography.
The measurement does not exceed the existing record. That is all the comparison establishes.
No record today. The partner is not at fault for its size.
I hope the catch still feels worthwhile to the person who brought it.
A quiet outing can be good without producing the biggest thing.
The understudy has failed to exceed the star's dimensions. A very narrow review.
Not every living thing needs to become a superlative.
Below benchmark. That does not make the specimen useless.
A small body can carry a whole life quite comfortably.
A fair measurement, but not the only reason to value the catch.
I wonder what else distinguishes this one besides its length.

contexts.subject: The enthusiast rejects a submitted Pokemon because it is not Magikarp.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_DoesntLookLike.text: Uh… That doesn't look much like\na MAGIKARP.$

replies.text: An ambitious attempt to introduce a new category. The judge remains unmoved.
The comparison is restricted to Magikarp. This submission does not qualify.
Wrong Pokemon for the question. No need to bother it further.
An easy mistake in the selection, perhaps. We can leave it there.
He asked for one particular species. That is fair enough.
The guest has arrived at an exceptionally exclusive fish show.
A different creature has briefly been asked to fit a very specific silhouette.
Input validation catches another mismatch. Good that he checks.
The little contest has a narrow doorway.
At least he declined without putting the Pokemon down.
I wonder whether he gets hopeful every time someone opens a Poke Ball.

contexts.subject: A fishing enthusiast cannot provide an intended gift because the bag is full.

Route12_FishingHouse_Text_NoRoomForGift.text: Oh, no!\pI had a gift for you, but you have\nno room for it.$

FuchsiaCity_House2_Text_YouHaveNoRoomFor.text: Oh, no!\pI had a gift for you, but you have\nno room for it!$

VermilionCity_House1_Text_NoRoomForNiceG.text: Oh, no!\pI had a nice gift for you, but you\nhave no room for it!$

replies.text: The generosity is ready. The bag is considerably less ready.
The gift transfer failed for lack of space; its contents should not be assumed received.
Make room before asking him to try again.
A kind offer, stopped by an awkwardly full bag.
A little sorting would make the next visit easier.
The benefactor's plans have collided with our portable collection of everything.
A full bag can make a generous moment unexpectedly sad.
Capacity failure. Resolve the container problem before repeating the transfer.
Something offered cannot enter a place with no room left.
The gift is still his to keep until we are prepared for it.
I wonder which unnecessary thing has been taking up that last bit of space.

contexts.subject: The woman in the secluded retreat explains Fly after giving it or on return visits.

Route16_House_Text_ExplainHM02.text: HM02 is FLY.\nIt's a wonderfully convenient move.\pPlease, put it to good use.$

replies.text: A quiet retreat and a way to leave by sky. She has excellent taste in exits.
Fly offers a useful travel option. Her explanation applies on later visits as well.
A generous lesson. We can respect her quiet place in return.
She wants a little privacy, and still made time to help us.
We can put the move to good use without making her home a busy stop.
The reclusive host has given us an unusually convenient departure route.
A private place, and a gift that makes the wider world less far away.
A transport upgrade from someone who has chosen to avoid the traffic. Elegant.
A little hidden room has opened a way into the sky.
Discreet and generous is a very good combination.
I wonder whether flying is how she comes and goes from here.

contexts.subject: The retreat's resident cannot give HM02 because the bag is full.

Route16_House_Text_DontHaveAnyRoomForThi.text: You don't have any room for this.$

replies.text: A secret retreat discovered, a useful gift blocked by socks and supplies. Typical bag politics.
The HM transfer did not happen. We need room before receiving it.
Sort the bag, then ask again. No need to crowd her.
We have made a quiet visit rather awkward.
A little preparation would have made accepting the kindness easier.
The promised convenience has encountered the least convenient part of our luggage.
A small disc, a completely occupied bag. A disproportionate obstacle.
Tiny object, insufficient capacity. Clear the buffer first.
The way into the sky is waiting outside a very full pocket.
A tidy bag would have been a better introduction.
I wonder how rarely someone comes this far and cannot carry the gift home.

contexts.subject: A traveler recommends Lavender's Name Rater for help with Pokemon nicknames.

Route11_EastEntrance_1F_Text_ManInLavend.text:
Don't you think it's hard to think
up good names for POKéMON?\pEspecially if you've caught a
whole bunch?\pIn LAVENDER TOWN, there's a man
who rates POKéMON nicknames.\pHe can even help you rename your
POKéMON, too.$

replies.text: Professional help for the moment you run out of names before running out of Pokemon.
An outside opinion can help with naming, though the trainer's own preference still matters.
Useful lead. A name should still suit the partner living with it.
I find names difficult. It is reassuring that someone enjoys helping with them.
A little thought now can make the name pleasant to use every day.
Lavender employs a critic for the smallest creative decisions with the longest afterlife.
An official assessor of the noises we make when calling friends. Peculiar profession.
A naming service! I would ask what criteria he uses.
Names are small things that can become very hard to set down.
A second opinion can be helpful when you have stared at the same ideas too long.
I wonder what the most memorable name he has heard was.

contexts.subject: A traveler gives directions to Lavender through Rock Tunnel from Cerulean.

Route11_EastEntrance_1F_Text_RockTunnelT.text: If you're aiming to reach LAVENDER\nTOWN, take ROCK TUNNEL.\pYou can get to ROCK TUNNEL from\nCERULEAN CITY.$

replies.text: Directions with a mountain in the middle. We should prepare for that part.
The route connects through Cerulean and Rock Tunnel. A useful sequence of landmarks.
Check supplies and light before taking the tunnel.
Clear directions help, even when the route itself sounds daunting.
A good place to pause and plan the next stretch.
The itinerary offers an underground chapter before the destination.
A dark way through can still be the right way forward.
Route established. Terrain requirements still need checking.
The road to a quiet town bends through a very dark place.
Helpful directions are better when they name the difficult section plainly.
I wonder how often they guide travelers who expected a simpler route.

contexts.subject: After the Pokedex reward, the aide explains the Itemfinder's directional limits.

Route11_EastEntrance_2F_Text_ExplainItem.text:
There are items on the ground that
may be hidden from view.\pUse the ITEMFINDER to detect any
hidden items close to you.\pThe machine is a bit limited.
It can't pinpoint item locations.\pWhat it does is show the direction
where the item is.\pUse it to get your bearings, then
search the suspect area by hand.$

replies.text: It points toward the treasure but leaves us the dignity of poking around in the dirt.
The aide clearly distinguishes directional detection from precise localization.
Useful lead. Still need eyes and patience to finish the job.
I appreciate being told the limit before expecting it to do everything.
A practical tool with practical instructions. Good gift.
The machine supplies suspense; the ground still requires a personal investigation.
A device for finding what the hurried world has overlooked.
Excellent documentation! State the capability and the limit together.
A little needle toward something quietly waiting nearby.
Knowing what a tool cannot do prevents a lot of disappointment.
I wonder what the aide first found while learning to use it.

contexts.subject: A traveler recommends the magnificent view from the upstairs lookout.

Route12_NorthEntrance_1F_Text_LookoutSpo.text: There's a lookout spot upstairs.\nThe view is magnificent.$

replies.text: A small climb with a scenery reward. My kind of optional challenge.
Elevation can reveal the layout of a place that is hard to see from the road.
Worth a look while we have a quiet moment.
A place to stop and look sounds lovely after all the walking.
A view can be a perfectly good reason to take a short break.
The upstairs room has received a glowing review without charging admission.
Sometimes the best part of a road is a place to stop facing forward.
A higher vantage point! Useful for orientation as well as enjoyment.
A few stairs can make the world feel wider.
A good recommendation does not always need a shop attached.
I wonder what part of the view they like most.

contexts.subject: A bereaved girl explains Return after passing on her departed Pokemon's TM.

Route12_NorthEntrance_2F_Text_ExplainTM2.text: TM27 is a move called RETURN…\pIf you treat your POKéMON good,\nit will return your love by working\lits hardest in battle.$

replies.text: That gift has a memory inside it. We should treat it gently.
Her explanation links the move to the relationship she remembers with her Pokemon.
A gift like that deserves respect. It mattered to someone she loved.
She is sharing something that belonged to a life she misses.
We can honor the kindness by caring well for the partners still with us.
A small inheritance from a bond that did not end neatly with goodbye.
Something used in love has found another place to be useful.
The practical explanation carries more weight knowing why she no longer needs it.
A little trace of an old affection, passed into another pair of hands.
She gave us more than a useful disc. We should remember that.
I wonder what her partner was like when she talks about that trust.

contexts.subject: The bereaved girl cannot give the TM because our bag is full.

Route12_NorthEntrance_2F_Text_DontHaveRo.text: You don't have room for this.$

replies.text: That is a tender offer to have stopped by a badly organized bag.
The intended transfer did not occur. The significance of her offer deserves care.
Make room. Do not rush her while we sort it.
I wish we had been ready to accept something that means so much.
A little sorting is all we need. Her generosity can wait without pressure.
An unexpectedly clumsy obstacle in a delicate conversation.
A full pocket can be an awfully small thing to interrupt something important.
Capacity problem. Fix it quietly rather than making her repeat the whole story.
The offered memory is waiting outside a crowded place.
We should make room with more care than this moment first received.
I hope the interruption does not make her feel the gift was unwanted.

contexts.subject: The gate worker recognizes our Pokedex project and says Oak's aide passed through.

Route15_WestEntrance_1F_Text_OaksAideCam.text: Are you the kid who's working on\na POKéDEX?\pPROF. OAK's AIDE came by here.$

replies.text: Our homework has developed a reputation ahead of us.
The aide's recent visit is a useful lead connected to our research task.
Worth checking nearby. The worker remembered why we might need them.
It feels strange and nice to be recognized for something we are working on.
A small message passed along can save a lot of searching.
The research expedition has acquired a modest roadside information network.
Someone remembered our work even before meeting us properly.
Relevant lead, supplied at the right point on the route. Helpful.
The path has kept a little message for us.
Attentive service. They connected the visitor with the work instead of just pointing vaguely.
I wonder how far ahead the aide is.

contexts.subject: After rewarding Pokedex progress, the aide explains Exp. Share.

Route15_WestEntrance_2F_Text_ExplainExpS.text: EXP. SHARE is an item to be held\nby a POKéMON.\pThe POKéMON will receive a share\nof the EXP. Points without having\lto battle.$

replies.text: A way for a quieter teammate to learn while the others take the lead. Lovely.
The held item allows experience sharing without requiring direct participation.
Useful for bringing someone along without throwing them in unready.
I like the idea that being there can help a partner learn.
A careful way to include a newer teammate in a longer journey.
The supporting cast gains something without being thrust into every difficult scene.
A place beside the others can become its own small lesson.
Shared progress without full load. Useful for a developing partner.
Someone can grow quietly in the company of stronger footsteps.
A useful reward, especially when the team's progress is uneven.
I wonder which partner would benefit most from carrying it now.

contexts.subject: The gate guard refuses foot traffic on Cycling Road.

Route16_NorthEntrance_1F_Text_NoPedestri.text: No pedestrians are allowed on\nCYCLING ROAD!$

Route18_EastEntrance_1F_Text_NeedBicycle.text: You need a BICYCLE to go out on\nCYCLING ROAD!$

replies.text: The road has a dress code, and it is two wheels.
The route is restricted to cyclists. Walking through is not an available option.
Fast bikes and walkers are a poor mix on a narrow slope. Fair rule.
It is disappointing to stop, but the warning is clear.
Better to know at the gate than feel stranded halfway down.
The scenic corridor insists on a very particular mode of entrance.
A road can be public and still a poor place for feet.
Access requirement is explicit: bring a bicycle.
Some paths are meant for a different rhythm of travel.
A practical rule, even when it changes our plans.
I wonder how many people arrive expecting to walk the whole way.

contexts.subject: A gate traveler praises the downhill coastal Cycling Road.

Route16_NorthEntrance_1F_Text_CyclingRoa.text: CYCLING ROAD is a downhill course\nby the sea. It's a great ride.$

replies.text: Sea air and gravity helping. A very persuasive combination.
The slope makes this direction easier, though it increases the need for braking control.
Enjoy the ride. Keep enough room to stop.
That sounds like a lovely stretch when the wind is gentle.
A pleasant descent is a good reward for reaching this end of the road.
The coast supplies the scenery while the hill supplies the pace.
For once, the ground is willing to do some of the work.
Potential energy put to enjoyable use! Check the brakes first.
A road sloping toward sea air feels like a small invitation.
A good ride is easier to enjoy when you know what the road will do.
I wonder what time of day the water looks best from the road.

contexts.subject: A cyclist enjoys a relaxed outing on his new bike with his girlfriend.

Route16_NorthEntrance_2F_Text_OnBikeRide.text: I'm on a relaxing ride on my new\nbike with my girlfriend.$

replies.text: A new bike and good company. That is a very complete afternoon.
A relaxed shared outing is a sensible way to get familiar with new equipment.
Good plan. Keep a pace they both enjoy.
It sounds nice to spend time together without making a competition of it.
A simple day out can be the one you remember warmly.
A pleasant itinerary with an unusually good balance of company and scenery.
New wheels, familiar company, no urgent destination. A decent arrangement.
A gentle test ride with a companion. Good way to notice any problems early.
Two people making a small ordinary journey feel worth keeping.
Relaxed is doing the important work in that plan.
I wonder whether they picked the route together.

contexts.subject: The girlfriend looks forward to riding together on their new bicycles.

Route16_NorthEntrance_2F_Text_RidingToge.text: We're going riding together on our\nnew bikes.$

replies.text: Two new bicycles. They have skipped straight to a coordinated expedition.
Matching activity, separate bicycles. Each rider can still choose a comfortable pace.
Hope they leave room to enjoy the ride instead of racing it.
She sounds happy about the together part most of all.
A good shared outing leaves time to stop when something catches your eye.
The new wheels have found a very pleasant first chapter.
An ordinary road becomes a little more theirs by riding it together.
Two fresh machines on a first outing! Check the fittings before the descent.
A road can hold two separate tracks moving comfortably beside each other.
A little coordination can be charming when nobody has to match perfectly.
I wonder what made them choose new bikes at the same time.

contexts.subject: After the Pokedex reward, the aide explains that a held Amulet Coin raises prize money when its Pokemon participates.

Route16_NorthEntrance_2F_Text_ExplainAmu.text: An AMULET COIN is an item to be\nheld by a POKéMON.\pIf the POKéMON appears in a winning\nbattle, you will earn more money.$

replies.text: A lucky coin with very specific attendance requirements. Read the fine print.
The holder must participate in a winning battle for the increased reward to apply.
Useful. Keep the holder safe rather than chasing extra cash.
It is good that the aide explained the condition clearly.
A little more income can help with supplies when we use it thoughtfully.
The lucky charm insists on appearing in the scene before collecting its fee.
A coin that apparently prefers to watch the battle itself.
Conditional effect. Participation requirement matters as much as the reward.
A little metal circle that wants to travel into the work.
Useful accessories deserve instructions. This one certainly has them.
I wonder which partner would be most comfortable carrying it.

contexts.subject: A traveler warns that Cycling Road is uphill from the southern entrance.

Route18_EastEntrance_1F_Text_CyclingRoad.text: CYCLING ROAD is all uphill from\nhere.$

replies.text: We have found the end where gravity stops being our friend.
Entering from this side changes the same road into a much more demanding climb.
Take it steady. No shame in stopping before the legs give out.
That is a useful warning before the work begins.
A drink and a sensible pace belong in that plan.
The scenic ride has turned the page to its considerably less merciful edition.
The same road, with all its kindness facing the other direction.
Elevation gain ahead. Revise the time and energy estimates.
The road is about to ask more from each turn of the wheels.
A clear warning is kinder than letting someone discover the slope halfway up.
I wonder how many cyclists decide to change plans after hearing that.

contexts.subject: The Safari attendant accepts our decision not to enter.

replies.text: No safari today. The Pokemon can enjoy a visitor-free afternoon from us.
We declined the paid visit. No entry has been purchased.
Fine. We can come back when we are ready.
It is nice to leave the choice open without being hurried.
A better-prepared visit will be more enjoyable anyway.
The proposed expedition has been postponed before its first muddy footstep.
A closed plan, with the door still politely open.
Cancellation handled cleanly. Good service.
The reserve can wait for a different afternoon.
A pleasant answer to someone deciding against the purchase.
I wonder what season the regular visitors enjoy most.

contexts.subject: The Safari attendant refuses entry because we lack the admission fee.

replies.text: The safari has met a more ordinary obstacle than wild Pokemon: the budget.
Insufficient funds prevented entry. No successful admission occurred.
Keep the money we have. We can return later.
An awkward stop, but there is no need to dwell on it.
The team's supplies come before an extra outing.
The expedition has been defeated by arithmetic at the front desk.
A wide reserve, a narrow purse. Another day, perhaps.
Fee requirement not met. No change of route into the reserve.
Some doors wait for coins rather than courage.
We can accept the answer without making the attendant's day harder.
I wonder how many visitors forget to set the entrance fee aside.

contexts.subject: The attendant ends our Safari visit early and asks for remaining Safari Balls.

FuchsiaCity_SafariZone_Entrance_Text_Ple.text: Please return any SAFARI BALLS\nyou may have left.$

replies.text: Adventure concluded early. Return the special equipment and keep the interesting memories.
The remaining Safari Balls belong to the visit and are being collected on exit.
We chose to leave. Hand back the equipment and let the team rest.
There is nothing wrong with ending a visit when you have had enough.
A shorter outing can still be a good one.
The expedition takes a voluntary bow before the final bell.
An early ending does not erase what was pleasant before it.
Equipment return closes the session. Sensible process.
The gate can be the right destination before the clock says so.
A calm exit is better than forcing the day to fill its whole allowance.
I wonder which part of the visit will stay with us most.

contexts.subject: The attendant closes a completed Safari visit and invites us back.

FuchsiaCity_SafariZone_Entrance_Text_Cat.text: Did you catch your fair share?\nCome again!$

replies.text: The day has collected enough little surprises for one visit.
The session ended after its available time or Safari Balls were exhausted.
Done for now. Good time to check how everyone is doing.
A friendly ending makes leaving feel less abrupt.
A quiet rest sounds good after all that searching.
The curtain falls on a collection of encounters the schedule could not have predicted.
Some meetings stay with you even after the gate closes.
Session resources exhausted. Review what happened before planning another.
The reserve keeps its remaining mysteries for another day.
An invitation back is a pleasant finish, whatever the catch count.
I wonder what the attendants enjoy hearing from returning visitors.

contexts.subject: Mom recognizes our choice to set out and says Professor Oak was looking for us.

PalletTown_PlayersHouse_1F_Text_AllBoysL.text: MOM: …Right.\nYou chose your own time to set out.\lIt said so on TV.\pOh, yes. PROF. OAK, next door, was\nlooking for you.$

PalletTown_PlayersHouse_1F_Text_AllGirls.text: MOM: …Right.\nYou chose your own time to set out.\lIt said so on TV.\pOh, yes. PROF. OAK, next door, was\nlooking for you.$

replies.text: She is letting the journey be ours, while still remembering the next-door message.
Her response respects the decision while passing along a practical detail.
Good to know someone is keeping an eye out without holding us back.
Leaving feels different when the person at home understands.
A familiar voice and one useful reminder before we go.
A departure receives parental approval and a modest errand attached.
Home can open its door outward without becoming less home.
Decision acknowledged, relevant message delivered. Efficient family briefing.
The first road begins in a room where somebody knows your name.
She makes room for independence without making it feel lonely.
I wonder how much she guessed before we said anything.

contexts.subject: After resting at home, Mom says we and our Pokemon look well and sends us off.

PalletTown_PlayersHouse_1F_Text_LookingG.text: MOM: Oh, good! You and your\nPOKéMON are looking great.\lTake care now!$

replies.text: Home has inspected the team and approved us for more wandering.
A familiar rest has left both trainer and partners visibly better.
Good. Head out rested instead of proving how tired we can get.
A simple take care can carry more warmth than a long speech.
Nothing fancy. Just a good rest and someone glad to see us well.
The homeward interlude closes with a kindly renewed blessing.
A familiar room has given back a little of what the road took.
Recovery confirmed. Better starting condition for the next outing.
Home has a way of returning your own footsteps to you.
She notices the Pokemon too. That makes the welcome feel complete.
I wonder whether she watches until we are out of sight.

contexts.subject: A parent weighs clever nicknames against simple memorable ones.

ViridianCity_House_Text_NicknamingIsFun.text: Coming up with nicknames is fun,\nbut it's not so easy to do.\pClever names are nice, but simple\nnames are easier to remember.$

replies.text: A clever name is excellent until you have to shout all seven syllables across a field.
Memorability and originality can conflict. The intended use should guide the choice.
Pick something the partner can recognize and you can call clearly.
A simple name can become special through who answers to it.
The name you enjoy saying every day is often the right one.
As a collector of elaborate words, I reluctantly concede the practical argument.
A small familiar word can hold a surprising amount of affection.
Good naming includes retrieval speed. Especially during a hurried moment.
A plain word changes when somebody beloved starts answering it.
Clever is optional. A name that feels right lasts longer.
I wonder which name took them the longest to choose.

contexts.subject: A child proudly says their father also loves Pokemon.

replies.text: That is a lovely thing to be proud of your dad for.
Shared affection can make learning about Pokemon a family activity.
Good. Children notice how the grown-ups treat their partners.
They sound glad to have that interest in common.
A home is warmer when kindness is something a child can point out.
A concise character reference from a deeply invested family member.
A little pride in somebody else's gentleness. Rather lovely.
Good example identified and enthusiastically reported.
The small person has noticed which things make the large one kind.
That is a sweet introduction to someone who is right here.
I wonder what they most enjoy doing with the Pokemon together.

contexts.subject: After handing over Oak's Parcel, the clerk thanks us and asks us to greet Oak.

ViridianCity_Mart_Text_SayHiToOakForMe.text: Okay, thanks! Please say hi to\nPROF. OAK for me, too.$

replies.text: One delivery, with a friendly hello tucked under the wrapping.
The handoff is complete and the clerk has supplied a personal message for the recipient.
Straightforward errand. Keep the parcel safe on the way back.
It is nice when an errand carries a little familiarity between people.
A simple favor can make the next visit to town feel more friendly.
The courier's assignment includes a small conversational attachment.
An ordinary package carrying a little connection between two places.
Parcel received, destination known, extra greeting recorded.
A small journey keeps familiar people in one another's day.
The clerk trusts us with the delivery. We should be careful with it.
I wonder how often Oak orders something from this shop.

contexts.subject: A customer remarks that the Viridian shop sells many Antidotes.

ViridianCity_Mart_Text_ShopDoesGoodBusin.text: This shop does good business in\nANTIDOTES, I've heard.$

replies.text: That is a very practical review of the local wildlife.
Strong demand may reflect the hazards of nearby routes. Useful preparation information.
Worth carrying some before heading toward the forest.
An oddly worrying way to hear a shop is doing well.
Better to buy the useful thing before the team needs it.
The local economy offers a concise warning about what lives outside town.
A successful shop can be an indirect portrait of an unpleasant afternoon.
Sales patterns can reveal local risks. Noted.
The shelves remember what the grass has been doing to travelers.
A useful rumor to hear while we can still choose supplies.
I wonder how many visitors arrive without knowing they need one.

contexts.subject: A customer prepares Potions for unexpected injuries.

ViridianCity_Mart_Text_GotToBuySomePotio.text: I've got to buy some POTIONS.\pYou never know when your POKéMON\nwill need quick healing.$

replies.text: A small bottle of being glad you planned ahead.
Accessible recovery supplies help manage uncertainty on the road.
Good habit. Buy what the team needs before leaving town.
It is reassuring to have an answer ready for a bad moment.
A sensible reserve makes the whole outing less fragile.
The most useful supporting character may be a bottle bought before the plot starts.
An ordinary purchase with a potentially very welcome future.
A spare recovery option is basic redundancy. Good planning.
A little help carried quietly until the right moment arrives.
Practical preparation rarely looks exciting in the shop.
I wonder what they learned to pack after their first long walk.

contexts.subject: A visitor appreciates being invited to use the Pokemon Center PC.

ViridianCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_FeelF.text: Please feel free to use that PC in\nthe corner.\pThe receptionist told me so.\nIt's so kind of her!$

replies.text: A public corner that actually feels welcoming. Nice work by the receptionist.
Clear permission helps newcomers use a shared resource confidently.
Good to be told what is available instead of having to guess.
A small welcome can make an unfamiliar room feel much easier.
Helpful staff can turn a building into a place you are comfortable returning to.
The receptionist has made an ordinary amenity feel like hospitality.
A little permission can lift a surprising amount of hesitation.
