Accessible tool, clear instructions, welcoming introduction. Excellent.
A useful place has left a small light on for strangers.
They remember the kindness as much as the service. That says something.
I wonder how many first-time visitors she has helped settle in.

contexts.subject: A traveler explains that towns ahead have free Pokemon Center healing.

ViridianCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_PokeC.text: There's a POKéMON CENTER in every\ntown ahead.\pThey charge no money, so don't\nbe shy about healing POKéMON.$

replies.text: A road with places to recover along it. That makes the distance feel kinder.
Reliable access to free care can substantially reduce the burden of travel.
Use the help. No reason to keep the team hurting.
It is reassuring to know there will be another welcoming place ahead.
Care should not be the thing we hesitate to ask for.
A network of merciful pauses stitched through the journey.
The world has left some doors open without asking what is in your purse.
Distributed recovery facilities. An excellent piece of regional infrastructure.
A lighted room waits somewhere beyond each long stretch.
A useful reassurance, especially for a traveler counting coins carefully.
I wonder how much easier the road feels once people learn that.

contexts.subject: A visitor explains that Pokemon Centers restore hurt, tired, or fainted Pokemon.

ViridianCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_PokeC.text: POKéMON CENTERS heal your tired,\nhurt, or fainted POKéMON.\pThey make all POKéMON completely\nhealthy.$

replies.text: A place that welcomes the entire list of ways a day can go badly.
The service addresses fatigue and injury as well as fainting.
Bring the team in before things get worse. That is why the help is here.
I like that tired is enough of a reason to come.
A proper recovery is worth making time for.
The journey's troubles meet a reassuringly capable counter.
A place where needing help is an ordinary arrival.
Recovery capability noted. Use it rather than carrying damage into the next test.
A room where the day's sharp edges can be put down.
Clear explanation. Nobody should feel they need to wait until a partner faints.
I wonder how many worried trainers feel better as soon as they reach the door.

contexts.subject: A student is trying hard to memorize their notes.

ViridianCity_School_Text_TryingToMemoriz.text: Whew! I'm trying to memorize all my\nnotes.$

replies.text: That is the sound of a head trying to become a filing cabinet.
Retrieving ideas in small pieces may be easier than repeatedly rereading everything.
Take breaks. A tired head does not learn by being scolded.
I know that feeling when the page seems larger every time you look at it.
A little rest can make the next pass less frustrating.
The notebook's contents are staging a difficult relocation into memory.
Paper remembers things with an unfair lack of effort.
Test one idea at a time. Otherwise it is hard to know what stuck.
Words settle better when given a quiet little space between them.
They sound determined. I hope someone has shown them a manageable method.
I wonder which part keeps slipping away when they close the notebook.

contexts.subject: The teacher advises reading the blackboard carefully.

ViridianCity_School_Text_ReadBlackboardC.text: Okay!\pBe sure to read what's on the\nblackboard carefully!$

replies.text: The important words are already written down. A merciful sort of lecture.
Careful reading matters when similar conditions require different responses.
Worth knowing the basics before a partner needs help.
I appreciate having time to read rather than being asked to remember it instantly.
A little attention here can save panic on the road.
The lesson has wisely taken a form that does not vanish once spoken.
An ordinary board holding several ways to make a bad moment less bad.
Read the labels before the emergency. Excellent general rule.
Small chalk marks can carry someone safely through a difficult day.
Good advice. Careful is the useful part.
I wonder which lesson the teacher wishes travelers remembered best.

contexts.subject: A student objects to us looking at their personal notes.

ViridianCity_School_Text_HeyDontLookAtMy.text: GIRL: Hey!\nDon't look at my notes!$

replies.text: The notebook has an owner. We have discovered this by annoying her.
Personal study notes are not automatically public reference material.
Her notes. Ask before looking.
I would be embarrassed too if someone read over my shoulder.
A little permission would have made this a different conversation.
The unauthorized reader has been removed from the study group.
An open page is not necessarily an open invitation.
Private document. Access denied, clearly enough.
Words can need a little room around them, just like people.
She is allowed a corner of the work that belongs to her.
We should let her study without making the day more awkward.

contexts.subject: A resident tries to teach Nidoran to sit.

replies.text: A small lesson, with a very important little audience.
Consistent, patient cues are more useful than simply repeating them louder.
Give Nidoran time to understand what is being asked.
The quiet everyday practice is rather nice to see.
A little patience makes learning easier for both of them.
The household's smallest performer is rehearsing a very concise routine.
A modest request, potentially a very grand achievement.
Clear cue, patient repetition, then acknowledge the right response.
A little creature is learning one of the household's shared words.
Training can look this ordinary and still matter.
I wonder what Nidoran already knows how to do.

contexts.subject: The family describes the challenges of training a traded Pokemon and wishes for badges.

PewterCity_House1_Text_TradeMonsAreFinic.text:
Our POKéMON's an outsider, so it's
finicky and hard to handle.\pAn outsider is a POKéMON that you
get in a trade.\pIt grows fast, but it may ignore an
unskilled TRAINER in battle.\pIf only we had some BADGES…$

replies.text: A new partner brings its own opinions. Apparently several strong ones.
A traded Pokemon's training requirements can differ from what a novice expects.
Learning to handle a partner takes work. Keep treating it well while learning.
A new home must be an adjustment for Nidoran too.
Patience matters while they learn each other's habits.
The household has discovered that a new cast member does not arrive fully rehearsed.
Being unfamiliar is difficult on both sides of a greeting.
The family needs experience, not simply a stronger command signal.
Two lives learning how to share a room can take time.
I hope they see a partner adjusting, not just a problem to manage.
I wonder whether the original trainer explained Nidoran's habits.

contexts.subject: A resident distinguishes naturally learned moves from those taught by people.

PewterCity_House2_Text_MonsLearnTechniqu.text: POKéMON learn new techniques as\nthey grow.\pBut some moves must be taught to\nthem by people.$

replies.text: Some lessons arrive with growing up. Others require somebody with a lesson plan.
A Pokemon's available techniques can reflect both development and instruction.
Pay attention to what the partner learns and what it still needs help with.
It is interesting how many different ways there are to learn.
Knowing which kind of lesson is needed saves a lot of waiting.
The repertoire grows through experience, with occasional outside editing.
Not every new thing has to be discovered alone.
Built-in learning and external instruction. Useful distinction.
Some doors open with time; others need someone to show the handle.
Good advice for anyone assuming every useful move will simply appear.
I wonder which lesson first made them notice the difference.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that status conditions aid capture but never guarantee it.

PewterCity_House2_Text_MonsEasierCatchIf.text:
A POKéMON becomes easier to 
catch if it has a status problem.\pSleep, poison, burn, or paralysis…
Those are all effective.\pBut catching POKéMON is never
a sure thing!$

replies.text: A better chance is still a chance. The Pokemon has not signed the paperwork.
Status can influence capture probability without making the outcome certain.
Know the risk to the Pokemon. Do not keep hurting it out of frustration.
I appreciate the reminder that a creature is not a guaranteed result.
A calm, careful attempt is better than treating a failed throw as an insult.
The lesson ends with a sensible warning against a guaranteed happy ending.
An advantage is not an entitlement. Worth remembering.
Probability improved, certainty unchanged. Important distinction.
A living creature is not obliged to become the answer you hoped for.
That final caution is as useful as the technique itself.
I wonder how many beginners expect the first useful trick to work every time.

contexts.subject: A customer regrets paying a shady seller for a weak fish Pokemon.

PewterCity_Mart_Text_BoughtWeirdFishFrom.text: A shady old guy sucked me into\nbuying this weird fish POKéMON!\pIt's totally weak and it cost ¥500!$

replies.text: Be annoyed with the salesman. The fish did not write the sales pitch.
The misleading transaction and the Pokemon's worth are separate questions.
The seller made the promises. Treat the partner properly.
I hope the fish does not become the target of that disappointment.
A bad purchase story can still become a good partnership with time.
The persuasive merchant has departed, leaving the innocent supporting fish with the review.
A creature should not have to answer for the person who sold it.
Bad sales information does not make the received partner defective.
A small life has arrived wrapped in somebody else's dishonest words.
The poor fish was the only participant who did not choose the deal.
I wonder whether the new trainer has given it a real chance yet.

contexts.subject: A customer encourages patient care for apparently weak Pokemon.

PewterCity_Mart_Text_GoodThingsIfRaiseMo.text: Good things can happen if you raise\nPOKéMON diligently.\pEven the weak ones can surprise\nyou if you don't give up on them.$

replies.text: A little faith gives a small partner room to surprise everybody.
Sustained care can reveal capabilities that an early impression misses.
Give the team time. Nobody begins at their best.
It is lovely advice to hear beside all the bottles for quick improvements.
Daily care may be quiet work, but it adds up.
The unassuming cast member is being allowed a proper character arc.
An ordinary creature can become extraordinary company before anybody notices its strength.
Long-term investment beats judging the first test result alone.
Some things need a season before the first visible sign.
Being patient with a partner is a good look on anyone.
I wonder which Pokemon taught them that lesson.

contexts.subject: A caller reacts to news of Team Rocket at Mt. Moon and snaps at our interruption.

PewterCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_TeamRoc.text: What!?\pTEAM ROCKET is at MT. MOON?\nHuh?\pI'm on the phone!\nScram!$

replies.text: Bad news, bad timing, and apparently we supplied the interruption.
The caller is occupied with worrying news. We should not assume we heard the full account.
Give them space. We can remember the warning about Mt. Moon.
They sound alarmed. I would rather let them finish the call.
It is no time to press for a conversation they did not choose.
A tense call has acquired an unwelcome live audience. We can remove that part.
Worry makes an ordinary interruption feel much sharper.
Partial report received. Better to seek reliable details later.
A small receiver has made the room feel less safe.
The tone was rough, but the news clearly upset them.
I wonder who is calling from near the mountain.

contexts.subject: A visitor grows sleepy while explaining Jigglypuff's song.

PewterCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_WhenJig.text: Yawn!\pWhen JIGGLYPUFF sings, POKéMON get\ndrowsy…\p…Me, too…\nSnore…$

replies.text: The explanation has become its own demonstration. Very convincing.
The listener's drowsiness appears to support the reported effect of the song.
At least this is a safe place to get sleepy.
An audience drifting off does not always mean the singer did badly.
A comfortable chair would be useful right about now.
The review concludes with the critic unconscious. A decisive endorsement.
A soft song quietly winning an argument with wakefulness.
Observed effect matches the warning. Very efficient teaching.
A room full of small breaths slowing into the same rhythm.
That is a lovely sound to underestimate at your peril.
I wonder whether anyone ever makes it to the end of the song awake.

contexts.subject: A child plans to trade Clefairy for a wanted Pikachu.

PewterCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trading.text: I really want a PIKACHU, so I'm\ntrading my CLEFAIRY for one.$

replies.text: A new partner is exciting. I hope Clefairy is headed somewhere kind too.
A successful exchange should account for the needs of both Pokemon.
Be sure both trainers understand the deal and can care for the new partner.
I hope they have thought about saying goodbye as well as saying hello.
A good new home matters on both sides of the trade.
The desired arrival deserves a thoughtful farewell for the departing companion.
A change can be welcome and still have a tender edge.
Two transfers, two sets of care requirements. Check both.
One little friendship changes shape as another begins.
Wanting a particular look is only the start of choosing a partner.
I wonder what made Pikachu the one they wanted.

contexts.subject: Another trainer explains trading one of two Pikachu with the child.

PewterCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trading.text: I'm trading POKéMON with that kid\nthere.\pI had two PIKACHU, so I figured\nI might as well trade one.$

replies.text: Both trainers want a change. That is a promising place to start.
The exchange offers each trainer something different from their current collection.
Make sure the new trainer knows how to look after Pikachu.
Having two does not make the one leaving any less individual.
A little advice about Pikachu's habits would be a good parting gift.
A familiar companion finds a new role in somebody else's story.
Two similar creatures can still leave very different spaces behind.
Useful swap, provided the handoff includes more than the Poke Ball.
An ordinary exchange carries a small life across a large change.
I hope the choice considers the particular Pikachu, not just the duplicate slot.
I wonder which habits the new trainer will discover first.

contexts.subject: The museum attendant accepts our decision not to buy admission.

replies.text: The ancient bones can wait. They are unusually experienced at it.
We declined admission and can return when the visit suits our plans.
No rush. Better visit when we have time to look properly.
It is nice to leave an interesting place for a day when you can enjoy it.
A museum is worth more than a hurried dash between errands.
The prehistoric cast remains available for a later audience.
Some old things will not mind another quiet afternoon.
No transaction, no complication. Straightforward.
The past is not going anywhere before we come back.
A polite ending leaves the future visit feeling welcome.
I wonder which exhibit would catch our eye first next time.

contexts.subject: The museum attendant welcomes us after admission or invites us to enjoy an existing visit.

replies.text: Permission to stare at remarkable old things. Happily accepted.
A chance to inspect evidence of lives and events far beyond ordinary experience.
Good place to slow down and look carefully.
A quiet visit sounds lovely after the road.
A little time indoors with something interesting is a good use of an afternoon.
The audience is admitted; the ancient cast has been ready for some time.
A room where being old and strange is considered an accomplishment.
Time to examine the exhibits. I have questions about the displays.
A quiet doorway into things that lasted longer than their own days.
A welcoming introduction matters even in a room full of objects.
I wonder which exhibit visitors linger beside longest.

contexts.subject: The museum attendant cannot admit us because we lack the fee.

replies.text: Even the past has a ticket counter. Another day, perhaps.
The fee could not be paid, so the admission did not proceed.
Keep the supplies budget. We can return later.
An awkward answer, but no reason to be embarrassed.
An interesting visit will still be here when we can spare the money.
Our historical ambitions have met a very present-day accounting issue.
The ancient world waits beyond a rather ordinary small sum.
Budget constraint. Delay the optional visit.
The door can wait without making the world behind it smaller.
A declined ticket is a practical detail, not a judgment.
I wonder whether the outdoor part has anything worth seeing meanwhile.

contexts.subject: The museum worker describes ancient Pokemon genetic material in amber and resurrection research.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_AmberContainsG.text: AMBER contains the genetic matter\nof ancient POKéMON.\pThere's a LAB somewhere trying to\nresurrect POKéMON from AMBER.$

replies.text: A little tree sap kept an ancient instruction book. Trees are excellent accidental librarians.
Preserved genetic material could be scientifically valuable. The reported research is remarkable.
Worth serious study. Ancient life deserves careful handling if it returns.
It is strange to think something so old might carry enough of a life to begin again.
An extraordinary idea needs patient, careful people working on it.
A golden fragment holds the possibility of a very old character returning to the page.
A small hard thing holding a soft possibility for longer than we can imagine.
Information preserved across that much time! The reconstruction problem is astonishing.
A tree's old wound may have kept a way back for something lost.
It makes that small piece of amber feel much larger.
I wonder what first convinced researchers the material could still be useful.

contexts.subject: The worker explains that amber began as tree sap that hardened over time.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_AmberIsFossili.text: AMBER is actually sap, that gooey\nstuff that oozes from trees.\pThe ancient sap fossilized over\ntime to become rock-hard AMBER.$

replies.text: A tree made something sticky, and time turned it into museum material. Nice teamwork.
A familiar biological material can become a durable record through fossilization.
Good reminder that remarkable things can begin very ordinarily.
I like knowing the simple beginning behind that golden color.
Something once messy became worth keeping carefully.
A modest woodland substance has enjoyed a spectacularly long career change.
Time has a peculiar talent for making old messes beautiful.
Natural material changing properties across a very long process. Fascinating.
The tree let go of a little golden time.
Knowing what it began as makes the finished thing more interesting.
I wonder how many visitors guessed its origin before hearing that.

contexts.subject: An older visitor is grateful to have lived long enough to see dragon bones.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_ShouldBeGratef.text: I should be grateful for my long\nlife.\pNever did I think I would get to\nsee the bones of a dragon!$

replies.text: An old visitor meeting a much older surprise. That is lovely.
An unfamiliar discovery can remain meaningful at any age.
Good to still find something that makes the day feel new.
There is so much wonder in that one small sentence.
I hope there are more unexpected good days waiting for them.
A long life has saved room for one astonishing late chapter.
Growing old without exhausting your capacity to be amazed. A fine ambition.
Decades of experience, still delighted by new evidence. Excellent outlook.
An old pair of eyes finding one more reason to stay curious.
Wonder suits people at every age.
I wonder what they imagined dragons looked like before seeing the bones.

contexts.subject: The researcher asks us to get the Old Amber examined after entrusting it to us.

replies.text: The secret is portable now. We should carry it carefully.
The next step is examination by an appropriate laboratory, rather than assuming the hypothesis.
Get it checked. Keep it safe until then.
He sounds hopeful enough that the request feels very important to him.
A careful delivery matters when someone trusts us with something irreplaceable.
The scientific mystery has left the museum in a travel-sized form.
A little old thing carrying a very new hope.
Independent examination is the right next test. We can handle the transport.
Someone's quiet hope has been placed in our hands.
He is trusting us to take the idea seriously. We should.
I wonder what he hopes the lab will find first.

contexts.subject: A museum visitor notes the two rare prehistoric Pokemon fossil exhibits.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_WeHaveTwoFossi.text: We have two fossils of rare,\nprehistoric POKéMON on exhibit.$

replies.text: Two very old introductions. They have been waiting a while for visitors.
A small collection can still preserve significant evidence of past species.
Worth looking properly. Fragile history does not get a replacement.
It is strange to stand near the shape of a life that old.
Only two displays, but plenty to spend time thinking about.
An ancient double bill, with an exceptionally long interval since the first appearance.
Two silences that still have quite a lot to say.
Two specimens, countless questions. A promising ratio.
The room keeps a little of a vanished world upright.
A small exhibit can be more memorable than a crowded one.
I wonder which fossil people recognize first.

contexts.subject: A visitor doubts that the ordinary-looking Moon Stone is special.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_WhatsSpecialAb.text: MOON STONE, huh?\pWhat's so special about it?\nLooks like an ordinary rock to me.$

replies.text: A rock is excellent at keeping its qualifications to itself.
Appearance alone is insufficient to determine a material's properties.
Ordinary-looking things can still matter. Worth reading the label.
I understand the surprise. The name promises more than the shape reveals.
A quiet appearance does not make something less useful.
The exhibit has been challenged to look more impressive on demand.
Some strange things have the manners to look completely ordinary.
External casing tells you less than you think. Test the properties.
A secret can be small enough to fit in an unremarkable stone.
The display might need a better explanation, rather than a shinier rock.
I wonder what they expected it to look like.

contexts.subject: An older visitor recalls buying a color TV to watch the 1969 Moon landing news.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_BoughtColorTVF.text: July 20, 1969!\pHumankind first set foot on the\nmoon that day.\pI bought a color TV just so I\ncould watch that news.$

replies.text: A new television for a very new view of the world. Memorable shopping trip.
A major event can anchor a very precise personal memory.
Some days make people remember exactly where they were.
I like hearing how a huge event fits inside an ordinary living room.
They kept the excitement all these years. That is lovely.
An immense human milestone remembered partly through the furniture bought to witness it.
A room lit by something far beyond the room. A good memory.
A whole new viewing setup for one extraordinary event. I understand completely.
A distant footprint left a small bright mark in someone's home.
The purchase is part of the memory now, not just the picture.
I wonder who gathered around the screen with them.

contexts.subject: A museum staffer points out this month's space exhibit.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_RunningSpaceEx.text: This month, we're running a space\nexhibit.$

replies.text: Old bones downstairs, very large questions upstairs. Good museum range.
A rotating exhibit gives familiar visitors a reason to return.
Worth taking the time if we are already here.
I like when a familiar building still has something new to show.
A quiet way to spend an afternoon without going very far.
The program has expanded from ancient lives to a rather larger setting.
A room that makes the sky feel a little less empty.
Space hardware! I would like a close look at the mechanisms.
A little building keeping room for an enormous outside.
A changing exhibit keeps the place from feeling frozen in time.
I wonder what they chose as the centerpiece.

contexts.subject: A child excitedly wants their father to catch a Pikachu.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_AskedDaddyToCa.text: I want a PIKACHU!\nIt's so cute!\pI asked my daddy to catch me one!$

replies.text: One very specific wish, delivered at full small-person enthusiasm.
The interest is clear; the responsibilities of caring for a Pokemon still need discussion.
Hope the grown-up explains the care as well as the catching.
It is sweet how much happiness they can fit into saying one name.
A new companion needs a ready home, not just an excited welcome.
The requested addition to the family has an enthusiastic advance review.
A small person imagines an equally small new friend.
Clear request. Now someone needs to check the care requirements.
A little wish with ears and a bright yellow shape.
They know exactly what they like. The practical details come next.
I wonder whether they have ever met a Pikachu close up.

contexts.subject: The father promises his child a Pikachu soon.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_PikachuSoonIPr.text: Yeah, a PIKACHU soon, I promise!$

replies.text: That promise may be more difficult than the very short sentence suggests.
A specific promise creates an expectation that practical preparation should support.
Make sure the home is ready before bringing one back.
He sounds fond, and perhaps a little overwhelmed by the repeated request.
A promise about a living companion deserves more care than a surprise toy.
The parental contract has been renewed under energetic negotiation.
A little promise can become very large in a child's memory.
Commitment recorded. Supplies and care plan should follow.
Soon can stretch a long way for someone small.
I hope he means the promise, rather than simply ending the conversation.
I wonder whether he has started finding out where Pikachu live.

contexts.subject: The bicycle clerk ends a visit; this same goodbye follows refusal, cancellation, or voucher exchange.

replies.text: A polite finish, whether we came to browse or had the right paperwork.
This goodbye alone does not establish which transaction, if any, took place.
We are done here for now. Check what we actually have before heading out.
A friendly goodbye makes it easy to come back with questions.
Good to finish the conversation before planning the next trip.
The shop closes this scene with a versatile line of retail courtesy.
An ordinary farewell, wisely vague about the contents of our pockets.
Interaction complete. Verify the resulting equipment before choosing the route.
The door opens back onto whatever road we are ready for.
A courteous ending does not need to make a sales pitch.
I wonder how many people return just to ask another bike question.

contexts.subject: The bicycle clerk asks about our bike and recommends roads and caves for riding.

CeruleanCity_BikeShop_Text_HowDoYouLikeN.text: How do you like your new BICYCLE?\nDo you like how it rides?\pYou can take it out on CYCLING\nROAD and even into caves!$

replies.text: He sold the wheels and kept some enthusiasm for the journeys afterward.
A follow-up about actual use is welcome after the equipment handoff.
Good bike. Still need to watch the ground in a cave.
It is nice when somebody remembers that the purchase was the beginning.
A helpful suggestion can turn a useful thing into a favorite part of the day.
The bicycle's next chapter receives a cheerful endorsement from its former custodian.
A little machine opens more of the road to ordinary afternoons.
A use recommendation! Cave riding still deserves careful visibility checks.
Two wheels can change how far away a place feels.
He seems to care whether it is a good fit after it leaves the shop.
I wonder which route he recommends to someone testing a new bike.

contexts.subject: A shopper prefers a practical city bicycle with a shopping basket.

CeruleanCity_BikeShop_Text_CityBikeGoodE.text: A plain city bike is good enough\nfor me.\pAfter all, you can't put a shopping\nbasket on a mountain bike.$

replies.text: A basket is a strong argument. Hills cannot carry your groceries home for you.
The preferred design matches the actual use case rather than maximum performance.
Buy the tool for the job you do. Sensible.
I like someone knowing what they need without apologizing for it.
A shopping basket is excellent bicycle technology in my opinion.
An unfashionably persuasive defense of arriving home with the purchases intact.
A small useful thing often makes a daily life better than a grand impressive one.
Requirements first, equipment second. Exactly the right order.
A quiet machine for carrying the ordinary things that keep a home going.
Practical can be a style of its own when it suits the person.
I wonder what route they take for their regular shopping.

contexts.subject: A youngster admires the bicycles but balks at their cost.

CeruleanCity_BikeShop_Text_BikesCoolButE.text: These bikes are cool, but they're\nway expensive!$

replies.text: The bicycle is shiny. The price has a much sharper edge.
Admiration does not make an item affordable. A sensible distinction.
Good to look before spending. No need to buy beyond your means.
It is difficult when something appealing feels so far out of reach.
A planned purchase is nicer than a long regret over the cost.
The display has made an excellent impression; the price tag has staged a rebuttal.
A beautiful thing can remain something you simply look at.
Desirable specification, unacceptable cost. Common engineering problem.
The little gap between wanting and having can look very wide in a shop.
They have an eye for the design and a reasonable concern about the bill.
I wonder whether they are saving for one or just enjoying the display.

contexts.subject: The youngster admires the bike we now own.

replies.text: Our wheels have received a very enthusiastic outside review.
They noticed the new equipment immediately. It clearly made an impression.
Nice compliment. The useful part is how it rides.
A little unexpected admiration can make you feel rather visible.
It is fun when someone shares your pleasure in a new thing.
The bicycle makes its public debut to encouraging critical notices.
A small bright moment of shared appreciation.
Positive user-adjacent feedback! I still want to check the mechanism.
Two circles have acquired a surprising amount of attention.
A sincere compliment with no little sting attached. Lovely.
I wonder which detail of the bike first caught their eye.

contexts.subject: A resident describes Team Rocket damaging his home and stealing an expensive Dig TM.

CeruleanCity_House2_Text_RocketsStoleTMF.text:
Those miserable ROCKETS!\pLook what they've done to my
house!\pThey stole a TM for teaching
POKéMON how to DIG holes!\pI was going to use it on a
MANKEY or a SANDSHREW…\pThat cost me a bundle, it did!$

replies.text: A home should not become somebody else's shortcut to stealing things.
The damage and the stolen purchase are separate harms he has to deal with.
They broke into his home. He deserves help getting it put right.
Hearing him explain what he had planned for it makes the loss feel personal.
The repair work and the lost money are a lot to leave one household with.
A criminal escapade leaves an ordinary person counting damage in the room he lives in.
A familiar place should not become evidence of someone else's cruelty.
Broken property, stolen tool, disrupted plans. That is real damage.
They put a hole through more than a wall.
He had a plan for something he paid for. They took both the thing and his peace.
I wonder who is helping them make the house secure again.

contexts.subject: After losing the Dig TM, the resident makes a new plan to teach Diglett.

CeruleanCity_House2_Text_TeachDiglettDig.text: I figure what's lost is lost.\pI decided to teach DIGLETT how to\nDIG without a TM.$

replies.text: A bad day has not managed to steal his entire next plan. Good.
He has found an alternative approach suited to another Pokemon.
He should not have had to adapt. Glad he has something to work toward.
It is nice to hear a little resolve returning to the room.
A practical new plan can make a damaged day feel less stuck.
The stolen prop will not be allowed to cancel the whole production.
A small beginning growing around an ugly interruption.
A different tool may solve the same problem. Good adaptation.
The next path can begin beside the place someone broke.
He is choosing what comes next without pretending the theft was fine.
I wonder whether working with Diglett will become something he really enjoys.

contexts.subject: The other resident bitterly jokes about Team Rocket digging into trouble.

CeruleanCity_House2_Text_TeamRocketTryin.text: TEAM ROCKET must be trying to DIG\ntheir way into no good!$

replies.text: A very literal crime has left room for a very pointed joke.
Wordplay can express frustration without making the damage less serious.
The joke is fair. So is being angry about the house.
Sometimes a little humor is the only part of a bad situation you can choose.
I hope the practical repairs are getting as much attention as the anger.
An apt line, delivered from a home that supplied far too much research material.
A dry remark from somebody with plenty of reason not to feel amused.
Unfortunate practical demonstration. The criticism is accurate enough.
A sharp little word left beside a much larger hurt.
At least the joke points toward the people responsible.
I wonder whether they have been able to sleep comfortably since it happened.

contexts.subject: A woman encourages us to discuss trading Pokemon with her husband.

CeruleanCity_House3_Text_PleaseTradeWith.text: My husband likes trading POKéMON.\pYou're collecting POKéMON for your\nPOKéDEX, aren't you?\pWould you please trade with him?$

replies.text: He has a very effective personal introductions department.
A trade could benefit both collections if their requirements align.
We can hear the offer without owing anyone a trade.
It is nice that she wants to help him meet someone with the same interest.
A good exchange still needs to suit both people and both Pokemon.
The enthusiast's spouse has taken charge of recruiting a potential audience.
A little household matchmaking, but for Pokemon collections.
An invitation to compare needs. Sensible first step.
A shared interest can make a stranger feel closer to the table.
She sounds keen, though the actual choice stays with the people trading.
I wonder whether he has been waiting for a particular partner.

contexts.subject: A customer explains that Repel effectiveness depends on the leading Pokemon.

CeruleanCity_Mart_Text_RepelWorksOnWeakM.text:
REPEL not only keeps bugs away,
it also works on weak POKéMON.\pPut your strongest POKéMON at the
left of the POKéMON LIST.\pIf your first POKéMON is strong,
REPEL's effect is boosted.$

replies.text: The bottle and the front of the team have to agree on the plan.
Lead strength influences the encounters Repel can suppress. Useful preparation detail.
Check the lead before relying on the bottle.
A small detail that would be easy to miss until the grass interrupted.
Good to learn the condition while we still have time to organize the team.
The repellent's performance apparently includes a casting requirement.
Even a promise of quiet has its qualifications.
Effect depends on configuration. Always check the settings first.
The one walking first changes which meetings the road allows.
Clear advice. The label alone might leave that part out.
I wonder how many trainers discover the connection by accident.

contexts.subject: A shopper describes Rare Candy as unavailable in shops and capable of rapid growth.

CeruleanCity_Mart_Text_DoYouKnowAboutRar.text: Do you know about RARE CANDY?\nThey don't sell it in shops.\pI think it makes POKéMON grow\nvery quickly all of a sudden.$

replies.text: A sweet with an unusually ambitious side effect. Not ordinary pocket candy.
They describe a rare growth aid, though their wording makes the knowledge secondhand.
Treat it as a useful item, not a substitute for knowing the partner.
It sounds remarkable. I would want to understand it before using one.
Definitely label that carefully before anybody mistakes it for dessert.
A confection whose promised results greatly exceed an ordinary sugar rush.
A small wrapped thing with a much less small consequence.
Rapid change from a tiny item. I would like to know the mechanism.
Some sweets carry more than sweetness into a day.
The word rare seems to be doing real work if the shop cannot sell it.
I wonder who first told them what it does.

contexts.subject: A visitor repeats vague rumors that Bill goes to great lengths for rare Pokemon.

CeruleanCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_BillD.text: That BILL!\pI heard that he'll do whatever it\ntakes to get rare POKéMON.\pHe's not above doing all sorts\nof things, I've heard.$

replies.text: That is a lot of rumor with not much actual event attached.
Vague secondhand claims provide little basis for judging his conduct.
Ask what he actually did before repeating that.
I would rather hear from him than decide who he is from whispers.
Being enthusiastic does not make every rumor about you fair.
An impressive cloud of insinuation, with the details conspicuously absent.
A person can disappear under other people's unfinished sentences.
Need specifics and a reliable source before drawing conclusions.
A name travels faster when nobody asks what is carrying it.
That sounds designed to invite assumptions without having to defend them.
I wonder whether the speaker has ever actually met Bill.

contexts.subject: Another visitor thinks criticism of Bill's Pokemon enthusiasm is jealousy.

CeruleanCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Every.text: Have you heard about BILL?\pEveryone calls him a POKéMANIAC!\pI think people are just jealous of\nBILL, though.\pWho wouldn't want to boast about\ntheir POKéMON?$

replies.text: A collection can be impressive without making every critic jealous. Still, let him enjoy it.
Jealousy is one possible explanation, not something we can establish from the nickname.
Judge how he treats the Pokemon. The nickname tells us little.
It is kind that someone wants to give him a fair hearing.
A sincere interest deserves more than being reduced to gossip.
The defense has an energetic advocate, though its evidence remains mostly enthusiasm.
People are allowed a little oddness around the things they love.
Both the rumor and its explanation need better data.
A strange name can conceal an ordinary person caring very deeply.
Good to push back on mockery without pretending we know everyone's motives.
I wonder what the speaker likes most about Bill's collection.

contexts.subject: A local admires Bill's large collection, including rare Pokemon.

CeruleanCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_BillC.text: BILL has lots of POKéMON!\nHe collects rare ones, too!$

replies.text: His reputation has a very busy household behind it.
Maintaining a varied collection involves a substantial amount of knowledge and care.
A lot of partners means a lot of responsibility.
They sound impressed in a simple, unguarded way.
The daily care behind that collection must be considerable.
A brief review of a collection too extensive for a brief visit.
A person's curiosity can fill a surprisingly large part of a town's conversation.
Variety is interesting. I would want to know how he organizes the care.
Many little lives gathered under one very curious roof.
Admiration without a nasty rumor attached. A refreshing change.
I wonder which of his partners the local knows best.

contexts.subject: A visitor recommends trading with friends for varied Pokemon and faster growth.

CeruleanCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_TryTr.text:
Why don't you go upstairs and try
trading POKéMON with your friends?\pYou could get a lot more variety
by trading.\pThe POKéMON you get in trades grow
quickly, too.$

replies.text: Friends can introduce us to Pokemon our own road has not met yet.
Trading can broaden a collection and alter training considerations.
Talk through the trade. Make sure the new partner fits the team.
Knowing the person on the other side would make the change feel easier.
A trade is worth considering for the partnership, not just quick progress.
The upstairs invitation promises a wider cast through friendly negotiation.
The world can grow larger through someone else's familiar companion.
Useful option. Different partners bring different requirements as well as benefits.
A friend can open a road that does not appear on the map.
A good exchange gives both sides something they actually want.
I wonder what unusual partner someone upstairs has brought today.

contexts.subject: After giving the Old Rod, the Fishing Guru encourages fishing in seas and rivers.

VermilionCity_House1_Text_FishingIsAWayO.text: Fishing is a way of life!\nIt is like the finest poetry.\pFrom the seas to rivers, go out\nand land the big one, my friend.$

replies.text: He has given us the starter equipment for a very patient kind of adventure.
Trying multiple habitats is sensible advice for a new angler.
Generous gift. No need to rush the first catch.
He seems glad to have somebody new to share it with.
A quiet hour beside the water could be a good use of this.
A new pupil is sent forth with a rod and a warmly oversized philosophy.
A little tool for meeting the things beneath a quiet surface.
Basic equipment, broad field opportunities. Good beginning.
The still water has become somewhere we can ask a small question.
He gives the welcome as enthusiastically as the equipment.
I wonder where he would recommend casting for the very first time.

contexts.subject: The Fishing Guru is disappointed when we say fishing does not interest us.

replies.text: He had a whole fishing friendship ready to unfold. Perhaps another visitor.
An honest answer can disappoint without being unkind.
We do not need to pretend. He can keep enjoying it.
It is difficult to say no when the question comes with that much hope.
A different hobby can still make a perfectly good afternoon.
The proposed fellowship has found a small incompatibility at its founding meeting.
Not every shoreline needs to become everyone's favorite place.
Interest not shared. No benefit in forcing the next step.
The river still has plenty of other people to call toward it.
A polite refusal is better than a borrowed enthusiasm that disappears tomorrow.
I wonder what he talks about with visitors who do not fish.

contexts.subject: The Fishing Guru remembers us and asks about our fishing.

VermilionCity_House1_Text_HowAreTheFishB.text: Hello there, {PLAYER}!\pHow are the fish biting?$

replies.text: We have a regular fishing correspondent now. Updates may contain splashing.
He is interested in how we used the equipment he shared.
Good of him to remember. Makes a return visit easy.
A familiar greeting can make the little house feel welcoming at once.
A hobby is nicer when somebody wants to hear the ordinary stories too.
The mentor requests the next dispatch from the waterfront.
An ordinary question that makes it clear he kept a place for us in mind.
Follow-up support! He seems genuinely invested in the outcome.
The water has given us another small reason to visit someone.
He has turned a one-time gift into an ongoing acquaintance.
I wonder whether he has a good catch story ready to share in return.

contexts.subject: The local trader accepts our decision not to trade.

replies.text: A proposed swap has ended without any swapping. Everyone keeps their original companions.
The refusal leaves the trade uncompleted and the existing arrangement intact.
No deal today. We are allowed to decide that.
A little disappointment, but nobody needs to force it.
Better to wait for an exchange both sides actually want.
The negotiation concludes before the cast changes hands.
A small no can save a much more difficult regret.
Requirements did not align. Cancel cleanly and move on.
Some roads meet without anyone needing to change directions.
They accepted the answer. That matters.
I wonder whether they have been hoping to make this trade for long.

contexts.subject: The trader rejects the selected Pokemon because it is not the requested species.

VermilionCity_House2_Text_ThisIsNoMon.text: …This is no {STR_VAR_1}.\pIf you get one, please trade it\nto me!$

replies.text: A different introduction from the one they had arranged. Fair enough to decline.
The selected species did not meet the specified trade condition.
Wrong partner for this offer. We can leave it there.
An awkward selection, but not a serious problem.
Both sides should get what they actually agreed to.
The casting call has a specific role, and this visitor belongs to another story.
A mismatch, not a flaw in the Pokemon. An important little difference.
Validation caught the wrong input. No transfer should follow.
A companion is not made less worthy by arriving at the wrong door.
The request was specific. The refusal can stay simple.
I wonder how often a visitor selects the wrong one by accident.

contexts.subject: The local trader thanks us after completing the in-game trade.

replies.text: A new hello and a grateful goodbye in the same little moment.
The trade completed before the thanks. Both trainers now have new care responsibilities.
Deal done. Get to know the new partner properly.
I hope both Pokemon find the next part of their lives comfortable.
A little familiar advice can help a new partner settle in.
The exchange concludes with a modest line for a fairly large change.
A new name in the group, an old companion beginning somewhere else.
Transfer confirmed. Time to check the new partner's needs and habits.
Two small journeys have crossed and continued in different hands.
A sincere thank-you makes the handoff feel considered.
I wonder which habit we will notice about our new companion first.

contexts.subject: The trader asks after the Pokemon given to us and reports that ours is doing well.

VermilionCity_House2_Text_HowIsMyOldMon.text: How is my old {STR_VAR_2}?\pMy {STR_VAR_1} is doing great!$

replies.text: They remembered the friend who left, not just the one who arrived. I like that.
A follow-up on both Pokemon gives the exchange a reassuring continuity.
Good to hear the partner is doing well. Good that they asked about ours too.
It is lovely when a new home does not erase the old person's care.
A short visit can reassure both sides after a big change.
The former cast members receive a warm update from their next chapters.
Affection does not always stop at the edge of an exchange.
Post-transfer check-in. Excellent practical and personal follow-through.
A thread between two homes remains pleasantly unbroken.
They sound interested rather than possessive. That is a good balance.
I wonder what new little habit their new partner has shown them.

contexts.subject: A resident sends a letter north to Saffron with Pidgey.

VermilionCity_House3_Text_PidgeyFlyLette.text: I'm getting my PIDGEY to fly a\nletter to SAFFRON in the north.$

replies.text: A little bird carrying a piece of somebody's day across town lines.
A familiar route and a trained messenger can make a dependable communication system.
Hope the route is safe for Pidgey. Important cargo still needs a safe trip.
A letter feels more personal when you can picture the bird carrying it.
It is nice to keep in touch in a way someone has taken time over.
The correspondence has acquired an exceptionally feathered courier.
A small warm body carrying words that cannot fly by themselves.
Light payload, capable carrier, clear destination. Practical arrangement.
A little folded voice traveling under a pair of wings.
An ordinary errand with rather lovely details.
I wonder whether Pidgey recognizes the person at the other end.

contexts.subject: The resident wants to exchange Mail with many people through the Union Room.

VermilionCity_House3_Text_SendMyPidgeyTo.text: I want to exchange MAIL with all\nsorts of people.\pI send my PIDGEY to a UNION ROOM\nto exchange MAIL for me.$

replies.text: Pidgey is helping them meet more pen pals than their own feet can manage.
A wider correspondence network can introduce a useful variety of perspectives.
A nice interest. Keep the messages and the messenger safe.
I like that the goal is hearing from different people.
A small note can make a stranger's day unexpectedly friendly.
The postal project has ambitions beyond its original neighborhood.
A collection of words from people who might otherwise remain far away.
More contacts means more organization. I hope they label the replies.
Many little voices, folded into the same welcoming place.
Mail makes a personal exchange feel like something you can keep.
I wonder what they like asking someone in a first letter.

contexts.subject: A shopper condemns Team Rocket for trafficking and abandoning Pokemon deemed useless.

VermilionCity_Mart_Text_TeamRocketAreWic.text:
There are wicked people who will
use POKéMON for criminal acts.\pTEAM ROCKET traffics in rare
POKéMON, for example.\pThey also abandon POKéMON that
they consider unpopular or useless.\pThat's the sort of horrid people
they are, TEAM ROCKET.$

replies.text: A Pokemon's worth is not whatever a criminal can sell it for.
They describe exploitation followed by neglect. Both place the Pokemon's welfare at risk.
Using partners and throwing them away is rotten. No excuse.
I hate thinking of a Pokemon waiting for someone who simply decided it was not useful.
A living companion deserves care even when it cannot do what someone hoped.
A business model with cruelty in every stage of the transaction.
Calling a creature useless says far more about the speaker.
A plan that treats living beings as disposable parts is a bad plan at its foundation.
Something abandoned still has a life after the person stops looking.
Popularity is a dreadful measure of whether a creature deserves a home.
I wonder who helps the Pokemon left behind by them.

contexts.subject: A shopper thinks a Pokemon's behavior depends on its trainer.

VermilionCity_Mart_Text_MonsGoodOrBadDep.text: I think POKéMON can be good or\nbad. It depends on the TRAINER.$

replies.text: The person holding the treats does have a lot of influence. Still, Pokemon have their own minds.
Training strongly influences behavior without making a Pokemon merely an extension of its trainer.
Trainers are responsible for what they teach and allow.
I hope people remember that a badly treated Pokemon can need help too.
A kind routine can make a real difference to how a partner feels around people.
The director bears responsibility, though the cast is more than a set of puppets.
A creature can learn fear from someone and still deserve a gentler life.
Input matters, but a living partner is not a predictable machine.
The hands beside a creature can teach it whether the world is safe.
A good reminder for people blaming the Pokemon while ignoring the trainer.
I wonder what experience made the shopper think about that.

contexts.subject: A visitor explains differences between same-level Pokemon and the effects of training.

VermilionCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trai.text: Even if they are the same level,\nPOKéMON can have very different\lstats and abilities.\pA POKéMON raised by a TRAINER is\nstronger than one in the wild.$

replies.text: A level is one number, not the entire Pokemon's introduction.
Equal levels do not imply equal attributes. Training history and individual traits matter.
Look at the actual partner. Do not let one number do all the thinking.
It is reassuring that the little differences between partners still count.
Careful training means paying attention to those differences.
The single-number biography has been found wanting. Entirely fair.
Two lives can reach the same milestone by very different roads.
One summary value cannot describe a whole system. Check the actual properties.
The same mark on a ruler can meet two very different shapes.
A good reminder against judging a team at a glance.
I wonder which pair of Pokemon first made that difference obvious.

contexts.subject: A worried trainer reports that poison caused their Pokemon to faint on the road.

VermilionCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Pois.text: My POKéMON was poisoned!\nIt fainted while we were walking!$

replies.text: That must have been a frightening walk. Good that they reached help.
A lingering condition can worsen outside battle. The Center is the appropriate next stop.
They are here now. Get the partner treated before going anywhere else.
I can hear how much it shook them to have it happen between battles.
Rest and proper care first. Supplies for next time can come afterward.
The danger followed them past the end of the battle. An unpleasant lesson.
An ordinary path can become a very long one when someone beside you is hurting.
Persistent damage caught them between encounters. Recovery and prevention both matter.
A small worsening can make each step toward help feel farther.
I hope somebody reassures them while the Pokemon is being treated.
I wonder how far they had to come before reaching the Center.

contexts.subject: A visitor says type weaknesses prevent any Pokemon from being universally strong.

VermilionCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_AllM.text:
It is true that a higher-level
POKéMON will be more powerful…\pBut, all POKéMON will have weak
points against specific types.\pSo, there appears to be no
universally strong POKéMON.$

replies.text: Even the biggest champion has a bad matchup waiting somewhere.
Power is conditional. Type relationships can outweigh a simple level advantage.
Have backup. Strong does not mean safe from everything.
It is comforting that a single imposing opponent is not the whole story.
A thoughtful team matters more than one impressive partner carrying everyone.
The invincible lead has been politely informed that the script contains exceptions.
Nothing has to be flawless to be worth trusting.
Every design has tradeoffs. Build the team around covering them.
Even an old wall has a place where the ivy gets through.
A useful correction to the idea that bigger numbers solve every problem.
I wonder which matchup most surprised the visitor.

contexts.subject: After giving the VS Seeker, the trainer explains rematch detection and battery charging.

VermilionCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_UseD.text: Use that device and you'll find\nTRAINERS looking for a rematch.\pYou have to charge its battery to\nuse it, though.$

replies.text: A little device for asking old opponents whether they fancy another round. Civilized.
The rematch aid requires charge and detects interested trainers rather than forcing a battle.
Useful. Still check the team before asking for another match.
I like that both sides get to want the rematch.
Seeing a familiar trainer again can be a nice reason to revisit a road.
A practical instrument for arranging a sequel with a consenting cast.
An old encounter does not have to stay finished forever.
Clear purpose, limited battery. Charge before scheduling a field test.
A small call sent out to people whose paths have crossed ours.
Good instructions. The charging detail matters before the next outing.
I wonder which familiar trainer we would most like to meet again.

contexts.subject: On a return visit, the trainer explains using the VS Seeker on roads after charging it.

VermilionCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Expl.text:
How do you use the VS SEEKER?
There's nothing to it.\pUse it like beep-beep-beep, and
TRAINERS around you will notice.\pIf any TRAINER wants a rematch,
it will let you know immediately.\pCharge its battery and use it
while you're on a road.$

replies.text: Beep-beep-beep is a wonderfully precise part of that explanation.
The instructions specify location, charge, and the other trainer's interest. Useful conditions.
Charge it, use it on the road, check who is ready. Clear enough.
A friendly offer to explain again makes asking less embarrassing.
A little preparation keeps a planned rematch from becoming a wasted trip.
The technical manual has been condensed into several encouraging beeps.
An invitation carried in a tiny electronic chirp.
Operation instructions with sound effects! Surprisingly memorable.
A small signal asks whether an old meeting has another shape left in it.
They make it sound simple without forgetting the requirements.
I wonder whether they have a favorite person to challenge again.

contexts.subject: A devoted fan asks us to admire his Pikachu's tail.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Admire.text: Won't you admire my PIKACHU's\nadorable tail?$

replies.text: An unusually specific appreciation assignment. The tail is doing fine work.
Affection often sharpens attention to small physical details.
Good tail. Happy trainer. No harm in a little admiration.
It is sweet to see someone so pleased by a familiar little detail.
A partner you know well can keep giving you small reasons to smile.
The fan club presents a featured tail with entirely unrestrained enthusiasm.
A small bright shape with a surprisingly large audience.
Distinctive form, expressive movement. I see the appeal.
A little zigzag carrying a great deal of affection.
A striking silhouette does deserve appreciation.
I wonder whether Pikachu knows how often that tail gets introduced.

contexts.subject: After hearing about the other fan, Pikachu's owner claims twice the cuteness.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Pikach.text: Humph!\pMy PIKACHU is twice as cute as\nthat one!$

replies.text: Twice as cute! I would like to inspect the official cuteness ruler.
The comparison lacks a defined scale and appears strongly influenced by affection.
Both Pokemon can be liked. No tournament needed.
I would rather not make anyone feel their partner has to lose this.
Everybody can go home believing their own companion is special.
The cuteness arms race has entered its first mathematically unsupported escalation.
A bold use of arithmetic in the service of complete bias.
No measurement method supplied. I am marking this as an enthusiastic opinion.
Affection has looked at a ruler and decided to cheat.
A little rivalry is amusing until someone expects us to judge.
I wonder how often these two restart this exact debate.

contexts.subject: A fan lovingly describes Seel's squeal when hugged.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_AdoreM.text: I just adore my SEEL!\nIt's so lovable!\pIt squeals, “Kyuuuh,” when I\nhug it!$

replies.text: That is a very warm review for a Pokemon shaped for cold water.
She notices a familiar response that has become meaningful between them.
Good to see a partner loved for more than battles.
She remembers the exact little sound. That is lovely.
The everyday affectionate moments are worth talking about too.
A detailed testimonial from the hug department.
A small familiar noise can become a whole reason to smile.
Recognizable positive interaction, fondly reported. Excellent outcome.
A little sound that means the room feels safe.
She enjoys the partner, not just the idea of owning one.
I wonder whether Seel recognizes the tone she uses to talk about it.

contexts.subject: Seel's owner retaliates by claiming double the attractiveness.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_SeelFa.text: Oh, dear!\pMy SEEL is far more attractive.\nBy double, I would say.$

replies.text: The cuteness calculations have become a diplomatic incident.
An equally unsupported counterestimate. Neither claim requires us to choose a winner.
They can both be proud without making it a fight.
I would quietly admire both and avoid being appointed judge.
Perhaps the Pokemon could get along while the people compare imaginary scores.
The rival nation of Seel has issued a proportionally inflated response.
Love has once again discovered suspiciously convenient mathematics.
Independent measurement has been replaced by escalating confidence.
Two hearts have invented a contest nobody needed.
The devotion is charming. The arithmetic is a complete accessory.
I wonder whether they enjoy the argument more than they admit.

contexts.subject: After his long story, the chairman gives a Bike Voucher and explains redemption in Cerulean.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Explai.text:
Take that BIKE VOUCHER to the
BIKE SHOP in CERULEAN CITY.\pExchange that for a BICYCLE
free of charge!\pDon't worry, my favorite FEAROW
will FLY me anywhere I need to go.\pSo, I have no need for a BICYCLE.\pI hope you like cycling!$

replies.text: A long horse story has turned into a bicycle. Unexpectedly practical ending!
The voucher has a specific redemption point, and he clearly has no personal need for it.
Generous reward for listening. Take it to the right shop.
He noticed he kept us and tried to thank us properly.
A useful gift from somebody genuinely happy to share his enthusiasm.
Our patient audience has earned a wheeled exit from future lengthy performances.
A rambling affection has left us with a very practical kindness.
A clear handoff with redemption instructions. Excellent finish.
One person's overflowing story has opened a longer road for someone else.
He remembered the listener at the end. That saves the whole speech for me.
I wonder how many people have left this club planning their first ride.

contexts.subject: The chairman accepts our decision not to hear his Pokemon story.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_ComeBa.text: Oh. Come back when you want to\nhear my story!$

replies.text: The story has been stored for later, at very full length I imagine.
He accepted the refusal and left the invitation available.
Good. We can choose when we have time to listen.
A kind ending. Being enthusiastic does not have to mean insisting.
Another day may leave more room for a proper conversation.
The monologue returns to its dressing room, still impeccably prepared.
Some long stories improve when both people have chosen the afternoon for them.
Presentation deferred. Useful to establish audience availability first.
A story can wait quietly until someone has room to hear it.
He did not make us feel rude for having another plan.
I wonder whether he has the opening memorized by now.

contexts.subject: The chairman greets us again but realizes we did not return for another Pokemon story.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_DidntC.text: Hello, {PLAYER}!\pDid you come see me about my\nPOKéMON again?\pNo?\nToo bad!$

replies.text: He had the next story warmed up before the greeting finished.
He remembers the earlier audience and hopes to repeat the conversation.
Nice to be remembered. We still get to choose how long to stay.
I would feel a little bad saying no, even after hearing him once.
A familiar welcome is pleasant, even if today's visit is short.
A returning audience member has narrowly escaped being booked for the sequel.
His enthusiasm seems to have survived the interval completely unharmed.
Repeat presentation offered, not currently requested. Clear enough.
A familiar voice finding its favorite path almost immediately.
He sounds disappointed, but he remembers us kindly.
I wonder whether he has acquired any new stories since the last one.

contexts.subject: The chairman cannot give his Bike Voucher because the bag is full.

replies.text: We found room for the long story and somehow no room for the tiny voucher.
The intended reward did not transfer. Space must be cleared first.
Sort the bag. His gift can wait a moment.
It is awkward to be unprepared after he tried to thank us.
A little tidying will make accepting the kindness much simpler.
A grand monologue has been followed by a minor luggage crisis.
The smallest paper can be too much for a crowded pocket.
Capacity problem at the final handoff. Easy fix with a little sorting.
A road-opening gift has stopped at a very small closed door.
No reason to make the generous part of this feel hurried.
I wonder which pocket has room for a more sensible arrangement.

contexts.subject: A club member remarks on the chairman's very vocal enthusiasm.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Chairm.text: Our CHAIRMAN is very vocal about\nPOKéMON.$

replies.text: The building has probably learned every Rapidash story by vibration.
His interest is clearly expressed often enough to be a defining social trait.
No doubt about what he cares about. Hope he lets others speak too.
A quiet visitor might have trouble finding a place to begin.
Enthusiasm can make a room welcoming when it leaves room for another voice.
A chairman whose volume faithfully reflects the size of his affection.
Silence is not among his particular hobbies.
Strong output signal. Need to check how well the input works.
Some people fill a room by caring about something very loudly.
A club needs listeners as well as somebody certain to keep talking.
I wonder which story the regular members hear most often.

contexts.subject: A member affirms the chairman's love for Pokemon but thinks Pokemon like Daisy most.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Chairm.text: Our CHAIRMAN really does adore his\nPOKéMON.\pBut the person who is most liked by\nPOKéMON is DAISY, I think.$

replies.text: Loving Pokemon and being their favorite are two related, very different contests.
The speaker distinguishes affection expressed toward Pokemon from the trust they return.
The partners get their own opinion. Good to remember.
Daisy must make them feel comfortable without needing to announce it.
Quiet care often tells a Pokemon more than a grand speech.
The chairman has the loudest declaration; Daisy appears to have the more persuasive audience.
Gentleness can be recognized without ever advertising itself.
Reported response is useful feedback. Enthusiasm alone is not the whole method.
Some people become a safe place without trying to be the center of it.
Daisy's reputation seems to come from the Pokemon themselves. A good source.
I wonder what little things Daisy does that make them settle so easily.

contexts.subject: A local recounts that Cubone's mother was killed trying to escape Team Rocket.

LavenderTown_House1_Text_RocketsKilledCu.text: Those horrible ROCKETS!\nThey deserve no mercy!\pThat poor CUBONE's mother…\pIt was killed trying to escape from\nTEAM ROCKET.$

LavenderTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Cubon.text: I saw CUBONE's mother trying to\nescape from TEAM ROCKET.\pShe was killed trying to get away…$

replies.text: That poor little one. There is no clever thing to say that makes that smaller.
The loss is devastating. Cubone needs safety and patient care rather than more demands.
Make sure Cubone is safe now. What happened to its mother was cruel.
It is hard to hear. I hope the little one has somebody gentle nearby.
A quiet, safe home is the least Cubone deserves after that.
No adventure makes this acceptable collateral. It is a family torn apart.
Grief is already heavy enough without a small creature carrying it alone.
There is nothing to improve about that account except making sure the danger stops.
A little life has lost the shelter it knew first.
The people looking after Cubone now need all the patience they can give.
I am glad someone is telling what happened instead of letting it disappear.

contexts.subject: A local believes the Tower's ghost has been soothed and is gone.

LavenderTown_House1_Text_GhostOfPokemonT.text: The ghost of POKéMON TOWER is\ngone!\pSomeone must have soothed its\nrestless spirit!$

replies.text: I am glad the story can end with some peace instead of another fight.
The local interprets the disappearance as a restless spirit finding relief.
Good. There has been enough pain tied to that place.
A gentler ending feels important here.
I hope the people who were frightened can begin to feel comfortable again.
A troubled presence has been given a quieter final line.
Some stories are kindest when they finally become still.
The disturbance has ended. That matters to everyone still living nearby.
The old hurt may no longer be walking the halls.
I like that they say soothed rather than simply driven off.
I wonder whether the Tower feels different to its visitors now.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater confirms a changed nickname and enthusiastically praises the result.

LavenderTown_House2_Text_FromNowOnShallB.text: Done! From now on, this POKéMON\nshall be known as {STR_VAR_1}!\pIt is a better name than before!\nHow fortunate for you!$

replies.text: A new name, delivered with enough confidence to carry the whole Pokemon.
The selected nickname has been applied. The quality judgment remains enthusiastically subjective.
Done. Make sure it is a name we actually want to keep calling.
He sounds so pleased with it that I would find it difficult to disagree.
A name can feel more familiar each time you use it kindly.
The editor has approved the revised title with customary restraint: none whatsoever.
A little word finding a new place to live.
Label updated. Now test whether it remains easy to say in a hurry.
The same companion steps into a different little sound.
A good name should feel like it belongs when the excitement settles.
I wonder how the partner will react when it hears the new name.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater praises an unchanged nickname as somehow vastly improved.

LavenderTown_House2_Text_FromNowOnShallB.text: Done! From now on, this POKéMON\nshall be known as {STR_VAR_1}!\pIt looks no different from before,\nand yet, this is vastly superior!\pHow fortunate for you!$

replies.text: Same name, upgraded approval. Invisible improvements are remarkably convenient.
No observable lexical change. The confidence level, however, has increased dramatically.
Name stayed the same. Glad he is satisfied with the work.
I think he simply wants everyone to leave feeling pleased.
If we already liked the name, keeping it is a perfectly good result.
A masterful revision in which the editor changes only the review.
Nothing happened, but with considerable professional assurance.
No modification detected. Claimed performance increase remains unverified.
The old word has been welcomed back wearing an invisible ribbon.
A complete rebrand of the exact same thing. Confident presentation.
I wonder how often he gives that speech with a perfectly straight face.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater refuses to alter a traded Pokemon's nickname while calling it impeccable.

LavenderTown_House2_Text_TrulyImpeccable.text: {STR_VAR_1}, is it?\nThat is a truly impeccable name!\pTake good care of {STR_VAR_1}!$

replies.text: A compliment that also closes the naming desk. Nicely disguised refusal.
The existing trainer history prevents renaming through this service.
Keep the name it arrived with. That is the rule here.
At least he says it in a way that makes the partner sound special.
A familiar name may be a comforting part of the change of home.
The critic has found perfection precisely where he lacks editorial authority.
A little thread from the old home remains in place.
Permission limit encountered. No change applied.
An old name stays beside a new pair of footsteps.
A tactful way to explain a limit without criticizing somebody else's choice.
I wonder what story the original trainer had behind that name.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater refuses to rate an Egg.

LavenderTown_House2_Text_ThatIsMerelyAnE.text: Now, now.\nThat is merely an EGG!$

replies.text: The Egg has declined to submit a working title. Fair enough.
The service does not apply to an unhatched Egg.
Let it hatch before worrying about a nickname review.
There will be plenty of time to find the right name later.
For now, warm and safe is a much more important description.
The title cannot be reviewed before the main character has entered.
A quiet beginning, temporarily protected from criticism.
Unsupported input. Good that the rater checks first.
A name can wait outside the shell until someone is ready to answer.
Perhaps merely is a little unfair. The Egg has quite a lot ahead of it.
I wonder what name will come to mind when it finally hatches.

contexts.subject: The Name Rater accepts cancellation without changing a nickname.

replies.text: The old name has survived another appointment with the critic.
No change was applied. The current nickname remains intact.
No rush. A name can wait until we are sure.
It is good to be able to hesitate without making the visit awkward.
Keeping a name you like is already a valid choice.
The editorial meeting concludes with the manuscript happily unaltered.
Some familiar words do not need to become different today.
Cancellation preserved the existing setting. Predictable and useful.
The little sound that already belongs can stay where it is.
A polite ending leaves room to think without pressure.
I wonder how many visitors discover they liked the old name all along.

contexts.subject: A shopper searches for temporary battle stat items and asks where to buy them.

LavenderTown_Mart_Text_SearchingForStatR.text:
I'm searching for items that raise
the stats of POKéMON.\pThey're effective over the course
of a single battle.\pX ATTACK, X DEFEND, X SPEED, 
and X SPECIAL are what I'm after.\pDo you know where I can get them?$

replies.text: A clear shopping list, unfortunately delivered to the wrong shelf.
They distinguish temporary battle effects from lasting training changes. Useful specificity.
Worth asking the clerk before walking the whole town.
It is frustrating to know exactly what you need and not where to find it.
A little local advice could save them a long unnecessary trip.
The supplies are specified; the acquisition chapter remains unwritten.
A modest shopping problem can consume a surprisingly large afternoon.
Good requirements, missing supplier. A familiar logistical snag.
The right little bottle is somewhere beyond this particular counter.
They have done the homework on what they want. Directions are the missing piece.
I wonder which battle they are preparing those items for.

contexts.subject: A shopper reminds us to buy Revives for fainted Pokemon.

LavenderTown_Mart_Text_DidYouBuyRevives.text: Did you buy some REVIVES?\nThey revive any fainted POKéMON!$

replies.text: A practical reminder delivered before the road gets the chance to be unpleasant.
A reserve can prevent one fainted partner from ending the entire outing.
Good to carry some if the route is long.
It is comforting to have a way to help after a difficult match.
We should plan the supplies around the team, not just the destination.
A small purchase recommended by the department of avoiding a miserable walk home.
Some things are most welcome precisely when you wish you did not need them.
Recovery supplies are a sensible backup. Check the count before leaving.
A small way to help a tired companion return to its feet.
The advice is useful without inspecting how badly our last battle went.
I wonder whether they learned to carry one after a rough trip.

contexts.subject: A shopper explains that paired trainers require two Pokemon in a double battle.

LavenderTown_Mart_Text_TrainerDuosCanCha.text: Sometimes, a TRAINER duo will\nchallenge you with two POKéMON\lat the same time.\pIf that happens, you have to send\nout two POKéMON to battle, too.$

replies.text: Two opponents means twice as many people trying to look confidently at us.
A double battle changes coordination and targeting, not simply the number of participants.
Have two ready. Do not leave the second partner as an afterthought.
It sounds harder to follow when everyone acts at once.
Good reason to prepare the whole team rather than one favorite.
The encounter may expand into an ensemble with very little warning.
A second companion should be more than a person filling an empty chair.
Two active units create interaction effects. Plan their moves together.
A pair of footsteps needs a shared direction.
A useful warning for someone expecting every challenge to look the same.
I wonder whether the shopper has a favorite pair to send out together.

contexts.subject: A local condemns Team Rocket's willingness to commit any crime for money.

LavenderTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Rocke.text: TEAM ROCKET will do anything for\nthe sake of money!\pThere is no job too dirty, no deed\ntoo heinous, no crime too wicked!$

replies.text: Money is a poor excuse for making the world less safe for everyone else.
The accusation reflects a pattern of exploitation, not a harmless preference for profit.
People and Pokemon get hurt. That is what their greed costs.
They sound angry in a way that comes from being frightened for too long.
There are lines nobody should cross just because somebody pays.
An enterprise whose only consistent principle appears to be the cash at the end.
A purse is a very small thing to build a whole conscience around.
A goal that ignores every constraint can produce immense damage.
They keep taking things money cannot return afterward.
The people left coping with the harm do not get a share of the profit.
I wonder what this town has seen that the rest of the region has not heard yet.

contexts.subject: A visitor remarks that Cubone skulls command high prices.

LavenderTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Peopl.text: You know how the CUBONE species\nwears skulls, right?\pPeople will pay a lot for one.$

replies.text: That belongs to a living creature's story, not somebody's shopping list.
Demand can encourage harm when buyers ignore where an object came from.
A price tag does not make taking one acceptable.
That is an awful thing to hear here, knowing what happened.
A Pokemon's safety should matter more than what someone will pay.
A cold little market fact with a much warmer cost hidden inside it.
Some things become uglier the moment someone assigns them a price.
An incentive for cruelty is still cruelty, even when described as demand.
A keepsake of loss should not become another reason to cause it.
Calling it valuable leaves out the creature it matters to most.
I wonder whether the buyers ever ask the question they most need answered.

contexts.subject: A newcomer hears Mr. Fuji also originally came from elsewhere.

LavenderTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_HearM.text: I recently moved to this town.\pI hear that MR. FUJI's not from\nthese parts originally, either.$

replies.text: Two people from elsewhere can both become part of the same little town.
A shared experience of arriving may offer the newcomer a point of connection.
Being new does not mean you cannot belong.
It is comforting to find someone who has made a home after arriving from away.
A place becomes home through what people do there, not just where they began.
The newcomer has found a possible guide to the art of becoming local.
A town is partly made of people who once stood at its edge.
Local knowledge can be acquired. Origins do not prevent useful belonging.
Roots can grow in soil they did not start in.
That could be a nice first conversation between them.
I wonder what brought the newcomer here.

contexts.subject: A volunteer notices that Mr. Fuji is unexpectedly absent.

LavenderTown_VolunteerPokemonHouse_Text_.text: That's odd, MR. FUJI isn't here.\nWhere'd he go?$

replies.text: A familiar room feels different when its usual person is missing.
His absence is unusual enough for someone here to notice immediately.
Worth checking on him before assuming he is simply busy.
Their uncertainty makes the quiet in here feel heavier.
I hope somebody knows where he planned to go.
An ordinary absence has become the room's most pressing unanswered line.
People leave a particular shape in the spaces they care for.
Unexpected absence. Start by checking his last known plan.
The room is listening for familiar footsteps.
It is good that the people here notice when someone does not return.
