The adoption has been courteously postponed pending adequate accommodation.
The large doll has identified an entirely predictable spatial problem.
We should organize the decoration category before another attempt.
Something offered kindly can wait without turning cold.
She understood that lack of room wasn't lack of appreciation.
I'd thank her for keeping it while we sort things out.

contexts.subject: After the gift, the collector simply shares her fondness for plush dolls.

replies.text: A perfectly reasonable fondness for small faces that never argue about bedtime.
A collection can offer comfort as well as visual variety.
She enjoys them. That's enough reason to keep a few.
I like a room with something soft to rest your eyes on.
Some little things make coming home feel nicer.
An entirely unembarrassed declaration of allegiance to the plush arts.
Quiet companions with no interest in small talk. Understandable taste.
I'd ask how she keeps the older fabric in good condition.
A soft shape can hold a comforting familiarity.
You can tell she enjoys choosing them, not just accumulating them.
I'd ask which doll has been with her the longest.

contexts.subject: A resident wonders whether Sootopolis cave entrance was intended to keep something inside.

SootopolisCity_House7_Text_CaveMadeToKee.text: The cave that links SOOTOPOLIS and\nthe outside world…\pIt seems as if the cave was made to\nkeep something from getting out.\pOr am I just imagining things?$

replies.text: That's a very different question from where the exit is.
The form of a passage does not by itself establish the intention behind it.
Worth being cautious. Speculation isn't proof something is trapped there.
A familiar doorway feels different once somebody asks that.
I'd want to know before treating the place like an ordinary shortcut.
The entrance has acquired the disquieting possibility of being a lock.
A cave with a possible containment function. Comforting local conversation.
I'd compare the structure with actual evidence of deliberate construction.
A boundary can face inward as easily as outward.
She leaves room for being mistaken. That's useful with a thought this unsettling.
I'd ask what feature first made her wonder about it.

contexts.subject: The Seedot enthusiast responds to a canceled showing by inviting a future large Seedot.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text: You don't have a big SEEDOT?\nThat's too bad…\pIf you get a big SEEDOT, please\ncome show me.$

replies.text: His enormous Seedot appointment will have to wait for an enormous Seedot.
No specimen was shown. No size comparison has been established.
We can return if we find the right partner.
He sounds disappointed, but the invitation is still friendly.
A very particular hobby comes with very particular visitors to wait for.
The grand exhibition has been postponed through lack of its principal attraction.
The search for a disproportionately impressive acorn continues.
We should verify the species before another attempt.
A wish can remain waiting without becoming an obligation.
He knows what he wants to see. We don't need to bring something just to fill the silence.
I'd ask what makes a Seedot unusually large in his experience.

contexts.subject: The Lotad enthusiast responds to a canceled showing by inviting a future large Lotad.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text: Don't you have a big LOTAD?\nHow disappointing…\pIf you get a big LOTAD, please\ncome show me!$

replies.text: The big Lotad fan is waiting for a big Lotad. At least the instructions fit together.
The canceled selection leaves the size question unanswered.
We haven't shown one. We can leave it at that.
There is something gentle about being invited back for a small shared enthusiasm.
I would ask about the pond before volunteering to find him a giant.
The hall awaits its broad-leafed guest of honor.
A very specialized disappointment. Manageable, fortunately.
A later visit is an option, not a reason to rush out and catch something.
A little house can hold a very wide expectation.
His enthusiasm doesn't need to become a task for every visitor.
I'd ask about the largest Lotad he has actually seen.

contexts.subject: The selected Pokemon is not Seedot and cannot enter that size comparison.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text: Oh, now this is quite something…\nBut it's not a SEEDOT!$

replies.text: Our candidate has many excellent qualities and one very decisive lack of Seedot.
An incorrect species cannot be used for the requested comparison.
Wrong species. Simple mistake.
I wouldn't want our partner to think it needs to be somebody else.
He asked for an acorn-shaped guest. We brought a different introduction.
The exhibitor admires the arrival while rejecting the category.
A flawless example of not being a Seedot.
Check the selection before asking the measurement question again.
A creature is not diminished by being the wrong answer to one question.
His interest is narrow. That doesn't have to make the meeting unpleasant.
I'd laugh softly, correct the choice, and keep the partner comfortable.

contexts.subject: The selected Pokemon is not Lotad and cannot enter that size comparison.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text: Well, isn't this something!\nBut it's no LOTAD!$

replies.text: Definitely a Pokemon. Unfortunately not the particular leafy one on the invitation.
The comparison cannot proceed with the wrong species.
Our mistake. We can choose again or move on.
A mismatched introduction is a small problem, not an embarrassing disaster.
Nobody should expect the wrong guest to become the right one on demand.
The candidate has failed only the test of possessing the requested name.
A fine creature, tragically short of the required Lotadness.
We should check the species before worrying about the size.
What it is remains more important than what someone hoped to see.
He can be excited about Lotad without dismissing the one we brought.
I'd make the correction without keeping our partner on display.

contexts.subject: The displayed Seedot does not exceed the enthusiast previous size observation.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text: {STR_VAR_2}, is it?\pHmm… I've seen a bigger SEEDOT\nthan this one.$

replies.text: Our Seedot is still exactly Seedot-sized for itself. A perfectly respectable measurement.
This specimen did not exceed the existing comparison. That is a narrow result.
Fine. Our partner doesn't need to win a size argument.
I like it as it is. Being larger isn't a kind of happiness.
A small partner still deserves a proper welcome.
The record remains intact, and the protagonist remains entirely worthy of a snack.
Our acorn has declined to become monumental. Reasonable.
A comparison should not turn into a reason to overtrain or overfeed it.
A small tree begins without apologizing for its size.
I would keep his disappointment from becoming our partner's problem.
I'd ask about its habits instead of staying fixed on the measurement.

contexts.subject: The displayed Lotad does not exceed the enthusiast previous size observation.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text: {STR_VAR_2}?\pHmm… I've seen a bigger LOTAD\nthan this one here.$

replies.text: Not the largest leaf in the pond. Still a very good leaf with a Pokemon underneath.
The existing size reference remains larger. Nothing else about the Pokemon was assessed.
Size isn't the only thing worth knowing about our partner.
I'd rather notice how comfortable it is than whether it breaks a record.
It doesn't need to grow for the sake of somebody else's family argument.
The championship is postponed; the ordinary charm remains undefeated.
A perfectly adequate amount of Lotad.
We can accept the result without trying to force a different size.
A small floating leaf still holds its own place on the water.
I'd give the partner some attention after being reduced to a comparison.
I'd ask what makes this particular Lotad distinctive beyond the numbers.

contexts.subject: A large Seedot excites its admirer and earns an Elixir when the bag permits.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text:
{STR_VAR_2}!
Oh, my gosh, this is a big one!\pIt might even beat the big LOTAD
my younger brother saw!\pThanks for showing me.
This is my thanks!$

replies.text: Our Seedot has accidentally joined a very intense family debate.
He observed an unusually large specimen; the cross-species claim remains his comparison.
Glad he enjoyed meeting it. The partner still deserves a calm goodbye.
I don't think Seedot expected to receive quite so much attention today.
A happy visitor and a generous thank-you. That's a pleasant meeting.
The acorn contender has entered the household championship to thunderous approval.
A small species has produced a large disruption in sibling relations.
We should keep the actual observation separate from declaring either species always larger.
One ordinary creature has become somebody's extraordinary afternoon.
His joy is infectious, even if the rivalry is rather silly.
I'd remember the way his voice changed when he saw it.

contexts.subject: A large Lotad excites its admirer and earns an Elixir when the bag permits.

SootopolisCity_LotadAndSeedotHouse_Text_.text:
{STR_VAR_2}!
Wow, that is big!\pIt might be even bigger than the huge
SEEDOT my big brother saw.\pThanks for showing me!
This is my thanks!$

replies.text: A great big Lotad has become a great big point in a brotherly argument.
He has a new large observation. It does not settle the size of every individual.
Good to make someone happy. Let's not crowd the partner.
It's sweet to see him this delighted by a Pokemon he loves.
He made the meeting feel like a little celebration.
The broad-leafed champion has arrived before an exceedingly receptive audience.
A leaf has tipped the balance of domestic power.
I'd keep track of the measurement rather than only the triumphant comparison.
A familiar kind of creature can still bring an unexpected wonder.
I like enthusiasm most when it leaves the Pokemon room to be comfortable.
I'd ask what he noticed first: the leaf, the body, or his brother's likely reaction.

contexts.subject: The Seedot admirer cannot deliver the Elixir reward because the bag is full.

replies.text: The Seedot made an impression. The reward has failed to make an entrance.
The size observation stands, but the item transfer failed.
We'll make room if we want the reward. No harm done to the showing.
It's nice that the good part of the meeting doesn't depend on the item.
One more reason to organize the bag before accepting thanks.
The award ceremony has encountered a spectacularly overqualified collection of luggage.
An Elixir has been defeated by the quantity of everything else.
Clear capacity before repeating the transfer attempt.
A moment can remain generous even while an object must wait.
The compliment arrived safely. We can sort the practical part next.
I'd thank him for the thought while checking what can be stored elsewhere.

contexts.subject: The Lotad admirer cannot deliver the Elixir reward because the bag is full.

replies.text: A giant Lotad fit into the conversation more easily than one Elixir fit into the bag.
The failed transfer does not undo his observation of the Pokemon's size.
Sort the bag. The reward hasn't been received yet.
I would rather take a calm moment than spill everything across the floor.
A useful thank-you still needs somewhere safe to go.
The generous finale has paused for an inventory intermission.
The pocket has displayed a stronger defense than expected.
We need an open item slot before this exchange can finish.
A full hand cannot receive, even when the intention is warm.
His excitement can survive a short delay while we make room.
I'd leave the partner comfortable while we deal with the luggage.

contexts.subject: A resident compares Wallace, his mentor Juan, and the Elite Four reputations.

SootopolisCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Wal.text:
WALLACE is rumored to be the toughest
TRAINER in the whole HOENN region.\pThis town's GYM is led by the TRAINER
who taught WALLACE.\pBut the ELITE FOUR… They're said to be
even stronger than WALLACE's mentor.\pHow strong could they be?$

replies.text: That is a very tall stack of people said to be stronger than somebody else.
Training lineage and reputation do not by themselves determine an exact ranking.
Enough strong people to learn from. One challenge at a time.
The next room always sounds larger when someone describes the one beyond it.
I'd rather ask how they prepare than keep climbing the rumor ladder.
A hierarchy of formidable names, balanced carefully on the word rumored.
The intimidating comparison has developed an additional intimidating comparison.
We can study actual strategies without needing to settle every ranking.
A long shadow can be made from several stories told together.
They sound fascinated as much as afraid. That's a useful way to stay curious.
I'd ask which of those Trainers they have personally watched battle.

contexts.subject: A woman describes her brother enthusiasm for finding Secret Bases.

MossdeepCity_House4_Text_BrotherLikesToF.text: My little brother says he likes to go\nfind people's SECRET BASES.$

replies.text: Her brother treats every suspicious tree as a possible invitation.
Searching for hidden places is a different interest from making one.
Finding a base doesn't mean skipping a polite hello.
I wonder what tiny clue makes him most certain someone lives there.
I'd pack a snack if his searches take all afternoon.
An amateur detective specializing in unusually decorated holes.
A hobby whose success somewhat undermines its subject's name.
I'd ask how he distinguishes a base entrance from an ordinary feature.
A hidden place can draw someone gently away from the obvious path.
Discovering something is nicest when its owner still gets a choice about visitors.
I'd ask which base he remembers finding first.

contexts.subject: After League completion, the brother enjoys visiting bases for Pokemon battles.

MossdeepCity_House4_Text_BrotherLikesToV.text: My little brother says he likes to\nvisit people's SECRET BASES and have\lPOKéMON battles.$

replies.text: The hidden clubhouse has become a very personal place to arrange a battle.
A visit now provides both social contact and a challenge.
Ask the owner first. Their home isn't automatically an arena.
I hope they find a place for the fragile things before starting.
A battle is nicer when everybody has agreed and the room is ready.
The secret setting has acquired a regular action sequence.
Indoor combat beside treasured dolls. A confidence I do not share.
I'd check the available space before letting the teams loose.
A place of welcome should remain one after the challenge.
The visiting part matters as much as the victory.
I'd ask how they make the rules comfortable for both Trainers.

contexts.subject: The base enthusiast recognizes the area of the player Secret Base.

MossdeepCity_House4_Text_YouMadeSecretBa.text: Was it you who made a SECRET BASE\nnear {STR_VAR_1}?$

replies.text: Our secret has developed an address and apparently a local audience.
He has associated the nearby location with our activity.
He found it. We should establish when visitors are welcome.
I suddenly wish I had tidied a little more carefully.
A guest is fine, but some notice before arriving would be kind.
The hidden retreat has failed a determined child's inspection.
Secrecy has been reviewed and found wanting.
I'd ask what clue gave the location away. Useful information.
A hidden doorway can still be known to a careful pair of eyes.
He is pleased to connect the place with a person he has met.
I'd ask what he noticed first when he found it.

contexts.subject: A visitor admires the Mossdeep Gym duo coordinated attacks.

MossdeepCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_GymLe.text: The GYM LEADERS in this town are\na formidable duo.\pTheir combination attacks are, like,\nexcellent and wow!$

replies.text: Two opponents agreeing on a plan sounds much more worrying than two opponents merely standing there.
Coordination can create effects that neither participant achieves alone.
Prepare for how they work together, not only each one separately.
It must be striking to see the timing come together.
A good pair notices what the other is about to need.
The formidable duo has earned a review consisting partly of delighted noises.
A pair with functioning teamwork. A serious complication.
I'd study the interaction between their moves before choosing counters.
Two separate paths can make one stronger pattern.
Their shared rhythm matters as much as individual confidence.
I'd ask which combination made the visitor react that way.

contexts.subject: After giving Dive, Steven explains deep-water entry and limits on resurfacing.

MossdeepCity_StevensHouse_Text_ExplainDi.text:
STEVEN: While you're using SURF, you
should notice dark patches of water.\pUse DIVE if you come to deep water
like it. You'll drop to the seafloor.\pWhen you want to come back up, use
DIVE again.\pIn some places, it won't be possible
for you to surface, though.$

replies.text: Down is useful, but remembering where up works seems especially useful.
Entry and surfacing conditions are not identical. Plan both before descending.
Know the way back up before exploring. That's the first rule.
The dark patches look different once you know they are doors.
We should prepare for the whole trip, not just the exciting first plunge.
A new passage opens beneath the scenery, with important restrictions on the exit.
The seafloor is available. So is the possibility of poor planning.
I'd keep track of surfaces we can safely return through.
A hidden path still needs a remembered way home.
He made sure the warning came with the invitation to explore.
I'd ask what experienced divers check before entering an unfamiliar patch.

contexts.subject: Steven mentions the underwater cavern discovered by Stern between Mossdeep and Sootopolis.

MossdeepCity_StevensHouse_Text_Underwate.text: STEVEN: Apparently, there's an\nunderwater cavern between\lMOSSDEEP and SOOTOPOLIS.\pYou know, the one that CAPT. STERN\nfound in his submarine.$

replies.text: A place between two familiar towns that was hiding underneath the usual directions.
The discovery gives us a specific location to investigate rather than a general rumor.
We should learn the route before heading down there.
It is strange how close something can be while nobody sees it.
I'd ask what Stern found and what supplies the trip required.
The map has acquired a deeper chapter between two existing headings.
A local cavern, inconveniently separated from us by an ocean's worth of overhead.
Knowing where it is doesn't yet tell us whether the entrance is safe.
The water keeps another landscape folded beneath this one.
I'd like to know whether the people studying it have concerns visitors should hear.
I'd ask Steven which parts of the report are confirmed.

contexts.subject: Steven letter explains his extended training journey and entrusts a Beldum to the player.

MossdeepCity_StevensHouse_Text_LetterFro.text:
It's a letter.\p… … … … … …\pTo {PLAYER}{KUN}…\pI've decided to do a little soul-
searching and train on the road.\pI don't plan to return home for some
time.\pI have a favor to ask of you.\pI want you to take the POKé BALL on
the desk.\pInside it is a BELDUM, my favorite
POKéMON.\pI'm counting on you.\pMay our paths cross someday.\pSTEVEN STONE$

replies.text: He left room in his own journey for trusting us with someone he cares about.
The letter records a deliberate choice of a new caretaker, not an abandoned possession.
That's real trust. We should think carefully about taking responsibility.
A quiet room feels different with somebody's goodbye waiting on the desk.
I'd want to know the Beldum has a good routine ready if we accept.
A departure letter becomes an introduction to a life continuing in other company.
Soul-searching with an unusually substantial favor left in its wake.
We can honor the request by preparing for the Pokemon's actual needs.
A closed door behind one traveler can open beside another.
His fondness is clear. The choice deserves more than a quick look at the Ball.
I'd remember to tell him how Beldum is doing when our paths cross again.

contexts.subject: The Sun Stone giver says Magma presence makes his beach walks unsafe.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_CantStr.text: With TEAM MAGMA around, I guess\nstrolls on the beach aren't safe.$

replies.text: They've even spoiled the simple business of going for a walk.
A security threat affects ordinary movement beyond the targeted facility.
Stay where it's safe for now. A beach walk can wait.
It is a small loss inside the large trouble, but it still matters.
People deserve to enjoy their neighborhood without planning around criminals.
The villainy has interrupted a chapter that should have needed no conflict at all.
A quiet stroll. Apparently too much to ask of an occupied island.
We should make sure the routes people use every day are secure too.
A familiar shore can feel far away when fear stands in the path.
He isn't asking for anything extravagant, just his normal day back.
I'd ask where he feels safe waiting while this is dealt with.

contexts.subject: The Sun Stone giver mentions Hoenn long-standing meteor showers.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_HoennFa.text: The HOENN region has been famous for \nits meteor showers for a long time.$

replies.text: Hoenn has apparently been receiving little sparkly visitors for quite a while.
A long record of sightings could reveal useful seasonal patterns.
Worth seeing from somewhere safe and quiet.
I like imagining people watching the same sky long before we arrived.
A night outside with something warm to drink would suit that nicely.
The sky has maintained a very old habit of giving people stories.
A celestial event with the courtesy to occur above most conversation.
I'd ask where local observers get the clearest view.
A brief light can join many generations in the same upward glance.
Something spectacular can still belong to ordinary people looking up together.
I'd ask which meteor shower he remembers most vividly.

contexts.subject: A scientist explains that small faults can compromise launches but the dream motivates continued work.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_RocketL.text:
A rocket launch demands perfection.
Not even a 1% margin of error is allowed.\pEven if it's 99% okay, the whole thing
is useless if 1% happens to be no good.\pDespite that, we never stop trying.
Why? It's a dream that never ends.$

replies.text: A rocket is a very large argument for checking the tiny parts.
A critical subsystem failure can invalidate the performance of the whole vehicle.
Then every check deserves the time it takes.
It must be tiring to care that much about every small thing.
The people doing the checking need rest too. Tired eyes miss details.
A magnificent dream rests on a multitude of deliberately unromantic inspections.
The exciting achievement depends on an exhausting quantity of being correct.
Perfection is an ambition; repeated testing and redundancy are how you approach reliability.
A great upward light begins with many patient hands on the ground.
Their care is part of the achievement, even when nobody sees the checks.
I'd ask what they learned from the last fault they caught before launch.

contexts.subject: A scientist is determined to continue the launch despite Magma targeting the center.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_MagmaHa.text: Those MAGMA thugs have their sights\nset on our SPACE CENTER.\pBut we can't allow anything that minor\nto interfere with our rocket launch!$

replies.text: Determination is good. Calling thieves minor doesn't make their hands smaller.
Maintaining the schedule should not override a credible security risk.
Secure the people and fuel first. The launch can wait if it has to.
I understand not wanting to let them take the day away.
The people here matter more than keeping the plan on time.
The heroic refusal to be delayed should leave room for a sensible safety check.
A minor incident involving criminals and rocket fuel. An interesting definition.
They need to evaluate the threat as a real system hazard.
A dream should not require pretending the danger is small.
His resolve is admirable. The staff still deserve a plan that protects them.
I'd ask who is coordinating security while the launch team works.

contexts.subject: Steven is watching for Team Magma planned fuel theft and suggests the player inspect the town meanwhile.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_StevenM.text:
STEVEN: {PLAYER}{KUN}, have you read that
proclamation already?\pTEAM MAGMA is coming after the rocket
fuel on this island.\pI don't know what they'd need it for,
but they can't be allowed to take it.\pI'll keep an eye on things for
a while longer.\pIn the meantime, why don't you go
check out the town?$

replies.text: Someone dependable is watching the fuel. That makes the room feel a little steadier.
He separates what is known about the threat from the still-unknown motive.
Good. We'll stay alert and keep out of the staff's way.
It helps that he sounds serious without making everyone panic.
People nearby may need information as much as another worried face.
A capable ally keeps guard while the wider setting waits to be understood.
Competence and uncertainty in the same sentence. Reassuringly honest.
We can learn the town's layout while he monitors the immediate target.
A calm person can hold a little space against a gathering disturbance.
He's giving us room to act without pretending we already know the whole plan.
I'd ask who to tell if we notice anything unusual around town.

contexts.subject: A scientist explains that Mossdeep sunshine and stable winds favor rocket launches.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_Mossdee.text: MOSSDEEP has mainly sunny weather,\nand its winds are stable.\pIt's an ideal location for launching\nrockets.$

replies.text: Even a rocket appreciates the sky behaving itself before it leaves.
Predictable weather reduces one important source of launch uncertainty.
Good reason to build here. Still check the conditions every time.
I like learning why a place suits the work people chose for it.
Some jobs begin with finding the right day, not just the right tools.
The spectacular launch has a surprisingly mundane ally in reliable weather.
A location selected partly for its lack of atmospheric drama. Sensible.
A good site removes problems before the design has to solve them.
A steady wind can help carry an ambitious wish beyond it.
The place is part of what makes their work possible.
I'd ask what weather change makes them postpone a launch.

contexts.subject: A scientist is puzzled by Magma motive for stealing rocket fuel.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_WhyWoul.text: Why would TEAM MAGMA want to steal\nour rocket fuel in the first place?$

replies.text: Not knowing their reason doesn't make a missing tank sound any better.
The target is clear even though the intended application remains uncertain.
Stop the theft first. Work out the motive without handing them the fuel.
It must be unnerving when someone wants something dangerous and won't explain why.
They shouldn't have to guess what harm their own supplies might be used for.
The villains have supplied a destination for the theft but omitted its final act.
Rocket fuel and criminal intent. An adequate reason for concern without further detail.
We can assess the immediate storage risk while investigating the rest.
A hidden purpose can still cast a very visible threat.
The uncertainty makes clear information especially important.
I'd ask what quantities they threatened to take and who heard the warning.

contexts.subject: An elder rejects his own thought that age makes astronaut ambition too late and resolves to try.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_Wouldve.text: If only I was a little younger, I would\nhave liked being an astronaut…\pNo… It's not too late!\nI can and will try!$

replies.text: He caught his own dream trying to slip out the door and invited it back.
The next useful question is what requirements he can realistically work toward.
Good. Find out what's needed before deciding for himself that it's impossible.
I liked hearing the hesitation change into a little courage.
There is something lovely about giving an old wish a fresh morning.
A regret revises itself into the opening line of a new attempt.
An ambition has successfully appealed against premature retirement.
He can ask about training and see which concrete steps remain available.
An old seed may still answer when someone brings it water.
Trying doesn't have to mean pretending it will be easy.
I'd ask what part he wants to learn first.

contexts.subject: The aspiring astronaut fears fuel theft will end his spaceflight hopes.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_MagmaCa.text: If TEAM MAGMA takes the rocket fuel,\nI won't be able to go to space!\pThey can't be allowed to get away\nwith such an outrage!$

replies.text: They aren't only taking fuel. They're trying to carry off somebody's next chance.
The threatened resource supports a program that people have committed hopes to.
He deserves a safe chance to try. Keep the fuel secured.
He had just given himself permission to want this.
It's cruel to make people fight for the ordinary chance to pursue a dream.
A personal ambition becomes collateral in someone else's grand plan.
The thieves have found a very efficient way to become universally disliked.
Security protects the future use of the fuel, not merely the tank itself.
An imagined journey can be wounded before it begins.
His anger makes sense. Someone is treating what matters to him as expendable.
I'd like to hear his plans again once the danger has passed.

contexts.subject: A visitor hopes space travel will eventually be available to ordinary people.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_WishOrd.text: I wish ordinary people could go into\nspace one day…$

replies.text: An ordinary afternoon that includes leaving the planet would be quite an upgrade.
Wider access would require substantial advances in reliability, cost, and support.
Good dream. Make it safe before making it common.
It is nice to imagine a distant place becoming something you could really visit.
People would still ask what to pack and whether there will be food.
The extraordinary voyage hopes to become a chapter available to an ordinary life.
A larger selection of travel anxiety. Progress is generous.
Making complicated systems usable by more people is an exciting challenge.
A far light can become a place instead of only a point to wish upon.
It would be lovely if wonder weren't reserved for the unusually fortunate.
I'd ask what they would want to see first from up there.

contexts.subject: A visitor guesses Magma may want the fuel for space travel.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_DoesMag.text: TEAM MAGMA…\nDo they want to go to space, too?$

replies.text: I'd rather the first clue to someone's travel plans weren't theft.
The fuel could suggest several uses. Spaceflight is only one hypothesis.
Whatever they want, taking the center's fuel isn't acceptable.
It's a natural guess in this room, but I wouldn't be comfortable assuming it.
Wanting a journey doesn't make everyone else's work yours to take.
The missing motive is briefly filled by the nearest available genre.
A criminal space program. Somehow not the most reassuring interpretation.
We should look for evidence of compatible equipment before accepting that theory.
A thing's usual purpose does not tell us every use someone might force on it.
They are trying to make the danger understandable. That doesn't mean the guess is right.
I'd ask what the staff know rather than build the whole story from the fuel.

contexts.subject: A shopper prepares paralysis and poison cures for Shroomish encounters in Petalburg Woods.

RustboroCity_Mart_Text_BuyingHealsInCase.text: I'm buying some PARLYZ HEALS and\nANTIDOTES.\pJust in case I run into SHROOMISH\nin PETALBURG WOODS.$

replies.text: That shopper has imagined the mushroom-shaped problem before meeting it.
Preparing for known status effects is more useful than buying without a scenario.
Good preparation. Keep the cures where they're easy to reach.
It helps to know what worries you before entering the woods.
A small bit of shopping can save a very uncomfortable walk back.
The forest excursion has received a properly researched packing list.
A mushroom has influenced the shopping before appearing in person. Efficient.
We should match supplies to the conditions likely along our route.
The woods can be gentle-looking and still ask for care.
They're preparing for their partner's comfort, which is worth noticing.
I'd ask whether they learned this from a previous trip.

contexts.subject: A shopper upgrades healing supplies after their Pokemon evolves and gains HP.

RustboroCity_Mart_Text_ShouldBuySuperPot.text: My POKéMON evolved.\nIt has a lot of HP now.\pI should buy SUPER POTIONS for it\ninstead of ordinary POTIONS.$

replies.text: The Pokemon grew, and the shopping list is trying to keep up.
A fixed healing amount becomes less adequate as maximum HP increases.
Check the team's current needs instead of packing for the team we used to have.
It's nice when growing stronger also means someone notices you need different care.
A bigger partner may need a bigger helping of recovery.
Character development has produced a practical amendment to the inventory.
Evolution has submitted an expense request.
Compare recovery per use against what the partner actually needs now.
Care should change as the one receiving it changes.
They are adjusting a familiar habit instead of assuming it will always fit.
I'd ask what else surprised them after the evolution.

contexts.subject: A shopper buys Escape Rope as a way out of caves.

RustboroCity_Mart_Text_GettingEscapeRope.text: I'm getting an ESCAPE ROPE just in\ncase I get lost in a cave.\pI just need to use it to get back to\nthe entrance.$

replies.text: A way back to the door is an excellent thing to pack before getting lost.
An exit option reduces the consequences of uncertain navigation.
Good. Know how to leave before pushing farther in.
I would feel a little calmer knowing the entrance isn't our only plan.
Being prepared to stop is part of being prepared to explore.
The intrepid explorer has wisely purchased an ending before the adventure begins.
A retreat made portable. One of civilization's finer ideas.
Keep it accessible rather than beneath the rest of the equipment.
An unknown passage feels kinder when a way home remains possible.
A backup isn't pessimism. It gives curiosity room to be sensible.
I'd ask whether they have a particular cave in mind.

contexts.subject: A shopper distinguishes the market interesting goods from items exclusive to the Mart.

SlateportCity_Mart_Text_SomeItemsOnlyAtM.text: The MARKET does have some interesting\nmerchandise.\pBut there are some items you can only\nget at a POKéMON MART.$

replies.text: Two shopping places, each convinced the other one doesn't have quite everything.
Different inventories serve different purchasing needs.
Check both lists before walking all over town.
I like learning the little reasons people choose one familiar shop over another.
A market for surprises, a Mart for the particular thing you came for.
The town supports both wandering curiosity and a very specific shopping list.
A productive rivalry between organized shelves and interesting stalls.
We can plan which stops are necessary instead of buying a substitute in a hurry.
An ordinary errand can show the different ways a town lives.
It's nice when the shopper can appreciate both without dismissing either.
I'd ask which item usually brings them back here.

contexts.subject: A shopper hopes a Great Ball will help catch an elusive Pokemon.

SlateportCity_Mart_Text_GreatBallIsBette.text: A GREAT BALL is better than a POKé BALL\nat catching POKéMON.\pWith this, I should be able to get that\nelusive POKéMON…$

replies.text: A better Ball helps, but the elusive Pokemon may still have its own plans.
Improved capture performance changes the odds rather than guaranteeing an outcome.
Useful gear. Still prepare the encounter properly.
I hope the next meeting feels less frustrating for both of them.
A good tool shouldn't make us forget patience with the Pokemon.
The next attempt receives an equipment upgrade, not a rewritten ending.
An improved container has been assigned an ambitious expectation.
I'd consider the target's condition and the Ball together.
An encounter remains a meeting even when we arrive with better tools.
I'd be careful that wanting a catch doesn't turn the whole outing sour.
I'd ask what keeps making that Pokemon so difficult to meet.

contexts.subject: A shopper describes temporary battle stat items such as X Attack and X Defend.

MauvilleCity_Mart_Text_ItemsToTemporaril.text:
There are items that temporarily
elevate the stats of POKéMON.\pThe ones I know you use in battle
are X ATTACK and X DEFEND…\pI do believe that there are others
like them.$

replies.text: A useful boost that doesn't move into the Pokemon permanently.
These items affect the current battle state rather than lasting growth.
Know how long the benefit lasts before planning around it.
It's easy to miss the temporary part when the promise sounds exciting.
A short-term helping hand still needs a good moment to use it.
A brief flourish added to the performance, not a new line in the biography.
Temporary excellence. A manageable subscription.
Timing matters because using an item also takes an opportunity to act.
A passing strength can be useful without becoming who someone is.
I would keep the exact effect clear instead of just trusting the bright label.
I'd ask which one they actually found useful in a difficult battle.

contexts.subject: A shopper considers choosing a move versus using an item as an important Trainer responsibility.

MauvilleCity_Mart_Text_DecisionsDetermin.text: Use a certain move, or use an item\ninstead…\pThe TRAINER's decisions determine how\nbattles turn out, I think.$

replies.text: Our partners do the hard movement. We still have to do the careful thinking.
Action selection can matter as much as the nominal strength of the available options.
Make the call that helps the team, not the one that looks boldest.
It is a lot of trust to have someone wait for your next decision.
Sometimes giving a partner a little help is better than asking for one more attack.
The person outside the direct struggle remains responsible for its direction.
An excellent reminder that enthusiasm is not itself a battle plan.
We should compare immediate benefit with the risk of delaying another action.
A quiet choice can turn the path of a loud moment.
That responsibility should make us attentive rather than eager to blame a partner.
I'd ask what choice they remember wishing they'd made differently.

contexts.subject: A shopper strongly recommends temporary X Special boosts.

VerdanturfTown_Mart_Text_XSpecialIsCruci.text: For any POKéMON match, X SPECIAL\nis crucial.\pIt jacks up the power of some moves\neven though it's only for one battle.$

replies.text: Crucial for every match sounds like the shop shelf wrote part of that sentence.
A special-attack boost is useful only when the move set and situation can exploit it.
Good tool in the right battle. Not a substitute for choosing well.
I would want to know whether our partner's moves actually need that help.
An enthusiastic recommendation still deserves a look at the ingredients of the plan.
A useful accessory has been promoted to universal savior. Bold marketing.
Every battle is a suspiciously large number of battles.
Check the relevant stat and the opportunity cost before using it.
A thing can help without being the answer to every door.
The certainty is louder than the explanation. I'd ask for a specific example.
I'd hear about the battle where it worked best for them.

contexts.subject: A shopper cannot find a winning Battle Tent guide and expects to rely on personal judgment.

VerdanturfTown_Mart_Text_NoStrategyGuide.text: They don't seem to sell any winning\nstrategy guides for the BATTLE TENT…\pIt seems one must rely on one's\nown wits after all…$

replies.text: The shelf has declined to do the thinking part for us.
A guide could inform preparation, but no fixed text can choose every response.
Learn the rules, then pay attention to the actual battle.
It's daunting when the answer isn't waiting neatly on a page.
Useful advice helps most when you still understand why you're following it.
The aspiring victor discovers the adventure contains an unpurchasable component.
The guaranteed-winning manual remains conspicuously out of stock.
We can observe a few matches and work out what decisions matter.
An unwritten path can still be walked one clear step at a time.
Not having a script doesn't mean having to go in uninformed.
I'd ask somebody who competed what surprised them most.

contexts.subject: A shopper recommends Nest Balls and points out their local availability.

VerdanturfTown_Mart_Text_NestBallOnWeake.text: The NEST BALL works better on\nweakened POKéMON.\pVERDANTURF is the only place you can\nbuy it.$

replies.text: A special Ball with a special purpose. We should be clear what that purpose is.
Nest Balls depend on the target's level; low HP and low level are different conditions.
Check how it works before expecting a catch.
A small distinction in the explanation can change what someone expects.
I'd ask a second question rather than buy a whole bag on a vague promise.
The specialist tool deserves a more precise introduction than the sales pitch offers.
A charming name is not a full set of instructions.
We should compare the effect with the Pokemon we're actually trying to catch.
A name can suggest a refuge while the mechanism follows its own rules.
Local advice is useful when we know exactly what it means.
I'd ask which Pokemon the shopper has successfully used it with.

contexts.subject: A Trainer weighs evolving Skitty with a Moon Stone against its changed appearance.

FallarborTown_Mart_Text_DecidingSkittyEv.text:
I'm having a hard time deciding if I
should make my SKITTY evolve or not.\pI only have to use this MOON STONE,
but it's so hard to decide…\pIf I make it evolve, it will become
much stronger.\pBut it will look so different, too.$

replies.text: A familiar little face matters. I'd also like to know how Skitty feels about changing it.
Evolution changes several traits; strength and appearance are not the only considerations.
No rush. Make the choice with the partner in mind.
I'd find it difficult to separate loving a familiar face from fearing a change.
A stronger partner should still be a happy partner. Take some time.
A character's future is being debated between affection for the present and possibility ahead.
A permanent transformation deserves more than a hurried aisle decision.
I'd learn what changes in capability before using the stone.
A new shape need not erase who has been dear to us.
Attachment isn't silly. It just needs room for the Pokemon's own future too.
I'd spend a little time with Skitty away from the counter before deciding.

contexts.subject: A shopper decides to sell a found Nugget because it has little practical use.

FallarborTown_Mart_Text_SellNuggetIFound.text: This NUGGET I found here…\nI suppose I'll have to sell it, seeing\las how it has no other use.$

replies.text: A lucky shiny rock is about to become several useful ordinary things.
An object with high exchange value can still have little direct utility to its finder.
If he doesn't want to keep it, useful supplies are a fair trade.
I would remember where I found it, even after selling it.
A small lucky find can pay for a very practical shopping trip.
The treasure concludes its narrative by financing more mundane necessities.
Gold has the peculiar talent of becoming almost anything else.
I'd check the offered price before selling. No need to hurry a good find.
A thing can leave our hand while its lucky moment stays.
Having no use for it doesn't mean it needs to remain clutter.
I'd ask how it caught their eye in the first place.

contexts.subject: A shopper explains using X Speed to act earlier in battle.

LavaridgeTown_Mart_Text_XSpeedFirstStrik.text: Use X SPEED to add to a POKéMON's\nSPEED in battle.\pThat will help it get in the first\nstrike--a decided advantage!$

replies.text: Getting there first is helpful, provided we know what we want to do when we arrive.
Higher Speed can alter action order, though other priority conditions still matter.
Useful advantage. Don't forget the turn spent setting it up.
Being quicker feels reassuring when the next moment matters.
A head start is useful when the rest of the plan is ready.
The cast member receives assistance arriving before the opposing line.
Punctuality weaponized. Intriguing product category.
We should compare the speed difference before using it automatically.
The first step matters because of where it lets the next step land.
I'd rather be clear than hurried, even with a faster partner.
I'd ask when that shopper found the extra speed most useful.

contexts.subject: A shopper recommends Mt Chimney local specialty as a Pokemon treat.

LavaridgeTown_Mart_Text_LocalSpecialtyOn.text: On MT. CHIMNEY's peak, there's a local\nspecialty that you can buy only there.\pGive it to a POKéMON--it will be elated.$

replies.text: A mountain trip with a snack recommendation attached. Excellent geography.
A local specialty can have both a regional identity and a practical use.
Worth a look if we're going that way. Don't drag the team uphill just for a rumor.
I like bringing something back that reminds you where the day took you.
Now I want to know what makes the mountain version different.
The summit has added a culinary incentive to its existing dramatic scenery.
A snack whose travel requirements are more ambitious than mine.
I'd ask where the vendor is and whether supplies depend on the time.
A small taste can carry a whole place back down the mountain.
A recommendation for making our partner happy is a nice kind of souvenir advice.
I'd ask what the Pokemon does that makes its delight so obvious.

contexts.subject: A shopper prefers Super Repel longer duration over ordinary Repel.

FortreeCity_Mart_Text_SuperRepelBetter.text: SUPER REPEL lasts a long time,\nand it gets the job done.\pIt's much better than an ordinary\nREPEL.$

replies.text: Fewer spray stops means fewer times I have to remember where the bottle went.
Longer duration changes convenience as well as total trip consumption.
Good for a planned stretch of travel. Keep watching where we walk.
A quieter walk can be pleasant when we just need to reach somewhere.
I'd compare how much route one bottle covers before stocking up.
The journey receives fewer interruptions, including interruptions to renew the interruption preventer.
A longer interval between chores. Persuasive.
We should compare duration per cost, not simply the size of the label.
A clear passage is useful when we know why we are passing through.
Convenience can be worth paying for on a tiring day.
I'd ask which route made them start preferring this one.

contexts.subject: A shopper prefers carrying extra supplies for unforeseen problems.

FortreeCity_Mart_Text_StockUpOnItems.text: I always stock up on more items than\nI'm sure I'll need.\pYou never know what might happen.\nBetter to be safe than sorry!$

replies.text: A spare is useful. Twelve spares may require a second person to carry the first eleven.
A reserve should be sized around plausible risks and transport capacity.
Prepare for trouble without making the pack the trouble.
I understand feeling calmer when the bag has an answer ready.
I'd cover the essentials first, then leave room for what the road brings.
The expedition is prepared for contingencies, and perhaps for some of their relatives.
Reassurance has weight. The shoulders should be consulted.
A simple checklist can prevent both shortages and needless duplicates.
A bag can carry preparation without carrying every imagined fear.
Feeling safe is important. So is being able to move comfortably.
I'd ask which spare they were happiest to have on their last trip.

contexts.subject: A boy explains that Rare Candy immediately raises a Pokemon by one level.

FortreeCity_Mart_Text_RareCandyMakesMonG.text: A RARE CANDY makes a POKéMON grow\nimmediately by one level.$

replies.text: An entire level inside one little sweet. Lunch has some catching up to do.
It provides immediate level advancement rather than a normal meal's role.
Useful item. Still need practice with whatever comes from the growth.
I'd give the partner a moment to understand what feels different afterward.
A remarkable sweet is still no replacement for regular food and care.
Character development, delivered in unexpectedly compact confectionery.
A sugary abbreviation of a longer process. Conveniently rare.
We should consider who benefits most before using a limited item.
A quick step forward still leaves a journey to make sense of it.
I'd want the partner comfortable with its new strength, not merely stronger on paper.
I'd ask whether the boy has watched a Pokemon try one himself.

contexts.subject: A shopper praises Revive but warns that it does not replenish move PP.

MossdeepCity_Mart_Text_ReviveIsFantastic.text: REVIVE is fantastic!\pGive it to a fainted POKéMON,\nand the POKéMON will arise.\pBut be careful, REVIVE doesn't restore\nthe used-up PP of moves.$

replies.text: Getting back up and being ready for everything are two different sorts of better.
Restoring consciousness and HP does not replenish move usage capacity.
Check the whole partner's condition before sending it back in.
I wouldn't want being able to stand mistaken for being ready to continue.
A recovery item can help without replacing a proper rest.
The fallen character returns, but the script's remaining lines are still finite.
Revival has limits. A reassuringly honest product review.
We should review remaining moves as well as the restored HP.
Returning to the path does not erase how far someone has already walked.
They need us to notice the exhaustion that one item doesn't solve.
I'd check whether a Center visit is the better next step.

contexts.subject: A shopper values Max Repel longest duration.

MossdeepCity_Mart_Text_MaxRepelLastsLong.text: MAX REPEL keeps all weak POKéMON away.\pOut of all the REPEL sprays, it lasts\nthe longest.$

replies.text: The longest quiet spell in a bottle. Helpful when we have somewhere definite to be.
Maximum duration may reduce the number of applications a long route requires.
Useful. It still doesn't replace looking where we step.
An uninterrupted stretch can be nice when everybody is tired.
We can choose it for a long trip instead of using the biggest thing for every short walk.
The traveler's pause in encounters receives an extended edition.
A larger allowance of peace before the next practical task.
I'd compare the route length with the actual duration needed.
A quiet passage can be chosen without disliking what lives beside it.
The convenience should fit our plans rather than decide them.
I'd ask which journey made the longer duration worth it for them.

contexts.subject: A sailor describes local Net and Dive Balls and their different capture specialties.

MossdeepCity_Mart_Text_NetAndDiveBallsRa.text:
The NET and DIVE BALLS are rare POKé
BALLS that are only made in MOSSDEEP.\pA NET BALL is effective against
BUG-type and WATER-type POKéMON.\pA DIVE BALL works best on POKéMON
at the bottom of the sea.$

replies.text: Two kinds of Ball, two very different ideas of who belongs in the customer list.
Net Balls key on types; Dive Balls key on the underwater encounter setting.
Choose for the actual encounter. Similar colors don't mean similar uses.
It's nice to know why something is made in the town where we're standing.
A specialist tool earns its space when the trip actually calls for it.
The local industry has produced a pair of impressively specific invitations.
The sea has generated several product categories. Predictable economic behavior.
We should keep the two conditions distinct when packing.
The same water can hold different reasons for choosing a thing.
Knowing the purpose makes the shelf less overwhelming.
I'd ask the sailor which one he uses on his own trips.

contexts.subject: A shopper explains that PP Up raises a move use capacity.

SootopolisCity_Mart_Text_PPUpIsGreat.text: PP UP is great!\pIt raises the POWER POINTS, the PP,\nof a POKéMON move.$

replies.text: A favorite move gets a little more room before it needs a rest.
It increases a move's capacity rather than simply refilling the current amount.
Use it on something the partner will actually keep using.
It's useful to know the difference between more room and a refill.
A little more endurance can help, but we should still notice when the team needs a break.
The reliable line receives permission for a few additional repetitions.
An enlarged allowance of one particular activity. Sensible specialization.
We should choose the move deliberately before using a limited item.
A well-known path can be given a little more distance.
The best choice is the one that fits the partner, not simply our newest move.
I'd ask which move the shopper thought worth improving.

contexts.subject: During the crisis, a shopper fears leaving shelter despite wanting to understand events.

SootopolisCity_Mart_Text_TooScaryOutside.text: What…\nWhat is happening?\pI really want to know, but it's too\nscary to go outside.$

replies.text: Wanting an answer doesn't mean you have to walk into danger to get it.
The desire for information can be met without unnecessary exposure.
Stay inside. We can seek reliable news without sending him out.
Not knowing makes every sound outside feel larger.
He needs a calm update and somewhere safe to wait.
The extraordinary event has trapped an ordinary person between curiosity and fear.
A perfectly reasonable objection to conducting firsthand fieldwork today.
Clear information inside the shelter would reduce both confusion and risky trips.
A window can feel too small for the fear beyond it.
His hesitation is sensible. Nobody needs to shame him into bravery.
I'd ask whether the shop has received a recent message from someone trustworthy.

contexts.subject: A shopper speculates that the abnormal weather signals something awakening.

replies.text: That is a much larger explanation than forgetting to bring an umbrella.
The weather is observable; its proposed cause still needs evidence.
Something is wrong. We don't need a complete theory to take shelter.
A half-spoken question can make the room feel very quiet.
I would rather give him what we know than add another alarming guess.
The weather has prompted a question old stories are unusually ready to answer.
An ominous hypothesis has entered the shop without buying anything.
We should separate direct reports from interpretations while the situation develops.
A disturbance can feel older than the sky it darkens.
He is trying to give the fear a shape. That doesn't establish the answer.
I'd ask what he saw change before deciding what caused it.

contexts.subject: A shopper enthusiastically praises Full Restore combined HP and status recovery.

SootopolisCity_Mart_Text_FullRestoreItem.text: Do you know FULL RESTORE?\pFull restoration of HP!\nEradication of all status problems!\pIt's truly an item of your dreams!$

replies.text: A bottle with more than one helpful answer inside. That's efficient kindness.
Combined recovery can resolve HP loss and status in a single use.
Useful when both problems need solving. Keep one ready for a hard stretch.
It sounds reassuring to have a broad answer when something goes wrong.
A good emergency supply still leaves room for a proper rest afterward.
The comprehensive remedy has acquired an understandably enthusiastic reviewer.
Several problems, one bottle. A rare economy of effort.
We should save the combined effect for situations that actually benefit from it.
A helpful thing can make a frightened moment feel a little more manageable.
The dream is useful recovery, not an excuse to keep pushing forever.
I'd ask what situation made the shopper appreciate it so much.

contexts.subject: The greeter welcomes the player to Lilycove Department Store.

replies.text: A whole tower of things we didn't know we might want until we walked in.
A larger store makes the floor directory an especially useful first stop.
Check the list before we start wandering.
It's a lot of room and a lot of people all at once.
Let's find what we came for before the bags fill themselves.
The grand entrance opens onto several floors of possible subplot.
An impressive building dedicated to making a short errand less likely.
A good layout should help us find a specific item without searching every floor.
A bright doorway can hold more choices than we need today.
A friendly greeting makes an enormous store feel a little easier to enter.
I'd ask which floor has the thing at the top of our list.

contexts.subject: A shopper enjoys the store enough to buy many unplanned things.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_1F_Text_IBu.text: Whenever I come to the DEPARTMENT\nSTORE, I always end up buying all sorts\lof things because it's so fun.$

replies.text: Every shelf has apparently volunteered to come home with her.
The pleasurable browsing experience is influencing purchases beyond the original need.
Have fun. Leave enough money and room for the trip home.
I'd want a quiet moment to decide which things I really liked.
A little planned treat is easier to enjoy than a bagful of surprises at the till.
The store has an unusually successful talent for expanding the supporting cast.
A hobby with an alarming receipt length.
A short list and spending limit would make the choices easier.
A pretty thing can be enjoyed without being carried away.
I like browsing too. The trick is keeping the room's excitement separate from your own taste.
I'd ask which unexpected purchase she was happiest about later.

contexts.subject: A girl looks forward to her mother buying furniture for her.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_1F_Text_Mom.text: Today, my mom is going to buy me some\nnice furniture.$

replies.text: She is already furnishing the room in her head while her feet are still downstairs.
Choosing a space can help a child feel ownership and comfort at home.
Good day for her. Make sure it fits through the door.
I wonder which corner she's been imagining differently.
A comfortable place for her own things is a lovely gift.
The interior designer has arrived with maternal funding.
A room renovation with a very enthusiastic small client.
Measure the space before falling in love with the biggest piece.
A new little corner can make a familiar room feel newly hers.
I'd let her describe what she wants the room to feel like.
I'd ask which piece she is most excited to choose herself.

contexts.subject: A Trainer buys a present for Azumarill after a contest victory.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_1F_Text_Buy.text: I'm buying something for my AZUMARILL\nas a reward for winning a CONTEST.$

replies.text: Azumarill won a contest and now gets to win the shopping trip too.
The gift marks a shared achievement, though its value depends on what Azumarill enjoys.
Nice. Pick something the partner likes, not just something that looks grand.
I like that the victory includes a happy ordinary moment afterward.
A favorite treat can say well done more clearly than an expensive guess.
The triumphant performer has earned a modest shopping epilogue.
A champion with a potentially excellent gift budget.
I'd narrow the choices by Azumarill's actual habits.
An achievement can be remembered through a small act of affection.
The reward should make the partner feel celebrated, not displayed.
I'd ask what Azumarill gets most excited about outside contests.

contexts.subject: A cook stresses knowing how to use items properly.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_2F_Text_Lea.text: Learn to use items properly.\nThat's basic, really.$

replies.text: Owning a very useful thing is only half the very useful arrangement.
Understanding the application conditions is necessary to obtain the intended effect.
Read the instructions before the emergency.
I'd rather ask a basic question here than guess under pressure later.
I agree about learning. Calling it basic doesn't help someone who hasn't been taught.
The equipment list has been accompanied by a curt request for competence.
A sensible lesson in a slightly uninviting wrapper.
Test understanding with a clear example instead of assuming familiarity.
A helpful object needs a hand that knows what it offers.
People learn better when the explanation leaves them room to be beginners.
I'd ask which mistake the cook most often sees people make.

contexts.subject: A shopper considers a gift for her husband waiting at home.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_2F_Text_Goo.text: My husband is waiting at home.\nWhat would make a good gift for him?$

replies.text: The best aisle may be the one that reminds her of something he said last week.
A good prediction of his preferences is more useful than the item's general popularity.
Something he will use or genuinely enjoy. Doesn't have to be elaborate.
I like the thought of her picturing his face before choosing.
A favorite small comfort is often better than the most expensive shelf.
An absent character has become the quiet center of the shopping scene.
A present selected for an actual person. A promising departure from gift panic.
I'd start with a need or interest he has mentioned recently.
A familiar wish can guide a hand through an unfamiliar shelf.
Choose something that says she noticed him, not simply that she went shopping.
I'd ask what he has been enjoying doing at home lately.

contexts.subject: A sailor stocks up before a long journey.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_2F_Text_Sto.text: I'm leaving on a long journey soon.\nI need to stock up on items.$

replies.text: A long journey is easier when the useful little things aren't all back at home.
Supply planning should reflect route length, likely hazards, and opportunities to restock.
Good. Check the essentials before adding extras.
Packing makes a journey feel real before you've taken the first step.
I'd plan meals and water alongside the battle supplies.
The adventure is still in its most practical preparatory chapter.
An expedition begins with shopping and optimism. One is easier to measure.
A checklist will catch gaps more reliably than buying whatever looks useful.
A bag can hold a little foresight for the road ahead.
I hope the preparations include a comfortable way to carry everything.
I'd ask where the route next gives them a safe place to stop.

contexts.subject: A shopper observed increased Speed after giving Carbos.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_Gav.text: I gave a CARBOS to my POKéMON,\nand its SPEED went up.$

replies.text: A little extra speed, and now the Trainer has to keep up with the explanation.
The reported increase follows a relevant training supplement rather than a temporary battle boost.
Useful if speed suits the partner's role. Keep the rest of the training balanced.
I'd want to see how the partner feels using the change.
A helpful supplement works best alongside an ordinary healthy routine.
The character has acquired faster entrances through a remarkably small purchase.
An accelerated Pokemon and a presumably unchanged walking companion.
We should track the result and remember there are limits to supplementation.
A quick step should still lead somewhere chosen carefully.
Strengthening a trait makes sense when it fits who the partner is.
I'd ask where the Trainer first noticed the added speed.

contexts.subject: A shopper recommends Protein and Calcium for distinct attacking stats.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_Ite.text: For quickly toughening up POKéMON,\nitems are the best.\pPROTEIN boosts ATTACK,\nand CALCIUM raises SP. ATK.$

replies.text: Two kinds of strength, and the bottles don't get to swap their jobs.
Attack and special attack support different move categories. The distinction is important.
Match the item to the moves the partner actually uses.
I would rather understand the choice than make someone stronger in the wrong direction.
A supplement is only helpful when it fits the rest of the plan.
The preparation montage has developed a branching nutritional syllabus.
Two bottles, two attack statistics, several opportunities to read the label.
We should check which stat governs the intended moves before buying.
Different strengths can live behind the same familiar face.
The right choice serves the Pokemon's role, not the shopper's impatience.
I'd ask what kind of battle the shopper is preparing for.

contexts.subject: A shopper weighs Iron physical Defense against Zinc special Defense.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_Wan.text: I want my POKéMON to have more\nendurance.\pI'm trying to decide whether to raise\nDEFENSE with IRON, or SP. DEF with ZINC.$

replies.text: Two ways to be sturdier. The hard part is knowing what is likely to hit you.
The relevant defensive stat depends on the category of incoming moves.
Cover the weakness that actually matters to the partner.
It is nice that they are thinking about enduring a battle, not only hitting harder.
I'd look at the team's needs before choosing which bottle feels more reassuring.
The defender's preparation depends on which sort of trouble the next scene contains.
A choice between two kinds of not being knocked over. Both appealing.
We should compare likely threats rather than raise both numbers without a purpose.
A shelter is strongest where it answers the weather that reaches it.
More endurance should mean more comfort, not permission to ignore distress.
I'd ask which attacks have been giving the partner trouble.

contexts.subject: A shopper struggles to choose between offensive and defensive TM moves.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_4F_Text_Att.text: Hmm…\pAn attacking move…\nOr a defensive move…\pIt's no easy matter to decide which TM\nmoves should be taught to POKéMON…$

replies.text: A strong move is helpful. Being able to stay for the next turn is also persuasive.
The value of either option depends on the partner's role and existing coverage.
Choose what the team lacks, not simply whichever sounds more impressive.
A quieter defensive choice can be difficult to recognize as the brave one.
I'd think about the whole team before choosing what one partner should learn.
The author must decide whether the next line delivers a blow or changes the scene.
An attacking answer or an answer to being attacked. Context insists on participating.
We can identify a real failure in the current plan and choose what fixes it.
A held ground can matter as much as a forward step.
The move should make sense for the one learning it, not only the shelf description.
I'd ask which situation made the shopper want a new move.

contexts.subject: A shopper cites a catalog listing fifty kinds of TM moves.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_4F_Text_Fif.text: There are so many different kinds of\nTM moves.\pA catalog I read said there are fifty\ndifferent kinds.$

replies.text: That's a lot of little lessons for something with only four spaces to remember them.
A catalog's count describes the listed collection, not the usefulness of every option.
Plenty of choices. We only need the ones that fit the team.
I think I would want one question answered before looking at all fifty.
A large menu is easier when you know what you came hungry for.
The course catalog is extensive; the student is permitted a much smaller timetable.
A comprehensive selection, with an excellent chance of decision fatigue.
I'd group them by the problems they solve instead of reading the entire list at once.
Many possible paths can wait while we choose the next useful step.
A number can impress without making the choice clearer.
I'd ask which unfamiliar TM the shopper is most curious about.

contexts.subject: A shopper wants every TM but recognizes Pokemon can only know four moves at once.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_4F_Text_Pok.text: I'd like to get all the different TMs,\nbut a POKéMON learns only four moves.$

replies.text: The collection wants a warehouse. The Pokemon would like us to make four decisions.
Owning all options does not remove the constraint on simultaneous use.
Four useful moves beat a bag full of indecision.
A smaller set can feel reassuring when every choice has a clear place.
You can enjoy collecting without expecting one partner to use the whole collection.
An enormous library meets an uncompromising four-line script.
The inventory may be ambitious. The move list remains concise.
We need complementary functions rather than four versions of the same solution.
A small vessel asks us to choose what truly belongs inside it.
Limits can help the partner's role feel clear instead of unfinished.
I'd ask which four the shopper actually finds hardest to choose between.

contexts.subject: A parent considers buying a doll for herself as well as for her children.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_5F_Text_Pla.text: This place is full of cute DOLLS.\pI should buy some for me, instead of\njust for my children.$

replies.text: Grown-ups are allowed a small soft friend too. No child-shaped permission slip needed.
Enjoyment of a comforting object does not require a particular age.
Get one she likes. Nothing wrong with enjoying her own home.
I like hearing someone remember that their own little wishes count too.
She can choose a treat for herself without taking anything from the children.
The patron of children's collections finally commissions a piece for her own.
Adulthood has many burdens. It need not include a ban on plush creatures.
I'd ask what size and place would make it easy to enjoy at home.
A small soft thing can belong to any tired hand.
I'd encourage her to pick the one she keeps looking back at.
I'd ask which doll she would choose if nobody else had an opinion.

contexts.subject: A shopper considers buying every cute mat rather than choosing one.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_5F_Text_Sel.text: They sell many cute MATS here.\pI wonder which one I should get?\nMaybe I'll buy them all…$

replies.text: A room has only so much floor before the mats start stacking like sandwiches.
Buying every option avoids choosing but creates a storage and placement problem.
Pick the one that fits the room. We can leave some for another day.
I would want to picture how it feels under the familiar furniture.
One well-chosen thing often feels nicer than a pile of almost-right ones.
The decorating decision threatens to become a complete acquisition of the floor department.
An ambitious attempt to solve taste with quantity.
Measure the available area and compare the colors before buying.
A lovely pattern needs space around it to be seen.
I'd choose the mat that ties the room together instead of competing with it.
I'd ask what the rest of the room looks like first.

contexts.subject: During the crisis, a shopper explains that dangerous weather has closed the rooftop.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_5F_Text_Clo.text: I think they closed the rooftop\nbecause the weather is wild today.$

replies.text: A roof is a poor place to argue with wild weather. Staying inside sounds wise.
Closing the exposed area is an appropriate response to hazardous conditions.
Keep it closed until it's safe. Shopping can wait.
It's unsettling when an ordinary stairway suddenly leads somewhere you shouldn't go.
I'd rather everyone be indoors than hurry through a sale outside.
The weather has removed a floor from the day's available itinerary.
The open-air shopping experience has become excessively open to the air.
They should keep the barrier clear and explain the closure to visitors.
A familiar height can become a different place under a changed sky.
A plain explanation helps people accept the detour without feeling dismissed.
I'd ask whether the staff have reliable information about reopening.

contexts.subject: A child chooses a doll while waiting until old enough to raise a Pokemon.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_5F_Text_Get.text: I'm not big enough to raise POKéMON,\nso I'm getting a cute DOLL instead.$

replies.text: A little pretend companion can keep a real future companion's place warm.
The doll offers enjoyment without the responsibilities of a living Pokemon.
Good start. There's time to learn before taking care of a partner.
I wonder which Pokemon the doll lets her imagine meeting.
She can enjoy the soft part now and learn the daily care a little at a time.
The future Trainer rehearses companionship with an exceptionally patient understudy.
A beginner's partner with admirably forgiving care requirements.
Learning what a real Pokemon needs will make the eventual meeting easier.
A small wish can sit beside you while you grow toward it.
It's a kind way to let her enjoy the dream at her own pace.
I'd ask what name she wants to give the doll.

contexts.subject: A shopper eagerly attends the rare clear-out sale and plans to stock up.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStoreRooftop_Text.text: Yes! I've been waiting a long time for\nthis clear-out sale.\pThey have items that you can only get\nhere. I'm going to load up, that I am!$

replies.text: The long-awaited sale has arrived, and his bag is about to discover why he was waiting.
Limited availability can create urgency beyond an item's actual usefulness.
Get what he'll use. Rare doesn't automatically mean needed.
I can hear how long he has been looking forward to the visit.
I'd make a list before the excitement starts filling every spare pocket.
The anticipated event finally opens its doors to a devoted audience of one.
The clearance table has successfully produced a sense of destiny.
Check the dimensions and price before making a large decorative commitment.
A rare opening can invite a hurried hand. Pause long enough to choose.
A good find should still fit the life it's going home to.
I'd ask which particular item made the wait worthwhile for him.

contexts.subject: A shopper cannot find a predictable schedule or television advertisement for clear-out sales.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStoreRooftop_Text.text: Don't they have set dates for their\nclear-out sales?\pI watch TV, but they never show any\ncommercials.$

replies.text: The sale is behaving more like a rare bird than a shop appointment.
An unpredictable schedule makes planning difficult even for interested customers.
Ask the staff. Waiting for a commercial isn't much of a plan.
It is frustrating to keep checking when nobody tells you what to expect.
A notice near the entrance would save people a wasted trip.
The grand commercial event has neglected the small business of announcing itself.
A sale marketed primarily through uncertainty. Bold.
A clear posted date would solve this more reliably than repeated television watching.
An opening is kinder when people know when to look for it.
He shouldn't have to turn an errand into a guessing game.
I'd ask where the department store publishes its notices.

contexts.subject: A rooftop visitor complains of thirst near the vending machines.

replies.text: His next grand adventure should probably involve a cup of water.
Thirst is a useful signal to act on before continuing a warm outing.
Get a drink and sit down for a moment.
The rooftop can feel warmer than you expect after all those stairs.
Water first. Choosing the perfect flavor can happen after the urgent part.
The towering shopping expedition has reached an unglamorous physiological requirement.
A dramatic condition with a potentially undramatic solution nearby.
He should check the vending machines rather than keep announcing the shortage.
A little water can bring the afternoon back into proportion.
Comfort sometimes asks for something very plain.
I'd point out the machines and give him room to get a drink.

contexts.subject: Club members recognize us and announce they are becoming our fans.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_Y.text:
Are you maybe…
… …\pYou are!
You are {PLAYER}!\pWe were just talking about you!\pWe were talking about how an
incredibly good TRAINER appeared.\pAnd that someone is you!
You're so cool!\pSo, we decided that we'll become
your FAN CLUB!\pWe all hope you'll keep battling
and show us how cool you are.\pThat way, maybe other people will
become fans just like me.$

replies.text: We have a fan club! Do we need to learn how to wave professionally?
They have connected our battles with a public reputation. That is a substantial change.
Nice of them. The team still comes before putting on a show.
That is a lot of attention to walk into all at once.
It is lovely that our work has made somebody happy.
An audience has formed without our ever booking a venue.
I had not prepared a face for being celebrated indoors.
Unexpected public recognition! There should be a briefing for this.
Our footsteps have apparently been arriving in stories before us.
A warm welcome. I hope they remember we can have ordinary days too.
I wonder which battle first got them talking about us.

contexts.subject: An enthusiastic fan promises continued support.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_A.text: I'll always be cheering for you!\pGo, {PLAYER}, go!$

replies.text: A little cheering to carry along the next long stretch.
Encouragement can be welcome without changing the work ahead.
Good of her. We will keep looking after the team.
She sounds so certain. It is a little overwhelming and very kind.
A kind voice can make a difficult day feel less solitary.
The cheering section has renewed its season ticket.
A stranger has decided to be warmly invested. Rather nice.
Positive feedback received. No technical adjustment required.
A small voice leaves a bright little echo.
She gives the encouragement generously. That suits her.
I wonder whether she cheers this loudly from the sidelines too.

contexts.subject: Our remaining fan believes in us and wants others to see our serious battling.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_I.text: I'll always believe in you,\n{PLAYER}.\pPlease show the others what you're\nlike when you battle seriously.$

replies.text: She kept her little flag raised when the crowd wandered off.
Her support has persisted independently of the group's current preference.
One sincere supporter is worth hearing. We still set our own pace.
It means something when encouragement stays after the room gets quiet.
We can appreciate her faith without making every day a performance.
The audience has shrunk; the commitment has not.
A single steady voice can be easier to hear than a crowd.
Support retained through changing conditions. That seems genuine.
One light remaining is still a light.
She wants people to see what she sees. A sweet impulse.
I wonder what part of our battling made that impression on her.

contexts.subject: A former fan says we lost our drive and now prefers another trainer.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_W.text:
I'm sorry.
I was your fan before.\pBut now, you seem to have lost
the drive you had before.\pLately, I think {STR_VAR_1} has been
a lot cooler.$

replies.text: The cheering has changed addresses. We can still have a perfectly good afternoon.
Her interpretation of our motivation is not a direct measurement of it.
Her choice. We do not owe her a busier schedule.
That stings, though she is allowed a different favorite.
The team's well-being still matters more than keeping strangers impressed.
The critic has moved to another production and issued a rather personal review.
A quiet season need not explain itself to every former admirer.
Preference changed. Our goals do not need an automatic update.
An echo fading does not mean the road has disappeared.
