She can move on without deciding what is happening inside us.
I wonder how much of our journey she actually sees.

contexts.subject: A club member respects our strength but remains loyal to another favorite.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_E.text:
Oh!
{PLAYER}!\pEveryone's been all excited about
you recently.\pI can understand why.
I know that you're strong.\pBut, do you know what?\pOnce I became {STR_VAR_1}'s fan,
I can't just stop being a fan.$

replies.text: Fair enough! A fan club is not compulsory uniform day.
She distinguishes recognizing ability from choosing a personal favorite.
Her choice. Respect does not require switching sides.
I appreciate how kindly she explained it.
There is room to admire more than one person without changing loyalties.
A graceful refusal to follow the room's newest enthusiasm.
A favorite can remain a favorite without everyone else's permission.
Independent preference maintained. Completely reasonable.
Not every flower needs to turn toward the same light.
She can appreciate us without making a performance of joining in.
I wonder what first made her a fan of that trainer.

contexts.subject: A member admires the way trainers look during battles.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_T.text: I think TRAINERS are so cool when\nthey're battling.\pDon't you think so, too?$

replies.text: The focused look does have something to it. Mine is mostly trying to count.
Skilled coordination can be visually impressive as well as effective.
Best when they are paying attention to the team, not the audience.
There is something striking about seeing somebody fully absorbed in what they know.
I like the quieter moments when a trainer notices what a partner needs.
Concentration supplies its own rather convincing costume.
A composed exterior can conceal an impressive amount of internal panic.
Competence looks good when the decisions actually work.
A person and a creature briefly moving toward the same thought.
Confidence works best when it is supported by real care.
I wonder which small gesture she notices most during a battle.

contexts.subject: The youngster asks us to autograph his shorts.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_C.text:
Oh! It's {PLAYER}!
Too cool!\pOh!
Oh, yeah!\pCan you autograph something?
How about my shorts?$

replies.text: The shorts have been offered as official memorabilia. I hope the ink survives laundry.
An unusual writing surface with predictable durability concerns.
Only if everyone is comfortable. A piece of paper works too.
I would be very nervous trying to sign clothing neatly.
That is a souvenir with a complicated washing schedule.
Fame has reached the critical stage of being asked to endorse trousers.
A signature whose public life depends on the laundry.
Fabric needs the right ink. Otherwise this is a very temporary autograph.
A little name asked to live on a very active pair of legs.
He has chosen a canvas that is clearly important to his personal style.
I wonder whether he plans to wear them or display them afterward.

contexts.subject: The youngster compares faith in our victories to his lifelong faith in shorts.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_C.text:
However hot it's been…\pAnd however cold it may get…\pI've always believed in, and worn,
shorts!\pI'm counting on you to keep
winning!\pI believe in you just as much as
I believe in shorts!$

replies.text: We have joined shorts in his most trusted category. Tremendous company.
The analogy is peculiar, but the commitment appears consistent.
Glad he is cheering. We still get to have a difficult day.
That is a lot of faith, explained in a very unexpected way.
He has found two things that make him happy. Good for him.
Our reputation now stands beside a garment with an unbroken seasonal record.
A wonderfully specific hierarchy of personal loyalties.
Established reference point, unusually ambitious comparison.
He knows what he believes in, right down to the knees.
His brand is consistent. His expectations of our win record are ambitious.
I wonder whether he has any other great convictions beyond these two.

contexts.subject: The youngster proudly shows that his mother embroidered Brock's name on his shorts.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_B.text:
BROCK's my hero!
He's a man among men!\pHeheh, I got my mom to do
something for me.\pI got her to embroider “BROCK”
on my shorts!$

replies.text: His mom has contributed official lettering to the fan club uniform.
A family member turned his enthusiasm into a personal keepsake.
Nice of his mother to make something that matters to him.
A small handmade thing can mean much more than merchandise.
That sounds like an affectionate way for her to join his interest.
The hero's name has been immortalized in a highly mobile textile edition.
A little stitchwork preserving a large enthusiasm.
Custom fabrication for a very satisfied user. Excellent.
Someone's patient hands made room for his favorite name.
A homemade detail makes the outfit his own.
I wonder whether she chose the lettering or let him design it.

contexts.subject: The youngster swears loyalty to Brock even as the last remaining fan.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_B.text: …  …\p…  …\nI'm BROCK's fan!\pEven if I were his only fan,\nI swear it on my rock-hard will,\land on my shorts!\pI'll be his fan to the bitter end!$

replies.text: The shorts have been called as witnesses to a very solemn oath.
His preference remains stable despite social pressure to change it.
He can like Brock without needing a crowd behind him.
It is nice that other people changing their minds does not make him feel wrong.
A genuine favorite does not need to win a room vote.
A vow of rock-hard loyalty, countersigned by the shorts.
A small stubborn affection standing pleasantly on its own.
Preference held independently of popularity. Reasonable.
One little flag stays where it was planted.
He has made the loyalty theatrical, but it seems sincere.
I wonder what Brock did that he remembers so strongly.

contexts.subject: The youngster sees Brock as the person he wants to become like.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_B.text: BROCK's the last word on cool,\nend of story!\pNow there's a guy who I want to\nbe like!$

replies.text: A hero can be a good starting point. He still gets to become himself.
A role model is most useful when admired qualities are identified specifically.
Learn what is worth learning. No need to copy the whole person.
It is sweet to hear a future imagined with that much certainty.
I hope he admires the care behind the strong-looking part too.
An impressive figure has become a rough draft for somebody's future.
A borrowed example can help you find your own shape.
Useful to ask which traits he wants to practice first.
A small person has found a taller outline to grow toward.
Admiration suits him. A little room for his own taste would suit him too.
I wonder what he would ask Brock if they met.

contexts.subject: An older fan says our battling recalls his youth and wishes us success.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_H.text:
{PLAYER}, I've had the pleasure of
watching you battle.\pIt brings back sweet memories of
my own long-lost youth.\pMay you continue to find success.
You have a fan in me!$

replies.text: We gave him a little of an old afternoon back. That is a lovely compliment.
A present experience has connected with a meaningful earlier memory.
Good to know he enjoyed watching. Sounds like he has stories of his own.
There is a gentle warmth in how he remembers being young.
A shared interest can bridge quite a few years without much effort.
The spectator recognizes a familiar fire in a new generation's scene.
An old memory stirred kindly instead of aching. I am glad.
Experience across generations can make the feedback interesting.
A long-quiet part of someone's life answered a little when we battled.
He gives the praise without trying to make it a claim on us. Lovely.
I would be curious to hear what his own early journeys were like.

contexts.subject: Our remaining older fan praises us extravagantly and asks us to promise to continue.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_N.text:
I have journeyed far and wide
across the lands.\pBut never have I seen a TRAINER
of your magnificence.\pTake courage in your abilities
and keep battling on!\pMake that a promise to me,
my young idol!$

replies.text: Magnificence is a large word to carry when I still misplace my own socks.
His praise is generous, but a promise about future battling remains our choice.
Kind of him. We do not need to promise a stranger our whole road.
It is lovely and a little too much all at once.
We can thank him warmly without turning every future day into an obligation.
A magnificent review, followed by a proposed long-term engagement.
I would prefer to remain slightly less magnificent and considerably less observed.
Positive assessment noted. Avoid committing beyond the team's needs.
A bright opinion can be held gently without becoming a heavy crown.
The praise should feel like a gift, not a contract.
I wonder which moment made such a strong impression on him.

contexts.subject: The older member does not recognize us and asks whether we want to join the fan club.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_H.text: Hmm…\nAnd you are?\pWere you hoping to sign up for\na membership in our FAN CLUB?$

replies.text: For one peaceful moment, we are simply a potential new club member.
He does not recognize us. No special status needs to be inferred.
No problem. We can be visitors without a reputation.
An ordinary introduction feels rather comfortable.
A club should be able to welcome someone without knowing their accomplishments.
The public figure has been recast as an interested member of the public.
Being unknown can be a pleasant little rest.
Identity not established. A simple introduction would resolve it.
A name can arrive quietly before the stories attached to it.
No need to announce ourselves like an important delivery.
I wonder how he welcomes people who are new to the whole hobby.

contexts.subject: The older member acknowledges our reputation but says we have not met his standard of greatness.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_Y.text:
Ah, so you are the much-
talked-about {PLAYER}.\pYou certainly do have the look of
a winner.\pBut for me to accept you as
a true POKéMON great…\p… …\pYou've still a ways to go!$

replies.text: His personal greatness committee has deferred the application. We can keep walking.
His standard is subjective and not clearly specified. It need not define our goals.
Fine. The team is not training for his approval.
That can be hard to hear when you did not ask to be evaluated.
We can value the work already done and still keep learning.
The critic has produced a high bar without providing its height.
An impressive-looking gate, built entirely from someone's opinion.
Undefined acceptance criteria. Not a useful target for planning.
Another person's distant horizon need not become ours.
He is allowed a standard. We are allowed our own reasons for traveling.
I wonder whether he ever explains what he thinks is still missing.

contexts.subject: The older member says repeated victories could make us a subject of fan-club discussion.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_Y.text:
All of us gathered here are fans
of POKéMON TRAINERS.\pThe way they look in battle…
They are the picture of coolness.\pPerhaps you will be talked about
here, too, if you keep winning.$

replies.text: Win enough, become table talk. An unusual prize to put on a training plan.
The club's attention appears contingent on visible performance. That is not the only measure.
We have better reasons to train than being discussed in this room.
I would rather be noticed by the partners who actually know the work.
The team's needs make a steadier guide than a room's changing excitement.
Repeated victories may purchase a speaking role in the club's weekly conversation.
Being worth discussing and being worth something are rather different matters.
External interest is feedback, not a required objective.
The road continues even when nobody tells stories about it.
A reputation can be pleasant. Chasing it sounds tiring.
I wonder how much the club knows about trainers' ordinary days.

contexts.subject: A child excitedly says she wants to become like us.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_W.text: It's {PLAYER}!\nIt's {PLAYER}!\pI want to be like {PLAYER} one day!$

replies.text: That is a big little compliment. We should try to deserve the kind part.
Admiration makes our conduct, not just our results, potentially influential.
Then show her how to look after a team as well as win.
I would want to say something useful, and probably forget every word.
She can learn from us and still find a journey that fits her.
The audience has begun imagining its own turn on the road.
A little future is looking at us with very wide eyes.
Role-model responsibility detected. Better demonstrate good habits.
A small bright wish has found a person to stand beside it.
A sincere compliment. I hope she keeps room to become herself too.
I wonder what part of our journey she most wants to try.

contexts.subject: The child celebrates being our only remaining fan as if she can have us to herself.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_E.text:
Everyone stopped being {PLAYER}'s
fan…\pBut that means I can have {PLAYER}
all to myself!\pYay! Go for it!
My one and only {PLAYER}!$

replies.text: A smaller fan club does not come with exclusive ownership of the trainer.
Her enthusiasm is affectionate, but exclusivity should not be confused with possession.
We can be kind without agreeing that we belong to her.
That is sweet and a little too close to a promise nobody made.
She can enjoy cheering without needing everyone else to disappear.
The diminished audience has mistaken vacancy for a private booking.
A person is not a collectible made rarer by fewer admirers.
One interested observer does not become the system administrator.
A small heart sometimes holds an idea more tightly than it knows.
A gentle boundary would help more than laughing at her.
I wonder whether she simply means she is glad to get a chance to talk.

contexts.subject: The child admires Sabrina and wants to be a psychic girl.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_W.text: Do you know what?\nI want to be like SABRINA!\pI want to be a psychic girl just\nlike her!$

replies.text: A future with psychic powers is certainly an ambitious first draft.
An admired figure can encourage curiosity even when their abilities are not easily reproduced.
Good to have a hero. There is plenty she can learn without copying every power.
She imagines herself so clearly. It is rather lovely.
I hope she finds someone patient to answer her questions.
The young admirer has selected a striking and mysterious model for the future.
A small person has found room in the world for being unusual.
A clear interest. Reliable information is the next useful step.
An odd gift can look like a door when someone you admire wears it well.
Cute and capable is a perfectly reasonable thing to admire.
I wonder which story about Sabrina first caught her imagination.

contexts.subject: The child remains Sabrina's fan even when everyone else favors us.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_W.text:
Even if I'm the only one, I won't
stop being SABRINA's fan.\pMy dream is to be like SABRINA,
cute, but cool.\pI want to be a psychic girl just
like her!$

replies.text: She has kept her favorite without asking the room to vote again.
Her admiration is not dependent on matching the group's current preference.
Her choice. No reason she needs to cheer for us.
It is nice that she still sounds happy being the only one.
A real favorite can be good company even in a room full of other opinions.
The small defender of a personal favorite holds her corner admirably.
She has made a comfortable little place outside the crowd.
Preference stable under social pressure. Perfectly fine.
One little star need not become the whole room's favorite to remain bright.
She is keeping her own taste. A useful skill to have early.
I wonder whether she knows other Sabrina fans outside this club.

contexts.subject: The child wonders if she can become an impressive trainer someday.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_C.text: I wonder if I can become a cool\nTRAINER one day?$

replies.text: A small start is still a start. Every impressive trainer had one.
Learning, support, and patient practice can develop abilities over time.
She can begin by learning how to care for a partner. Good first step.
I would rather encourage the question than make a grand promise about the answer.
A kind, steady trainer is already something worth aiming for.
An audience member has begun considering an entrance of her own.
The future is not a room she needs permission to imagine.
Start with manageable skills, then add the next challenge.
A path can begin with a little question asked quietly.
She does not have to look impressive before she starts learning.
I wonder what kind of partner she imagines beginning with.

contexts.subject: The rocker clarifies that he admires our battling rather than us personally.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_T.text:
Oh, man, oh, man!
Cool! Too cool!\p…Huh?
No, not you.\pJust the way you battle.
That's cool.$

replies.text: A compliment carefully fitted with an emergency exit.
He is distinguishing admiration for performance from personal attachment.
Fine by me. The team did good work.
That was a rather awkward correction to an already surprising compliment.
He can appreciate the skill without needing to know everything about us.
A favorable review followed by an emphatic disclaimer from the critic.
He has made admiration sound suspiciously like denying an accusation.
Specific feedback is useful. The defensive packaging is optional.
A person and the thing they do cast slightly different shadows.
He is allowed a precise compliment. A little more grace would finish it nicely.
I wonder what particular decision impressed him.

contexts.subject: The rocker enjoys being our only fan because it feels less stressful.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_I.text: Yo, {PLAYER}!\pLooks like I'm the only one left\nout of your fans.\pBut, you know, I like being an only\nfan… It's less stressful.\pKeep up and at it!$

replies.text: A one-person fan club has very manageable meeting arrangements.
He appears more comfortable without the social pressure of the wider group.
Fair enough. He can enjoy the battles without joining a crowd.
I understand finding the quiet version of something easier.
It is nice that he still sounds relaxed rather than disappointed.
The exclusive audience appreciates the improved legroom.
Fewer voices can leave more room to hear what you actually like.
Reduced crowding improves the experience for this user. Noted.
A little quiet corner of admiration, with no elbows to compete against.
He has found a way to enjoy the situation on his own terms.
I wonder what part of the crowded club felt stressful to him.

contexts.subject: The rocker admires another trainer's way of speaking and wants to meet him.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_L.text: {STR_VAR_1}'s cool, huh?\nI love the way he talks.\pI'd really relish a chance to meet\nhim in person once.$

replies.text: Some people make an ordinary sentence sound like an event.
Vocal style can strongly influence a public impression independently of battle skill.
Could be an interesting meeting. A good line is not the whole person.
A voice can stay with you in a very particular way.
I hope the real conversation is as pleasant as he imagines.
An admirer drawn by the dialogue as much as the action. A discerning interest.
A turn of phrase can become a strange little thing to carry around.
Distinctive presentation can make information remarkably memorable.
A voice can leave a shape after the words themselves are gone.
Delivery is part of style. I understand noticing it.
I wonder what phrase he keeps remembering.

contexts.subject: The rocker stays loyal to another trainer and enjoys being that trainer's only fan.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_I.text:
Huh, can you believe it?
Everyone turned into your fans.\pSo after all we've been through,
I'm the lone {STR_VAR_1} fan?\pEh, being the one and only
{STR_VAR_1} fan's my style, anyway.$

replies.text: He has turned an empty fan table into his preferred seat.
He is comfortable retaining a preference that no longer matches the group.
Good. No need to change favorites to fit the room.
It is nice that being outnumbered does not make him feel unwelcome.
He can enjoy the battles without needing a crowd to agree.
The lone critic has declared solitude an essential part of his aesthetic.
An eccentric little pleasure, and apparently quite sufficient.
Independent preference, positive experience. No fault to fix.
A single candle can make a corner feel like someone's own.
Keeping your taste is easier when you can laugh about the empty seats.
I wonder whether he would be delighted or annoyed to meet another fan.

contexts.subject: An enthusiastic woman praises our battling and calls herself our number-one fan.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_A.text:
Oh, my goodness!
Is it really you, {PLAYER}?\pI have to tell you, I adore the
way you battle.\pI hope you'll keep at it.
I'll be your number one fan!$

replies.text: The number-one position filled itself before we knew it was vacant.
She is expressing strong appreciation for a particular performance.
Kind of her. The partners deserve their share of the praise.
That much excitement makes me want to hide and smile at the same time.
It is lovely when somebody's enjoyment is so unguarded.
A glowing notice from a critic who has chosen a very prominent seat.
I hope there is no required speech for receiving that much enthusiasm.
Strong positive feedback. We can acknowledge it without promising a perfect record.
A bright voice welcoming the road into this little room.
Her delight is charming. No need to turn it into a contest over who cheers most.
I wonder what moment of the battle she would describe first.

contexts.subject: The woman realizes she is our only fan but cheers anyway.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_I.text:
Oh, my goodness!
If it isn't {PLAYER}!\pIt's so disappointing… I realized
I'm your number-one-and-only fan!\pWell, it can't be helped!
Let me cheer you on, at least!\pHurray, hurray, {PLAYER}!$

replies.text: Number one out of one still comes with a very determined cheer.
She acknowledges the changed crowd while continuing her own support.
Good of her. We can appreciate one voice without chasing the rest.
There is something touching about cheering after noticing nobody else joined in.
A small sincere welcome can mean more than a noisy room.
The diminished audience has elected to give an undiminished performance.
A little embarrassment, bravely made into kindness.
Support continues despite reduced participation. Seems genuine.
A voice can be warm without having another voice beside it.
She lets herself be disappointed and kind in the same breath.
I wonder whether she knows the cheer matters without the crowd.

contexts.subject: The woman enthusiastically praises another trainer's recent battle form.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_T.text: Recently, {STR_VAR_1} has been on\nfire.\pThe way he battles… It's just \nthe way that I like it!$

replies.text: Someone has been giving her very exciting matches to talk about.
Her enthusiasm is directed at a recent performance trend, not necessarily a permanent ranking.
Good for that trainer. We do not need to compete for every compliment.
It is nice to hear someone enjoy watching so much.
A good match can give people something pleasant to share for days.
The current favorite receives a vivid, if thankfully figurative, description.
A spark of someone else's good day has traveled into this room.
She likes the current style. Preferences can be that specific.
An unseen battle is still giving off a little heat in the telling.
She knows the kind of performance she enjoys. Fair enough.
I wonder what changed recently that caught her eye.

contexts.subject: The woman feels isolated because everyone discusses us while she prefers another trainer.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_E.text:
Oh, hello!
If it isn't {PLAYER}!\pLately, all everyone talks about
is you.\pI'm feeling lonesome because I
prefer {STR_VAR_1}.$

replies.text: A room can get very narrow when it discovers one subject and refuses to put it down.
Her isolation concerns the group's conversation, not merely her private preference.
She should be able to talk about her favorite too.
I know what it is like when there is no small opening for your own thought.
A club is nicer when more than one interest gets a turn.
The audience has become unanimous enough to forget it contains separate people.
A room full of voices can still leave someone feeling quite alone.
The conversation needs broader input, not a change to her preference.
There should be room at the table for a different little light.
Being enthusiastic does not mean everybody has to wear the same opinion.
I would rather ask what she likes about her favorite than make her defend it.

contexts.subject: Watching us inspires the woman to consider becoming a trainer herself.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_Y.text: Amazing!\n{PLAYER}, you really are amazing!\pInstead of just watching, maybe\nI should become a TRAINER, too.$

replies.text: The fan club may have accidentally launched a new expedition. Excellent side effect.
Observation has prompted interest in direct participation. A useful transition.
Start with care and the basics. There is room for a new trainer.
It is lovely when admiration turns into wanting to try something yourself.
She can begin small and find out which parts she enjoys.
A spectator has begun considering her own entrance, which is always an interesting moment.
A borrowed spark can become someone's own small fire.
Try a manageable first task. Much easier than planning an entire new identity.
The road has reached into the audience and found another pair of feet.
A genuine interest can look good before it looks impressive.
I wonder what kind of first partner she imagines.

contexts.subject: Our only remaining fan asks us to try harder so she has company in cheering.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_I.text: I'm your only fan…\nSigh… This is lonely…\pCan't you try harder and make the\nothers take notice of you?$

replies.text: We cannot fix her empty table by making the team perform on demand.
Her loneliness is real, but changing our schedule is not an automatic obligation.
The team does not owe anyone a perfect record to keep them company.
I feel for her, though that is a heavy request to put on a stranger.
A club could help her feel included without asking us to win more.
The lonely audience has submitted a rather demanding revision request.
An empty seat is not something another person has to win a battle to fill.
Wrong proposed fix. Broader club interaction would address the actual problem.
A lonely room should not become a weight on someone else's journey.
She deserves company. We deserve room to travel at our own pace.
I wonder whether anyone here asks her about interests beyond the scoreboard.

contexts.subject: The woman admires another trainer's dignity and wonders why the club does not agree.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_W.text: Master {STR_VAR_1} is so dignified…\nHe is so my type.\pWhy can't the others see the\ndignity he simply oozes?$

replies.text: Dignity is a quieter sort of favorite than another impressive win.
She is responding to manner and presence, qualities others may value differently.
She can admire that without convincing the whole room.
It is nice to notice how someone carries themselves, not just what they win.
Different people find different qualities reassuring. Nothing wrong with that.
A devoted critic appeals to the room's tragically unrefined appreciation of bearing.
A quiet presence can matter more to one person than a loud record.
Different evaluation criteria explain much of the disagreement.
Some people notice the stillness around a person first.
Poise is a real part of an impression. It just does not charm everyone equally.
I wonder what moment first made her think of him as dignified.

contexts.subject: The woman remains contentedly loyal to another trainer even as that trainer's only fan.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_B.text:
I believe in Master {STR_VAR_1}
with all my heart.\pEven if I am the only one to
believe in him.\pI won't ever feel lonesome, though.\pNot if I keep thinking about Master
{STR_VAR_1}.$

replies.text: Her favorite is still her favorite without an echo from the room.
She finds the preference rewarding without requiring social agreement.
That is her choice. No reason to take it away from her.
It is nice that she sounds settled rather than defensive.
A harmless enthusiasm can be good company on an ordinary day.
The loyal admirer declines to let a dwindling audience rewrite her opinion.
A private affection need not become a public petition.
Positive experience despite low popularity. No adjustment needed.
One little flame, quite content with its own corner.
She knows what she likes without borrowing everyone else's taste.
I wonder whether she has ever had the chance to tell him.

contexts.subject: A martial artist says our battle style is educational and urges us onward.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_Y.text: Hiyah!\pYour battling style is most\neducational.\pI hope that you will keep plugging\naway at success, hiyah!$

replies.text: A fan who brought a notebook in spirit. We should try to set a decent example.
He is attending to technique rather than only celebrating the result.
Good. Learning from a battle is worth more than just applauding it.
It is a thoughtful compliment, even delivered quite that loudly.
I hope he finds something useful for his own partners.
A critic who leaves the performance with practical notes. Excellent audience.
Admiration can become something useful in another person's hands.
Observed technique converted into possible improvements. Productive feedback loop.
A path can leave a little guidance for the next pair of feet.
He is interested in what works. That makes the praise feel considered.
I wonder which decision he would like to try himself.

contexts.subject: The martial artist resists his master's demand to stop watching and do more battling.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_W.text:
Instead of just watching others
battle, battle yourself!\p…My DOJO's MASTER chewed me out
like that…\pBut I won't let that stop me from
being your fan!\pI can't stop being your fan!$

replies.text: A person can practice and still enjoy cheering. There are enough hours for both, usually.
Observation and participation can complement one another rather than compete absolutely.
He should do the training he agreed to. He can still like watching us.
I understand wanting one interest that is simply yours to enjoy.
A balance would help more than making him choose a side.
The devoted spectator has encountered a director demanding he leave the audience.
Enjoyment does not always need to prove it is productive.
Observation needs practical follow-through, but practical work can allow spectatorship.
A voice cheering beside the road need not stop having its own footsteps.
His enthusiasm sounds real. I hope the master leaves room for it.
I wonder how much training time the watching actually takes away.

contexts.subject: The martial artist says only his dojo master deserves his respect and urges us to become fans.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_O.text:
Hiyah! There is but one TRAINER
who has my respect.\pAnd that is none other than my
MASTER at the FIGHTING DOJO.\pYou should become a fan of my
MASTER like me! Hiyah!$

replies.text: That is a very narrow guest list for respect. The invitation is enthusiastic, though.
Respect need not be an exclusive resource restricted to one person.
He can admire his master without dismissing everyone else.
I would rather not have to pass a loyalty test just to talk here.
There are many people worth learning from without replacing his favorite.
The disciple has opened a recruitment desk for a remarkably exclusive philosophy.
A single candle does not need every other candle put out.
One trusted source is not a complete reference library.
A path can have more than one person worth listening to.
Admiration looks better when it leaves room for ordinary courtesy.
I wonder what he most wants us to understand about his master.

contexts.subject: The martial artist says he sneaks out of the dojo to promote his master.

SaffronCity_PokemonTrainerFanClub_Text_N.text:
Hiyah! I respect my MASTER at the
FIGHTING DOJO.\pI will never become a fan of
anyone other than my MASTER!\pI will even sneak out of the DOJO
to spread word of his greatness.\pHiyah!$

replies.text: An unauthorized field trip in the name of extremely authorized admiration.
The secrecy suggests his method may not match the master's expectations.
If the master asked him to train, sneaking out is not much of a tribute.
He seems sincere, even if he has found an odd way to show it.
He might help his master more by asking what support is actually wanted.
A devoted publicist conducts a covert campaign for a man who may prefer him in class.
Loyalty has acquired an impressively disobedient practical method.
The stated goal and chosen behavior appear poorly aligned.
A shadow slipping away to praise the person it is hiding from.
A public tribute can still ignore the person supposedly receiving it.
I wonder whether the master knows where his most enthusiastic student goes.

contexts.subject: The news enthusiast complains of boredom when he has no new Wonder News.

CeruleanCity_House4_Text_NothingEntertai.text: Sigh…\nToo much time, too little to do…\pIs nothing entertaining happening\nanywhere?$

replies.text: A quiet day has failed his entertainment requirements. Perhaps he could go for a walk.
A lack of received news does not imply that nothing interesting is happening nearby.
Could make a plan instead of waiting for one to arrive.
Too much empty time can feel surprisingly heavy.
A small ordinary outing might help more than waiting for a spectacular story.
The resident critic has found today's entire world insufficiently eventful.
A comfortable room can become rather small when every minute echoes.
No new input. Maybe change the source rather than refreshing the same expectation.
The window remains full of a day that has not introduced itself yet.
He might find more to enjoy by looking beyond whatever arrives as news.
I wonder what kind of story he usually finds interesting.

contexts.subject: The enthusiast wishes his current news could be shared with more people.

CeruleanCity_House4_Text_WishCouldShareN.text: It seems such a shame to not share\nthis news with other folks…\pI wish I could tell someone…\nLet others know the news…$

replies.text: A good story has started bumping against the walls of his living room.
He sees information as something that gains value through appropriate sharing.
Good to share it if it is accurate and people want to hear.
It is nice that enjoying it makes him think of someone else enjoying it too.
A little interesting news can brighten an ordinary conversation.
The delighted audience member has volunteered to become a distributor.
A small bright thing asking for another pair of eyes.
Check the source before extending the network. Then share responsibly.
A story can be a little lamp passed from one room to another.
He wants the pleasure to travel farther than his own chair. Sweet.
I wonder whom he most wants to tell first.

contexts.subject: After enough news-related rewards, the enthusiast says he is happily occupied.

CeruleanCity_House4_Text_EnjoyingMyselfW.text: I'm quite enjoying myself with all\nsorts of news.\pYes, I am satisfied!\nI won't be bored for a while.$

replies.text: His boredom has been thoroughly outnumbered by things to read.
He has enough information to remain occupied for now. A clear stopping point.
Good. We can leave him to enjoy it.
It is nice to see the same room feel more lively to him.
A pleasant afternoon does not always need anything more than a good read.
The formerly restless critic has found a program sufficient to his tastes.
A chair can be a lovely place when the mind has somewhere to go.
Input queue full, user satisfied. No additional material required.
The quiet room now has a few more windows than before.
He sounds content without asking us for the next thing immediately.
I wonder which story he will return to after reading everything once.

contexts.subject: The news enthusiast cannot give his Berry reward because the Berry Pouch is full.

CeruleanCity_House4_Text_YourBerryPouchI.text: Hm? Your BERRY POUCH is full.\nMy gift remains ungiven, then.$

replies.text: Our news delivery succeeded; the thank-you has nowhere to land.
The intended Berry transfer failed. The speaker explicitly says the gift remains ungiven.
No reward received. Make space if we want to accept it later.
He sounds apologetic about a problem in our own bag.
A little sorting would make the next thank-you simpler.
The news has circulated more successfully than the accompanying fruit.
A crowded pouch interrupting an uncomplicated kindness.
Container capacity failure. Distinct from a successful reward.
A full little place has delayed the offered sweetness.
At least he states plainly that nothing has been handed over.
I wonder whether we have been keeping more Berries than we use.

contexts.subject: After giving the Powder Jar, the maker explains Berry crushing and requests powder for medicine.

CeruleanCity_House1_Text_GoCrushBerriesA.text:
There's something new on the second
floor of POKéMON CENTERS, at the\lDIRECT CORNER.\pThey installed a Wireless Adapter
machine for crushing BERRIES.\pThis is where you come in.\pI have a favor to ask, one that
I can entrust only to you.\pCould you make BERRY POWDER for
me using that machine?\pDon't forget, the machine is at the
DIRECT CORNER of POKéMON CENTERS.\pI'll concoct medicine for you if
you bring me some BERRY POWDER.\pDon't forget, crush BERRIES into
BERRY POWDER and bring it to me.$

replies.text: He has repeated the directions enough that even my distracted elbow remembers them.
The process links a supplied container, a preparation method, and a defined use for the material.
Clear enough. Check what we need before making the trip.
He sounds very eager to make sure the request is understood.
Preparing an ingredient properly matters when it is going into medicine.
The favor includes an unusually thorough rehearsal of the address.
A simple request made large by repeated directions and considerable hope.
Raw material, processing equipment, useful product. A proper workflow!
A little crushed fruit is meant to become a different kind of help.
He has made the instructions difficult to forget, at least.
I wonder which medicine he most enjoys making from it.

contexts.subject: The maker accuses us of lying about interest in Berries because we have none.

CeruleanCity_House1_Text_WhyMustYouLieNo.text: Why must you lie to me?\pHow many BERRIES do you have?\nNot a one!$

replies.text: An empty pouch is not proof of an empty interest. That was a sharp leap.
Owning a resource and being interested in it are separate conditions. His inference is unsound.
No need to call someone a liar over a missing Berry.
That is an upsetting answer to a question we thought was about liking something.
He could explain what we need without making an accusation.
The interview has unexpectedly become a prosecution with very poor evidence.
Apparently curiosity now requires a physical sample at the door.
Incorrect validation rule. Interest does not depend on current inventory.
A bare branch does not mean the tree dislikes fruit.
A gentler correction would have made him much easier to talk to.
I wonder whether he realizes how differently his question sounded to us.

contexts.subject: The maker lectures us about curiosity after we decline an interest in Berries.

CeruleanCity_House1_Text_TakeInterestInA.text: You have no interest in BERRIES?\pYoung one, it's important to take an\ninterest in all sorts of things.$

replies.text: There are many interesting things. We cannot carry all of them in one afternoon.
Broad curiosity is useful, but it does not require equal enthusiasm for every subject.
We answered honestly. He can leave it there.
Being told to enjoy something rarely makes it easier to begin.
He might make a better invitation by showing why he enjoys it.
A declined hobby has expanded into an unsolicited philosophy of education.
A mind can be open without furnishing a room for every visitor.
Time is limited. Choosing a focus is not a system fault.
Not every seed needs to take root in the same garden.
A little more welcome and a little less scolding might help his cause.
I wonder what first made him interested before he began recruiting others.

contexts.subject: After a successful powder exchange, the maker accepts our decision to stop trading.

CeruleanCity_House1_Text_HopeToSeeYouAga.text: That's fine, then.\nI'll hope to see you back again.$

replies.text: Exchange finished. The little pharmacy can take a breather from our menu browsing.
This goodbye follows a completed exchange and refusal of further trading.
Done for now. Check the supplies before heading out.
It is nice to finish without being pushed into another decision.
A useful ingredient has become something useful to carry. Good trade.
The transaction ends neatly rather than developing an unnecessary sequel.
A quiet close to a practical little bargain.
Exchange complete, menu closed, no extra operation requested.
Something gathered has changed into another kind of help.
A courteous finish matters after all the detailed choices.
I wonder how much of his day he spends preparing the next batch.

contexts.subject: The maker closes the selection menu and invites future powder trading.

CeruleanCity_House1_Text_SeeMeIfYoudLike.text: Come see me if you'd like to trade\nyour BERRY POWDER.$

replies.text: The menu has released us without requiring a purchase. A fine feature.
Closing the menu alone does not establish that an exchange occurred.
No need to choose something before we know what the team needs.
It is good to have room to think outside a long list of options.
We can come back with a clear plan instead of choosing just to finish.
The catalogue closes, leaving the invitation intact.
A page of possibilities can stay a page for today.
Menu exit handled cleanly. Existing holdings should remain as they were.
The little counter will be here when the right need arrives.
A calm invitation beats trying to rush a decision.
I wonder which option regular visitors choose most often.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that fainted Pokemon can still perform field moves.

Route2_House_Text_FaintedMonsCanUseField.text: A fainted POKéMON just has no\nenergy left to battle.\pIt can still use moves like CUT\noutside of battle.$

replies.text: Still able to help does not mean a tired partner no longer needs a rest.
The distinction concerns battle stamina versus some field capabilities.
Useful to know. Get them healed when we can.
I would feel bad asking too much from someone already worn out.
A partner helping on the way to care still deserves that care promptly.
The last reserve of usefulness should not become an excuse to postpone kindness.
A creature is more than the number that says it cannot battle now.
Different functions have different limits. Do not confuse capability with readiness.
A tired companion may still open the way home. Go home afterward.
A practical fact worth handling with a little judgment.
I wonder how often that knowledge has helped a stranded trainer.

contexts.subject: A traveler encourages searching different habitats to find different Pokemon.

Route2_ViridianForest_NorthEntrance_Text.text: Many POKéMON live only in forests \nand caves.\pYou need to be persistent and look\neverywhere to get different kinds.$

replies.text: A forest is not a cave with extra leaves. New place, new neighbors.
Habitat specialization makes varied exploration important for a complete record.
Look carefully. Do not rush every place like it is the last one.
There is something lovely about having a reason to notice the whole landscape.
Good preparation includes knowing which kind of place we are entering.
The wider cast refuses to assemble in a single convenient clearing.
The world has hidden different little lives in different kinds of quiet.
Broaden the sampling locations. Better data, more surprises.
Each place keeps a few names that belong especially to it.
Persistence is useful when it means patient attention instead of frantic searching.
I wonder which habitat the traveler most enjoys exploring.

contexts.subject: A traveler says certain thin roadside trees can be cleared with a Pokemon move.

Route2_ViridianForest_NorthEntrance_Text.text: Have you noticed the skinny trees\non the roadside?\pThey can be cut down by a special\nPOKéMON move, I hear.$

replies.text: The tiny tree has become a puzzle with roots.
The speaker suggests a specific field technique, though the claim is secondhand.
Know what we are clearing before swinging at every tree.
It is interesting how one small obstacle can shape an entire route.
A useful skill when the path actually calls for it.
A modest sapling has found a demanding role as the road's gatekeeper.
Even a small tree can make people reconsider their direction.
A capability gate disguised as vegetation. Memorable design.
A narrow trunk can still stand between two parts of a journey.
A specific obstacle is more useful to notice than a vague dead end.
I wonder what is on the other side of the trees they noticed.

contexts.subject: A traveler explains choosing to stop evolution and keep raising a Pokemon as it is.

Route2_ViridianForest_NorthEntrance_Text.text:
Do you know the evolution-cancel
technique?\pWhen a POKéMON is evolving, you
can stop the process.\pIt's a technique for raising
POKéMON the way they are.$

replies.text: A growing-up pause button. The Pokemon world keeps finding surprising options.
Delaying evolution offers control over timing while training continues.
A choice worth understanding before the moment arrives.
It is reassuring that change does not always have to happen immediately.
Take the partner and the plan into account before deciding.
The transformation may be deferred without canceling the rest of the story.
Something can remain familiar and still be learning.
Reversible timing decision. Useful option when the sequence matters.
A door can remain closed for a while without becoming a wall.
A thoughtful choice is better than changing just because it is available.
I wonder which partner made them want to wait.

contexts.subject: A traveler warns that Viridian Forest is a natural maze.

Route2_ViridianForest_SouthEntrance_Text.text: Are you going to VIRIDIAN FOREST?\nIt's a natural maze in there.\lBe careful you don't get lost.$

replies.text: The trees did not include a corridor numbering system. We should pay attention.
Similar-looking paths make landmarks and deliberate navigation useful.
Remember the way back. Keep the team together.
A little preparation makes a quiet forest much less intimidating.
We should leave enough time to return without hurrying.
The woodland setting comes with an unusually uncooperative floor plan.
A maze made by things that had no intention of making a maze.
Track turns and landmarks. Repeated scenery is how routes get confused.
The trees can make several paths wear the same face.
A plain warning is welcome before a confusing route.
I wonder which landmark locals use when they want to find the exit.

contexts.subject: A traveler warns that small Rattata can bite hard.

Route2_ViridianForest_SouthEntrance_Text.text: RATTATA may be small, but don't\nunderestimate its wicked bite.\pHave you caught one already?$

replies.text: Small teeth remain teeth. My ankles accept the warning.
Body size is not a reliable measure of the harm a bite can cause.
Give it space. Do not assume small means harmless.
A little creature still needs people to respect its boundaries.
Better to learn that from a warning than from a bandage.
The smallest resident declines a supporting role in anyone's complacency.
A modest silhouette, a pointed rebuttal to being underestimated.
Compact design can still deliver significant force. Noted.
A small shadow can hold a sharp edge.
A useful reminder for someone tempted to pick up every cute thing.
I wonder how many travelers are surprised by the same mistake.

contexts.subject: Oak's aide explains Flash after the reward or reminds us it helps navigate Rock Tunnel.

Route2_EastBuilding_Text_ExplainHM05.text: HM05 contains the hidden move\nFLASH.\pFLASH lights up even the darkest\nof caves and dungeons.$

Route2_EastBuilding_Text_CanGetThroughRo.text: Once a POKéMON learns FLASH, you\ncan get through ROCK TUNNEL.$

replies.text: A useful bit of light, earned by meeting enough new neighbors.
Flash addresses the visibility problem of dark routes such as Rock Tunnel.
Good. Prepare the light before entering the dark.
A little less uncertainty under the mountain sounds very welcome.
A practical reward for the next part of the journey.
The field research has paid out in improved lighting for the next setting.
A small answer to a very large amount of dark.
Visibility upgrade acquired. It should make navigation less error-prone.
A light carried beside you changes the shape of a cave.
Useful guidance, especially before someone learns the need halfway inside.
I wonder what part of Rock Tunnel people most often miss without light.

contexts.subject: The researcher cannot give Old Amber because our bag is full.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_DontHaveSpaceF.text: You don't have space for this.$

replies.text: Ancient history has waited this long; our bag can still make it wait another minute.
The specimen was not transferred. Its intended examination remains pending.
Make room. An old specimen deserves better than being jammed between supplies.
A serious favor deserves a more prepared pair of hands than ours just now.
We can sort the bag and return ready to carry it carefully.
A scientific breakthrough has been delayed by luggage management.
The old thing has survived time; it can survive a short wait for a proper place.
Capacity issue. Also, protect the specimen rather than forcing it in.
A piece of old sunlight is waiting outside a crowded pocket.
We should make room properly if we are going to accept that trust.
I wonder how the researcher has kept the amber safe until now.

contexts.subject: The badge enthusiast closes the explanation menu and invites another visit.

CeruleanCity_House1_Text_ComeVisitAnytim.text: Come visit me anytime you wish.$

replies.text: A little badge lecture, available whenever our curiosity comes back.
The menu has ended. This farewell does not specify which explanations were selected.
Good to know we can ask again instead of remembering it all at once.
I appreciate somebody making questions feel welcome.
A little learning is easier when there is time to return to it.
The lecturer leaves office hours agreeably open.
Some useful rooms are simply places where asking again is allowed.
Reference service remains available. No need to memorize the entire interface.
A patient voice can leave the door to a difficult subject open.
A generous invitation, without another test attached.
I wonder how often visitors return with a question they forgot the first time.

contexts.subject: Allen hopes for his first victory.

Route102_Text_AllenPostBattle.text: I haven't won once yet…\nI wish I would win soon…$

replies.text: The first win is being terribly slow about introducing itself.
He could look for one small improvement before the next match.
Keep learning. First win will need a plan.
It can feel lonely waiting for proof that you're improving.
A kind practice partner could make trying again easier.
A disappointing opening doesn't determine the length of the story.
The first good result can take an offensively long route.
A simpler strategy may reveal which part needs practice.
A little progress can arrive before the victory does.
He deserves encouragement that isn't an empty guarantee.
I'd like to hear about something that went better this time.

contexts.subject: Calvin says we should have warned him we were strong.

Route102_Text_CalvinPostBattle.text: Listen, you. If you're strong,\nyou should have told me before!$

replies.text: My strength announcement must have got lost behind my hello.
A challenge doesn't usually include advance disclosure of the result.
He challenged. We battled. That's fair.
I wouldn't know how to introduce myself with a warning.
He can be surprised without making it our fault.
An unexpected ending has inspired a demand for a much longer introduction.
I'll add a small ominous pause before my next greeting.
He learned more from the battle than a claim beforehand.
A person need not announce every strength before meeting someone.
Confidence is more convincing when it doesn't blame the other outfit.
He looked quite certain before the match, which makes this reaction interesting.

contexts.subject: Calvin wants his growth to keep pace with ours.

Route102_Text_CalvinRematchPostBattle.text: If you're going to get stronger,\nI'll get stronger, too.$

replies.text: A friendly competition with no fixed ceiling. Tall homework.
Comparing progress can help both sides avoid becoming complacent.
Good. We'll give each other something to work on.
It's nice when a rival sounds eager instead of resentful.
A steady practice friend makes the ordinary days more encouraging.
Two stories can push each other forward without needing the same ending.
Our improvement has acquired a very determined shadow.
He could choose a specific gap to close before our next meeting.
Another person's growth can call ours into motion.
A good rivalry leaves both people with room to develop.
I'd enjoy seeing which of us surprises the other next time.

contexts.subject: Calvin says he practiced since our last meeting and requests a rematch contact.

Route102_Text_CalvinRegister.text: I've been working hard at this since\nI saw you before.\pI'd like to battle you again, so can\nyou register me in your POKéNAV?$

replies.text: He brought the homework and a request for another assignment.
A return match would let him test what changed through practice.
Good effort. We'll see what it does next time.
It's lovely that he remembered the meeting as a reason to keep trying.
He should have something to feel proud of before the next result.
A returning rival has arrived with a revised edition.
He has been industrious while we were off being distracting.
We can compare the new approach with what happened before.
A familiar challenge can give patient effort a direction.
He wants the work to be seen. That's understandable.
I'd ask which new habit took the longest to learn.

contexts.subject: Calvin simply asks to keep in touch for another battle.

Route102_Text_CalvinRegisterShort.text: I'd like to battle you again, so can\nyou register me in your POKéNAV?$

replies.text: A future match, neatly filed under people worth meeting again.
A contact makes it easier to compare our progress later.
Sure. A fair rematch is worth coming back for.
I like a simple invitation that doesn't need a big speech.
We can arrange it when both teams are ready.
A short invitation can still open a rather long-running rivalry.
Brief, practical socializing. I support the format.
We can leave enough time between attempts to try something new.
A small request can leave a path open between people.
Friendly and direct. No dramatic persuasion needed.
The next time won't begin with two strangers sizing each other up.

contexts.subject: Rick says eye contact obliges trainers to battle.

Route102_Text_RickPostBattle.text: If you lock eyes with a TRAINER,\nyou have to challenge! It's a rule!$

replies.text: My eyeballs have been signing contracts without consulting me.
That custom explains many challenges, but comfort still matters.
A look isn't permission to push someone who's not ready.
That would make me nervous about where I looked.
It's all right to ask whether someone and their team are ready.
A glance should not require an entire combat scene every time.
I will be directing my mysterious gaze at the nearest shrub.
A clear invitation is better than guessing intent from eye contact.
A meeting can begin with a choice instead of an obligation.
Knowing the custom doesn't require making every glance confrontational.
I'd rather see a greeting before everyone reaches for their Pokemon.

contexts.subject: Tiana thinks more Pokemon will help her keep winning.

Route102_Text_TianaPostBattle.text: To keep winning my way up, I see that\nI have to catch more POKéMON.$

replies.text: More teammates mean more names to call before anyone answers.
Variety can help, though each partner needs time and attention.
Grow the team carefully. Numbers aren't a whole plan.
A new companion is exciting when there's room to know them.
Each addition needs ordinary care as well as training.
An expanded cast only works if no one becomes background furniture.
A bigger team can also mean a bigger pile of unfinished lessons.
She could identify the missing role before adding another Pokemon.
A new life deserves more than being an answer to a score.
A balanced team needs pieces that work together, not just more pieces.
I'd like to know which kind of partner she hopes to meet next.

contexts.subject: Liv insists the pair can do better and promises a future demonstration.

Route103_Text_AmyLivRegister.text: LIV: Really, we're a lot better…\nIt's true! We'll show you next time!$

replies.text: The improved version has been promised for our next visit.
They can use the interval to work on their coordination.
Then practice together. We'll see next time.
I hope Amy feels included in that confident promise.
They can keep the enthusiasm and give the team a break.
A strong advance announcement for a sequel still in rehearsal.
Their potential has issued a very emphatic press release.
One well-practiced interaction could make the next match different.
A promise grows steadier when both partners have room to help.
Confidence is a good start when it doesn't silence the other person.
I'd enjoy noticing what they change as a pair.

contexts.subject: Miguel wants us to revisit his delightful Pokemon.

Route103_Text_MiguelRegister.text: I'll get you to come out and look in\non my delightful POKéMON again!$

replies.text: A repeat appointment with the delightful department.
He seems keen to share his affection as much as battle again.
Happy to visit. Good to see a trainer like his team.
It's nice that he wants someone to notice what he loves.
A relaxed visit could give the Pokemon room to show their habits.
A recurring cast introduced by a thoroughly devoted publicist.
A social invitation where the Pokemon can carry the conversation.
We could compare what they have learned since the first meeting.
A shared fondness can make a new place familiar.
He wants an appreciative audience, and that can be a warm welcome.
I'd like to hear which little habit makes each one delightful to him.

contexts.subject: Cindy links greetings with goodbyes while hoping for another meeting.

Route104_Text_CindyPostRematch.text: “Hello” is the beginning of “good-bye.”\nI hope we meet again.$

replies.text: Goodbye is just hello doing a little traveling.
Repeated meetings can make an ordinary farewell feel less final.
We'll cross paths again if the roads line up.
That's a sad little thought with a hopeful end.
A kind goodbye makes returning easier.
An ending has quietly left its own opening line waiting.
A surprisingly efficient way to make a greeting sound haunted.
A contact can turn that hope into a practical arrangement.
A meeting can stay with us after the footsteps part.
A farewell can be graceful without pretending nobody will miss anything.
I'd remember the hope in that last sentence more than the sadness.

contexts.subject: Cindy sees another meeting as reason to exchange contacts.

Route104_Text_CindyRegister1.text: Hello, we meet again.\pWe seem to be drawn together. Let's\nregister each other in our POKéNAVS.$

replies.text: The road keeps arranging introductions. We might as well help.
A repeated encounter is a good opportunity to keep in touch deliberately.
Good idea. No need to rely on chance every time.
It's lovely when someone seems pleased we came back.
A familiar face can make a long route feel welcoming.
Coincidence has done its part; the characters can handle the address book.
A social plan endorsed by the suspicious frequency of our meetings.
We can arrange the next visit instead of waiting for the route to do it.
A small thread can be tied where paths have already crossed.
She makes a practical exchange feel like a little celebration.
Being recognized changes the whole feel of saying hello.

contexts.subject: Cindy wants contacts to commemorate the feeling of being drawn together.

Route104_Text_CindyRegister2.text: We should commemorate how we seem\nto be drawn to each other.\pLet's register each other in our\nPOKéNAVS.$

replies.text: A souvenir of repeatedly appearing in the same conversation.
She is giving a personal meaning to a practical exchange.
Worth keeping in touch if we both want to.
I like that the meeting feels worth marking to her.
A warm connection needn't wait for a special occasion.
A memento with room for another chapter instead of a display shelf.
Our tendency to meet has acquired official documentation.
The contact gives that feeling a straightforward use.
A passing connection can be given somewhere to rest.
A thoughtful little way to make an ordinary meeting memorable.
She wants the feeling to last beyond the place we happened to meet.

contexts.subject: Haley accepts choosing the battle while admitting she remains upset.

Route104_Text_HaleyPostRematch.text: I made the decision to battle, so\nI can accept this loss with grace.\pI am still upset about losing!$

replies.text: A graceful loss can still have a very annoyed lining.
Accepting an outcome doesn't require feeling pleased about it.
Fair. She's allowed to dislike losing.
I appreciate that she didn't pretend the feeling disappeared.
A break can help without making her disappointment wrong.
A gracious character is allowed an honest final aside.
Emotional consistency has wisely declined to fake a smile.
She can review the result after the frustration settles.
A feeling can remain without taking command of the next step.
Grace doesn't need to mean looking untouched by everything.
That honest admission made the gracious part feel more real.

contexts.subject: Haley visibly debates registering a strong rival then agrees.

Route104_Text_HaleyRegister1.text: You're strong, but should I register\nyou in my POKéNAV?\lMaybe I shouldn't…\pOkay, sure, I will register you!$

Route104_Text_HaleyRegister2.text: You're strong, but should I register\nyou in my POKéNAV?\lMaybe I shouldn't…\pOkay, sure, I will register you!$

replies.text: Our contact request survived a very small internal committee.
She seems interested despite some uncertainty about another challenge.
Fine by us. No pressure either way.
I understand rehearsing both answers aloud before choosing one.
Keeping in touch doesn't mean she has to battle immediately.
A brief drama in which the address book narrowly wins.
The whole debate happened without requiring us to say anything.
She can choose a comfortable time for the next test.
A hesitant yes can still be genuinely offered.
She let us see the indecision and then made her own choice.
I'd leave the next visit easy rather than turn that yes into a demand.

contexts.subject: Winston realizes wealth cannot guarantee battle success.

Route104_Text_WinstonPostRematch.text: I'm fabulously wealthy, but I can't\nseem to win at POKéMON…\pIt's so deep, the world of POKéMON…$

replies.text: His wallet has met a problem with no purchase button.
Resources can support care without replacing experience and judgment.
Can't buy the partnership. Have to build it.
It must feel strange when the usual shortcut doesn't reach the answer.
The team needs his time as well as his supplies.
An expensive setting has failed to write the ending for him.
A welcome limit on the universal shopping strategy.
Tools are only useful when the method fits the task.
Some things grow by being tended, not possessed.
The finest accessories cannot create the whole relationship.
He seems interested now that the answer isn't something he can simply order.

contexts.subject: Winston links his willingness to register us with having money.

Route104_Text_WinstonRegister1.text: Hm?\nAh, you've obtained a POKéNAV.\pI will gladly register you.\nAfter all, I have plenty of money.$

Route104_Text_WinstonRegister2.text: Hm?\nAh, you've obtained a POKéNAV.\pI will gladly register you.\nAfter all, I have plenty of money.$

replies.text: A very generous amount of money for exchanging contact details.
Wealth seems irrelevant to the actual registration, but the welcome is clear.
Sure. Doesn't cost him a compliment either.
I think he means to be welcoming in the way he knows.
A friendly exchange is worth more than its imagined price.
An aristocratic flourish on a pleasantly ordinary introduction.
The wallet insists on receiving a credit in every scene.
The tool is useful because of the connection, not its cost.
A small acquaintance can begin without anyone owing anything.
He makes status part of the greeting. We can keep the friendliness.
I'd remember the willingness to meet again rather than the financial explanation.

contexts.subject: Autumn wonders about an unusual rock protrusion uphill.

JaggedPass_Text_AutumnPostBattle.text: What is that odd rock protrusion\na little up the hill from here?$

replies.text: The hill has developed a suspiciously specific bump.
An unusual formation is worth observing before assigning an explanation.
Have a look. Keep footing on the slope.
It does stand out once someone points it out.
A short careful detour could satisfy the curiosity.
A small irregularity has successfully nominated itself as a mystery.
The landscape has acquired an attention-seeking detail.
I'd compare its shape with the surrounding rock.
A place can keep one little question on its surface.
An unexpected outline can change how the whole hill looks.
I'd like to see it from another angle before deciding what seems odd.

contexts.subject: Diana admires cyclists riding up the bumpy pass.

JaggedPass_Text_DianaPostBattle.text: Did you know?\pSome people cleverly ride their\nbicycles up this horribly bumpy pass.$

replies.text: Their bicycles are doing a great deal of arguing with gravity.
That requires equipment and technique suited to uneven terrain.
Impressive. Not a reason to try without practice.
It must feel strange watching wheels go where walking is hard.
I hope they leave enough energy to get back safely.
A determined ascent with considerably more bouncing than dignity.
A convincing demonstration of someone else's excellent balance.
I'd love to understand how they keep traction through the bumps.
A difficult path can reveal an unexpected kind of skill.
That's a look supported by real practical ability.
I'd watch how the rider changes position before each uneven stretch.

contexts.subject: Diana chooses to enjoy hiking instead of dwelling on losing.

JaggedPass_Text_DianaPostRematch.text: I'll forget about losing and just\nenjoy this bumpy hike.$

replies.text: The hill still has a nice afternoon available for her.
The result needn't determine the value of the rest of her outing.
Good choice. Plenty of trail left.
I like that she can return to something she enjoys.
A pleasant walk can give the disappointment room to settle.
A rough scene has not claimed the entire setting.
A useful way of putting a loss down without pretending it vanished.
A change of focus may help her notice the route again.
A day can hold more than the moment that hurt.
She doesn't need a perfect result to have a worthwhile outing.
I'd notice when her attention starts returning to the view.

contexts.subject: Diana asks for a rematch if we return to the area.

JaggedPass_Text_DianaRegister.text: Will you ever be back in this area?\nIf you do return, I'd like a rematch.$

replies.text: A return visit with a familiar challenge waiting on the slope.
A later match could show what both sides learn in the meantime.
We'll look for her when we come through.
It's nice being given a reason to remember a place.
A friendly stop could fit into another hike.
A recurring rival has chosen a suitably distinctive address.
A future appointment with a generous geographical margin.
The interval gives everyone time to change something useful.
A familiar face can wait along an unfamiliar day.
An open invitation is a good accessory to a favorite route.
The next visit will have this little meeting behind it.

contexts.subject: Eric claims his love of mountains exceeds ours despite losing.

JaggedPass_Text_EricPostBattle.text: Yes, I did lose at POKéMON…\pBut, when it comes to the love of\nthe mountains, I have you beat!$

replies.text: The mountains have wisely refused to keep that scoreboard.
Affection isn't something this battle can measure.
He can love them. We don't need to lose a second contest.
It's nice having somewhere he still feels certain.
He can enjoy the mountains without proving anyone likes them less.
A defeated rival has introduced an unjudgeable bonus round.
An excellent competition for someone unwilling to be checked.
We could talk about favorite trails instead of ranking feelings.
A mountain has room for more than one person's fondness.
His love doesn't get smaller when someone else enjoys the view.
I'd rather hear what makes this mountain matter to him.

contexts.subject: Ethan wants an Acro Bike for jumping ledges.

JaggedPass_Text_EthanPostBattle.text: If I had an ACRO BIKE, I'd be able to\njump ledges.$

replies.text: He has identified a very bouncy gap in his equipment.
A suitable bike could make certain ledges manageable with practice.
Right tool helps. Learn it before jumping.
Those ledges would feel different once he knew how to cross them.
Practice somewhere forgiving before making a difficult trip.
The obstacle has suggested an entirely new entrance.
A tempting solution with some very untempting landing possibilities.
The bike and the rider both need to suit the maneuver.
A path can open through learning as well as acquiring.
Useful equipment should fit the route and the person using it.
I'd like to see his first careful practice before the ambitious jumps.

contexts.subject: Ethan plans to get an Acro Bike from Rydel in Mauville.

JaggedPass_Text_EthanPostRematch.text: I should get an ACRO BIKE from RYDEL\nin MAUVILLE CITY…$

replies.text: The bouncing plan has acquired an actual shop address.
Knowing the supplier turns the idea into a practical next step.
Ask Rydel how to handle it too.
It's nice when a vague wish becomes somewhere you can actually go.
He can plan the return with time to try the bike first.
A useful lead has emerged from the previous chapter's obstacle.
The quest for additional bouncing now involves customer service.
He should compare the bike's capabilities with the route he wants.
A small errand can widen the next stretch of a journey.
A proper fit and a useful demonstration beat a rushed purchase.
I'd be curious what he notices when he returns to these ledges.

contexts.subject: Ethan expects better battles once he adjusts to the terrain and asks for contact.

JaggedPass_Text_EthanRegister.text: When I get more used to this bumpiness,\nI'll be sure to win!\pCan you register me in your POKéNAV?$

replies.text: The bumps have been assigned their share of the blame.
Familiarity with the ground may help him focus on decisions.
Learn the footing. We'll give him another match.
It can be hard thinking clearly when the ground keeps surprising you.
He can practice without rushing into the next result.
A confident sequel hinges on a less argumentative setting.
Terrain has become a remarkably convenient co-defendant.
He could separate movement practice from battle practice initially.
A familiar path can leave more attention for the person beside it.
Confidence fits better once he feels steady in the place.
I'd like to see what changes when the pass stops being the surprise.

contexts.subject: Julio is sore from his bicycle bouncing on the pass.

JaggedPass_Text_JulioPostBattle.text: My bicycle bounced around so much,\nmy rear end's sore…$

replies.text: The bicycle has provided considerably more feedback than requested.
Repeated impacts suggest a need to reassess the route, fit, or technique.
Take a break. No need to bounce through pain.
That sounds like the kind of joke that stops being funny on the next bump.
A comfortable rest would help more than another demonstration.
A lively travel scene has acquired an undignified closing complaint.
The pass has expressed its opinion directly through the saddle.
The setup may need adjusting before he repeats the same ride.
The body is allowed to object to the chosen path.
A bicycle should suit its rider as well as its terrain.
I'd rather see him stop comfortably than brave one more painful descent.

contexts.subject: Charlie struggles to throw balls while holding an inner tube.

AbandonedShip_Corridors_1F_Text_CharlieP.text: It's not easy throwing POKé BALLS\nwhile hanging on to an inner tube!$

replies.text: One arm is battling. The other has a very important floating job.
Dividing balance and throwing control makes the action harder.
Stay secure. The throw can wait.
I'd feel awkward trying not to tip while everyone watched.
A stable place to stop would make the whole thing easier.
An action scene with an unusually demanding prop.
An excellent argument for not attempting impressive gestures afloat.
He needs a stable base before worrying about accuracy.
Keeping himself supported matters more than a graceful throw.
Practical accessories do occasionally complicate the pose.
I'd watch how he manages the tube before adding another demand.

contexts.subject: Duncan thinks underwater travel would reach the ship's sunken lower parts.

AbandonedShip_Corridors_B1F_Text_DuncanP.text: The ship's bottom has sunk into the\ndepths.\pIf a POKéMON knew how to go underwater,\nwe might make some progress…$

replies.text: The lower deck has become a very wet basement.
Submerged spaces may be accessible with the right partner and preparation.
Plan the way back before going under.
It must be strange seeing rooms disappear beneath the surface.
The team should be rested before trying a difficult new route.
A familiar ship has an entirely different chapter beneath the waterline.
The basement has taken its damp problem much too far.
Access is only one question; navigation and condition matter too.
A place below the surface can remain close and unreachable.
The most intriguing part still needs a sensible approach.
I'd want to see how the rooms connect before choosing an underwater path.

contexts.subject: Dan wonders if someone else already found the treasure.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_DanPostBatt.text: DAN: We can't find any treasures…\nI wonder if someone got them already?$

replies.text: The treasure has left no forwarding address. Rude.
An unsuccessful search doesn't tell us whether the valuables were removed.
Could be gone. Could be somewhere unsearched.
It must be tiring looking when you don't know what you're looking for.
They can take a break without losing their whole chance.
A missing prize does not prove another protagonist reached the ending first.
The ship is making very poor guarantees to its visitors.
Record the checked rooms before drawing conclusions.
An empty search can still leave a story worth keeping.
He sounds more uncertain than excited now.
I'd ask whether they had a real clue or only a hopeful destination.

contexts.subject: Dan wants to leave but fears Kira's anger if he says so.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_DanPostRema.text: DAN: We can't find any treasures,\nwe lose at POKéMON…\pI want to go home… But if I say that,\nshe gets all angry with me…$

replies.text: Wanting to go home shouldn't be another thing he has to hide.
A joint outing needs both people to be able to express discomfort.
He gets a say. They should talk.
He sounds trapped by her reaction more than by the ship.
A safe way home matters more than forcing the outing to succeed.
The companion should not need permission to admit the story has become miserable.
A shared adventure isn't improved by one person quietly dreading it.
They need to review the plan together, including whether to stop.
A wish to leave deserves a listening ear, not anger.
His comfort should count as much as her imagined treasure.
I'd rather hear him answered gently than watch him make another excuse.

contexts.subject: Garrison saw a sparkle in a cabin.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_GarrisonPos.text: In a cabin somewhere on board,\nI saw something sparkle.$

replies.text: A little sparkle has volunteered to become a very large possibility.
Something reflective is a lead, not yet proof of value.
Look carefully. Watch the floor going in.
Tiny bright things can stand out strongly in a dark room.
A careful look is better than scrambling after a glint.
The mystery has acquired one small but persuasive visual cue.
A sparkle is all it takes for hope to become inconvenient.
I'd check the location from a stable position first.
A brief light can draw us into a much older place.
Interesting details deserve attention before grand conclusions.
I'd like to know how the glint changes when you move around it.

contexts.subject: Jani regrets being barefoot aboard the old ship.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_JaniPostBat.text: Walking around barefoot in this ship\nis kind of gross.$

replies.text: The floor is providing a very unappealing personal introduction.
Old surfaces can hold hazards beyond the unpleasant texture.
Get proper shoes before exploring farther.
I can almost feel the discomfort just hearing her say it.
Dry footwear would make this trip much kinder.
A setting that demands atmosphere should still permit decent shoes.
A bold sensory experiment that has reached its obvious conclusion.
Soles are useful protection when the condition of the floor is uncertain.
The ground needn't be endured directly to be understood.
This is one place where practical footwear completes the look.
She noticed a detail no picture of the ship could really convey.

contexts.subject: Kira has planned purchases before finding any treasure.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_KiraPostBat.text: KIRA: Where could the treasures be?\pI've already decided what I'm buying\nwhen we find the treasures!$

replies.text: The money has not arrived, but its schedule is fully booked.
Expected treasure is not the same as a resource already available.
Find it first. Spend it later.
The imagined reward seems brighter than the actual search.
They should still keep enough for the way home.
An extravagant epilogue has been written before the central mystery is solved.
Her imaginary fortune has a worryingly real shopping list.
A budget should distinguish hopes from confirmed supplies.
A wish can be enjoyed without becoming a promise.
Planning the purchases is half the fun, provided she knows it's still a fantasy.
I'd be curious which imagined purchase made the whole search feel worthwhile.
