contexts.subject: Kira insists on staying until training and treasure hunting succeed.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_KiraPostRem.text: KIRA: We're not leaving until we raise\nour POKéMON some more and we find\lthe treasures here!$

replies.text: That is a very heavy condition to put on everyone leaving.
A plan with no stopping rule can become unreasonable after setbacks.
Dan gets a say. So does the tired team.
I hope she hears if someone else needs to stop.
Food, rest, and a safe return can't depend on finding treasure.
An adventure needs an exit that isn't held hostage by the perfect ending.
A deadline would be kinder than this endless until.
Set a reasonable limit before trying more rooms or battles.
Determination should leave room for the companions carrying it.
A shared trip needs shared comfort, not one person's final demand.
I'd notice whether anyone beside her still looks eager to continue.

contexts.subject: Kira angrily announces registration as a consequence of our victory.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_1F_Text_KiraRegiste.text: KIRA: Oh, you make me so angry!\nI'm going to register you for that!$

replies.text: I was braced for a threat, and received contact information.
Her anger seems mixed with wanting another opportunity to battle.
Register if she wants. No grabbing our things.
It's an intense way to ask for another meeting.
A rematch can wait until the bad mood has passed.
An ominous consequence has turned out to be a recurring acquaintance.
My address book rarely receives declarations of vengeance.
A future match will be more useful with a calmer plan.
A hard feeling need not become the whole connection.
She can keep in touch without making it sound like punishment.
I'd hope the next greeting is warmer than this first invitation.

contexts.subject: Demetrius hides aboard the ship after getting in trouble with his mother.

AbandonedShip_Rooms_1F_Text_DemetriusPos.text: I'm in trouble with my mom, so I ran.\nKeep it a secret where I am!$

replies.text: This is a large, damp place for a problem that needs a conversation.
An old ship isn't a good refuge for avoiding a difficult talk.
Make sure he's safe. Then help him find a way home.
He sounds worried about the return more than happy to be here.
Someone should know he's safe without making this worse for him.
A dramatic hideaway may complicate an already difficult home scene.
I respect wanting space. This location is making a poor case for itself.
We can ask what support would make going back feel possible.
A little distance can help; disappearing somewhere unsafe can add another fear.
He needs a gentler next step than staying hidden on this wreck.
I'd ask if there's someone he trusts who can help him talk it through.

contexts.subject: Thalia doubts the neighboring visitor is merely sightseeing.

AbandonedShip_Rooms_1F_Text_ThaliaPostBa.text: The man next door…\pHe says he's just sightseeing,\nbut I don't know about that.$

replies.text: A mysterious stranger is sometimes just someone enjoying a cabin.
Suspicion needs observations before it becomes a reliable conclusion.
What did he actually do? Start there.
It's easy for an odd place to make an ordinary person seem secretive.
A polite question might help more than building a worry around him.
The setting is doing much of the work of making its visitor look suspicious.
A man looking at a ship has been cast in a very ambitious subplot.
We should separate unusual behavior from a guessed motive.
A quiet visitor can remain unknown without becoming a threat.
Some people look awkward simply because they're being watched.
I'd compare the actual behavior with what she imagines it means.

contexts.subject: Thalia becomes certain the man is plotting because he acts suspiciously.

AbandonedShip_Rooms_1F_Text_ThaliaPostRe.text: I'm sure that man's up to something!\nHe just acts so suspiciously!$

replies.text: Her theory has grown faster than the available evidence.
Repeated suspicion isn't the same as independent confirmation.
Still need facts. Looking odd isn't a crime.
I hope she doesn't make him feel cornered over a guess.
If something specific worries her, she can describe that clearly.
A sequel has increased the certainty without revealing the missing scene.
An ominous atmosphere is not a dependable witness.
Ask which action supports the conclusion and what else could explain it.
An unknown intention needn't be filled with our darkest guess.
She's become more certain, but the detail is still missing.
I'd listen for a concrete change rather than another stronger adjective.

contexts.subject: Thalia asks to register us as a memento of our strength.

AbandonedShip_Rooms_1F_Text_ThaliaRegist.text: You're such a tough TRAINER!\nLet me register you as a memento!$

replies.text: A keepsake that will occasionally ask how she's doing.
A retained contact makes the encounter more than a fixed memory.
Sure. Happy to be a friendly memory.
It's lovely when someone wants a meeting to last.
A later check-in can make this strange place feel less isolated.
A memento with the appealing possibility of a second chapter.
We fit rather efficiently into an address book.
She could note what she learned before the impression fades.
A short meeting can leave a long little thread.
A personal connection makes a better souvenir than a random trinket.
I'd like her to remember the company as well as the battle.

contexts.subject: A visitor is excited simply being aboard the ship.

AbandonedShip_Corridors_1F_Text_IsntItFu.text: Isn't it fun here?\nI get excited just being here!$

replies.text: The ship has stopped traveling and started providing excitement in place.
The structure itself seems enough to sustain their curiosity.
Enjoy the place. Watch where you step.
It's nice when someone is that happy just looking around.
A slow exploration sounds better than racing through every room.
A setting can carry a story before anyone finds a dramatic event.
Atmosphere without an admission queue. A rare convenience.
There's a lot to observe even without finding valuables.
An old place can give a new visitor a lively moment.
Some places reward being curious rather than looking impressive.
That excitement makes me want to notice what first caught their eye.

contexts.subject: A child delightedly celebrates being on a ship.

replies.text: An extremely accurate review. Full marks for enthusiasm.
The simple fact of being aboard is clearly exciting enough.
That's the spirit. Stay where it's safe.
That sort of uncomplicated joy is lovely to hear.
I hope someone keeps a careful eye on the little explorer.
The grand reveal was available before the first step aboard.
A short review that has found no room for cynicism.
A familiar structure can be entirely new to a child.
A small discovery can fill a whole afternoon.
No elaborate reason needed when the delight is that real.
I'd remember that face before any of the hidden rooms.

contexts.subject: A visitor expects amazing treasure while exploring.

AbandonedShip_Rooms2_B1F_Text_PerfectPla.text: This is a perfect place to go exploring!\nIt's exciting here!\pI bet there're amazing treasures on\nboard.$

replies.text: A very optimistic inspection of a very soggy property.
Exploration can be worthwhile even if the expected valuables aren't there.
Enjoy the search. Keep the return route clear.
The rooms must feel full of possibilities before you know them.
They should bring supplies rather than count on the ship providing them.
An enticing setting doesn't guarantee the treasure promised by the imagination.
A wreck has inspired an impressively luxurious daydream.
A route through the accessible rooms should come before searching every corner.
Curiosity can find something valuable without finding something to sell.
A good outing can survive a less glittering ending.
I'd be interested in which small discovery surprises them first.

contexts.subject: A visitor enjoys examining the rare old ship and other cabins.

AbandonedShip_Rooms_1F_Text_TakingALookA.text: Ships of this sort are rare, so I'm\ntaking a look around.\pHmhm…\nThere appear to be other cabins…$

replies.text: The ship is receiving a very thorough house call.
A rare vessel offers a useful chance to observe construction and layout.
Look carefully. Don't trust every floorboard.
It's nice being somewhere that makes ordinary rooms interesting.
A patient look can turn a small cabin into an afternoon.
A quiet reader of an unusually large historical document.
Some people want treasure. A peculiar room is often enough for me.
I'd compare the cabin arrangements and how they connect.
A place left behind can still invite attentive company.
The wear and little surviving details may be the most interesting part.
I'd love to hear what makes this type of ship unusual.

contexts.subject: A visitor feels seasick despite the ship not moving.

AbandonedShip_Rooms_B1F_Text_GettingQuea.text: Urrrrppp…\pI'm getting queasy just being aboard\nthis ship…\pIt's not even moving, but…$

replies.text: His stomach has filed a complaint based on the general theme.
Discomfort can persist even without the motion he expected.
Get some air. He doesn't need to prove anything.

A quiet spot off the ship would be a good first step.
The setting has convinced an unwilling audience far too thoroughly.
The ocean has outsourced its least charming effect to a stationary building.
He can leave the uncomfortable environment instead of testing his endurance.
The body doesn't need a persuasive explanation to ask for a pause.
He deserves comfort more than a review of whether it makes sense.
I'd help him find the way out before continuing the sightseeing.

contexts.subject: A hiker explains Flash and its Dewford badge requirement.

GraniteCave_1F_Text_ExplainFlash.text:
Teach that hidden move FLASH to
a POKéMON and use it.\pIt lights up even the inky darkness
of caves.\pBut, to use it, you need the GYM BADGE
from DEWFORD's POKéMON GYM.$

replies.text: A portable answer to the cave's missing lamps.
Light improves navigation, provided we meet the field-use requirement.
Get the badge first. Don't stumble in blind.
I would feel better seeing the floor before taking another step.
A little preparation can make the cave much less tiring.
The scene requires lighting before it requires a brave entrance.
Useful illumination, even if it ruins some of the atmosphere.
We should check the team and requirement before relying on the move.
A small light can give a large darkness manageable edges.
Practical visibility is worth more than looking fearless.
I'd watch how much more of the path appears once the light is there.

contexts.subject: Steven leaves after the letter delivery and exchange.

GraniteCave_StevensRoom_Text_IveGotToHur.text: Now, I've got to hurry along.$

replies.text: Our errand has successfully released one very busy stone enthusiast.
He seems ready to continue the work that brought him here.
Delivery done. Let him get on with it.
It's nice having finished what we came to do.
A completed errand makes the trip back feel lighter.
A brief acquaintance has left its next chapter somewhere beyond the cave.
A farewell with admirably little ceremonial delay.
We can check our own route now that the task is finished.
Some meetings are short and still leave a useful thread.
He leaves with purpose rather than a performance.
I'd remember how much happened during one little delivery.

contexts.subject: The rescued researcher hurries away because of a crisis.

PetalburgWoods_Text_ICantBeWastingTime.text: Uh-oh! It's a crisis!\nI can't be wasting time!$

replies.text: His quiet woodland stroll has become a very urgent workday.
The immediate danger is past, but he still has something important to do.
Let him go. He's got enough on his plate.
He sounds relieved and worried at the same time.
I hope he reaches somewhere safe before the next problem.
A rescue has not quite returned the story to an ordinary day.
His schedule has suffered a rather aggressive interruption.
The useful next step is to let him carry out the task.
A safe moment can still sit inside a larger worry.
He doesn't need another demand on his attention.
The sudden hurry makes the importance of those papers feel much clearer.

contexts.subject: A Bug trainer links a big Bug Pokemon with respect.

PetalburgWoods_Text_PeopleRespectYou.text: If you have a big BUG POKéMON,\npeople respect you for it.$

replies.text: A large bug certainly gets a very prompt introduction.
An imposing partner may attract attention without guaranteeing respect.
Respect comes from how he treats the team too.
I hope he enjoys the Pokemon beyond what others think.
The partner deserves care even when no one is impressed.
A striking supporting character cannot write the trainer's whole reputation.
A large bug is an excellent way to make certain conversations shorter.
Size is one trait; reliable behavior takes practice.
A small kindness can earn something a large outline cannot.
Presence can draw the eye. Character decides what people remember.
I'd notice whether he talks about the Pokemon itself or only the attention.

contexts.subject: Mike praises stopping construction to protect Pokemon.

RusturfTunnel_Text_MikePostBattle.text: They halted development here to\nprotect POKéMON, right?\lThere's a feel-good story!$

replies.text: A tunnel can wait longer than the creatures it might disturb.
Changing development to protect the habitat is a meaningful choice.
Good. The Pokemon live here too.
It's comforting hearing about people choosing a gentler way.
A road should help people without making its neighbors miserable.
An unfinished passage has a better story than a thoughtless completed one.
A rare construction delay with an explanation I actually like.
The design has to account for the lives already using the space.
A place isn't empty simply because no road crosses it.
It's good when practical progress leaves room for care.
I'd like to know which small signs showed the Pokemon were being disturbed.

contexts.subject: Wanda praises her boyfriend's raw-handed work for everyone, not only her.

RusturfTunnel_Text_BoyfriendOnOtherSideO.text:
On the other side of this rock…
My boyfriend is there.\pHe… He's not just digging the tunnel
to come see me.\pHe works his hands raw and rough
for the benefit of everyone.$

replies.text: A very hard-working romance with a public benefit attached.
She sees both the personal reason and the wider purpose of his effort.
He needs rest too. Raw hands don't make the work better.
She sounds proud of him and worried about him together.
I hope he lets her look after those hands when they meet.
A love story can help more people than the two at its center.
The romantic gesture has acquired an impressive infrastructure component.
His persistence deserves tools and protection as well as admiration.
Care can reach one person and still widen beyond them.
She doesn't make his kindness to everyone a rival to his love for her.
The way she corrects herself shows how much she wants his effort understood.

contexts.subject: The blocked tunnel forces a long detour through several towns.

RusturfTunnel_Text_ToGetToVerdanturf.text: To get from RUSTBORO to VERDANTURF,\nyou need to go to DEWFORD, then pass\lthrough SLATEPORT and MAUVILLE…$

replies.text: That's a very large journey to reach the other side of one rock.
A short direct distance can conceal a very long accessible route.

It must be hard knowing someone is so close and so far.
A trip that long deserves proper meals and stopping places.
One obstacle has written several extra chapters into a simple visit.
The geography has developed a remarkably cruel sense of humor.
Access matters more than straight-line distance when planning travel.
A near place can ask for many footsteps.
A practical route can be inconvenient without being optional.
I'd trace the whole detour before deciding how quickly it can be done.

contexts.subject: Wanda's boyfriend despairs over stalled digging separating them.

RusturfTunnel_Text_WhyCantTheyKeepDiggin.text:
… …\pWhy can't they keep digging?
Is the bedrock too hard?\pMy beloved awaits me in VERDANTURF
TOWN just beyond here…\pIf RUSTBORO and VERDANTURF were

replies.text: The rock is getting blamed for a very complicated distance.

He sounds lonely enough that the obstacle feels personal.
His hands deserve a rest while he works out a safer approach.
A blocked passage has become the whole visible shape of his longing.
An inconvenient rock has acquired enormous emotional responsibilities.
The reason for stopping matters more than guessing at the bedrock.
A wish to reach someone can be patient as well as strong.
He shouldn't have to wear himself out before asking for another way.
I'd listen to what he knows, not only what the frustration makes him assume.

contexts.subject: Wanda welcomes her boyfriend home to rest after the barrier is cleared.

RusturfTunnel_Text_WandaReunion.text: WANDA!\nNow I can see you anytime!\pWANDA: That's…wonderful.\pPlease, take some rest at my home.$

replies.text: The tunnel finally connected two people and a very overdue chair.
The practical barrier is gone; recovery can finally take priority.
Good. He has earned some care for those hands.
Her first thought was making him comfortable. That's lovely.
A rest at home sounds like the right celebration.
A long-awaited reunion ends with a wonderfully ordinary invitation.
A happy ending with sensible provisions for exhaustion.
The cleared route has changed an everyday visit, not only this one.
A door home can be the gentlest reward.
She welcomed the person, not just the effort he made.
I'd remember how small the remaining distance suddenly became.

contexts.subject: A defeated Magma grunt dismisses us as a rookie who belongs in the waves.

MtChimney_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: A rookie like you should be\nsplashing about in the waves!$

replies.text: A rookie has caused a remarkably experienced complaint.

It's easier for him to dismiss us than admit what happened.
He can be upset without ordering someone else away.
A defeated gatekeeper has begun improvising new admission rules.
The qualification process appears to have offended its own administrator.
We learned more from the match than that belated label.
A harsh word needn't become a boundary around someone.
The insult is trying to do work the battle couldn't.
I'd watch what he does next instead of arguing over his description.

contexts.subject: A grunt cannot reconcile promised happiness with universal opposition.

MtChimney_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: Our BOSS says, “It will make everyone\nhappy.”\pBut why does everyone keep getting\nin our way?$

replies.text: If everyone objects to the happiness plan, check the plan.

Ask who it's actually helping. Listen to the answer.
He sounds close to asking the question that matters.
People should get a say in what supposedly makes them happy.
A slogan is struggling to explain the reaction of its intended audience.

contexts.subject: Shannon says shared time grows trust between trainer and Pokemon.

VictoryRoad_B1F_Text_ShannonPostBattle.text: By being together all the time, trust\ngrows between POKéMON and TRAINERS.$

replies.text: Trust apparently enjoys all the ordinary walking we do together.
Repeated interactions let each partner learn what to expect.
Be there. Keep showing what they can count on.
The little familiar routines make a difference to me too.
A meal, a break, a small kindness. None of it is wasted.
The relationship is being written between the dramatic scenes.
A good defense of quiet time that doesn't produce a trophy.
Consistent responses make a partnership more predictable and reliable.
Familiarity becomes shelter when it is tended kindly.
A connection looks natural because of all the attention behind it.
I'd remember the ordinary habit that became a sign they trust us.

contexts.subject: Caroline warns that Victory Road and the League can exhaust travelers.

VictoryRoad_B2F_Text_CarolinePostBattle.text: VICTORY ROAD and the POKéMON LEAGUE\nare long and grueling challenges.\lBeware of fatigue!$

replies.text: A brave plan still needs somewhere to sit down.
Fatigue can undermine judgment before it becomes obvious in performance.
Check everyone. Rest before the team has to ask.
I'd rather pause than pretend the strain isn't showing.
Supplies and proper recovery matter as much as the next move.
A climactic journey has not repealed the need for an intermission.
Exhaustion is an uninvited opponent with no sense of fair timing.
We should plan recovery points instead of waiting for a failure.
A long path is kinder when we let it have pauses.
An impressive finish shouldn't require hiding how worn everyone feels.
I'd watch the little changes in pace before waiting for a dramatic sign.

contexts.subject: Dianne admires our courage and encourages us onward.

VictoryRoad_B2F_Text_DiannePostBattle.text: You do have guts! I like that!\nKeep it going!$

replies.text: Our nerves have received a surprisingly complimentary review.
Courage can be acting carefully while uncertainty remains.
We'll keep going. No need to be reckless.
It's nice when trying despite the nerves is enough.
A little encouragement can carry into the next hard stretch.
A brave character still deserves a sensible next scene.
Our unease has apparently been presenting itself with excellent posture.
We can use the motivation without skipping the checks.
A steady step can be brave without being loud.
Resolve suits someone best when it still leaves room to listen.
I'd remember the way she made the challenge sound possible.

contexts.subject: Felix admits feigning calm while tense near the League.

VictoryRoad_B2F_Text_FelixPostBattle.text: I can't help getting all tense knowing\nthat I'm nearing the POKéMON LEAGUE.\pIt's all I can do to feign calm.$

replies.text: His calm face is apparently doing overtime.
Outward composure doesn't reliably show the amount of anxiety underneath.
Can be nervous. Just keep making clear choices.
I understand looking quieter when everything inside gets louder.
A comfortable break might help more than another brave expression.
A polished performance can contain a very unsettled narrator.
An impressively honest review of a very familiar disguise.
A simple routine could give his attention something practical to follow.
A feeling needn't become visible to deserve kindness.
He doesn't owe the place an image of effortless confidence.
I'd let him stop performing calm for a moment while we talk.

contexts.subject: Julie suggests recalling past trainers through our badges.

VictoryRoad_B2F_Text_JuliePostBattle.text: Gaze on your collected BADGES and\nremember the TRAINERS you've faced.$

replies.text: Tiny metal bookmarks for a very busy journey.
A physical reminder can help retrieve the effort behind an achievement.
Earned each one. Worth remembering how.
I can picture certain moments more clearly when I look at them.
The people who helped between those battles belong in the memory too.
An entire history has been compressed into a small display.
Proof that all those awkward attempts eventually became something shiny.
Reviewing past adjustments could help with the next challenge.
A small object can hold a long road when we know how to look.
Each badge has more meaning than simply completing the set.
I'd remember one face and one surprising moment behind each of them.

contexts.subject: Owen repeats rumors of a strong young trainer from Petalburg.

VictoryRoad_B2F_Text_OwenPostBattle.text: The rumors I heard, that tough little\nkid is from PETALBURG CITY.$

replies.text: A small hometown has produced a very well-traveled rumor.
Word of a capable trainer can move farther than the trainer expects.
A rumor's a start. Better to meet the person.
It's strange thinking people hear about someone before knowing them.
I hope the actual person gets room beyond the reputation.
A local beginning has grown into a story told by strangers.
A reputation can enter a room several minutes ahead of its owner.
I'd compare the specific details rather than assume every young trainer fits.
A name can travel while its person is still walking.
An interesting introduction, provided the rumor doesn't become the whole portrait.
I'd ask which detail made the story stick with him.

contexts.subject: Vito loses for the first time and considers going home after family superiority.

VictoryRoad_B2F_Text_VitoPostBattle.text: I was better than everyone in my\nfamily. I've never lost before…\pI've lost my confidence…\nMaybe I'll go home…$

replies.text: A first loss can feel larger than a whole winning history.
His previous comparisons don't define his capacity to learn from this.
One defeat. Still room to become better.
It must hurt when the thing you felt sure about suddenly changes.
Home can be comforting without making the journey a failure.
A proud opening chapter has met an ending it didn't prepare for.
Being unfinished is an inconvenient discovery for an undefeated person.
He could separate the lost match from the conclusion that he cannot improve.
A shaken confidence can be tended without pretending nothing happened.
He doesn't need to look superior to remain worth taking seriously.
I'd want to hear what he enjoyed before every match became proof of being best.

contexts.subject: Jay says fifty years of marital arguments were settled with Pokemon battles.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_JayPostBattle.text: JAY: Fifty years of marriage…\pIf we ever argued, we always settled\nit with a POKéMON battle…$

replies.text: Fifty years of debates with unusually active witnesses.
A friendly ritual can help, provided both still feel heard afterward.
Fine if both agree. Winning isn't always being right.
I wonder whether the battles helped them laugh afterward.
A familiar routine can make a difficult conversation easier.
A long-running duet has developed an exceptionally competitive refrain.
An argument format with considerably more spectators than mine.
They still need to discuss the issue beyond the battle result.
A shared ritual can hold affection even when opinions differ.
The warmth in the memory matters more than the competition.
I'd love to hear about an argument they now find funny.

contexts.subject: Jay hopes to keep making happy memories after fifty years of marriage.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_JayPostRematch.text: JAY: Fifty years of marriage…\nMany things have happened.\pI hope that we will continue to make\nhappy memories together.$

replies.text: Fifty years, and she still wants another good afternoon together.
A long relationship can remain open to new shared experiences.
Good wish. Keep making time for it.
That's lovely, still looking forward beside someone so familiar.
Ordinary meals and little trips can become the memories that last.
A long story has not lost its interest in the next gentle chapter.
A wonderfully modest ambition with an enormous history behind it.
They could revisit a favorite place and notice what has changed.
A familiar hand can still lead into an unknown day.
She makes lasting affection sound alive rather than preserved.
I'd remember the future in her voice as much as the fifty years behind it.

contexts.subject: John fondly admits never beating his wife across fifty years.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_JohnPostBattle.text: JOHN: We've been married for\nfifty years.\pCome to think of it, I've yet to beat\nmy dear wife in a battle.$

replies.text: A fifty-year losing streak with an excellent companionship record.
He seems able to enjoy the relationship without winning the comparison.
Sounds like he's happy anyway. Good.
The fondness in that admission matters more than the record.
There must be a lot of shared laughs behind the losses.
A long-running rivalry has a remarkably affectionate narrator.
A defeat count impressive enough to become its own tradition.
He could probably describe her favorite strategy in exquisite detail.
A shared history can soften even a very persistent defeat.
He doesn't need to look superior to look content beside her.
I'd enjoy seeing her expression when he tells that story.

contexts.subject: John recalls daily Pokemon battles throughout fifty years together.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_JohnPostRematch.text: JOHN: Married for fifty years…\pOn reflection, the dear wife and I,\nwe battled day in and day out…$

replies.text: Their ordinary Tuesday apparently included a scheduled rivalry.
A repeated activity can become part of how a partnership remembers time.
Long habit. Glad they still enjoy it together.
I wonder which little pre-battle routine never changed.
Some memories grow from what you do together every day.
An epic relationship made partly from thousands of familiar little scenes.
A domestic schedule with an unusually lively competitive section.
Repeated practice must have given them very detailed knowledge of each other.
A ritual can keep changing while remaining recognizably theirs.
The shared history is what makes the habit feel special.
I'd love to hear about the day they unexpectedly did something different.

contexts.subject: John politely invites us to battle the couple again if paths allow.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_JohnRegister.text: JOHN: Young TRAINER, if the chance\narises, will you battle with us again?$

replies.text: A future visit to a very well-established double act.
Another match could let us observe how their coordination develops.
Gladly, when we're nearby and the team is ready.
It's kind that he leaves the timing open.
A familiar welcome makes returning to a difficult place nicer.
A courteous invitation from a cast I'd happily revisit.
A social appointment with an unusually impressive combined history.
We could compare the strategies without rushing through the conversation.
A meeting can leave a small thread between very different journeys.
Good manners give the challenge a warm shape.
I'd enjoy seeing what they remember about us when we return.

contexts.subject: Nicolas wonders when the long harsh road to being best will end.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_NicolasPostBattle.text: The road ahead remains long and harsh.\pWhen will my POKéMON and I become\nthe best?$

replies.text: Best is a destination that keeps moving its furniture.
A broad ranking is less actionable than a specific improvement goal.
Aim for better first. Best can wait.
The whole road can feel heavier when you only look at its far end.
A break doesn't cancel the progress already made.
An endless superlative can make every chapter feel unfinished.
An ambition with extremely unhelpful opening hours.
One measurable skill would make the next practice less vague.
A far wish needn't consume the small ground beneath today's feet.
A strong personal style matters more than chasing every comparison.
I'd ask what would make the next day feel worthwhile even without the title.

contexts.subject: Nicolas uses our continued strength as motivation for his own growth.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_NicolasPostRematc.text: You've obviously kept up your\nPOKéMON training.\pSo long as you remain strong, I, too,\ncan become stronger!$

replies.text: Our practice has become somebody else's renewable homework.
A consistently challenging opponent can provide useful comparison.
We'll keep working. He can meet us stronger.
It's nice when a rival finds encouragement in the gap.
His team still deserves time to recover between tests.
Two recurring characters have agreed not to let the story stand still.
A rather demanding form of mutual encouragement.
He could track which part of the gap actually narrows.
A familiar challenge can give effort a clear direction.
A good rivalry leaves room for both people to develop their own strengths.
I'd like to see a new idea from him, not just more of the old one.

contexts.subject: Nicolas wants contact so he can understand our strength.

MeteorFalls_1F_2R_Text_NicolasRegister.text: I want to know more about your power.\nLet me register you in my POKéNAV.$

replies.text: A contact request with a very competitive research question.
He can learn more by discussing decisions than only repeating battles.
We can compare notes. No secret miracle required.
It's flattering that he thinks there's something worth understanding.
A quiet conversation might help as much as another hard match.
A curious rival is more interesting than an unquestioning admirer.
A study of our power may include disappointingly ordinary practice.
We could explain one interaction rather than hand him a whole plan.
An honest question can turn a comparison into a connection.
He wants to look beneath the result, which is a better starting point.
I'd be curious which moment he most wants explained.

contexts.subject: Archie warns us to watch Magma before departing.

MeteorFalls_1F_1R_Text_ArchieFarewell.text: ARCHIE: {PLAYER}, you should keep\nan eye out for TEAM MAGMA, too.\pFarewell!$

replies.text: A warning is useful even when the messenger has his own agenda.
We can take the caution without accepting every part of his account.
We'll watch both groups. Decide by what they do.
The farewell feels more serious after that confrontation.
The people caught between them matter more than the rivalry.
A self-appointed guide has left us with a partial map of the conflict.
A useful warning wearing a suspiciously one-sided jacket.
Observe the actions directly instead of borrowing his entire conclusion.
A path can be watched without walking behind whoever pointed at it.
His confidence shouldn't decide whose story we believe.
I'd remember the warning and keep noticing what doesn't fit it.

contexts.subject: Cozmo explains being tricked into guiding Magma, who stole his meteorite.

MeteorFalls_1F_1R_Text_MeetProfCozmo.text:
I… I'm COZMO…
I'm a PROFESSOR…\pTEAM MAGMA asked me to guide them
to METEOR FALLS…\pBut they tricked me.
They even took my METEORITE away…\pAnd then another similar bunch,
TEAM AQUA showed up.\pAfter that…
I don't understand any of it.\pBut that TEAM MAGMA…\pWhat are they going to do with that
METEORITE at MT. CHIMNEY?$

replies.text: He thought he was helping a visit, not supplying a theft.
He was misled about the purpose of the expedition.
Not his fault they lied. Focus on what they took.
He sounds shaken and embarrassed at the same time.
Someone should let him explain without making him feel foolish.
A trusted guide has been used as a supporting character in someone else's scheme.
An honest mistake made worse by dishonest guests.
His observations could help reconstruct what happened and where they went.
Being deceived should not erase his right to be heard.
They abused his knowledge, which is different from him choosing their plan.
I'd listen to the details he remembers once he has time to steady himself.

contexts.subject: Cozmo worries what Magma will do with the meteorite at Mt. Chimney.

MeteorFalls_1F_1R_Text_WhatsTeamMagmaDoi.text: PROF. COZMO: But that TEAM MAGMA…\pWhat are they going to do with that\nMETEORITE at MT. CHIMNEY?$

replies.text: That is a much bigger worry than a missing rock.
Their destination and the stolen object give the concern a concrete basis.
Worth checking. No need to guess the worst as fact.
He sounds stuck on the part he can't explain.
The people near the mountain may need help too.
An unanswered question is pointing beyond the scene of the theft.
A rock-related mystery has become alarmingly volcanic.
We should verify the setup there instead of inventing a mechanism.
A stolen thing can carry a shadow farther than its owner knows.
His worry deserves an answer grounded in what actually happens.
I'd keep his question in mind when we see what they've built.

contexts.subject: An Aqua grunt wants promotion so he can order others around.

SeafloorCavern_Room1_Text_Grunt1PostBatt.text: I want to get a promotion so I can\nboss around the GRUNTS…$

replies.text: A management plan consisting entirely of becoming someone else's nuisance.
That ambition centers control rather than the responsibility of leading.
Power's not a reward for wanting to boss people.
He sounds more interested in authority than the people involved.
A leader should make work better for the people doing it.
A supporting character has mistaken cruelty for career development.
An exceptionally clear warning about the next supervisor.
He could learn to solve a problem before asking to assign it to someone else.
A higher place doesn't make an unkind wish wiser.
A better title won't improve the attitude wearing it.
I'd notice how he treats people who can't offer him a promotion.

contexts.subject: A grunt complains the stolen submarine is cramped.

SeafloorCavern_Room1_Text_Grunt2PostBatt.text: That submarine we jacked, man,\nit's brutal as a ride.\lIt's way too tight in there!$

replies.text: The stolen ride has declined to provide luxury seating.
A vehicle designed for specific use may not suit an improvised crowded trip.
Then maybe don't steal people's transport.
He sounds as if the journey was less glamorous than promised.
The discomfort doesn't excuse taking it from its owners.
The grand escape has received an unfavorable passenger review.
A criminal adventure with poor legroom. How terribly inconvenient.
Capacity should have been considered before their ambitious loading plan.
Taking a thing doesn't mean understanding the life it was built for.
An expensive entrance can still be an uncomfortable one.
I'd remember the ordinary complaint behind their dramatic operation.

contexts.subject: A grunt admires our defiance while admitting they cannot question the boss.

SeafloorCavern_Room3_Text_Grunt5PostBatt.text:
You know, we don't dare question
the motives of our leader.\pBut here you are, just some punk,
going up against our BOSS.\pMaybe…
You must be something…$

replies.text: The alarming part is how normal not asking has become.
An organization that forbids scrutiny makes its own errors harder to correct.
He can question him too. Shouldn't need our permission.
He sounds almost surprised that saying no is possible.
Being afraid to ask is a problem worth noticing.
A minor antagonist has glimpsed an alternative to following the script.
The first unsettling thought: perhaps obedience was never compulsory.
He should examine the purpose before judging our right to challenge it.
A question can open where a command has kept a person small.
He noticed our independence. I hope he keeps some for himself.
I'd watch whether the admiration becomes a question he asks aloud.

contexts.subject: Shelly regrets we are not Aqua members able to enjoy the boss's promised world.

SeafloorCavern_Room3_Text_ShellyPostBatt.text:
Ahahahaha!
You're so darn strong.\pIt's terribly disappointing that you're
not a TEAM AQUA member.\pYou could have enjoyed the fabulous
world our BOSS has promised as\lone of us…$

replies.text: The fabulous world seems short on invitations to disagree.
A promised benefit doesn't establish that the method is justified.
We'll keep our judgment. She can keep the uniform.
It's strange being welcomed and threatened by the same cause.
A better world should care about the people already living in it.
A recruitment speech has skipped the chapter about who bears the cost.
A utopia with suspiciously strict membership conditions.
We need evidence about consequences, not admiration of our utility.
A future that cannot hear refusal may not be gentle.
Her compliment doesn't make the offer less troubling.
I'd judge the promise by what they're doing here, not how grandly she describes it.

contexts.subject: A grunt cannot find the exit and insists he is not frightened.

SeafloorCavern_Room4_Text_Grunt3PostBatt.text: I can't find the way out!\pI'm not afraid. Don't get me wrong!$

replies.text: The exit is missing whether or not his pride is frightened.
We can address the navigation without debating his emotional state.
Needs a way out. No shame in saying it.
I wouldn't make him prove how calm he feels.
A clear direction is more useful than teasing.
A stranded antagonist is allowed a practical problem without a dramatic confession.
I also prefer my fear to remain off the official report.
Establish the last known point before trying another passage.
A lost person can need help without first naming the feeling.
Let him keep his composure while we discuss the route.
I'd ask which turns he remembers, not whether he's scared.

contexts.subject: A grunt blames his partner for leaving the map aboard the submarine.

SeafloorCavern_Room4_Text_Grunt4PostBatt.text: My partner forgot the map in that\nsubmarine!\pHow's that for being useless?$

replies.text: The map has stayed with the vehicle instead of the people needing it.
A shared navigation plan shouldn't depend on one easily forgotten item.
Blame won't draw a route. Work together.
It's harder to think when someone's making the mistake personal.
They need a way back more than an argument.
The missing prop is inconvenient; the hostile dialogue isn't helping.
A team has discovered that insults are poor substitutes for cartography.
Reconstruct the known route before adding more uncertain turns.
A shared mistake can be met with shared patience.
Calling a partner useless won't make the partnership work better.
I'd listen for which of them still remembers something helpful.

contexts.subject: A mourner remembers a cherished Zigzagoon at its resting place.

MtPyre_1F_Text_RestingPlaceOfZigzagoon.text: This is the final resting place of my\nZIGZAGOON. I cherished it…$

replies.text: I'd stay quiet enough to let them tell us about Zigzagoon if they want.
A remembered habit might be easier to share than the whole loss.
Give them room. Be there if they want company.
I wonder which little thing they miss most on an ordinary day.
That affection deserves a gentle listener, not a hurried answer.
A beloved life has more to its story than this final place.
A name can leave a much larger silence than anyone expects.
There's no problem here that needs a clever solution from us.
What was cherished can remain close in a small familiar memory.
They shouldn't have to make the grief look tidy for visitors.
I'd remember the name and listen without turning away from the quiet.

contexts.subject: Littleroot motto says the town cannot be shaded any hue.

LittlerootTown_Text_TownSign.text: LITTLEROOT TOWN\n“A town that can't be shaded any hue.”$

replies.text: No hue? The grass has been making a rather persuasive case for green.
An unusual motto. Perhaps they mean the town cannot be reduced to one impression.
A place can be small without being easy to sum up.
I like thinking home has room for more than the version we first remember.
I would remember the people here before choosing a color for them.
The town has politely declined the artist's entire palette.
A town refusing to be neatly categorized. I can appreciate that.
Literal reading fails immediately. We will have to allow the sign some poetry.
A familiar place keeps changing colors when we return to it.
A bold statement for a town with this much visible green.
I would like to see the same street in different light before choosing its color.

contexts.subject: Oldale advertises itself as a place where things begin scarce.

OldaleTown_Text_TownSign.text: OLDALE TOWN\n“Where things start off scarce.”$

replies.text: An admirably honest slogan. Most towns make you visit the shops before discovering that part.
A modest beginning still gives us useful points from which to learn.
We can start with what is here. More is not always the first thing we need.
A small beginning can leave room to notice who is beside you.
A few good supplies and somewhere safe to rest can be enough to begin.
The opening chapter has declared its limited production budget.
Low expectations, plainly stated. Oddly reassuring.
Scarcity makes planning important. Check what we need before heading out.
A small first step is still a step into the world.
Simple is fine. I hope nobody mistakes it for having nothing to offer.
I like finding the details a grander slogan would overlook.

contexts.subject: Petalburg motto describes people mingling with nature.

PetalburgCity_Text_CitySign.text: PETALBURG CITY\n“Where people mingle with nature.”$

replies.text: Mingling with nature. I hope the trees are better at small talk than I am.
Living alongside something is different from treating it as background. A worthwhile idea.
Then people should leave room for more than their own plans.
I like a town that makes the natural world sound like company.
A good neighborhood should have room for the creatures that were already here.
Nature has been invited to the gathering rather than hired as scenery.
I can manage a social event with trees. They rarely ask what my plans are.
I would like to see how the city makes that motto practical.
Roots and footsteps sharing a little ground.
I hope they keep it as a habit, not only a nice phrase on a sign.
I would look for the small places where people have made room for something growing.

contexts.subject: Rustboro motto connects nature and science.

RustboroCity_Text_CitySign.text: RUSTBORO CITY\p“The city probing the integration of\nnature and science.”$

replies.text: Nature and science together. I hope science remembered to wipe its feet before coming in.
Understanding nature should help us live with it, not give us an excuse to ignore it.
Good aim. The results should be good for the people and Pokemon living here.
I like the idea of learning about something because we want to care for it better.
Useful work ought to remember who has to live beside it.
The city has placed a very large question on a very small sign.
A good partnership, provided nobody appoints themselves the only one allowed to speak.
I would like to ask the people building things here what they have learned from the living parts.
Knowing a thing's name is a beginning, not the whole of knowing it.
I hope the attractive words have practical work behind them.
I would look for the places where the two actually meet, rather than just photograph the slogan.

contexts.subject: Dewford calls itself a tiny island in the blue sea.

DewfordTown_Text_TownSign.text: DEWFORD TOWN\n“A tiny island in the blue sea.”$

replies.text: Tiny island, enormous amount of sea. Very sensible of the town to mark its location.
A small place can have strong connections beyond its immediate shoreline.
Small enough to learn the streets. Plenty of world beyond them.
A little place surrounded by room to breathe.
I like imagining how many people know each other's ordinary routines here.
A small stage with an extravagant blue backdrop.
A modest introduction. I appreciate a town that does not oversell itself.
The limited land must make every useful bit of space matter.
A little ground can hold a whole life.
Tiny does not need to mean lacking. It depends what you want nearby.
I would like to see which small corner someone here considers the whole heart of the place.

contexts.subject: Slateport calls itself a port where people and Pokemon cross paths.

SlateportCity_Text_CitySign.text: SLATEPORT CITY\p“The port where people and POKéMON\ncross paths.”$

replies.text: A whole city built around bumping into someone interesting. I hope apologizing counts as networking.
Ports gather people with different routes and different reasons for traveling.
Then keep an eye on the team. A busy place is still full of individuals.
I like thinking a brief meeting can stay with someone after the paths separate.
Some crossings become friendships. Some become directions to a good meal. Both useful.
An ambitious intersection has grown streets, shops, and an audience.
A busy place to be quiet in. I will stay near you.
A lot of different journeys share the same infrastructure here. I would like to see how it works.
Two roads can meet for a moment without becoming the same road.
I like a city whose welcome leaves room for people who will not stay.
I would ask visitors what they are carrying away besides what fits in their bags.

contexts.subject: Mauville advertises a bright shiny city of fun.

MauvilleCity_Text_CitySign.text: MAUVILLE CITY\n“The bright and shiny city of fun!”$

replies.text: Bright, shiny, fun. I hope the pavement is not expected to satisfy all three at once.
A confident promise. I am curious which kind of fun the residents themselves prefer.
We can enjoy it without doing everything the city offers.
I would like to find the quieter sort of fun before the lights exhaust me.
Somewhere to sit with a good snack would satisfy the slogan for me.
Three enthusiastic adjectives have been elected to represent the whole city.
I will look for the dim, matte corner where the fun has reasonable opening hours.
Bright and shiny are easy to specify. Fun will need user testing.
Even a city of light needs somewhere gentle to rest.
Shiny can be lovely. It still helps to know what is underneath.
I would ask a resident where they go when they do not feel like being entertained.

contexts.subject: Verdanturf celebrates its windswept highlands and grass fragrance.

VerdanturfTown_Text_TownSign.text: VERDANTURF TOWN\p“The windswept highlands with the\nsweet fragrance of grass.”$

replies.text: A slogan for the nose. Finally, a sign working with the wind instead of against it.
The air seems central to how people describe this place. I would like to hear what they notice.
Fresh air and room to slow down. A good reason to stop.
I like that the town introduces itself with a feeling before a list of achievements.
A place where opening a window sounds like part of the attraction.
The wind has been given a permanent role in the town's introduction.
A breeze doing promotional work without asking anyone to smile.
I wonder which plants contribute most to the scent people recognize.
A familiar wind can make a place feel like home before the houses appear.
A pleasant impression that does not need to be polished.
I would want to remember the movement of the grass, not only its color.

contexts.subject: Fallarbor describes a farming community with small gardens.

FallarborTown_Text_TownSign.text: FALLARBOR TOWN\n“A farm community with small gardens.”$

replies.text: Small gardens. Sensible. A giant garden would keep asking us to have a giant afternoon.
Small plots can reflect a great deal of accumulated local knowledge.
People tending something together. A good foundation for a town.
I would like to know what someone planted because it reminded them of home.
A good meal begins with somebody doing ordinary work in a garden.
A modest setting with a great many patient stories growing inside it.
Small gardens leave room to know each plant's particular complaints.
I would ask which methods suit the conditions here. Practical local experience matters.
A small patch tended often can hold more care than a broad field ignored.
I like a place proud of something that needs regular attention.
I would ask a gardener which corner they would show a visitor first.

contexts.subject: Lavaridge advertises the Pokemon Center hot springs as a place to relax.

LavaridgeTown_Text_TownSign.text: LAVARIDGE TOWN\p“POKéMON CENTER HOT SPRINGS\nAn excellent place for relaxing!”$

replies.text: An entire town recommending sitting in warm water. I feel understood by the local government.
A chance to rest is useful. We should not confuse relaxing with staying in the heat indefinitely.
A break sounds good. We have earned one.
I like a destination that does not immediately ask us to improve at something.
Warm water, then a proper meal. I could make a very complete afternoon of that.
The itinerary has generously included an intermission.
A public invitation to stop being productive for a little while. Excellent civic policy.
I would like to know how they maintain the springs. After we enjoy the sitting part.
A place that offers warmth without asking us to burn.
Relaxing should not feel like another thing to perform correctly. We can just enjoy it.
I would leave the camera put away for a little while and remember being there.

contexts.subject: Fortree describes a treetop city frolicking with nature.

FortreeCity_Text_CitySign.text: FORTREE CITY\n“The treetop city that frolics with\lnature.”$

replies.text: Frolicking in the treetops. I will begin with the less ambitious art of using the walkway.
A city built among living things must keep adapting as those things grow.
Watch your footing. Admire the view after finding a steady place.
I like hearing the town described as part of the trees instead of above them.
I hope everybody gets help carrying the awkward things up to their homes.
The scenery has accepted the entire cast into its branches.
I am available for a restrained frolic near a reliable railing.
I would like to inspect the supports. Living foundations make an interesting design problem.
A home can be held by something still growing.
A lovely idea. I am choosing shoes for the walkways rather than the slogan.
I would like to see what a resident sees when they step outside before the city wakes.

contexts.subject: Lilycove motto marks where the land ends and sea begins.

LilycoveCity_Text_CitySign.text: LILYCOVE CITY\p“Where the land ends and the\nsea begins.”$

replies.text: The land ends here. Very helpful of the sign to warn my shoes.
The boundary is also a connection. Much of a coast's life comes from both sides.
A good place to stop and decide which way we want to go next.
An ending from one direction is a beginning from the other. I like that.
I would like to share a meal somewhere we can hear both the town and the water.
The edge of one setting opens directly into another. An economical transition.
A place with permission to look unfinished in one direction.
I wonder how the city plans around a boundary that never sits perfectly still.
A shore belongs to the meeting, not only to either side.
I like a place that gives the horizon a little room.
I would want the town in the picture, too, not just the view it looks out on.

contexts.subject: Mossdeep slogan asks people to cherish Pokemon.

replies.text: Cherish Pokemon. A short slogan with enough work inside it to fill the whole day.
A worthwhile principle. I would judge it by the everyday care it produces.
Good words. Keep them true when the Pokemon is tired or inconvenient, too.
I like that the welcome asks something kind instead of something impressive.
Care should include the ordinary days when nobody is watching.
The city has given itself a simple line and a lifelong performance to match.
A promise I would like to see kept on the difficult afternoons.
A clear goal. The practical details are where it becomes real.
A small creature should feel the truth of those words without needing to read them.
I hope the slogan includes the ones who are not especially cute or useful.
I would look for a quiet act of care that nobody expected a visitor to notice.

contexts.subject: Sootopolis calls itself a mystical city where history slumbers.

SootopolisCity_Text_CitySign.text: SOOTOPOLIS CITY\p“The mystical city where history\nslumbers.”$

replies.text: History is sleeping. We should probably stop reading the sign so loudly.
An evocative motto. I would like to know which parts of the history residents still live with.
We can respect an old place without treating its people like part of an exhibit.
I wonder what ordinary memories sit beside the stories visitors come to hear.
Someone still has to make breakfast in a city with a grand past.
A setting has promised an old story while keeping its first page carefully closed.
Sleeping history. A much gentler arrangement than history knocking on the door.
I would separate what is documented from what is remembered as legend. Both deserve clear names.
Old things can rest beneath the shape of an ordinary day.
Mystery is lovely. So is letting the residents have a life beyond it.
I would ask what a person here hopes future visitors will remember about their time.

contexts.subject: Pacifidlog celebrates morning sunlight smiling on the water.

PacifidlogTown_Text_TownSign.text: PACIFIDLOG TOWN\p“Where the morning sun smiles upon\nthe waters.”$

replies.text: A smiling morning sun. Mine usually arrives with a much less polite announcement from my stomach.
Light on moving water changes constantly. It must make familiar mornings feel different.
A good view to wake up to. Watch the boards before admiring it.
I would like one morning with no hurry except getting outside before the light changes.
Breakfast beside that water sounds like a very good start.
The town has hired the sunrise to deliver its daily opening scene.
I would appreciate the smile more if it arrived slightly later in the morning.
I wonder how much the changing light helps residents read the water.
The same sun finds a new path across the waves each day.
Some views do not need an elaborate introduction. This one still got a nice one.
I would get up early for that. Quietly, so nobody mistakes it for a new habit.

contexts.subject: Ever Grande describes a paradise of flowers, sea and Pokemon.

EverGrandeCity_Text_CitySign.text: EVER GRANDE CITY\p“The paradise of flowers, the sea,\nand POKéMON.”$

replies.text: Flowers, sea, Pokemon. A very persuasive list missing only the place to have lunch.
A memorable setting. I hope people leave room to enjoy it alongside the challenge ahead.
Take a moment to look around. We did not come this far only to hurry past it.
I like having something gentle waiting beside something that matters so much.
We should give the team a peaceful moment here before asking anything more.
The final approach has remembered that beauty can matter beside ambition.
A paradise placed beside a test. I vote we notice both.
A pleasant environment does not remove the need for preparation. We can appreciate it while checking.
Even at the edge of a great challenge, flowers are allowed to bloom for no reason at all.
We are allowed to remember the place, not only the result we hope to earn here.
I would like a picture of the team before the next door, with the flowers still part of it.

contexts.subject: Norman Gym sign describes him as pursuing power.

PetalburgCity_Text_GymSign.text: PETALBURG CITY POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: NORMAN\l“A man in pursuit of power!”$

replies.text: A man in pursuit of power. It would be a much stranger motto over the kitchen door.
Power is a broad goal. I am more interested in what he wants to do with it.
We can meet the trainer behind the words instead of arguing with the sign.
It is strange seeing someone familiar introduced as a public figure.
I hope he makes room for the people who want his company as well as his skill.
A father's ordinary name has acquired a rather formidable subtitle.
Your family introduction comes with a competitive warning label.
I would ask him what measure of progress he actually uses.
A pursuit can lead somewhere, or keep someone from seeing what is already beside them.
He gets to be more than the slogan. So do you.
I wonder how differently you read that sign from a visitor who has never met him.

contexts.subject: Roxanne Gym sign celebrates a Rock-loving honors student.

RustboroCity_Text_GymSign.text: RUSTBORO CITY POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: ROXANNE\p“The ROCK-loving honors student!”$

replies.text: An honors student who gets to drop rocks on the examiners. An ambitious education.
Her studies became a way to work with the Pokemon she loves. That is a good connection.
Good credentials. We will still pay attention to how she actually battles.
I like that loving something and studying it belong in the same introduction.
I hope she gets to enjoy the work without feeling she must always be the best student.
A distinguished academic record has found a very practical examination room.
She has put her interests on the sign. An effective filter for people bored by rocks.
Applying study in the field. I would like to know which lesson surprised her most.
She has followed a small fascination far enough to build a place around it.
A confident introduction that still lets her be enthusiastic about what she likes.
I would look for the little signs that she still enjoys learning, not only being accomplished.

contexts.subject: Brawly Gym sign calls him a big wave in fighting.

DewfordTown_Text_GymSign.text: DEWFORD TOWN POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: BRAWLY\l“A big wave in fighting!”$

replies.text: A big wave in fighting. I hope the entrance fee does not include getting splashed.
The metaphor promises force and momentum. I would like to see the technique behind it.
We can prepare for a strong fighter without letting the sign intimidate us.
I would rather know the person before deciding how frightening the wave is.
A strong challenge still needs a team that feels ready for it.
The local action hero has a suitably dramatic coastal billing.
I will approach with the quiet dignity of someone checking where the exits are.
An energetic introduction. It is not a substitute for a tactical briefing.
Even a large wave has a rhythm. We can learn to see it.
A vivid image. I would like to meet the person who gets to live with it every day.
I wonder whether the town chose that phrase or he did.

contexts.subject: Wattson sign calls him cheerfully electrifying.

MauvilleCity_Text_GymSign.text: MAUVILLE CITY POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: WATTSON\l“The cheerfully electrifying man!”$

replies.text: Cheerfully electrifying. Two words I would prefer kept apart when somebody shakes my hand.
A bright personality can make a difficult challenge feel more welcoming.
He sounds friendly. We should still take the electrical part seriously.
I like the thought of a strong opponent who is happy we came.
Someone who enjoys the work can make everyone around them more comfortable.
The comedy and the special effects appear to share one enthusiastic operator.
A cheerful man with access to electricity. The sign has responsibly warned us.
I am interested in the systems. I am cautiously optimistic about the host.
A warm welcome does not always arrive quietly.
He sounds like someone who will be difficult to forget.
I wonder whether his ordinary laugh is as memorable as the sign wants us to expect.

contexts.subject: Flannery sign celebrates her burning passion.

LavaridgeTown_Text_GymSign.text: LAVARIDGE TOWN POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: FLANNERY\l“One with a fiery passion that burns!”$

replies.text: A fiery passion that burns. The sign has left very little room for a cooling interpretation.
Enthusiasm matters. I would like to see how she turns it into good decisions for the team.
Take the passion seriously. Do not mistake excitement for a lack of skill.
I hope she gets to have quieter days without disappointing the sign.
It is good to love the work. It is also good to have someone make sure you rest.
An energetic lead has been introduced with enough fire for three promotional posters.
That is a lot of intensity to be asked to embody before breakfast.
Heat makes a vivid metaphor. The practical test is how she uses it.
A flame needs care if it is going to last.
She should get to be more than the loudest description of her.
I would like to hear her describe herself without the slogan doing it first.

contexts.subject: Winona sign describes a bird user taking flight into the world.

FortreeCity_Text_GymSign.text: FORTREE CITY POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: WINONA\p“The bird user taking flight into\nthe world.”$

replies.text: Taking flight into the world. I will start by taking the stairs without embarrassing myself.
A fitting image for someone whose work centers on Flying Pokemon.
A wide world ahead. We still need to watch the next step.
I like the possibility in that phrase. It sounds like she is still going somewhere.
A home can be a place to return to without being a place that holds you still.
Her introduction has given the horizon a part in the story.
A lovely ambition. I hope she is allowed a quiet landing now and then.
I would like to know how working with birds changed her idea of distance.
A wing belongs to the sky and to the creature that chooses where to go.
It leaves room for her to keep growing beyond the title. I like that.
I wonder what she hopes to see when she is the traveler instead of the person welcoming one.

contexts.subject: The twins sign calls Liza and Tate a mystic combination.

MossdeepCity_Text_GymSign.text: MOSSDEEP CITY POKéMON GYM\nLEADERS: LIZA & TATE\p“The mystic combination!”$

replies.text: A mystic combination. I hope the door does not ask us to provide an equally impressive partner title.
A partnership is part of their public identity. Coordination will be worth watching.
Two leaders. We should think about how the whole team works together.
I wonder what it feels like to be introduced as half of something before anyone meets you.
I hope both of them have space to be themselves inside the partnership.
A double billing with a shared promise of the inexplicable.
We should prepare a combination of our own. I suggest you, me, and a sensible plan.
The interaction between two systems can matter more than their individual outputs.
Two lights can meet without becoming one flame.
A memorable pair should still have room for two distinct people.
I would like to notice the differences as carefully as the similarities.

contexts.subject: Juan sign praises his beauty as pure water.

SootopolisCity_Text_GymSign.text: SOOTOPOLIS CITY POKéMON GYM\nLEADER: JUAN\p“The GYM LEADER with the beauty\nof pure water!”$

replies.text: The beauty of pure water. I have mostly encountered water looking suspiciously like my own wet face.
A graceful image. I would still judge his training by more than presentation.
An elegant introduction does not tell us the whole battle plan.
I hope he enjoys being himself as much as everyone enjoys describing him.
Water can be gentle and strong. I would like to see both given their due.
The leading man has received an exceptionally flattering contribution from the sign writer.
An enviable review. My own reflection has been less cooperative.
Presentation is clearly part of the experience. I am interested in the method beneath it.
Clear water can show depth without making a sound.
A beautiful image. It leaves a little room to decide what beauty means for ourselves.
I would like to see him in an ordinary moment before asking him to match the portrait.

contexts.subject: The explanation identifies the sign used for Pokemon Gyms.

PetalburgCity_Text_ThisIsGymSign.text: This is the GYM's sign. Look for it\nwhenever you're looking for a GYM.$

replies.text: A sign explaining how to find signs. We have reached the foundations of adventuring.
A recognizable symbol is useful when the town and its layout are unfamiliar.
Good to know what to look for when we need the next Gym.
I like instructions that assume we might be new without making it embarrassing.
A clear landmark can save a tired team a lot of wandering.
The tutorial has briefly introduced the scenery's own method of introducing itself.
I appreciate a symbol that does not change its mind in every town.
Consistent signage. Quietly important design work.
A small familiar mark can make a new road less uncertain.
Useful, clear, and easy to remember. A good sign doing its job.
I will watch for that shape before trying to memorize every street.

contexts.subject: Dewford Hall advertises an information exchange for everyone.

replies.text: An information exchange. I hope my vague recollections qualify as a useful contribution.
Sharing information is valuable. Knowing where it came from helps keep it valuable.
Listen first. We do not need to believe every confident voice in the room.
I like a place where somebody can come just to hear what other people have noticed.
A familiar room to talk in can be as important as the things people say.
A public stage on which gossip has requested the more dignified title of information.
Everyone's exchange. Including the person who is completely certain about something completely wrong.
I would start by asking how they check the facts they pass along.
A small town can send one thought through a great many lives.
I hope there is room for the person who has not found the right words yet.
I would like to hear the conversation before deciding which voice describes the whole room.

contexts.subject: The Contest Hall sign calls it a gathering place for trainers.

LilycoveCity_Text_ContestHallSign.text: POKéMON CONTEST HALL\n“The gathering place for TRAINERS!”$

replies.text: A gathering of trainers. I hope the waiting room has enough space for everyone's dramatic entrance.
A shared venue lets people compare very different ways of working with their Pokemon.
We can watch and learn without having to enter immediately.
I would like to see the quiet preparation as well as the big performance.
I hope the teams get encouragement when they are done, whatever the result.
A hall devoted to people who have decided their partners deserve an audience.
I am prepared to admire from somewhere that does not require introducing myself.
I would be interested in the practical preparation behind an apparently effortless performance.
A bright moment rests on many small, unseen ones.
Now that is a place to notice how personality changes the same basic idea.
I would want a picture of a trainer looking proudly at their partner after the performance.

contexts.subject: Marcos warns children against wandering in the dark cave.

MtMoon_1F_Text_MarcosPostBattle.text: Kids like you shouldn't be\nwandering around here in the dark.$

replies.text: Fair warning. The cave has been very stingy with streetlights.
Visibility and navigation are legitimate concerns regardless of age.
We came prepared. Still worth watching our footing.
I appreciate the concern, even wrapped in that scolding tone.
A little caution is reasonable when the way back is not obvious.
The cave's unofficial chaperone has issued a stern review.
Darkness is quite good at making familiar distances feel strange.
Age is less relevant than light, supplies, and a route plan.
A dark path asks people of every size to tread carefully.
He could offer directions along with the disapproval.
I wonder whether he has had to help someone lost here before.

contexts.subject: Josh admits entering the cave to impress girls.

MtMoon_1F_Text_JoshPostBattle.text: I came all the way down here to\nshow off to girls.$

replies.text: A dark cave is an ambitious place to rely on being noticed.
His chosen setting makes visual self-presentation unusually difficult.
Hope he packed for the cave, not just the entrance.
That is a rather honest explanation for an awkward plan.
An outing is easier when you also enjoy the place yourself.
A romantic campaign with poor lighting and an exceptionally bat-heavy venue.
A long way to come to be barely visible.
Requirements and environment seem poorly matched.
He followed a bright idea into a very dark room.
Confidence helps. So does choosing a place where people can see the outfit.
I wonder whether anyone he hoped to meet actually came this way.

contexts.subject: Miriam fears getting lost and asks how to leave the large cave.

MtMoon_1F_Text_MiriamPostBattle.text: How do you get out of here?\nIt's so big, I may get lost.$

replies.text: The mountain has more indoors than she ordered. Understandable concern.
She needs reliable directions rather than reassurance without a route.
Stay on a known path. Do not wander farther while unsure.
It is frightening when every passage looks like a possible mistake.
A calm pause and a clear route back would help.
The expedition has revised its objective from discovery to finding the door.
A large place can make a small uncertainty grow quickly.
Stop, establish a known position, then choose the exit route.
The next useful landmark may be the one that leads out.
She is sensible to ask before pretending she knows the way.
I wonder which entrance she came through.

contexts.subject: Jovan wonders where to find stronger Pokemon.

MtMoon_1F_Text_JovanPostBattle.text: I have to find stronger POKéMON.\nWhere might they be?$

replies.text: The next strong partner may need some help becoming strong first.
Habitat, training, and team needs all matter more than an undefined strength ranking.
Look after the team he has before blaming it for the loss.
I hope he is curious about new partners, not simply tired of the old ones.
A better plan can help an existing team more than a hurried replacement.
The casting search expands before the rehearsal schedule receives a review.
Strength is easier to ask for than to define usefully.
Specify the missing capability before looking for a new component.
A stronger branch still needs someone to tend the roots.
He might begin by noticing what his current partners already do well.
I wonder what he most needs the team to handle differently.

contexts.subject: Iris says rumors of rare fossils brought her to Mt. Moon.

MtMoon_1F_Text_IrisPostBattle.text: I came because I heard there are\nsome very rare fossils here.$

replies.text: A treasure hunt with very old treasure. Good reason to bring patience.
A fossil-bearing site can reward careful examination of ordinary-looking rock.
Worth searching carefully. Fragile finds need steady hands.
I understand coming a long way for a chance to find something extraordinary.
A good search needs time and enough supplies to leave comfortably afterward.
The mountain's oldest residents are attracting a new generation of visitors.
A little of the vanished world waiting in the walls.
A geological search! I would like to compare the layers.
The stone may have kept a shape the world no longer walks in.
A specific interest makes the cave feel like more than a shortcut.
I wonder what first made her interested in fossils.

contexts.subject: Kent insists he saw Team Rocket in the cave.

MtMoon_1F_Text_KentPostBattle.text: I saw them!\nI'm sure they're from TEAM ROCKET!$

replies.text: That makes the cave's shadows feel a little less ordinary.
A direct claimed sighting is more useful than a vague rumor, though details still matter.
Stay alert. Do not assume the next person down here is harmless.
He sounds certain enough that I would take the warning seriously.
We should keep the team ready and know our way back.
The underground excursion has acquired a rather unwelcome supporting cast.
Dark places do not need people deliberately making them worse.
Potential hostile presence. Reassess the route and supplies.
Some shadows have people inside them who mean harm.
A warning worth hearing, even from someone still a little shaken.
I wonder which way they were heading when he saw them.

contexts.subject: Robby praises Zubat as a dependable partner despite its toughness to catch.

MtMoon_1F_Text_RobbyPostBattle.text: ZUBAT is tough!\nBut if you can catch one, you'll\lbe able to count on it.$

replies.text: A difficult introduction can still become very good company.
The effort of catching a Pokemon and its value as a partner are separate questions.
Earn its trust after the catch. That is the important part.
It is nice to hear someone talk about Zubat with affection instead of annoyance.
A partner who knows the cave could be reassuring down here.
The frequently unwelcome cave resident receives a deserved favorable review.
Even a creature that startles everyone can be someone's dependable friend.
A cave-adapted partner has useful capabilities. Worth understanding them.
Something at home in the dark can make the dark less lonely.
He seems to value the bond beyond the difficult first meeting.
I wonder what Zubat did that made him trust it so much.

contexts.subject: The excavator says Brock sometimes helps dig for fossils under Mt. Moon.

MtMoon_1F_Text_BrockHelpsExcavateFossils.text: Hi, I'm excavating for fossils here\nunder MT. MOON.\pSometimes, BROCK of PEWTER GYM\nlends me a hand.$

replies.text: Brock has a second kind of rock appointment. A useful pair of interests.
Field excavation benefits from practical knowledge of stone as well as careful technique.
Good of him to lend a hand with the actual work.
It is nice to hear what someone does outside the role everyone knows.
Helping with a slow job says something good about a person.
The Gym Leader's off-duty chapter includes a rather patient supporting role.
Someone who knows stones is helping them tell a much older story.
Relevant specialist volunteering on site. Excellent collaboration.
A strong pair of hands making room for fragile old shapes.
A reputation feels more rounded when you hear the ordinary details.
I wonder which find Brock was most excited to help uncover.

contexts.subject: After losing, Miguel agrees that we may each choose one fossil.

MtMoon_B2F_Text_WellEachTakeAFossil.text: We'll each take a fossil!\nNo being greedy!$

replies.text: A fossil each. Much better than trying to fit all of prehistory in one pocket.
The agreement establishes a clear shared allocation before either item is taken.
Fair arrangement. Take one and leave the other.
I am glad the argument found a calm ending.
There is enough for both people to leave with something meaningful.
The excavation dispute concludes with a mercifully simple division of the cast.
An old world has enough room for two people's curiosity.
Two resources, two claimants, explicit allocation. Straightforward.
A little restraint can keep a discovery from turning bitter.
He has made the choice fair without making it complicated.
I wonder which one he hopes we leave for him.

contexts.subject: After our fossil selection, Miguel takes the remaining fossil.

MtMoon_B2F_Text_ThenThisFossilIsMine.text: All right.\nThen this fossil is mine!$

replies.text: Two explorers, two fossils, and no prehistoric tug-of-war. Good finish.
The agreed allocation is now complete; each person has one fossil.
Deal kept. We can move on without taking more than our share.
It is nice that both people get to be pleased with the discovery.
A shared find can leave two good stories instead of one argument.
The remaining ancient role has found its equally enthusiastic custodian.
The old stones are leaving by two separate little journeys.
Selection complete, remainder assigned. No ambiguity left.
Two shapes from the past have begun different roads into the present.
Fairness looks very ordinary when it is actually practiced.
I wonder whether he will take his fossil somewhere to be examined too.

contexts.subject: Miguel tells us the Cinnabar laboratory studies fossil regeneration.

MtMoon_B2F_Text_LabOnCinnabarRegenerates.text: Far away, on CINNABAR ISLAND,\nthere's a POKéMON LAB.\pThey do research on regenerating\nfossils.$

replies.text: Our old rock has a possible next appointment on an island. Quite a journey for a fossil.
A specialized laboratory is the appropriate place to investigate its potential.
Useful lead. Keep the fossil safe until we can get there.
The thought of that old shape moving again is difficult to imagine.
A remarkable possibility deserves patience and careful handling.
The prehistoric discovery has acquired a promising next chapter and a distant address.
A little trace of the old world may yet have somewhere new to go.
Regeneration research! The lab should have better answers than our guesses.
Something that rested in stone may be carried toward another beginning.
A clear recommendation makes a strange find easier to take seriously.
I wonder how Miguel first heard about that laboratory.

contexts.subject: The defeated grunt threatens to put us on Team Rocket's blacklist.

MtMoon_B2F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: You made me mad!\nTEAM ROCKET will blacklist you!$

replies.text: A list of people they dislike. We seem to have arrived with suitable qualifications.
The threat indicates ongoing hostility rather than a harmless complaint.
Stay alert. His threat does not make letting him hurt people acceptable.
I do not like being threatened in a place with so few exits.
Best keep moving together and stay aware of the route out.
A disreputable organization has expressed disappointment in our compatibility.
An unpleasant little honor, with potential practical consequences.
