contexts.subject: A worker fears that Rocket wants world domination through Pokemon.

SilphCo_6F_Text_RocketsTryingToConquerWo.text: TEAM ROCKET is trying to conquer\nthe world with POKéMON.$

replies.text: A very large ambition from people already being awful in one building.
The worker describes a feared broader objective. The immediate threat is serious enough.
Start by stopping what they are doing here. Staff need safety now.
That thought would make an already frightening day feel enormous.
One safe room and one safe person at a time still matter.
The villains' ambitions have expanded well beyond their already intolerable local conduct.
A huge threat can make it difficult to see the useful small thing in reach.
Scope uncertain. Immediate containment remains a practical priority.
A shadow can look endless when it falls across your own door.
The fear is real even if the whole plan is not known to the worker.
I wonder what they overheard that made them think the ambition was that large.

contexts.subject: The worker credits us for driving Rocket away.

SilphCo_6F_Text_RocketsRanAwayBecauseOfY.text: TEAM ROCKET ran away, and it's all\nbecause of you!$

replies.text: They can finally talk about Rocket in the past tense. Good change.
The immediate danger has ended, and they connect that outcome with our intervention.
Glad they are safe. The team did a lot of the hard work.
You can hear the relief under the excitement.
A normal day is a very good thing to help give back.
The former emergency becomes a story the survivor can tell from safety.
A frightening presence has become an absent one. That is enough for now.
Hostiles withdrew. Staff can begin recovering the space.
The room is no longer waiting for the next harsh footstep.
A generous thank-you. We can make sure the partners hear it too.
I wonder who they are most excited to tell that it is over.

contexts.subject: A worker thinks Rocket targeted Silph for its Pokemon-related products.

SilphCo_6F_Text_TargetedSilphForOurMonPr.text: They must have targeted SILPH for\nour POKéMON products.$

replies.text: Making useful things should not mean criminals get to choose your workday.
Valuable technology is a plausible motive, though the worker is inferring it.
The products can be replaced. The people need protecting first.
It is awful when something you helped make becomes a reason to feel unsafe.
I hope the company remembers the people behind those products after this.
Innovation has drawn an audience with unusually destructive purchasing methods.
A clever thing can attract people who care very little for its maker.
Threat model includes technology theft. Protect the staff along with the research.
Useful work has cast a shadow its makers did not ask for.
It is a sensible suspicion. The blame still belongs with the attackers.
I wonder which projects the staff were most worried about losing.

contexts.subject: A grateful employee suggests we work for Silph in the future.

SilphCo_6F_Text_ComeWorkForSilphWhenYour.text: Come work for SILPH when you\nget older.$

replies.text: An unusual recruitment process. Most interviews involve fewer occupied floors.
They see useful qualities beyond our immediate intervention. A warm compliment.
Kind offer. We have time to decide what work suits us.
It is flattering to hear someone imagine a place for you in their future.
A job worth choosing should leave room for a good ordinary life too.
The rescue concludes with a very informal invitation to join the staff list.
Someone has looked at a difficult day and found a possible future in it.
Interesting offer. I would have questions about the actual work and tools.
A new door has been mentioned, without asking us to walk through it today.
A friendly possibility is nicer than a demand for a promise.
I wonder which role the employee imagines us enjoying.

contexts.subject: After a successful Lapras handoff and naming flow, the employee explains Lapras's intelligence and swimming.

SilphCo_7F_Text_ExplainLapras.text:
It's a LAPRAS.
It's a very intelligent POKéMON.\pWe kept it in our lab, but it will
be much better off with you.\pI think you will be a good TRAINER
for LAPRAS!\pIt's a good swimmer.
It'll give you a lift across water!$

replies.text: A clever new companion, trusted to us with a very hopeful goodbye.
The handoff completed before this explanation. We now need to learn the individual's habits.
Welcome aboard, Lapras. A partner first, transport second.
I hope the change from the lab feels like a kinder, wider place to be.
We should give the new arrival time to settle before expecting anything.
A sheltered life opens into a journey, with a rather touching vote of confidence.
A larger world can be a gift when there is someone patient beside you.
An intelligent swimming partner! Lots to learn from, with no need to rush.
A life kept indoors is being trusted with a road made of water.
The employee sounds concerned about Lapras's future, not just the thank-you.
I wonder what Lapras will notice first outside the building.

contexts.subject: On a later visit, the Lapras employee worries that Rocket's boss reached the president.

SilphCo_7F_Text_RocketBossWentToBoardroo.text: TEAM ROCKET's BOSS went to the\nboardroom!\pIs our PRESIDENT okay?\nI'm worried.$

replies.text: A useful direction, with a very worried person at the end of it.
The boardroom is a specific lead. The president's current safety remains unknown to the worker.
Head there prepared. The staff need a clear answer about who is safe.
It is hard to hear how helpless the distance between floors makes them feel.
We can keep the worker out of danger while following the lead.
A familiar office has become the worrying destination of the whole building's attention.
Concern travels upward more quickly than reliable news.
Destination confirmed by report. Check the team before proceeding.
A closed room above has gathered a great deal of fear around it.
They want to know someone is all right, not hear another grand plan.
I wonder when they last received an update from upstairs.

contexts.subject: A researcher says Rocket came for the Master Ball.

SilphCo_7F_Text_RocketsAfterMasterBall.text: TEAM ROCKET was after the MASTER\nBALL, which catches any POKéMON.$

replies.text: A ball that catches anything would be a terrible thing to put in those hands.
A guaranteed capture device would be a powerful target for an exploitative organization.
Keep it away from Rocket. The partners they would use it on deserve better.
That makes the takeover feel very deliberate.
A useful invention can become frightening when the wrong people decide how to use it.
The criminal plot has selected a prop with exceptionally ugly implications.
A tool without a failure condition still needs a person with limits.
Capability alone is not safety. Access control matters enormously here.
A closed ball can be a much larger cage in the wrong hand.
The device is impressive. Their reason for wanting it is the disturbing part.
I wonder who on the project realized it was being targeted first.

contexts.subject: After Rocket leaves, the researcher says the Master Ball project was canceled.

SilphCo_7F_Text_CanceledMasterBallProjec.text: We canceled the MASTER BALL\nproject because of TEAM ROCKET.$

replies.text: A brilliant idea has left everyone with a very difficult decision about it.
Canceling further development may reflect the consequences of its misuse risk.
Better to stop than hand more power to people who will hurt partners with it.
It must be hard to set aside something you worked on for so long.
People matter more than finishing a project simply because it began.
The invention's extraordinary promise has acquired consequences the proposal could not ignore.
Sometimes the gentlest ending for a dangerous possibility is to leave it unfinished.
A capability can be technically successful and still fail a broader design review.
An unopened future can be a deliberate choice rather than a loss.
I hope the people who made it are given time to find work they feel good about.
I wonder how the team feels about the decision now the immediate danger is over.

contexts.subject: A worker fears what Rocket control would mean for Silph and its Pokemon.

SilphCo_7F_Text_BadIfTeamRocketTookOver.text: It would be bad if TEAM ROCKET\ntook over SILPH or our POKéMON.$

replies.text: They are worried about the people and Pokemon inside the company, not just the name on the door.
Institutional control would affect staff and living research subjects alike.
They are right to worry. Keep them away from the grunts.
It is awful having to imagine your familiar workplace under someone cruel.
The Pokemon kept here need safe people looking after them.
A corporate takeover becomes a very personal danger when the assets are alive.
A name on a building can conceal many small lives depending on the people inside.
Protect the living participants first. Equipment can wait.
The door sign is less important than who is allowed to hold the keys.
A reasonable fear from someone who knows what is at stake in the rooms.
I wonder whether the Pokemon have somewhere protected away from the occupied halls.

contexts.subject: The worker marvels that we drove Team Rocket out.

SilphCo_7F_Text_WowYouChasedOffTeamRocke.text: Wow!\pYou chased off TEAM ROCKET all by\nyourself?$

replies.text: Not alone. There were quite a few determined Pokemon involved.
The surprise is understandable, though the team deserves explicit credit.
The partners did the hard part beside us. Glad the worker is safe.
It feels strange to hear the whole day folded into one astonished sentence.
A good outcome belongs to everyone who helped make it possible.
The final summary has accidentally reduced an ensemble to a solo performance.
A remarkable day is easier to tell than it was to stand inside.
Successful outcome, shared effort. Include the full team in the record.
Many little strengths carried the same difficult hour.
We can accept the kindness while making room for the partners in it.
I wonder what part of the news first reached this floor.

contexts.subject: A frightened worker warns us away and cannot believe we can help.

SilphCo_7F_Text_ReallyDangerousHere.text: You!\nIt's really dangerous here!\pYou came to save me?\nYou can't!$

replies.text: They are trying to warn us even while they need help themselves.
Fear and an uncertain assessment of our ability explain the reaction.
Get them somewhere safer. No need to convince them with a speech.
They sound worried for us as well as themselves.
A practical safe step will mean more than a promise that everything will be fine.
The intended rescue meets a frightened person reluctant to see another person put at risk.
Concern can sound like refusal when it has nowhere safer to go.
Demonstrate a safe route rather than arguing about capability.
A scared voice is still trying to put a hand between us and the danger.
It is a kind instinct, however hopeless they feel.
I wonder whether they have watched anyone else get hurt trying to intervene.

contexts.subject: The previously frightened worker thanks us after the takeover ends.

replies.text: A quieter voice, with much less fear inside it. That is good to hear.
The danger has ended, and the gratitude follows a very real change in conditions.
Glad they can breathe again. The team did well.
A few plain words can hold an enormous amount of relief.
I hope they have someone to spend a calmer evening with.
The rescue finally becomes something the person can believe happened.
A room returned to the people who were frightened inside it.
A meaningful success condition: the staff feel safe enough to say this.
The voice has found a little warmth under the fear.
A sincere thank-you does not need more explanation than that.
I wonder when they last felt comfortable enough to smile.

contexts.subject: An employee fears the takeover means the end of Silph.

SilphCo_8F_Text_WonderIfSilphIsFinished.text: I wonder if SILPH is finished…$

replies.text: It is hard to imagine an ordinary next week while the building feels like this.
They are projecting an uncertain crisis into a permanent outcome. The uncertainty is understandable.
Start with keeping people safe. The company's future can be sorted afterward.
A familiar life can feel very fragile when the place it depends on is threatened.
They deserve a clear answer from someone responsible when the danger is over.
An entire working future has begun to look like a story ending mid-page.
A job can hold far more of a life than the tasks written under its title.
Current failure does not establish permanent collapse. First contain the immediate damage.
A building can feel like the edge of someone's whole world.
I hope the staff are included when people start deciding what comes next.
I wonder how long they have worked here.

contexts.subject: The employee thanks us after fears for Silph's future give way to safety.

replies.text: The end of the company has become a much nicer sentence. Good.
The immediate crisis has passed, leaving room for recovery rather than speculation about collapse.
They are safe. That comes before any name on the building.
It is lovely to hear the fear loosen its hold.
A future that includes ordinary work again must feel very welcome.
The threatened ending has become a beginning of the next working day.
A small thank-you from someone who briefly could not see what came next.
Emergency resolved. Recovery can proceed on a much steadier basis.
A little future has returned to the room.
I hope the relief lasts long enough for everyone to recover properly.
I wonder what they are most glad to have back.

contexts.subject: A worker fears Giovanni's cruelty and his view of Pokemon as tools.

SilphCo_8F_Text_ToRocketBossMonsAreTools.text:
TEAM ROCKET's BOSS is terribly
cruel!\pTo him, POKéMON are just tools to
be used.\pWhat will happen if that tyrant
takes over our company…$

replies.text: A living partner should never have to earn the right to be treated like it matters.
Treating Pokemon solely as instruments removes necessary concern for their welfare.
Keep him away from them. They deserve care, not a use assigned by him.
It is frightening to hear someone talk about living things without warmth.
Useful or not, every partner still needs a safe place and decent treatment.
A tyrant's efficiency is merely cruelty with a neatly labeled objective.
A creature is not a thing just because someone finds it convenient to think so.
Living partners are not interchangeable components. The premise is wrong.
A hand that only grasps has forgotten what holding safely means.
I understand why the staff are afraid of the kind of place he would make this.
I wonder whether any of the Pokemon here have already been put in his custody.

contexts.subject: After offering a restorative rest, the helper encourages us to continue.

replies.text: A rest first, a brave word afterward. That is the right order.
Encouragement is more useful when paired with practical recovery.
Good help. Now check the team before going back out.
It is easier to keep going when somebody has noticed you were tired.
A little care can make the next part feel manageable again.
The encouraging line arrives after the kind action that gives it weight.
A small safe pause holding the rest of the journey together.
Recovery completed before renewed effort. Excellent support sequence.
A little shelter can put the road back beneath your feet.
The encouragement feels earned by the care that came before it.
I wonder how many frightened people this helper has already steadied.

contexts.subject: After Rocket leaves, the helper thanks us.

replies.text: They offered us a rest when it mattered. I am glad the safety came back their way too.
The support was reciprocal: they helped us continue, and the intervention improved their situation.
They helped the team first. Good to have been useful in return.
It is lovely when a kind person gets to feel relieved too.
They made room for our rest. Now they deserve their own quiet evening.
The supporting character receives a safer ending for the whole scene.
A little care has traveled in both directions.
Shared effort produced the outcome. Their practical contribution mattered.
A warm place offered has become a warm place returned.
We should remember that we were helped along the way.
I wonder what they need after spending the day looking after others.

contexts.subject: An employee openly cries in fear during the takeover.

replies.text: They are frightened. Nobody needs to be witty about that.
An acute fear response deserves calm support and a safer setting.
Get them away from the danger. Let them cry if they need to.
I wish the room could feel gentler for them right now.
A calm voice and a safe place would help more than telling them to stop.
No audience commentary required. Just somebody having a terrible day.
There is nothing undignified about being unable to hide fear.
Reduce the threat and the noise. Emotional control is not the first priority.
A frightened voice needs room to tremble without being punished for it.
We can protect their dignity without pretending not to hear the distress.
I wonder whether someone they trust is still on this floor.

contexts.subject: Afterward, the employee asks us not to tell others they cried.

SilphCo_10F_Text_KeepMeCryingASecret.text: About me crying…\nPlease keep it a secret.$

replies.text: Their secret is safe. Being scared did not make them smaller.
Privacy is a reasonable request after a vulnerable moment.
We will not make their fear into gossip.
I understand wanting to keep that moment for yourself afterward.
They should not have to worry about being teased on top of everything else.
A private scene will remain private. Not every story belongs in the retelling.
Some memories deserve a closed little drawer.
Confidentiality request received. No reason to redistribute the information.
The shaky part of the day can rest without an audience.
Of course. Kindness includes knowing which details to leave alone.
I hope the people here would be gentle if they knew anyway.

contexts.subject: After giving the Master Ball, the president explains its guaranteed capture and asks for discretion.

SilphCo_11F_Text_ThatsOurSecretPrototype.text:
PRESIDENT: You can't buy that
anywhere.\pIt's our secret prototype MASTER
BALL.\pIt will catch any POKéMON without
fail!\pYou should be quiet about using it,
though.$

replies.text: An extraordinary gift with a very quiet introduction. We should think carefully before using it.
The prototype has exceptional capability, and the request for discretion is explicit.
Keep it safe. A powerful tool still needs a careful choice.
It feels like a lot of trust placed in one small object.
A generous reward does not mean we need to decide how to use it immediately.
The confidential prototype enters our care with a rather weighty final line.
Something can be tiny enough for a pocket and still carry a large responsibility.
Guaranteed capture is a remarkable claim. Secure storage first, questions later.
A small closed shape holding a very consequential possibility.
We can be grateful and still take time to understand the choice it gives us.
I wonder how the people who developed it feel about seeing it leave the lab.

contexts.subject: The president cannot give his reward because our bag is full.

SilphCo_11F_Text_YouHaveNoRoomForThis.text: You have no room for this.$

replies.text: An entire rescue, concluded by a pocket refusing one more object. Very practical anticlimax.
The intended reward did not transfer. Lack of space is the stated obstacle.
Sort the bag. No reason to make this harder for anyone.
It is awkward to be unprepared after such heartfelt thanks.
A little tidying will let us accept the generosity properly.
The grand gratitude has encountered the remarkably democratic limits of luggage.
A full bag is unimpressed by wealth, titles, and dramatic timing.
Capacity failure at handoff. No reward should be assumed received.
The small place we carry has held up a much larger moment.
We can fix our own inconvenience without making him feel responsible.
I wonder how much of the bag we have been carrying out of habit.

contexts.subject: The secretary thanks us on behalf of the president and all staff.

SilphCo_11F_Text_ThanksForRescuingUs.text: SECRETARY: Thank you for rescuing\nall of us.\pWe, from the PRESIDENT down,\nare indebted to you.$

replies.text: It is good that the thanks includes everyone, not just the biggest office.
Her wording recognizes the takeover as a threat across the whole workforce.
Glad the staff are safe. Every floor mattered.
A simple collective thank-you makes the whole building feel more human.
I hope everyone gets a quiet chance to recover, from the front desk upward.
The final acknowledgment gives the supporting cast its proper share of the ending.
A tall building is still mostly made of ordinary people's days.
Staff-wide safety restored. That is the outcome worth recording.
Many familiar rooms can begin to feel like their own again.
She remembered the people beyond the room. A thoughtful way to speak.
I wonder how the staff will mark their first peaceful day back.

contexts.subject: Connor admits working for both Silph and Team Rocket.

SilphCo_2F_Text_ConnorPostBattle.text: I work for both SILPH and TEAM\nROCKET.$

replies.text: Two employers, one remarkably ugly conflict of interest.
His divided allegiance directly compromises the people relying on him at Silph.
He helped endanger his own coworkers. A second job is no excuse.
That would make the people around him feel betrayed.
The coworkers trusted him with an ordinary working day.
The double role is less impressive than the damage it leaves behind.
An extra name on the pay slip does not divide the responsibility.
Conflicting access and incentives. A serious failure of trust.
He has brought a cruel voice through a familiar door.
Being trusted by people should mean more than another opportunity.
I wonder how many coworkers knew him before this happened.

contexts.subject: Jerry challenges us to navigate Silph's complicated interior.

SilphCo_2F_Text_JerryPostBattle.text: Can you solve the maze in here?\nIt's not easy, I tell you!$

replies.text: An office that requires maze skills has taken workplace confusion too literally.
A complex layout increases the value of a deliberate route record.
We can map it. No need to wander into every fight.
I would like a simple sign pointing to a simple staircase.
A confusing route is a good reason to pace the team carefully.
The architectural challenge has received a rather smug introduction.
An unreasonable amount of building between a person and the room they need.
Track state and position. Teleporters make casual intuition unreliable.
A corridor can hide its direction even when it is brightly lit.
The layout is impressive in precisely the way that makes visitors tired.
I wonder whether the regular staff still take wrong turns.

contexts.subject: The grunt identifies the diamond tiles as Silph teleporters.

SilphCo_2F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: Diamond-shaped tiles are teleport\nblocks.\pThey're transporters for this\nhigh-tech building.$

replies.text: A diamond-shaped shortcut with a rather uncertain destination. Step thoughtfully.
The tiles are transport devices, explaining the apparent discontinuities in the layout.
Remember where each one takes us. Useful does not mean simple.
It is unsettling when the next room is not physically beside the last one.
A little route note would save a lot of backtracking.
The floor has been given a supporting role in relocating the entire cast.
A small bright shape that makes distance briefly change its mind.
Built-in transporters! Fascinating, though the labeling needs work.
The room has little doors lying flat on the ground.
A clear explanation makes the floor much less mysterious.
I wonder whether each tile always leads to the same place.

contexts.subject: The grunt claims Silph will become associated with Team Rocket.

SilphCo_2F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: SILPH CO. will be associated with\nTEAM ROCKET!$

replies.text: That is a very polite word for threatening the people who work here.
A coerced takeover is not a voluntary association between equal parties.
The staff did not agree to this. He can stop dressing it up.
That sounds worse for how casually he says it.
A company is full of people who deserve a say in what happens to them.
The villainous proposal has borrowed the dullest possible business vocabulary.
An ugly act does not become mild when given an office-friendly name.
Consent is missing from this proposed integration. That matters.
A hand around a door handle can still be forcing its way inside.
He wants the name to sound respectable while the behavior stays cruel.
I wonder whether he has listened to a single employee's answer.

contexts.subject: The grunt tells us the Card Key opens Silph's doors.

SilphCo_3F_Text_GruntPostBattle.text: A hint? You can open doors with\na CARD KEY!$

replies.text: A very small answer to a building full of closed questions.
The Card Key is the relevant credential for the locked doors.
Find the key. Keep track of which route it opens.
At least the obstacle has a clear practical answer.
A useful lead before the team spends more energy searching blindly.
The reluctant informant introduces a crucial piece of office stationery.
A flat little thing deciding how large the building is allowed to be.
Access token identified. That explains the electronic locks.
One card can turn walls back into doorways.
A plain explanation is welcome, whatever his reason for giving it.
I wonder who was supposed to keep the key secure.

contexts.subject: Jose says Rocket promised to let him study Pokemon if he helped them.

SilphCo_3F_Text_JosePostBattle.text: Humph…\pTEAM ROCKET said that if I helped\nthem, they'd let me study POKéMON.$

replies.text: An interesting subject does not make the people offering access trustworthy.
A research opportunity does not justify aiding coercion or ignoring welfare.
He chose a chance to study over the safety of the people beside him.
I wish he had thought about what kind of studying those people would permit.
Curiosity needs care beside it, especially when the subject is alive.
The tempting offer has rather conspicuously omitted the moral cost of admission.
Knowledge gathered by cruelty is not made gentler by calling it curiosity.
Access is useful only within a sound method. Their method is already causing harm.
A door to understanding should not open by closing a cage.
Being offered something desirable does not erase what they asked him to do.
I wonder whether he ever asked what would happen to the Pokemon afterward.

contexts.subject: The grunt boasts that his boss has long wanted Silph.

SilphCo_4F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: Fwahahaha!\nMy BOSS has been after this place!$

replies.text: Wanting a place does not make its people something you get to take.
Prior ambition does not establish any legitimate claim to the company.
His boss wanted it. The staff wanted a safe workday. Their claim matters.
He sounds pleased about something the people here find terrifying.
An employer's dream is not more important than everyone else's safety.
An old desire is presented as though it were a deed of ownership.
Greed does not become history worth honoring just by lasting a long time.
Desired asset and authorized access are different states.
A long shadow still has no right to the room it falls across.
They have made wanting something sound like permission. It is not.
I wonder how much the staff knew of that interest before today.

contexts.subject: Rodney explains the electronic locks and their Card Key requirement.

SilphCo_4F_Text_RodneyPostBattle.text: The doors are electronically\nlocked.\pIt takes a CARD KEY to open the\ndoors here.$

replies.text: The doors are not being stubborn. They are being very specifically electronic.
The locks require the matching credential rather than physical force.
Find the Card Key. Do not waste the team's strength on the doors.
A clear explanation makes the maze feel a little less personal.
Knowing what we need saves a lot of unnecessary effort.
The building's refusal to admit us has a technical rather than dramatic cause.
The quietest barrier can still be a firm one.
Electronic authentication. Now the door behavior is less mysterious.
A little card can carry permission farther than a loud voice.
Useful detail, directly stated. Appreciated.
I wonder how the employees manage when someone misplaces a card.

contexts.subject: The grunt plans to report to the boss on the eleventh floor.

SilphCo_4F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: I better tell the BOSS on 11F!$

replies.text: A threat that accidentally includes an address. We should remember the useful part.
He identifies the boss's location while describing his intended report.
Eleventh floor. Keep ready; the warning may get there first.
It is unsettling knowing somebody could be waiting for us now.
A clear destination is useful, but not a reason to hurry the team.
The messenger supplies his destination with admirable generosity to the opposition.
A hostile voice has still managed to point the way.
Destination intel obtained. Expect possible increased alertness upstairs.
His hurried words have drawn a little line toward the top of the building.
He could have kept the floor number to himself. Fortunately, he did not.
I wonder whether the boss has already heard from the other floors.

contexts.subject: The grunt calls it unwise to oppose Team Rocket.

SilphCo_5F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: It's not smart to pick a fight with\nTEAM ROCKET!$

replies.text: Letting them carry on has its own fairly obvious disadvantages.
The statement offers intimidation rather than an argument about the conduct being opposed.
The people here need help. His warning does not change that.
He wants caution to mean doing nothing at all.
We can be careful and still refuse to leave people in danger.
The villain advises the audience that the whole plot would be easier without resistance.
A sensible concern for safety is being used to sell surrender.
Risk is real. So is the cost of leaving the problem untouched.
A dark road is still sometimes the road someone needs you to walk.
He has mistaken refusing to be frightened away for refusing to think.
I wonder whether that line has stopped many people before.

contexts.subject: Beau describes work on a ball intended to catch any Pokemon.

SilphCo_5F_Text_BeauPostBattle.text: We worked on the ultimate POKé\nBALL which would catch anything.$

replies.text: That is a very large promise to put inside a very small sphere.
A universal capture claim would represent exceptional technical capability and serious ethical choices.
Hope the people making it think hard about who gets to use it.
It is impressive and unsettling in the same breath.
A useful invention still needs people willing to ask who it could hurt.
The ultimate prop promises to remove the uncertainty from every encounter. A weighty claim.
A tool that never fails can make a careless intention much more dangerous.
Extraordinary design target. The failure modes extend beyond the mechanism itself.
A little closed room that could decide the next part of a life.
The work is impressive. I would like to hear the limits they set around it.
I wonder which question the researchers found hardest to answer.

contexts.subject: Dalton taunts us that the boss is still many floors above.

SilphCo_5F_Text_DaltonPostBattle.text: You're only on 5F.\nIt's a long way to my BOSS!$

replies.text: A tall building is not an argument. It is mostly stairs.
The remaining distance is practical information, even delivered as discouragement.
We will take the floors as they come. Watch the team's condition.
I would rather know how far it is than have to guess.
A long way is manageable with sensible pauses and supplies.
The obstacle's spokesman has reduced the threat to an elevation report.
The next floor is still only one floor away.
Remaining workload substantial. Pace resources rather than reacting to the taunt.
A high room is reached by small ordinary steps.
He has told us the scale of the problem. We do not have to borrow the attitude.
I wonder whether he ever takes the stairs himself.

contexts.subject: The grunt abruptly changes the subject to Koffing evolving into Weezing.

SilphCo_5F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: Which reminds me.\pKOFFING evolves into WEEZING!$

replies.text: An unexpected educational detour. The conversation has grown a second head.
The fact is relevant to Pokemon development, though oddly disconnected from his situation.
Useful fact. Does not excuse the work he is doing here.
It is a strange moment to start sharing something ordinary.
Knowing a partner's development is worthwhile in a much kinder setting than this.
The hostile encounter briefly becomes an unsolicited natural-history lesson.
A conversation trying to escape itself through a cloud of Pokemon trivia.
Correct topic, peculiar timing. No change to the immediate problem.
A small normal fact has wandered into a very abnormal day.
He sounds almost like an ordinary enthusiast for a moment.
I wonder what made that particular thought interrupt everything else.

contexts.subject: The grunt promises that his brothers will avenge him.

SilphCo_6F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: No matter!\nMy brothers will avenge me!$

replies.text: He has a surprisingly extensive family plan for losing battles.
The threat implies further coordinated hostility, whether the relationship is literal or organizational.
Keep alert. He is not the only hostile person here.
That makes it difficult to feel the encounter is really finished.
We should keep together and avoid giving them an easy opening.
The defeated speaker refers the sequel to a larger ensemble.
An unpleasant promise with several possible footsteps attached.
Potential reinforcement threat. Do not assume the route is clear.
One voice gone quiet may still have called another one closer.
He can stop trying to make his embarrassment everyone else's problem.
I wonder whether his brothers are as eager for the fight as he says.

contexts.subject: Taylor gives an odd geographic answer about Silph's Tiksi branch.

replies.text: That branch sounds like quite a commute from this office.
He offers a specific location claim, but it does not explain his choices here.
A branch office is not the pressing issue. The people here need safety.
That is a strange bit of ordinary company knowledge to hear now.
The company has people far away who may have no idea what is happening here.
The defeated employee diverts us into a distant corporate footnote.
A faraway place can feel unreal while the danger is in the next corridor.
Location detail noted, though its immediate usefulness is limited.
The building holds names of places beyond the windows we can see.
He has found a very distant subject to avoid the nearby problem.
I wonder whether anyone from this office has actually worked there.

contexts.subject: The grunt says standing for justice betrays the bad guys.

SilphCo_6F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: If you stand for justice, you\nbetray us bad guys!$

replies.text: That is a remarkably honest job description. Terrible argument, excellent labeling.
Opposing harmful conduct is not a betrayal of any legitimate obligation to him.
Fine. The bad guys can manage their disappointment.
He says it as if we had ever agreed to help them.
The people being hurt deserve more consideration than the people complaining about being stopped.
The villain has correctly identified his side and completely misunderstood our duties to it.
A very clear moral map, kindly supplied by the person standing on the wrong side.
No contractual dependency on the bad guys detected. Proceed.
A shadow is offended that someone brought a light.
It is considerate of him to make the disagreement that easy to understand.
I wonder whether he hears how strange that complaint sounds aloud.

contexts.subject: The grunt taunts our difficulty navigating toward the boss.

SilphCo_7F_Text_Grunt3PostBattle.text: You won't find my BOSS by just\nscurrying around!$

replies.text: Scurrying? I prefer exploratory walking with an occasionally wrong turn.
Random movement is inefficient. His taunt still points toward using a deliberate route.
Map the path. Do not let him hurry us into a mistake.
The layout is confusing enough without someone enjoying the confusion.
A calm plan saves more energy than trying to look certain.
The maze's heckler is less useful than a single well-placed arrow.
Being lost is unpleasant without a commentator.
Track the route and teleporter destinations. Better than reacting to the insult.
The way through is still there, however much he laughs at the searching.
He can keep the commentary. We need clear directions.
I wonder whether he knows the route or merely knows how to mock visitors.

contexts.subject: Joshua acknowledges our skill while expressing surprise at our age.

SilphCo_7F_Text_JoshuaPostBattle.text: Despite your age, you are a\nskilled TRAINER!$

replies.text: The team has supplied enough evidence to get past his first impression.
The observed performance is a better estimate than age-based expectation.
We trained for it. Age did not choose the moves.
It is nice to hear the skill recognized, even with the surprised little qualifier.
Young trainers still put real time and care into their teams.
The critic revises his forecast after consulting the actual performance.
A calendar has lost another argument with a determined person.
Model updated with evidence. Good, though the original shortcut was weak.
A small traveler can carry a long stretch of careful work.
He could have simply said skilled. The rest was his assumption.
I wonder how often he has underestimated someone that way.

contexts.subject: The grunt dismisses losing and promises retaliation from his brothers.

SilphCo_7F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: Doesn't matter.\nMy brothers will repay the favor!$

replies.text: If it does not matter, he has chosen an unusually threatening way to relax about it.
The dismissal conflicts with the promised retaliation. Continued hostility is the relevant fact.
Watch for the others. We are not finished just because he is.
I would rather not stand here while he imagines a second attack.
Keep the group together and the route in mind.
A supposedly insignificant defeat receives an ambitiously staffed revenge sequel.
Indifference is wearing a remarkably angry face.
Local win does not remove network risk. Keep checking the next corridor.
One stopped voice is pointing toward several more.
He is trying to make the threat do what his battle could not.
I wonder whether the others know they have been volunteered for this.

contexts.subject: The grunt urges us to leave before his boss becomes angry.

SilphCo_7F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: Go on home before my BOSS gets\nticked off!$

replies.text: The boss's mood is not a good regional safety system.
The warning implies danger without offering any justification for the operation.
People here are already in danger. We are not leaving them because he is annoyed.
It is unsettling how often the staff and grunts talk about that man's anger.
A boss who makes everyone afraid is part of the problem.
The local threat delegates its dramatic authority to someone supposedly more irritable upstairs.
An angry man is not a reason to accept an ugly situation forever.
Known hostile authority. Prepare carefully rather than treating the mood as a rule.
A distant temper should not decide how much safety everyone else gets.
He thinks fear of the boss will explain everything. It explains quite enough.
I wonder whether he is more afraid for us or for himself.

contexts.subject: The rival boasts that Pokedex study will help him defeat the League, then departs.

SilphCo_7F_Text_RivalPostBattle.text:
Well, {PLAYER}!
I'm moving on up and ahead!\pBy checking my POKéDEX, I'm
starting to see what's strong and\lhow they evolve!\pAm I a genius or what?\pI'm going to the POKéMON LEAGUE to
boot out the ELITE FOUR.\pI'll become the world's most
powerful TRAINER!\p{PLAYER}, well, good luck to you!
Don't sweat it!\lSmell ya!$

replies.text: Useful research, enormous confidence, and somehow still room for a parting jab.
Using the Pokedex to study capabilities and evolution is genuinely sensible preparation.
He can chase the League. We still have people in this building to help.
I wish he had noticed the frightened staff as clearly as his own next goal.
Learning is good. The current situation deserves some attention too.
The rival's future triumph receives an advance review written by the rival himself.
A busy ambition can make a person strangely inattentive to the room around them.
Research-informed planning is useful. Self-assigned genius rating is less measurable.
His eyes keep traveling toward a far door while nearby ones remain in trouble.
The practical part is worth hearing beneath the grand presentation.
I wonder whether anyone here will remember him as anything besides in a hurry.

contexts.subject: The grunt threatens to call for backup unless we retreat.

SilphCo_8F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: If you don't turn back…\nI'll call for backup!$

replies.text: He has found the part of the plan labeled ask someone else.
Potential reinforcement is a practical risk even when used as intimidation.
Keep ready. Do not stand around waiting for him to prove it.
That makes the quiet corridor feel less empty.
We should avoid leaving anyone exposed while the alert spreads.
The defeated opponent attempts to enlarge the cast by telephone.
A threat is not less unpleasant for arriving with company.
Escalation possible. Reassess route and remaining resources.
One call can put more sharp footsteps into the hallway.
He wants the warning to make the decision for us. We can still think carefully.
I wonder how close the nearest backup is.

contexts.subject: Parker asks what we think of Silph's maze-like interior.

SilphCo_8F_Text_ParkerPostBattle.text: So, what do you think of SILPH\nBUILDING's maze?$

replies.text: A strong case for putting the stairs somewhere less philosophical.
The layout is technically interesting but creates substantial navigation overhead.
Bad place to be lost during an emergency. That is my review.
I would like it more if fewer people were frightened inside it.
A useful building should make getting help easier, not harder.
An architectural critic requests a review from a captive research sample.
A bright labyrinth still feels like a labyrinth when you need the door.
Fascinating mechanism, poor wayfinding. Both can be true.
Many doors, not enough clear directions between them.
It has presence. It could use a kinder relationship with its visitors.
I wonder whether he helped design it or simply enjoys watching people navigate it.

contexts.subject: The grunt leaves further fighting to his brothers.

SilphCo_8F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: I'll leave you up to my brothers.$

replies.text: The next encounter has been assigned to somebody else's calendar.
His withdrawal does not imply that the broader threat has ended.
Fine. Watch the route for the next one.
I wish he sounded more interested in stopping than passing the danger along.
The team still needs a steady pace through the remaining floors.
The recurring villain role is handed down to the next available performer.
An unpleasant shift change, without any improvement in the job.
Local unit disengaging. Network still active.
A rough voice leaves the door open for another rough one.
He seems comfortable making other people finish the fight.
I wonder how much choice his brothers get in that arrangement.

contexts.subject: The grunt imagines how his life might differ if he began training at our age.

SilphCo_9F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: If I had started as a TRAINER at\nyour age…$

replies.text: A different start might have helped. A different next choice is still available.
The counterfactual is uncertain. His present conduct remains something he can change.
He can start making better choices now. The past is not an instruction.
That sounds almost like regret, before the sentence disappears.
It is not too late to care for Pokemon without using them to frighten people.
A villain briefly glimpses an unwritten earlier chapter and forgets to finish the line.
A missed beginning need not make every later door false.
Initial conditions matter, but they do not fix every future action.
An old path cannot be walked again. The next step is still under his own feet.
I hope he lets that thought change something rather than simply excuse it.
I wonder what he wanted to be before ending up here.

contexts.subject: Ed acknowledges that exploiting type weaknesses is effective.

SilphCo_9F_Text_EdPostBattle.text: Exploiting weak spots does work.\nThink about type advantages.$

replies.text: The matchup has delivered its lesson in very direct language.
Type relationships are a substantial tactical variable, as the result demonstrates.
Know the opponent. Raw strength is not the whole plan.
A clear lesson is something useful to take from a difficult match.
Good planning can save the team from unnecessary strain.
The defeated critic confirms the technique that just complicated his afternoon.
A small weakness can matter more than an imposing outline.
Correctly matched tool, improved result. Basic and effective.
A strong door can still have a small latch.
He has noticed something specific instead of reaching for an excuse.
I wonder what he will change in his own team's coverage.

contexts.subject: The grunt promises revenge from his brothers.

replies.text: Another family reunion I would rather miss.
He is invoking further hostility rather than accepting the encounter as finished.
Stay alert. No reason to give his friends an easy chance.
I wish the next corridor could simply be a corridor.
Keep the team close and the way back clear.
The revenge department appears to employ a great many relatives.
A tired threat, still capable of making the room less comfortable.
Potential linked threat remains. Check the next area carefully.
An angry voice points toward footsteps we cannot hear yet.
He is trying to make losing sound like an appointment we cannot cancel.
I wonder whether any of his brothers want a quieter life than this.

contexts.subject: The grunt tells us the boardroom is one floor above.

SilphCo_10F_Text_GruntPostBattle.text: Nice try, but the boardroom is up\none more floor.$

replies.text: One floor left to the right office. The directions are finally getting shorter.
A precise nearby destination helps narrow the remaining route.
Check the team, then go up prepared.
It is a little reassuring to know the search is not endless.
A short pause here could help before a difficult next room.
The reluctant guide places the next scene exactly one level overhead.
The journey's height has become a manageable number.
Destination one level up. Final readiness check is worthwhile.
The next ceiling is nearly the last one between us and an answer.
Useful directions, despite the tone they arrived in.
I wonder whether the people upstairs know help is this close.

contexts.subject: Travis urges us to leave after beating him.

SilphCo_10F_Text_TravisPostBattle.text: Are you satisfied with beating me?\nThen go on home!$

replies.text: This was never a sightseeing tour of his personal defeat. There are people to help.
He frames the visit as personal competition, ignoring the broader emergency.
We are not here just for him. Keep moving toward the staff who need help.
He sounds eager to make the whole situation smaller than it is.
Leaving now would not make the frightened people here safe.
A supporting antagonist attempts to declare himself the conclusion of the entire plot.
His embarrassment is not the only thing happening in this building.
Local obstacle cleared. Main objective remains unresolved.
One closed conversation does not mean the way ahead has ended.
He can finish his part without deciding ours is over.
I wonder whether he ever considers the people outside his own room.

contexts.subject: Giovanni retreats, condemns our interference, and claims all Pokemon exist for Team Rocket.

SilphCo_11F_Text_GiovanniPostBattle.text: Blast it all!\nYou ruined our plans for SILPH!\pBut, TEAM ROCKET will never fall!\p{PLAYER}! Never forget that all\nPOKéMON exist for TEAM ROCKET!\pI must go, but I shall return!$

replies.text: The Pokemon were not consulted about that ridiculous claim. They have lives beyond him.
He asserts ownership without any legitimate basis and promises continued hostility.
They do not exist for him. Keep ready until he is out of here.
I am glad he is leaving. The way he talks about living things is chilling.
No plan of his matters more than the care those partners deserve.
The retreating tyrant attempts to leave an entire world under his name in the final sentence.
A man can claim the sun too. It does not make the light his property.
The premise is false. A stronger declaration cannot repair it.
A closed hand imagines everything was made to fit inside it.
He has confused having power with being entitled to everyone else's lives.
I wonder whether he can imagine a Pokemon choosing something he did not order.

contexts.subject: The grunt asks whether we want to see his boss.

SilphCo_11F_Text_Grunt2PostBattle.text: So, you want to see my BOSS?$

replies.text: After this many floors, the direction of our interest seems fairly well established.
He recognizes the objective at last, though he has supplied no new detail.
Yes. The staff need this finished. No more stalling.
I would like the frightening part of this building to end.
The people here deserve an ordinary safe room again.
The final gatekeeper asks the question answered by the whole preceding staircase.
A very late opportunity for a remarkably obvious introduction.
Objective confirmed. Next step should be a clear route, not another query.
The name at the end of the corridor has been spoken enough.
He seems to have run out of more elaborate objections.
I wonder whether he expected anyone to come this far.

contexts.subject: The grunt warns that his boss favors tough Pokemon.

SilphCo_11F_Text_Grunt1PostBattle.text: Watch your step…\nMy BOSS likes his POKéMON tough!$

replies.text: A tough team still needs a decent person deciding what to ask of it.
Preference for strong Pokemon does not identify their exact capabilities or welfare.
We will be ready. His partners are not the ones choosing the cruelty.
I worry more about what he asks them to endure than how intimidating they look.
The stronger partner still deserves ordinary care.
The ominous introduction confuses physical power with any reason for trust.
A strong creature can still be trapped in a small-minded person's plan.
High expected capability. Prepare without assuming a particular composition.
Even a hard shell can carry something that needs gentleness.
A preference for tough partners tells us very little about being a good trainer.
I wonder what he values in them when they are not winning for him.

contexts.subject: A girl reports obtaining Cut from the neighbor and teaching her Pokemon.

RustboroCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_HMCut.text: The man next door gave me an HM!\pI used it to teach my POKéMON how to\nCUT down skinny trees.$

replies.text: A useful neighbor can turn a blocked path into a rather short errand.
Her experience gives us a specific local source for the HM.
Next door. Easy enough to ask about it ourselves.
I like hearing somebody pleased with a new thing they learned together.
I'd ask what path she finally managed to open.
A useful neighbor and a remarkably short trip. I could become enthusiastic about this sort of errand.
A neighborhood service specializing in inconvenient vegetation.
We should learn the conditions for using it before trying it outside.
A small doorway nearby may lead to several more distant openings.
She sounds pleased to pass the useful tip along.
I'd ask which partner she taught and how it took to the task.

contexts.subject: A boy wonders about differences between male and female Pokemon.

RustboroCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_MaleA.text: Just like people, there are male and\nfemale POKéMON.\pBut no one seems to have any idea how\nthey're different.$

replies.text: That's a question worth asking carefully instead of filling the gaps with guesses.
Differences vary by species. One general assumption won't describe them all.
Get to know the individual partner. A category won't tell us everything.
I like that there is still something to learn about familiar Pokemon.
I'd start by asking someone who has raised that particular species.
A grand question for a waiting room. We may need more than the nearest chair to answer it.
An excellent opportunity to admit that certainty would be premature.
We can compare actual observations instead of assuming a visible rule.
Two names for a distinction do not reveal every life inside them.
Curiosity is good when it leaves room for individuals to surprise us.
I'd ask what difference first made him wonder.

contexts.subject: Rydel cannot exchange the bicycle until the player brings it from storage.

MauvilleCity_BikeShop_Text_OhYourBikeIsI.text:
Oh? What happened to that BIKE
I gave you?\pOh, I get it, you stored it using your PC.\pWell, take it out of PC storage,
and I'll be happy to exchange it!\pMay the wind always be at your back
on your adventure!$

replies.text: We brought the wish to exchange a bike and forgot the bike-shaped part.
The exchange requires the existing bicycle to be physically available.
Get the bike, then come back. Straightforward fix.
I'm glad he explained it without making the mistake feel enormous.
An errand is easier when you bring the thing the errand is about.
Rydel is admirably patient with a bicycle exchange to which we have brought no bicycle.
A bicycle transaction impeded by a total absence of bicycles on our side.
We should retrieve the original before asking for the replacement.
A journey can wait while we return for what we meant to carry.
His friendly farewell leaves room for us to return less forgetful.
I'd check the bag before making the trip back again.

contexts.subject: The old man rewards interest in herbal medicine with Charcoal; bag-full failure replaces the gift source.

LavaridgeTown_HerbShop_Text_YouveComeToL.text: You've come to look at herbal medicine\nin LAVARIDGE?\pThat's rather commendable.\pI like you! Take this!$

replies.text: He likes a curious visitor enough to share something useful.
Interest in his subject prompted a tangible expression of approval.
Kind of him. Let's remember who gave it to us.
It's nice when asking about someone's interest brightens the whole meeting.
I'd hear him out before deciding what to do with the gift.
He rewards curiosity very promptly. I should remember to ask the next question before admiring the gift.
An agreeable exchange rate between attention and charcoal.
We should learn its use so the gift doesn't become unexplained luggage.
A simple question can open a generous hand.
He seems pleased to share the interest as much as the object.
I'd ask what first drew him to herbal medicine.

contexts.subject: The museum attendant welcomes the visitor after admission or during an ordinary greeting.

replies.text: Permission to be curious in a room full of things ready for it.
The invitation is to observe and learn at our own pace.
Good. Let's look around without getting in anybody's way.
I like an unhurried welcome before a place asks for our attention.
We can take our time with the exhibits that interest us most.
A welcome with room to wander afterward. The attendant has excellent instincts about visitors.
An official invitation to browse quietly. Excellent.
I'd start with the display that explains what the instruments are measuring.
A little room can open onto an ocean of questions.
The greeting makes looking around feel welcome instead of intrusive.
I'd ask which exhibit the staff member enjoys showing visitors.

contexts.subject: The woman recognizes affection and gives a Soothe Bell when the bag permits.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Pokemo.text: Your POKéMON really adores you.\pFor you, a most compassionate\nTRAINER, a gift from the FAN CLUB!$

replies.text: Our partner's fondness was noticed, and now there's a little bell to remember it by.
She is responding to observed affection rather than a claimed training record.
Good to know the partner feels that way. The gift is a bonus.
I like praise that notices the quiet parts of being together.
The ordinary care has become visible to someone else.
The Pokemon has given us an excellent reference. I shall try to remain worthy of the recommendation.
A favorable review with an unexpectedly musical enclosure.
We can appreciate the item while keeping the routine that earned the compliment.
A little sound can accompany something that was already warm.
The best part is knowing the partner is happy beside us.
I'd thank her for seeing that, as well as for the bell.

contexts.subject: Amid the center crisis, staff report the rocket launch is still imminent.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Haywire.text: I know that things are a little\nhaywire right now, but…\pThe rocket's launch is imminent!$

replies.text: The launch clock is continuing while the rest of the room has developed a very bad day.
The launch status and the security situation are distinct but interacting concerns.
Check that proceeding is safe. A schedule doesn't outrank the people here.
It must be difficult to concentrate with all this happening around them.
I'd want the crew to have enough calm and support for those final checks.
The rocket is punctual. I wish the criminals had chosen a less inconvenient day to be criminals.
A launch and a crisis sharing a timetable. Unhelpful coordination.
They should reassess the risk rather than continue only because the clock says so.
A bright wish needs careful hands, especially when the room is shaking.
I hope the staff can say stop if something no longer feels safe.
I'd ask where visitors should wait so the team has space to work.

contexts.subject: Despite the crisis, staff confirm the numbered rocket launch succeeded safely.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Haywire.text: I know that things are a little\nhaywire right now, but…\pThe rocket launched safely!\nThat's successful launch no. {STR_VAR_1}!$

replies.text: One thing reached the sky safely in the middle of all this trouble. That's worth a breath.
A safe launch is confirmed even though the facility has other unresolved problems.
Good work. Now keep the staff and the rest of the center safe too.
That must be a difficult sort of relief, with the room still unsettled.
The crew deserves to know that careful work mattered today.
A safe launch in the middle of this mess. Someone here deserves a quiet chair and an extravagant compliment.
A successful departure despite an excessively eventful ground floor.
They can preserve the result and still review how the disruption affected procedures.
A small clear light can remain true inside a troubled day.
I'd make room for their relief without pretending everything else is settled.
I'd ask the team about it when they finally have a calm moment afterward.

contexts.subject: The daily lottery draw is already used and the clerk asks the player to return tomorrow.

replies.text: Today's numbers have done their day's work. Tomorrow can have a turn later.
The daily opportunity is exhausted. Repeating the request won't alter the result.
We're done for today. Plenty else to do.
A clear limit makes it easier to stop wondering about one more try.
We can let a small part of the day stay small.
Tomorrow remains surprisingly immune to being asked for sooner. Best let the clerk get on with the afternoon.
The clerk has assigned the next attempt to time itself. Sensible.
We should note the interval rather than make the same check repeatedly.
A little chance can wait beside the next sunrise.
No need to build the whole day around a possible prize.
I'd take the reminder and go enjoy the rest of the store.

contexts.subject: The player declines the lottery draw and receives a polite farewell.

replies.text: No ticket today. Our afternoon can remain gloriously unnumbered.
No draw was taken. The visit ended without a result to interpret.
Fine choice. We can keep moving.
It's nice when choosing not to take part stays simple.
A little chance doesn't have to be part of every shopping trip.
I enjoy a little suspense. I also enjoy deciding I have had quite enough suspense without taking any.
An uneventful outcome requiring no investigation. Lovely.
We can use the visit for the things we actually came to do.
An unopened possibility can remain unopened.
The clerk kept the welcome after the answer became no.
I'd say thanks and leave room for the next visitor.

contexts.subject: The lottery visit ends after a completed draw; this shared farewell does not distinguish wins from misses.

replies.text: The numbers have had their moment. We can let the rest of the day begin again.
The brief suspense is over. We can return our attention to the rest of the outing.
Done here. Let's move on without chasing the moment.
I like having a clear end to a little suspense.
A lottery can be one small stop instead of the whole outing.
The suspense has ended, and the rest of the afternoon is still ours. A pleasantly generous arrangement.
A tidy closing line after an unusually numerical conversation.
Let's check our shopping list before choosing another floor to visit.
A chance has passed through the day and left the road continuing.
Whatever the result, we can keep the rest of the visit pleasant.
I'd give the next person room at the counter.

contexts.subject: A lottery prize is held because the player lacks bag space.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_1F_Text_NoR.text: Oh?\nYou seem to have no room for this.\pPlease make room in your BAG and\nlet me know.$

replies.text: The prize has our name on it, but the bag hasn't found a little room for that name.
The entitlement is recorded; the item has not yet transferred.
Make space, then collect it. No need to rush or buy another ticket.
It's reassuring that the prize won't vanish just because the bag is awkward.
A tidy pocket can be a surprisingly useful part of good fortune.
Good fortune has encountered bad packing. A deeply unheroic obstacle, but at least we know how to fix it.
A winning number has encountered an unwinnably full pocket.
We should free capacity before returning to collect the held item.
Something promised can remain safe while a place is made for it.
The clerk made the next step clear without making the delay embarrassing.
I'd ask where to collect it after sorting our supplies.

contexts.subject: A previously held lottery prize is delivered; a repeated storage failure replaces this source.

LilycoveCity_DepartmentStore_1F_Text_Pri.text: {PLAYER}?\nYes, I've been expecting you.\pThis is the prize we've been holding\nfor you.$

replies.text: A little piece of earlier good luck has finally found its way into our hands.
The recorded prize is now collected after the earlier capacity problem.
Good. We followed up instead of leaving it forgotten.
It's nice to be remembered when you return for something.
The clerk kept the promise while we dealt with the practical part.
The clerk remembered us and the prize. I appreciate competence most when it quietly makes my day easier.
An unresolved prize has ceased being administrative history.
We should check the received item and keep the bag organized afterward.
A small postponed kindness has reached the day it was waiting for.
I appreciate how ordinary and welcoming the handoff feels.
I'd make sure to thank the clerk for holding it safely.

contexts.subject: The curator awards the Glass Ornament for completing the collection; no-room branch replaces this source.

LilycoveCity_LilycoveMuseum_2F_Text_Toke.text: This is merely a token of my gratitude.$

replies.text: A little bright thank-you for helping put so much life on the walls.
The ornament acknowledges a completed contribution to the public collection.
Kind of him. Give it a safe place when we get home.
I think his happiness about the paintings is the part I'd remember most.
A thoughtful reward can keep a shared accomplishment close.
The curator has excellent taste in thank-yous. We should find somewhere that does not invite a tragic tumble.
A fragile award for a fortunately less fragile achievement.
We should place it somewhere steady, away from a busy edge.
A bright object can hold the memory of a room coming alive.
It will look nicest where we can see it without having to fuss over it.
I'd tell the artist and the team how happy the curator sounded.

contexts.subject: A resident romantically imagines difficult travel, including homesickness.

PetalburgCity_House1_Text_GoOnAdventure.text:
Sigh…\pI wish I could go on an adventure
with some POKéMON…\pCrawl through some damp grass…
Climb rocky, rugged mountains…\pCross the raging seas…
Wander about in dark caves…\pAnd, sometimes, even get a little
homesick…\pIt must be fabulous to travel!$

replies.text: Even the homesick bit made the imaginary itinerary. That's a thoroughly imagined adventure.
They recognize discomfort as part of travel, though experiencing it may feel different.
Good dream. Pack for the damp grass, not only the grand view.
I like that wanting to leave doesn't mean forgetting what home feels like.
A cold night becomes more manageable when you actually prepared a warm meal.
They have even romanticized damp socks. I admire the enthusiasm and recommend a short trial journey.
A romantic appreciation of discomfort best tested in small doses.
I'd start with a short trip and learn what the equipment needs to handle.
A far road can be dear even before we learn the weight of its weather.
The dream can stay lovely while becoming a little more practical.
I'd ask which place they would choose for the first real outing.

contexts.subject: An older resident remembers roaming the seas and mountains in youth.

PetalburgCity_House1_Text_TravelingIsWon.text: Traveling is wonderful!\pWhen I was young, I roamed the seas\nand the mountains!$

replies.text: Some of those journeys are still taking a happy little walk through their voice.
Remembered travel often preserves particular encounters more strongly than distances.
Sounds like they have stories worth sitting down for.
I wonder which quiet moment stayed after the difficult miles faded.
I'd ask about the meal that tasted best after a long day.
Someone should ask for the long version. A person who smiles like that at an old trip has earned a listener.
A veteran traveler has found an excellent way to cross mountains without standing up.
I'd ask what their equipment was like when they first went out.
A far landscape can remain near inside a familiar voice.
It's lovely when remembering doesn't become a demand that everyone travel the same way.
I'd ask which place they would most like to see again.

contexts.subject: A former challenger remembers Norman strength and dedication.

PetalburgCity_House2_Text_BattledNormanO.text: I battled NORMAN once, but, whew,\nhe was way too strong.\pHow would I put it?\pI just got the feeling that he\nlives for POKéMON.$

replies.text: Norman apparently made his point without needing the challenger to remember every move.
The experience left an impression of sustained commitment rather than only power.
Worth learning from. Dedication shows in the decisions.
It sounds like losing still left them with something to admire.
I'd be curious about the routine behind that much confidence.
Norman seems to make an impression that survives the loss. An irritatingly effective kind of opponent.
A man who lives for Pokemon sounds inconvenient to challenge before lunch.
I'd ask what specific choice made the dedication so obvious.
A practiced life can leave its shape in a single encounter.
They saw something about the person behind the strong team.
I'd ask what they changed in their own training after that match.

contexts.subject: A resident connects Norman new Gym role with his family moving from far away.

PetalburgCity_House2_Text_NormanBecameGy.text: NORMAN became our town's new\nGYM LEADER.\pI think he called his family over from\nsomewhere far away.$

replies.text: A new Gym Leader means a new home for more people than the badge case suggests.
A professional move can reshape the daily lives of an entire household.
Hope the family gets time to settle as well as the Leader does.
A long move can make ordinary introductions feel surprisingly important.
Someone should show them the good place to buy dinner before praising the new Gym.
The new Leader has a family to settle, too. The town should offer directions to groceries as well as the Gym.
A new job, a new town, and presumably several boxes that refuse to unpack themselves.
A family's practical needs are part of making that transition work.
One person's new door can move a whole home's horizon.
I'd welcome the family as people, not only as extensions of the job.
I'd ask whether anybody has helped them get to know the neighborhood.

contexts.subject: A shopper recommends Repel when traveling quickly.

PetalburgCity_Mart_Text_RepelIsUseful.text: Do you use REPEL?\nIt keeps POKéMON away, so it's\luseful when you're in a hurry.$

replies.text: Sometimes we want new introductions. Sometimes we want to reach the next town before dinner.
Avoiding incidental encounters can make a route's travel time more predictable.
Useful when we're in a hurry. Still watch the route.
An uninterrupted walk can be nice when everybody needs a quiet stretch.
I'd save it for the days when arriving matters more than exploring.
I am delighted to learn that reaching a destination need not require greeting every creature along the way.
A little bottle of fewer interruptions. Persuasive.
We should use it for a specific stretch rather than spray without a plan.
Passing quietly can be a choice without being a rejection of the place.
It's fine to decide what kind of outing we have energy for.
I'd ask which part of the route usually slows that shopper down.

contexts.subject: A shopper advises carrying Antidotes rather than leaving a Pokemon poisoned while walking.

PetalburgCity_Mart_Text_TakeSomeAntidote.text: Do you have any ANTIDOTES with\nyou?\pIf you walk around with a poisoned\nPOKéMON, it will lose HP until it faints.\lTake some ANTIDOTES with you.$

replies.text: A partner shouldn't have to carry poison along with the rest of the trip.
An unresolved status can continue causing harm after the encounter ends.
Treat it promptly. Don't ask the partner to walk it off.
I wouldn't want them trying to keep up while feeling worse with every step.
Keeping the right cure handy is a simple bit of care.
The argument for packing Antidotes is persuasive enough that I would rather not arrange a demonstration.
An excellent product recommendation supported by an unpleasantly convincing reason.
We should check status after an encounter, not only remaining HP.
A journey should not ask an injured creature to suffer silently beside it.
Good advice notices what the partner feels after the excitement ends.
I'd check our supply before heading back into the grass.

contexts.subject: A shopper emphasizes care for Pokemon who are presently weak.

PetalburgCity_Mart_Text_WeakWillGrowStro.text: Even if a POKéMON is weak now,\nit will grow stronger.\pThe most important thing is love!\nLove for your POKéMON!$

replies.text: Small strength is still strength with somewhere to grow.
Present ability is not a fixed limit on future development.
Care for them and train at a pace they can handle.
It's good to hear somebody speak kindly about the beginning.
Affection needs practical shape: food, rest, patience, and sensible practice.
Nobody begins impressively. It is helpful when people remember that before addressing a beginner.
An encouraging refusal to treat a beginner as a failed expert.
We should choose challenges that build confidence rather than overwhelm.
A little shoot needs tending before anyone asks it for shade.
Loving them also means noticing who they are, not only what they might become.
I'd ask about a partner that surprised this shopper as it grew.

contexts.subject: A visitor explains type strengths and weaknesses.

PetalburgCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Many.text: There are many types of POKéMON.\pAll types have their strengths and\nweaknesses against other types.\pDepending on the types of POKéMON,\na battle could be easy or hard.$

replies.text: Even a very strong partner can meet a problem that wants a different answer.
Matchup effects change the value of otherwise similar moves and stats.
Learn the matchups. Have another option ready.
I like knowing there is a reason a battle suddenly feels harder.
Sharing the work between different partners makes a lot of sense.
A formidable partner is excellent. A formidable partner with a second plan is considerably less exhausting.
An excellent system for making confidence occasionally inconvenient.
We should check both types before assuming a single advantage settles it.
A strength can meet its boundary without becoming worthless.
No one partner needs to be the best answer to everything.
I'd ask which matchup first caught the visitor by surprise.

contexts.subject: A visitor observed an Oran Berry restoring Pokemon HP.

PetalburgCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Oran.text: When my POKéMON ate an\nORAN BERRY, it regained HP!$

replies.text: A Berry with a helpful second job after being a Berry.
A consumed held Berry can provide recovery without a separate Trainer action.
Useful little backup. Don't rely on one to solve every injury.
It's nice when a partner has a little help ready before it needs to ask.
A useful snack is a wonderful invention the tree already worked out.
A snack that helps at the right moment. I respect an item with the courtesy to make itself useful.
A snack with measurable benefits. Delightfully direct.
We should know when it activates and replace it after use.
A small fruit can carry a moment of relief.
A caring little detail, especially if the Trainer remembers to prepare another.
I'd ask which Pokemon tried it and what its first reaction was.

contexts.subject: A visitor marvels at the Pokemon Storage System inventor.

PetalburgCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_PCSt.text: That PC-based POKéMON Storage\nSystem…\pWhoever made it must be some kind\nof a scientific wizard!$

replies.text: A scientific wizard is a very good title for making something this useful.
The system's convenience hides a substantial amount of design work.
Good work deserves recognition, even when we don't know the maker yet.
It's nice when someone wonders about the person behind an everyday thing.
A useful service can make a long journey easier in ways you stop noticing.
Scientific wizard seems a reasonable compliment. I trust the actual inventor receives a little time off, too.
A wizard whose spell probably involved a remarkable quantity of testing.
I'd love to know which problems they had to solve before it felt so simple.
A quiet machine can carry the trace of many patient days.
Convenience is worth appreciating when somebody worked hard to make it possible.
I'd ask what part first made the visitor stop and marvel.

contexts.subject: A visitor recommends checking the chosen starter own types and experimenting with moves.

PetalburgCity_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Star.text: Your starter has its own strengths\nand weaknesses, too.\pCheck its types on the SUMMARY\nscreen and try different moves!$

replies.text: Our first partner gets to be itself, rather than whatever the first lesson expected.
The individual starter's actual typing is more informative than a generic assumption.
Know the partner we've got. Build from there.
I like being told to learn this particular Pokemon instead of memorize a ready-made story.
Trying a few suitable moves can teach us what feels comfortable together.
I approve of advice that begins by noticing which Pokemon is actually standing beside us.
A useful reminder to inspect the actual creature before applying the familiar theory.
We can compare its types and available moves before choosing how to train.
A first meeting can open a path nobody else would take in quite the same way.
The best beginning is paying attention to the partner beside us.
I'd ask which move the starter seems most confident using so far.

contexts.subject: Wally father thanks the player and explains the move to relatives for his health.

PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_ThanksFor.text:
You're…
Ah, you must be {PLAYER}{KUN}, right?\pThank you for playing with WALLY a
little while ago.\pHe's been frail and sickly ever
since he was a baby.\pWe've sent him to stay with my relatives
in VERDANTURF TOWN for a while.\pThe air is a lot cleaner there
than it is here.\pWhat's that? Where's WALLY?
He's already left, our WALLY.\pI wonder where he could have
gotten by now?$

replies.text: A short outing with Wally meant a lot more to this house than we could see.
His parents are weighing a familiar history of illness against a promising change.
Glad we could help. We should give them clear news when we have it.
He sounds grateful and worried in the same breath.
A happy first Pokemon doesn't make the family stop worrying overnight.
A first catch can be a very large event to the family waiting at home. We should remember that.
A parent's gratitude tends to arrive carrying several unspoken questions.
Reliable contact would help them adjust to him being away.
Hope can move into a home without immediately sending fear away.
I'd listen to the concern without reducing Wally to being frail.
I'd ask what kind of updates would help them feel closer to his trip.

contexts.subject: Wally father quietly wonders how his absent son is doing.

PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_WonderHow.text: I wonder how our WALLY is doing?$

replies.text: A short question that probably visits him many times a day.
Uncertainty becomes tiring when someone important is out of contact.
If we hear something solid, we should pass it along.
I know how a familiar room can feel full of someone who isn't there.
A little message could mean more to him than the sender realizes.
I suspect he has asked that question while doing nearly everything else today. A message would be a kindness.
Distance is especially rude when it refuses to provide updates.
A regular check-in would do more than repeated reassurance without new information.
A far road can echo inside a quiet house.
He doesn't need a grand report, just something real.
I'd ask when he last heard directly from Wally.

contexts.subject: Wally father looks forward to his son expected return.

PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_WallyIsCo.text: WALLY's coming home soon.\nI'm looking forward to that.$

replies.text: Soon is a lovely word when somebody you miss is inside it.
An expected return gives the waiting a more definite shape.
Good. Wally will have a lot to tell them.
I imagine the house already feels different just from knowing that.
I'd ask what meal he wants ready for the homecoming.
His son coming home is clearly the event he most wants to attend. Some priorities are beautifully straightforward.
An approaching end to the parent's least favorite pastime: waiting.
I'd confirm the plan so they know when to expect him.
A doorway can seem warmer before anyone steps through it.
He sounds pleased about the ordinary company, not only the news Wally will bring.
I'd love to hear what Wally chooses to share first.

contexts.subject: Wally father cannot believe his son traveled as far as Ever Grande alone.
