PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_YouMetWal.text: Oh? You met WALLY in\nEVER GRANDE CITY?\pOh, {PLAYER}{KUN}, don't be silly.\pHe may have gotten healthy, but he\ncan't go somewhere far away like\lthat all by himself.$

replies.text: His picture of Wally is still standing much nearer home than Wally actually is.
New evidence conflicts with a long-established expectation of limited independence.
He needs to hear it clearly. Wally earned that journey.
It must be hard to let an old fear make room for a new truth.
I'd explain what we actually saw instead of arguing about what should be possible.
Wally has traveled farther than his father can quite imagine. We can offer details without making it an argument.
Reality has delivered an update his expectations are declining to install.
Specific details may help him revise the assumption without feeling cornered.
Someone can travel beyond the size of another person's worry.
He is underestimating Wally out of a habit built from concern. It can still change.
I'd want him to hear the whole story from Wally himself too.

contexts.subject: Wally mother remembers his rare bright smile after catching his first Pokemon.

PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_WallyWasR.text: WALLY was really happy when he told\nus that he caught a POKéMON.\pIt's been ages since I've seen him\nsmile like that.$

replies.text: That first Pokemon brought home a smile the whole family had missed.
She noticed a meaningful change in his mood, not merely the successful catch.
Good. A partner can give someone a reason to look ahead.
I like that she remembers his face more than the event itself.
A happy little story can feed a parent's hope for a long time.
That is a lovely thing to have helped happen. The family remembers a smile rather than a number in a record.
A small Pokemon has made a remarkably large difference to this room.
I'd ask what he has enjoyed doing with his partner since then.
A little joy can return light to a face people know by heart.
Her happiness about his happiness says more than any grand praise.
I'd make sure Wally knows how fondly she remembers that moment.

contexts.subject: Wally mother privately reveals his unannounced departure and trusts his determination.

PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_WallyLeft.text:
I want you to keep this a secret
from my husband…\pBut our WALLY left VERDANTURF TOWN
without telling anyone.\pYou know, WALLY is frail, but
he's surprisingly strong-willed.\pI'm sure that he'll come back safe
and sound one day!$

replies.text: She knows he left quietly and is trying to let hope speak louder than worry.
Her confidence in his will is distinct from knowing his present safety.
He should send word. Independence doesn't need to leave everyone guessing.
Keeping the worry private probably makes it heavier.
I'd encourage a real message from Wally rather than another round of hoping alone.
Her confidence is trying very hard to sound effortless. Wally could spare her some work by sending a message.
A determined young Trainer has created an exceptionally anxious information shortage.
A simple contact plan could respect his freedom and reduce the worry at home.
Trust can open a hand while fear keeps checking the empty palm.
She sees his strength. It would be kind if he gave her something solid to hold onto too.
I'd ask whether there is a way for him to contact the family directly.

contexts.subject: After the Surf gift, Wally father describes travel opportunities across water.

PetalburgCity_WallysHouse_Text_SurfGoAll.text: If your POKéMON can SURF, you'll be\nable to go to all sorts of places.$

replies.text: The water on the map has just become a collection of possible roads.
A new movement capability changes which destinations are accessible.
Plan the crossing and the return. New access still needs good judgment.
It is exciting when a familiar shore stops being the edge of everything.
We should pack for the trip beyond the water, not only the first crossing.
A useful gift, followed by an unusually large choice of where to go. I recommend deciding before entering the water.
The map has become larger without the paper increasing. Inconveniently clever.
We should find safe entry points and understand the currents.
An old boundary can become a path with a trusted companion beside us.
A new freedom is nicest when the partner is comfortable sharing it.
I'd ask which water route local travelers would recommend trying first.

contexts.subject: A visitor appreciates freely available Pokemon Center healing.

OldaleTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Pokemon.text: POKéMON CENTERS are great!\pYou can use their services as much\nas you like, and it's all for free.\lYou never have to worry!$

replies.text: A long road feels kinder when getting help doesn't depend on the coin purse.
Accessible care removes a significant barrier to treating injury promptly.
Use it when the team needs it. No reason to make them push through.
It's comforting to know a safe stop is there even on an awkward day.
A place that helps tired travelers without making them choose against dinner is wonderful.
Free recovery is a splendid idea. I see no reason to test whether we can manage without something this helpful.
A free rest, offered without an elaborate speech. Civilization at its best.
We should know the Center locations along the planned route.
A little light in a window can mean help without a price.
Being able to ask for care easily is worth appreciating.
I'd ask whether the visitor has a particular nurse they remember helping them.

contexts.subject: A visitor explains that the Center PC is available to any Trainer.

OldaleTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Trainer.text: That PC in the corner there is\nfor any POKéMON TRAINER to use.\pNaturally, that means you're welcome\nto use it, too.$

replies.text: An intimidating-looking machine with a surprisingly welcoming invitation.
Clear public access matters when a service looks like it might belong to staff.
Good to know. Use it carefully and leave it ready for the next person.
It's nice when someone says explicitly that you're allowed to be there.
A shared useful thing works best when everybody leaves it tidy.
An explicit welcome to use the machine saves a great deal of standing beside it looking meaningfully uncertain.
A reassuring clarification before curiosity becomes an awkward apology.
I'd look at the available functions before making a change.
A familiar corner can become less closed with one kind sentence.
That small welcome makes learning a new thing much less uncomfortable.
I'd ask where first-time users can find the instructions.

contexts.subject: The new Wireless Club is still being adjusted and is not available yet.

OldaleTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Wireles.text: The POKéMON WIRELESS CLUB on\nthe second floor was built recently.\pBut they say they're still making\nadjustments.$

replies.text: The new room is nearly ready, but nearly isn't an invitation to press every button.
Completion of the structure does not imply the service has finished testing.
Let them get it working properly. We can return later.
I would rather wait than have the first visit turn into a confusing problem.
A safe opening is better than a hurried one.
Waiting is tiresome. Discovering why a service needed more testing would probably be worse.
New and usable have not yet agreed to mean the same thing.
Final adjustments are part of delivering a service that people can trust.
A closed door can be protecting the beginning that waits behind it.
Clear expectations make the delay easier to understand.
I'd ask how they'll let visitors know when the room is ready.

contexts.subject: After the Club opens, a visitor reports trading there immediately.

OldaleTown_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_TradedI.text: The POKéMON WIRELESS CLUB on\nthe second floor was built recently.\pI traded POKéMON right away.$

replies.text: They waited for the doors to open and made a new introduction straight away.
The completed service has already supported an actual exchange.
Good. Hope the new partner is settling in well.
A first visit can become memorable very quickly when a Pokemon comes home with you.
I'd ask what familiar routine will help the new partner feel welcome.
The room opens, and someone immediately makes a friend-shaped change to their journey. An excellent beginning.
An opening ceremony with remarkably tangible souvenirs.
I'd ask whether using the service felt clear to a first-time visitor.
A room can make a new bond possible on its very first day.
The excitement should leave room for the Pokemon's own change of surroundings.
I'd ask about the person they traded with and what they learned from each other.

contexts.subject: A shopper plans to buy many Poke Balls and meet many Pokemon.

OldaleTown_Mart_Text_ImGoingToBuyPokeBal.text: I'm going to buy a bunch of POKé BALLS\nand catch a bunch of POKéMON!$

replies.text: An enthusiastic shopping list with a whole crowd of future introductions imagined inside it.
The equipment supports the plan, but each new partner also creates care responsibilities.
Prepare to look after them as well as catch them.
I'd want time to learn the little habits of the first one too.
A growing team needs more than a growing pile of Balls.
An ambitious plan. I would ask who is doing the feeding before applauding the projected size of the household.
A large collection begins with a bag. Maintaining it is a larger subject.
I'd plan for supplies and training time alongside capture equipment.
Many meetings can be wonderful when each life remains more than a number.
Enthusiasm is a good beginning if it leaves room for thoughtful choices.
I'd ask which Pokemon they most hope to meet first.

contexts.subject: A shopper cannot buy Poke Balls because the Mart is sold out.

OldaleTown_Mart_Text_PokeBallsAreSoldOut.text: The clerk says they're all sold out.\nI can't buy any POKé BALLS.$

replies.text: The adventure shopping list has found a shelf-shaped hole in its plans.
The limitation is stock availability, not the shopper's preparation.
Ask when the next delivery comes. No point blaming the clerk.
It's disappointing when the thing you came for is the one missing thing.
A short wait might be easier if they have another errand to do meanwhile.
The shelf is empty, and taking offense will not restock it. We can ask a useful question instead.
Demand has successfully outrun the box in the back room.
We can find another supplier or return after the next shipment.
A beginning can pause without closing.
The clerk probably isn't enjoying having the same disappointing conversation all day either.
I'd ask whether they know another nearby shop with stock.

contexts.subject: A shopper recommends Potions before injury leads to fainting.

OldaleTown_Mart_Text_RestoreHPWithPotion.text: If a POKéMON gets hurt and loses its HP\nand faints, it won't be able to battle.\pTo prevent your POKéMON from fainting,\nrestore its HP with a POTION.$

replies.text: A little help now is nicer than waiting for a partner to stop standing.
Preventive recovery can reduce the risk of an avoidable faint.
Don't wait until the last safe moment to act.
A partner should not have to look desperate before we notice.
Keeping supplies handy makes it easier to respond when somebody needs help.
If a little help prevents a dramatic collapse, I favor the little help. Drama is overrated when it hurts.
A modest intervention before a more inconvenient collapse. Sensible.
We should estimate the likely incoming damage, not stare only at the current number.
Care can arrive before the hurt becomes a crisis.
Their trust grows when they see us act before the situation becomes frightening.
I'd check our stock before making the next stretch of road.

contexts.subject: The aide explains Birch absence and preference for research outdoors.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text:
Hunh? PROF. BIRCH?\pThe PROF's away on fieldwork.
Ergo, he isn't here.\pOh, let me explain what fieldwork is.\pIt is to study things in the natural
environment, like fields and mountains,\linstead of a laboratory.\pThe PROF isn't one for doing desk work.
He's the type of person who would\lrather go outside and experience\lthings than read about them here.$

replies.text: The laboratory is missing its professor because the professor has gone to the actual Pokemon.
Field observations can answer questions the controlled room cannot.
Makes sense. Ask where he went before searching the whole countryside.
I like the thought of somebody caring enough to go see the place for themselves.
He probably needs someone to remind him to eat while he's out there.
Birch seems reliably located wherever the comfortable chair is not. I imagine the aide gives these directions often.
A scientist who can leave his chair. A startlingly mobile discipline.
The notes still matter when he gets back. Fieldwork needs a good record.
A question can lead a person beyond the walls where it began.
The aide sounds used to explaining why the busiest desk is empty.
I'd ask what part of the local habitat he is investigating today.

contexts.subject: The aide reiterates Birch preference for firsthand outdoor work.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text: The PROF isn't one for doing desk work.\nHe's the type of person who would\lrather go outside and experience\lthings than read about them here.$

replies.text: His chair must have a very restful job.
Firsthand experience is valuable when it is recorded and compared carefully.
Good to get out there. Good to finish the paperwork afterward too.
Some people understand a place better after standing quietly inside it.
A working day outdoors still needs an ordinary lunch break.
Experience is valuable. So are the notes that let somebody else understand what the experience showed.
An admirable affection for reality over the desk where it gets summarized.
I'd want his observations organized so other people can use them too.
The grass may offer a question the page has not learned to ask.
I hope the aide's own work is appreciated while the professor is away.
I'd ask what surprising thing he brought back from the last trip.

contexts.subject: The aide describes Birch research and warm enjoyment of his child help.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text: PROF. BIRCH is studying the habitats\nand distribution of POKéMON.\pThe PROF enjoys {RIVAL}'s help, too.\nThere's a lot of love there.$

replies.text: Research with somebody you love sounds like a good reason to keep coming back muddy.
A shared task can make time together productive without making it less personal.
Good. Hope they both enjoy the work, not only the results.
It's nice that somebody notices the fondness around all those facts.
Working together can leave you little ordinary memories no report includes.
The work sounds useful, but the fondness is the detail that makes me want to hear more.
A laboratory with affection in the observations. Not an invalidating variable.
I'd ask which part of the fieldwork the child likes helping with.
A question shared kindly can become a way of being close.
They see each other doing something they care about. That's valuable.
I'd love to hear about a discovery they made together.

contexts.subject: After the player agrees to meet the rival, Birch recommends learning Trainer basics from them.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_G.text: PROF. BIRCH: Great!\n{RIVAL} should be happy, too.\pGet {RIVAL} to teach you what it\nmeans to be a TRAINER.$

replies.text: A new neighbor can also be someone who knows which beginner mistakes have sharp edges.
A peer with experience can translate the basics into practical examples.
Listen, ask questions, and learn the partner we've actually got.
It's easier to meet somebody when there is a small thing to do together.
A friendly lesson could spare us a very uncomfortable first trip.
A helpful neighbor with experience is a fine beginning. Nobody sensible expects us to know everything already.
A sensible plan: locate the person who has already made some of the mistakes.
We can ask for one useful lesson rather than pretend to understand everything.
A first road feels kinder when someone can point out its turns.
Being related to a Trainer doesn't remove the right to be a beginner.
I'd ask what they wish someone had explained on their first day.

contexts.subject: May describes exploring for different Pokemon she finds cute; this does not prove the preceding Ball gift succeeded.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_C.text:
MAY: It's fun if you can get a lot of
POKéMON!\pI'm going to look all over the place
because I want different POKéMON.\pIf I find any cute POKéMON, I'll catch
them with POKé BALLS!$

replies.text: May has a whole journey planned around meeting faces that make her smile.
A personal interest can motivate broad field exploration without determining every choice.
Find good partners and learn what they need. Cute comes with responsibilities too.
I like how much she is looking forward to the meetings themselves.
A growing team means a growing amount of ordinary daily care.
May has a splendidly candid reason for exploring. I would rather hear that than an unnecessarily grand justification.
A scientific tour guided partly by the urge to say aww. Understandable.
I'd ask how she prepares for a species she hasn't raised before.
A fond glance can be the start of learning someone carefully.
What feels cute becomes deeper once you know the particular Pokemon.
I'd ask which unexpected encounter made her happiest so far.

contexts.subject: Brendan describes seeking diverse Pokemon he finds cool; the preceding gift may have failed.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_C.text:
BRENDAN: You know it's more fun to
have a whole bunch of POKéMON.\pI'm going to explore all over the place
to find different POKéMON.\pIf I find any cool POKéMON, you bet
I'll try to get them with POKé BALLS.$

replies.text: Brendan has turned cool into a perfectly serviceable reason to go exploring.
Interest can drive observation, though careful care must follow any capture.
Good to be eager. Think past the exciting first encounter too.
I'd like hearing what makes a Pokemon stand out to him.
The impressive newcomer will still need a familiar routine afterward.
Cool is a fine first impression. I should like to hear what he notices once the Pokemon feels at home.
Cool remains a scientifically broad category with excellent travel potential.
I'd ask what he learns from a partner after the first impression settles.
Wonder can invite a meeting; attention turns it into knowledge.
An exciting collection works best when the individual partners remain visible.
I'd ask which Pokemon changed his mind after he got to know it.

contexts.subject: May considers where to search for Pokemon next.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_M.text: MAY: I wonder where I should go look\nfor POKéMON next?$

replies.text: The map has too many promising corners for one afternoon. A nice kind of problem.
A useful destination would depend on which habitats or species she wants to investigate.
Pick one route and prepare for it. The rest can wait.
Sometimes choosing the next place feels harder than walking there.
I'd ask where she can stop for a meal along the way.
The terrible inconvenience of several appealing destinations. She should choose one before the afternoon leaves without her.
An excellent question to ask before leaving through the nearest door.
A short list of unanswered questions could help choose the next field site.
A road can wait patiently while curiosity chooses its direction.
She doesn't need to see everything on one trip for it to count.
I'd ask what she most hopes will surprise her next.

contexts.subject: Brendan considers where to search for Pokemon next.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text: BRENDAN: Where should I look for\nPOKéMON next…$

replies.text: A whole region of possibilities and only one pair of shoes.
Comparing missing observations with known habitats would narrow the choice.
Go where there's something useful to learn, not merely farther away.
I like having a moment between arriving home and planning to leave again.
I'd check what needs restocking before committing to the next long route.
There is plenty of region left. I suggest he pick a question before attempting to walk through all of it.
An itinerary would give the restless feet some useful supervision.
I'd pick the site that answers the most interesting current question.
The next place need not be distant to be unfamiliar.
A good destination suits the kind of day he actually wants.
I'd ask which place he keeps thinking about even after returning here.

contexts.subject: May pauses outdoor research to help at the lab.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_M.text: MAY: I think I'll take a short break\nfrom fieldwork.\pI think I'll help the PROF here for\na while.$

replies.text: A journey can have a useful indoor chapter without becoming less of a journey.
Lab work can organize and interpret the observations fieldwork gathers.
Good change of pace. Rest the feet and finish some useful work.
I like the thought of a familiar room after so many unfamiliar roads.
A steadier day might make proper meals a little easier too.
The professor gets some help, and May gets a little less mud. I hope she also gets a proper chance to rest.
A temporary truce with being indoors. Promising.
I'd ask which field notes she most wants to make sense of.
Something learned far away can take root in a quiet room.
Helping here can be a choice rather than a retreat from what she enjoys.
I'd ask what she is looking forward to learning on this side of the work.

contexts.subject: Brendan takes a fieldwork break to assist Birch in the lab.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text: BRENDAN: For the time being,\nI'm taking a break from fieldwork.\pI'll be helping out the PROF here\nfor a while.$

replies.text: Brendan has found a way to keep helping without adding another layer of road dust.
Research benefits from alternating collection with analysis.
A break from the road can still be time well used.
I wonder whether the quiet feels strange after moving around so much.
I'd let the break include actual rest as well as another kind of work.
A useful change of work, provided he remembers that a different task does not automatically count as a holiday.
The chair has finally recruited an investigator.
He can compare results across trips instead of gathering more before reviewing any.
A returning traveler can carry many places into one room.
It's good to see helping the professor treated as its own worthwhile thing.
I'd ask what question he brought home that he wants the lab to answer.

contexts.subject: May asks about the player future plans and chooses to remain helping Birch.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_M.text:
MAY: {PLAYER}{KUN}, after this…
What are you going to do?\pAre you going to keep battling
and sharpening your skills?\pOr are you going to try filling
the NATIONAL POKéDEX?\pI'm staying here to help the PROF.$

replies.text: May has chosen her next chapter and leaves ours open for us to choose.
Battling, collecting data, and supporting research are distinct valid goals.
We'll pick our own next step. Glad she has one she wants.
It's nice when friends can take different paths without making it a goodbye forever.
A plan can be worthwhile even when it looks quieter from the outside.
May knows what she wants to do and still asks what interests us. A considerably nicer habit than prescribing our future.
A future with options rather than a compulsory escalation. Civilized.
We can choose according to what interests us, not simply what comes next on a list.
A familiar room and a far road can each hold a living wish.
She asks without trying to make our choice match hers.
I'd ask which part of helping here she wants to get better at.

contexts.subject: Brendan prefers patiently raising his chosen partner over broad collecting.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text: BRENDAN: Rather than collecting\nPOKéMON, I prefer slowly and \lsteadily raising the one I chose.$

replies.text: One companion can make a very large adventure without a very large head count.
Depth of experience and breadth of sampling are different interests.
Fair choice. Put the time into the partner he knows.
I like hearing somebody enjoy the unhurried part of getting to know a Pokemon.
The familiar everyday habits are a real part of raising someone.
One well-known partner can be excellent company. He need not turn a personal preference into a competitive quantity.
A respectable preference for one known individual over a rapidly expanding guest list.
He can study progress carefully when he keeps returning to the same partner.
Roots grow deep by staying, not only by reaching farther.
That sounds like his own preference rather than a judgment on everyone else's.
I'd ask what small change he has noticed in that partner lately.

contexts.subject: May asks whether the player has visited the Battle Frontier.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_M.text: MAY: Oh, hi, {PLAYER}{KUN}!\nHave you gone to that place,\lthe BATTLE FRONTIER?$

replies.text: May has heard about another place with a lot of possible stories inside it.
She is asking about a destination, not assuming we have already experienced it.
Worth learning the rules before planning a visit.
I'd want to know what it felt like there before hearing only the results.
A new destination means another reason to check the travel supplies.
She asks as if there is something interesting to hear, not a box we should already have ticked. I like that.
Another location with the word battle in its invitation. How restful.
I'd compare what the facilities offer before deciding which to try.
A distant place begins to feel nearer when a familiar person asks about it.
We can answer honestly without making visiting another obligation.
I'd ask what May has heard that made her curious about the place.

contexts.subject: Brendan asks whether the player has visited the Battle Frontier.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text: BRENDAN: Hey, {PLAYER}!\nHave you gone out to that place,\lthe BATTLE FRONTIER?$

replies.text: The Frontier has apparently reached home in the form of everybody asking about it.
A new challenge merits learning its constraints before treating it like the familiar ones.
We'll go when we're prepared and interested.
It's nice to compare plans without needing to have already been everywhere.
I'd ask where visitors usually rest between the different challenges.
Another tempting destination. I am pleased that the question does not come with an immediate departure time.
The region has found another way to make the itinerary longer.
I'd ask which facility he thinks tests a genuinely different skill.
A new door can wait while we finish looking at the room we're in.
No need to make the answer impressive. It is a conversation, not a progress report.
I'd ask whether Brendan has been and what surprised him most.

contexts.subject: Birch confirms the completed Hoenn Pokedex and offers a choice of rare regional partners; no choice is yet made.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_C.text:
PROF. BIRCH: Oh, {PLAYER}{KUN}!
Let's have a look at your POKéDEX.\p… … … … … …
… … … … … …\pYes, there's no doubt about it.\pYou really have completed the HOENN
region's POKéDEX.\pThat's more than just impressive.\pI have a gift for you.\pConsider it my show of appreciation
for the fantastic work you've done.\pMy gift is a rare POKéMON only found
in another region!\pYou can have any one of these
three POKéMON!$

replies.text: All those meetings have become a completed book, and now there may be one new hello.
He has verified the completed regional record and offers a separate future responsibility.
That's real work recognized. Take time choosing the new partner.
I think I'd want a quiet moment to take in the finished record first.
A living thank-you deserves a proper place in our plans.
A wonderful acknowledgment, and a decision worth making carefully. The Pokemon is a future companion, not a ceremonial accessory.
A remarkably substantial reward with substantially more needs than a medal.
We should learn about each species before accepting the care of one.
An ending can offer a new life beside the road rather than close the road.
The achievement is ours already. We don't need to hurry the next decision.
I'd ask Birch what each partner is like in an ordinary day.

contexts.subject: Birch reiterates the still-open choice among three rare regional Pokemon.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_C.text: PROF. BIRCH: These are rare POKéMON\nonly found in another region!\pYou can have any one of these\nthree POKéMON!$

replies.text: Three possible new friends, and thankfully nobody has put a timer beside them.
The offer remains open. No species has been selected by this conversation.
Meet them, learn what they need, then decide.
It is a big choice even after a very long journey.
I'd think about the home and routine we can actually offer.
There is no prize for answering fastest. There may be a very happy partner if we answer thoughtfully.
Three excellent candidates for a responsibility larger than a collection slot.
Compare temperament and care needs, not only battle possibilities.
A willing companion is a life, not punctuation at the end of a record.
There is room to appreciate all three without pretending we can accept everyone.
I'd ask which one Birch thinks enjoys traveling most.

contexts.subject: After declining a particular Johto choice, Birch encourages an unhurried decision.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_T.text: PROF. BIRCH: Take your time before\nyou decide.\pThey're all invaluable POKéMON.$

replies.text: He knows a good partner is worth more than a quick answer.
An irreversible responsibility benefits from an unhurried comparison.
Good. No need to choose while we're unsure.
I like being allowed to care about the decision without looking indecisive.
We should choose when the plan for looking after them feels clear.
A professor recommending patience. I shall cherish this rare encounter with sensible authority.
A rare authority figure correctly prescribing more time.
We can ask another practical question instead of treating hesitation as failure.
A patient hand is a kinder beginning than a hurried reach.
Every option can be precious without one being right for us today.
I'd spend a little time noticing how each Pokemon responds around people.

contexts.subject: After a successful Johto partner gift, Birch says the completed regional record does not end the journey.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_G.text:
PROF. BIRCH: Listen, {PLAYER}{KUN}.
You've completed the HOENN POKéDEX,\lbut your POKéMON journey isn't over.\pThere is no end to the road
that is POKéMON.\pSomewhere, there is a grassy patch
that's waiting for you!$

replies.text: The book is complete, but the grass outside has never learned to stop being interesting.
A completed catalog does not exhaust what can be observed about its subjects.
Good reason to keep learning. No reason to rush.
I like a finished task that still leaves us somewhere gentle to go tomorrow.
A new partner also gives familiar places something new to teach us.
An achievement can be finished while curiosity remains active. A merciful alternative to inventing another urgent deadline.
The world has regrettably refused to become fully explained by a checklist.
We can revisit a known habitat with better questions and a different team.
The same green patch can hold a new meeting on another morning.
Finishing something doesn't mean we have to stop enjoying it.
I'd choose one familiar place to visit again without a list to complete.

contexts.subject: After the National upgrade, Birch reminds the Champion that Pokemon journeys continue.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_G.text:
PROF. BIRCH: But listen.
You've become the CHAMPION,\lbut your POKéMON journey isn't over.\pThere is no end to the road
that is POKéMON.\pSomewhere, there is a grassy patch
that's waiting for you!$

replies.text: Champion sounds enormous, but there's still ordinary grass willing to surprise us.
A title marks an achievement without removing future opportunities to learn.
We can set the next goal ourselves now.
It is a relief to hear the journey can keep being curious instead of always grand.
Maybe the next good day can be a walk, a meal, and a quiet new meeting.
I approve of the next adventure being allowed to begin in ordinary grass rather than somewhere dramatically inconvenient.
A prestigious title has failed to frighten the grass into predictability.
New records can begin from close observation instead of another bigger challenge.
A high peak does not use up every small path below it.
We can enjoy being here without turning the title into a daily performance.
I'd like to hear which ordinary place Birch would revisit first.

contexts.subject: Birch guesses where the rival is and recommends resting at home when tired.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_B.text:
PROF. BIRCH: {RIVAL}?
Gone home, I think.\pOr maybe that kid's scrabbling around
in tall grass again somewhere…\pIf you or your POKéMON get tired,
you should get some rest at home.$

replies.text: His directions contain a little uncertainty, but the rest advice is perfectly clear.
He offers two possible locations and one dependable recovery option.
Check home if we need rest. We don't have to keep searching tired.
It's nice when the answer includes remembering we're people who get worn out.
A familiar doorstep and a meal can improve the next part of the day.
Birch is uncertain about his child and certain about the value of rest. We can use the reliable half of the answer.
An ambiguous location paired with an excellent excuse to sit down.
We can separate the search for the rival from our own need to recover.
A road can wait while home takes us in for a little while.
He makes taking a break sound ordinary, which it should be.
I'd check in at home before setting out on another guess.

contexts.subject: Birch encourages exploration and admits he is eager to return to fieldwork himself.

LittlerootTown_ProfessorBirchsLab_Text_C.text: PROF. BIRCH: Countless POKéMON\nawait you!\pArgh, I'm getting the itch to get out\nand do fieldwork again!$

replies.text: He's trying to send us exploring, but his own feet seem to be volunteering first.
His enthusiasm for new observations remains active despite his experience.
Good to see him still curious. We can take the next route at our own pace.
I like it when someone's work still makes them want to get up and go.
I'd make sure he packs lunch before following that itch into the grass.
He is enthusiastically recommending the precise activity he would rather be doing himself. Refreshingly transparent.
A scientist visibly resisting an argument with his own chair.
I'd ask which unanswered question is pulling him outside today.
A familiar world can keep offering a new reason to look closely.
His enthusiasm is inviting as long as we still get room to choose.
I'd love to hear where he would go if he could leave right now.

contexts.subject: A townsman admires PC storage for items and Pokemon.

LittlerootTown_Text_CanUsePCToStoreItems.text: If you use a PC, you can store items\nand POKéMON.\pThe power of science is staggering!$

replies.text: Science has given traveling pockets a rather impressive set of assistants.
Remote storage is useful precisely because a traveler cannot carry everything comfortably.
Useful system. Keep track of what we actually have with us.
It is easy to forget how strange an everyday convenience seemed the first time.
Not carrying the whole pantry is a real improvement to a journey.
An ordinary errand receives an unexpectedly grand tribute to human ingenuity.
A remarkable machine devoted partly to the ancient problem of too much stuff.
A good interface should make the location of each thing clear.
A small corner can offer a little more room to a crowded journey.
A useful thing deserves appreciation even after it becomes familiar.
I'd ask what he first stored when he learned the system existed.

contexts.subject: A boy wonders when Birch makes time for home between lab work and field research.

LittlerootTown_Text_BirchSpendsDaysInLab.text: PROF. BIRCH spends days in his LAB\nstudying, then he'll suddenly go out in\lthe wild to do more research…\pWhen does PROF. BIRCH spend time\nat home?$

replies.text: The professor's schedule sounds full enough to need its own map.
Alternating work locations is not necessarily the same as taking time away from work.
A busy job still needs room for home.
It's a thoughtful question to ask about someone who's always doing something.
I hope somebody reminds him that a meal at home counts as a worthwhile plan.
The tireless researcher may need an appointment with his own front door.
Two workplaces are not a holiday from either.
He could schedule actual time off instead of calling a change of location a break.
A familiar light may be waiting while a curious mind keeps following another question.
His family probably wants some of the ordinary person behind the important work.
I'd ask whether Birch ever talks about what he enjoys doing at home.

contexts.subject: The twin warns that wild Pokemon emerge from tall grass.

LittlerootTown_Text_IfYouGoInGrassPokemo.text: Um, um, um!\pIf you go outside and go in the grass,\nwild POKéMON will jump out!$

replies.text: The grass is not empty scenery. It apparently has a guest list with surprise arrivals.
Vegetation provides cover for creatures that may not be visible from the path.
Look ahead and keep a safe way back.
Something familiar-looking can feel different when you know someone might be inside it.
A little warning helps a beginner prepare instead of panic.
The scenery has been introduced as an active participant in the outing.
Grass with occupants. An important footnote to a peaceful walk.
We should know the route before stepping into an unfamiliar patch.
A green surface can keep many small lives from view.
The child is trying to make sure we know what other people assume.
I'd ask which Pokemon they've actually seen near the edge of town.

contexts.subject: The twin keeps an unaccompanied beginner from entering dangerous grass.

LittlerootTown_Text_DangerousIfYouDontHa.text: It's dangerous if you don't have\nyour own POKéMON.$

replies.text: The little guard is taking a very large responsibility seriously.
The warning concerns a lack of support in an environment with wild encounters.
Listen to the warning. We can prepare before going out.
I'd rather be stopped kindly than discover the risk alone.
There is no shame in waiting until we have the help we need.
The shortest person present has supplied the most sensible travel policy.
A safety lecture with an unusually small lecturer. Still correct.
We need a safer plan rather than a way around the person warning us.
A path can wait until the traveler is ready to meet it.
They're trying to protect us, not embarrass us.
I'd ask who nearby can help us prepare properly.

contexts.subject: The twin hears alarming Pokemon cries and asks the player to investigate.

LittlerootTown_Text_CanYouGoSeeWhatsHapp.text:
Um, hi!\pThere are scary POKéMON outside!
I can hear their cries!\pI want to go see what's going on,
but I don't have any POKéMON…\pCan you go see what's happening
for me?$

replies.text: The child heard something wrong and had the sense to ask for help.
An unusual sound is evidence of a disturbance, though its cause is not yet known.
We should check carefully. Don't send the kid toward it.
I don't like hearing fear from somewhere I can't quite see.
Let's find out whether somebody needs help before guessing at the noise.
A quiet town has acquired a problem loud enough to interrupt an ordinary afternoon.
An alarming sound and an honest admission of limited equipment. Sensible child.
Approach with a clear view and keep an escape route available.
A cry can pull a thread from one small life toward another.
They were right to say they couldn't handle it alone.
I'd listen for where the sound is coming from before we move closer.

contexts.subject: After the rescue, the twin expresses relief that Birch is safe.

LittlerootTown_Text_YouSavedBirch.text: You saved PROF. BIRCH!\nI'm so glad!$

replies.text: The scary sound has become a happy little piece of news.
The child now knows the person in danger received help.
Good. No need for them to keep worrying at the edge of town.
You can hear the relief more clearly than the words.
I'm glad somebody came back with an answer the child could feel good about.
The worried witness has finally been allowed a favorable ending.
An anxious question has received a much better answer than more noise.
They helped by noticing the problem and asking for support.
A frightened little moment has found its way back toward ordinary daylight.
They should know asking for help mattered too.
I'd tell them Birch is safe without making the danger sound exciting to imitate.

contexts.subject: Once the adventure begins, the twin wishes the player luck.

LittlerootTown_Text_GoodLuckCatchingPoke.text: Are you going to catch POKéMON?\nGood luck!$

replies.text: Our very small town guard has become our very small cheering section.
A simple good wish can mark a change from concern to confidence.
Thanks. We'll take care out there.
I like a goodbye that makes the road feel a little friendlier.
A kind little send-off is a good thing to carry into the day.
The former gatekeeper now endorses the adventure. Excellent progression.
A brief blessing from the local authority on grass hazards.
We can keep the earlier safety advice alongside the encouragement.
A voice from home can remain warm after the town is out of sight.
They look happy that we get to try something new.
I'd wave back so they know we heard them.

contexts.subject: After moving in, Mom admires the tidy room and asks the player to check the desk belongings.

PlayersHouse_2F_Text_HowDoYouLikeYourRoo.text:
MOM: {PLAYER}, how do you like your
new room?\pGood! Everything's put away neatly!\pThey finished moving everything in
downstairs, too.\pPOKéMON movers are so convenient!\pOh, you should make sure that
everything's all there on your desk.$

replies.text: A new room gets familiar one little thing on the desk at a time.
Checking belongings after a move is a sensible final step before assuming everything arrived.
Good. Let's make sure the important things are here.
It is nice when a strange new place starts having your own small corners.
The movers did the hard part. We can finish by noticing what might be missing.
The unfamiliar setting has been furnished with the beginnings of a home.
A neat desk. A temporary but admirable condition.
We should check the essentials before settling everything permanently in place.
A room becomes ours through the little things that recognize our hands.
She wants us comfortable here, not merely unpacked.
I'd take a quiet look around before the next busy part begins.

contexts.subject: Mom credits the Pokemon movers and sends the player upstairs to set a new clock.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_MoversPokemonGoSetC.text:
The mover's POKéMON do all the work
of moving us in and cleaning up after.\lThis is so convenient!\p{PLAYER}, your room is upstairs.
Go check it out, dear!\pDAD bought you a new clock to mark
our move here.\lDon't forget to set it!$

replies.text: The movers carried a whole household, and our assignment is to help time move in too.
A clock is a small practical anchor when the rest of a routine has changed.
Thank the movers. Then we can sort the room upstairs.
A new clock feels like the house is ready to start sharing our days.
I hope the Pokemon who did the heavy work get a proper break.
The move concludes with the modest ceremony of telling the new room what time it is.
An impressive labor force rewarded, I trust, with more than compliments.
Check the time carefully once so it won't be a nuisance later.
An unfamiliar house can begin to keep familiar hours.
Convenience should include care for the ones doing the carrying.
I'd ask whether there is anything small we can help tidy before going upstairs.

contexts.subject: Mom encourages the player to look at their new room.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_ArentYouInterestedI.text: MOM: Well, {PLAYER}?\pAren't you interested in seeing your\nvery own room?$

replies.text: She has been waiting to show us a little place that's especially ours.
A personal space can make a larger move feel more manageable.
Worth a look. We've come a long way to get here.
I might linger at the door for a moment before it feels like my room.
There is comfort in knowing where you'll put your bag at the end of the day.
The host requests an audience for the most personal part of the new setting.
A room without an audience. A promising invitation.
We can check the layout before deciding where everyday things should go.
A new threshold can feel gentle when someone is glad to show it to us.
She sounds excited about giving us somewhere comfortable.
I'd notice what she thought to put there before we arrived.

contexts.subject: Mom enjoys the new house and invites the player to appreciate it.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_IsntItNiceInHere.text: MOM: See, {PLAYER}?\nIsn't it nice in here, too?$

replies.text: She wants the unfamiliar walls to hear a friendly first opinion.
Shared approval can make settling into a new environment easier.
Looks like a good place to come home to.
It takes a little time, but I can see what she means.
A house feels nicer once you can imagine the ordinary mornings in it.
The new household receives an enthusiastic review from its first resident critic.
A pleasant room before daily clutter develops its full ambitions.
The space looks workable. I'd ask which practical detail she is happiest with.
Warmth often arrives before familiarity does.
I like that she wants us to enjoy the move, not just endure the boxes.
I'd ask which little part made it feel like home to her first.

contexts.subject: After the missed television report, Mom recommends meeting Professor Birch next door.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_GoIntroduceYourself.text: Oh, yes.\nOne of DAD's friends lives in town.\pPROF. BIRCH is his name.\pHe lives right next door, so you should\ngo over and introduce yourself.$

replies.text: A whole new neighborhood starts with one hello through the next door.
An existing family connection can make the first introduction less uncertain.
Easy place to start. We can introduce ourselves politely.
Next door is a manageable distance for meeting someone new.
I'd avoid arriving at the exact moment they're trying to eat.
The next scene is conveniently located within one neighborly walk.
A social obligation with excellent geographic restraint.
We can ask who is home rather than assume the professor is there.
A short path can begin a long acquaintance.
A familiar connection helps, but we still get to make our own impression.
I'd ask Mom what Birch is like before knocking.

contexts.subject: Mom asks whether the player introduced themselves to Birch.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_DidYouMeetProfBirch.text: MOM: Did you introduce yourself to\nPROF. BIRCH?$

replies.text: The first neighborly errand has become a perfectly ordinary question from home.
She is checking whether a specific introduction happened, not demanding an accomplishment.
Tell her how it went. She wanted us to have a friendly contact nearby.
It is nice when somebody cares about the small beginning of your day.
An ordinary update can help a new place feel less unfamiliar for both people.
The introductory mission receives a brief domestic follow-up.
A mercifully simple request for a progress report.
If he was out, we can say so and ask when to try again.
A little shared news can tie a house to the street around it.
She wants to know we aren't quite strangers here anymore.
I'd tell her one detail from the visit rather than just yes or no.

contexts.subject: Mom encourages the journey while reminding the player they can always return home.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_DontPushYourselfToo.text: Don't push yourself too hard, dear.\nYou can always come home.\pGo for it, honey!$

replies.text: Home isn't a place we have to earn our way back into. That's good to remember.
A reliable place to recover makes exploration less costly when plans go badly.
Listen to her. Come back before exhaustion makes the decision for us.
I like knowing the door stays open even on the days we don't have a proud story.
A meal and a familiar chair can be a very important part of an adventure.
The journey receives permission to pause without being judged unfinished.
A standing invitation to retreat into comfort. Sensible family policy.
We should treat home as a real option, not only an emergency fallback.
A path can stretch far while one doorway remains near inside us.
Her encouragement leaves room for us to be tired, which makes it kinder.
I'd make sure she knows we heard the offer, not only the send-off.

contexts.subject: After healing the team at home, Mom sends the player off with care.

replies.text: Rested partners, a warm goodbye, and one less reason to hurry.
The recovery is complete; the next stretch can begin from a better condition.
Good break. Let's take that care onto the road too.
A familiar voice makes leaving a little easier.
The ordinary comforts have done their work. We should let ourselves appreciate it.
The domestic interlude ends with a small blessing rather than a grand command.
A well-rested departure. I approve of the improvement.
We can check the route calmly now that everyone has recovered.
A little warmth can follow us past the threshold.
I like that she makes caring sound ordinary instead of exceptional.
I'd turn back for a proper goodbye before walking off.

contexts.subject: Mom offers a simple goodbye during the early home visit.

replies.text: A little goodbye with the next hello already tucked inside it.
An expected return changes the feeling of a departure.
We'll be back. Take the road carefully.
I like the quiet certainty in see you.
A familiar person expecting you back is a good reason to look after yourself.
The scene closes without pretending the relationship has ended.
A concise farewell. Even I can leave that without an awkward reply.
We can let her know if the day's plans change.
A door can stay open in the sound of a goodbye.
It is warm without trying to hold us in place.
I'd wave so she doesn't have to wonder whether we heard.

contexts.subject: After the flying Pokemon broadcast and color choice, Mom marvels that unknown Pokemon remain.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_StillUnknownPokemon.text: MOM: Well, isn't that something!\nThere are still unknown POKéMON.$

replies.text: Even the familiar sky still has somebody nobody can quite introduce yet.
A well-known region can retain undocumented or poorly understood life.
Interesting report. We'll keep our eyes open without chasing every rumor.
I like that a quiet evening at home can suddenly make the outside feel enormous.
A good discovery starts with noticing, not deciding the answer before meeting it.
The world interrupts a domestic evening to announce an unfinished cast list.
The catalog has failed to eliminate surprise. Excellent news.
We should distinguish the actual sighting from the uncertain identification.
A familiar window can still open onto something unnamed.
Her delight makes the unknown feel inviting rather than something to possess.
I'd ask what she imagines when she hears about it.

contexts.subject: After giving Running Shoes, Mom celebrates the first partner and offers home as a refuge.

LittlerootTown_Text_ComeHomeIfAnythingHa.text:
… … … … … … … …
… … … … … … … …\pTo think that you have your very own
POKéMON now…\lYour father will be overjoyed.\p…But please be careful.
If anything happens, you can come home.\pGo on, go get them, honey!$

replies.text: She is proud, worried, and helping our feet anyway. That's a lot of love in one goodbye.
Her support combines practical equipment with an available place to recover.
Take the encouragement and the warning. We don't have to be brave every minute.
I like being sent out without being made to feel we have to stay away.
We should bring ourselves and the partner home for a good rest sometimes.
The departure is blessed by someone who also keeps the return path open.
An adventure approved with a sensible right of withdrawal.
Good shoes help, but the pace should still fit the team's condition.
A loving hand can help tie the shoes and still let the road begin.
Her pride doesn't make her forget the ordinary person doing the walking.
I'd look back once before the house slips out of sight.

contexts.subject: The rival mother welcomes the new neighbor and points toward her child upstairs.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_OhYoureTheNewNeighbo.text:
Oh, hello. And you are?\p… … … … … … … … …
… … … … … … … … …\pOh, you're {PLAYER}{KUN}, our new next-door
neighbor! Hi!\pWe have a {STR_VAR_1} about the same
age as you.\pOur {STR_VAR_1} was excited about making
a new friend.\pOur {STR_VAR_1} is upstairs, I think.$

replies.text: Our arrival has been turned into somebody else's hoped-for new friend.
A shared neighborhood and similar age offer a starting point, not a guaranteed friendship.
Friendly welcome. We can go say hello without making it a big event.
It's reassuring to know the other person may have been nervous about meeting us too.
A kind introduction takes a little of the awkwardness out of a new door.
The neighboring household has prepared a remarkably hopeful welcome for a stranger.
A new acquaintance located one staircase away. Manageable.
We should introduce ourselves instead of assuming they already know everything about us.
Two unfamiliar days can meet through one open doorway.
She makes us sound welcome before we've done anything impressive. I like that.
I'd ask her child's name once more before going upstairs.

contexts.subject: The rival mother describes Birch and their child shared enthusiasm for Pokemon.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_LikeChildLikeFather.text: Like child, like father.\pMy husband is as wild about POKéMON\nas our child.\pIf he's not at his LAB, he's likely\nscrabbling about in grassy places.$

replies.text: This family has apparently inherited a very strong urge to investigate the nearest grass.
A shared interest can be learned and enjoyed across generations.
Good that they share it. Hope they remember to come home too.
She sounds fond of a habit that probably gets mud everywhere.
I'd guess the household has become very good at packing lunches.
The family resemblance is easiest to spot in the direction they both wander.
A hereditary shortage of interest in sitting still.
I'd ask which parts of the work they each enjoy differently.
The same curiosity can grow in more than one familiar face.
Shared interests still leave room for the child to choose a distinct path.
I'd love to hear which one first taught the other something new.

contexts.subject: The rival mother says Pokemon have distracted her child from the player visit.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_TooBusyToNoticeVisit.text: That {RIVAL}!\pI guess our child is too busy with\nPOKéMON to notice that you came\lto visit, {PLAYER}{KUN}.$

replies.text: A very interesting Pokemon can make an entire visitor temporarily invisible.
Focused attention sometimes excludes social signals that would otherwise be obvious.
We can say hello clearly or leave them to the task. No need to take it personally.
I know the feeling of looking up and discovering someone has been waiting.
A gentle reminder works better than treating it like an insult.
The engrossed scholar has accidentally edited the visitor out of the room.
An impressive field of selective perception.
We could ask when would be a less distracting time to visit.
A mind following one bright thing may miss the quiet knock beside it.
I would give them a chance to notice without making them feel scolded.
I'd ask what has caught their attention so completely.

contexts.subject: The rival mother directs the player to Route 103 and fondly notes the family restlessness.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_WentOutToRoute103.text: Oh, {RIVAL} went out to ROUTE 103\njust a little while ago.\pLike father, like child.\n{RIVAL} can't stay quietly at home.$

replies.text: A specific route is much better than somewhere with grass.
A recent departure and named destination provide a useful search lead.
Route 103. We can prepare for the trip before following.
It's nice to have someone know where the person we want went.
I'd check our supplies rather than turn a visit next door into an unplanned hungry walk.
The absent character has left us a reasonably specific next page.
The family's outdoor tendency has once again outpaced the visitor.
We should learn the route's layout before assuming it is a short errand.
A friend's trail can lead a little beyond the familiar houses.
She sounds used to the movement without being cross about it.
I'd ask which way they usually enter the route.

contexts.subject: The rival mother encourages travel but advises reassuring the player mother with home visits.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_ShouldGoHomeEverySoO.text:
I think it's wonderful for people to
travel with POKéMON.\pBut you should go home every so often
to let your mother know you're okay.\pShe might not say it, but I'm sure she
worries about you, {PLAYER}{KUN}.$

replies.text: A short hello at home can be a very large answer to someone else's quiet worry.
Regular contact reduces uncertainty without requiring the journey to stop.
Good advice. We can let home know we're all right.
It's easy to forget how long a quiet afternoon can feel to the person waiting.
A message and a meal together can do both people good.
The traveler is reminded that departure leaves another story running at home.
A sensible requirement for occasionally reporting that we remain intact.
We could agree on a check-in rather than leave the timing to chance.
A far road can keep one small thread tied to a familiar door.
Reassurance is kindest when we offer it before somebody has to ask.
I'd ask when our mother last had a clear update from us.

contexts.subject: The rival sibling asks whether the new neighbor already has a Pokemon.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_DoYouHavePokemon.text: Hi, neighbor!\pDo you already have your\nown POKéMON?$

replies.text: In this neighborhood, asking about your Pokemon seems to come right after hello.
The question opens a concrete topic between unfamiliar people.
Easy enough to answer. We can introduce the partner if they're comfortable.
I like having something kind to talk about when names still feel new.
A friendly question can make a doorway feel less like somebody else's territory.
The new neighbor receives the locally standard preliminary interview.
A social introduction with an appealingly specific subject.
We can explain what we've learned about our particular partner so far.
A small curious question can make room for a new friendship.
They are interested without assuming what we should have done already.
I'd ask whether they have a favorite Pokemon too.

contexts.subject: May nervously welcomes the new neighbor, hopes for friendship, then remembers helping Birch.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_MayWhoAreYou.text:
Huh?
Who… Who are you?\p… … … … … … … …
… … … … … … … …\pOh, you're {PLAYER}{KUN}.
So your move was today.\pUm… I'm MAY.
Glad to meet you!\pI…
I have this dream of becoming friends\lwith POKéMON all over the world.\pI… I heard about you, {PLAYER}{KUN}, from
my dad, PROF. BIRCH.\pI was hoping that you would be nice,
{PLAYER}{KUN}, and that we could be friends.\pOh, this is silly, isn't it?
I… I've just met you, {PLAYER}{KUN}.\pEheheh…\pOh, no! I forgot!\pI was supposed to go help Dad catch
some wild POKéMON!\p{PLAYER}{KUN}, I'll catch you later!$

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_MayWhoAreYou.text:
Huh?
Who… Who are you?\p… … … … … … … …
… … … … … … … …\pOh, you're {PLAYER}{KUN}.
So your move was today.\pUm… I'm MAY.
Glad to meet you!\pI…
I have this dream of becoming friends\lwith POKéMON all over the world.\pI… I heard about you, {PLAYER}{KUN}, from
my dad, PROF. BIRCH.\pI was hoping that you would be nice,
{PLAYER}{KUN}, and that we could be friends.\pOh, this is silly, isn't it?
I… I've just met you, {PLAYER}{KUN}.\pEheheh…\pOh, no! I forgot!\pI was supposed to go help Dad catch
some wild POKéMON!\p{PLAYER}{KUN}, I'll catch you later!$

replies.text: She managed a hello, a whole dream, and an overdue errand in one nervous breath.
She states a wish for friendship without pretending the relationship already exists.
Friendly start. Let her get to her work; we can talk again.
I understand saying too much because you really want the first meeting to go well.
It's sweet that she hoped we'd be nice before she knew anything impressive about us.
An earnest introduction briefly races ahead of its own confidence.
A charmingly crowded sentence has remembered its appointment at last.
We can meet again when neither person has somewhere else to rush.
A small beginning can be bright without knowing what it will become.
I'd meet the openness gently instead of teasing the nervousness.
I'd remember the dream she chose to tell a stranger first.

contexts.subject: Brendan corrects his assumption about the neighbor gender, offers catching help, and remembers his errand.

RivalsHouse_1F_Text_BrendanWhoAreYou.text:
Hey!
You…\pWho are you?\pOh, you're {PLAYER}, aren't you?
Moved in next door, right?\pI didn't know that you're a girl.\pDad, PROF. BIRCH, said that our new
next-door neighbor is a GYM LEADER's\lkid, so I assumed you'd be a guy.\pMy name's BRENDAN.
So, hi, neighbor!\pHuh? Hey, {PLAYER}, don't you have
a POKéMON?\pDo you want me to go catch you one?\pAw, darn, I forgot…\pI'm supposed to go help my dad catch
some wild POKéMON.\pSome other time, okay?$

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_BrendanWhoAreYou.text:
Hey!
You…\pWho are you?\pOh, you're {PLAYER}, aren't you?
Moved in next door, right?\pI didn't know that you're a girl.\pDad, PROF. BIRCH, said that our new
next-door neighbor is a GYM LEADER's\lkid, so I assumed you'd be a guy.\pMy name's BRENDAN.
So, hi, neighbor!\pHuh? Hey, {PLAYER}, don't you have
a POKéMON?\pDo you want me to go catch you one?\pAw, darn, I forgot…\pI'm supposed to go help my dad catch
some wild POKéMON.\pSome other time, okay?$

replies.text: He guessed wrong, introduced himself, offered a Pokemon, and remembered work. Busy hello.
The initial assumption was unsupported. At least the real introduction can begin now.
Now he knows who we are. We can take the friendly offer in that spirit.
I think we'd both do better with a quieter second conversation.
Being a Gym Leader's child doesn't tell somebody everything about you.
An introduction has survived several rapid revisions and an interrupted act of generosity.
A remarkable amount of mistaken certainty in the opening minute. Recoverable.
We can learn about each other directly instead of leaning on family descriptions.
A first impression can be corrected while the door is still open.
I'd let him move past the mistake while keeping room for us to be ourselves.
I'd ask about the errand next time, when he isn't rushing to remember it.

contexts.subject: May checks her Pokemon and packed items before leaving.

replies.text: An adventure beginning with a checklist. My favorite kind of preventable disaster prevention.
Checking readiness before departure reduces avoidable field problems.
Good routine. Finish the check before getting distracted.
It's a reassuring little sound, hearing someone make sure they're ready.
I'd add something to eat before the list is declared complete.
The thrilling expedition pauses for its deservedly boring preparations.
A heroic inventory of basic competence. Refreshing.
A consistent check helps more than trusting a vague feeling of readiness.
The first careful step can happen before the front door.
I'd let her finish rather than make her start the count again.
I'd ask what she always checks twice before a long outing.

contexts.subject: Brendan checks restored Pokemon and equipment before leaving.

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_BrendanGettingReady.text: POKéMON fully restored…\nItems all packed, and…$

replies.text: His feet may be ready, but he's sensibly asking the bag and the team as well.
Independent checks of team condition and equipment cover different failure modes.
Good. An early check beats a late walk back.
I like the quiet pause before a place stops feeling nearby.
I'd make sure the water and food got the same attention as the Balls.
The would-be explorer begins with the unromantic art of not forgetting things.
Preparation has interrupted haste before haste becomes a story.
I'd keep the checklist short enough to use every time.
A journey is helped by the small things we remember before it begins.
He is taking the partner's condition into account before his own eagerness.
I'd ask what he learned to pack after the last unexpected problem.

contexts.subject: May reviews uncaught and potentially evolving Pokemon while considering another trip.

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_MayJustCheckingMyPok.text:
MAY: {PLAYER}{KUN}!\pI was just checking my POKéDEX.\pThere's still a lot of POKéMON that
I've seen but haven't caught.\pAnd there are many others that
I think will evolve.\pI wonder where I should go catch
some POKéMON next?$

replies.text: Her list contains both places to go and possibilities already sitting beside her.
Missing observations may come from travel or from following the development of known partners.
Good to review what she already has before rushing out for more.
A quiet look at old notes can make the next day feel full of possibilities.
I'd give the team time to settle before deciding on another long trip.
The field notes suggest several next chapters, including one much closer to home.
The catalog has become an itinerary with several competing destinations.
We can separate what needs a different habitat from what needs patient raising.
A familiar creature may still hold a future we haven't met.
It's nice that growth counts as a discovery, not only the new arrival.
I'd ask which possible evolution she is most curious to see.

contexts.subject: Brendan takes pride in his growing Pokedex and feels eager to travel again.

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_BrendanJustCheckingM.text: BRENDAN: Hey, it's {PLAYER}.\pI was just checking out my POKéDEX.\pThere are still many POKéMON that\nI need to catch, I know, but this\lis looking pretty good.\pChecking this POKéDEX out gives me\nthe urge to hit the road again.$

replies.text: The pages have done the dangerous thing of reminding his shoes they have a job.
Reviewing completed observations can motivate the next round of fieldwork.
Good progress. Plan the next outing before the urge makes all the decisions.
I like seeing someone pleased with what's there as well as curious about what's missing.
Enjoy the return home long enough to restock and rest.
The record of past adventures has begun recruiting him for another.
An encyclopedia with a suspiciously effective ability to make people stand up.
He can choose the next question from the notes rather than wander without a purpose.
A small page can hold enough remembered road to make a room feel brief.
Pride in the effort is healthy when it doesn't forbid a pause.
I'd ask which entry brings back the clearest memory for him.

contexts.subject: May wonders where to search and imagines unexpectedly meeting the player.

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_MayWhereShouldIGoNex.text: MAY: I wonder where I should go catch\nsome POKéMON next?\pWouldn't it be funny if we ran into each\nother, {PLAYER}{KUN}?$

replies.text: A big region can suddenly feel small when a familiar face appears on the path.
Overlapping interests make an unplanned meeting more plausible than pure chance.
Could happen. We'd stop to say hello.
I like the thought of somebody hoping to run into us out there.
An unexpected friend is a good reason to pack one extra little snack.
The next setting may include a pleasantly unscheduled reunion.
A coincidence that would at least have sensible geographic reasons.
We can tell her our rough plans without needing to turn it into an appointment.
Two wandering paths can keep a little room for crossing.
She makes the possible meeting sound warm rather than competitive.
I'd ask where she'd most enjoy taking a quiet break if we did meet.

contexts.subject: Brendan considers a catching trip and offers a friendly battle if paths cross.

RivalsHouse_2F_Text_BrendanWhereShouldIG.text: BRENDAN: I'm having a hard time deciding\nwhere I should catch POKéMON next.\pHey, {PLAYER}, if I see you while I'm out\ncatching POKéMON, I can pitch you a\lbattle if you'd like.$

replies.text: In Brendan's version of a chance meeting, hello comes with a battle attached.
The offer is conditional and optional. No challenge has been accepted yet.
A friendly battle's fine if both teams are ready when we meet.
I'd like enough warning to make sure everyone is comfortable first.
We can have a good meeting even if the partners need a break.
The prospective reunion has an optional action scene penciled in.
A social plan with remarkably predictable escalation.
I'd check our partners' condition instead of treating the encounter itself as consent.
Two paths can cross without either being required to clash.
It's nice that he leaves room for whether we'd actually like to.
I'd ask where he plans to explore, then see what the day brings.

contexts.subject: The player declines a rating; Birch assumes the record is too small to review.

gBirchDexRatingText_Cancel.text: Hm? Oh, you haven't caught enough\nPOKéMON to make it worthwhile.$

replies.text: We said not now, not please estimate the contents of our book without opening it.
Declining a review doesn't establish how many observations we have collected.
We can choose when to show him. No explanation needed.
I might simply not feel like being assessed today.
A quiet visit can stay a quiet visit without a report attached.
A bold conclusion from a closed book. Even I usually open the first page.
The unexamined record has received a remarkably confident preliminary review.
We can return when we actually want the feedback.
A page does not become empty because it isn't offered to another pair of eyes.
He could let a refusal remain a refusal instead of dressing it as inadequacy.
I'd tell him we'll ask when we're ready and leave it there.

contexts.subject: Birch recommends more careful observation in grassy habitats.

gBirchDexRatingText_LessThan10.text: Go into grassy areas more and look\nfor POKéMON more carefully.$

replies.text: The grass probably has more to show us if we stop treating every patch like a hallway.
Slower observation can reveal species missed during a direct crossing.
Look carefully and keep a safe path. No need to rush the early learning.
A small movement is easier to see when you give the place a quiet moment.
I'd take enough supplies to stay comfortably instead of hurrying back hungry.
The advice costs nothing but attention, which is inconveniently easy to spend elsewhere.
An invitation to stare at grass with academic intent. Acceptable.
We can compare edges, dense patches, and different times rather than repeat one approach.
A green place can become unfamiliar when we really begin to look.
The useful part is care in looking, not making the first page seem embarrassing.
I'd start by noting which sounds come from which parts of the grass.

contexts.subject: Birch recognizes emerging catching skill but warns later work becomes harder.

gBirchDexRatingText_LessThan20.text: I guess you're getting the hang\nof it. But, it gets harder from here.$

replies.text: We've learned the first handful of tricks. The Pokemon have apparently saved more tricks for later.
Early fluency is progress, even when the remaining cases are less familiar.
Good start. Keep preparing instead of assuming every meeting will be the same.
I like being allowed to feel pleased before hearing what still lies ahead.
The next difficult bit will be easier with a rested team and steady habits.
An encouraging review with the sensible warning that the world has not run out of surprises.
Competence has arrived. Convenient universal competence remains unavailable.
We can build on the method while adapting it for different situations.
A first sure step is still worth taking before the road bends.
Growing confidence should leave room for questions.
I'd ask which later challenge he thinks is most worth preparing for.

contexts.subject: Birch advises persistence because some Pokemon inhabit particular places.

gBirchDexRatingText_LessThan30.text: Some POKéMON only appear in\ncertain areas.\lYou must be persistent.$

replies.text: The missing Pokemon may have very specific ideas about where to receive visitors.
Distribution is uneven. Revisiting the same habitat won't answer every gap.
Try the right place, then give it time.
It helps to know not finding someone doesn't always mean you looked badly.

contexts.subject: Birch praises the player talent after reviewing many collected entries.

gBirchDexRatingText_LessThan90.text: You've collected this many…\nYour talent is remarkable!$

An eye can learn to notice what it once walked past.

contexts.subject: Birch recommends Safari Zone species not commonly encountered elsewhere.

contexts.subject: Birch marks a major hundred-kind milestone and praises the record.

gBirchDexRatingText_LessThan110.text: You've finally reached\nthe 100-kind mark.\pThis is an impressive POKéDEX!$

replies.text: That is a wonderfully large pile of different hellos.

contexts.subject: Birch suggests Pokemon encounters inside breakable rocks.

contexts.subject: Birch recommends exchanges with other Trainers to broaden the record.

A different journey can place a new familiar face beside our own.

contexts.subject: Birch mentions Pokemon whose evolution follows strong affection for their Trainers.

gBirchDexRatingText_LessThan140.text: I've heard of POKéMON that evolve\nwhen they come to fully love their\lTRAINERS.$

replies.text: Some growth needs a friend-shaped reason to feel ready.

Quiet care, repeated patiently, matters more than demanding a quick result.
A transformation has a relationship at its center rather than an impressive special effect.
Affection produces an unusually tangible change of circumstances.

A living thing can unfold differently when it knows it belongs.

replies.text: Even the professor has looked at the list and discovered the region had more room than expected.

replies.text: Some neighbors apparently choose the same day to become very easy to notice.

contexts.subject: Birch praises the record as a useful picture of Hoenn Pokemon.
