Four matches deserve a ready team and enough time.
The ambitious ensemble scene has accepted a postponement.
A refusal that survived without a compulsory emotional sequel.
We can assess supplies before committing to a long sequence.
A path can stay open without being the next path we take.
Good manners make a challenging invitation much more appealing.
I'd remember the easy welcome when we're actually ready for the whole family.

contexts.subject: A traveler warns the Elite Four exceed Gym Leaders and require preparation.

Route111_Text_ToughToKeepWinningUpTheRan.text: If you don't raise your POKéMON some\nmore, it could be tough to keep winning\lup through the ranks.\pI've heard the POKéMON LEAGUE's\nELITE FOUR are far stronger than\lany GYM LEADER.$

replies.text: The next rung is apparently several rungs wearing one coat.
Different levels of challenge can expose gaps familiar matches don't.
Prepare before climbing. Don't let a winning streak rush us.
A bigger challenge feels less frightening when we can plan for it.
The team needs care as well as stronger options.
A successful early chapter doesn't automatically supply the finale's answer.
The homework has acquired an intimidating committee.
We can identify what the current team hasn't yet had to handle.
A far goal can be approached without demanding the future arrive today.
Confidence fits better when the preparation has room to grow.
I'd ask which part of the harder challenge people most often underestimate.

contexts.subject: A traveler struggled through four consecutive Winstrate matches.

Route111_Text_WinstrateFamilyDestroyedMe.text: I challenged the WINSTRATE family,\nbut four matches in a row is tough\lgoing… They destroyed me.$

replies.text: A family gathering with an unusually unforgiving guest itinerary.
Consecutive battles test endurance and resource management as well as individual skill.
Four in a row is rough. Rest before another try.
That sounds discouraging after hoping for one manageable challenge.
The team deserves recovery before discussing what went wrong.
An ensemble has turned a visit into an exhausting serial.
A persuasive argument against accepting every household invitation at once.
He could review where supplies or coverage first became limiting.
A long ordeal can feel different from one isolated defeat.
A rough experience doesn't need to become his whole reputation.
I'd listen for which match changed the day from difficult to overwhelming.

contexts.subject: A hiker describes an intermittently visible sand tower.

Route111_Text_ShouldBeMirageTowerAroundH.text: There should be a tower made of sand\naround here somewhere.\pBut for some reason, it can be seen\nsometimes, and sometimes not.\pThat's why I call it the MIRAGE TOWER.$

replies.text: A tower that refuses to keep ordinary opening hours.
Changing visibility makes repeated observation useful before drawing conclusions.
Keep bearings. Don't chase a glimpse blindly.
It must be strange knowing a place by when you can't see it.
A search out here still needs water and a way back.
A setting has developed the temperament of a highly selective guest star.
Architecture with an unusually private social schedule.
I'd compare conditions whenever it becomes visible.
An absent shape can still leave a place full of questions.
A landmark that changes the whole view by disappearing is remarkable.
I'd love to see the moment someone first realizes the empty space has changed.

contexts.subject: The hiker has not seen the sand tower since our last conversation.

Route111_Text_MirageTowerHasntBeenSeenSi.text: Since I spoke to you, the tower of sand\nhasn't been seen.\pPerhaps it really was\nthe MIRAGE TOWER…$

replies.text: The tower has maintained its very exclusive relationship with visibility.
Not seeing it again doesn't by itself settle what it was.
Keep the memory. Don't turn the absence into proof.
An unseen place can feel stranger after you've talked about it.
He can keep looking without wearing himself out over it.
The mystery has supplied an interval instead of another appearance.
A building has managed to become even less socially available.
We could note the last confirmed sighting and compare later conditions.
An empty space can hold the shape of something remembered.
The missing view may be as memorable as the original glimpse.
I'd ask which detail he still sees most clearly when the tower isn't there.

contexts.subject: The hiker is startled by falling sand and asks about the tower interior.

Route111_Text_ThatWasShockingSandRainedD.text:
Whoa…
That was shocking.\pSand rained down in chunks all of
a sudden.\pWhat was it like inside?
Were there sandy ghosts and such?$

replies.text: A very dramatic weather report from what used to be architecture.
Firsthand observations would be more useful than his guess about ghosts.
Make sure everyone's safe before telling the story.
He sounds excited and shaken at once.
A safe return matters more than making the inside sound impressive.
The setting has given its audience an unexpectedly physical ending.
A sandstorm with an unusually specific source of dramatic timing.
I'd describe what actually happened before theorizing about the unseen.
A crumbling place deserves a little quiet after the surprise.
Curiosity can wait for the travelers to recover their footing.
I'd remember the sound and sudden movement before trying to make it a grand tale.

contexts.subject: The hiker sees the fragile tower but fears entering.

Route111_Text_MirageTowerClearlyVisible.text:
I see it!
The tower of sand!\pThe sand tower they called a mirage
is clearly visible!\pBut it looks so fragile…
It could crumble away anytime…\pI want to go inside it, but I can't
get my courage up for it…$

replies.text: A building can be impressive without being a sensible invitation.
Visible fragility is relevant evidence, not a failure of courage.
He doesn't have to go inside. Trust the warning signs.
It's all right to enjoy the view without proving anything to it.
Staying safe doesn't make the outing less worthwhile.
A remarkable setting needn't demand its admirer become the next protagonist.
Admiration from a sensible distance remains a valid artistic response.
Assess stability before treating access as permission.
A thing can be beautiful and still ask us not to approach.
The outline is striking enough without turning it into a test.
I'd rather watch the changing shape than urge him across a boundary he feels.

contexts.subject: A traveler forgot an uncle's Rock Smash advice and identifies his house.

Route111_Text_MauvilleUncleToldMeToTakeR.text: Oh, no!\pMy uncle in MAUVILLE told me to take\nROCK SMASH with me if I was going to\lROUTE 111!\pMy uncle? He lives across from\nthe bike shop in MAUVILLE.$

replies.text: The advice has arrived in memory slightly after the rocks.
Prior route information can prevent a predictable access problem.
Remember it for the next trip. Don't force the boulders.
It's awkward realizing someone already told you the useful part.
A little list before leaving can save a long return.
The helpful footnote has returned after the obstacle entered the scene.
A family recommendation with belatedly convincing supporting geology.
We can identify the needed capability before planning the next route.
A remembered voice can become useful even when it arrives late.
Practical advice often becomes memorable once it meets an actual inconvenience.
I'd like to know what else his uncle thought worth saying before that trip.

contexts.subject: The Magma guards conclude they must block passage while their crew is away.

Route112_Text_CantLetAnyonePassUntilThey.text: You got it. And until they come back,\nwe're not to let anyone pass, right.$

replies.text: A conversation has turned the road into someone else's waiting room.
Their orders explain the blockage without justifying it.
They don't own the route. Keep that in mind.
It's frustrating having ordinary travel caught inside their plans.
The people needing to pass deserve consideration too.
A side conversation has appointed itself gatekeeper of the whole setting.
An impressive amount of authority borrowed from an absent supervisor.
We should note the condition they mentioned without assuming it's permanent.
A path can be held for a time without belonging to the hands across it.
A uniform doesn't make the inconvenience a fair one.
I'd notice who else is being kept waiting by this little arrangement.

contexts.subject: A hiker weighs descending ledges against difficulty returning to Lavaridge.

Route112_Text_NotEasyToGetBackToLavaridg.text: Eh, I'd like to get to MAUVILLE, but if\nI went down these ledges, it'd be no\leasy matter to get back to LAVARIDGE.$

replies.text: The easy way down has forgotten to include a convenient way up.
A route should be evaluated in both directions before committing.
Check the return first. Saves a hard surprise.
It's strange when one little step can change the whole trip back.
A longer day needs enough supplies to make the return comfortable.
A simple exit has hidden several chapters of its eventual return.
The ledges are offering an extremely one-sided transport agreement.
We can compare the complete loop, not only the next descent.
A path can invite movement without promising to undo it.
Practical footwear won't fix a route that wasn't planned.
I'd trace the whole way back before calling the descent convenient.

contexts.subject: A man marvels at technology turning volcanic ash into glass.

Route113_Text_AshCanBeFashionedIntoGlass.text: Wahahaha! Today's technology is a\nwondrous thing!\pTake this volcanic ash here.\nIt can be fashioned into glass.$

replies.text: The dust in our shoes has a much more elegant career available.
Processing can reveal useful properties in a familiar raw material.
Good use for it. Better than leaving it in everyone's eyes.
It's lovely imagining something clear beginning in all this gray.
A useful craft can give a difficult part of the weather another purpose.
An unpromising background detail has become the central material.
An excellent redemption arc for airborne inconvenience.
I'd love to see the heating and shaping stages in detail.
A rough little thing can hold a clearer future.
The transformation matters as much as the finished shine.
I'd like to compare the raw handful with the glass it becomes.

contexts.subject: A child enjoys seeing footprints while walking through ash.

Route113_Text_FunWalkingThroughAsh.text: It's fun walking through the volcano's\nashes on the ground and grass.\pYou can see where you walked--it's\nreally neat!$

replies.text: The ground is keeping a very enthusiastic record of the walk.
A visible trace makes ordinary movement easier to observe.
Enjoy the tracks. Watch where the next step goes.
I like the thought of seeing the path we'd otherwise forget.
A little ordinary discovery can make a long walk fun.
The traveler has become briefly responsible for writing on the setting.
A record of my wandering that requires no additional notebook.
Different steps might reveal interesting patterns in how the surface moves.
A small trace can show that we were here without staying forever.
An accidental pattern can be more charming than a perfect one.
I'd notice how the newest step changes the story already on the ground.

contexts.subject: A man recommends using Berry Crush with friends.

Route114_Text_TryBerryCrushWithFriends.text: You should try the BERRY CRUSH\nmachine with your friends.$

replies.text: An invitation to make a useful mess with company.
A shared process can make coordination part of the enjoyment.
Sounds fine if everyone wants to join.
It's nice having something to do while getting comfortable together.
Making things with friends can be as good as the result.
A social scene benefits from a practical shared task.
A gathering where the machinery can handle some of the small talk.
Timing and clear signals would help the group work smoothly.
A small task can make room for a shared rhythm.
An activity feels welcoming when there's room to learn it awkwardly.
I'd remember who made everybody laugh while they worked.

contexts.subject: A man enjoys deciding whether to plant, use, or keep Berries.

Route114_Text_FunToThinkAboutBerries.text: Which BERRY should be planted?\nShould you use or hoard BERRIES?\pIt's fun to think about.$

replies.text: A small fruit has created a surprisingly full committee agenda.
Different uses make the choice depend on present needs and future plans.
Plan around the team. No need to hoard automatically.
It's nice when a little practical choice is enjoyable instead of stressful.
Growing and using both belong in a well-stocked kitchen.
A modest resource has several entirely plausible plot lines.
A dilemma refreshingly unlikely to destroy a region.
We can reserve what a clear growing plan needs and use the rest sensibly.
A seed can be a beginning without making every meal a lost possibility.
A collection should serve what you enjoy, not become another obligation.
I'd like to see which choice he makes when a favorite Berry is involved.

contexts.subject: A man explains that Roar drives Pokemon away.

Route114_Text_ExplainRoar.text: TM05 contains ROAR.\nA ROAR sends POKéMON scurrying.$

replies.text: A very forceful way to request some personal space.
The move changes the encounter rather than simply adding another hit.
Useful when used carefully. No need to frighten things for fun.
I understand wanting a little distance from an overwhelming situation.
The Pokemon on either side still deserve consideration.
A single line can abruptly change which characters remain in the scene.
A battle technique suspiciously close to my internal social strategy.
We should understand the exact effect before making it part of the plan.
A boundary can be useful without becoming a habit of pushing everyone away.
A strong presence works best when the intention is clear.
I'd notice what the team needs the distance for, not only how dramatically it arrives.

contexts.subject: A traveler contrasts cave suspense with ordinary roads.

Route115_Text_NeverKnowWhenCavePokemonWi.text: Exploring a cave isn't like walking\non a road.\pYou never know when wild POKéMON will\nappear. It's full of suspense.$

replies.text: The cave has a much less predictable guest list than the road.
Visibility and terrain change what we can anticipate about encounters.
Stay ready. Don't let the suspense make the choices.
I can hear every little movement more clearly once I'm expecting something.
Supplies and a safe return route help make uncertainty manageable.
A setting can create tension before a new character ever appears.
Atmosphere is lovely until it starts interrupting every third step.
We can reduce uncertainty through observation without pretending it disappears.
An unknown passage can ask for care rather than fear.
The place deserves preparation beyond looking adventurous.
I'd watch how people move differently once the daylight stops guiding them.

contexts.subject: The tunnel digger is eager to work.

Route116_Text_WantToDigTunnel.text: Nnn… Roar!\pI want to dig that tunnel!$

replies.text: A man with an extremely focused hole-related ambition.
He seems motivated enough to sustain a patient task.
Give the hands a sensible plan before all that enthusiasm.
It's nice hearing someone sound so sure what they want to do.
Work like that needs food and proper breaks too.
A protagonist has announced the central verb of his entire chapter.
An impressive commitment to making somewhere less solid.
The method and conditions matter as much as the willingness.
A clear intention can begin with one careful small action.
Determination works best with equipment that actually fits.
I'd love to hear what opening that tunnel would change in his ordinary day.

contexts.subject: The digger celebrates the thug leaving so work can resume.

Route116_Text_GoonHightailedItOutOfTunne.text: Nnn… Roar!\pThat goofy goon hightailed it out of\nthe tunnel! I can go back to digging!$

replies.text: The tunnel has shed its least useful obstacle.
Removing the disruption lets him return to the intended careful work.
Good. Check the Pokemon are settled before starting again.
He sounds relieved to have his ordinary task back.
A quiet check inside would be kind after all that commotion.
The unwanted subplot has ended, leaving the patient main work intact.
A villain's departure has improved both the mood and the workplace.
We should assess the conditions rather than assume nothing changed.
A familiar purpose can feel newly welcome after being interrupted.
He doesn't need a grand celebration to be clearly pleased.
I'd notice the first moment he relaxes enough to think about the work again.

contexts.subject: The digger fears the intruder will upset noise-sensitive tunnel Pokemon.

Route116_Text_DiggingTunnelWhenGoonOrder.text:
Nnn… Roar!
What's going on?\pI was digging the tunnel without any
tools when some goon ordered me out!\pThat tunnel's filled with POKéMON
that react badly to loud noises.\lThey could cause an uproar.\pThat's why we stopped using heavy
equipment for tunneling…\pI'm worried that the goon will do
something stupid and startle the\lPOKéMON into an uproar.$

replies.text: He stopped the loud machines; the intruder has supplied another kind of racket.
His concern connects the interruption with a known sensitivity in the habitat.
Keep it quiet. Find out what the intruder is doing.
It's upsetting when someone ignores care that took so much patience.
The Pokemon deserve the calm the workers tried to give them.
An unwelcome visitor has disrupted more than the visible work schedule.
An exceptionally poor place to introduce an obnoxious personality.
Observe the disturbance before escalating the noise ourselves.
A sheltered place can hold lives that need a gentler approach.
His frustration makes sense because the quiet was deliberate, not accidental.
I'd listen for how the Pokemon are reacting as well as the man telling us.

contexts.subject: The grateful Devon employee says their new Ball will be sold in Rustboro.

Route116_Text_NewBallAvailableAtMart.text: Our new POKé BALL will be available\nat the POKéMON MART in RUSTBORO.\pPlease do try it out!\nThank you and bye-bye!$

replies.text: Our delivery has produced both gratitude and a product announcement.
A practical availability note lets us decide whether it suits future needs.
Thanks. We'll check what it does before buying more.
It's nice that he remembered us beyond the original errand.
A useful gift can make the return trip feel worthwhile.
A rescue subplot has acquired a very polite commercial epilogue.
An advertisement with actual appreciation attached. Better than most.
We can compare the Ball's purpose with the encounters we plan.
A kindness can return in an unexpectedly ordinary form.
A good recommendation leaves the choice with the person receiving it.

contexts.subject: The employee cannot give his Repeat Ball because our bag is full.

Route116_Text_BagIsJamPacked.text: Your BAG is jam-packed.\nI can't give you this REPEAT BALL.$

replies.text: The gift has arrived. Its accommodation hasn't.
We need enough space before accepting the item.
Make room and return. No need to waste it.

A quick sort could make room without turning the whole visit into a chore.
A generous scene has met the practical limits of its prop storage.
Our luggage has rejected a compliment on purely physical grounds.

A gift can wait while we make a place for it.
An overfull bag doesn't have to become an embarrassing performance.

contexts.subject: Briney is distraught after an intruder abducts Peeko during their walk.

Route116_Text_ScoundrelMadeOffWithPeeko.text: Ohhh, what am I to do?\pWe were on our walk, PEEKO and I, when\nwe were jumped by an odd thug…\pThe scoundrel made off with my\ndarling PEEKO!\pWrrrooooooaaaar! PEEKO!$

His grief is not an opportunity for a clever answer.

A missing presence can make even the familiar road feel wrong.

contexts.subject: A man asks for help finding dropped glasses.

Route116_Text_CanYouHelpMeFindGlasses.text: I dropped my glasses…\nCan you help me find them?$

replies.text: A search made inconvenient by needing the very thing being searched for.
A systematic look near the last known location should help.
Worth a look. Ask where he last had them.
It's a small loss that can make everything else harder.
A patient extra pair of eyes could be a real help.
A minor prop has acquired an unusually important role in the scene.
A missing object with an unkindly circular effect on finding it.
We can check one area thoroughly before widening the search.
A little practical help can steady a frustrating moment.
Useful things rarely feel as ordinary once they go missing.

Route116_Text_CantFindGlassesNotHere.text: Hmm…\nI can't find my glasses anywhere…\lMaybe they're not around here…$

replies.text: The search has exhausted this patch before exhausting the whole world.

Retrace the route. Don't keep circling without a clue.

contexts.subject: The man identifies our BlackGlasses as unrelated to his lost pair.

Route116_Text_NotWhatImLookingFor.text: Hmm…\nThese are BLACKGLASSES.\lThey're not what I'm looking for…$

replies.text: Right category, very confidently wrong glasses.
A resemblance isn't enough to establish that an object is his.

A promising clue has politely resigned from the central mystery.
A false lead with unusually good manners.
The mismatch may help clarify what details distinguish his own pair.
A small disappointment can leave the next question clearer.
The name alone wasn't going to settle whether the style was right.

contexts.subject: After checking BlackGlasses, the man decides to search elsewhere.

Route116_Text_NotWhatImLookingForMaybeTh.text: Hmm…\nThese are BLACKGLASSES.\lThey're not what I'm looking for…\pMaybe my glasses aren't around\nhere…$

replies.text: The glasses are innocent, and this part of the route is being released.

Try the last sure spot. Don't blame the wrong pair.
I hope a new place makes the search feel less stuck.
A little patience is worth more than rushing past everything again.
The false clue has helped the story move out of the room.
An empty conclusion, but at least it has a direction.
He can note what differs before widening the search.
A missing thing can ask us to remember more carefully, not only look harder.
He shouldn't have to make the disappointment look tidy.
I'd want to know whether he remembers taking them off somewhere rather than dropping them.

contexts.subject: A gardener proudly shows the flowers they planted.

Route117_Text_ArentTheseFlowersPretty.text: What do you think?\nAren't these flowers pretty?\pI planted them all!$

replies.text: A very colorful answer to what patient hands can do.
The visible garden carries the results of repeated care.

It's lovely being shown something someone made grow.
A tended patch can make the whole route feel welcoming.
The creator has invited us to notice the finished scene.
A proud introduction with excellent natural supporting detail.

A little care can become somewhere many people enjoy passing.

contexts.subject: A traveler delightedly describes the air as tasty.

replies.text: A five-star meal with absolutely no washing up.
That sounds like an enthusiastic description of the fresh air.
Good place for a breather, apparently.
I know the feeling, even if I wouldn't have found those words.
Fresh air can make an ordinary break feel wonderful.

An excellent menu for someone uninterested in making a decision.

An odd compliment, but a very sincere one.

contexts.subject: A traveler was surprised their Pokemon learned a move at Day Care.

Route117_Text_DayCarePokemonHadNewMove.text: I left my POKéMON at the DAY CARE.\pWhen I got it back, it had a new move\nthat I didn't teach it.\lI was really, really surprised.$

replies.text: The Pokemon returned with homework completed nobody remembered assigning.
Growth can alter a moveset while a partner is away.
Check what changed before the next battle.
It must be strange realizing they had their own little experience without you.
I'd spend some ordinary time together getting familiar again.
A supporting character has developed during an off-page chapter.
A quiet absence has apparently been extremely productive.
We should test the new capability rather than assume the old plan still fits.
A familiar companion can return with a small unknown part.
Change can be interesting even when it wasn't on the original schedule.

contexts.subject: The fisherman encourages trying our new rod anywhere there is water.

Route118_Text_TryYourLuckFishing.text: Wherever there's water, try your luck\nat fishing.$

replies.text: A new hobby with a very large selection of possible addresses.
Different locations could offer different encounters worth comparing.
Choose a safe place. Learn the rod before getting ambitious.
A quiet first try sounds rather nice.
A packed snack helps when the fish aren't following the schedule.
An ordinary patch of water has become the start of another kind of scene.

Start with a clear casting area and a manageable position.
A little waiting can make a familiar shore feel new.
The outing doesn't need a spectacular catch to suit us.

contexts.subject: The fisherman interprets our disagreement as disliking fishing.

replies.text: One answer has been promoted into our entire aquatic biography.
Disagreeing about the rod doesn't establish a general dislike.
Can choose not to. No explanation required.

A declined prop needn't remove the whole activity from the character's future.

contexts.subject: The fisherman encourages varied catches using our Good Rod.

Route118_Text_TryCatchingMonWithGoodRod.text: Try catching all sorts of POKéMON\nwith your GOOD ROD.$

replies.text: The rod has a rather ambitious social calendar now.

An expanded guest list with a substantial amount of waiting between arrivals.

An unexpected meeting can matter without becoming a possession.

contexts.subject: A girl appreciates Pokemon enabling sea and river crossings.

Route118_Text_CanCrossRiversWithSurf.text: Even if there isn't a boat, you can\ncross rivers and the sea if you have\la POKéMON that knows SURF.\pPOKéMON can be counted on to do so\nmuch!$

replies.text: A very loyal bridge with its own lunch preferences.

A shared journey can be held up by an ordinary act of trust.

I'd notice the little signals that tell us how comfortable the Pokemon is.

contexts.subject: Steven leaves room to raise favorites or many kinds of Pokemon.

Route118_Text_StevenQuestions.text:
STEVEN: Hi, {PLAYER}{KUN}!\pIt's me, STEVEN!
We met in the cave near DEWFORD.\pHave you met many kinds of POKéMON
since I last saw you?\pThere are many, many kinds of POKéMON
in this wide world of ours.\pIf you wanted to raise only your
favorites, that's fine.\pPerhaps you find it more fun to raise

contexts.subject: Scott praises our rival victory and predicts success at Fortree Gym.

Route119_Text_ScottWayToGoBeSeeingYou.text:
SCOTT: Hahahah!
Way to go, {PLAYER}{KUN}!\pI just passed by a TRAINER riding
a BIKE.\pYou just beat that TRAINER, didn't you?
It was pretty obvious that you did.\pThe kid looked really upset with
a face all red from anger.\pI sure seem to run into you often.
Are you off to FORTREE GYM next?\pI expect that you'll do well at the GYM.
Well, I'll be seeing you!$

replies.text: Scott has an astonishing talent for arriving just after the difficult bit.

Good to hear. The other kid deserves some space too.

A hard match shouldn't make the loser into the whole joke.

It's strange recognizing a harmless memory inside this group.
Waiting can make people talk about surprisingly ordinary things.
The antagonist has briefly stepped outside the role to remember a normal afternoon.
An oddly relatable footnote in an otherwise unappealing organization.
The similarity explains the feeling, not the purpose of the gathering.
An ordinary life can remain visible beneath a chosen uniform.
A shared small experience doesn't make every larger choice the same.
I'd remember how normal the voice became for that one little recollection.

contexts.subject: An Aqua member resents queueing and paying museum admission.

SlateportCity_Text_WhyAreWeLiningUp.text: Why are we even lining up and paying?\nWe should just march in!$

replies.text: The ticket office has encountered a very entitled review.
Shared access works better when everyone respects the same conditions.
Pay like everyone else. They don't own the place.
It's unpleasant hearing ordinary courtesy treated as an obstacle.
The people keeping the museum open deserve support.
An unwanted guest has objected to the plot's basic rules of entry.
A uniform has apparently been mistaken for an exemption card.
Admission and capacity rules serve more people than the impatient visitor.
A common doorway can ask for patience without becoming unfair.
A confident entrance isn't worth much if it ignores everyone waiting.
I'd notice the people doing the actual work while he complains about the fee.

contexts.subject: An Aqua member brusquely asks what we want.

replies.text: A greeting with all the cushioning removed.
A direct question can still be answered without matching the hostility.
Keep it brief. No need to make it a quarrel.
I'd rather give a simple answer than defend my whole presence.
A little space can keep a sharp moment from growing.
A minor confrontation needn't be promoted into a full scene.
A wonderfully efficient demonstration of social unavailability.
We can state the practical reason and watch the response.
A harsh first word needn't choose the shape of every word after it.
He can be answered plainly without rewarding the attitude.
I'd notice whether the answer changes how he sees us at all.

contexts.retired: Always followed by the museum sign-reading sequence; its final paraphrase is separately bound.

contexts.subject: An Aqua member uncertainly paraphrases the museum sign for us.

SlateportCity_Text_SaysSomethingLikeSeaI.text: Let's see…\pUm… I think it says something like\n“the life in the sea is endless.”\pYup, I'm pretty sure that's what\nit says.$

replies.text: A very confident service with a slightly improvised final answer.
He marks uncertainty, which is useful; we could read the actual wording too.
Worth checking the sign ourselves.
It's kind of funny watching someone try to sound sure while guessing.
A plain I don't know would be easier to work with.
A reluctant narrator has introduced a suspiciously approximate quotation.
The performance is more certain than the reading comprehension.
We should distinguish the visible text from his interpretation.
A little uncertainty can be admitted without making the person smaller.
The helpful gesture would look better without pretending the guess is exact.
I'd remember his hesitation as part of the answer, not just the words.

contexts.subject: A grunt looks forward to a hot-spring reward promised by the leader.

SlateportCity_Text_HotSpringsAfterOperat.text: When this operation's over, I'll take\nyou to a hot spring spa!\pThat's what our leader said.\nI can't wait!$

replies.text: A pleasant reward shouldn't make the assignment stop needing questions.
An incentive doesn't establish that the work itself is justified.
Think about what they're doing first. Spa can wait.
He sounds genuinely excited about the ordinary good part.
A treat shouldn't cost other people their peace.
A comforting epilogue has been offered before anyone reviews the preceding harm.
The recruitment package has discovered warm water.
Evaluate the task independently from the benefit promised afterward.
A hoped-for comfort needn't carry us into an unkind choice.
A lovely destination can't fix an ugly way of getting there.
I'd notice whether the promise is the only part of the plan he can explain.

contexts.subject: A secretive merchant requires Secret Power before selling group goods.

gText_ComeBackWithSecretPower.text:
Do you know the TM SECRET POWER?\pOur group, we love the TM SECRET
POWER.\pOne of our members will give it to you.
Come back and show me if you get it.\pWe'll accept you as a member and sell
you good stuff in secrecy.$

replies.text: A shopping club with an unusually outdoorsy entrance exam.
The shared skill appears to be their condition for access.
Find out what we need before promising to join.
It's a peculiar invitation, but at least the next step is clear.
Useful things shouldn't make us forget whether the group suits us.
A secret society has revealed itself as remarkably retail-oriented.
An exclusive club with a very practical merchandise department.
We can learn the capability without treating membership as the main reward.
A hidden little gathering can still be approached by choice.
Exclusivity alone doesn't make the goods worth wanting.
I'd be curious what they like making, beyond keeping it secret.

contexts.subject: A resident wonders whether far-reaching lighthouse light startles sea Pokemon.

SlateportCity_Text_WonderIfLighthouseSta.text: The light of the lighthouse reaches\ndozens of miles away.\pI wonder if it doesn't startle POKéMON\nin the sea.$

replies.text: A helpful light can still ask the neighbors how it feels.
It's worth considering the effects of human infrastructure on nearby wildlife.
Good question. Watch what the Pokemon actually do.
I like that they noticed the lives beyond the ships.
A useful thing can be made kinder by paying attention.
The background beacon has acquired a much wider cast of possible observers.
An excellent question about the unintended audience.
Observed responses would help distinguish a concern from an actual disturbance.
A light can guide one traveler while changing another's night.
Good design considers who didn't ask to be part of it.
I'd notice the water around the beam as carefully as the ships following it.

contexts.subject: A vendor explains Berry Crush machines and offers medicine for powder.

SlateportCity_Text_ExplainBerryPowder.text:
I recently had machines installed at
POKéMON CENTERS for crushing BERRIES.\pThe BERRY CRUSH machines are at
the DIRECT CORNER upstairs.\pDid you know?\pCould you make BERRY POWDER for
me using those machines?\pI can make you all sorts of medicine
if you bring me lots of BERRY POWDER.$

replies.text: The Berry has a very useful career beyond sitting in our bag.
Processing ingredients can make their properties useful in a different form.
Worth learning the exchange before gathering everything.
It's nice being shown what a small effort can become.
A good preparation begins with knowing the ingredient and the process.
An ordinary fruit has acquired a surprisingly practical next chapter.
A bazaar with an actual reason to appreciate our modest collecting habits.
We should understand quantities and intended use before starting.
A familiar thing can hold more than one kind of help.
A practical offer is better when the choice stays clear.
I'd enjoy seeing the careful work behind the medicine, not just the counter display.

contexts.subject: The vendor welcomes a later exchange after we leave the powder menu.

SlateportCity_Text_ComeBackToTradeBerryP.text: Come back if you'd like to trade your\nBERRY POWDER for some medicine.\pI'm always running a bazaar here.\pDid you know?$

replies.text: The bazaar has politely survived our indecision.
We can return after checking what the team actually needs.
Another time works. Don't trade just to finish a conversation.
It's nice that leaving doesn't close the welcome.
A considered choice is better than collecting medicine we won't use.
A modest transaction can wait for a more useful role in the story.
An unusually low-pressure farewell from a very informative vendor.
Review supplies before deciding which exchange would help.
A useful offer can remain on the shelf until its moment.
An open invitation is more appealing than a pushed sale.
I'd return knowing what we came for rather than feeling obliged to choose something.

contexts.subject: After an exchange the vendor invites us back with more Berry Powder.

SlateportCity_Text_WhenYouGetMoreBringIt.text: Okay! When you get some more\nBERRY POWDER, bring it to me, please!$

replies.text: A successful swap with a small future supply request attached.
A repeatable exchange can be planned around actual needs.
Good trade. No need to turn every Berry into homework.
It's nice knowing where a future little collection could go.
I'd keep enough for the things the team already uses.
The practical subplot has left a very straightforward sequel route.
A polite invitation to return with a more specific kind of dust.
We can compare the use of the powder with the use of the original Berries.
A small routine can become useful without becoming an obligation.
The best repeat purchase is one that still fits what we need.
I'd remember the welcome without treating it like another task that has to be finished today.

contexts.subject: Scott enthusiastically assumes we will try the Battle Tent.

SlateportCity_Text_TakingBattleTentChall.text:
SCOTT: Oh, hey!
If it isn't {PLAYER}{KUN}!\p{PLAYER}{KUN}, let me guess--you're going
to take the BATTLE TENT challenge?\pYeah! That's a good idea!
That's a really great idea!\pAfter all, a tough TRAINER is
the perfect fit for the BATTLE TENT!\pGive it your best effort!$

replies.text: Scott can turn standing near a door into a very ambitious itinerary.
The format may suit us, but the decision still deserves preparation.
We'll decide when we're ready. Good to hear the support.
It's encouraging, though I don't want to feel rushed by being noticed.
The team needs a comfortable start more than an impressive entrance.
An enthusiastic observer has written the next scene before confirming the protagonist's plans.
His confidence has arrived several steps before our actual schedule.
Learn the rules before accepting his assessment of the fit.
A friendly push can be taken as encouragement without becoming a command.
The invitation works better when it leaves room for our own pace.
I'd like to compare the experience with what he imagined once we've actually tried it.

contexts.subject: The waiter interprets our silence as the strong silent personality type.

SSAnne_1F_Corridor_Text_LeStrongSilentTy.text:
Bonjour!
I am le waiter on this ship!\pI will be happy to serve you
anything you please!\p… … …
Ah! Le strong silent type!$

replies.text: Sometimes silence means confidence. Sometimes it means still reading the menu.
He inferred a personality from a very limited response. Efficient, but not reliable.
Quiet does not always need an explanation.
I would be relieved and embarrassed to have my hesitation handled that neatly.
He is trying to keep the welcome comfortable. Good service instinct.
The waiter supplies a character description when the guest declines to provide dialogue.
An excellent strategy: remain quiet until someone assigns you an impressive motive.
Missing input has been given a very flattering default value.
A little silence has been offered a comfortable chair in the conversation.
He managed the awkward pause kindly. That is a real skill.
I wonder how many different kinds of quiet guest he has met.

contexts.subject: A crew member warns that bored passengers may challenge us.

SSAnne_1F_Corridor_Text_PassengersAreRes.text: The passengers are restless from\nthis long voyage.\pYou might be challenged by the\nmore bored ones!$

replies.text: Cabin fever has apparently developed a battle schedule.
A confined, lengthy trip can leave passengers looking for stimulation.
Keep the team ready. We can choose a quiet room when they need rest.
I would prefer boredom to announce itself without quite so much eye contact.
A relaxed cruise for one person may be an unexpected match for another.
The leisure program has begun recruiting guests directly from the corridor.
A long voyage gives an idle competitive streak far too much room.
Unscheduled challenges likely. Manage resources before exploring every cabin.
The sea keeps people close enough for their restlessness to meet.
A useful warning before the next passenger decides we are entertainment.
I wonder what activities the crew planned before the battles took over.

contexts.subject: A hushed passenger identifies himself as an agent pursuing Team Rocket.

SSAnne_1F_Room1_Text_ImAGlobalPoliceAgen.text: Ssh…!\nI'm a GLOBAL POLICE agent.\pI'm on the trail of TEAM ROCKET.\nThey're up to nothing good!$

replies.text: An undercover introduction with a very short period of remaining under cover.
He claims an investigative role and a specific target. Discretion would be appropriate.
Keep his business quiet. No need to make him easier to spot.
I would feel awkward being told a secret before knowing where to stand.
I hope the investigation keeps the ordinary passengers safe too.
The secret agent announces his secret occupation to the nearest available stranger.
A whisper is not a lock, but we need not make it less private.
Sensitive information volunteered. Avoid redistributing it casually.
A quiet pursuit is moving among the holiday voices.
He sounds serious. We can respond with a little care instead of curiosity alone.
I wonder what led the trail onto this ship.

contexts.subject: Tyler eagerly asks to become friends so we can trade and spend time together.

SSAnne_1F_Room2_Text_TylerPostBattle.text: Listen, listen!\nLet me be your friend, okay?\pThen we can trade POKéMON and\ndo stuff.$

replies.text: A battle has become an enthusiastic application for friendship. Nice turn.
A shared activity can provide a natural start to a new acquaintance.
He can ask. No need to rush the whole friendship in one breath.
That is very direct. I would probably smile before finding an answer.
It is lovely when someone leaves a match wanting more company.
The former opponent proposes a much friendlier sequel.
An awkwardly sincere invitation. Those can be good ones.
Shared interest identified. Start with a manageable conversation.
A little meeting has found somewhere new to grow.
He makes the welcome clear without pretending to be sophisticated about it.
I wonder which Pokemon he would most like to tell a new friend about.

contexts.subject: Ann is upset that her Pokemon were hurt and demands Pokemon Center healing.

SSAnne_1F_Room2_Text_AnnPostBattle.text: You hurt my poor POKéMON!\pI demand that you heal them at a\nPOKéMON CENTER!$

replies.text: A battle should end with care for the partners, even when the complaint comes loudly.
Her concern is legitimate, though responsibility for recovery should not be reduced to an accusation.
Make sure her team gets help. No need to argue over the result.
She sounds more worried about them than about losing.
Getting the partners comfortable matters more than defending anyone's pride.
The match receives an impassioned review from the person watching her team hurt.
A familiar partner looking tired can make every word come out sharply.
Post-battle recovery is the immediate practical requirement.
The fight is finished; the care still has something left to do.
Her fear could use a calm answer rather than another sharp one.
I wonder whether she knows the nearby cabin offers a place to rest.

contexts.subject: A parent describes traveling around the world with their children.

SSAnne_1F_Room2_Text_CruisingAroundWorld.text: We are cruising around the world,\nmy children and I.$

replies.text: A whole family collecting new horizons. That could fill several dinner conversations.
Shared travel can provide children with a broad range of direct experiences.
Hope they are taking the journey at a pace everyone enjoys.
It must be lovely to have those memories belong to all of you.
A familiar family meal can make even a distant port feel less strange.
A family story with an exceptionally expansive choice of settings.
A moving little home, with unfamiliar shores outside it.
A large itinerary needs room for different ages and energy levels.
The world keeps changing beyond the window while the familiar voices stay.
A good trip gives everyone a little say in what they notice.
I wonder which place the children keep talking about.

contexts.subject: A passenger enjoys the cruise's elegance and comfort.

SSAnne_1F_Room3_Text_CruiseIsElegantAndC.text: A world cruise is so elegant yet\ncozy!$

replies.text: Fancy and comfortable at once. A rare treaty between stiff collars and pillows.
The setting combines novelty with a controlled, familiar base of accommodation.
Good to enjoy a journey without having to prove it was uncomfortable.
A place can feel special and still let you relax. I like that.
A comfortable room makes the unfamiliar parts of travel easier to enjoy.
The grand adventure has agreed to provide a soft chair between scenes.
A journey with enough gentleness left in it to feel like rest.
Good comfort design is easy to miss when it works.
A little warm room moving across a very large cool world.
Elegance works best when the people inside it can actually breathe.
I wonder which small part of the ship makes it feel cozy to them.

contexts.subject: A traveler always brings Wigglytuff along.

SSAnne_1F_Room3_Text_AlwaysTravelWithWig.text: I always travel with WIGGLYTUFF.\nI never leave home without it.$

replies.text: A reliable travel companion and an excellent round silhouette in every port.
A familiar partner provides continuity across unfamiliar settings.
Good to have someone who knows you when the place is new.
That sounds less like a habit and more like not wanting to leave a friend behind.
Shared little routines can make any stop feel more like home.
The recurring companion receives a permanent place in every new setting.
A familiar presence can make a strange room feel less borrowed.
Reliable companion, well-practiced routine. Strong travel setup.
Home can sometimes be the one traveling beside you.
The partnership is part of how the traveler sees the world. Lovely.
I wonder which part of the voyage Wigglytuff enjoys most.

contexts.subject: A passenger mistakes us for staff and orders cherry pie.

SSAnne_1F_Room4_Text_WaiterCherryPiePlea.text: Waiter, I would like a cherry pie,\nplease!$

SSAnne_1F_Room4_Text_WaitressCherryPiePl.text: Waitress, I would like a cherry\npie, please!$

replies.text: I also support cherry pie, but my support does not include knowing where the kitchen keeps it.
They have mistaken our role. A brief correction should resolve the request.
Wrong person. Point them toward the actual staff.
I would have to remember I am allowed to explain the mistake.
A good order, delivered to the wrong apron. I sympathize with the craving.
An unexpected casting call for the role of pastry courier.
A stranger has looked at us and seen the possibility of dessert.
Request routed to the wrong service provider. Redirect.
A small wish for sweetness has wandered into our path.
Perhaps we look competent. Perhaps they simply did not look closely.
I wonder whether the cherry pie is as good as the confidence of that order.

contexts.subject: Arthur angrily demands privacy after the battle.

SSAnne_1F_Room5_Text_ArthurPostBattle.text: I wish to be left alone!\nGet out!$

replies.text: The cabin has become a very clear request for fewer visitors.
His wish to end the interaction is unambiguous, despite the harsh delivery.
Leave the room. No reason to give him another excuse.
I would rather let him have his quiet now.
A little space can end the uncomfortable part of this quickly.
The private performance has concluded with an emphatic evacuation notice.
A room with a door is useful for precisely this kind of mood.
Session closed. Best not to keep sending input.
The next useful step is simply outside the cabin.
He could be more courteous. We can still respect the privacy.
I wonder whether he really wanted company at all before the match.

contexts.subject: After resting in the cabin, our host is pleased we and the team look refreshed.

SSAnne_1F_Room6_Text_GladEveryoneIsRefre.text: I'm glad to see that everyone is\nlooking refreshed and chipper.$

replies.text: A little land-like comfort in the middle of the moving water. Much appreciated.
The rest helped the whole traveling group, and the host noticed.
Good help. We should head out only when everyone is ready.
It is lovely to be welcomed as tired people rather than another challenge.
A proper rest is one of the kindest gifts a traveler can get.
The journey resumes after a mercifully gentle interlude.
A strange ship briefly felt like somewhere familiar enough to sleep.
Recovery complete. Helpful condition check before resuming.
A quiet room has put a little steadiness back into the day.
The host's kindness includes the Pokemon. That makes it feel complete.
I wonder how many guests have been relieved to find this cabin.

contexts.subject: When we decline rest, the host explains that we remind them of a younger sibling.

SSAnne_1F_Room6_Text_SorryYouLookLikeMyB.text: Oh, I'm sorry for fussing over you.\nYou look like my little brother…$

SSAnne_1F_Room6_Text_SorryYouLookLikeMyS.text: Oh, I'm sorry for fussing over you.\nYou look like my little sister…$

replies.text: We accidentally borrowed a familiar face and received the family kindness attached to it.
A resemblance prompted a caring offer. There is no harm in declining it.
Kind of them. We can thank them without needing the rest right now.
That is a sweet explanation for fussing over a stranger.
A small family habit has made the ship kinder to someone new.
A passing resemblance has opened the door to a very sincere welcome.
A familiar absence can make a stranger unexpectedly easy to care about.
Offer declined, reason explained, no pressure added. Good interaction.
A remembered face has left a little warmth in this room.
They make the explanation personal without demanding anything back.
I wonder when they last saw the sibling they are thinking of.

contexts.subject: Thomas says we should be kind to friends.

SSAnne_1F_Room7_Text_ThomasPostBattle.text: You should be nice to friends!$

replies.text: A good rule, though losing a battle is not always a failure of friendship.
Kindness matters. It should be distinguished from avoiding every competitive loss.
Agreed. A fair match still needs decent treatment afterward.
A friendship should have room for both trying your best and caring how it felt.
A little care after a difficult game can keep the game worth sharing.
A sound moral with a somewhat broad application to the scoreboard.
Being kind is usually quieter than winning the argument about kindness.
Cooperation and competition can share a room if the boundaries are clear.
A friend should still feel like a friend when the result goes wrong.
A good reminder, provided it works in both directions.
I wonder what kindness looks like to him after a match.

contexts.subject: A crew member describes the liner's international trainer parties at its ports.

SSAnne_2F_Corridor_Text_ThisShipIsLuxury.text: This ship, she is a luxury liner for\nTRAINERS of the world!\pAt every port, we hold parties with\ninvited TRAINERS.$

replies.text: A moving party venue with an ocean-sized hallway between stops.
Regular port events bring together travelers from different training communities.
Sounds lively. Hope there is still somewhere quiet for the teams.
It must be exciting to hear new voices at every stop.
The kitchen must have a very ambitious schedule.
A traveling company gathers a new audience each time the setting changes.
A room of strangers that keeps being rebuilt by the next shore.
Repeated events, changing guest lists. Serious logistical work.
The ship carries a little invitation from one piece of land to the next.
A gathering can feel special when it includes people who rarely share a place.
I wonder which port gives the crew their favorite welcome.

contexts.subject: The rival mentions the seasick Cut master and recommends visiting him.

SSAnne_2F_Corridor_Text_RivalPostBattle.text:
{RIVAL}: I heard there was a CUT
master on board.\pBut he was just a seasick old man!\pCUT itself is really useful.
Yup, it'll be handy.\pYou should go see him, too.
Smell ya!$

replies.text: A useful lead could have traveled without the insult to the poor seasick man.
The practical information is clear: someone aboard can help with Cut. His illness is separate.
We can check on the captain without making fun of him.
It is unkind to turn someone feeling awful into a punchline.
A little help for the sick person should come before asking what he can teach us.
The rival hands us a useful address wrapped in an entirely unnecessary review of the resident.
A capable person is still capable when the sea briefly defeats their stomach.
Function and current condition are distinct. Useful lead, poor presentation.
A rough crossing does not erase the things someone's hands have learned.
He could have passed on the information with a little more grace.
I wonder whether anyone has actually helped the captain feel better.

contexts.subject: A well-traveled passenger excitedly shows the unusually sleeping Pokemon they saw.

SSAnne_2F_Room1_Text_SleepingMonLookedLi.text: I've journeyed far and wide, but in\nall my travels I've never seen\lany POKéMON sleep like this one!\pIt was something like this!$

replies.text: A lifetime of travel, and a nap still managed to surprise them. Excellent Pokemon.
An unusual observed behavior can remain memorable even to an experienced traveler.
Good to keep noticing things instead of deciding you have seen everything.
I like that much experience has not used up their surprise.
An ordinary-looking rest can be a very extraordinary thing to someone new.
The worldly traveler has discovered a spectacularly uneventful new act: sleeping.
A large stillness can apparently leave quite an impression.
Behavioral observation worth recording. The illustration helps.
The world still has something unfamiliar curled up inside it.
A good traveler remembers what stood out, not just where they went.
I wonder how long they watched before deciding the nap was remarkable.

contexts.subject: Brooks insists he would have beaten us fifteen years ago.

SSAnne_2F_Room2_Text_BrooksPostBattle.text: Fifteen years ago, I would\nhave won!$

replies.text: A formidable opponent, safely located fifteen years away from this match.
A hypothetical past performance cannot change the observed current result.
Maybe. The battle we actually had is the one we can learn from.
It can be hard when a familiar skill no longer feels the same.
Past pride does not have to become present disappointment with the whole self.
The critic submits a glowing review of an unavailable earlier edition.
The past makes a very cooperative place to store an undefeated self.
Historical benchmark cannot be rerun. Work with the present configuration.
An old path is not less real because the feet walk differently now.
He can remember being capable without dismissing what the team did today.
I wonder what his favorite battle from those years was.

contexts.subject: Dale says the ship's party is probably already over.

SSAnne_2F_Room2_Text_DalePostBattle.text: Party?\pThe cruise ship's party should be\nover by now.$

replies.text: We may have arrived just in time for the traditional leftover conversation.
He believes the event has ended. We should not assume the current schedule from the invitation alone.
Then enjoy the rest of the ship. No point racing a finished party.
It is a little sad to realize an event has already happened without you.
There may still be something good in the kitchen, though I would ask politely.
The promised social scene has left only its final echo in the corridor.
A room can feel very different after the last excited voice leaves it.
Event window apparently closed. Choose the next available activity.
The ship has begun folding away one part of the day.
A finished party still leaves the people and their stories aboard.
I wonder what the crew most enjoys once the formal event is done.

contexts.subject: A traveler recalls Pokemon carrying people across water.

SSAnne_2F_Room3_Text_SeenMonsFerryPeople.text: Ah, yes, I have seen some POKéMON\nferry people across the water!$

replies.text: A living ferry with the option to have a personal opinion about the route.
Some Pokemon have the size and swimming ability to support human travel.
A strong swimmer still needs a sensible load and safe conditions.
Sharing the water with a trusted partner sounds peaceful.
A comfortable crossing should be comfortable for the Pokemon too.
The sea supplies a road, the companion supplies a rather more personal vessel.
A journey that depends on knowing the creature beneath you.
Buoyancy and load-bearing capability, plus an actual partnership. Interesting combination.
A warm back can make the water feel less like a boundary.
Travel looks different when the transport needs care as well as a destination.
I wonder which Pokemon the traveler saw carrying someone.

contexts.subject: The passenger explains Cut's use and warns that an HM move is hard to forget.

SSAnne_2F_Room3_Text_SomeTreesCanBeCutDo.text:
Small trees can be chopped down
using the move CUT.\pBut remember this!
CUT is an HM technique.\pOnce learned, it is not so easily
discarded.$

replies.text: A tree-clearing lesson with a long-term place in the lesson book. Choose thoughtfully.
The field utility and the removal restriction are both important parts of the choice.
Know who will learn it before committing. Useful advice.
I appreciate hearing the difficult part before the decision.
A useful move deserves a place that fits the partner's wider needs.
The convenient new skill comes with a surprisingly persistent contract.
A small cleared path can leave a lasting mark on the one who clears it.
Hard-to-reverse configuration change. Plan the slot first.
A way through the trees may take root in the partner's own habits.
Clear guidance includes the condition people might otherwise miss.
I wonder how the passenger learned that caution.

contexts.subject: Lamar says he prefers Pokemon that are both strong and rare.

SSAnne_2F_Room4_Text_LamarPostBattle.text: Personally, I prefer strong and\nrare POKéMON.$

replies.text: A very exclusive preference. I hope ordinary kindness still gets through the door.
Rarity and battle capability are distinct attributes, neither a substitute for good care.
His choice. Common partners can still be worth trusting.
I hope he sees the individual once the rare first impression wears off.
Every partner needs care on the days it is not impressive.
A carefully curated cast, selected for both performance and limited availability.
A creature is not made less interesting because someone else has met one.
Scarcity is not a direct measure of capability. Worth separating the requirements.
A small common life can still have an uncommon place beside someone.
Taste is personal. Treating it as a ranking of worth gets ugly quickly.
I wonder which partner he values for reasons that do not fit those two words.

contexts.subject: Dawn admires and envies our strong Pokemon.

SSAnne_2F_Room4_Text_DawnPostBattle.text: Oh, I adore your strong POKéMON!\nOh, how I envy you for them!$

replies.text: The team has collected an admirer. A well-earned compliment after the work.
Visible strength reflects care and training as well as individual capabilities.
They put in the effort. Glad someone noticed.
It is lovely to hear the partners praised so warmly.
A good bond takes more than simply wishing for the strongest arrival.
An enthusiastic review of the cast, with a little longing in the final line.
A creature doing well can make the care behind it briefly visible.
Positive result worth tracing back to the preparation, not just the appearance.
The partners carry a little of the road that taught them.
Admiration is nicer when it remembers they are companions, not accessories.
I wonder which partner's performance caught her attention first.

contexts.subject: A passenger recommends Fuchsia's Safari Zone for its rare Pokemon.

SSAnne_2F_Room5_Text_HaveYouGoneToSafari.text: Have you gone to the SAFARI ZONE\nin FUCHSIA CITY?\pThere are many kinds of rare\nPOKéMON.$

replies.text: A ship carries travel tips as efficiently as it carries luggage.
A reserve with varied habitats is a useful destination for species observation.
Worth hearing. Prepare before paying for the visit.
A place that left them excited enough to tell strangers sounds interesting.
A good outing needs time, supplies, and room to enjoy it calmly.
The passenger's review points toward a rather lively shore excursion.
Some places remain pleasantly crowded in the mind after you leave.
Varied species in a concentrated area. Good field-study opportunity.
A distant patch of land has followed the traveler aboard as a story.
A personal recommendation feels different from a poster at the dock.
I wonder which encounter made them recommend it so readily.

contexts.subject: The child remembers a happy Safari Zone visit with their father and wants to return.

SSAnne_2F_Room5_Text_WeThinkSafariZoneIs.text: Me and my daddy think the SAFARI\nZONE is awesome!\lI wish we could go there again.$

replies.text: The best review is sometimes simply wanting to go back with the same person.
A shared positive experience has become a clear family memory.
Good to hear the day was enjoyable for both of them.
I like that the favorite part includes their dad being there.
A good outing can keep making a family happy long afterward.
A young critic awards the excursion an enthusiastic request for a sequel.
A little remembered afternoon has become somewhere to wish toward.
High repeat-visit interest. Strong user satisfaction report.
A place and a familiar hand have become one warm memory.
The enthusiasm is entirely convincing without any fancy description.
I wonder which part of the day they retell to their dad most often.

contexts.subject: A passenger reports that the captain looks pale and feels very ill.

SSAnne_2F_Room6_Text_CaptainIsAwfullySic.text: The CAPTAIN said he's awfully sick.\nHe was all pale.$

replies.text: Being in charge of a ship does not give the stomach command of the sea.
His condition deserves care regardless of his experience or role.
Someone should check on him rather than just passing the news around.
It sounds miserable to feel that unwell somewhere you are expected to lead.
A little practical help would be kinder than another story about the pallor.
The captain's authority has encountered an uncooperative bodily department.
A capable person can still need somebody to bring a little comfort.
Human maintenance issue, not a failure of command. Get appropriate help.
The sea has found a place where rank means very little.
I hope the staff are giving him privacy as well as help.
I wonder whether he has been able to rest at all.

contexts.subject: A passenger remarks that seasickness affects many people.

SSAnne_2F_Room6_Text_ManyPeopleGetSeasic.text: I hear many people get seasick.$

replies.text: The sea is very generous with that particular unwanted souvenir.
Motion sickness is a familiar travel response, not a measure of courage or experience.
No shame in feeling ill. Find a safe place to recover.
It is reassuring to know the problem is not just you.
People deserve a little patience when the trip stops feeling pleasant.
An extremely successful voyage activity that nobody purchased a ticket to enjoy.
The body sometimes reviews travel less favorably than the itinerary does.
Movement input and human response can be poorly matched. Not a moral issue.
A moving floor can make even familiar balance feel far away.
A kind reminder when someone is embarrassed about feeling unwell.
I wonder what advice the experienced crew gives first-time passengers.

contexts.subject: A crew member praises the captain's swordsmanship and ability to teach Cut.

SSAnne_3F_Corridor_Text_CaptainTeachesCu.text: Our CAPTAIN is a sword master.\nHe's awesome at using CUT.\pThey say he even teaches CUT\nto POKéMON!$

replies.text: A captain with a very precise second skill. The crew sounds proud of him.
A practiced human technique being taught to Pokemon is an interesting form of instruction.
Useful skill. Hope he teaches it with the same care it takes to use.
It is nice to hear the crew admire something their captain works at.
A good teacher leaves someone else able to do the useful thing too.
The captain's legend includes an unexpectedly educational flourish.
A sharp tool becomes less frightening when the hand behind it is patient.
Transferable technique across different bodies. I would like to see the teaching method.
A practiced motion finding another pair of hands, or paws.
Expertise is more impressive when somebody can explain it kindly.
I wonder how the captain first began teaching Pokemon.

contexts.subject: Phillip describes jellyfish Pokemon drifting past the ship at sea.

SSAnne_B1F_Room1_Text_PhillipPostBattle.text: When we're out at sea, jellyfish\nPOKéMON sometimes drift by.$

replies.text: A slow little parade beside a very large boat. Lovely sight.
A ship provides repeated opportunities to observe marine species in open water.
Fine to watch. Give them room if we go into the water.
It sounds peaceful to see them go by without needing to do anything.
An ordinary workday can still offer a good little view.
The voyage includes a drifting supporting cast unconcerned with the passenger schedule.
Small pale shapes making the great water feel inhabited.
Passive observation from a stable platform. Good way to notice patterns.
The sea sends little translucent thoughts past the hull.
A detail worth noticing between all the grand ports and formal parties.
I wonder whether the crew recognizes a change in the water by what drifts past.

contexts.subject: Barny says he had planned to make us his assistant.

SSAnne_B1F_Room1_Text_BarnyPostBattle.text: I was going to make you my\nassistant, too!$

replies.text: An employment offer we narrowly escaped before reading the duties.
He had a role in mind for us without first establishing our interest.
Ask before recruiting someone. We already have plans.
That is a surprising amount of expectation from one short meeting.
A favor is easier to agree to when somebody actually explains it first.
A casting decision announced after the prospective performer has already declined by winning.
A stranger's plan for your day is remarkably easy to acquire.
Unrequested assignment. Requirements and consent both missing.
His imagined road has tried to borrow our feet.
He seems certain he was offering an honor. A little discussion would help.
I wonder what he thought the assistant would be doing.

contexts.subject: Huey says the sailors caught all their Pokemon while at sea.

SSAnne_B1F_Room2_Text_HueyPostBattle.text: We caught all our POKéMON while\nwe were out at sea.$

replies.text: The team is a living collection of places the ship has passed.
The crew's encounters reflect sustained access to marine habitats.
Hope the catches became well-cared-for partners, not just onboard trophies.
It must be strange to remember a meeting by the stretch of ocean around it.
A crew and its Pokemon probably learn a lot of shared routines aboard.
The ship's route has supplied the entire supporting cast.
A horizon can keep returning as a familiar companion beside you.
Consistent sampling environment explains the team composition.
The sea has sent a few of its lives traveling above it.
A team can tell you something about the life its trainer actually leads.
I wonder which one has been with the crew longest.

contexts.subject: Dylan recommends a fishing rod for Pokemon living in deep water.

SSAnne_B1F_Room3_Text_DylanPostBattle.text: Sea POKéMON live in deep water.\nYou'll need a ROD to fish them up!$

replies.text: A long line is a much better plan than trying to reach down very confidently.
A rod provides access to encounters unavailable from an ordinary shoreline search.
Bring the right tool. Do not lean over the rail chasing a glimpse.
There is something strange about so much life hidden beneath an empty-looking surface.
A sensible tool makes the attempt safer and less tiring.
The deep-water cast requires a more specialized invitation.
A line reaches where looking harder cannot.
Tool extends the accessible environment. Basic but useful.
A little thread asks a question too deep for the eye.
Practical advice from somebody who spends time around the water.
I wonder which deep-water catch he most enjoys finding.

contexts.subject: Leonard cheerfully asks whether we want to become a sailor.

SSAnne_B1F_Room4_Text_LeonardPostBattle.text: Hahaha!\nWant to be a sailor, mate?$

replies.text: An inviting laugh, followed by an entire career possibility. Busy conversation.
A warm invitation is pleasant; the work itself would deserve a fuller explanation.
Could be good work. Learn what the ordinary days involve before signing on.
It is nice to be asked, though I would have so many questions.
A life with shared meals and changing shores has its appeal.
The unofficial recruitment office operates through laughter and a remarkably broad opening question.
A road made of water is still a road someone can choose.
Interesting possibility. Need a role description, training plan, and equipment list.
A familiar port can become the beginning rather than the end of the day.
He makes the life sound welcoming without a polished pitch.
I wonder what made him decide to go to sea.

contexts.subject: Duncan asks if we visited Vermilion's Fishing Guru.

SSAnne_B1F_Room4_Text_DuncanPostBattle.text: Did you see the FISHING GURU in\nVERMILION CITY?$

replies.text: The local fishing network apparently extends all the way below deck.
A local expert is a useful connection for someone beginning to fish.
Worth visiting if we need advice or a rod.
It is nice when a familiar name turns up in an unexpected place.
A recommendation from a sailor carries a little practical weight.
The waterfront community supplies a recurring supporting character.
A hobby can tie a surprising number of rooms together.
Relevant specialist referral. Sensible.
A name from the shore has followed us across the gangway.
He sounds as if nearly every visitor should make the introduction.
I wonder whether the sailors compare catches with the Guru when they are in port.

contexts.subject: The sailor proudly describes Machoke's ability to move heavy rocks.

SSAnne_B1F_Room5_Text_MachokeHasStrength.text: My buddy MACHOKE is super strong!\pHe has enough STRENGTH to move\nbig rocks!$

replies.text: A powerful buddy, introduced with a very large amount of pride.
Strength can serve practical work as well as battling. Appropriate loads still matter.
Strong partner. Give Machoke rest between the heavy jobs.
I like that he says buddy before describing what Machoke can do.
A helpful partner deserves appreciation even when no heavy lifting is needed.
The sailor's trusted companion receives an impressively concrete testimonial.
A familiar pair of hands making an impossible-looking task ordinary.
High load capability. Good technique still belongs in the plan.
A great deal of force can still belong to a gentle companion.
He sounds fond, rather than merely pleased to have strong help.
I wonder what Machoke likes doing when the work is finished.

contexts.subject: After his recovery and HM01 gift, the captain explains clearing small trees with Cut.

SSAnne_CaptainsOffice_Text_ExplainCut.text: Using CUT, you can chop down\nsmall trees.\pWhy not try it with the trees\naround VERMILION CITY?$

replies.text: A little help for his bad afternoon became a way through our next obstacle.
The final explanation follows the successful HM handoff and identifies its field use.
Useful gift. Good that he feels better too.
It is nice when a small kind act ends with both people helped.
He turned his gratitude into something genuinely useful on the road.
The seasick master's scene ends with a practical lesson rather than a demonstration.
A little care has opened a path, quite literally.
Capability acquired with a clear first test location. Good instruction.
A difficult crossing has left a new way through the trees.
He made the gift easy to understand, even while still recovering.
I wonder how many travelers remember the captain when they use that move.

contexts.subject: Now feeling better, the captain says the S.S. Anne will leave soon and bids farewell.

SSAnne_CaptainsOffice_Text_SSAnneWillSet.text: CAPTAIN: …Whew!\pNow that I'm not sick anymore,\nI guess it's time.\pThe S.S. ANNE will set sail soon!\pFarewell, until our return to\nVERMILION CITY!$

replies.text: His stomach has finally authorized the sailing schedule. Good news for the whole ship.
His improved condition allows the voyage to continue. The farewell is explicit.
Good to hear he is well. We should be ready to disembark.
A kind goodbye makes the ship feel a little less temporary.
I hope the next stretch of sea treats him more gently.
The captain returns to his proper role and closes the visit with a formal farewell.
A borrowed room, a short acquaintance, and a door about to become a gangway again.
Departure approaching. Finish essential business before leaving the ship.
A little floating world is preparing to carry its own road away.
He remembers to leave the goodbye warm after a miserable day.
I wonder what port he is most looking forward to next.

contexts.subject: The captain cannot give HM01 because our bag is full.

SSAnne_CaptainsOffice_Text_YouHaveNoRoom.text: Oh, no!\nYou have no room for this!$

replies.text: A kindness returned has met the one thing aboard less flexible than our bag: nothing.
The HM transfer did not complete. No successful gift should be inferred.
Make room first. Let the captain recover while we sort it.
I wish we had been ready to accept his thanks.
A little preparation will make the next handoff easier.
The grateful captain's generous flourish has collided with luggage capacity.
A tiny disc, an entirely full pocket, an unnecessarily awkward ending.
Capacity issue. Clear space rather than repeating the failed handoff.
A little place needs to open before the gift can open a larger one.
No need to rush him through another explanation while he still feels ill.
I wonder what in the bag has outlived its usefulness.

contexts.subject: A crew member says the party has ended and the ship will depart soon.

SSAnne_Deck_Text_ShipDepartingSoon.text: The party's over.\nThe ship will be departing soon.$

replies.text: The party is folding up, and the whole building is about to leave. Strong closing signal.
The available visit window is ending. It is sensible to review unfinished business.
Keep the team together. We do not want anyone left behind.
There is a particular little sadness when a place prepares to carry on without you.
We should make our last stops without making the crew chase us.
The temporary venue is about to take its entire stage elsewhere.
A familiar room can be gone from shore by evening. Ships are strange.
Departure window near. Check the group and belongings before disembarking.
The small world beside the dock is remembering it belongs to the sea.
A clear notice is kinder than a surprise gangway closing.
I wonder what the deck looks like once the guests have all gone ashore.

contexts.subject: A sailor is tired from scrubbing the deck.

replies.text: That shining deck did not become shiny by admiring the sea. Somebody worked.
The comfort of passengers depends on sustained physical maintenance.
Hard work. Give the sailor room to finish safely.
It makes you notice the ordinary care behind such a polished ship.
I hope the crew gets a proper rest after the guests stop tracking things in.
The elegant setting briefly reveals the labor behind its impeccable appearance.
A bright surface can hide a great deal of someone else's tiredness.
Maintenance is real work, especially on a surface everyone keeps using.
The ship's ordinary shine has a pair of aching arms behind it.
Clean floors are part of good design, and cleaning them should not be invisible.
I wonder how long one full pass of the deck takes.

contexts.subject: An ill passenger comes on deck for air.

SSAnne_Deck_Text_FeelSeasick.text: Urf… I feel ill…\pI got seasick, so I stepped out to\nget some air…$

replies.text: A little breeze is much better company than another clever comment right now.
They have moved to a place that may feel more tolerable. Give them room.
Make sure they stay somewhere steady and safe while they feel ill.
That sounds miserable. I would keep the conversation short.
A quiet moment and someone checking they are steady would be kind.
The luxurious voyage has briefly narrowed to the question of not feeling awful.
The sea can be beautiful and terrible company for a stomach.
Reduce demands. A moving deck still needs careful footing.
The body has asked for a little more sky around it.
No teasing. Feeling unwell in public is difficult enough.
I wonder whether a crew member nearby knows they need help.

contexts.subject: Edmond wonders how many Pokemon species exist in the world.

SSAnne_Deck_Text_EdmondPostBattle.text: How many kinds of POKéMON do you\nthink there are in this big world?$

replies.text: Every new shore seems capable of adding another name. That is an excellent kind of big question.
The total depends on observation and classification that may still be incomplete.
Enough to keep us learning. No reason to rush past the ones beside us.
I like a question that makes the horizon feel full instead of empty.
A wide world means there is always another good reason to stay curious.
The cast list appears larger than any one traveler's program.
A number that keeps a little space around the unknown.
An open research question! Complete observations are harder than confident estimates.
The world may know more names for itself than we have learned to hear.
A better question than deciding the familiar ones are all there is.
I wonder which new meeting most changed his estimate.

contexts.subject: Trevor doubts his father's claim that only one hundred Pokemon kinds exist.

SSAnne_Deck_Text_TrevorPostBattle.text: My pa said there are 100 kinds of\nPOKéMON. I think there are more.$

replies.text: A child has looked at the horizon and suspected the list needs more pages.
Questioning a fixed total in light of broader experience is reasonable.
Worth checking. Even a parent can have an outdated answer.
It is nice that he can respect his father and still be curious beyond the answer.
Learning together could make a good next conversation between them.
The inherited encyclopedia has received a polite request for a revised edition.
The world often turns out to be larger than the first number someone gave us.
A claim ready for verification. Good instinct.
A small doubt can make the map grow in a useful direction.
He is making room for what he has not seen yet. Lovely habit.
I wonder which Pokemon first made him think the count was too small.

contexts.subject: A busy cook asks us to get out of the working kitchen.

SSAnne_Kitchen_Text_BusyOutOfTheWay.text: You, mon petit!\nWe're busy here!\lOut of the way!$

replies.text: The galley is not a spectator sport while people are carrying hot things. Time to move.
An active workspace needs clear routes for staff and equipment.
Out of the way. Hot food and a moving ship are enough trouble already.
I would rather not become one more thing someone has to step around.
Fair request. A busy kitchen needs its floor more than its visitors need a look.
The accidental audience has been removed from a performance involving knives and heat.
A room can be interesting and still be a poor place to stand.
Keep the access path clear. Functional space outranks curiosity here.
The room is moving with work; we should not be its stubborn still point.
A sharp tone is understandable when the floor is crowded and the trays are hot.
I wonder how much room the crew has when every station is busy.
