Something quiet remains while the bright dangers change around it. Worth noticing.
Keeping one familiar face can make the new lineup feel safer than it really is.
I'd compare what changed with what stayed. Both choices tell us something about her approach.

contexts.subject: The Maniac identifies the flamboyant Dome Ace as the Dome leader.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_DomeAceIsThe.text: Bet you didn't know this!\pOne of those top TRAINERS that SCOTT\ncalls the FRONTIER BRAINS is there.\pIt's this flamboyant TRAINER called\nthe DOME ACE that runs the place.$

replies.text: Flamboyant sounds well matched to a building that wants everyone looking at it.
His title establishes the facility connection. His style is a separate description.
The Dome has a showman in charge. Skill still decides the battle.
I wonder whether he's quieter when the audience has gone home.
A lively host can make a place welcoming. I'd like to see how he treats a nervous challenger.
A grand venue has acquired a leader unwilling to let the architecture do all the showing off.
The Dome has apparently hired personality on the same scale as its roof.
I'd ask how his strategies use the tournament format. That's the practical question.
Some people step into bright spaces as though the light has been expecting them.
He sounds conscious of presentation. I'm curious whether the whole place reflects his taste.
I'd like to hear him explain what he enjoys about an audience.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Dome Ace initial Dragon-Flying, Water-Ground, and Fire-Flying roster.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_DomeAceSilve.text: Have you battled the DOME ACE?\pWhen he's treating the opponent\nlightly, he uses these three POKéMON:\pA DRAGON & FLYING DRAGON POKéMON,\na WATER & GROUND MUD FISH POKéMON,\land a FIRE & FLYING FLAME POKéMON.$

replies.text: Two flying dangers and one grounded-looking surprise. I'd keep my feet and my guesses careful.
The reported dual types create distinct weaknesses. A single broad label won't describe the roster.
Check the matchups before choosing. That's what the Dome gives us time for.
Treating an opponent lightly doesn't sound like the same thing as bringing weak partners.
I'd plan around the whole trio instead of picking the one that looks easiest.
His supposedly casual welcome includes an alarming amount of wings and elemental force.
Being treated lightly is apparently still a substantial physical experience.
We should examine which pair handles the possible matchups with the fewest gaps.
Air, water, and fire leave little room for a careless step.
The casual attitude might be the least useful part of this information to trust.
I'd ask how opponents usually choose against that mix. The selection itself sounds difficult.

contexts.subject: The Maniac describes the Dome Ace serious Dragon-Flying, Water-Ground, and Steel-Psychic lineup.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_DomeAceGoldM.text:
Have you battled the DOME ACE
when he's serious?\pWhen he's demonstrating his strategy,
he uses these three POKéMON:\pA DRAGON & FLYING EON POKéMON,
a WATER & GROUND MUD FISH POKéMON,\land a STEEL- & PSYCHIC-type IRON LEG\lPOKéMON.$

replies.text: The flame has made room for iron legs. His serious plans have a very heavy footstep.
Steel and Psychic coverage replaces the earlier Fire-Flying component. That changes our selection problem.
A new lineup needs a fresh choice. Don't just reuse the last pair.
I wonder which partner he trusts when the strategy starts going wrong.
We'll want a plan with room to adapt, rather than one perfect-looking opening.
The grand strategy now includes something with iron legs. Subtlety has developed considerable weight.
An imposing roster has become more imposing in a different direction. Helpful of it.
I'd compare coverage across all three before deciding what to leave in reserve.
A changed shape can hide a familiar intention. We need to observe both.
He seems to change the impression as well as the matchups. That can unsettle a challenger.
I'd ask what choice made people realize he was taking them seriously.

contexts.subject: The Maniac identifies the eccentric Factory Head as the rental facility leader.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_FactoryHeadI.text: Bet you didn't know this!\pOne of those top TRAINERS that SCOTT\ncalls the FRONTIER BRAINS is there.\pIt's this freaky TRAINER called\nthe FACTORY HEAD that runs the place.$

replies.text: The Factory Head is described as freaky. I'd prefer at least one useful measurement with that.
That's a subjective characterization, not an explanation of his methods.
An unusual manner doesn't tell us how he'll battle.
I'd rather hear what he's like from someone who spoke with him kindly.
People call unfamiliar things strange quickly. Let's meet him before deciding.
A title, a building, and one unhelpfully broad adjective. The report could use revision.
The mystery has received a rude nickname instead of a description.
His handling of unfamiliar rentals interests me more than his manner.
An odd shape to another person's eye may be entirely comfortable from within.
Calling someone freaky says a little about the speaker, too.
I'd ask what he actually did. Specific behavior tells a better story.

contexts.subject: The Maniac says the Factory Head uses three rentals under similar conditions to challengers.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_FactoryHeadS.text:
Have you battled the FACTORY HEAD
already?\pLet me think… When he goes to battle,
he just gets three rental POKéMON.\pHe battles under pretty much the same
conditions as you.$

replies.text: He gets unfamiliar partners too. Nobody has hidden a lifelong best friend behind the counter.
Comparable rental conditions shift the contest toward evaluation and adaptive decision-making.
Same kind of uncertainty for both sides. Learn the team quickly.
That makes me curious how he introduces himself to each new partner.
He has to work with the team he's given. There's something fair about that.
The expert has agreed to use the same unpredictable ingredients as the guests. Admirable confidence.
No private super-team in the cupboard. Only considerable expertise.
His advantage may be how efficiently he assesses unfamiliar combinations.
A stranger can become a partner quickly when someone knows how to listen.
Similar conditions don't erase experience, but they do make his choices interesting to watch.
I'd ask which rental combination challenged him to think differently.

contexts.subject: The Maniac confirms the serious Factory Head still battles with rental Pokemon.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_FactoryHeadG.text:
Have you battled the FACTORY HEAD
when he's serious?\pWhen he goes seriously to battle,
he still gets three rental POKéMON.\pHe battles under virtually the same
conditions as you.$

replies.text: Even the serious version gets rentals. He hasn't upgraded to bringing his own certainty.
The higher-stakes encounter preserves the rental constraint. Expertise remains the distinguishing factor.
Same rental system. Expect better decisions, not a fixed familiar team.
His confidence must come from understanding new partners rather than knowing them beforehand.
That takes a lot of attention. A borrowed team still deserves to be understood.
When serious, he continues obeying the inconvenient part of his own challenge. A respectable commitment.
The training wheels were never hidden in his office. Slightly alarming news.
We shouldn't expect a memorized roster to solve this. Adaptation is the task.
He trusts his ability to begin again with someone unfamiliar. That's a particular strength.
Consistency in the rules makes the stronger performance more impressive.
I'd love to hear how his first minute with a rental team differs from an ordinary challenger's.

contexts.subject: The Maniac identifies the intimidating Pike Queen as the Pike leader.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PikeQueenIsT.text: Bet you didn't know this!\pOne of those top TRAINERS that SCOTT\ncalls the FRONTIER BRAINS is there.\pIt's this scary TRAINER called\nthe PIKE QUEEN that runs the place.$

replies.text: A scary trainer inside the giant snake. The building is doing very consistent introductions.
The description suggests an imposing manner. It doesn't establish her actual temperament toward visitors.
Be respectful. Intimidation isn't a battle result.
I wonder whether she's tired of strangers arriving already afraid of her.
I'd give her the chance to be a person before turning her into a warning.
The title and venue have cooperated on a rather thorough first impression.
A frightening reputation has found suitably unsubtle architecture.
We need to learn how she battles, not only how people describe meeting her.
A guarded face can collect stories it never chose to tell.
People may confuse a reserved expression with an invitation to gossip.
I'd ask somebody for an actual encounter rather than one more alarming adjective.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Pike Queen good-mood Poison, Bug-Rock, and Water team.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PikeQueenSil.text:
Have you battled the PIKE QUEEN
before?\pWhen she's in a good mood, they say
she uses these three POKéMON:\pA POISON-type FANG SNAKE POKéMON,
a BUG & ROCK MOLD POKéMON,\land a WATER-type TENDER POKéMON.$

replies.text: That's the good-mood team? I'd hate to learn which face the snake makes when annoyed.
The mood explanation is hearsay. The reported types still offer practical preparation clues.
Poison, Bug and Rock, then Water. Prepare for the mix.
I wouldn't count on her being gentle just because someone says she's in a good mood.
A pleasant mood doesn't mean she'll stop caring for her own team's chances.
Her allegedly cheerful reception still arrives with fangs and formidable defenses.
Good mood is a relative term. The opponents appear fully equipped regardless.
We can assess status protection and coverage against that reported lineup.
A calm surface doesn't promise a soft welcome beneath it.
I'd use the roster details and leave the speculation about her feelings aside.
I'd ask what happened in the battle itself. Her expression can't tell the whole story.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Pike Queen serious Poison, Steel-Ground, and Water-Flying lineup.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PikeQueenGol.text:
Have you battled the PIKE QUEEN
when she's serious?\pWhen she's seriously annoyed, they say
she uses these three POKéMON:\pA POISON-type FANG SNAKE POKéMON,
a STEEL & GROUND IRON SNAKE POKéMON,\land a WATER- & FLYING-type ATROCIOUS\lPOKéMON.$

replies.text: The snake now has a second, iron snake for company. That's a very firm commitment to snakes.
The reported substitutions alter both defensive profiles and offensive coverage substantially.
New team, different problems. Check our answers to each one.
I wish he described her choices without deciding exactly how angry she must be.
We'll prepare better by thinking about the partners than by worrying about her mood.
An already imposing roster has acquired iron and an additional reputation for menace.
The serious team has doubled down on long bodies and alarming introductions.
We need to account for the new dual types rather than repeat the earlier plan.
Iron changes the weight of a threat even when the shadow looks familiar.
Her intensity may be real. The rumor has still decorated it quite enthusiastically.
I'd compare the actual matchups before letting those descriptions decide how afraid to feel.

contexts.subject: The Maniac identifies the Arena Tycoon while emphasizing her cute appearance.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_ArenaTycoonI.text: Bet you didn't know this!\pOne of those top TRAINERS that SCOTT\ncalls the FRONTIER BRAINS is there.\pIt's this cute TRAINER called\nthe ARENA TYCOON that runs the place.$

replies.text: I'd rather know how she battles than how successfully she impressed his eyes.
Appearance is not evidence of strategic ability. Her leadership role is the relevant fact.
She runs the Arena. Take her seriously.
I wonder how often she has to get past that introduction before people listen.
Being cute doesn't make the job easier. She's still responsible for a hard challenge.
A formidable specialist has been introduced using the least useful item on her qualifications list.
An expert has been reduced to an adjective. Efficiently uninformative.
I'd ask what she values under the Arena judging rules.
A small face can hold a very large intention. Neither needs explaining away.
A compliment can still leave out the part of a person that matters to the conversation.
I'd ask someone who's battled her what choice surprised them.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Arena Tycoon Bug-Fighting, Dark, and Bug-Ghost testing team.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_ArenaTycoonS.text:
Have you battled the ARENA TYCOON
before?\pWhen she's assessing the foe's ability,
she supposedly uses these POKéMON:\pA BUG & FIGHTING SINGLE HORN POKéMON,
a DARK-type MOONLIGHT POKéMON,\land a BUG & GHOST SHED POKéMON.$

replies.text: That last combination sounds like a very small surprise with very firm opinions about being hit.
The reported Bug-Ghost partner makes appropriate coverage particularly important.
Have a way to handle every partner. No room to switch around a bad opening.
I think the unusual little one would make me pause longest.
The order matters as much as the list. We should think through who follows whom.
A compact roster with plenty of opportunity to punish an overconfident entrance.
The small stranger may be the reason a large plan stops functioning.
We need to examine coverage and sequence under the Arena's fixed-order rules.
An apparently slight thing can decide which doors stay closed.
The lineup rewards attention to details that an impressive first glance could miss.
I'd ask how challengers usually handle the partner they least expected to struggle with.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Arena Tycoon serious Dark, Ghost-Poison, and Grass-Fighting roster.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_ArenaTycoonG.text:
Have you battled the ARENA TYCOON
when she's serious?\pWhen she battles for keeps,
she supposedly uses these POKéMON:\pA DARK-type MOONLIGHT POKéMON,
a GHOST & POISON SHADOW POKéMON\land a GRASS- & FIGHTING-type\lMUSHROOM POKéMON.$

replies.text: Shadows, poison, and a mushroom ready for a fight. That's a crowded little list of worries.
The serious roster changes the coverage requirements while retaining the Dark partner.
Plan the sequence again. Familiarity with one member won't cover the rest.
The same quiet-looking partner stays while the others change. I'd remember that.
We should choose a team that can handle trouble after the first matchup goes wrong.
Her serious approach has provided several entirely different ways to spoil a comfortable plan.
A mushroom has entered the serious roster. People underestimate mushrooms at their convenience.
I'd test the proposed order against the full set of reported threats.
A familiar shadow remains among new ones. Recognition isn't the same as safety.
It's a good reminder to look again instead of assuming we've already understood somebody.
I'd ask which matchup people found hardest to recover from under those Arena rules.

contexts.subject: The Maniac calls the Palace Maven sinister while identifying the facility leader.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PalaceMavenI.text: Bet you didn't know this!\pOne of those top TRAINERS that SCOTT\ncalls the FRONTIER BRAINS is there.\pIt's this sinister TRAINER called\nthe PALACE MAVEN that runs the place.$

replies.text: Sinister is a big word to hand somebody before we've even said good afternoon.
That characterization is subjective. We know his role, not the basis for the description.
Let's meet him before borrowing the rumor's opinion.
A quiet older person can look strange to someone who doesn't know them.
I'd judge him by how he treats the Pokemon in his care.
The report supplies an ominous adjective where a useful observation ought to be.
A sinister reputation may simply be a private person surrounded by inventive visitors.
I'd like to know how his team is prepared for autonomous battles.
A face in shade isn't proof of what lives behind it.
People sometimes make a whole costume out of somebody else's first impression.
I'd ask for a story from someone who's actually spoken with him.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Palace Maven Poison-Flying, Normal, and Water-Ice roster.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PalaceMavenS.text:
Have you battled the PALACE MAVEN
before?\pWhen he's testing the opponent's
spirit, he's said to use these POKéMON:\pA POISON & FLYING-type BAT POKéMON,
a NORMAL-type LAZY POKéMON, and a\lWATER- & ICE-type TRANSPORT POKéMON.$

replies.text: A bat, a sleepy sort, and a water traveler. I'd like to hear how they all spend an ordinary morning.
The reported types matter, but Palace behavior also depends on natures and available moves.
We need a suitable partner, not just a favorable type chart.
They sound like such different companions. I wonder what he likes about each one.
I'd pay attention to what they choose without commands. That's the Palace's real complication.
An unusual household, introduced as a formidable test. Both descriptions may fit perfectly well.
The lazy partner has an important job. I support accessible career opportunities.
Our preparation needs to account for autonomous choices as well as these matchups.
Three different temperaments may share a quiet understanding we haven't seen yet.
The description gives shapes and types. How they behave will make the encounter personal.
I'd ask how challengers adjusted after seeing the first uncommanded move.

contexts.subject: The Maniac describes the Palace Maven serious Fire, Normal, and Water lineup.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PalaceMavenG.text:
Have you battled the PALACE MAVEN
when he's serious?\pWhen he throws his entire might into
battle, he's said to use these POKéMON:\pA FIRE-type LEGENDARY POKéMON,
a NORMAL-type LAZY POKéMON,\land a WATER-type AURORA POKéMON.$

replies.text: Fire and water have changed, but the lazy partner kept the position. Must be a very effective nap.
The reported Fire and Water replacements alter coverage. The retained Normal partner deserves attention.
Prepare for the changed team. Don't treat the familiar one as harmless.
I wonder whether his partners feel the difference when he takes a match seriously.
I'd focus on a reliable fit for our own partner before worrying about the impressive descriptions.
His entire might apparently still includes an expert in conserving effort. Sensible delegation.
The lazy one remains employed at the highest level. Strong evidence for the value of rest.
The moves and natures may matter more than the roster's imposing titles suggest.
A still center can remain while the surrounding weather changes completely.
Repeated choices tell us something about trust. He seems to have plenty in that familiar partner.
I'd compare how the returning partner behaves now with the earlier encounter.

contexts.subject: The Maniac identifies the fiery Pyramid King as the expedition facility leader.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PyramidKingI.text: Bet you didn't know this!\pOne of those top TRAINERS that SCOTT\ncalls the FRONTIER BRAINS is there.\pIt's this fiery-hot TRAINER called\nthe PYRAMID KING that runs the place.$

replies.text: A fiery king inside a dark pyramid. At least he should be easy to notice when he arrives.
His reported intensity suggests a forceful manner. It doesn't yet explain his battle strategy.
He runs the expedition challenge. Take the route and the trainer seriously.
I wonder whether that energy makes the dark feel less lonely or more alarming.
I'd rather know how he prepares his partners for the long climb.
A king, a pyramid, and a temperament that seems unlikely to go unnoticed in either.
A fiery presence in a dark building. The atmosphere has been thoroughly organized.
I'd ask what skills he designed the expedition to test.
Some people carry a flame into a room without making it any warmer. We haven't met him yet.
The title makes a strong impression. I'm more curious about the person doing the work.
I'd ask an explorer what his arrival felt like after all those floors.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Pyramid King Rock, Ice, and Steel testing roster.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PyramidKingS.text:
Have you battled the PYRAMID KING
before?\pWhen he's checking the foe's power,
he apparently uses these POKéMON:\pA ROCK-type ROCK PEAK POKéMON,
an ICE-type ICEBERG POKéMON,\land a STEEL-type IRON POKéMON.$

replies.text: Rock, ice, and iron. His team sounds as though somebody ordered three very stubborn landmarks.
The reported elemental spread presents three distinct defensive profiles. Prepare specific answers.
Three tough matchups. Save enough strength for whoever waits at the top.
Meeting that team after a long climb sounds rather overwhelming.
Our supplies and condition before the encounter may matter as much as the team choice.
The summit reception appears to have been assembled from exceptionally unyielding materials.
A geological committee has been convened to object to our arrival.
We need coverage without assuming we'll reach the encounter at full resources.
Stone, frost, and metal wait at the end of a tiring path. The climb is part of their weight.
He chose a memorable trio. I'd rather remember the useful weaknesses than just the imposing shapes.
I'd ask what condition successful explorers reached him in. That changes the whole story.

contexts.subject: The Maniac reports the Pyramid King serious Ice-Flying, Electric-Flying, and Fire-Flying roster.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_PyramidKingG.text:
Have you battled the PYRAMID KING
when he's serious?\pWhen he's pumped with hot power,
he apparently uses these POKéMON:\pAn ICE & FLYING FREEZE POKéMON, an
ELECTRIC & FLYING ELECTRIC POKéMON,\land a FIRE- & FLYING-type FLAME\lPOKéMON.$

replies.text: The solid landmarks have taken flight and brought three kinds of weather with them.
All three reported partners share Flying typing while differing strongly in their other coverage.
Different team at the summit. Recheck the plan before another climb.
Looking up after reaching the top would feel rather unfairly appropriate.
I'd prepare the whole journey around having enough left for that encounter.
The king has replaced three immovable objects with three extremely mobile objections.
Having climbed to the top, we are apparently expected to look higher still.
A shared type may offer a route through the matchup, but the secondary types complicate it.
The summit has acquired wings. A finished climb doesn't promise stillness.
The whole impression changes. I'd avoid letting the spectacle distract from the details.
I'd ask which partner changed the pace of the battle most sharply.

contexts.subject: The Maniac recommends Tower Doubles as a foundation for learning Frontier double battles.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_DoubleBattle.text:
Sure, there are several places where
you can enter DOUBLE BATTLES.\pBut the DOUBLE BATTLE ROOMS of
the BATTLE TOWER are, like, basic!\pThey're where you should learn about
how DOUBLE BATTLES are played here\lin the BATTLE FRONTIER.$

replies.text: A place to learn two-at-once thinking before we try two-at-once panicking elsewhere.
A stable format provides a useful baseline before adding other facilities' special rules.
Learn the basics here. Then take them somewhere harder.
I like a clear place to begin. The whole island feels less overwhelming that way.
Getting comfortable with cooperation first sounds better than piling on every rule at once.
A rare piece of guidance that begins with a manageable first step rather than a grand destiny.
The basics have a building. Convenient, though rather tall.
We can isolate the coordination problem before introducing additional constraints.
Two paths are easier to follow when the ground beneath them stays familiar.
A good starting place can make an unfamiliar format feel much more welcoming.
I'd ask which mistake beginners make most often. That would be a useful first lesson.

contexts.subject: The Maniac warns that opponents develop strategies specifically for double battles.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_DoubleBattle.text: Watch yourself in the battles here.\pI hear there are TRAINERS that have\nstrategies they developed just for\lDOUBLE BATTLES.$

replies.text: Two partners aren't just one battle with an extra pair of elbows. People have made plans about this.
Interactions between active partners create strategies unavailable in a single battle.
Expect teamwork from the opponent. Build some of our own.
I think the surprising part would be realizing both opposing moves were one idea.
A partner can help another partner in ways that don't look impressive alone.
The second opponent is not decorative. An important clarification for the overconfident.
Two minds may be conspiring. Best not to treat them as separate inconveniences.
We should examine combined effects and avoid evaluating each move in isolation.
Two small actions can cast one much larger shadow.
The relationship between the choices may matter more than either choice by itself.
I'd ask for an example of a combination that surprised him.

contexts.subject: The Maniac suggests trying other double-battle facilities after mastering the Tower basics.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_DoubleBattle.text: Once you're confident and comfortable\nwith DOUBLE BATTLES here, you should\lthink about challenging other places\loffering DOUBLE BATTLES.$

replies.text: Once two-at-once feels normal, the island has kindly prepared several fresh ways to confuse us.
Transfer the established coordination skills, then account for each new facility's rules.
Get comfortable first. Then choose a new challenge deliberately.
I like being allowed to feel ready before moving on.
A new setting can keep a familiar skill interesting. No need to rush there today.
Graduation from the basics comes with a delightful brochure of further complications.
Competence has earned the right to become slightly bewildered somewhere new.
We can add one unfamiliar rule set at a time and see how the existing plan adapts.
A familiar step can carry you somewhere the path has changed.
Confidence should make room for curiosity instead of assuming the next place works the same way.
I'd ask which facility he recommends next and why. The reason matters more than the title.

contexts.subject: The Maniac suggests looking carefully for familiar trainers or followers in the Battle Salon.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_MultiBattleA.text: All sorts of TRAINERS gather in\nthe BATTLE SALON.\pJust think--you may run into your\nfriends or followers!\lYou should look carefully!$

replies.text: A familiar face among all those possible partners would be a very pleasant surprise.
The Salon's available trainers can include people connected with earlier encounters. Worth checking.
Look at the trainers and their teams. Familiarity is useful, but fit still matters.
I'd feel less nervous if someone I knew was waiting there.
It would be nice to see how someone has grown since the last time we met.
An ordinary partner search may unexpectedly turn into a reunion. A superior use of a waiting room.
The crowd may contain someone who already knows our peculiarities. Efficient matchmaking.
We should inspect the partner's available Pokemon and moves before committing.
Paths cross again in odd rooms. It's worth looking up before passing through.
A familiar person can change the whole feeling of an unfamiliar place.
I'd like to hear what brought them back. A reunion deserves more than a quick team check.

contexts.subject: The Maniac recommends the Link Multi challenge for battling beside a strong friend.

BattleFrontier_Lounge2_Text_LinkMultiBat.text: If you're with a friend, head for the\nLINK MULTI BATTLE ROOM.\pIf you play with a strong friend,\nyou can expect to see tough foes!$

replies.text: Bring a strong friend and the Tower supplies a stronger reason to talk tactics together.
A known partner allows deliberate coordination, though the opposition scales into a serious challenge.
Agree on the plan before the first battle. Friendship won't read minds.
It sounds easier to face a tough room with someone I already trust beside me.
I'd want us both comfortable saying when the plan needs to change.
A friendship offered the opportunity to conduct a very organized disagreement with strangers.
A fine test of companionship, provided neither mistakes blame for strategy.
We can coordinate complementary partners and avoid conflicting moves before entering.
Trust is a good beginning. Listening is how it survives the difficult part.
A strong friend should also be someone you can talk honestly with after a mistake.
I'd ask them how they work out a plan together. That's the part I'm most curious about.

contexts.subject: The girl says this partner prefers attacking even when badly hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlAt.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it likes to battle!\nIt will battle even if it has a lot\lof ouchies!$

replies.text: A determined little fighter. We'll have to notice when determination needs a pause.
She describes a persistent attack preference under pressure, not immunity to injury.
It may keep attacking. We still need to protect it.
That sounds brave, but I'd want it to know stopping isn't disappointing us.
Some partners don't ask for a break. We ought to pay attention anyway.
A stirring commitment to battle, accompanied by an unfortunate lack of self-preservation paperwork.
Stubborn courage. Useful, until it begins negotiating on behalf of an exhausted body.
We can prepare suitable offensive options without assuming it'll choose recovery when needed.
A flame can keep reaching upward after the wick has nearly gone. Watch closely.
It's easy to admire that drive and forget the little creature carrying it.
I'd compare her reading with what we've actually noticed when the partner is tired.

contexts.subject: The girl says this attacking partner becomes protective of itself when hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlAt.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it likes to battle!\nBut if it gets enough ouchies,\lit will worry about itself!$

replies.text: It likes a good fight and also has an opinion about when enough is enough. Sensible.
Her reading predicts a shift from offense toward self-protection as its condition worsens.
Expect the preference to change under pressure. Plan for both parts.
I'm glad there's room for looking after itself in that brave little personality.
Wanting to battle and wanting to be safe can belong to the same partner.
An enthusiastic combatant with a functioning complaints department. Excellent.
It has discovered that enthusiasm and preserving oneself aren't natural enemies.
A defensive option may become more useful once its priorities shift.
A bold step can become a careful one without ceasing to belong to the same creature.
That change sounds understandable. I'd rather notice it than call it losing nerve.
I'd watch for the first sign that it wants to protect itself. That could tell us plenty.

contexts.subject: The girl says this aggressive partner turns toward indirect tactics when hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlAt.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it likes to battle!\nBut if it gets enough ouchies,\lit will turn sneaky!$

replies.text: It starts with a brawl and keeps a little bag of trouble for when the brawl gets uncomfortable.
The reported preference shifts from direct attacks to interference under pressure.
Give it useful options for both approaches.
I wonder whether it looks different when it starts trying to outwit the opponent.
Changing tactics can be wiser than simply trying to hit harder while worn out.
A straightforward fighter with a concealed second opinion about straightforward fighting.
When enthusiasm encounters pain, cunning has been asked to take over.
We should account for the lower-condition preference when checking its available moves.
A straight path can bend around a thorn. That is still a way forward.
I'd be careful not to treat that shift as disobedience. It may be the partner adapting.
I'd ask what she notices that tells her the difference between those two moods.

contexts.subject: The girl says a self-protective partner starts attacking when sufficiently hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlDe.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it looks after itself!\nBut if it gets enough ouchies,\lit will hit back!$

replies.text: A careful little one, right up until somebody spends too long testing its patience.
She predicts a reversal from defensive choices toward attack under pressure.
Cautious doesn't mean harmless. Remember that.
I understand being quiet until something finally pushes too far.
I'd rather keep it comfortable than rely on hurting it to bring that side out.
A reserved partner with a rather emphatic final response to persistent inconvenience.
The boundary is polite until it isn't. A familiar arrangement.
Its offensive options should remain useful even if it seldom favors them at first.
A sheltered creature may still have teeth behind the door.
People mistake self-protection for weakness until the expression changes.
I'd watch how it signals discomfort before that switch. There may be earlier clues.

contexts.subject: The girl says this partner consistently favors protecting itself.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlDe.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it looks after itself!\nIt says it worries about itself whether\lor not it has a lot of ouchies!$

replies.text: This little one has read the safety instructions and intends to keep the booklet.
The reading suggests a stable defensive preference across different levels of pressure.
It values staying safe. Work with that instead of fighting it.
I don't think wanting to protect itself is something to be embarrassed about.
A careful partner deserves a plan that doesn't demand constant recklessness.
A consistent philosophy, apparently untroubled by the audience's appetite for spectacle.
Self-preservation remains in fashion through every stage of the encounter.
We can check whether the moves give that preference productive options.
Some creatures carry their shelter with them in the choices they make.
I'd rather understand its caution than dress it up as a personality flaw.
I'd compare the reading with how it behaves outside battles. The contrast could be interesting.

contexts.subject: The girl says a protective partner turns to indirect interference when hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlDe.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it looks after itself!\nBut if it gets enough ouchies,\lit will turn sneaky!$

replies.text: First it minds its own business. Then it makes the opponent's business considerably more difficult.
The predicted shift is from self-protection toward disrupting the opponent under pressure.
Cautious first, disruptive later. We can prepare around that.
It sounds as though it changes from hiding the trouble to trying to control it.
A good plan should give it useful choices before and after that change.
A private little creature with a practical backup policy of becoming somebody else's problem.
The careful partner keeps a small reserve of mischief for emergencies. Sensible.
We should inspect the support options instead of assuming defensive moves cover both preferences.
When the shelter stops feeling safe, the hands begin rearranging the shadows outside.
I like knowing there's more to it than the first cautious impression.
I'd ask how she distinguishes protective behavior from the later indirect tactics.

contexts.subject: The girl says an indirect tactician attacks directly when hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlSu.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it likes to be sneaky!\nBut if it gets enough ouchies,\lit will hit back!$

replies.text: A sneaky start, then a very direct complaint if things get painful. Quite clear by the end.
Her reading predicts a shift from interference toward direct offense under pressure.
Don't leave it without an attack it can actually use.
I wonder whether the opponent ever notices the change before it happens.
I'd give that partner room for both cleverness and a straightforward answer.
The subtle approach has a point at which it formally resigns and hands over to force.
Mischief, followed by a firm rejection of further subtlety.
The moves should support the change rather than leave the favored late approach unavailable.
A winding path can end in one very straight line.
It may look playful at first. That doesn't mean every later choice will stay playful.
I'd watch for the point where its attention changes. The transition might be easy to miss.

contexts.subject: The girl says an indirect tactician becomes self-protective when hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlSu.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it likes to be sneaky!\nBut if it gets enough ouchies,\lit will worry about itself!$

replies.text: It enjoys making trouble until trouble gets personal. Then it quite reasonably checks the exits.
The described preference changes from disruption toward self-protection under pressure.
A defensive option matters once it's worn down.
It can be clever and still need somewhere safe when the battle turns hard.
I'd rather help it protect itself than expect the mischief to last forever.
A cunning opening, with a sensible clause reserving the right to look after oneself.
The prankster has discovered personal consequences and adjusted the program.
We should plan for both preferences instead of giving it only interference moves.
A creature can enjoy stirring the water and still seek a quiet bank afterward.
Its playful side doesn't cancel the need for care when it's struggling.
I'd ask whether her reading matches the partner's habits in unfamiliar places, too.

contexts.subject: The girl says this partner prefers indirect tactics even when hurt.

BattleFrontier_Lounge5_Text_NatureGirlSu.text: Hmhm…\pThis one says it likes to be sneaky!\nIt says it likes to be sneaky even\lif it has a lot of ouchies!$

replies.text: A committed little schemer. Even a difficult afternoon apparently can't interrupt the plotting.
She reports a consistent interference preference regardless of the pressure state.
Give it useful indirect options. Still watch its condition.
I wonder whether it enjoys the clever part more than the battle itself.
Keeping a familiar approach may help it feel steady. We still need to know when to stop.
A dedicated specialist, unwilling to abandon the elegant nuisance even under duress.
Mischief has survived the emergency review and remains official policy.
We should check that the available support moves can accomplish something under Palace rules.
Some creatures keep tying knots even while the wind pulls hard at the thread.
It's a distinct little personality. I'd want the plan to respect it without demanding too much.
I'd watch which tactics it returns to most often. Repetition can reveal a preference clearly.

contexts.subject: The interviewer interprets declining to discuss battle feelings as cool detachment.

BattleFrontier_BattleTowerLobby_Text_Don.text: Oh, so you don't think much about it?\nYou're one cool customer.$

replies.text: We've said very little and somehow acquired an entire calm personality. Quick work.
Declining an interview doesn't establish an absence of strong feelings.
Not talking about it isn't the same as not caring.
Sometimes I feel too much to explain it neatly to a stranger.
We can keep a feeling to ourselves without needing a flattering explanation for it.
An unanswered question has been converted into a character study. Economical journalism.
Silence has been assigned a fashionable interpretation without consulting its owner.
The information wasn't collected. A conclusion about temperament goes beyond the evidence.
A closed mouth can hold an entire storm. Stillness isn't a weather report.
Cool customer sounds nice. It still isn't something we actually told him.
I'd rather leave the question open than have a quick label stand in for an answer.

contexts.subject: The interviewer calls the player fickle after a canceled answer.

BattleFrontier_BattleTowerLobby_Text_Cha.text: Hunh? You changed your mind?\nI guess you're fickle.$

replies.text: Changing one answer has apparently changed our whole reputation. That's an efficient notebook.
A canceled response may reflect uncertainty or privacy. Fickleness is only one interpretation.
We're allowed to change our mind about an interview.
I don't always find the right words on the first try. That shouldn't be a fault.
If someone can't answer comfortably, pushing a label onto them won't help.
The interview has ended with an unsolicited review of our decision-making character.
A blank answer has displeased the questionnaire. The questionnaire will recover.
Stopping an incomplete answer is better than recording something misleading.
Some words don't want to be set down just because a box is waiting.
He could leave room for hesitation without making it sound like a flaw.
I'd rather give a considered answer later than force a quick one now.

contexts.subject: The interviewer thanks the player after receiving a battle-feelings answer.

BattleFrontier_BattleTowerLobby_Text_Tha.text: Okay, so that's how you feel?\nThat's quite original.\pThanks!$

replies.text: The feeling has been safely delivered to the notebook. I hope it behaves in there.
He has accepted the response without demanding a different emotional account. Good.
Question answered. Nice to get a simple thanks.
I'm glad he let the answer belong to us instead of explaining it back.
A small honest answer can be enough. Not every interview needs a grand revelation.
An original contribution to the public record of people being nervous about battles.
The emotion has been documented. It may now return to ordinary employment.
The answer is submitted. We can see whether our feelings change after more experience.
A feeling put into words can look slightly different once it's resting outside us.
He noticed the answer as an individual one. That's a pleasant way to close.
I'd be interested to compare what people say before and after their first difficult match.

contexts.subject: A woman worries a recorded streak makes an embarrassing defeat more consequential.

BattleFrontier_BattleTowerLobby_Text_Win.text: The number of matches you win in a row\nis recorded.\pI'd better not get beaten in\nan embarrassing way!$

replies.text: The record keeps the wins. Her imagination seems determined to keep an illustrated loss as well.
The numerical record doesn't capture every detail of a defeat. Her concern adds an imagined audience.
A loss is a result. It doesn't have to become a public disgrace.
I understand worrying about how a mistake will look. It can make the room feel crowded.
She might enjoy the battles more if she leaves a little room to be human.
A simple streak counter has acquired an exceptionally severe critic living inside it.
The number is recorded. The embarrassment appears to be self-administered.
She can use the record to measure progress rather than predict humiliation.
A tally can become a mirror if you stare at it too long.
I'd hate for the fear of looking awkward to keep her from trying something useful.
I'd ask what she considers embarrassing. The standard may be much harsher than anyone else's.

contexts.subject: A boy advises being ready for the Tower round commitment.

BattleFrontier_BattleTowerLobby_Text_Can.text: Once you've entered the BATTLE TOWER,\nyou can't leave until you either lose\lor you beat seven TRAINERS in a row.\pYou'd best be certain that you're up\nto the challenge.$

replies.text: That's a longer appointment than just poking our heads through the door. Good to know.
A full round requires planning, with formal suspension distinct from simply leaving.
Know the commitment before entering. Don't wander in half-ready.
I like being warned before finding out I can't simply step away.
We should settle food, rest, and whatever else needs doing before starting.
The Tower asks that curiosity make an actual appointment before entering.
A casual visit has discovered a rather firm closing clause.
We can prepare for the full sequence and learn the proper suspension procedure.
A doorway can ask more of us than the first room reveals.
Clear expectations make it easier to choose without feeling trapped later.
I'd ask the attendant exactly how to pause properly before we begin.

contexts.subject: The greeter or information guide ends by wishing the visitor enjoyment of the Frontier.

BattleFrontier_ReceptionGate_Text_EnjoyB.text: We hope you enjoy all that the BATTLE\nFRONTIER has to offer!$

replies.text: Seven big challenges and permission to enjoy ourselves between them. I'll keep both parts.
The guide leaves the destination to us after providing the available information.
Good. We can choose our own pace from here.
I like that the farewell is about enjoying the visit, not proving something.
A good day can include a challenge and a quiet break. No need to fill every minute.
A pleasantly broad assignment. I intend to include something comfortable in our interpretation.
Enjoy everything is ambitious. I'll begin with one manageable thing.
We can choose a facility after checking its rules and our team's readiness.
An open welcome is a gentler threshold than a demand to be impressive.
They've made space for the visit to mean different things to different people.
I'd take a little time to look around before choosing where to start.

contexts.subject: Scott welcomes the player, encourages exploration, and invites a visit to his quarters.

BattleFrontier_ReceptionGate_Text_ScottG.text:
SCOTT: It's great to see you here,
it really is!\pI hope you'll take your time and
explore everywhere.\pNaturally, I hope you'll also experience
the pure essence of battling.\pI also have my quarters here, so feel
free to visit if you have time.$

replies.text: Scott's dream has actual doors now, and he's invited us through several of them.
His personal welcome connects the facilities to the long project that brought him here.
We'll look around. No need to sprint straight into a challenge.
He seems genuinely happy we came. That's a nice way to enter an unfamiliar place.
I'd visit him after settling in. He must have plenty of stories about getting this ready.
A proud host has remembered to include visiting his own cramped quarters in the grand itinerary.
The invitation has finally grown into an entire island. Scott seems pleased with the proportions.
I'd like to ask how the place went from an idea to all these working facilities.
A long-carried wish has become somewhere other people can walk. He deserves a moment to enjoy that.
He wants us to see the whole place instead of just chasing a result immediately.
I'd ask which corner he'd show a first-time visitor himself. The answer would tell us what he loves.

contexts.subject: Scott recognizes the complete silver Symbol set and successfully gives a Lansat Berry.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_YouveCol.text:
SCOTT: Are you enjoying things in
the BATTLE FRONTIER?\p…Wait a second…
Oh!\pYour FRONTIER PASS!
You've collected the full set\lof silver symbols!\pThat's more than impressive!
You are tough, just as I suspected!\pNormally, I wouldn't do something
like this, but this is a special time!\pI want you to have this.
I'm sure you can put it to proper use.$

replies.text: Seven silver Symbols have turned Scott's ordinary greeting into a very excited inspection.
The complete set represents success across seven distinct formats. A substantial breadth of skill.
Every silver Symbol earned. Good work deserves a quiet moment.
I like how genuinely surprised he sounds, even after saying he believed in us.
A little Berry carries a lot of effort behind it now. We'll look after the gift.
Scott suspected greatness and is still rather delighted to encounter the evidence in person.
Seven hard-earned marks have produced one very enthusiastic man and a Berry.
Success across different rules means the team adapted repeatedly. That's worth recognizing.
Seven small signs hold a very long path between them.
He noticed the whole set before we needed to announce it. That feels good.
I'd ask which accomplishment surprised him most. He sounds ready to tell us.

contexts.subject: Scott recognizes the complete gold Symbol set and successfully gives a Starf Berry.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_YouveCol.text:
SCOTT: I hope you're enjoying
everything in the BATTLE FRONTIER.\p…Wait a second…
Oh, my disbelieving eyes!\pYour FRONTIER PASS!
You've gathered up the full set\lof gold symbols!\pThat's more than stupendous!
You're incredible, just as I suspected!\p… … … … … …\p{PLAYER}, you've got to accept this!\pI think you will be able to
appreciate the value of my gift!$

replies.text: Scott has checked his eyes, checked the pass, and apparently run out of ordinary compliments.
Completing every gold Symbol demonstrates repeated success under the Frontier's strongest tests.
The whole gold set. We know what each one cost to earn.
He went quiet for a moment. I think that was the most sincere part.
That's a gift worth keeping carefully. Not because it replaces all the work behind it.
A collector of exceptional trainers has encountered evidence that briefly exceeds his prepared vocabulary.
The pass has startled the man responsible for inventing reasons to fill it.
The complete set reflects adaptability and persistence, not just one favorable matchup.
Gold doesn't show every tired step. We remember those even when the light catches it.
I like the moment when his practiced confidence turns into genuine astonishment.
I'd want to hear everyone's memory of the hardest part. The set means something different from each angle.

contexts.subject: Scott cannot give the achievement Berry because the Berry pocket is full.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_BerryPoc.text: Your BERRY POCKET seems to\nbe stuffed.$

replies.text: The achievement fits on the pass. Its Berry reward is having a harder time fitting anywhere.
The reward wasn't delivered. Capacity, rather than eligibility, is blocking it.
Make room in the Berry pocket. We can collect it later.
It's a small delay after a big achievement. Nothing we've earned has changed.
Let's sort the Berries carefully. No reason to waste something useful just because we're excited.
A remarkable accomplishment has been briefly stalled by a very ordinary inventory problem.
The celebration has encountered the practical limits of fruit storage.
We need a suitable free slot before repeating the collection step.
A full pocket can pause a gift without diminishing the hands that earned it.
I appreciate a clear explanation. We don't have to wonder whether the reward disappeared.
I'd check what we can use or store before returning. A simple plan should settle it.

contexts.subject: After the Berry reward, Scott congratulates himself for recognizing the player talent.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_SoGladIB.text: I must say I have the gift of knowing\na good TRAINER when I see one.\pI'm so glad I had the foresight to\nbring you here!$

replies.text: He's proud of us and has very kindly saved a second serving of pride for himself.
His invitation helped create the opportunity. The performance still belongs to the trainer and team.
He made a good call. We did the battles. Both can be true.
He sounds happy to have been right about someone. That's rather human.
I'm glad his welcome led somewhere good. The team still deserves most of this praise.
An excellent achievement, now featuring a brief commemorative tribute to Scott's judgment.
Our success has earned Scott a small personal trophy in his own mind.
Spotting talent matters, but so does what happened after the invitation.
He planted the welcome. Many other hands tended what grew after it.
He's slipping himself into the congratulations. At least he's cheerful about it.
I'd ask what first caught his attention. Now would be a good time for a specific answer.

contexts.subject: After the shield reward, Scott expresses expectations for future achievements.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_Expectin.text: I'll be expecting to hear even greater\nthings about you now!$

replies.text: We've received a shield and immediately been assigned a larger supply of expectations. Busy gift.
He acknowledges the current achievement while predicting further progress. The prediction isn't an obligation.
Good to be recognized. We can still choose the next goal ourselves.
I'm glad he's pleased. I hope we can enjoy this before thinking about being greater again.
A reward deserves a little time to be simply enjoyed, without becoming the next deadline.
The congratulations have barely sat down before the expectations are standing up again.
The shield blocks attacks. Its effectiveness against ambitious compliments remains untested.
We can evaluate the next challenge after reviewing the effort that earned this recognition.
A milestone can be a resting place before it becomes a sign pointing onward.
Belief is encouraging when it leaves someone room to set their own pace.
I'd take time to remember what we just accomplished before asking what comes next.

contexts.subject: Scott postpones the shield gift because decoration storage has no room.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_ComeBack.text: Oops, well, if you have too much\nstuff, come back for this later.$

replies.text: A shield waiting for a place to stand. Even an honor needs a little floor space.
The decoration hasn't been received. Scott explicitly leaves collection open for later.
We'll make room and return. The achievement isn't going anywhere.
I'm glad he made it sound like a delay instead of losing the chance.
We can look through what we already have before deciding where the shield belongs.
A hard-earned honor is waiting in the temporary department of furniture logistics.
The shield has been defeated by a complete lack of shelf space. A humiliating matchup.
We should free a decoration slot, then repeat the gift collection.
A place must be made before a new memory can sit among the old ones.
I'd rather choose its place thoughtfully than cram it into whatever corner happens to open.
A return visit will give us another chance to hear Scott sound proud. That's no hardship.

contexts.subject: After giving introductory points, Scott explains earning and spending Battle Points.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_ExplainB.text:
SCOTT: You can check your Battle
Points on your FRONTIER PASS.\pThe more success you have here at
the BATTLE FRONTIER, the more Battle\lPoints you will collect.\pUse your Battle Points the way you
see fit, like trading them for items.$

replies.text: A little starting help and directions to the prize counter. Scott understands a welcoming packet.
The points are credited, and the Pass provides a way to check the balance. Useful orientation.
We have the points. We'll choose what to spend them on.
I like that he leaves the choice with us after explaining it.
We don't need to spend them immediately. A useful thing later can be a good first choice.
The grand welcome has acquired a practical allowance and a clear set of spending instructions.
A small purse of possibilities. The cushions are presumably already campaigning.
We can compare rewards with their costs before setting a longer-term point goal.
A gift can remain a possibility for a while. It needn't become an object at once.
Choose as we see fit is a pleasant thing to hear from someone giving a gift.
I'd look through the exchange choices before deciding which points goal feels worthwhile.

contexts.subject: After the introductory gift, Scott enthusiastically expects future achievements.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_Expectin.text: I'm expecting great things from you!$

replies.text: Scott's optimism has apparently booked a very long stay. We'll take the first challenge first.
He is expressing confidence rather than reporting a future result. The work remains ahead.
We'll do the work at our own pace.
It's nice to be believed in. It's also a little heavy when someone says it that confidently.
I'd like us to enjoy the visit while we discover what we're actually ready for.
A concise statement containing an impressively large quantity of future pressure.
Great things are expected. Ordinary lunch remains necessary in the meantime.
A useful next step is choosing one facility and learning its specific rules.
A hopeful gaze can feel warm and weighty at the same time.
He means it kindly. We still get to decide what success should look like for us.
I'd ask what he enjoys seeing in a first-time challenger besides the final result.

contexts.subject: Scott praises his handpicked Frontier Brains and expects the player to impress them.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_HaveYouM.text:
SCOTT: Have you met any of
the FRONTIER BRAINS?\pBetter yet, have you obtained any
symbols from them?\pI handpicked the FRONTIER BRAINS
as the toughest TRAINERS anywhere.\pBut I'm sure that seeing how tough
you are will startle even them!$

replies.text: He picked the toughest people he could find, then invited us to surprise them. Mischievous host.
His confidence suggests a serious test, but it doesn't replace information about each specialist.
They were chosen for a reason. We'll prepare instead of relying on his confidence.
I wonder which of them was hardest for him to persuade to come here.
He seems proud of everyone involved. I'd like the challengers to feel welcome as well as tested.
The proud organizer is preparing to watch his carefully selected experts be startled by his other discovery.
He has assembled both sides of the problem and seems delighted with himself.
I'd ask how their specialties shaped the different facilities. That could guide our preparation.
Seven strong wills gathered by one persistent invitation. The meetings must have been interesting.
He makes the place sound like a collection of people he genuinely admires.
I'd ask him to tell us about recruiting one of them. Those stories won't appear on a record board.

contexts.subject: Scott hints that wild Pokemon can be found somewhere within the Frontier.

BattleFrontier_ScottsHouse_Text_MayFindW.text:
SCOTT: You don't just train for battle,
right?\pI think I remember you working on
a POKéDEX as well.\pWell, guess what?\pYou may run into wild POKéMON in
the BATTLE FRONTIER somewhere…\lFufufu!$

replies.text: He's hidden a little nature walk inside his enormous battle invitation. Sneaky hospitality.
A useful habitat lead, though he hasn't specified the species or exact location.
We'll look carefully. No reason to charge after an unknown encounter.
I'm glad there's something here that didn't come just to enter a tournament.
A quiet search could be a welcome change from the buildings and crowds.
An island of organized contests has retained a few residents who declined to register.
The wildlife has apparently ignored the admission criteria. Admirable independence.
We can investigate accessible areas and note any actual sightings rather than assume the species.
Even a place built for people has corners that answer to something else.
He remembered another interest of ours. That makes the hint feel personal.
I'd ask where people last saw something unusual, then explore without disturbing its shelter.

contexts.subject: The Pike hint attendant apologizes after the player declines advice.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: I see…\nI apologize for my impertinence…$

replies.text: An offer, a no, and a perfectly polite retreat. A very well-behaved fork in the road.
The attendant accepts the refusal without insisting that guidance is needed.
No offense taken. We can choose for ourselves.
I like that saying no doesn't make the room uncomfortable.
It's considerate to offer help and just as considerate to let someone decline.
Advice withdrawn with such elaborate courtesy that I feel we ought to thank the punctuation.
The guidance has stepped back without haunting us about it.
We can use our own judgment. The declined hint doesn't reveal anything about the rooms.
A hand offered and gently withdrawn leaves the path open.
They left our choice intact. Good manners can be that simple.
I'd remember the offer if we wanted advice on another visit.

contexts.subject: The attendant reports a Pokemon scent from the indicated path without guaranteeing its outcome.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: It seems to have the distinct aroma\nof POKéMON wafting around it…$

replies.text: A Pokemon smell is a clue. My nose would probably submit the much less useful report of smells indoors.
The scent is a hint category, not a complete account of what the room contains.
A clue, not a promise. Stay prepared.
I wonder how long they've worked here to recognize a path by its smell.
I'd use the hint without treating the room as safe before we've seen it.
The report is fragrant and deliberately incomplete. A distinctive information service.
The corridor has offered an aroma instead of a guarantee. Sensible of it.
We can weigh this clue against the team's current condition before choosing.
A scent arrives before its source. It doesn't always tell the whole story.
The uncertainty is part of the advice. I wouldn't trim it away just to feel confident.
I'd ask what they've actually smelled there before. Experience may make the hint more useful.

contexts.subject: The attendant senses people or a possible trainer down the indicated path.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: Is it… A TRAINER?\nI sense the presence of people…$

replies.text: Someone ahead. Whether they brought a battle or just conversation remains annoyingly important.
The attendant reports a human presence while remaining uncertain about the role.
People ahead. Keep the team ready without assuming a fight.
I think the pause before trainer matters. They aren't certain.
It might be help or a challenge. We should choose with enough strength for either.
The report confirms possible company while declining to guarantee the quality of the visit.
A person may be waiting. Humanity continues its excellent record of being ambiguous.
A human presence narrows the possibilities without settling the encounter.
A presence behind a door can be a welcome or a weight. We haven't heard its voice yet.
I'd listen to the uncertainty instead of remembering only the word trainer.
I'd be curious what made them sense a person rather than a Pokemon.

contexts.subject: The attendant reports possible whispering from the indicated path.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: I seem to have heard something…\nIt may have been whispering…$

replies.text: The room is whispering and the hint is whispering about the whispering. Very discreet confusion.
A tentative auditory report. It doesn't establish who produced the sound or why.
Could be voices. Don't turn a sound into a certainty.
I'd probably stop and listen, too. Quiet voices make me curious and nervous at once.
We'll keep the team prepared. A soft sound doesn't mean a gentle encounter.
A possibly whispered message has been relayed with appropriately whispered confidence.
The uncertainty is quiet, but admirably persistent.
We have an observation to consider, not enough detail to deduce the room's result.
A wall can make an ordinary voice sound as though it belongs to a secret.
I'd avoid filling the quiet with a story more certain than what they actually heard.
I'd ask whether the sound repeated. One little detail could change how we read it.

contexts.subject: The attendant describes an unexplained feeling of nostalgia from the indicated path.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: For some odd reason, I felt a wave\nof nostalgia coming from it…$

replies.text: A corridor that feels like an old memory. I wonder whether it also remembers where we left our lunch.
The reported sensation is subjective. Its meaning within this challenge still requires caution.
An odd clue. We'll judge the room when we reach it.
I wonder what kind of memory it brought back. They sounded surprised by it.
A familiar feeling can be comforting without being a reliable promise.
The directions have become unexpectedly sentimental. I hadn't packed for a reunion with a hallway.
Nostalgia from an unopened room. Even the past is being coy today.
We can consider the hint without assigning it an outcome we haven't observed.
Sometimes a place touches a memory before we find its name. That doesn't tell us what's waiting.
It's an evocative description. I'd be careful not to mistake the feeling for evidence of safety.
I'd ask what felt familiar. The answer might tell us more about the attendant than the room.

contexts.subject: The attendant senses something dreadful down every path near the Pike Queen encounter.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: From every path I sense a dreadful\npresence…$

replies.text: All three doors have received the same unsettling review. That does simplify the comparison.
The warning applies across the available paths. It doesn't identify a safer alternative.
Check the team before moving. There isn't a clearly safe choice here.
I don't like hearing every path described that way. At least we know to be careful.
I'd take a moment to see how everyone's doing before stepping into another room.
A choice of three distinct routes to one thoroughly consistent atmosphere.
The doors have formed a united front of bad impressions.
With no differentiated hint, preparation matters more than trying to infer a favored door.
Three shadows can belong to the same waiting shape.
A warning that clear deserves attention without letting it decide how frightened we have to be.
I'd ask whether anything can be checked before we proceed. Practical details help when the mood turns ominous.

contexts.subject: The attendant approaches to warn of an especially difficult event ahead.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeThreePathRoom_T.text: I am sorry to say…\pA terrifying event, yes, a horrible one,\nis about to befall you…\pI urge you to pay the utmost care\nand prepare for the worst…$

replies.text: That's the sort of warning that makes the whole corridor sit up straighter.
The attendant has singled out the next event as unusually difficult. Prepare rather than assume the result.
Stop and check what we can. A warning is useful only if we act on it.
They came over to tell us. That makes me take the concern seriously.
I'd rather spend an extra moment getting ready than rush to look fearless.
An exceptionally emphatic warning from a place that already considers giant snakes welcoming.
The ordinary uncertainty has been upgraded to an official ominous announcement.
We should review the team's condition and available protections before continuing.
A careful voice has stepped into our path. It's worth becoming still enough to hear it.
They're trying to help us prepare. We don't need to turn that into a prediction of failure.
I'd focus on what we can still check instead of imagining the worst in elaborate detail.

contexts.subject: A fortunate room restores the whole team and the attendant sends the player onward.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeRoomNormal_Text.text: I urge you to enjoy the rest of your\nBattle Choice challenge…$

replies.text: Everyone restored, and no battle bill attached. That's a room I'd happily recommend.
The healing is complete. The next choices can be made from a much stronger condition.
Whole team restored. Good break. Don't waste it by getting careless.
It's a relief seeing everyone steadier before we move on.
A little help at the right time can change the whole journey. Thank the attendant.
A rare room whose hospitality includes precisely what tired visitors were hoping for.
Good fortune has briefly become tangible and extremely welcome.
We can reassess the route now that the team's immediate condition has improved.
A hard path has offered a gentle hand for once.
The farewell feels warmer when everyone is actually better off for the visit.
I'd remember this room after the challenge. Helpful surprises deserve a place beside the difficult ones.

contexts.subject: After defeating the tough trainer, the team receives full healing and a farewell.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeRoomNormal_Text.text: I urge you to enjoy the rest of your\nBattle Choice challenge…$

replies.text: A hard fight, then a proper recovery. Nice when a room remembers the second half.
The victory was followed by full restoration. That removes the immediate condition cost of the encounter.
Won the fight and recovered. Ready to think about the next choice.
I'm glad the effort didn't leave everyone carrying the same exhaustion onward.
A tough test is easier to appreciate after somebody helps the team recover.
The demanding reception has redeemed itself with excellent aftercare.
A difficult room has concluded by returning what the battle borrowed. Much appreciated.
We should use the improved condition while still preparing for varied rooms ahead.
A bruise can fade before its lesson does. This room has allowed that.
The recovery makes the congratulations feel practical instead of merely decorative.
I'd ask which choice helped us most in that fight while the details are still clear.

contexts.subject: After healing one or two partners, the attendant bids the player farewell.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeRoomNormal_Text.text: The best of luck to you.\nFarewell.$

replies.text: Some welcome help, though we should check exactly who still needs a rest.
The partial restoration has finished. This shared farewell doesn't specify whether one or two were healed.
Check the team. The farewell doesn't mean everyone is restored.
I'm glad somebody got help. I'd want to make sure nobody else is quietly struggling.
A little recovery helps. Let's not assume it covered every partner.
A courteous departure after a useful but limited amount of hospitality.
Luck has provided assistance rather than a complete renovation.
We need to inspect the remaining condition before selecting another path.
A hand can help part of the burden without lifting all of it.
I'd appreciate the help and still take stock. Both responses fit.
I'd look over each partner before moving. The detail matters more than the broad farewell.

contexts.subject: After a startled Pokemon attacks, its trainer explains and asks whether the team is all right.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeRoomNormal_Text.text: It attacks without warning if it is\nstartled by another person…\pAre you and your POKéMON all right?$

replies.text: Being startled explains the sudden attack. It doesn't check our poor team's condition for us.
The explanation identifies a trigger. We should still assess the actual effects on each partner.
Check the team first. Then give that Pokemon more space.
It sounds frightened rather than cruel. Our partners still need looking after.
I'd make sure everyone is settled before having a long conversation about what happened.
A useful explanation, arriving rather late in the ideal sequence for avoiding an ambush.
The apology has arrived after the damage. Timing remains a difficult art.
Knowing the trigger should help prevent another incident. It doesn't undo the first one.
Fear can strike outward before anyone finds its name. We should tend what it touched.
I appreciate being asked. I'd also like them to keep visitors from startling it again.
I'd answer after checking the team. A polite reassurance shouldn't hide a real problem.

contexts.subject: The trainer apologizes again for the earlier startled-Pokemon incident.

BattleFrontier_BattlePikeRoomNormal_Text.text: I do apologize for what happened…\nI do hope your POKéMON are fine.$

replies.text: The apology is kind. I'd also welcome a plan that keeps the next visitor out of the splash zone.
The repeated apology acknowledges the incident, but doesn't establish that its effects are gone.
We should check our partners rather than assume they're fine.
I think they feel bad. I also don't want to pretend nothing happened just to comfort them.
A sincere apology is a start. Helping prevent another accident would make it stronger.
Regret is welcome. A little practical prevention would make an excellent companion to it.
The remorse appears genuine. Unfortunately, remorse isn't a healing move.
They could give the Pokemon more space and warn people before another close approach.
A frightened creature needs care. So do the ones caught in its fear.
We can accept the apology without calling the whole situation harmless.
I'd ask how they plan to help the Pokemon feel safer around visitors.

contexts.subject: After declining to quit, the attendant asks the player to continue choosing a tag partner.

BattleFrontier_BattleTowerMultiPartnerRo.text: Then, please find a partner from\nthe TRAINERS gathered here.$

replies.text: The search continues. Somewhere in this room is a pair of Pokemon waiting for our very careful introduction.

Take the time to choose well. No need to grab the nearest volunteer.
I'd like to hear how each person talks about their partners, not just which moves they know.
A good match should make both sides comfortable with the plan.
The committee has declined to leave and must now resume the difficult work of choosing company.
The partner search has survived its first attempt to become an exit.
We can compare move interactions before committing to a team.
Staying leaves the possibility open. We still have to walk toward someone.
I'd choose someone we can communicate with, as well as a useful pair of Pokemon.
I'd ask a little more before deciding. This room is full of potential stories and teammates.

contexts.subject: A grunt concludes future invasions should be unannounced.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Grunt1P.text: Okay, I get it already! The next time,\nwe'll come unannounced.$

replies.text: The problem was the stealing, not the quality of the invitation.
He has revised the announcement instead of examining the objective.
Wrong lesson. Leave the center alone.
It's unsettling hearing someone make the harmful part sound settled.
The staff deserve more than a less polite version of the same trouble.
An antagonist has mistaken a presentation note for a moral revision.
A spectacularly narrow interpretation of what went wrong.
The method and purpose need review beyond how early anyone was warned.
A hidden harm doesn't become kinder by arriving quietly.
Changing the entrance won't improve the conduct wearing it.
I'd notice what he still refuses to question while planning the next approach.

contexts.subject: On a later talk the defeated guard asks us to report he never abandoned his post.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Grunt2P.text: Please, tell our leader that\nI never abandoned my post.\lThat I stayed to the bitter end…$

replies.text: His next worry is the boss's review, not why the post needed defending.
He is focused on compliance rather than the consequences of the assignment.
Tell the truth. He still chose what he was guarding.
He sounds more worried about blame than angry with us.
Fear of punishment doesn't make this a good place to work.
A defeated guard has requested a favorable narrator for his performance report.
An unfortunate career built around how convincingly one remains in the way.
He could ask what the duty served instead of only whether he fulfilled it.
A command can make a very small room around a person's choices.
He wants his loyalty seen. I hope he also learns to question where it goes.
I'd remember both the fear in his request and the choice he still made.

contexts.subject: A defeated grunt warns one win does not establish a winning streak.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_1F_Text_Grunt3P.text: Don't think you're on a roll just\nbecause you've beaten me!$

replies.text: One win is indeed one win. We have not rented a parade.
He's right that the next opponent still needs independent attention.
We'll stay ready. No need to argue the count.
He sounds as if he wants the result to feel smaller.
The team still deserves a quick check after the match.
A defeated obstacle has supplied a useful warning in an ungracious wrapper.
A rather sharp way to state extremely basic arithmetic.
We can carry the information forward without borrowing his mood.
A step won doesn't remove the need for the next careful step.
The warning can be useful without making the delivery appealing.
I'd watch what changes ahead rather than stand here discussing our reputation.

contexts.subject: A grunt does not know the fuel's purpose and sends us to the leader upstairs.

replies.text: He has helped steal something without reading the important part.
The admission reveals a lack of understanding, not a harmless objective.

The supporting cast has not been given the central motivation.
A remarkably important omission in the job briefing.

A hand can carry something dangerous without knowing the weight of the choice.
A uniform shouldn't replace having a reason for what you do.

contexts.subject: After the three-battle sequence a grunt wonders whether they help the leader at all.

MossdeepCity_SpaceCenter_2F_Text_Grunt5P.text: Are we being useful to our leader\nat all?$

replies.text: A better question might be whether the leader is asking anything worthwhile.
Usefulness to a supervisor isn't the same as a good result for everyone affected.

Loyalty isn't much of a fit if it leaves no room to think.

replies.text: A larger committee has produced the same awkward conclusion.
