He sounds certain of the feeling, less certain of the facts.
I wonder which actual clue has kept him looking all this time.

contexts.subject: An older trainer explains that certain evolutions need both trading and a held item.

SixIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_SomeMons.text:
You know of POKéMON that evolve
only upon trading, yes?\pBut did you know that there are
still others?\pSome POKéMON evolve only when
traded while holding specific items.$

replies.text: A change with a very particular packing list. Worth checking before the handoff.
Some triggers require multiple conditions rather than the trade alone.
Know the requirements before asking a friend to help.
It is easy to miss one small condition in a complicated change.
A little preparation saves disappointment for both trainers.
The transformation scene has added a specific prop requirement.
Some futures need a meeting and the right small thing carried into it.
Compound condition. Both inputs have to be present.
A journey can depend on what travels quietly beside the traveler.
Good detail to share before someone assumes every trade works the same way.
I wonder which species taught the trainer to check the held item.

contexts.subject: The rival accepts that the islands cannot complete the Pokedex and chooses to collect at his pace, with a final jab.

SixIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_RivalImp.text:
{RIVAL}: Hey, {PLAYER}!
How's your POKéDEX filling up?\pIt looks like it's impossible to get
all the POKéMON by hanging around\ljust these parts.\pMaybe there are POKéMON we don't
know about somewhere far away…\p… … …  … … …  … … …\pWell, if I can't do it, there's no
way for you to get it done.\pI'm not going to get all desperate
over this.\pI'll keep collecting POKéMON at my
own pace while I train them.\pThat's what I'll do.
So there's no point staying here.\lI may as well leave for home.\pThat's that, then!
Smell ya later!$

replies.text: A sensible plan has nearly made it through an entire rival speech without an elbow attached.
He recognizes geographic limits and proposes sustainable progress. The comparison with us is unnecessary.
His pace is his. Ours is ours. Good to hear he is not forcing the whole job.
There is a little relief in the decision beneath all the familiar bravado.
A routine that cares for the team is better than a desperate collection sprint.
The rival discovers moderation and hurriedly disguises it as another declaration of superiority.
A quieter plan is allowed to be wise without being everybody else's defeat.
Sampling limits recognized, objective revised. Sound adjustment under noisy packaging.
The map has become large enough to let the next step be small again.
He could leave the insult behind and keep the useful part.
I wonder what partner he will spend time training when he gets home.

contexts.subject: The scientist steals the Sapphire, plans to sell it, and gives a warehouse password before leaving.

SixIsland_DottedHole_SapphireRoom_Text_S.text:
I knew that there was a SAPPHIRE
here, so it belongs to me!\pI'll sell it to TEAM ROCKET for
serious money.\p…D-don't glare at me like that!\pIf you want it back, why don't you
go get it after I sell it?\pI'll even tell you one of the
passwords to TEAM ROCKET's\lWAREHOUSE.\pThe WAREHOUSE password I know is
“Yes, nah, CHANSEY.”\pI'm done.
Don't think badly of me!$

replies.text: Knowing where a stone is does not make stealing it clever or fair. At least he spilled a lead.
He asserts ownership without a valid basis, then supplies actionable information about the warehouse.
Remember the password. His request for a good opinion can wait until he earns one.
It is ugly to hear someone narrate taking the thing we worked to reach.
A useful lead does not make his theft a favor. We should follow it prepared.
The opportunist exits with a stolen prop and the extraordinary request that the audience review him kindly.
A pocket can hold a gem without holding a decent reason for taking it.
Resource stolen, recovery route partially disclosed. Record the credential accurately.
A blue little thing has been pulled into a very small-minded plan.
He wants the profitable part of being cruel without the uncomfortable part of being judged.
I wonder whether the buyers are as trustworthy as he imagines.

contexts.subject: The scientist admits he cannot enter the ruins.

replies.text: A closed door has found somebody very determined to keep frowning at it.
The access method remains unknown. Closer observation is a better next step than force.
Look for the mechanism before trying to break anything.
It is frustrating to stand so close to something you came to understand.
A patient look can save the place from a frustrated decision.
The eager explorer has reached a rather literal limit in the opening chapter.
A door is allowed to remain a question for a while.
Unknown interface. Inspect the markings before choosing an input.
Old stone keeping its answer behind a familiar-looking shape.
He could ask for help without needing to look certain first.
I wonder which approaches he has already tried.

SixIsland_RuinValley_Text_CantFigureOutH.text: I can't figure out how I'm supposed\nto get inside.$

contexts.subject: The Heracross enthusiast sings her devotion when no measuring attempt begins.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_LoveItNe.text: Hera, hera, HERACROSS!\nBig and shiny, it's the bug boss!\lLove it, need it, HERACROSS!$

replies.text: A remarkably specific little anthem. Heracross has a committed publicity department.
A narrow interest can inspire close attention, though size should not eclipse individual care.
Nothing wrong with a favorite. Keep the actual partner comfortable.
It is sweet to hear enthusiasm that is not trying to sound sophisticated.
She has made a whole cheerful moment out of one Pokemon she loves.
The local Heracross society opens with its enthusiastic national song.
A strange small joy, worn without embarrassment. I respect that.
Clear subject expertise, strong user enthusiasm. Unusually musical introduction.
A little shining creature has filled her room with a tune.
She knows her theme and commits to it completely.
I wonder whether the tune changes when a particularly big one visits.

contexts.subject: After rewarding a record Heracross, the enthusiast immediately hopes to see a larger one.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_WantToSe.text: I want to see a much, much bigger\nHERACROSS than that one.\pOh, how I adore them, big\nHERACROSS!$

replies.text: A record falls, and her imagination grows a bigger horn at once.
The record has advanced. The next target remains optional, not a measure of every future catch.
Good result. No need to make the partner keep proving its size.
Her joy is obvious, even if the next wish arrives very quickly.
We can enjoy the good catch before making the day another search.
The reigning champion receives applause and an immediate request for a larger sequel.
A living creature should be more than a mark somebody wants to move up a wall.
Benchmark updated. Further improvement is not compulsory.
A little number has made her picture something even larger.
Enthusiasm is charming. Knowing when to be pleased with what is here helps too.
I wonder whether she keeps a drawing of each new record holder.

contexts.subject: The measured Heracross equals the existing record.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_ItsXSize.text: Huh? This {STR_VAR_2} measurement…\nOh, boo! It's the same as before.$

replies.text: An equally impressive bug has somehow produced a disappointed noise. Tough judging room.
The measurement matches the previous record rather than exceeding it.
Still a fine partner. A tie is not a flaw.
It seems unfair for matching something remarkable to sound like a failure.
A good outing does not need an ever-larger ruler mark.
The exclusive size competition has found a perfectly matched rival and declined to celebrate.
A little living sameness can still be interesting.
Repeated measurement at the benchmark. Useful, even without a new maximum.
The same height can hold an entirely different little life.
She might notice more if she looked beyond the figure on the page.
I wonder how different the two partners are in every way she did not measure.

contexts.subject: The enthusiast dismisses the Heracross as smaller than the recorded best.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_ItsXSize.text: Oh, it's just {STR_VAR_2}.\nThe HERACROSS before was bigger.\pIt was {STR_VAR_3}, the biggest\nHERACROSS you've brought me.$

replies.text: A shorter horn is still attached to a whole worthy Pokemon. The ruler can relax.
The size comparison establishes only that this one is below the current maximum.
No record. No reason to make the partner feel unwanted.
I would hate for the little one to hear only disappointment in the greeting.
Care should not depend on being the biggest arrival in the room.
The critic has confused a narrow contest result with a complete character review.
A living thing does not need a superlative before it deserves warmth.
Below benchmark is a measurement, not a defect report.
Smallness has not made the life inside any less complete.
A real eye for a creature should notice something besides the one feature it prefers.
I wonder what this one does that would make its own trainer smile.

contexts.subject: The enthusiast rejects another species and describes the Heracross appearance she expects.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_ThisWont.text: Oh, no! This won't do!\pHERACROSS looks much more macho\nand cool, and has a lovely horn!$

replies.text: Wrong contest, perfectly good Pokemon. It can leave without adopting the required horn.
The selected species does not qualify for this particular comparison.
That partner is fine as it is. Select the right one if we want the measurement.
An awkward mistake does not need quite that much dramatic disappointment.
We can correct the selection without making the Pokemon part of the joke.
The exclusive casting call insists on a horn and an exceptionally specific silhouette.
An unfamiliar shape has been told it is wrong for being itself. Unhelpful.
Species mismatch detected. No need to insult the input.
The narrow doorway belongs to the contest, not to the world's idea of worth.
She knows what she asked for. A kinder refusal would still work.
I wonder whether she notices the difference between excitement and making another partner feel small.

contexts.subject: The Heracross reward cannot fit in our bag.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_YourBagI.text: Your BAG is full.\nMy reward won't fit.$

replies.text: The measuring was ready. The bag was the part that failed the size test.
The reward transfer did not complete because of capacity.
Make room before another handoff. No need to hurry the partner around.
An awkward little finish to something she was so excited about.
A moment of sorting can spare everyone another failed exchange.
The size competition has been unexpectedly defeated by a different small container.
A crowded bag turning somebody's enthusiasm into a sigh.
Capacity check failed. Keep the reward separate from the completed measurement.
A little offered thing has no place left to sit in our pockets.
We should manage our own belongings before making her repeat the offer.
I wonder what has been taking up that last bit of space.

contexts.subject: A neighbor reports his exact height because the Heracross enthusiast measured him too.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House2_Text_MyNeighb.text: My height is 67.0 inches on the\nbutton.\pI know it is this precisely because\nmy neighbor measured me.$

replies.text: The measuring project has escaped the insect category and reached the neighbors.
A precise figure, though the circumstances of the measurement are more memorable than the number.
Hope he agreed to be measured. A hobby still needs boundaries.
I would be surprised to become part of the local record book that way.
At least he seems willing to tell the story without much annoyance.
The nearby measurement office has expanded its services with remarkable geographic efficiency.
A small town is a dangerous place to stand near an enthusiast with a ruler.
An exact reported value. I would still ask about the method and repeatability.
A familiar person reduced, briefly, to a very specific mark on the wall.
An unexpected form of neighborhood participation. At least he knows his number now.
I wonder whether the neighbor gets asked to confirm the measuring equipment regularly.

contexts.subject: An elder contrasts the island-count explanation with a legend of creation in seven days.

SevenIsland_Text_IslandsMadeInSevenDays.text:
These islands are called the SEVII
ISLANDS because there are seven.\p…Or at least that's what the young
people believe.\pThe truth is, these islands are so
named because they are said to\lhave been made in seven days.$

replies.text: Seven islands, seven days, and at least two opinions waiting by the same sign.
He offers a traditional naming account. A legend is not the same as verified geological history.
Interesting story. Let it stay a story until there is evidence for more.
I like hearing the older meaning a familiar name has for someone.
A name can carry several generations' different ways of belonging to a place.
The island's title receives competing editorial notes from two generations.
A little old tale still tucked inside an ordinary name.
Alternative etymology reported. Needs a historical source for confirmation.
Seven pieces of land, held together by a story as well as water.
The elder wants the old account remembered, even if the young use a simpler one.
I wonder who first told him that version.

contexts.subject: A local warns that the island's largely natural state makes hiking harder.

SevenIsland_Text_IslandVirtuallyUntouche.text: This island has been left virtually\nuntouched in its natural state.\pIt could be a little difficult to\nhike around because of that.$

replies.text: A beautiful place can still decline to provide convenient stairs. We should dress accordingly.
Limited development changes accessibility and route conditions. Preparation matters.
Watch the ground. An open view does not promise an easy trail.
I like that the wildness is described honestly, without pretending it is effortless.
Water, time, and a way back belong in the plan.
The setting has retained its own design rather than accepting the visitor's preferred floor plan.
A place does not have to be easy for us to be worth leaving intact.
Low infrastructure, higher navigation demand. Check equipment.
The island still lets its paths grow in their own handwriting.
Good guidance tells you about the difficult part as well as the lovely view.
I wonder which section locals find most rewarding to walk slowly.

contexts.subject: The retired battler remembers traveling widely and now enjoys watching matches.

SevenIsland_House_Room1_Text_OnlyEnjoyme.text:
I may not look like much now,
but when I was younger…\pI flew everywhere, challenging
TRAINERS wherever I found them.\pNow, my only source of enjoyment
is reminiscing about the past while\lwatching battles.$

replies.text: A long road has become a comfortable chair with a very lively view.
A continuing interest can change form as a person's circumstances change.
Good to keep enjoying the thing without needing to do it the old way.
I would like to hear one of the journeys behind that quiet introduction.
A shared match can make an ordinary afternoon feel full again.
The former performer has taken a well-informed seat in the audience.
A life does not have to stop being interesting when its footsteps slow down.
Participation mode changed. The experience and interest remain useful.
An old path still moves when someone else's battle brings it to mind.
It is nice when enthusiasm lasts beyond the role everyone once knew.
I wonder which match from those traveling years stays clearest in memory.

contexts.subject: A customer links Pikachu's hasty personality with its Speed.

SevenIsland_Mart_Text_MonHavePersonaliti.text: POKéMON have personalities of their\nown, just like people.\pMy PIKACHU has a HASTY nature,\nso it grew to be a speedy POKéMON.$

replies.text: A little personality that apparently arrives before the rest of the room is ready.
Individual nature can influence growth, though the partner is more than that mechanical effect.
Learn the Pokemon's habits. A stat is not its whole character.
It is lovely to hear someone notice a familiar partner as an individual.
A fast little companion still needs a calm routine and proper rest.
The compact biography includes both temperament and a remarkably brisk entrance.
A small creature with its own way of occupying the afternoon.
Individual parameters matter. They still do not replace observing the actual partner.
A little hurry has learned a yellow shape.
Personality is often what makes a familiar companion recognizable in a crowd.
I wonder which tiny impatient habit makes the customer smile most.

contexts.subject: A shopper has finished preparing to explore the ruins.

SevenIsland_Mart_Text_PreparationsComple.text: Okay, preparations are complete\nfor me to explore the RUINS.$

replies.text: A full checklist is a very satisfying kind of departure music.
Preparation reduces avoidable uncertainty, though the site still requires careful attention.
Good. Check the route back as well as the supplies going in.
It is nice to hear excitement with a little practical steadiness under it.
A good outing starts before the first interesting stone.
The expedition has reached the point where the props are ready and the road can begin.
A bag packed for questions instead of emergencies alone.
Prepared kit, clear destination. Strong start.
The little things are gathered so the larger old place can be met calmly.
Planning can be part of enjoying something, not just the boring delay before it.
I wonder which part of the ruins the shopper most wants to see.

contexts.subject: An angler buys supplies for the last island of a Sevii fishing tour.

SevenIsland_Mart_Text_NeedToFishOnSevenI.text: I need to fish on SEVEN ISLAND.\pThat will complete my fishing tour\nof the SEVII ISLANDS.\pI'd better stock up on some\nPOKé BALLS first, though.$

replies.text: The final shore in a very splashy travel journal. Good reason to stock up.
A comparative island tour could reveal interesting differences in catches and conditions.
Prepare for this water, not just the six places before it.
The last planned stop can feel exciting and a little sad at once.
Leave time to enjoy the day instead of turning the last entry into a rush.
The extensive angling series approaches its final scheduled episode.
A collection of quiet places, tied together by one patient habit.
Final sampling site pending. Check the consumables before departure.
Seven shores gathered along one little line cast into the sea.
The supplies are practical; the personal project gives them character.
I wonder which island has been the angler's favorite so far.

contexts.subject: A visitor hints that different connections lead to different island experiences, leaving discovery to us.

SevenIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Events.text: On this island, different events\noccur depending on connections.\pWhat are those connections?\pThey are for you to discover on\nyour own.$

replies.text: A helpful-sounding mystery with all the directions carefully removed.
The claim is broad and offers no particular event or method we can verify yet.
We can explore without pretending we know exactly what the hint means.
It is nice to leave a little room for meetings we could not plan.
A small conversation can matter without being the start of a grand secret.
The local oracle has provided an intriguing premise and declined to write the next scene.
A life does change through the people it happens to touch. No prophecy needed.
Vague dependency statement. We will need actual observations.
Some roads are made by the voices that meet along them.
An invitation to be curious is pleasant, even without an answer attached.
I wonder which connection the visitor is remembering while saying that.

contexts.subject: A traveler marvels at the many fast Seagallop ferries without knowing all their destinations.

SevenIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_DidYou.text:
Did you ride a SEAGALLOP ferry
to get here?\pThere are at least ten of those
high-speed ships.\pI don't know where they all go,
though.$

replies.text: A whole fleet of fast boats! Our little crossing was one page of a much larger timetable.
The number and routes are reported imperfectly. The traveler admits not knowing the full network.
Use the actual schedule before choosing a boat. Admiration is not a map.
It is strange realizing how many other journeys are passing just beyond your own.
A reliable ferry can make distant places part of an ordinary day.
The local transport system has a much larger recurring cast than our own ticket revealed.
Many little moving rooms keeping the islands from feeling quite so separate.
A coordinated fleet is serious infrastructure. I would love to see the route diagram.
The water holds more paths than the shore lets us see at once.
A useful reminder to ask the crew instead of guessing where every ship goes.
I wonder which route the traveler would take simply to see the view.

contexts.subject: A visitor recommends Trainer Tower to confident trainers.

SevenIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_CheckO.text: If you're confident, you should\ncheck out TRAINER TOWER.$

replies.text: A tall place for testing a big feeling. Confidence should bring a supply plan.
A specialized challenge may be useful, but confidence alone does not establish readiness.
Check the team before trying it. Nobody needs to prove anything while tired.
I would like to know the rules before deciding how brave I feel.
A good challenge is one we can leave with the partners still cared for.
The competitive itinerary has acquired an optional vertical chapter.
A tower is a very visible way to ask whether someone wants more battles.
Need specifications and entry rules before committing resources.
A high doorway waiting for a particular kind of determined footstep.
A recommendation can stay an option. We do not need to answer it immediately.
I wonder which part of the Tower keeps people coming back.

contexts.subject: A martial artist explains that even Bruno trained with Brawly and values partnership as well as solo practice.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_BrunoTrai.text:
Training by oneself is certainly
not a bad thing.\pBut it's also not bad to aim for
the top with a partner.\pEven BRUNO…
He trained with a fellow by the\lname of BRAWLY before.$

replies.text: Strong people still learn from someone standing beside them. Good to hear.
A training partner can provide feedback and challenges unavailable in solitary practice.
Work alone when it helps. Ask someone else when that helps more.
It is reassuring to hear help spoken of as part of strength.
A good partner notices when the effort needs a rest as well as a push.
The formidable fighter's biography includes a valuable second voice in the rehearsal room.
Ambition need not make a person lonely by design.
External feedback improves testing. A trusted partner is a very useful resource.
Two paths can help each other find steadier ground.
A good example without making either way of training the only respectable one.
I wonder what Bruno and Brawly each learned from the other's approach.

contexts.subject: On a return interaction after dancing, the host cheerfully repeats the invitation.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_House_Text_Cha.text: Dance, dance!\nCHANSEY Dance!\pYou join in, too!\nDance, dance!$

replies.text: The dance has survived our first performance and is requesting another audience. Brave little dance.
A familiar shared routine can be enjoyable without needing a new outcome each time.
Good fun if everyone wants to join. No need to rush the day.
It is easier the second time when you already know nobody expects perfection.
A happy little house can be a welcome rest along the road.
The local troupe retains its signature number with commendable enthusiasm.
A strange small ritual, kept warm by repetition.
Repeatable recreational protocol. Much more inviting than that description sounds.
A few familiar steps holding a little brightness in the room.
The confidence to enjoy a silly routine is quite charming.
I wonder whether every visitor adds one slightly different mistake to the dance.

contexts.subject: The host keeps encouraging us after we decline the dance.

replies.text: The enthusiasm can stay. Our feet are still allowed to say no.
An invitation should remain voluntary after the answer.
Not now. He can keep enjoying it without recruiting us.
Being urged again makes it harder to stay comfortable about an honest no.
A tired traveler may prefer a seat to a routine, however cheerful.
The eager director has missed the part where the guest declined the role.
A harmless dance can become less harmless to the mood when it will not accept a refusal.
Request declined. Repeating it does not change consent.
A happy room should still leave a quiet corner for somebody who will not dance.
The welcome would be warmer if it left room for different ways to enjoy the visit.
I wonder whether he knows some visitors are happiest simply watching.

contexts.subject: After the dance and recovery, the host happily notices our renewed energy.

replies.text: A strange little dance has left the day lighter. Excellent use of feet.
The shared activity has concluded with practical recovery and a cheerful acknowledgment.
Good rest, unexpected method. The team looks better.
I may have been embarrassed, but it is difficult not to smile now.
A little play and a little care make a good stop on a long route.
The curious performance earns its happy closing line through a genuinely useful result.
A small silly thing can make a serious tiredness feel less absolute.
Recreation and recovery in one routine. Efficiently delightful.
The room has put a little spring back where the road had taken it.
It is lovely when the odd local custom turns out to be welcoming.
I wonder how the host first decided this dance belonged with this place.

contexts.subject: Jaclyn needs to focus so she can Teleport home.

SixIsland_GreenPath_Text_JaclynPostBattl.text: I am so scatterbrained!\pI need to focus so I can TELEPORT\nproperly to my house!$

replies.text: A wandering thought is inconvenient when the rest of you plans to follow it.
A transport technique requiring concentration should wait until she feels steady.
Pause and get focused. No need to risk an uncertain jump.
I understand the worry of having your mind drift at the wrong moment.
A quiet rest might help before attempting the way home.
The next scene depends on its performer remembering the correct destination.
A scattered mind is allowed to ask the body to wait a little.
Destination certainty first. The operation can follow.
The thought of home should be clear before the feet try to arrive there.
She has noticed the problem. That is better than pretending confidence.
I wonder what familiar detail of home helps her concentrate.

contexts.subject: The defeated Rocket asks if we have seen any rare Pokemon.

SixIsland_OutcastIsland_Text_RocketPostB.text: So listen, you haven't seen any\nrare POKéMON, have you?$

replies.text: That is not a sightseeing report I feel eager to provide him.
Given his affiliation, sharing locations could expose the Pokemon to harm.
No leads for him. The rare partners can stay out of his reach.
I dislike how casually he returns to looking for something to take.
The residents here deserve more privacy than his question does.
The defeated antagonist resumes his shopping inquiry with remarkable persistence.
A curious question can be an unkind tool in the wrong mouth.
Sensitive habitat information. Do not distribute to a known risk.
Some small lives are safer remaining outside his map.
He has not given us any reason to help with that search.
I wonder how many travelers have answered without thinking where the information goes.

contexts.subject: Tylor feels he cannot go home without catching something.

SixIsland_OutcastIsland_Text_TylorPostBa.text: I can't very well go home without\ncatching something, though.$

replies.text: Home is not going to inspect the bag for proof the day was worthwhile.
A self-imposed catch requirement can turn a manageable outing into unnecessary risk.
He can go home tired and empty-handed. Better than pushing too far.
It is hard when a plan becomes a rule you feel ashamed to change.
A safe return can be the good outcome even without a new partner.
The traveler has mistaken the intended ending for a binding contract.
An unfinished list is lighter than an exhausted person.
Stop conditions should include fatigue, not just goal completion.
A road home should remain open even when the water gives nothing back.
He does not owe anyone a trophy from every afternoon outside.
I wonder what he would tell a friend in the same situation.

contexts.subject: Mymo is exhausted despite reaching only the halfway point.

SixIsland_OutcastIsland_Text_MymoPostBat.text: I'm only at the halfway point…\nI'm beat…$

replies.text: Half the route has used more than half the person. Time to revise the plan.
Remaining distance should be compared with actual stamina, not the original schedule.
Rest or turn back while there is enough strength to do it safely.
It sounds daunting to see the rest of the way while already spent.
A shorter day is better than making the last stretch an emergency.
The itinerary has become substantially more optimistic than its traveler.
A halfway mark is useful precisely because it lets you reconsider.
Energy budget insufficient for the current plan. Adjust now.
The distance ahead should not drown out what the tired body is saying.
There is nothing stylish about pretending exhaustion is imaginary.
I wonder whether there is a safe shore nearby for a proper stop.

contexts.subject: Nicole found the farther island uninteresting and asks whether we are heading there.

SixIsland_OutcastIsland_Text_NicolePostB.text: Are you headed for the island up\npast here?\pI didn't see anything interesting\nthere.$

replies.text: Her idea of interesting may not be ours. Still useful to hear the trip was uneventful.
The evaluation is subjective. A quiet site can still merit observation.
We can decide after checking the route and why we want to go.
Sometimes a place becomes interesting through the little things someone else overlooked.
A long trip should have a reason beyond proving a stranger wrong.
The destination has received a brief unfavorable notice from one returning critic.
An empty-looking island may still have quite a lot of quiet in it.
Single-user report. Check against our own objective before accepting the conclusion.
A small shore can be enough when the point is looking closely.
An honest opinion is welcome when it stays an opinion.
I wonder what Nicole had hoped to find there.

contexts.subject: Ava prefers swimming in the sea to a pool.

SixIsland_OutcastIsland_Text_AvaPostBatt.text: AVA: You know, I do prefer the\nsea over any pool.$

replies.text: The sea has a much larger ceiling and a considerably less tidy edge. I see the appeal.
Open water offers variety along with conditions that require more judgment.
Her preference. Keep the current in mind while enjoying it.
It must be lovely knowing a stretch of water well enough to feel at home.
A beautiful swim still needs energy left for the way back.
The swimmer favors the grand natural venue over the controlled rehearsal room.
A pool ends where the sea keeps beginning. A convincing difference.
Variable environment, richer experience, greater preparation needs.
The wide water refuses to hold the same shape around every stroke.
A strong preference can still leave room to respect the limits of the place.
I wonder which little stretch of coast made her decide that.

contexts.subject: Geb holds onto his sister because the water is too deep to stand.

SixIsland_OutcastIsland_Text_GebPostBatt.text: GEB: I'm hanging onto my sister\nbecause I can't touch the bottom.$

replies.text: Then staying together is not optional play. He needs reliable support.
Inability to stand changes the immediate risk. Adequate flotation matters.
Get him somewhere safe and shallow before asking for anything else.
That sounds frightening if she moves faster than he can follow.
A safe outing should fit the smaller swimmer too.
The sibling partnership has a very practical meaning in deep water.
A familiar hand is important. It should not be the only safety plan.
Insufficient footing. Add proper flotation or change location.
The water has become too large for his own feet to answer.
He should be able to enjoy the day without needing to cling for safety.
I wonder whether his sister knows how much he depends on that hold.

contexts.subject: Bethany compares raising Pokemon lovingly with a mother raising a child.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_BethanyPostBa.text: In the same way your mother raised\nyou full of love, you should raise\lyour POKéMON.$

replies.text: A useful comparison when it means patience rather than just telling the little one what to do.
Consistent care is essential, though family experience varies between people.
Look after the partners because they depend on us. Simple enough.
A familiar kind of kindness can be something you choose to pass on.
Daily food, rest, and patience say more than one grand promise of love.
The lesson asks the traveler to become a source of the care they once received.
A small safe life grows from many ordinary gentle days.
Stable supportive environment. A good foundation for any developing partner.
A shelter once given can become something the hands learn to offer.
A kind principle, without needing everyone's home story to be the same.
I wonder which little act of care Bethany most remembers.

contexts.subject: Allison clarifies that she wants responsible Pokemon care rather than no catching.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_AllisonPostBa.text: I'm not saying that you shouldn't\ncatch POKéMON.\pI just want people to raise their\nPOKéMON responsibly.$

replies.text: Catch thoughtfully, care properly. A much clearer request than a blanket argument.
She distinguishes acquiring partners from meeting the responsibilities that follow.
Fair point. The job starts when the ball stops moving.
It is reassuring that the concern leaves room for a good way to do things.
A safe home and a workable routine should come before another catch.
The critic supplies a constructive revision instead of canceling the whole premise.
Wanting a creature is the smallest part of making room for its life.
Acquisition and ongoing maintenance are different tasks. Both need planning.
A closed ball should open onto something kinder than an empty promise.
Clear standards are better than assuming every trainer is careless.
I wonder which responsibility she most often sees people forget.

contexts.subject: Garret points us to the Heracross measurer near Pattern Bush.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_GarretPostBat.text: There's a girl near the BUSH who\nmeasures HERACROSS for TRAINERS.$

replies.text: A specialist with a very particular ruler. The local bug news travels well.
A nearby measuring service can provide consistent comparison if the method is reliable.
Worth a visit if the partner is comfortable being handled.
It is nice that such a small interest can have its own local expert.
An odd little hobby can still be kind when the Pokemon's comfort stays first.
The field expedition receives directions to an unusually exclusive review panel.
A little enthusiasm has become a landmark people can point toward.
Specialized measurement station! I would ask how the scale is calibrated.
The path has a place for someone who notices the small differences in a horn.
A clear recommendation is useful. A record should remain a game, not a judgment of the partner.
I wonder whether Garret has brought a Heracross to be measured.

contexts.subject: Jonah plays with the possible sounds and meanings of the word appeal.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_JonahPostBatt.text: By the way, “appeal” is a weird\nword, if you think about it.\pLike, is it like an orange peel?\nOr like a ringing bell?$

replies.text: An orange peel ringing like a bell is exactly the kind of thought I wanted from this walk.
Similar sounds can suggest unrelated meanings. English enjoys being inconvenient.
A harmless puzzle. Better than another threat about losing.
I like somebody noticing how strange an ordinary word can become.
If the orange starts ringing, I am taking it out of the fruit bowl.
A roadside linguist has discovered that language will gladly trip over its own shoes.
Words are very old things with surprisingly loose floorboards.
Sound similarity does not imply shared function. Still an entertaining test.
A familiar little word has opened its coat to reveal two unrelated objects.
A playful question can make a dull stretch much more memorable.
I wonder whether he has been turning that word around all afternoon.

contexts.subject: Vance plans to bring his younger brother to Pattern Bush.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_VancePostBatt.text: I'm going to bring my little brother\nhere next time.$

replies.text: A good place becomes even better when you know someone else would love seeing it.
A shared outing can introduce a younger child to a habitat with useful guidance.
Good plan if he keeps the pace safe for the younger one.
It is lovely to picture someone enjoying a place before they have even arrived.
Bring enough water and time for little legs and long questions.
The field trip receives an enthusiastic advance booking for a smaller guest.
A familiar path can become new again through someone else's first look.
Adapt the route for the least experienced participant.
One person's wonder is being kept ready for another pair of eyes.
A thoughtful invitation is better than simply buying a souvenir.
I wonder which little part Vance most wants to point out first.

contexts.subject: Nash compares the ground patterns with his grandfather's clothes.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_NashPostBattl.text: The funny patterns on the ground…\pThey look like the patterns on my\ngrandpa's clothes.$

replies.text: The mysterious forest floor has accidentally borrowed Grandfather's wardrobe.
An association can help notice a pattern without establishing how it formed.
Good eye. The resemblance is worth remembering, even if it explains nothing yet.
I like how a strange place can suddenly connect to something familiar at home.
A small family memory can make the unknown feel less distant.
The ancient-looking design receives an unexpected domestic costume reference.
A familiar shape hiding inside something unfamiliar. A pleasant kind of strange.
Pattern recognition triggered. Now compare the actual structures.
The ground has worn a little echo of somebody's old coat.
A repeating design is a repeating design, whether it is on cloth or beneath the grass.
I wonder whether his grandfather would see the resemblance too.

contexts.subject: Cordell admires our hat and asks us to give it to him.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_CordellPostBa.text: Ayup, you townies come around all\nso dandy with a hat that flashy…\pHow about giving me that?$

replies.text: The hat has attracted another very ambitious compliment. My head would like to keep its roof.
Admiration does not require transferring ownership of the item.
Nice that he likes it. We are allowed to keep our own hat.
I would find that request much harder to answer than a simple compliment.
A practical bit of shade is still something the traveler needs.
The costume review unexpectedly becomes a request to acquire the wardrobe.
A small personal belonging need not leave every time somebody asks brightly.
Property request optional. No technical need to comply.
The shade over one pair of eyes need not become someone else's souvenir.
He has good taste. His assumption about the gift policy needs work.
I wonder which hat he would choose if he went looking for his own.

contexts.subject: Dalia enthusiastically describes a deep breath of fresh air.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_DaliaPostBatt.text: First, exhale.\nBlow everything out.\pWhen you can't exhale anymore,\ninhale the clean air!\pIsn't it refreshing?$

replies.text: A very simple local attraction, with unlimited space around the ticket booth.
A comfortable breath and a quiet pause can feel refreshing without becoming a cure-all.
Fine to slow down a moment. No need to strain at breathing.
I like the little pause when the place becomes something you can feel, not just see.
A quiet rest in clean air can be a lovely part of the walk.
The outdoors receives a recommendation based entirely on its most portable feature.
A little room inside the day, made by stopping for a breath.
Simple recovery pause. Much easier than overengineering the moment.
The trees have left something gentle in the space between the words.
An ordinary pleasure does not need a complicated explanation to be worth noticing.
I wonder whether she has a favorite quiet spot for that pause.

contexts.subject: Joana worries whether she is the only girl who loves collecting Bug Pokemon.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_JoanaPostBatt.text: I'm going to keep on collecting\nBUG POKéMON.\pAm I the only girl like that?$

replies.text: She is certainly not the only person allowed to love a small many-legged neighbor.
An interest is not restricted by gender. Absence of nearby examples does not imply she is alone.
Like what she likes. The bugs do not require a membership category.
It is hard when you cannot see someone like yourself enjoying the same thing.
I hope she finds a friend who is just as excited to compare the tiny details.
The specialist's genuine enthusiasm deserves a wider cast than she currently knows.
An unusual joy is not a mistake just because it feels lonely.
Population sample too small for that conclusion. Keep the interest.
A little creature can be a perfectly good reason to step outside any expected shape.
She gets to make the interest look like her, rather than copy someone else's idea.
I wonder which Bug Pokemon she would show another interested girl first.

contexts.subject: Riley plans to observe the night sky from Pattern Bush.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_RileyPostBatt.text: I'm going to observe the night sky\nhere.$

replies.text: A day with a second view waiting after sunset. Good planning.
An observation session benefits from checking conditions and choosing a safe position beforehand.
Know the way back before the light goes. Then enjoy the sky.
A quiet night outside sounds lovely with the right company or a little safe solitude.
A warm layer and something to drink will make the wait kinder.
The daytime explorer stays for the setting's less brightly lit second act.
The ground has offered its patterns; the sky may have a few of its own.
Excellent dark-site potential. I would check cloud cover and glare.
A little patch of land waiting for the enormous ceiling to change.
A deliberate evening plan is better than simply realizing it got dark.
I wonder which part of the sky Riley hopes will be clearest tonight.

contexts.subject: Marcy dismisses a cut and suggests spit will cure it.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_MarcyPostBatt.text: A little cut like that…\nA little spit's enough to cure it!$

replies.text: A small cut deserves a cleaner plan than that.
Saliva is not an appropriate substitute for cleaning a wound. Use clean water and proper care.
Clean it properly. Small does not mean ignore it.
I hope she is not brushing it off because somebody taught her to hide pain.
A clean rinse and a proper dressing make more sense than a boast.
The confident folk remedy could use a substantially better editor.
A little care is not an embarrassing amount of care.
Contamination is not a repair method. Clean the injury.
A small hurt should not need to grow before it is allowed attention.
Looking unbothered is less useful than actually looking after the cut.
I wonder whether someone nearby has a proper first-aid kit.

contexts.subject: Layton wonders why grass will not grow in certain patterned areas.

SixIsland_PatternBush_Text_LaytonPostBat.text: There are places here in PATTERN\nBUSH where grass won't grow.\pWhat could be the cause of such\na phenomenon?$

replies.text: A patch of missing grass can be a very interesting thing when the rest of the place is growing.
Soil, disturbance, moisture, and other conditions could explain it. The pattern is worth recording.
Look carefully before digging it up. The clue may be in the undisturbed shape.
I like a question that begins with noticing something absent.
A patient look can tell us more than an eager handful of soil.
The curious observer has discovered a mystery written in negative space.
A blank place can have more to say than the crowded part around it.
Control samples! Compare the bare ground with the grass beside it.
The growing things have left a little silence with edges.
An unusual pattern deserves attention without a rushed dramatic explanation.
I wonder whether the shape changes with the seasons.

contexts.subject: Stanly recommends considering the mysteries of the world every day.

SixIsland_RuinValley_Text_StanlyPostBatt.text: I suggest to you that you, too,\ngive a thought to the secrets and\lmysteries of our world once a day.$

replies.text: One mystery a day sounds manageable. Unless today's mystery is where yesterday went.
Regular curiosity is an excellent habit, provided an unanswered question is allowed to stay open.
A little thought before assuming we understand a place. Fair advice.
I like that he makes room for wondering in an ordinary day.
Something to turn over while dinner simmers. No need to solve it before eating.
A daily appointment with the unexplained. I admire his scheduling.
Some questions make good company even without an answer.
A daily puzzle could keep a notebook wonderfully untidy.
The world has no shortage of small doors that open inward.
Curiosity is appealing. Pretending every hunch is a discovery is less so.
He seems to find something worth noticing wherever he stops.

contexts.subject: Foster notes that most of the ruins scattered around Sevii are very old.

SixIsland_RuinValley_Text_FosterPostBatt.text: There are several ruins on the\nSEVII ISLANDS.\pThe majority of them date back\na long way.$

replies.text: The islands have been keeping old things in lots of different corners.
Several sites could offer useful comparisons, though age alone does not establish a shared origin.
Plenty to explore. We should leave the old stone where it belongs.
It is strange to stand somewhere that has outlasted so many lives.
A long history deserves more patience than a quick poke around.
These islands have quite a back catalogue beneath the holiday scenery.
Old walls do not need to be empty of meaning just because their builders are gone.
Different sites, different construction methods. That could fill several notebooks.
Time leaves its belongings scattered rather generously here.
The islands wear their age in interesting places.
I wonder what details would connect one ruin to another.

contexts.subject: Larry has found the ruins but cannot work out how to enter them.

SixIsland_RuinValley_Text_LarryPostBattl.text: Those ruins over there…\pI haven't had any luck in finding\nhow I can get inside.$

replies.text: Finding the door and finding how it opens are apparently separate adventures.
A visible entrance does not always reveal its mechanism. Careful observation comes first.
No reason to force it before we understand the entrance.
He sounds like he has been circling the same question for a while.
We can take a proper look without turning the door into rubble.
The building has supplied a setting and withheld its invitation.
A closed door can be impressively stubborn without saying a word.
Let's study the seams and markings before testing any theories.
Some thresholds make visitors introduce themselves very slowly.
Prying something open is rarely the most elegant first impression.
I wonder which detail he has been walking past without noticing.

contexts.subject: Daryl encourages the player to enjoy climbing.

replies.text: He makes going uphill sound like a party with unusually tired legs.
The view and the exercise are convincing benefits. Sensible footing remains essential.
Enjoy the climb. Keep enough strength for getting down.
It feels good when the effort itself becomes part of the pleasure.
A climb gives the packed lunch a remarkably appreciative audience.
An enthusiastic recommendation from a man already above ground level.
I appreciate a hobby that lets you pause and stare into the distance.
Finding a stable route up is a satisfying problem in motion.
The hill has not moved, yet reaching it changes the afternoon.
He has the unmistakable glow of someone enjoying his own difficult idea.
I like how a familiar landscape rearranges itself as we gain height.

contexts.subject: Hector cannot interpret the strange patterns engraved on the ruin door.

SixIsland_RuinValley_Text_HectorPostBatt.text: The door to the ruins…\nIt has these strange patterns\lengraved on the outside.\pI don't know what they mean,\nthough.$

replies.text: The door has writing and neither of us has brought its reading glasses.
The repeated marks may form a writing system. Recording their arrangement would be useful.
Copy the markings accurately before guessing what they mean.
Somebody meant those marks to be understood. That makes the silence stranger.
A careful copy will last longer than trying to memorize the whole door.
A message with its reader missing. The door has excellent dramatic restraint.
Words can become ornaments when everyone forgets how to read them.
Look for repeated groups. A pattern can give us a foothold without a translation.
Stone remembers a message more patiently than people remember a language.
Even an unreadable inscription deserves better than careless rubbing and scratches.
I would compare the marks before deciding they are only decoration.

contexts.subject: Rose would like to visit the woods but is frightened of Bug Pokemon.

SixIsland_WaterPath_Text_RosePostBattle.text: I want to go to the woods over\nthere, but…\pThere are lots of BUG POKéMON.\nThey scare me a little.$

replies.text: Wanting to visit the woods while fearing its tiny residents is a tricky invitation.
Learning which species live there may make the uncertainty less intimidating.
She can choose a short path with company. No need to prove anything.
Wanting to go and feeling afraid can happen at the same time.
A gentle first visit sounds better than marching her straight into a swarm.
The woods have attracted a visitor who objects to part of the cast.
I understand admiring a place from a very deliberate distance.
Knowing where the bugs tend to gather might help her plan a comfortable route.
The woods can wait while she makes acquaintance with its smaller neighbours.
Someone laughing at her fear would make a poor walking companion.
I wonder whether one calm encounter would change the way she sees them.

contexts.subject: Edward prefers audiences not to see the effort behind a polished performance.

SixIsland_WaterPath_Text_EdwardPostBattl.text: As a performer, I don't want people\nto know about the effort I put in.$

replies.text: So the trick is to work very hard at looking like you did not work very hard.
Concealing preparation can shape an audience's experience. It does not diminish the practice.
He put in the work. No shame in that, whether people see it or not.
I understand wanting the finished thing to speak before the nerves do.
A smooth meal has a very messy preparation table somewhere behind it.
The illusion of effortlessness is a remarkably demanding profession.
I suspect the hidden effort deserves a comfortable chair afterward.
A clean result can hide a mountain of revisions. I know that mountain.
Some kinds of grace have very tired feet beneath them.
Polish works best when you cannot see someone anxiously checking it.
Backstage tells one story; the audience sees the one he chose to share.

contexts.subject: Samir feels unable to escape the expectations attached to being a Swimmer.

SixIsland_WaterPath_Text_SamirPostBattle.text: I couldn't lift the stigma of being\na SWIMMER…$

replies.text: A swimsuit should not come with a permanent description of your whole personality.
A trainer category is a useful shorthand, but a poor account of an individual.
He can choose a different approach. The label does not get a vote.
It sounds tiring to feel people have decided who you are before you speak.
Nobody should be stuck with one specialty just because it is what people remember.
A typecast man is asking for a wider range of material. Fair enough.
Being recognizable can become a very small room.
Try something that surprises him first. Other people's expectations can catch up.
Water is a place to swim, not a shape a person must keep.
One look should never do all the work of knowing somebody.
I would like to hear what he enjoys when nobody is sorting him into a group.

contexts.subject: Denise spends time with the Pokemon her boyfriend gave her when they are apart.

SixIsland_WaterPath_Text_DenisePostBattl.text: When I can't be with my boyfriend,\nI spend time with the POKéMON he\lgave me.$

replies.text: A gift that can keep you company has a pretty unfair advantage over a souvenir mug.
A shared association can make companionship especially meaningful during an absence.
Good that the Pokemon gets real time with her, too.
The gift has become part of her everyday life. That feels tender.
Time spent together is a lovely way to care for a living gift.
A memento with its own personality inevitably improves the love story.
Missing one person does not have to make the whole room empty.
That is a gift with a relationship of its own to build.
Affection has found a warm little place to wait between visits.
She seems fond of the Pokemon for more than who gave it to her.
I like that the ordinary hours together matter as much as the giving did.

contexts.subject: Earl asks whether there are mountains nearby.

SixIsland_WaterPath_Text_EarlPostBattle.text: Aren't there any mountains around\nthese parts?$

replies.text: Surrounded by water and already shopping for the opposite direction.
A local map would answer that more reliably than guessing from this stretch of shore.
Best ask a local before setting off with climbing gear.
He has a very clear idea of what would make the visit better.
A mountain trip needs a bit more planning than spotting a hill over lunch.
The traveller requests a change in scenery with considerably more altitude.
Some people arrive on an island and immediately look for somewhere higher to stand.
We should check the terrain before recommending a climb.
Even beside the sea, his thoughts have gone uphill.
His holiday preferences are refreshingly specific.
I wonder what makes a mountain worth visiting to him.

contexts.subject: Miu admits that losing makes her feel sad.

SixIsland_WaterPath_Text_MiuPostBattle.text: MIU: It makes me all sad inside\nwhen we lose…$

replies.text: Aw. Losing can sit in your middle like a very unwelcome pebble.
Disappointment is a normal response to an outcome she cared about. It will not define her next battle.
Let her be disappointed without making the loss bigger than it was.
She can say she is sad. She does not have to smile for us.
A quiet break might be more welcome than immediate advice.
A small defeat can feel enormous from inside it. No need to review it aloud.
There is nothing embarrassing about caring how something turns out.
Once the sting eases, she can choose one thing to try differently.
The little cloud may stay for a while. We can leave gently.
A gracious winner should know when to stop celebrating.
I hope her sister gives her room to feel it, then helps her laugh again.

contexts.subject: Mia apologizes to her Pokemon after losing.

replies.text: She is checking on her Pokemon before finding someone to blame. I like that.
Concern for the team is valuable. The result alone does not establish that she failed them.
Get them rested. She does not need to carry the whole loss as guilt.
They may want her beside them more than they want an apology.
Care after a hard battle means more than finding the perfect words.
A tender apology from a trainer whose team already knows she cares.
I would rather hear that than see someone turn their hurt on the Pokemon.
Rest first, then review what could help next time. In that order.
Her concern is reaching them, even through the disappointment.
A loss is rough enough without deciding it makes her unworthy of her team.
That little apology says a great deal about how she sees them.

contexts.subject: Miah says acting unlike her appearance is a deliberate strategy.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Entrance_Text_.text: What's that?\nI don't act the way I look?\pHeh, that's a part of my strategy!$

replies.text: She has weaponized the surprise of being a whole person. Excellent.
Expectations can affect decisions. Deliberately confounding them is a plausible tactic.
Anyone judging her by a glance gave her that opening.
I like that she enjoys catching people off guard.
A little surprise can make people pay proper attention.
She has made the audience's lazy assumptions part of her material.
Being difficult to summarize is a respectable advantage.
A strategy that makes the opponent supply their own wrong information. Clever.
A face is a poor map of what someone might do next.
She knows precisely what people assume, and charges them for it.
That is a useful reminder to keep looking after the first impression.

contexts.subject: Mason sings about sending out Pokemon and making girls cheer.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Entrance_Text_.text: Lalalah…\nMy POKéMON, I send them out,\lall the girls scream and shout!$

replies.text: He has written the cheering into the song. Saves waiting for reviews.
The projected audience response is rather more confident than the available evidence.
He seems capable of providing his own applause.
He certainly does not have trouble singing where people can hear him.
That much confidence could season a very large pot.
A chorus that helpfully informs its audience when to become besotted.
I admire how little outside encouragement his fantasy requires.
Built-in cheering. Efficient, though the audience may want an override.
The hills have been given a very specific idea of romance.
Confidence is charming until it starts writing other people's reactions.
He seems to be having a wonderful time with his own soundtrack.

contexts.subject: Nicolas recognizes strong visiting trainers and asks about Trainer Tower.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Entrance_Text_.text: TRAINERS like you from cities,\nthey sure are tough.\pYou'll be headed for the TOWER,\nwon't you?$

replies.text: We apparently look like people on the way to more battling. Not an unreasonable guess.
He may be noticing a pattern among visitors headed toward the Tower.
The Tower can wait until the team is ready.
He sounds curious about where the visiting trainers are going.
Worth checking our supplies before turning one battle into several more.
Our reputation has acquired an itinerary before we have settled on one.
A destination can gather a very particular sort of traveller around it.
A challenge attracting skilled visitors would give the locals plenty to observe.
The road carries rumours of its travellers ahead of them.
He has picked up on the look of someone who came prepared.
I wonder how many Tower challengers he has met along this path.

contexts.subject: Madeline says Pokemon understand kindness from their trainers.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Entrance_Text_.text: If you treat your POKéMON with\nkindness, they'll understand.$

replies.text: They notice the gentle things even when nobody gives those things a score.
Consistent treatment gives Pokemon much more evidence than a single affectionate gesture.
Be kind when it is inconvenient, too. That is when it matters.
I think they hear it in how someone handles an ordinary mistake.
Daily care says a great deal without needing a speech.
A relationship has more dialogue in its actions than its grand declarations.
Quiet kindness is still quite visible to the one receiving it.
The little repeated choices are doing important work.
Gentleness leaves a trace even where hands leave no mark.
It is lovely when care is part of the routine rather than a display.
Watch a trainer between battles and you learn a different part of the story.

contexts.subject: Eve intends to work harder alongside Jon.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Entrance_Text_.text: EVE: I'm going to work harder with\nJON.$

replies.text: They have a next step and someone to take it with. That helps.
Practising together should give them useful information about coordinating their choices.
Good. Give the team a rest before the next session.
She sounds determined without turning against her partner.
Working at it together can make even the awkward attempts worth something.
The partnership has survived its review and booked another rehearsal.
A shared plan is a pleasant thing to leave a loss with.
They can test combinations instead of simply trying everything harder.
Two people can tend the same small spark of resolve.
I like that she puts the next effort in the plural.
I wonder which part of their teamwork they will try changing first.

contexts.subject: Jon feels happy with Eve whether they win or lose.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Entrance_Text_.text: JON: When I'm with EVE, I feel\ngiddy whether I win or lose.\pIt's magical!$

replies.text: He has found a way to come out smiling regardless of the score.
Companionship appears to contribute more to his enjoyment than the result itself.
Good company makes a rough battle easier to take.
He sounds very sure about the part that matters to him.
That is a rather lovely reason to look forward to practice.
The romance subplot has quietly overruled the tournament standings.
A loss has failed to make much of an impression on that particular happiness.
An excellent source of motivation. Eve may still want him to learn the tactics.
Some kinds of warmth travel well through a disappointing afternoon.
He is making no attempt whatsoever to look less smitten.
Eve could probably tell how he feels without hearing a word of that.

contexts.subject: Cyndy considers postponing Trainer Tower until she improves.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_CyndyPost.text: The way I am now, I may have to\nhold off on TRAINER TOWER…$

replies.text: The Tower will still be tall after a little more practice.
Reassessing readiness after new evidence is sensible planning.
Better to prepare than force a challenge she does not feel ready for.
Waiting can be a choice she makes for herself, too.
Rest and practice are a useful part of the trip, not a wasted detour.
She has moved the grand challenge to a later chapter with better preparation.
An unfinished ambition need not become an urgent punishment.
A few focused improvements could make the next attempt feel very different.
The tower is patient stone. It need not set her pace.
Knowing when to pause is its own kind of confidence.
I wonder what she will want to feel stronger about before returning.

contexts.subject: Evan says trainers must develop their own judgment instead of relying on strong Pokemon.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_EvanPostB.text: You see them every so often,\nTRAINERS with awesome POKéMON\lwho have no idea what to do.\pBefore training POKéMON, TRAINERS\nthemselves need to grow up.$

replies.text: A mighty team still needs somebody making sensible decisions at the front.
Resources cannot fully compensate for poor judgment. Experience matters on both sides of the partnership.
The trainer has work to do as well. Fair point.
It must feel lonely to be trusted with all the strength and none of the guidance.
The best ingredients still need someone paying attention to the pan.
An impressive cast cannot rescue a director who has not read the scene.
Power is a rather poor substitute for knowing what you are doing.
Learning to use what you have is its own substantial skill.
A strong companion should not have to carry an inattentive mind as well.
An impressive lineup loses its shine when the trainer stops thinking.
You learn a lot by watching who adjusts when a plan goes wrong.

contexts.subject: Jackson says the tiny world seen from the stars still deserves protection.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_JacksonPo.text: From far out among the stars, our\nplanet is just a drop of water.\pBut we want to protect that drop\nof water for everyone.$

replies.text: A drop of water can hold a lot of people who need somewhere to stand.
Scale does not determine value. A small world can contain everything important to its inhabitants.
Small from far away. Still our home to look after.
Thinking of everyone living on that little dot makes it feel more precious.
Looking after a place starts with what we leave behind here.
A vast perspective that arrives at a very practical obligation. I like it.
The dark around a small light does not make the light less worth keeping.
We can begin protecting the whole by taking care of the part within reach.
A tiny blue thing is still large enough to hold every familiar voice.
Perspective suits him. It has made his concern larger rather than colder.
I would like more people to look at a beautiful place and think about its future.

contexts.subject: Katelyn recognizes the Running Shoes as a sign of the player's mother's affection.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_KatelynPo.text: Your mom bought those snazzy\nRUNNING SHOES for you?\pShe must adore you.$

replies.text: A pair of shoes can say please go explore and please come home at the same time.
A practical gift can express close attention to someone's needs.
Good shoes. A good person thinking ahead for us.
It is sweet that she notices the affection in something so ordinary.
Useful gifts keep taking care of a journey long after the giving.
A mother's good wishes have been travelling at ground level all along.
Love can be very quiet and still survive an unreasonable amount of walking.
Excellent design, and an even better reason for choosing it.
Some blessings have laces and sensible soles.
She has noticed the story behind something people usually glance past.
Every scuff now belongs to a journey someone helped make possible.

contexts.subject: Leroy thanks the player for useful battle data.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_LeroyPost.text: The way you battle has given me\na lot of useful data.\pThanks so much!$

replies.text: We have become an educational experience. I hope the notes include the exciting bits.
A battle is more informative when the observations lead to a testable adjustment.
He learned something. Good use of a loss.
I like that he can sound grateful while still wanting to improve.
A result worth thinking over is something useful to take home.
The reviewer has found the experience instructive. A gracious notice.
Defeat has been filed under research. A comfortable shelf for it.
Now comes the fun part: changing one thing and seeing what happens.
A difficult moment has left him with something he can use.
He makes a much better impression thanking someone than finding excuses.
I wonder what he noticed in our choices that surprised him.

contexts.subject: Michelle recognizes her tendency to anger and tries deep breathing.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_MichelleP.text: For some reason, I get furious\nover the slightest thing.\pI'll calm myself by breathing\ndeeply.$

replies.text: Taking a breath gives the next angry sentence a chance to miss its appointment.
A deliberate pause can help interrupt a response before it becomes automatic.
She noticed the problem. Taking a moment is a solid start.
It can be hard to hear yourself getting sharp before the words are out.
Stepping back for a breath is better than making someone else absorb the temper.
She has wisely introduced a pause before the next dramatic outburst.
A little silence is useful when the alternative has teeth.
That brief delay gives her another choice besides the first impulse.
Air has no opinion about the argument. That can be helpful.
Knowing your own temper is useful; choosing what to do with it matters more.
I respect that she says it plainly instead of dressing it up as someone else's fault.

contexts.subject: Lex appreciates the battle as experience for his student Nya.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_LexPostBa.text: LEX: I think it was a good\nexperience for NYA.\pYou have my gratitude.$

replies.text: A lesson with actual surprises in it. Much harder to nap through.
A varied opponent can expose assumptions that familiar practice leaves untested.
Useful experience, if he gives her room to learn from it.
I hope he asks what she noticed before explaining everything himself.
A good teacher can help turn the difficult bits into a next step.
The mentor has welcomed an unscheduled guest lecturer.
Experience teaches more gently when someone helps untangle it afterward.
They have fresh examples to work through instead of only repeating theory.
A lesson can arrive wearing the face of a stranger.
His gratitude is welcome. Nya should get some credit for her effort, too.
I wonder whether teacher and student noticed the same turning point.

contexts.subject: Nya wants further tutoring and hopes to continue studying with Lex.

SevenIsland_SevaultCanyon_Text_NyaPostBa.text: NYA: I think I'm going to need\nmuch more seasoning and tutoring\lunder LEX…\p…So, LEX, please, may I stay with\nyou like this?$

replies.text: More seasoning, she says. Learning apparently comes with a spice rack.

The apprentice has requested an extension to her character development.

A mentor worth keeping should welcome her growing independence, too.
There is still a path ahead, and she has chosen company for it.

contexts.subject: Brandon dates the ruins to at least fifteen hundred years ago but cannot explain their purpose.

SevenIsland_TanobyRuins_Text_BrandonPost.text: The TANOBY RUINS date back at\nleast 1,500 years.\pBut it's a baffling mystery as to\nwhy it was built in the first place.$

replies.text: Fifteen hundred years is a long time to keep a place's purpose to itself.
Dating a site and interpreting its function are separate questions. His distinction is useful.
Old enough to deserve a careful look. Keep our hands off anything fragile.
So much time, and we are still asking what someone meant to build.
A place can outlast every ordinary explanation people once gave visitors.
The date survives; the premise remains stubbornly unavailable.
Age has preserved the question more thoroughly than the answer.
Construction details might tell us what the missing written record cannot.
The stones have kept their years and lost their introductions.
An honest unknown is more interesting than a confident story made up on the spot.
I wonder what an ordinary day here looked like when the walls were new.

contexts.subject: Benjamin wonders if these ruins and others he has heard of shelter mystical Pokemon.

SevenIsland_TanobyRuins_Text_BenjaminPos.text: I hear there are other ruins like\nthe one here.\pMight they be the resting places\nof other mystic POKéMON?$

replies.text: An old ruin makes a very impressive bedroom, if that is actually what it is.
That is an interesting hypothesis. Similar-looking ruins alone would not establish the same function.

I like hearing what people imagine, as long as there is room to be surprised.
If anything does rest here, barging in would be poor manners.

An abandoned-looking place may simply have unfamiliar residents.

contexts.subject: Edna came with Clifford to paint the old buildings.

SevenIsland_TanobyRuins_Text_EdnaPostBat.text: I said that I wanted to paint an\nold building.\pSo CLIFFORD brought me here.$

replies.text: The ruins have acquired a portrait appointment. I hope they hold still.
Painting can encourage sustained observation of details a passing visitor misses.
A quiet reason to make a long trip. Hope she finds a good spot.
I like the idea of spending enough time here for the light to change.
A painting gives the visit something to become after they go home.
The old architecture has finally met someone interested in its better angles.
Old stone and patient attention seem well suited to each other.
The changing shadows could make the same wall look completely different.
She is borrowing a little afternoon light to take home.
The worn surfaces should give her far more to work with than a perfect new wall.
I would love to see which part she chooses to leave inside the frame.

contexts.subject: Clifford admires the player's independent exploration and study of Pokemon.

SevenIsland_TanobyRuins_Text_CliffordPos.text: Ah, so you are studying POKéMON\non your own…\pYes, you certainly are quite the\nextraordinary person, indeed.$

replies.text: That is a generous description of us walking around with questions and spare snacks.
Independent observation has value, though it improves further when findings can be checked.
Kind of him. Still plenty for us to learn.
It is nice when someone sees effort in a thing we are still figuring out.
A warm compliment can make the long way here feel even more worthwhile.
An unexpectedly glowing review from a fellow traveller. I shall accept gracefully.
He has noticed the curiosity rather than only the results. That is kind.
Exploring does teach things a diagram cannot quite prepare you for.
A stranger has offered a small bright thing to carry onward.
He gives a compliment without trying to make himself part of it. Lovely manners.
I like meeting someone who is pleased to see another person's curiosity.

contexts.subject: Dario reflects on future encounters and the connections between people.

SevenIsland_TrainerTower_Text_DarioPostB.text: In your future, I sense that you\nwill meet many others.\pI think you will be linked to each\nother by a strange power.$

replies.text: A path can introduce you to someone your entire plan forgot to include.
Repeated chance encounters can have lasting effects without being predictable in advance.
We will meet more people. Worth treating this meeting well, too.
Some brief conversations stay with you longer than you expect.
A stranger can become someone you are glad you stopped for.
A traveller's future is crowded with characters who have not introduced themselves yet.

Paths cross quietly before anyone knows what the crossing will mean.
He seems interested in people beyond what they can do for him.

contexts.subject: Rodette wonders about a peculiar Pokemon sleeping somewhere on the island.

SevenIsland_TrainerTower_Text_RodettePos.text: Somewhere on this island, peculiar\nPOKéMON are sleeping.\pCould it be that they're waiting\nfor you?$

replies.text: Somewhere out there, a mysterious Pokemon may be having a very undisturbed nap.
An intriguing report, though we should distinguish a local story from a confirmed sighting.
If it is sleeping, we need not rush to bother it.
She makes the island feel as though it has a secret breathing quietly nearby.
A sleeping Pokemon deserves a gentler search than shouting into every cave.

The possibility is interesting enough without making promises about what we will find.
I would start by asking what anyone has actually observed.
A sleeper need not be waiting for an audience, whatever the story says.
Mystery is appealing. Claiming it is waiting specifically for us feels a little presumptuous.

contexts.subject: Eli explains that battling the pair requires two Pokemon.

replies.text: Two opponents, two partners. The invitation has a headcount.
He has stated the format clearly. A second eligible Pokemon is required.

A little preparation, then we can decide whether to accept.
The double act has a sensible minimum cast requirement.
A postponed battle is not much of a tragedy.
We need the right setup before testing a two-Pokemon strategy.
The road remains open even when a challenge waits.
A straightforward condition. No need to make an occasion of it.

contexts.subject: Anne enthusiastically invites a battle but asks for two Pokemon first.

Route8_Text_AnneNotEnoughMons.text: ANNE: Hi, hi! Let's battle!\nBut bring two POKéMON.$

replies.text: That welcome came with an exclamation mark and a small attendance rule.
Her enthusiasm remains intact despite postponing the challenge.
She can keep the invitation. We will choose when we are ready.
She sounds pleased by the idea of a battle before it has even begun.
Nice to have an invitation we can prepare for instead of rush into.
An eager hostess whose only request is a complete guest list.
That is quite a bright welcome for a battle we cannot start yet.
We could use the time to consider how our two choices would work together.
A cheerful challenge can wait at the roadside without turning sour.
Her excitement makes the requirement sound like a future plan.
I like seeing someone enjoy the prospect of meeting a new team.

contexts.subject: Gia refuses to battle without Jes and asks for another Pokemon.

Route12_Text_GiaNotEnoughMons.text: GIA: I can't bear to battle\nwithout my JES!\pDon't you have one more POKéMON?$

replies.text: Gia has decided her battle buddy is an essential piece of equipment.
Her condition concerns the partnership rather than simply the number of opponents.

contexts.subject: Jes says he and Gia belong together and will only accept a paired battle.

Route12_Text_JesNotEnoughMons.text: JES: GIA and I, we'll be\ntogether forever.\pWe won't battle unless you have\ntwo POKéMON of your own.$

replies.text: Forever is a big promise. For now it apparently includes matching battle plans.

contexts.subject: Kiri and Jan require two Pokemon before their paired battle can begin.

Route14_Text_KiriNotEnoughMons.text: KIRI: We can battle if you have\ntwo POKéMON.$

Route14_Text_JanNotEnoughMons.text: JAN: You want to battle?\nYou don't have enough POKéMON.$

contexts.subject: Mya offers a challenge with a two-Pokemon requirement.
