A master at work, with an unusually delicious field of expertise.
So this is what control over one's life looks like. It involves berries.
Smooth timing like that tells me they know the machine well.
Skill can be lovely even in the smallest everyday task.
Competence is always an excellent look.
I would ask how long it took them to get that good.

contexts.subject: A blender participant is impatient to begin.

replies.text: The berries are ready, the person is ready, and patience has left.
The introductory phase has exceeded their preferred duration.
Ready to start. No mistaking that.
They have probably been waiting a while.
Ingredients ready? Then there is no need to let them wait.
Our eager collaborator would like to skip directly to the action.
Patience was apparently left outside with the coats.
I understand that urge to stop discussing a machine and use it.
Some people greet possibility by reaching for the handle.
Enthusiasm has a very short waiting list today.
Their whole attention is already on the next batch.

contexts.subject: A participant eagerly wonders what Pokeblock the batch will produce.

BerryBlender_Text_WhatKindOfPokeblockWil.text: I wonder what kind of {POKEBLOCK} I'll get?\nThis is so exciting!$

replies.text: A tiny mystery snack! I support this very edible suspense.
The ingredients and timing should make the result interesting.
We will find out when the batch is done.
That anticipation is half the fun of making something.
I always like the moment before tasting a new batch.
A thrilling mystery, with a conveniently bite-sized resolution.
For once, the unknown appears to have a pleasant flavor.
We have put in the ingredients. Now comes the reveal.
A little uncertainty can sweeten the wait.
I wonder what color the finished batch will be.
Their excitement is making me curious about the result too.

contexts.subject: A fan swoons over muscular appeals and sweat in Toughness Contests.

LilycoveCity_ContestLobby_Text_ToughCont.text: The TOUGHNESS CONTEST is like\nextreme, man!\pThose muscular appeals…\nCascading sweat… I swoon!$

replies.text: They came for the muscles and got the full splashy experience.
The physical presentation seems central to their enthusiasm.
They have a clear favorite. Very clear.
That is a lot of feeling about a very strenuous contest.
Someone should make sure the enthusiastic spectators have water too.
A passionate critic, overwhelmed by the sheer force of perspiration.
The atmosphere is apparently humid with admiration.
An event with impressive output and very enthusiastic cooling requirements.
Their delight has an oddly specific weather pattern.
They appreciate every strenuous detail of the presentation.
I would never have guessed sweat could get such a glowing review.

contexts.subject: A trainer feels daily care has brought their Pokemon to peak contest condition.

LilycoveCity_ContestLobby_Text_LavishedC.text: Day in and day out, I lavished my care\non this POKéMON.\pIts condition is peaking.\nToday, victory is mine!$

replies.text: All that everyday care gets its big day today. Good luck to them.
Consistent preparation is a strong basis for confidence.
They put the work in. Time to trust their partner.
I like hearing pride in the quiet work before the contest.
Day after day of care matters more than one lucky morning.
The grand prediction rests on a great many ordinary, careful days.
Their certainty has been fed and groomed for quite some time.
That sounds like a well maintained partner ready for the real test.
The daily kindness is already something worth being proud of.
A polished result begins long before anyone sees the final look.
I would ask what part of their routine made the biggest difference.

contexts.subject: A resident visits the contest hall daily to see many Pokemon.

LilycoveCity_ContestLobby_Text_WholeVari.text: You can see a whole variety of\nPOKéMON here.\pThat's why I make this place a regular\npart of my daily stroll.$

replies.text: A daily stroll with a changing cast of little celebrities. Excellent route.
A regular visit offers a pleasantly varied set of observations.
Good place to see new partners without going far.
That sounds like a lovely reason to get out each day.
A little walk and a hall full of interesting company.
A daily audience member for a show that keeps changing.
A routine with enough variety to avoid feeling like one.
Same building, different Pokemon. Very efficient sightseeing.
Returning can still bring surprises when we look closely.
A daily dose of fresh faces and excellent presentation.
They probably notice changes that a one-time visitor would miss.

contexts.subject: A child proudly describes smooth Pokeblocks made with the whole family.

LilycoveCity_ContestLobby_Text_MadePokeb.text: I made {POKEBLOCK}S with Mom, Dad, and\nBig Sister. They turned out great!\pI bet you can make smoother, better\n{POKEBLOCK}S if you have more people.$

replies.text: The whole family helped! That batch has four sets of proud fingerprints.
Coordinated participation can improve the blend. A nice family experiment.
They worked together and made something good.
That sounds like the sort of afternoon a child remembers.
A good recipe and a family around it. Hard to improve on that.
A family production with an unusually smooth final act.
The snacks appear to have survived a committee beautifully.
Four people keeping time together is genuinely impressive.
The cubes hold a little bit of an afternoon together.
A family collaboration that turned out both smooth and memorable.
They are just as proud of who helped as of what they made.

contexts.subject: A visitor enthusiastically likes battles against Tubers and Twins.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_2F_Text_Girls.text: The girl TUBERS, they're cute, hey?\nTo battle against a cute TUBER…\pWhoop, it's so awesome!\pAnd the TWINS! Aren't they cute?\nA 2-on-2 battle with TWINS…\pWhoop, it's unbearably fun!$

replies.text: That is a very energetic list of favorite opponents. I hope the battles are fair.
They appear particularly enthusiastic about those trainer classes.
Enjoy the match. Respect the other trainer.
They certainly have a favorite kind of battle.
The young trainers deserve a fair challenge and a kind opponent.
A highly animated review of the local battle scene.
Their enthusiasm has more exclamation points than I can comfortably hold.
Double battles do give everyone a lot to keep track of.
Every opponent deserves to be treated with care.
A rather loud declaration of a very specific preference.
I would be more interested in hearing how the actual battles went.

contexts.subject: A visitor always carries a Game Boy Advance for unexpected challenges.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_2F_Text_Never.text: You never know when and where\npeople will challenge you.\pThat's why I never leave home without\nmy GAME BOY ADVANCE.$

replies.text: Prepared for any challenge, provided it fits in that little machine.
A portable device does make spontaneous matches easier to arrange.
They travel prepared. Keep it out of the rain.
It is nice to have a familiar game ready wherever you go.
Something to share while waiting makes a useful travel companion.
Adventure is apparently incomplete without a smaller adventure in the pocket.
They have made boredom's survival considerably less likely.
Portable play is a very convincing engineering achievement.
A small familiar thing can make anywhere feel more welcoming.
One essential accessory, selected with admirable certainty.
I wonder how many friendships started with that little machine.

contexts.subject: A graphic artist asks whether Hoenns Pokemon are interesting.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_2F_Text_ImThe.text: I'm the GRAPHIC ARTIST! Aren't the\nPOKéMON of HOENN interesting?$

replies.text: Very interesting! Some look as if their feet were a delightful last-minute idea.
The range of shapes and adaptations is certainly impressive.
Plenty of interesting partners around here.
There is always another little detail I had missed.
Their personalities make those interesting faces even better.
Hoenn offers an extraordinarily memorable collection of characters.
Some of them look like beautiful ideas that ignored all objections.
The variety of workable shapes is an endless source of curiosity.
An odd silhouette can become very dear once we know its owner.
Hoenn certainly has no shortage of striking designs.
I keep finding a new favorite detail in a familiar Pokemon.

contexts.subject: A programmer is surprised to be addressed and wonders about the local slots.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_2F_Text_ImThe.text: Me? You're talking to me?\nI'm the PROGRAMMER.\pI wonder what the SLOTS are\nlike here.$

replies.text: We found the programmer during a very serious investigation of shiny levers.
An interesting local curiosity, though the outcomes may be costly data.
Just keep track of what you spend.
They seemed startled that we stopped to talk.
A little curiosity is fine. Keep enough money for the trip.
Our unexpected interview has interrupted a private study of the slots.
Even the programmer is susceptible to a suspiciously blinking machine.
I would be curious about the mechanisms before pulling anything.
Curiosity is a fine traveler, when it carries a little caution.
Those flashing lights do have a very deliberate appeal.
I wonder whether they watch the machine or the people playing it.

contexts.subject: A guest enjoys the sea breezes heartening sensation.

LilycoveCity_CoveLilyMotel_2F_Text_SeaBr.text: The sea breeze tickles my heart.\nIt feels wonderful here!$

replies.text: The breeze found their heart. It mostly finds my loose hair.
A lovely description of a very immediate sensation.
Good air. Good place to pause a moment.
That is a gentle way to say it feels good here.
A sea breeze can make even a simple lunch feel special.
A tiny review of the coast, delivered entirely from the heart.
The wind is being unusually considerate today.
Fresh air does improve a room without any complicated machinery.
Some places reach us through the smallest moving things.
The coast has supplied its own excellent finishing touch.
They sound as though they have already found the best part of the visit.

contexts.subject: A resident insists Pokemon are partners and regrets that some people treat them as tools.

LilycoveCity_House1_Text_PokemonPartners.text: POKéMON are partners to people.\nThey aren't our tools.\pUnfortunately, there are some people\nwho fail to understand that…$

replies.text: They have feelings and favorite places too. We should remember who is helping us.
Ability does not cancel a living partner's needs or preferences.
They trust us. We owe them better than being used.
I am glad someone said it so plainly.
Care belongs in the everyday things we do for our partners.
A partnership asks more of us than simply giving orders.
Being useful should never be the price of being treated kindly.
A partner gets a say. That changes how every plan should work.
A living being is more than what it can do for us.
Respect should be part of how a trainer carries themself.
You can learn a lot by watching how someone treats their Pokemon.

contexts.subject: A father recalls his surprise at quadruplets and enjoys seeing them play together.

LilycoveCity_House3_Text_HappyToHaveQuad.text: When my wife gave birth to quadruplets,\nyou bet I was shocked.\pBut, now, seeing them play together,\nit makes me happy.$

replies.text: Four little surprises, now playing together. His house must be wonderfully loud.
An unexpected family size, followed by a very genuine source of happiness.
Four at once. Glad he can enjoy the chaos.
Watching them together must make the busy days feel different.
That is a lot of small plates and a lot of love around the table.
The startling opening has become his favorite ongoing story.
Four simultaneous arrivals. I understand needing a moment to process that.
A household scaled up much faster than the original plan.
Surprise grew into a familiar, noisy kind of joy.
Four children means an impressive range of tiny opinions.
His face probably changes every time he watches them together.

contexts.subject: A resident repeats an uncertain claim that the planets biggest mysteries lie undersea.

LilycoveCity_House4_Text_MysteriesAtBott.text: This planet's biggest mysteries are\nat the bottom of the sea.\pSomebody said that, but I don't know…$

replies.text: Hard to check the biggest mystery when it is sitting under all that water.
A plausible place for unanswered questions, though the ranking needs evidence.
Plenty down there we cannot see. Worth respecting.
I like that they left room to be unsure.
The sea still keeps plenty beyond what we bring home.
A grand claim, sensibly accompanied by a small shrug.
The mysteries chose an excellent place to avoid awkward questions.
Deep water does make investigation rather complicated.
Some secrets remain simply because reaching them is difficult.
A little uncertainty suits a claim that enormous.
I would ask where they heard it before planning an expedition.

contexts.subject: A resident passes along a report of a trench between Mossdeep and Sootopolis.

LilycoveCity_House4_Text_UnderwaterTrenc.text: There's a deep underwater trench\nbetween MOSSDEEP and SOOTOPOLIS.\pThat's what someone told me, anyway.$

replies.text: A whole trench under the sea. The ocean has an extra downstairs.
Useful geographical information, though I would verify it before diving.
Good lead. Get proper bearings before heading out.
There is more beneath that crossing than I imagined.
That sounds like a place to prepare carefully before exploring.
The route between cities apparently has a rather dramatic basement.
The sea has depth beyond its already excessive depth.
A trench would make accurate mapping especially important.
The water hides the shape of the land below it.
A remarkable feature to have out of sight between two cities.
I would like to know who first told them about that crossing.

contexts.subject: A youngster explains public Colosseum records and feels embarrassed about losses.

MauvilleCity_PokemonCenter_2F_Text_Young.text:
Did you know that you can link battle
at the COLOSSEUM here?\pThey put up your record on the wall
for everyone to see.\pIt's embarrassing if you lose more
often than you win…$

replies.text: A wall cannot show how much someone learned. It is mostly good at holding numbers.
A record measures outcomes, with very little detail about improvement.
Losses happen. The wall does not get the final word.
I would find that public record a bit intimidating too.
Anyone practicing is allowed to have a rough stretch.
The scoreboard offers a notoriously incomplete biography.
The wall has never battled anyone. Its opinion is limited.
Numbers need context, especially when someone is learning.
A string of losses can still hold courage and progress.
A bad record is no reason to make someone feel small.
I would rather hear about their most memorable match.

contexts.subject: A woman hopes many link battle wins will earn her fans.

MossdeepCity_PokemonCenter_2F_Text_Woman.text: If I win a whole lot of link battles\nand show everyone how good I am,\lI might get a fan following!$

replies.text: First win the battles, then learn to wave without dropping anything.
Repeated wins could attract attention. Sportsmanship might keep it.
Win fairly. Treat the people watching well.
I think being kind to an opponent would impress me too.
A good winner makes other people happy to cheer.
An ambitious career plan with applause already penciled in.
She has planned the admirers before the difficult part. Admirably efficient.
Consistent results and a good attitude would be a strong combination.
The people who stay often notice more than the wins.
A following is easier to keep when the manners match the talent.
I wonder what she hopes people will remember about her battles.

contexts.subject: Both cycling gate attendants encourage speed with caution around others; text is byte-identical.

Route110_SeasideCyclingRoadNorthEntrance.text: On CYCLING ROAD, you can go all out\nand cycle as fast as you'd like.\pIt feels great to go that fast, but try\nnot to crash into anyone!$

Route110_SeasideCyclingRoadSouthEntrance.text: On CYCLING ROAD, you can go all out\nand cycle as fast as you'd like.\pIt feels great to go that fast, but try\nnot to crash into anyone!$

replies.text: Go very fast, remain very uncrashed. A sensible two-part instruction.
Speed is enjoyable with enough stopping distance and attention.
Watch the people ahead. Leave room to stop.
I would rather enjoy the ride than surprise somebody.
Fast wind, happy rider, nobody flattened. Sounds good.
A stirring invitation with an entirely reasonable collision clause.
Freedom of the road ends at the person directly in front of us.
Brakes deserve just as much appreciation as the pedals.
A good ride leaves everyone else a good day too.
Looking ahead is an excellent accessory at any speed.
The warning tells me this attendant has seen a few close calls.

contexts.subject: A glass workshop employee enjoys blowing a flute while the boss speaks.

Route113_GlassWorkshop_Text_FunToBlowGla.text: It's fun to blow a glass flute while\nmy boss is talking.\pHuff-huff! Puff-puff!$

replies.text: A tiny musical interruption with full workplace enthusiasm.
A fascinating experiment in how long a supervisor tolerates accompaniment.
Hope the boss has a sense of humor.
I might wait until the boss finishes. Unless they asked for a duet.
That is one way to season a workday. Possibly too loudly.
Every speech apparently deserves an unsolicited flute part.
They have found a way to be both employed and extremely noticeable.
A glass flute makes a remarkably efficient interruption device.
A little mischief, carefully carried on a breath.
Bold workplace styling. Potentially brief employment.
I am curious whether the boss has stopped noticing by now.

contexts.subject: A resident wonders whether Pokemon spirits revive in the Cave of Origin.

Route119_House_Text_RumorAboutCaveOfOrig.text: I heard about a cave called the CAVE\nOF ORIGIN.\pPeople rumor that the spirits of\nPOKéMON are revived there. Could\lsomething like that really happen?$

replies.text: That is a big story for one cave to carry. I wonder who first told it.
An intriguing belief. A rumor alone cannot establish what happens there.
Old story. We should treat the place with respect.
I can understand wanting a story like that to be true.
A place tied to that much hope must mean a lot to people.
The cave has acquired a legend far larger than its entrance.
People have always asked the dark to return what they miss.
I would want to distinguish the local history from the claim itself.
Some rumors tell us what people long for as much as what they know.
That is the kind of story that changes how you enter a place.
I would listen to more than one local account before deciding.

contexts.subject: A saved researcher thanks the player but remains puzzled by Aquas intentions.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_1F_Text_WhatWe.text: Hello!\nWe've been saved by your actions!\pWhat I don't understand is what on\nearth the AQUAS were up to.$

replies.text: I am glad they are safe. The Aquas left a mess of questions behind.
Their objective remains unclear, but the researchers can work safely again.
They are safe. We can worry about the rest after checking everyone.
It must feel strange to be relieved and confused at once.
Getting people safe was the first thing that mattered.
A rescue completed, with the villains' reasoning still stubbornly absent.
The danger left. Its explanation apparently missed the exit.
I would check the equipment and make sure everyone is accounted for.
Relief can arrive before understanding does.
They deserve a quiet day after that interruption.
I would ask what the Aquas actually tried to reach while they were here.

contexts.subject: An attendant introduces Safari Zones natural habitats and Pokemon catching.

Route121_SafariZoneEntrance_Text_Welcome.text:
Welcome to the SAFARI ZONE!\pHere, you may witness many kinds of
POKéMON rarely seen in HOENN.\pAnd, you'll see them in their wild,
untamed state in natural habitats.\pWhat's more, we've thrown open the
gates to POKéMON TRAINERS.\pYou're encouraged to catch POKéMON
for keeps!\pCome in and enjoy the SAFARI ZONE!$

replies.text: Wild Pokemon in their own habitats. We are guests with very special invitations.
Observing them in their surroundings should be as rewarding as finding them.
Respect the area and the Pokemon. Good outing follows.
I would like a quiet look around before doing anything else.
A little patience will make this visit much nicer for everyone.
An invitation to adventure, with the wildlife retaining top billing.
We have entered a place where the residents owe us no conversation.
A protected habitat is worth exploring carefully.
Walk gently. There is a whole living place around the paths.
An outing works better when visitors remember whose home it is.
I would love to see which Pokemon appear when we stop rushing.

contexts.subject: A fisherman seeks unusual Water Pokemon and asks where the lake is.

SafariZone_North_Text_Fisherman.text: I'm on a mission to find WATER POKéMON\nyou don't see in HOENN.\pDo you have any idea where the lake is?$

replies.text: A Water Pokemon mission needs water. We have identified the crucial first step.
Finding the lake would certainly improve the search conditions.
Look for water first. Then a safe bank.
I hope the lake is easier to find than the rare Pokemon.
A drink for the fisherman might be useful along the way too.
A noble expedition, briefly delayed by the location of its main ingredient.
The mission is ambitious. The navigation remains a work in progress.
Water is an excellent starting requirement for this particular search.
The rarest thing right now appears to be a clear direction.
A little local guidance would suit this expedition beautifully.
I would ask which Water Pokemon they are hoping to find.

contexts.subject: A visitor plans to catch rare Pokemon and trade with friends.

SafariZone_North_Text_Man.text: I'm going to catch a lot of rare POKéMON\nhere and trade them with my friends!$

replies.text: Rare finds to share with friends. That makes the excitement travel farther.
Trading can let the whole group compare very different discoveries.
Good plan. Make sure each partner gets a good home.
I like that their friends are already part of the outing.
Coming back with something to share always feels nice.
The expedition has planned its triumphant reunion before its first catch.
Their friends are about to receive very lively souvenirs.
A group can explore more possibilities by sharing what each finds.
May the excitement carry kindness along with it.
A rare find feels even better when a friend appreciates it.
I wonder what their friends hope to find in return.

contexts.subject: A visitor reaches a remote Safari area too exhausted to catch Pokemon.

SafariZone_Northwest_Text_Man.text: Gasp… Gasp…\nI…made it out here…but…\pI'm exhausted… I don't have the\nenergy to catch POKéMON…$

replies.text: They reached the rare Pokemon and spent all their catching energy on walking.
Their travel budget appears to have been measured in stamina.
Sit down. Catch your breath before doing anything else.
That is a disappointing time to realize how tired you are.
Water and a quiet break first. The Pokemon can wait.
A triumphant arrival, followed immediately by negotiations with their legs.
The expedition has discovered the rare limit of its own enthusiasm.
The plan needed a reserve of energy for the actual destination.
Let the place come to them for a while. No need to hurry.
A rest is a perfectly respectable part of the itinerary.
They might spot something lovely just by sitting quietly here.

contexts.subject: A visitor thinks feeder Pokeblocks attract Pokemon with similar natures.

SafariZone_RestHouse_Text_FatMan.text: If you put a {POKEBLOCK} on the FEEDER,\nPOKéMON are attracted to it.\pI think POKéMON with the same sort of\nnature are drawn by a certain {POKEBLOCK}.$

replies.text: A snack can bring together creatures with the same opinion of that snack.
An interesting pattern. Nature and flavor preferences might be linked.
Useful tip. Watch what comes to the feeder.
That sounds like something you learn by waiting quietly.
A shared taste can make a surprisingly good introduction.
A tiny buffet with a remarkably particular guest list.
Even the wilderness has people who agree about lunch.
We could compare which visitors choose each kind of block.
The food we leave can tell us who enjoys returning.
A feeder with its own very selective clientele.
I would like to watch a few batches before guessing the pattern.

contexts.subject: A visitor explains that Pokeblocks especially help with Pokemon prone to flee.

SafariZone_RestHouse_Text_PsychicM.text: If you use {POKEBLOCK}S, wild POKéMON won't\nbe so quick to run away.\pIt's not much use to give {POKEBLOCK}S to\nPOKéMON that don't flee easily.$

replies.text: A snack gives the nervous ones a reason to stay for one more moment.
The benefit would be greatest when fleeing is otherwise likely.
Makes sense. Give a nervous Pokemon some space too.
A calm moment seems better than chasing after them.
A treat works best when the guest already has a reason to leave.
A tactical use of hospitality for a very brief audience.
The promise of a snack has delayed many a hasty departure.
Useful to apply the right tool to the actual problem.
Patience and a small offering can make staying feel easier.
Good advice: notice what the individual Pokemon needs.
I would watch how comfortable they seem before moving closer.

contexts.subject: A youngster reports catching Pokemon without Pokeblocks by approaching closer.

SafariZone_RestHouse_Text_Youngster.text: I don't have any {POKEBLOCK}S, but I caught\na good number of POKéMON.\pYou can improve your chances of making\na catch by getting closer to them\lbefore throwing a SAFARI BALL.$

replies.text: No snacks, still plenty of catches. Their quiet shoes deserve some credit.
Distance can affect an attempt independently of the bait used.
Move carefully. Close does not mean crowding them.
I would take the quiet approach over a sudden rush.
A patient approach can help when the treat pouch is empty.
A successful expedition with the catering department entirely absent.
They have proved that an empty snack bag need not end the day.
A useful result from changing the distance instead of the supplies.
Going gently matters more than simply going nearer.
They made the most of what they brought. Resourceful.
I wonder how they learned to judge a comfortable approach.

contexts.subject: A boy explains that Pokemon gather around a feeder containing Pokeblocks.

SafariZone_South_Text_Boy.text: Did you know?\pIf you put a {POKEBLOCK} in that square box,\nPOKéMON gather around.$

replies.text: A square box that summons hungry company. I understand its appeal.
A feeding station makes the visitors easier to observe.
Good spot to wait quietly and watch.
I like that the Pokemon can choose to come over.
Set out something good and give the guests room.
A surprisingly modest box with excellent powers of invitation.
The local gathering place has a very practical attraction.
Simple container, very effective way to bring visitors together.
A patient offering can make a little place feel busy.
It seems the little square box knows how to host.
We could learn a lot by watching who arrives first.

contexts.subject: Both Safari construction workers explain an area is closed; exact texts match.

SafariZone_South_Text_AreaOffLimits1.text: This area is still under construction.\nIt's off-limits, sorry!$

SafariZone_South_Text_AreaOffLimits2.text: This area is still under construction.\nIt's off-limits, sorry!$

replies.text: Under construction means the adventure is still getting its shoes on.
We should stay clear until the work is completed.
Closed means closed. Plenty else to see.
I would rather not interrupt people working.
We can enjoy the open part and let them finish safely.
A future adventure, currently occupied by people with actual jobs.
The unfinished area has wisely declined our visit.
We should give the crew space to finish the job.
A boundary is easy to respect when we listen to it.
An unfinished area is best viewed after the workers say it is ready.
I would be curious to see it when the work is done.

contexts.subject: A visitor regrets forgetting a bike needed to explore farther into Safari Zone.

SafariZone_South_Text_Man.text: I want to keep going deeper, but I\nforgot to bring a BIKE.\pSomething tells me that rare POKéMON\nlive in the outlying areas.$

replies.text: Their adventure remembered everything except its wheels. That is frustrating.
A useful reminder to check access requirements before setting out.
Stay within reach on foot. Bring the bike next time.
That is a disappointing discovery this far into the day.
There is still a good walk to enjoy where we can reach.
An expedition defeated by one conspicuously absent bicycle.
The rarest sight today is the bike they left behind.
A transport requirement is difficult to improvise around.
The nearer paths may still have something worth finding.
A bicycle would complete this particular travel arrangement.
I wonder what they have already spotted on the way in.

contexts.subject: A youngster suspects Pokemon ate a feeder Pokeblock without being noticed.

SafariZone_South_Text_Youngster.text: I put a {POKEBLOCK} on the {POKEBLOCK} FEEDER.\nBut it seems to have disappeared.\pI guess POKéMON must have eaten it\nwithout me noticing.$

replies.text: A mysterious disappearing snack. The suspects were very polite about it.
A reasonable explanation, though direct observation would confirm it.
Probably eaten. Quiet visitors are still visitors.
I like imagining a shy Pokemon waiting until nobody looked.
An empty feeder can be a very nice review of the food.
A tiny culinary mystery with a very plausible hungry culprit.
The unseen guests have left an elegantly empty plate.
We might catch the next visit by watching from farther away.
Some visitors only arrive when they feel unobserved.
A vanished treat can still be a successful invitation.
I would keep a little distance and watch the next one.

contexts.subject: A visitor wonders whether ignored Pokeblocks reflect Pokemons food preferences.

SafariZone_Southwest_Text_Woman.text: Sometimes, when I toss a {POKEBLOCK} at \nPOKéMON, it gets ignored.\pDo POKéMON have likes and dislikes\nabout what they eat?$

replies.text: Probably! I too have strong opinions about unexpected cubes of food.
Individual taste is a sensible explanation worth checking.
They have preferences. An ignored snack is an answer.
I would rather know what they enjoy than insist on my first choice.
Absolutely. A treat is only a treat if the eater likes it.
A rejected offering need not be a rejection of the entire friendship.
The Pokemon have declined the chef's suggestion without comment.
Different blocks could help test whether the flavor is the issue.
Even a small creature can have a very firm opinion.
Taste is personal. The presentation cannot solve everything.
I would compare what that same Pokemon chooses next time.

contexts.subject: A museum model reminds a visitor of the Abandoned Ship near Dewford.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_2F_Text_Remi.text: I saw a model of a ship here.\pIt reminded me of the ABANDONED SHIP\nnear DEWFORD TOWN…$

replies.text: A little model brought back a very big ship. Memories fit in odd places.
A familiar shape can make a distant place feel quite immediate.
That wreck would leave an impression.
I wonder which detail made them think of it.
Seeing the model must bring the real ship to mind so clearly.
A small exhibit has opened the door to a much larger story.
One tidy model, one rather less tidy memory of a ship.
It would be interesting to compare the model's design with the wreck.
Sometimes an object carries us somewhere else for a moment.

contexts.subject: Scott wakes from a nap, prefers battles but encourages enjoying Hoenns different events.

contexts.subject: A mother explains smooth low-feel high-level Pokeblocks and values partners, cooperation and family.

LilycoveCity_House3_Text_ExplainPokebloc.text:
Oh, good! You're a smart soul!
This is a bit long, so listen up!\pAre you ready?\pIf you look at {POKEBLOCK}S, you should see
that they are rated on how they feel.\pThe lower the feel rating,
the better it is. Don't forget this!\pA good {POKEBLOCK} has a low feel
rating and a high level.\pA POKéMON can eat more good
{POKEBLOCK}S than ordinary ones, too.\pAnd this is important.\pIf you want to make smooth {POKEBLOCK}S,
use different kinds of BERRIES.\pDon't be stingy--the kinds of BERRIES
affect the smoothness of {POKEBLOCK}S.\pAnd another thing.\pThe more people blending BERRIES,
the smoother the {POKEBLOCK}S.\pThat's why you should talk to other
people and make {POKEBLOCK}S together.\pThat's about all you need to know to

contexts.subject: A florist explains watering berries and dropped berries sprouting again.

It is kind that there is already another welcome waiting.
There is time to enjoy what we have before collecting more.
The day's botanical hospitality has formally drawn to a close.
The berries have finished their public appearances for today.
A sensible schedule keeps a generous project manageable.
Good things can return without needing to last all day.
A gracious end to today's giving. We can leave it there.
I would enjoy coming back to hear how the garden has changed.

contexts.subject: The Berry Masters wife proudly hopes their four grandchildren will surpass her husband.

Route123_BerryMastersHouse_Text_JoyNever.text: Our four grandchildren should become\nmore accomplished than my husband.\pJoy never goes out of my life!$

replies.text: Four growing grandchildren and a proud grandparent. That is a full garden of joy.
Her confidence in the next generation is rather lovely.
She is proud of them. Good reason to be happy.
The warmth in that makes the whole house feel different.
A family with plenty of young people to share its knowledge.
The family legacy has four eager possibilities and one delighted witness.
Her husband has acquired four very small future rivals.
Passing knowledge along can build something bigger than one person's work.
Joy has found several familiar faces to keep returning in.
She has a very charming way of boasting about the whole family.
I would ask what each grandchild is most excited to learn.

contexts.subject: The computer holds game code; the description warns that changing it could introduce bugs.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_3F_Text_ItsTheG.text: It's the game program! Messing with\nit could bug out the game!$

replies.text: I have touched enough buttons today. This one can remain mysterious.
An untested edit could affect much more than the line we change. Leave their work intact.
Their work. Their keyboard. Hands off.
A wrong note is easy to hear. A wrong instruction might wait hours to hurt something.
Do not season somebody else's recipe while they are away from the stove.
The world's least welcoming guest book. Sensible, really.
A tiny mistake waiting to become everyone's afternoon.
Interesting system. Inspection permission does not include permission to modify it.
Some spells deserve the courtesy of being left exactly as written.
Imagine coming back from lunch and finding a stranger has improved your job.
I would rather ask how they made it than find out how easily I can break it.

contexts.subject: A developer is playing a game instead of working.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_3F_Text_Someone.text: Someone's playing a game instead of\nworking!$

replies.text: Maybe this is research. I would also like a job with suspiciously enjoyable research.
Playing can reveal design problems. The description does suggest this is a break, though.
Let them have five minutes. We just walked into their office.
You can learn a lot by listening to somebody else's song. Also, sometimes you just like it.
Taste the food before serving it. This may be a very long tasting.
A convincing disguise for avoiding work: do something almost related to it.
The deadline cannot see them if they remain perfectly still.
Could be a useful comparison. Could also be a spectacularly good distraction.
Even diligent hands sometimes wander toward a little joy.
We are staring at their screen. We have become the office problem.
I wonder which part they keep coming back to. That usually tells you something.

contexts.subject: A script is on the desk; the player decides against reading its ending.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_3F_Text_ItsScri.text: It's the script!\nBetter not look at the ending!$

replies.text: Good. I like arriving at surprises with my eyebrows unprepared.
Knowing the conclusion would change how we interpret every earlier scene.
Close it before one sentence ruins a whole adventure.
I want the last note to mean something when we finally hear it.
No dessert before dinner. Even if the dessert has a very tempting title.
A fellow writer's ending, undefended on a desk. We shall exercise immense restraint.
Let the future retain at least one locked drawer.
Respect the intended sequence. And their unpublished draft.
An unopened ending still has room to surprise us.
Absolutely no reading the last page. I need to worry in the correct order.
I would rather remember how we reached the ending than just what happened.

contexts.subject: A Super NES console is on display in the game shop.

replies.text: It is like a tiny adventure machine. Much less walking than our usual arrangement.
A whole set of rules inside one box. I can see the appeal.
Looks fun. We should finish what we came here for first.
I wonder what its music sounds like through the shop speakers.
Does it come with snacks, or is that a separate department?
A heroic quest with a chair included. A formidable competitor.
A small box promising to consume a large evening.
The controller is a neat solution to having far too few hands inside the screen.
A window to somewhere else, with a cord to remind you to come back.
We could lose an entire rainy afternoon to that. I mean that fondly.
People must remember their first games the way we remember our first routes.

contexts.subject: The player notices an RPG but says there is no time to play.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_AnRP.text: An RPG!\nThere's no time for that!$

replies.text: Another adventure? My adventure pockets are already full.
We have limited time and several unfinished obligations. Sensible restraint.
One journey at a time. Ours still needs us.
It can wait. A good story will still be there when we have room to listen.
Starting another long commitment while hungry is how dinner becomes tomorrow.
A quest inside a quest. At last, a way to be behind on two destinies.
We have enough unfinished business without buying it in a box.
Scope control. An unexpectedly difficult skill in a game shop.
Leave that road unwalked for now. It will keep.
I want it. I also want us to arrive somewhere before the shop closes.
Maybe later we can compare its idea of traveling with the real thing.

contexts.subject: A puzzle game looks likely to be addictive.

replies.text: Just one more round is a very suspicious sentence. It always brings friends.
A clear goal and immediate feedback can make stopping surprisingly difficult.
Decide when to stop before you start. Easier that way.
I would keep thinking about the unfinished pattern after putting it down.
That has the same danger as tasting one more spoonful until the pot is empty.
An innocent little puzzle, applying for ownership of our evening.
A neat arrangement of pieces. A less neat arrangement of tomorrow's sleep.
Simple rules can produce excellent problems. I respect that design.
A little knot asking to be untied. Then another knot. Then dawn.
We would both say one round and both know we were lying.
I like seeing the instant somebody notices the solution. Their whole face changes.

contexts.subject: The vending machine successfully dispenses the selected drink.

replies.text: It worked! A tiny metal waiter with excellent boundaries.
Payment accepted and the chosen drink delivered. A reassuringly clear transaction.
Drink secured. Keep the empty can until we find a bin.
That little clunk is a surprisingly satisfying sound.
Excellent. Now we can stop pretending thirst is a personality.
The machine has fulfilled its entire character arc in one clunk.
A cold drink emerging from a warm afternoon. A modest miracle.
One input, one correct output. I wish every machine behaved that well.
The rooftop has offered a small, cold kindness.
That was the sound of us becoming slightly easier to travel with.
A quick drink and a look at the city. I like this stop.

contexts.subject: The vending purchase cannot fit because the bag is full.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_No.text: There's no more room for stuff!$

replies.text: The bag has voted against hydration. We should reorganize the committee.
The purchase needs free storage space. Sorting the bag is the useful next step.
Make room first. No reason to keep feeding the machine.
There is something very sad about being this close to a cold drink.
We packed for every emergency except wanting a beverage.
Our expedition has been defeated by the dimensions of a can.
The smallest obstacle today is also, apparently, insurmountable.
Capacity limit reached. Move something before attempting another purchase.
A crowded bag has shut the door on a very small comfort.
We are carrying an entire lifestyle and have nowhere to put a drink.
This is a good moment to check what we have been carrying without using.

contexts.subject: The vending purchase fails because the player lacks enough money.

replies.text: It is being very firm about the part where we pay it.
The displayed price exceeds our funds. Another attempt will not change that.
Count what we have before choosing again.
A cold drink would be nice. We can manage without buying one right now.
We should save the coins we have for what we actually need.
A machine immune to charm. A chilling adversary even without the drink.
The thirst remains. The money also remains, technically.
Insufficient funds is a clear answer. No amount of button pressing revises it.
Some doors open with coins. This one can remain closed for now.
We can leave without making being short on money into a whole performance.
Let us find a place to rest anyway. Buying something need not be the price of a pause.

contexts.subject: A photograph shows Blaine and Mr. Fuji smiling together.

CinnabarIsland_Gym_Text_PhotoOfBlaineAnd.text: It's a photo of BLAINE and\nMR. FUJI.\pThey're standing shoulder to\nshoulder with big grins.$

replies.text: They look like they were having a really good day. I am glad somebody kept it.
The photograph shows a friendship, not just two names we know separately.
Good picture. They look comfortable together.
Those smiles feel less formal than the ones people save for portraits.
I hope there was a good meal somewhere on that day.
A glimpse of people before we met them in their official roles.
Even people with difficult histories have days worth keeping.
Useful reminder that a person's life extends beyond the role we see.
A bright moment, kept where the years cannot quite reach it.
That is the kind of smile you get around someone who knows your embarrassing stories.
Someone chose to keep this friendship visible. I like that.

contexts.subject: Anthony regrets losing some of his allowance in the battle.

ViridianForest_Text_AnthonyPostBattle.text: I lost some of my allowance…$

replies.text: That was snack money before it became battle money. I can see why he looks glum.
A limited allowance makes even a modest loss feel significant.
He should keep enough for what he needs before risking another match.
It sounds worse when you have to wait for the next allowance.
A little budgeting could leave him with lunch even after a rough battle.
The adventure has encountered its first stern financial review.
A small loss can cast an impressively large shadow over a child's afternoon.
Worth keeping essential supplies separate from money he can afford to lose.
The pocket feels lighter long before the disappointment does.
No need to make him feel small about an amount that matters to him.
He will probably remember this battle every time he passes a shop today.

contexts.subject: A forest visitor ran out of Poke Balls while catching Pokemon.

ViridianForest_Text_RanOutOfPokeBalls.text: I was throwing POKé BALLS to\ncatch POKéMON, and I ran out.\pThat's why you can never have too\nmany POKé BALLS.$

replies.text: The enthusiasm lasted longer than the supplies. A very familiar sort of expedition.
A reserve is useful, though more supplies still need to fit a sensible budget.
Check the bag before heading farther into the forest.
Finding another Pokemon just after running out must feel particularly unfair.
A supply check is less exciting than a catch, but earns its place in the morning.
The hunt has reached an intermission sponsored by an empty pocket.
Ambition is remarkably good at forgetting to count its equipment.
A short checklist would prevent a very predictable interruption next time.
An empty pouch has a way of making every rustle more interesting.
He has converted an inconvenient afternoon into advice for strangers.
I wonder which encounter made him realize he had used the last one.

contexts.subject: Charlie enjoys how quickly Bug Pokemon evolve.

ViridianForest_Text_CharliePostBattle.text: BUG POKéMON evolve quickly.\nThey're a lot of fun!$

replies.text: A bug team does not make you wait long for the next surprise.
Rapid development makes changes easy to observe over a relatively short period.
He likes watching them grow. Good reason to keep paying attention.
It is lovely when caring for a team brings changes you can actually notice.
You could look away for a snack and come back to a different little face.
His favourite cast is admirably efficient about entering its next act.
A small creature can be very dramatic about changing its shape.
That quick turnaround gives him plenty of chances to compare each stage.
Tiny lives can carry a surprising number of transformations.
He sounds delighted by the team he already has. That is appealing.
I wonder which evolution first made him fall in love with Bug Pokemon.

contexts.subject: Doug reacts to losing by planning to catch stronger Pokemon.

ViridianForest_Text_DougPostBattle.text: That totally stinks! I'm going to\ncatch some stronger ones!$

replies.text: A stronger bug might help, but the plan still needs somebody thinking at the other end.
Changing the team is one option. Reviewing the decisions would provide useful evidence first.
His current team deserves a chance to improve, too.
I hope the Pokemon do not mistake his frustration for how he feels about them.
Replacing ingredients does not fix a pan nobody is watching.
The dissatisfied director has immediately proposed replacing the cast.
A new Pokemon is a rather unfair place to put all his hopes of never losing.
Find the actual weak point before replacing parts at random.
Stronger companions will still need a patient hand guiding them.
An upgrade is not much use if he brings the same careless attitude along.
I would like to know what he thinks stronger means after that match.

contexts.subject: Rick asks for quiet so the forest bugs are not frightened away.

ViridianForest_Text_RickPostBattle.text: Ssh! You'll scare the bugs away.\nAnother time, okay?$

replies.text: Right. Tiny bug audience, tiny bug volume. I can work with that.
Reducing sudden noise should make observing nearby Pokemon easier.
Keep it quiet. We are in their space.
I like the forest better when we can hear the small sounds underneath us.
A quiet pause seems fair after all that battling.
The resident audience has requested a less thunderous performance.
Silence is a very reasonable thing to bring into the woods.
Let's stop moving for a moment and see what comes back out.
The small hidden things need room to decide we are harmless.
An excellent reminder that being present does not require being conspicuous.
We might notice far more if we wait instead of announce ourselves.

contexts.subject: Sammy is looking for things he dropped and asks for help finding them.

ViridianForest_Text_SammyPostBattle.text: Sometimes, you can find stuff on\nthe ground.\pI'm looking for the stuff I\ndropped. Can you help me?$

replies.text: The forest floor has temporarily become his very inconvenient storage system.
Retracing his route would narrow the search more effectively than searching everywhere at once.
Watch our footing. We can look without trampling the smaller clues.
Losing something in all these leaves must feel discouraging.
Start where he last remembers having it, then work back slowly.
The treasure hunt has the useful complication that the treasure already has an owner.
Leaves are extremely committed to concealing other people's belongings.
Divide the ground into small patches so we do not keep checking the same place.
The woods keep what falls until somebody notices the absence.
Finding it should come before lecturing him about secure pockets.
I wonder whether the colour would stand out better from another angle.

contexts.subject: A visitor says the friends who came to catch bugs are eager to battle.

ViridianForest_Text_FriendsItchingToBatt.text: I came here with some friends to\ncatch us some BUG POKéMON!\pThey're all itching to get into\nsome POKéMON battles!$

replies.text: A bug-catching outing has turned into a whole committee of challenges.
A shared interest has given the group several ways to enjoy the forest together.
Good to know what the group is here for. Keep the team ready.
It sounds like the sort of trip they will talk about together afterward.
Catching, battling, then comparing stories. Quite a full afternoon.
The woodland excursion has developed a distinctly competitive second half.
A group of eager bug enthusiasts is a surprisingly lively thing to encounter.
Friends can make testing a new team feel like part of the outing.
The forest has become the meeting place for several small ambitions.
I like a group that arrives excited about the place instead of bored by it.
I wonder whether they all came for the same kind of Bug Pokemon.

contexts.subject: A traveller needs a rest after the tunnel journey from Cerulean.

Route3_Text_TunnelFromCeruleanTiring.text: Whew… I better take a rest…\nGroan…\pThat tunnel from CERULEAN takes a\nlot out of you!$

replies.text: That tunnel seems to have taken the spring right out of his walking.
Fatigue after a long passage is a useful signal to pause before continuing.
Rest here. No prize for stumbling through the next stretch exhausted.
He sounds tired enough that a quiet place to sit would mean a lot.
A drink and a proper stop are worth making time for.
The journey has earned an intermission without needing a dramatic incident.
An ordinary rock can become excellent furniture after a long walk.
We should account for the return journey when planning our own energy.
Even a familiar road grows long under tired feet.
There is no need to make resting look more dignified than it is.
I wonder how long he has been telling himself the next stop is close enough.

contexts.subject: A young admirer recognizes the Boulder Badge and wants to become a respected Gym Leader like Brock.

Route4_Text_PeopleLikeAndRespectBrock.text:
Oh, wow, that's the BOULDERBADGE!
You got it from BROCK, didn't you?\pBROCK is cool. He's not just tough.
People like and respect him.\pI want to become a GYM LEADER
like him.$

replies.text: Being tough got his attention. Being liked and respected seems to have kept it.
His ambition includes the social responsibilities of leadership, not only strength.
A good example can give a kid something solid to aim for.
I like that he notices how people feel around Brock.
Being someone a town can rely on is a worthwhile part of the dream.
The badge has prompted an aspiring leader to describe his ideal character.
It is pleasant when admiration reaches beyond who can win a fight.
A leader has to keep more than a strong team working well.
Some ambitions begin with noticing the kindness around someone else's strength.
Respect has made a stronger impression on him than a title alone could.
I wonder which little thing Brock did that made him seem worth following.

contexts.subject: A traveller has tripped over a Geodude.

Route4_Text_TrippedOverGeodude.text: Ouch! I tripped over a rocky\nPOKéMON, GEODUDE!$

replies.text: A rock that can object to being tripped over adds a whole new difficulty to walking.
Camouflage can make a Pokemon difficult to distinguish from the terrain.
Check the injury, then watch the ground before stepping again.
I hope both the traveller and the startled Geodude are all right.
A short pause to check the ankle beats limping all afternoon.
The scenery has objected to being treated as ordinary scenery.
The ground is already difficult enough without having opinions.
Uneven footing is a good reason to slow down and actually scan the path.
Sometimes the stone underfoot is having its own inconvenient day.
A painful reminder that not every obstacle is trying to be an obstacle.
I wonder how many people have mistaken that same Geodude for part of the path.

contexts.subject: A trainer checks the six Poke Balls on their belt.

Route4_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_CanHaveSixM.text: Okay, set six POKé BALLS in my\nbelt…\pYeah, that'll do it. At most, you\ncan have six POKéMON with you.$

replies.text: A belt check is the quiet little cousin of a heroic departure.
Checking the team before travelling is a sensible habit.
Know who is with you before heading back onto the road.
There is something reassuring about making sure everyone is accounted for.
A quick check saves reaching for something that is not there later.
The adventurer is completing the essential business of counting the cast.
Small routines do a lot of work keeping a journey from coming apart.
An equipment check is useful precisely because it is so easy to skip.
Six small circles can carry a very busy day.
Practical checks are hardly glamorous, but I appreciate someone doing them.
It makes me wonder what sort of team those six Balls belong to.

contexts.subject: A trainer recommends PC storage when there is no room for more Pokemon.

Route4_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_ShouldStore.text: Sometimes, you'll have too many\nPOKéMON with you to add any more.\pIn that case, you should just\nstore some using any PC.$

replies.text: A good reminder to make room before enthusiasm brings home another companion.
Planning team capacity ahead avoids an unnecessary interruption while travelling.
Sort the team where there is time to think.
It can be hard to decide who comes along when everyone matters.
A little preparation at the Center makes the next leg simpler.
The expanding cast requires a more deliberate travelling arrangement.
Even a fond collection eventually demands practical decisions.
Choose the team for the trip rather than wait for the capacity problem to choose for us.
Not every companion needs to take every road at the same time.
A useful piece of advice, offered without turning it into a lecture.
I wonder how often travellers only notice the full team at the next encounter.

contexts.subject: A Tower visitor is exhausted by the stairs rather than the battles.

TrainerTower_Lobby_Text_StairsTougherTha.text: Gasp, gasp…\nGasp…\pNever mind battling! These stairs…\nThey're tougher than any battle…$

replies.text: The stairs have an undefeated record and refuse to shake hands afterward.
Repeated climbing can be substantial exertion even without a single battle.
Catch a breath. The stairs are not going anywhere.
I feel a little less embarrassed about wanting to pause now.
The climb has definitely earned him somewhere comfortable to sit.
A formidable opponent with neither dialogue nor a weakness chart.
Architecture can be extraordinarily rude to a pair of tired legs.
A practical reminder that access routes are part of a building's real difficulty.
The tower asks a price from the body before it asks the team anything.
No shame in losing an argument with several flights of stairs.
I wonder how many challengers arrive ready for everything except the climb.

contexts.subject: A challenger is nervous about the unknown trainers waiting in the Tower.

TrainerTower_Lobby_Text_WonderWhatKindsO.text: I'm here to see how good I am.\pI wonder what kinds of TRAINERS\nare waiting for me?\pIt's nerve-racking!$

replies.text: The mystery opponents are currently undefeated at making this person's stomach wobble.
Uncertainty can feel more demanding than a known challenge of the same difficulty.
One battle at a time. No need to fight every possibility in advance.
Wanting to know how good you are can feel frightening right before the answer.
A steady breath and a supply check give the nerves something useful to do.
The unseen cast has created considerable suspense without making an entrance.
Imagination is remarkably energetic when asked to invent possible defeats.
They can prepare the team without needing to predict every opponent.
The closed door has become larger in thought than it is in the wall.
I appreciate someone admitting the nerves instead of trying to look untouchable.
I wonder what sort of challenger they hope to be when the first match begins.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man reports that the two deposited Pokemon seem to get along very well.

gDaycareText_GetAlongVeryWell.text: The two seem to get along\nvery well.

replies.text: Good news from the small social department. They seem happy with the company.
A favourable compatibility report, though it is still a brief observation rather than a whole relationship.
Good that they are settling in together.
That is a comforting thing to hear while they are away from us.
Pleasant company makes a temporary stay feel easier.
The boarding house has delivered an unusually glowing review of its roommates.
A peaceful little arrangement is worth appreciating.
Nice to hear the pairing seems to be working without trouble.
Two familiar presences have found a comfortable rhythm beside each other.
Getting along well is lovely news without needing to embellish it.
I wonder what the man noticed that made him sound so certain.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man reports that the two Pokemon seem to get along.

gDaycareText_GetAlong.text: The two seem to get along.

replies.text: A perfectly respectable roommate report. No tiny arguments noted.
The report suggests reasonable compatibility without claiming anything more specific.
They are doing all right together. Good to know.
A simple bit of reassurance can make leaving them here feel easier.
Sounds like their stay has some comfortable company in it.
A modest review, refreshingly free of invented romantic complications.
Ordinary peace rarely gets enough credit.
A working arrangement does not need dramatic results to count as good news.
Sometimes the kindest report is that two lives fit quietly beside each other.
Comfortable company is worthwhile even without a spectacular friendship story.
I wonder whether they have found something they like doing together.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man says the two Pokemon do not seem to like each other much.

gDaycareText_DontLikeOther.text: The two don't seem to like\neach other much.

replies.text: Not every pair becomes best friends. We do not need to issue matching friendship badges.
This is a compatibility assessment, not evidence by itself of conflict or poor care.
No need to force them to be close. Keep an eye on how they are doing.
It is all right if familiar company takes a while, or never becomes their favourite.
Sharing a place does not oblige anyone to adore the other guest.
The proposed duo has declined to supply an instant friendship subplot.
A lack of fondness need not become a scandal.
We can consider a different pairing instead of insisting the current one should work.
Two lives can share a patch of shade without growing toward each other.
There is no prize for making a reluctant pair look charming.
I would pay attention to their comfort rather than imagine a whole quarrel from one report.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man says the Pokemon prefer playing with other Pokemon instead of each other.

gDaycareText_PlayOther.text: The two prefer to play with other\nPOKéMON than each other.

replies.text: They have declined the arranged playdate and selected their own tiny social calendar.
The report describes incompatible pairing preferences. It does not establish that either Pokemon is unhappy.
They can choose different company. That is fine.
Being comfortable with others is still company, even if it is not this particular pair.
No need to make two guests sit together just because they arrived together.
The cast have requested separate scenes and a wider circle of acquaintances.
A polite refusal to become the friendship someone else had planned.
A different pairing may work better than trying to force this one.
They have found other little paths through the same garden.
Choosing their own companions seems fair to me.
I wonder which Pokemon each of them actually enjoys spending time with.

contexts.subject: Oak recommends searching more patches of grass to begin filling the Pokedex.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan10.text: You still have lots to do.\pGo into every patch of grass you\nsee and look for POKéMON!$

replies.text: The grand scientific plan currently begins with looking carefully in the grass. I can do that.
Sampling more locations should reveal species a narrow search would miss.
Start nearby and pay attention. No need to rush the whole region.
A big task can feel less frightening when the next step is that small.
We can make a day of exploring without expecting to finish everything at once.
The professor has supplied a humble but promising opening chapter.
A great undertaking can begin with being slightly more attentive to weeds.
Let's compare different patches rather than repeatedly searching the same corner.
The grass has been living its own busy story beside our feet.
It is practical advice. No grand pose required to begin.
I wonder what we have already walked past without noticing.

contexts.subject: Oak praises early progress and recommends collecting Flash from his aide.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan20.text: It looks as if you're getting on\nthe right track!\pI've given one of my AIDES a FLASH\nHM. Make sure you go get it!$

replies.text: Encouragement and a reminder to collect something useful. A nicely practical compliment.
The advice connects research progress with equipment that supports further exploration.
Worth checking with his aide before heading somewhere dark.
It feels good that he notices the beginning instead of only the distance left.
A useful errand to fit into the next stretch of travel.
The professor has paired his favourable review with a rather illuminating recommendation.
A small beginning has earned more than a distracted nod.
Better equipment can make careful exploration much easier.
A little knowledge has opened the possibility of carrying more light.
He remembers the practical help instead of leaving us with praise alone.
I like hearing him sound pleased before the collection is anywhere near finished.

contexts.subject: Oak recommends adding a greater variety of species to the Pokedex.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan30.text: Your POKéDEX could use a bit more\nvolume still!\pTry to catch other species of\nPOKéMON!$

replies.text: The book wants more different neighbours, rather than a long queue of the same little face.
Increasing species variety addresses the particular gap he has identified.
Try a different habitat instead of repeating the same route.
It helps to have a clearer aim than simply doing more.
A change of scenery could make the next bit of work enjoyable, too.
The editor requests a broader cast rather than additional appearances by old favourites.
Variety is a kinder assignment than endless repetition.
Let's look for habitats we have not sampled much yet.
The map has more voices than the ones nearest the road.
A fuller collection should show the place's variety, not just our habits.
I wonder which kind of habitat has been missing from our travels.

contexts.subject: Oak recognizes the effort and reminds the player to collect an Itemfinder from his aide.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan40.text: Good, it's apparent that you're\ntrying hard!\pI've given one of my AIDES an\nITEMFINDER. Be sure to collect it!$

replies.text: He has noticed our hard work and knows a device that may notice the things we miss.
An Itemfinder would add another means of observing otherwise overlooked surroundings.
Useful reminder. We should speak to the aide when we are nearby.
It means something that he notices the effort behind the pages.
A practical tool makes a good follow-up to kind words.
A favourable review comes with a recommendation for finding the less obvious props.
Apparently curiosity may now receive technical assistance.
A detector could help us examine places our eyes have already dismissed.
The overlooked things may soon become a little harder to overlook.
He makes progress feel worth noticing without pretending the work is finished.
I wonder how many useful little details are lying just outside our attention.

contexts.subject: Oak praises the collection and recommends getting the Amulet Coin from his aide.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan50.text: Your POKéDEX is coming along quite\nwell!\pI've given one of my AIDES an\nAMULET COIN. Be sure to get it!$

replies.text: A little praise and a reminder about an amulet. Our errands are getting surprisingly shiny.
He offers a practical reward alongside the assessment rather than only a ranking.
We can check with the aide. No need to turn the whole trip toward money.
His approval feels warmer when he remembers something that might help the journey.
A bit of financial breathing room can make practical travel choices easier.
The professor's encouraging review includes a potentially lucrative footnote.
Research apparently has the occasional less threadbare fringe benefit.
Worth collecting the useful tool before making assumptions about what it will solve.
An ordinary errand has acquired a small promise of good fortune.
He seems genuinely pleased to help the next part go more smoothly.
I like that the reminder is specific enough to act on.

contexts.subject: Oak celebrates passing fifty species and recommends collecting Exp Share from an aide.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan60.text: Ah, you've finally topped 50\nspecies!\pI've given one of my AIDES an EXP.\nSHARE. Be sure to go get it!$

replies.text: Fifty species! That is a lot of different ways for the grass to surprise us.
A substantial sample, and the suggested aid could support development across the team.
Solid progress. We should check with his aide when it suits the route.
Fifty feels much more real when somebody says it aloud like that.
That is a milestone worth a proper sit-down and something nice to eat.
The research has reached fifty entries and earned an enthusiastic editorial note.
A number has become large enough to sound like the days we spent earning it.
A useful tool and a measurable milestone. A satisfying report.
Fifty little records carry a great many roads behind them.
The work shows, even if each day only added a little.
I wonder which of those encounters we will remember most clearly years from now.

contexts.subject: Oak calls the growing Pokedex quite respectable.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan70.text: Hoho! This is turning into quite the\nrespectable POKéDEX!$

replies.text: Respectable! Our wandering has officially become a respectable activity.
The assessment recognizes sustained progress rather than a single unusual find.
Good work, steadily done. Worth being pleased with.
A calm bit of praise can stay with me longer than a big fuss.
It is good to stop and appreciate what all those days have added up to.
The collection has received the professor's considered seal of approval.
Respectable is a pleasantly solid word for a heap of small discoveries.
A growing record shows what consistent attention can accomplish.
A little work repeated has made a shape large enough for someone else to see.
He sounds satisfied with the care that has gone into it.
I wonder whether he remembers how his own first collection began.

contexts.subject: Oak recommends fishing to discover more Pokemon.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan80.text: Very good!\pI think you'll collect even more\nPOKéMON by going fishing!$

replies.text: The next research method involves standing by water and trying to look patient.
Fishing samples a habitat that walking through grass cannot adequately represent.
Check the rod and find safe footing before casting.
A quieter kind of searching might make a nice change.
Time beside the water can be enjoyable even before anything bites.
The professor has prescribed a slower-paced chapter with an unpredictable supporting cast.
A perfectly respectable reason to stare into water for a while.
Different water and different locations could produce useful comparisons.
The surface is only the lid on another crowded little world.
It is a good reminder that our usual route does not show us everything.
I wonder what lives beneath places we have only looked across.

contexts.subject: Oak guesses that the player enjoys collecting things.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan90.text: Wonderful! Let me guess… You\nlike to collect things, don't you?$

replies.text: The large collection may have given our collecting habit away. Subtle detective work, Professor.
Repeated choices can reveal a preference, though curiosity may matter as much as collecting.
We have certainly put the work in.
It is a little funny to be recognized through all the things we stopped to notice.
There is pleasure in seeing the small efforts gathered together.
The evidence has led the professor to a charmingly obvious character assessment.
A fond accusation, supported by quite a substantial pile of evidence.
Collecting gets especially interesting when the entries start revealing patterns.
Gather enough little wonders and people begin to recognize the habit.
He makes the observation sound affectionate rather than possessive.
I wonder whether he recognizes a younger version of himself in that habit.

contexts.subject: Oak admires the difficult work behind the Pokedex collection.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan100.text: I'm impressed!\nIt must have been difficult to do!$

replies.text: He can see the long walks hiding between the neat little entries.
The record represents substantial effort that the finished list does not directly display.
It took work. Nice to have that recognized.
I like that he notices it was not always easy.
A good result has a lot of ordinary tiring days tucked behind it.
The reviewer has remembered that the polished volume required an expedition.
Some praise feels better because it includes the difficult part.
A tidy record hides plenty of failed approaches and useful revisions.
The finished pages have not forgotten the miles, even when they look quiet.
He appreciates the effort without demanding we make it look effortless.
I wonder which part of the journey he imagines when he says that.

contexts.subject: Oak enthusiastically celebrates reaching one hundred species.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan110.text: You've finally hit 100 species!\nI can't believe how good you are!$

replies.text: One hundred! That number has enough legs to march right out of the notebook.
A hundred species is a substantial body of observation, gathered encounter by encounter.
A hundred. We earned a moment to enjoy that.
It is hard not to smile when he sounds that pleased.
That deserves something better than eating while walking to the next task.
The hundredth entry has secured a wonderfully enthusiastic review.
A large round number has arrived carrying a surprisingly warm feeling.
A hundred entries give us plenty of interesting details to compare.
A hundred small doors opened, each onto a life that was already there.
He sounds delighted enough for the celebration to feel shared.
I wonder how different the first entry looks to us after all these others.

contexts.subject: Oak admires the inclusion of evolved Pokemon in the collection.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan120.text: You even have the evolved forms\nof POKéMON! Super!$

replies.text: The book has room for the little faces and the faces they grew into.
Recording multiple developmental stages adds important information beyond species variety alone.
Good to see growth getting its share of the attention.
There is something lovely about recognizing a familiar Pokemon in a changed shape.
Time and care can leave their own kind of record in those pages.
The professor appreciates that the story includes more than the opening appearance.
Change is easier to understand when somebody bothered to notice both sides of it.
Comparing stages can show which traits persist and which change dramatically.
A growing creature carries its earlier shape somewhere inside the new one.
I like that the collection notices development instead of only novelty.
I wonder which transformation surprised us most when we first saw it.

contexts.subject: Oak recommends trading with friends to expand the Pokedex.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan130.text: Excellent! Trade with friends to\nget some more!$

replies.text: Apparently the next missing entry might begin with saying hello to somebody.
Trading can connect records and opportunities that separate journeys would not provide.
Make any trade carefully. Both sides should understand what they are agreeing to.
It is nice when a big task gives people a reason to meet.
Friends can help each other without turning every meeting into an errand.
The solo research project has been advised to invite a few collaborators.
A collection can become more interesting when it acquires other people's stories.
Comparing what we have found could reveal useful gaps before arranging a trade.
Two roads can lend each other something neither found alone.
A fair exchange should feel good to everyone when the conversation ends.
I wonder which entries carry the clearest memory of the person we traded with.

contexts.subject: Oak says the player has become a true professional at collecting Pokemon.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan140.text: Outstanding!\nYou've become a real pro at this!$

replies.text: A real pro! I should probably stop looking surprised every time the grass moves, then.
Expertise often begins to show in consistent choices rather than impressive terminology.
High praise from someone who knows the work.
It feels strange and good when somebody says you have become capable.
All those ordinary days have turned into skills we do not have to think about as much.
The apprenticeship has received an unexpectedly distinguished review.
Competence can arrive quietly before a compliment points it out.
Practice has made some once-difficult tasks feel almost automatic.
A path walked often has begun to recognize our feet.
It is lovely to hear expertise recognized without making it sound unreachable.
I wonder which part of this now feels natural that once seemed impossible.

contexts.subject: Oak extravagantly declares the player a Pokemon Professor.

PokedexRating_Text_LessThan150.text: I have nothing left to say!\nYou're the POKéMON PROFESSOR now!$

replies.text: A professor? Do we need a desk, or can the title travel in a backpack?
That is very generous praise. There remains quite a difference between a thorough collection and every research skill.
He is proud of the work. We can accept that without claiming to know everything.
I think he means it kindly enough that we can just let ourselves be pleased.
A title that grand deserves a comfortable seat before we try it on.
The professor has reviewed the work and offered to hand over the reviewer's chair.
A magnificently oversized compliment can still have a sincere heart.
I like the praise, though I would still have a notebook full of questions.
Knowing much has not made the remaining unknowns any smaller.
He is being wonderfully extravagant with his approval.
I wonder whether he enjoys saying that as much as we enjoy hearing it.

contexts.subject: Oak congratulates the player on completing the regional Pokedex.

replies.text: All those encounters have finally filled the whole list. That is a very big little book.
A completed regional record is an extraordinary result, even as questions about its subjects remain.
We finished it. Take the moment before finding another task.
I am glad he sounds as happy about the end as he was about the beginning.
This deserves a celebration we actually sit down to enjoy.
The final entry has earned its closing applause without ending our curiosity.
A finished list can hold a surprising amount of unfinished wonder.
That is a complete set of observations to start asking more detailed questions from.
The last empty space has become a memory of something alive.
A long project deserves more than a quick checkmark when it is done.
I would like to remember the faces around us at this particular moment.

contexts.subject: Oak looks forward to the growing National Pokedex.

PokedexRating_Text_LookForwardToFilledNa.text: I'll be looking forward to seeing\nyou fill the NATIONAL POKéDEX!$

replies.text: A bigger book means the next rustling patch can still have something new to introduce.
Expanding the scope adds substantial work, but also makes comparisons across regions possible.
One new entry at a time. No need to turn the whole thing into a race.
His expectation sounds more like interest than impatience. I like that.
A long project needs ordinary rest built into it.
The professor has expressed interest in the sequel before the current expedition is over.
A larger horizon can be inviting without becoming an order to hurry.
There are new habitats and patterns to compare beyond the familiar record.
The edges of the known world have moved, and the questions have followed.
It is nice to have someone looking forward to what we will notice next.
I wonder which unfamiliar place will give us the next surprising entry.

contexts.subject: Oak sincerely thanks the player for realizing his lifelong Pokedex dream.

PokedexRating_Text_ThankYouMadeDreamReal.text: Thank you, {PLAYER}!\nSincerely, thank you!\lYou've made my dream a reality!$

replies.text: Oh. This was not just a very large list to him. We helped something precious become real.
Years of research and hope can make an achievement deeply personal to the researcher.
He meant every word. We did something that matters to him.
I would rather let that thank-you sit quietly for a moment.
It is lovely when a long effort gives someone that much joy.
The grand project has ended in something wonderfully simple: a sincere thank-you.
A dream looks different when it finally has somewhere to stand.
All those separate encounters have added up to a result he once could only imagine.
Someone's long-held hope has found a place in the daylight.
He has dropped every formal word and just let the happiness show.
That is the kind of expression a person remembers without needing a picture.

contexts.subject: The Double-Edge tutor leaves the offer available after a refusal.

replies.text: A technique we can return for. The road has left us a bookmark.
Keeping the offer open lets us choose based on the team's actual needs.
We can decide later. No reason to rush the choice.
I like an invitation that survives a quiet no.
Time to think is useful before choosing a move.
A postponed lesson, with the door still courteously open.
