The absence of pressure makes returning rather more appealing.
We can compare the move with our current options first.
An offered path can remain a path without becoming an obligation.
A refusal received with grace is always a good look.
I wonder how many travellers eventually come back for that lesson.

contexts.subject: The Double-Edge tutor encourages the player to keep striving toward the League.

Text_DoubleEdgeTaught.text: Keep that drive going for the\nPOKéMON LEAGUE!\pTake a run at them and knock 'em\nout!$

replies.text: That encouragement has enough momentum to jog ahead and wait for us at the next corner.
Determination helps, but a League attempt also needs a prepared team.
Keep going carefully. Drive does not replace preparation.
It is nice to hear someone sound certain we can keep improving.
A bit of encouragement travels well between proper rest stops.
The mentor has supplied a stirring send-off toward greater opposition.
Ambition is easier to carry when somebody has said a kind word over it.
We can turn that energy toward a specific improvement in the team.
A warm push at the back need not become a shove toward danger.
His confidence in a traveller is an unexpectedly generous parting gift.
I wonder whether he remembers the advice that kept him going.

contexts.subject: The Thunder Wave tutor is disappointed that the convenient move is declined.

replies.text: Convenient is a good recommendation, but it is not the same as compulsory.
A useful technique can still be unsuitable for a particular team.
We heard the offer. The choice is still ours.
He can like the move without needing us to agree today.
Not every useful thing belongs in the plan at once.
The pitch has reached its final appeal to convenience.
A little disappointment need not turn our answer into a negotiation.
There are trade-offs even when a technique is handy.
An unused possibility need not disappear from the world.
He should let the recommendation stand without chasing the refusal.
I wonder which situation first made the move feel indispensable to him.

contexts.subject: The tutor explains Thunder Wave paralysis and notes that some Pokemon are immune.

Text_ThunderWaveTaught.text:
THUNDER WAVE causes paralysis in
the target POKéMON.\pA paralyzed POKéMON may be unable
to move in battle.\pIt's an ELECTRIC-type move, so it
won't work on some POKéMON.$

replies.text: A useful trick still has somebody out there who does not find it impressive.
The exception matters. A strategy based on paralysis needs an alternative.
Know what it will not work on before relying on it.
I appreciate hearing the limits along with the advantages.
A fallback plan belongs beside every favourite trick.
A rare sales pitch improved by admitting where the product fails.
Certainty has been politely interrupted by the existence of exceptions.
Good information. We should plan for immunity as well as success.
A net is useful partly because you know what can pass through it.
Practical advice is better when it includes the awkward details.
I wonder how often opponents expect that move and prepare around it.

contexts.subject: The Rock Slide tutor teases the player for declining the move.

Text_RockSlideDeclined.text: Oh, so you are scared after all.$

replies.text: Not choosing falling rocks is not automatically a failure of courage.
A declined technique does not provide evidence about the trainer's fear.
He can keep the teasing. We can keep our answer.
I do not like a choice being turned into a dare.
There are perfectly sensible reasons to pass on a move.
The instructor has mistaken a recruitment pitch for a bravery test.
A small taunt is a poor argument for taking a lesson.
We should decide by team fit rather than react to a provocation.
A falling stone does not need us to prove anything beneath it.
That little jab adds nothing useful to the offer.
I wonder whether he knows how to hear no without teasing someone.

contexts.subject: The Rock Slide tutor reflects that using it inside the tunnel could be frightening.

Text_RockSlideTaught.text: It might be scary to use it in this\ntunnel…$

replies.text: Falling rocks inside a tunnel is a sentence that makes the ceiling feel closer.
A confined space deserves particular caution around falling debris.
Keep that sort of force away from an unstable tunnel.
I would rather not find out how the ceiling feels about it.
A lesson about rockfalls is a good time to think about the people nearby.
An impressive technique with a distinctly alarming choice of venue.
The tunnel is already providing enough stone overhead for my taste.
The surroundings matter as much as the move's intended target.
The mountain has no need of help shedding pieces onto us.
A thrill loses its appeal quickly when everyone has to stand beneath it.
I would check the space and the people around us before imagining any demonstration.

contexts.subject: The Mega Punch tutor insists the player will return after appreciating the move.

Text_MegaPunchDeclined.text: You'll be back when you understand\nthe worth of MEGA PUNCH.$

replies.text: He has predicted our return with the confidence of someone who has not asked our plans.
He values the technique highly; that does not make our future choice certain.
He can wait. We are not obliged to prove his prediction.
I would find the invitation easier to like without the certainty about us.
A good offer can stand without insisting everyone must eventually accept it.
The instructor has written himself a triumphant return scene without consulting the visitor.
A confident prediction is still only a prediction, however loudly it stands.
We can assess the move without adopting his rivalry or his expectations.
An open door needs no prophecy about who will cross it.
He could let the technique speak for itself and make a better impression.
I wonder whether anyone has ever simply walked away without looking back.

contexts.subject: The Mega Punch tutor declares camaraderie and insults the nearby Mega Kick trainer.

Text_MegaPunchTaught.text: Now, we are comrades in the way of\npunching!\pYou should go before you're seen\nby the misguided fool who trains\lonly his silly kicking over there.$

replies.text: We have joined the punching club and immediately received its gossip bulletin.
His enthusiasm for one technique does not establish that the alternative is foolish.
We need not take sides in their argument.
I like the welcome more than the insult attached to it.
Enjoying one specialty does not require spoiling somebody else's.
Membership apparently includes a complimentary feud with the neighbouring school.
Two grown enthusiasts have found a remarkably small hill to quarrel on.
Punching and kicking solve different problems. The rivalry adds no useful data.
One man's devotion has grown an unnecessary little thorn.
The warm welcome would look better without someone else's dignity under its shoe.
I wonder how long they have been making exactly these speeches about each other.

contexts.subject: The Mega Kick tutor predicts the player will come crawling back.

Text_MegaKickDeclined.text: You'll come crawling back when you\nrealize the value of MEGA KICK.$

replies.text: A return invitation has somehow put mud on its own welcome mat.
The condescension contributes nothing to evaluating the move.
We said no. He can manage without the insult.
I would rather return because I wanted to learn, not because he wanted to gloat.
Teaching works better when the learner is not being talked down to.
The proposed reunion is rather more humiliating in his version than I care for.
An invitation that imagines us crawling can remain unanswered.
The useful question is whether the move fits our team, not his pride.
There is no need to kneel before a door simply because it remains open.
What an unappealing way to advertise another conversation with himself.
I wonder whether he mistakes making people defensive for being persuasive.

contexts.subject: The Mega Kick tutor declares a bond through kicking and disparages the punching tutor.

Text_MegaKickTaught.text: Now, we are soul mates in the way\nof kicking!\pYou should run before you're seen\nby the deluded nitwit who trains\lonly simple punching over there.$

replies.text: Soul mates in kicking is a very specific place to find belonging.
Shared enthusiasm is pleasant. The dismissal of punching is not a technical comparison.
We learned a technique, not an obligation to join his feud.
That is a lot of closeness to announce before we have even left.
A shared specialty can be enjoyable without making the neighbours into enemies.
The kicking fraternity has welcomed us and immediately disclosed its ancient grievance.
An impressively narrow basis for declaring a meeting of souls.
Both techniques deserve judging on their uses rather than their instructors' pride.
A bond made through movement need not require standing against someone else.
The enthusiasm is charming until it drags the other tutor into it.
I wonder whether those two would miss having each other to complain about.

contexts.subject: The Counter tutor invites the player to return if interested later.

Text_CounterDeclined.text: You're not interested? Come see\nme if you change your mind.$

replies.text: A no has been accepted without launching a counterattack. Nicely done.
A standing offer allows a later decision when the team's needs may differ.
We can return if we need it. Nothing to settle now.
It is easier to think clearly when the offer does not push back.
A useful lesson will still be useful after we have had time to consider it.
A courteous exit leaves the next meeting entirely possible.
I appreciate an invitation that does not follow us down the road.
We can evaluate the technique against our current options in peace.
Some offers are kind enough to remain still while we move on.
That is a graceful way to leave a future conversation open.
I wonder how the move became this person's favourite thing to teach.

contexts.subject: The Counter tutor asks whether the player has been using the move.

Text_CounterTaught.text: Are you using that COUNTER move\nI taught your POKéMON?$

replies.text: The teacher wants to know what happened after the lesson. That is a nice detail.
Following up on practical use can reveal whether instruction transferred into actual decisions.
Useful to think about when it helped and when it did not.
I hope the question leaves room for an honest answer either way.
A skill becomes more familiar when there is time to try it and talk it over.
The instructor has requested news from the technique's subsequent adventures.
A lesson has acquired an afterlife interesting enough to ask about.
Feedback from real battles would be more useful than guessing how it went.
A taught thing changes when somebody carries it out into the world.
Remembering a former pupil makes a better impression than reciting the same pitch.
I wonder which part of using it the tutor most wants to hear about.

contexts.subject: The Body Slam tutor sends the player off with an exuberant boing.

replies.text: A cheerful refusal accepted with a sound effect. That is a refreshingly bouncy goodbye.
The enthusiasm has survived a declined lesson with no apparent difficulty.
Friendly enough. We can leave without an argument.
I did not expect the goodbye to make me smile like that.
A light parting can improve an otherwise ordinary stop.
The lesson has been declined; the instructor's spring remains fully wound.
A conversation can end pleasantly without anyone getting what they offered.
That much energy seems to be part of the tutor's standard equipment.
Some people leave a little bounce in the air after speaking.
An unembarrassed bit of silliness is rather appealing.
I wonder whether anyone manages to hear that goodbye without smiling.

contexts.subject: The Body Slam tutor celebrates with an emphatic bouncing sound.

replies.text: That is either celebration or a person briefly becoming a spring.
A memorable sound makes for a remarkably concise closing remark.
He seems pleased. Hard to miss that.
I think that was a happy goodbye. It was certainly an energetic one.
A cheerful little finish to the visit.
The closing statement has dispensed with words and retained all its enthusiasm.
An entire mood expressed with a very elastic syllable.
A spring-loaded farewell would apparently be entirely on brand here.
The air has been left slightly rounder by that sound.
I respect committing that completely to a ridiculous little flourish.
That is the sort of sound a visitor remembers longer than the formal explanation.

contexts.subject: The Metronome tutor insists the move is fun after the player declines.

Text_MetronomeDeclined.text: I tell you, it's a lot of fun!$

replies.text: Fun is an excellent recommendation. It is still allowed to be somebody else's fun.
Enjoyment varies between trainers. His preference does not settle our choice.
We can pass without arguing about whether he enjoys it.
It can be fun and still not feel right for us today.
A favourite activity is tempting, but it does not have to be shared by everyone.
The enthusiastic review has remained enthusiastic in the face of a poor booking.
At least he has not mistaken fun for a solemn duty.
A move's unpredictability may be enjoyable without fitting our current plan.
A playful possibility can wait without losing its sparkle.
The pitch works better when it leaves space for different tastes.
I wonder what unexpected move made him laugh the hardest.

contexts.subject: The tutor describes Metronome producing moves the Pokemon does not normally know.

Text_MetronomeTaught.text: Tch-tch-tch!\nThat's the sound of a METRONOME.\pIt tweaks your POKéMON's brain into\nusing moves it doesn't even know.$

replies.text: An unexpected move hiding inside a little ticking gesture. The surprise has a very small door.
The unpredictability is central to the technique; a specific outcome should not be assumed.
A surprise can go either way. Keep that in mind.
I can see why he likes the moment before finding out what happens.
A little improvisation is fun when the consequences are manageable.
A performer that refuses to disclose its next line until the cue arrives.
Uncertainty has acquired a charmingly regular little sound.
We cannot build a plan around one guaranteed result from that.
A small gesture opens a box without promising what lives inside.
It is an appealing idea precisely because it is so difficult to predict.
I wonder how differently each trainer remembers the same unpredictable move.

contexts.subject: The Seismic Toss tutor confidently expects the player to return.

Text_SeismicTossDeclined.text: Is that so?\nI'm sure you'll be back for it.$

replies.text: Another teacher with a very confident forecast about our future footsteps.
Interest may change later, but there is no reason to treat that as inevitable.
He can keep the offer. We can keep moving.
I prefer an invitation to a prediction made on my behalf.
We can decide when there is a good reason, rather than a point to prove.
The instructor has pencilled in our return without asking for availability.
The future remains free to disappoint his appointment book.
The move should earn a place through usefulness, not insistence.
A door can stay open without calling every departing traveller back.
A little less certainty about strangers would improve the welcome.
I wonder whether he has ever asked what a visitor actually needs.

contexts.subject: The Seismic Toss tutor encourages persistence with a toss-in-the-towel pun.

Text_SeismicTossTaught.text: I hope you won't toss in the towel.\nKeep it up.$

replies.text: He has managed to toss a pun into the encouragement. No towel required.
A little wordplay can make an otherwise ordinary reminder more memorable.
Keep trying, sensibly. Fair advice beneath the joke.
That was a gentle way to tell someone not to give up.
A small joke can make encouragement easier to take along.
The tutor has closed with a pun and an entirely serviceable moral.
A harmless joke is a respectable place to hide a kind thought.
A memorable phrase can help the useful advice survive the walk away.
A light word can still keep a little resolve from sinking.
I like encouragement that does not need to look terribly important.
I wonder how long he has been waiting for somebody new to hear that one.

contexts.subject: The Softboiled tutor hopes to chat again after the lesson is declined.

Text_SoftboiledDeclined.text: I'll always be keeping an eye out\nfor you.\pI hope we can chat again.$

replies.text: The offer was declined and the person still wants to see us. That feels nice.
The conversation has value to the tutor beyond whether the technique is accepted.
A friendly goodbye. No debt attached to it.
I like that a future chat does not have to be another lesson.
It is lovely when a visit can be enough on its own.
The invitation has quietly changed from instruction to company.
A little warmth survives the absence of a useful transaction.
That is a good way to keep a conversation open without applying pressure.
A familiar face can be welcome without arriving with a request.
There is something charming about wanting another conversation rather than another chance to persuade.
I wonder what we would talk about if we stopped simply to say hello.

contexts.subject: The Softboiled tutor offers a simple wish of good luck.

Text_SoftboiledTaught.text: I wish you the best of luck!$

replies.text: A small good-luck wish can fit into almost any pocket.
A brief expression of goodwill makes a perfectly complete farewell.
Kind of the tutor. We can carry that onward.
I like a goodbye that leaves the day feeling a little gentler.
A little kindness is welcome even when there is nothing more to arrange.
A concise farewell with no unnecessary flourish obscuring the warmth.
The simplest good wishes often avoid saying too much.
Practical instruction and a friendly send-off make a good combination.
A kind word has been set lightly beside the road.
Good manners need not be elaborate to leave a lovely impression.
I wonder whether the tutor knows how much a small wish can improve a day.

contexts.subject: The Substitute tutor wistfully says the move seems fun.

replies.text: A little disappointed, but still fond of the idea. That is all right.
The appeal is personal, and declining it does not invalidate the tutor's enjoyment.
We can leave the idea with someone who clearly likes it.
I can hear the little wish behind the offer.
Not everything enjoyable has to become part of our own plans.
The rejected proposal retains its enthusiastic author. A survivable review.
A small disappointment need not become a dramatic rejection of the person.
We can appreciate the concept without deciding to use it.
A playful thought can remain bright even when nobody picks it up today.
Different ideas of fun can coexist quite comfortably.
I wonder what the tutor imagines first when thinking about that move.

contexts.subject: The Substitute tutor daydreams about sheltering in a Kangaskhan pouch.

Text_SubstituteTaught.text: Boy, what I'd give to crawl inside\na KANGASKHAN belly pouch…$

replies.text: A Kangaskhan pouch does sound cosy. I suspect the actual resident has priority, though.
The thought is understandable, but the pouch serves a biological purpose rather than guest accommodation.
Comfortable thought. Leave the pouch to the youngster.
I understand wanting somewhere warm to hide for a little while.
That is a very portable idea of a comfortable afternoon.
The daydream has requested a rather exclusive form of lodging.
A harmless wish for shelter, with a substantial practical size problem.
Warmth and protection: an excellent design, already occupied.
Some dreams are simply about being small enough to be carried safely.
It is an unexpectedly tender fantasy behind a very practical lesson.
I wonder whether seeing a youngster tucked in there first gave the tutor that idea.

contexts.subject: The Swords Dance tutor accepts the player's refusal without fuss.

replies.text: A no that gets to be a complete answer. Always refreshing.
The tutor has accepted a different choice without demanding justification.
That settles it. We can move on comfortably.
It is nice when refusing something does not make the air change.
An easy response leaves everyone free to enjoy the rest of the day.
A modest exit, with no theatrical wounded pride to tidy away.
A conversation need not acquire a bruise every time somebody says no.
We can keep considering our options without a debate following us.
An unchosen path has been left peacefully where it was.
Quiet acceptance is a better look than trying to win every exchange.
I like how little work the tutor makes us do to leave politely.

contexts.subject: The Swords Dance tutor wishes strength could keep increasing forever.

Text_SwordsDanceTaught.text: If only we could keep getting\nstronger and stronger, eh?$

replies.text: Forever is a lot of practice. I hope there are water breaks somewhere in it.
Improvement has limits and trade-offs; indefinite growth is an aspiration rather than a guarantee.
Stronger is useful. Knowing when to stop matters, too.
I wonder whether constant improvement would ever let someone feel satisfied.
Strength needs time to recover as well as time to grow.
An ambitious wish for a sequel with no final volume.
Endless progress sounds suspiciously like never being allowed a day off.
A clear goal gives improvement more direction than simply demanding more.
Even growing things pause when the season asks them to.
Wanting to grow is appealing. Never feeling enough sounds exhausting.
I wonder what becoming stronger would let the tutor actually do differently.

contexts.subject: The Explosion tutor agrees that the technique is terrifying after it is declined.

Text_ExplosionDeclined.text: Yeah, you're right.\nIt is too terrifying.$

replies.text: A rare instructor willing to agree that the alarming thing is, in fact, alarming.
Recognizing a technique's severe trade-offs is a valid reason to decline it.
A sensible caution. We can leave it there.
It is a relief not to have the fear turned into a challenge.
Some ideas are easier to appreciate from a comfortable distance.
The frightening pitch has received a mutually agreed curtain call.
Agreement has saved us a very unnecessary argument with a bad idea.
A dramatic option is not automatically a useful one for our plan.
We are allowed to leave some kinds of thunder sleeping.
I appreciate the tutor finally hearing the practical objection.
I wonder whether anyone has ever looked more relieved by a declined lesson.

contexts.subject: The Explosion tutor finds the idea of using the move on a volcano thrilling.

Text_ExplosionTaught.text: Using EXPLOSION while on this\nvolcano…\pWhat a terrifying thrill!$

replies.text: An explosion on a volcano feels like adding an exclamation mark to another exclamation mark.
A volatile setting is a reason for caution, not evidence that a risky demonstration is appropriate.
A thrill is no reason to put people nearby at risk.
I would prefer the volcano to remain scenery rather than join the demonstration.
The setting already supplies enough heat and uncertainty for one visit.
The spectacle has become so ambitious that I would like to leave the audience.
The mountain is already doing an excellent job of seeming ominous.
We should account for the environment before considering a powerful move.
Sleeping fire needs no visitor enthusiastically knocking on its door.
That is a rather large risk to dress up as an exciting anecdote.
I would rather remember the view than a demonstration nobody needed.

contexts.subject: Copycat asks whether the player dislikes Mimic after the offer is declined.

replies.text: We can like an idea without signing up for every version of it.
Declining a lesson does not necessarily indicate dislike of the technique.
No need to turn the choice into a judgment about her favourite move.
I hope she does not hear the answer as a rejection of her.
Enjoying something and choosing it today are different questions.
The rejected offer has been mistaken for an unfavourable review of the whole concept.
A single no has been asked to explain a suspicious amount.
We may simply prefer the team's existing moves. There are several possibilities.
A reflection need not copy every choice to remain friendly.
She can keep her enthusiasm without making us justify different tastes.
I wonder whether she enjoys the move or making people react to it more.

contexts.subject: Copycat gleefully mimics the player's own thanks and conversation.

Text_MimicTaughtFemale.text:
{PLAYER}: Hi!
Thanks for what you did for us.\p{PLAYER}: Pardon?\p{PLAYER}: Is it really that fun to
copy what I say and do?\pCOPYCAT: You bet!
It's a scream!$

Text_MimicTaughtMale.text:
{PLAYER}: Hi!
Thanks for earlier!\p{PLAYER}: Pardon?\p{PLAYER}: Is it that fun to mimic my
every move?\pCOPYCAT: You bet!
It's a scream!$

replies.text: We have met a conversational echo that is thoroughly enjoying itself.
Her imitation depends on timing and observation as much as repeating the words.
She got the reaction she wanted. Hard to miss how pleased she is.
Hearing your own greeting come back must feel a little strange.
Even the thank-you has come back for a second helping.
The visitor has unexpectedly become the source material for the performance.
A mirror has developed opinions and found the whole situation hilarious.
Good mimicry takes careful observation of details people usually ignore.
A borrowed voice has returned wearing a mischievous smile.
She clearly enjoys catching the little details that make someone recognizable.
I wonder which gesture gave her the quickest way to imitate us.

contexts.subject: The Cape Brink tutor protests a rejected lesson and says she will persist.

Text_YouRejectIt.text: Gaah! You reject it?\nNo, I won't be dissuaded!$

replies.text: A dramatic protest does not make our answer less of an answer.
Her commitment to teaching does not override the learner's choice.
She can keep the offer. She needs to respect the refusal.
That is a lot of feeling to place on someone deciding about a lesson.
A willing pupil is worth waiting for rather than wearing down.
The mentor has responded to a declined role with an alarmingly forceful appeal.
Determination is less charming when aimed at someone else's boundaries.
She may care deeply about passing it on, but consent still matters.
An old wish should not become a hand gripping someone else's sleeve.
A graceful pause would do more for her cause than another protest.
I wonder whether the fear of losing the knowledge makes every refusal feel final to her.

contexts.subject: The Cape Brink tutor feels at peace after passing on all her knowledge.

Text_PassedOnEverythingIKnow.text: Gasp, gasp, gasp…\pI have no regrets now.\nI've passed on everything I know.\pNow I can live out my life knowing\nmy work is done.$

replies.text: Her knowledge has found somewhere new to live. I can see why she sounds relieved.
Teaching preserves a skill beyond one person's ability to continue practising it.
She finished something that mattered to her. Let her have the moment.
It sounds as though she has been waiting to take that breath for a long time.
There is comfort in knowing something precious will not end with you.
The lifelong work has found its next chapter in somebody else's hands.
An ending can be gentler when something important keeps going.
Passing on the method is a substantial achievement in its own right.
The old flame has caught another wick, and the room has not grown darker.
Her relief feels far more personal than a simple lesson completed.
I wonder who first trusted her with the knowledge she has now passed onward.

contexts.subject: The Cape Brink tutor urges careful use of the technique she entrusted to the player.

Text_MakeBestUseOfMove.text: I implore you to make the best\nuse of that move and gain power!$

replies.text: She has handed over something important and wants it treated as more than a novelty.
A learned technique becomes valuable through informed application rather than possession alone.
Use it thoughtfully. Power needs judgment beside it.
I can hear how much she wants the teaching to mean something beyond this visit.
Something entrusted to us deserves a bit of care in how we use it.
The mentor has requested a worthy future for her life's work.
A powerful gift can carry a quieter request for responsibility.
Understanding when to use it matters as much as knowing how.
What has been passed onward still asks for a careful hand.
She is asking us to respect the work, not merely admire the result.
I wonder what use of the technique would make her feel proudest.

contexts.subject: The Cape Brink tutor realizes the presented Pokemon is not the one she had hoped to teach.

replies.text: A hopeful guess has come back down to earth rather quietly.
She has corrected her initial assessment rather than insisting it must be right.
Wrong fit for the lesson. That does not make the Pokemon lesser.
The change in her voice sounds like a disappointment she knows is her own.
Not being right for one lesson is no criticism of the learner.
The anticipated apprentice has turned out to be a mistaken identification.
A small retreat from certainty is sometimes the most honest part of a conversation.
A specialized technique can have narrow requirements without judging overall ability.
A door that does not open for this visitor need not be a cruel one.
At least she takes back the assumption instead of blaming the Pokemon.
I wonder what small detail first made her think she had found the right pupil.

contexts.subject: The Cape Brink tutor says teaching relieved her and made her feel young again.

Text_FeelRejuvenated.text: After I passed on my knowledge to\nyou, I felt so much relief.\pIn fact, I feel rejuvenated,\nas if I were younger again!$

replies.text: The lesson seems to have taken a weight off her shoulders rather than years off the calendar.
Relief and renewed purpose can change how energetic a person feels.
Good to see her feeling lighter after all that worry.
She sounds as though she can finally enjoy having finished something.
A burden set down leaves room for a very different kind of day.
The veteran teacher has discovered that finishing her work need not mean finishing herself.
A good ending has unexpectedly offered her some room to begin again.
Passing knowledge onward can be energizing instead of merely exhausting.
Something long held has left her hands and returned as lightness.
The relief has made a warmer impression than any grand declaration could.
I wonder what she might feel like doing now that the worry is quieter.

contexts.subject: The Cape Brink tutor is moved that she lived to pass on the technique.

Text_TaughtMove.text: Gasp, gasp, gasp…\pI didn't think I could teach that\nmove while I still lived…$

replies.text: That lesson has been waiting inside a very long hope. No wonder she needs a breath.
A long-held uncertainty has been resolved through the successful transfer of a skill.
It meant a lot to her. Give her time to catch her breath.
I do not think this is a moment that needs us to fill the silence.
Some accomplishments deserve a seat and a quiet minute before anything else.
The triumph is not the spectacle of the move, but that she got to teach it at all.
A feared ending has been interrupted by something continuing.
The important result here is that the knowledge no longer rests with only one person.
A long-kept ember has finally found another place to burn.
Her relief makes the whole visit feel much more intimate than a routine lesson.
I wonder how many years she has imagined this particular moment.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man reassures the player that the deposited Pokemon is doing fine.

DayCare_Text_YourMonIsDoingFine.text: Ah, it's you! Good to see you.\nYour {STR_VAR_1}'s doing fine.$

replies.text: A small status report can be a very welcome thing when somebody else is watching your friend.
A routine reassurance, with no claim about growth or any specific change.
Good to hear they are doing all right.
Sometimes that is exactly the little bit of news you came back hoping for.
It is comforting to hear about the ordinary well-being, not only the results.
The caretaker has supplied the peaceful update every anxious visitor appreciates.
Nothing dramatic happening can be the nicest news available.
A simple check-in confirms the stay is proceeding normally.
A familiar life is carrying on gently while we are elsewhere.
A warm update makes the service feel a little more personal.
I wonder what the Pokemon has been enjoying while we have been away.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man cannot hand over the Egg until there is room in the party.

DayCare_Text_YouHaveNoRoomForIt.text: You have no room for it…\nCome back when you've made room.$

replies.text: A small passenger still needs a proper place before we take it along.
Party capacity must be resolved before the Egg can be transferred safely.
Make room first. The Egg can wait here.
There is no need to hurry the handover just because we came to collect it.
A bit of preparation makes carrying something delicate less awkward.
The new arrival is awaiting a suitable place in the travelling arrangement.
A practical delay, not a rejection of the little thing waiting.
We should sort the team before trying the collection again.
Something small can still ask for space that is truly its own.
It is better to leave with room prepared than juggle the problem on the doorstep.
I wonder how different the next leg of the journey will feel with an Egg along.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man agrees to keep the Egg after the player declines it.

replies.text: He has accepted the choice and kept the little passenger somewhere cared for.
The refusal has a clear resolution: the Day-Care man retains the Egg.
The choice is settled. No need to keep pressing it.
I am glad the conversation ends without making the refusal cruel.
Taking responsibility is a choice that should be made willingly.
The prospective new chapter has been left in its caretaker's hands.
An unaccepted beginning still belongs somewhere in the world.
A clear decision avoids leaving everyone uncertain about the handover.
Not every small life that crosses our road must travel under our roof.
A considerate response gives the decision a clean and respectful ending.
I wonder whether he often ends up caring for Eggs travellers choose not to take.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man introduces his work and directs service requests to his wife.

DayCare_Text_ImDaycareManSpeakToMyWife.text: I'm the DAY-CARE MAN.\pI help take care of the precious\nPOKéMON of TRAINERS.\pIf you'd like me to raise your\nPOKéMON, have a word with my wife.$

replies.text: He has supplied the important introduction and pointed us toward the actual arrangements.
A clear division of responsibilities makes it easier to know whom to ask.
His wife handles the arrangements. We know where to go.
It is nice to hear someone talk about the Pokemon as precious.
Care is easier to trust when the people doing it seem to value the guests.
The proprietor has introduced the household and correctly identified the booking desk.
A little practical information wrapped in a warm description of the work.
Clear handoffs are useful even in a service run by only two people.
A resting place begins to feel welcoming when its keeper speaks gently of its guests.
He sounds proud of helping without making himself the centre of the introduction.
I wonder how many travellers' Pokemon they have come to know over the years.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care man asks the player to care well for the Egg being handed over.

replies.text: A small bundle comes with a very ordinary and very important request.
Care during transport matters even before we know which Pokemon will emerge.
Keep it secure and travel thoughtfully.
It is a gentle little handover for something whose whole beginning is still ahead.
We can make room in the day for being careful rather than simply rushing onward.
An unknown new character has arrived with a caretaker's brief blessing.
The quiet part before an introduction can feel surprisingly full.
We should plan for a fragile passenger, not treat it like spare equipment.
A small closed world has been entrusted to our footsteps.
The request is simple enough that it deserves to be taken seriously.
I wonder which ordinary moment the Egg will choose to make memorable.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care service cannot complete the withdrawal because the player lacks the fee.

replies.text: The reunion has met a very unromantic number on the bill.
The stated service fee remains unmet, so the withdrawal has not completed.
We need the fee before collecting the Pokemon. No point arguing here.
It is a disappointing thing to find out when you came back to see them.
We should keep the collection cost in mind before spending elsewhere.
The heartfelt reunion has been postponed by the accounts department.
An ordinary bill can be a surprisingly effective plot obstacle.
We can plan the required money before trying the transaction again.
A practical debt stands in the space between arrival and reunion.
Better to understand the cost now than pretend the exchange happened.
I wonder how often travellers forget the fee while planning to come back.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care keeper closes the visit and leaves the service available for another time.

replies.text: A simple goodbye, with the next visit left comfortably possible.
The conversation has ended without implying any particular service was completed.
We can leave it there and decide later.
It is nice when a routine visit can end without any fuss.
There will be another chance if the service suits our plans.
The curtain falls on a perfectly ordinary visit, with no sequel demanded.
An uneventful ending can be a very pleasant thing.
We have time to consider the team before making another arrangement.
A door remains available without following us down the path.
A polite farewell asks very little and leaves a good impression.
I wonder what other travellers will be stopping in after us today.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care lady tells the player that her husband was looking for them.

DayCare_Text_HusbandWasLookingForYou.text: My husband was looking for you.$

replies.text: A small change of errand. The person we came to see knows who wants to see us.
The message gives us a specific person to check with rather than a vague hint.
We should ask him what he needs.
It sounds as though there is something waiting to be said, not something to guess at.
Best speak to him before heading off on the next stretch.
The household has supplied a tidy handoff to the next conversation.
A useful message, refreshingly free of elaborate mystery.
We can get the actual information directly from him.
An ordinary doorstep has become the beginning of a different conversation.
It is considerate of her to remember and pass that along.
I wonder whether he has been watching the road for us to return.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care keeper asks for party space before a deposited Pokemon can be returned.

DayCare_Text_YourPartyIsFull.text: Your POKéMON party is full.\nMake room, then come see me.$

Route5_PokemonDayCare_Text_YouveGotNoRoo.text: You can't take this POKéMON back\nif you've got no room for it.$

replies.text: We have arrived for a reunion with every travelling place already occupied.
The withdrawal requires a free party slot before it can complete.
Make room, then collect the Pokemon.
A short practical delay is better than an awkward handover.
We can sort the team calmly and come straight back.
The returning cast member needs somewhere to stand before joining the scene.
Even a happy reunion has its logistical details.
A quick team adjustment resolves the capacity issue.
The familiar companion is waiting for an actual place, not merely a wish.
Preparation would have made the visit smoother, but the fix is straightforward.
I wonder whether the Pokemon has already noticed us coming back to the door.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care keeper refuses a deposit that would leave the player without a Pokemon able to battle.

DayCare_Text_WhatWillYouBattleWith.text: If you leave me that POKéMON,\nwhat will you battle with?\pCome back another time.$

Route5_PokemonDayCare_Text_WhatWillYouBa.text: If you leave me that POKéMON,\nwhat will you battle with?$

replies.text: Leaving every capable partner behind would make the next challenge rather one-sided.
The remaining team needs at least one Pokemon able to handle a battle.
Keep a capable partner with us. Sensible boundary.
It is a practical kindness to catch that before we leave.
A care arrangement should not leave the rest of the journey unprepared.
The proposed boarding arrangement has accidentally removed the expedition's entire defence.
Some helpful plans need someone to point out the obvious missing piece.
Check the remaining team, not only the Pokemon we want to leave.
A road asks for company that can still help us meet what comes.
A well-timed refusal can be more useful than an unquestioning yes.
I am glad someone checked what our team would look like after the choice.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care keeper will not accept the player's only Pokemon.

DayCare_Text_YouHaveJustOneMon.text: Oh? But you have just one\nPOKéMON.\pCome back another time.$

Route5_PokemonDayCare_Text_OnlyHaveOneMo.text: Oh? You only have one POKéMON\nwith you.$

replies.text: The only travel buddy cannot stay here while we go off being an entire expedition alone.
Retaining a travelling partner is a basic requirement before making a deposit.
We need someone with us on the road. Come back with another partner first.
It would feel strange to leave with nobody beside us.
We should prepare the rest of the team before arranging a stay.
The guest list has attempted to absorb the entire travelling cast.
A very small headcount can create a very obvious practical problem.
The service can wait until our travelling team has another eligible member.
An empty road is not what this care arrangement is meant to give us.
The rule is easy to understand once you picture the walk away.
I wonder how many first-time visitors only realize that at this exact moment.

contexts.subject: The Route 5 keeper completes a deposit and asks the player to return after some time.

Route5_PokemonDayCare_Text_ComeSeeMeInAW.text: Come see me in a while.$

replies.text: A little stay has begun. We can let the caretaker actually have some time to do the job.
The deposit is followed by a clear invitation to return after a suitable interval.
They are in his care now. We can check back later.
Walking away can feel odd even when the arrangement is a good one.
We can plan a return without hovering on the doorstep.
A temporary farewell, with the next meeting built gently into it.
A small absence can be ordinary without feeling entirely ordinary.
Let the arrangement run for a while before evaluating the result.
One set of footsteps rests here while the road keeps ours for a little longer.
A clear return invitation makes the parting feel less abrupt.
I wonder what new little habits the Pokemon will have picked up when we return.

contexts.subject: The laboratory founder photograph identifies Dr. Fuji.

CinnabarIsland_PokemonLab_Entrance_Text_.text: A photo of the LAB's founder…\nDR. FUJI?!$

replies.text: Mr. Fuji helped start this place? He has more chapters than I knew.
The founder's photograph connects his name to this laboratory. That is a useful fact, not his whole history.
So he helped build this place. There is a lot we have not asked him.
I know him through what he does now. This is a much earlier verse.
People can spend years building something before we ever learn their name.
We have found an earlier chapter with a surprisingly familiar face.
A familiar face in an unfamiliar part of his life.
Founding a laboratory takes more than knowing how to use one. Interesting background.
Some roots run farther than the branches we first notice.
Imagine every person we meet having a whole life we have barely opened.
I would like to know who took this picture and what the lab looked like that day.

contexts.subject: An amber pipe is displayed in the research room.

replies.text: Very pretty. Also not something I should test by blowing into it.
Amber used as a crafted object rather than a specimen. I wonder about its provenance.
Look with your eyes. It is still somebody else's property.
I expected notes and equipment. This feels like a personal detail.
That has the look of something whose owner knows exactly where it belongs.
One small object can make a room belong to a person rather than a profession.
An old material given a very particular purpose.
Interesting material choice. I would ask before making assumptions about its use.
A little piece of resin with another life folded around it.
It is a distinctive thing to keep in a research room. Someone chose it.
The small objects people keep often tell a different story from the plaques.

contexts.subject: Researchers name three legendary birds, admit their locations are unknown and plan to explore the cavern near Cerulean.

CinnabarIsland_PokemonLab_ResearchRoom_T.text:
There's an e-mail message.\p… … …\pThere are three legendary bird
POKéMON.\pThey are ARTICUNO, ZAPDOS, and
MOLTRES.\pTheir whereabouts are unknown.\pWe plan to explore the cavern
close to CERULEAN.\pFrom: POKéMON RESEARCH TEAM…$

replies.text: They wrote down what they do not know. That feels like a good start for an adventure.
The message separates known names from unknown locations. Their Cerulean expedition is a plan, not a confirmed sighting.
Three birds. No confirmed locations. Do not turn that into a promise about the cavern.
There is something exciting about a message that ends with people deciding to go look.
We would need supplies for an expedition, not just enthusiasm and a very impressive bird list.
A lead, three legends and a great deal left to discover. An excellent opening, provided we pack.
The unknown is doing quite a lot of work in that message.
Their next step is field observation. Good. A theory needs something to push back against it.
Three names, and the world still keeping their whereabouts to itself.
I appreciate a report that does not pretend a guess is a discovery.
I want to see what their field notes say when they return. Especially what surprised them.

contexts.subject: A carefully arranged stone cairn bears Tectonix name.

FiveIsland_MemorialPillar_Text_HereLiesT.text: Boulders and rocks are neatly piled\nup as a cairn.\p“Here lies TECTONIX” is engraved\non a boulder.$

replies.text: They took time to place every stone. We can take a little time to be quiet.
The careful arrangement says this place is tended. We should respect it.
Mind where you step. This matters to someone.
We do not have to fill this silence.
A name, a place, and somebody making sure neither is forgotten.
We arrived at the edge of somebody else's grief. We should enter gently.
A name kept above ground by patient hands.
Leave the cairn exactly as we found it.
The stones are doing the work of remembering. Let them.
There is no clever thing we need to say here.
I can remember this place without taking anything from its quiet.

contexts.subject: A can of lemonade has been left at Tectonix grave.

FiveIsland_MemorialPillar_Text_HereLiesT.text: “Here lies TECTONIX” is engraved\non a boulder.\pThere is a LEMONADE placed as an\noffering in front of the grave.$

replies.text: Somebody remembered a favorite drink. That is a very particular kind of love.
The offering preserves a personal detail. Remembering someone can be that specific.
Leave the can there. It belongs to this moment.
A favorite drink can say more than a grand speech.
Knowing what someone liked to drink means you shared ordinary days with them.
The smallest detail here makes the name feel like someone who was known.
An ordinary can, carrying more than it was made to hold.
We should not tidy away something that was deliberately left.
A little sweetness offered across a distance no road can cross.
It is such a familiar way to care for somebody. That is what makes it hurt.
I hope whoever left it knows the gesture can matter even without an audience.

contexts.subject: Many Pokemon are confined in a warehouse pen.

FiveIsland_RocketWarehouse_Text_ManyMons.text: There are many POKéMON locked\naway in the pen…$

replies.text: They should not have to wait in here wondering what happens next.
Confinement in this warehouse is a welfare concern. We should look for a safe way to release them.
Find the lock. Stay alert for anyone guarding it.
They are living creatures. The room is treating them like stock.
We need to help them, not stand here deciding how awful this is.
Somebody has mistaken a collection of lives for an inventory.
A room full of reasons to stop being patient with Rocket.
Assess the door and the surroundings. Opening it safely is the priority.
No creature belongs in a cage simply because someone found a buyer.
Let us be useful to them. They do not need us to make a speech.
I want the next thing they see outside that pen to be a safe way out.

contexts.subject: The pen is unlocked and the Pokemon appear to have escaped.

FiveIsland_RocketWarehouse_Text_PenUnloc.text: The pen door is unlocked.\nThe POKéMON appear to have fled.$

replies.text: Empty in the best possible way. I hope they found somewhere safe.
The open door and empty pen indicate they left. Their safety beyond it is still unknown.
Good. Keep the exit clear in case any come back.
For once, an empty room is the hopeful part.
No one left inside. That is a relief worth taking a breath for.
An absence with a much better story behind it.
The cage has finally become a useless piece of furniture.
Door unlocked, occupants gone. Do not secure it again.
The room has lost its prisoners. May the paths outside be kinder.
I am glad there is nobody here for us to worry at through the bars.
I wish we could see where they went. For now, having left is enough.

contexts.subject: A technical report concerns magnetic waves and Pokemon evolution; the player cannot understand it.

FiveIsland_RocketWarehouse_Text_ReportWi.text: A report with graphs and text is on\nthe PC monitor.\p“The Influence of Magnetic Waves\non POKéMON Evolution”…\p… … … … … …\pIt's too difficult to understand…$

replies.text: I recognize the words separately. Together they have formed a very tall fence.
The title concerns magnetic waves and evolution. We should not claim to understand methods we have not evaluated.
We cannot read enough of it to know what they did. Remember where it is.
It is unsettling to find careful work in a place used so carelessly.
A complicated report is not proof that the people using it have good intentions.
An impressive stack of graphs can still belong to a terrible enterprise.
The graphs are very tidy. That makes the rest of this place no better.
Technical detail requires review. The title alone cannot establish a result.
A difficult page does not become wise merely because we cannot read it.
I refuse to let a graph make me forget the pen in the next part of this warehouse.
Someone who understands the subject should examine this. We should preserve the evidence.

contexts.subject: Pokemon photographs and fossils are displayed together in the wardens house.

FuchsiaCity_WardensHouse_Text_MonPhotosF.text: POKéMON photos and fossils are on\ndisplay.$

replies.text: Somebody has been collecting reasons to be amazed for a very long time.
Living observations and ancient remains, side by side. A nice reminder of the timescale involved.
A careful collection. Leave it that way.
There are so many different kinds of memory in one display.
I like a house that makes room for things its owner cares about.
A personal collection with a much larger world behind every piece.
Life, held still in two very different ways.
Photographs preserve appearances; fossils preserve physical traces. Useful companions.
A wall where recent days and very old years can sit together.
This feels collected with interest rather than arranged to impress visitors.
I would love to hear the story behind the oldest photograph here.

contexts.subject: Old Pokemon merchandise is kept on display.

replies.text: Somebody kept their favorites. Even the slightly wobbly-looking ones.
Age alone does not explain why these were kept. Personal attachment often does.
If it matters to the owner, it does not need to impress us.
I like things that stayed loved after they stopped being new.
You can tell a lot about a kitchen from the mug nobody will replace. This feels similar.
A modest museum of things that once made somebody happy.
Yesterday's little treasures, spared the indignity of being thrown away.
Older designs can be interesting. So can the reasons someone preserves them.
A shelf can be an anchor for a younger version of yourself.
I would absolutely keep something ridiculous for sentimental reasons. I have no defense.
The wear is part of the story. I hope nobody tries to make everything look new.

contexts.subject: The magazine prize drawing application has already been clipped out.

LavenderTown_VolunteerPokemonHouse_Text_.text: POKéMON FAN MAGAZINE\nMonthly Grand Prize Drawing!\pThe application form is…\pGone! It's been clipped out.\nSomeone must have applied already.$

replies.text: Somebody has already sent their little rectangle of hope.
The missing form suggests an entry was submitted. It tells us nothing about the result.
Someone beat us to the form. Good luck to them.
I hope waiting for the answer gives them something nice to look forward to.
No form left. We can at least avoid spilling anything on the rest of the magazine.
A tiny subplot has departed through the post.
A neat little hole where somebody put their optimism.
Application removed. Looking through the remaining pages will not produce another one.
A small wish has left this shelf and gone traveling.
Whoever clipped it out was very ready to win. I respect the enthusiasm.
I wonder whether they chose carefully or filled it in the moment they saw it.

contexts.subject: A Mt Moon sign warns visitors that Zubat feeds on blood.

replies.text: Useful warning. I would prefer to remain an unsuitable snack.
A feeding adaptation, described with considerably more alarm than context.
Stay aware of the Zubat. No need to frighten every one we see.
That sign is not doing much for their public image.
We are not on the menu. Let us keep it that way without bothering them.
A factual warning delivered like a poster for a very small horror film.
The cave has posted its dietary preferences.
Know the local wildlife and avoid unnecessary contact. Straightforward advice.
A cave creature being a cave creature. We are the visitors.
Imagine your entire introduction to strangers being the least flattering thing about lunch.
I would like to learn how they live here, from a sensible distance.

contexts.subject: A self-proclaimed expert recommends enjoying Pokemon trades with friends.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_RoofRoom_Text_T.text:
There is nothing that I don't know,
like I wrote on the blackboard.\pI know about the world of POKéMON
in your GAME BOY ADVANCE!\pGet together with your friends and
enjoy trading POKéMON!$

replies.text: Nothing he does not know? I could probably confuse him with a sufficiently ordinary sandwich.
The trading advice is sensible. The claim of unlimited knowledge is less defensible.
Useful advice can survive a little less boasting.
I like the part about enjoying something with friends.
Shared interests make good reasons to spend an afternoon together.
The authority has announced his expertise and generously allowed the audience to mingle.
Knowing everything would leave a person very little to be curious about.
Trading with friends can turn separate discoveries into a shared project.
A full cup is not always evidence of an endless well.
The confidence is rather large, but the social advice has some charm.
I wonder which question he most enjoys being asked.

contexts.subject: A visitor recommends the Union Room as a chance to meet new friends.

CinnabarIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Vis.text:
Do you have lots of friends?\pLinking up with the usual friends
is fun, of course.\pBut how about visiting the
UNION ROOM every so often?\pWho knows, you may end up making
new friends.\pI think it would be worth your time
to check the UNION ROOM.$

replies.text: A room where today's stranger might become tomorrow's familiar wave. That sounds nice.
A shared activity can make meeting unfamiliar people feel more approachable.
We can have a look when we feel like company.
Knowing there is a reason to start talking makes a new room less frightening.
There is room for new friends without making old ones any less important.
The established cast need not be the final cast of the journey.
A meeting place can do some of the awkward introductory work for everyone.
A common interest gives the first conversation something practical to begin with.
An unfamiliar doorway may hold a voice that eventually feels familiar.
A little openness can make a familiar routine feel fresh again.
I wonder what first brings people in, and what makes them return.

contexts.subject: Bill accepts that the player is not ready to leave on the island trip.

CinnabarIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_OhN.text: Oh, you're still not done yet?$

replies.text: A trip can wait while the unfinished things stop waving at us from the doorstep.
Deferring departure allows existing plans to be completed before adding another journey.
We will go when we are ready. Good that he understands.
It is easier to enjoy an invitation when there is room to finish saying goodbye first.
A little time to prepare can make the actual trip much smoother.
The next chapter has agreed to wait for the loose ends to be tied.
An invitation is kinder when it does not become a countdown.
We can check the team and supplies before choosing to depart.
A waiting boat need not make every other task suddenly urgent.
It is nice when someone hears not yet as a real answer.
I wonder which last errand we will remember just before we finally set off.

contexts.subject: The fossil researcher is disappointed when the player declines the offer.

replies.text: The scientist has discovered that enthusiasm is not a substitute for permission.
A declined offer remains a valid choice, even when the researcher is disappointed.
No is enough. We need not make the experiment happen today.
It is all right to leave something unusual undecided for a while.
A curious opportunity deserves thought rather than being accepted to avoid awkwardness.
The proposed marvel has encountered the entirely ordinary right to decline.
A disappointing answer is still an answer, not a research obstacle to overcome.
We can return if the proposal fits our plans later.
Some doors can remain closed without being lost forever.
His disappointment does not need to become our responsibility.
I wonder whether he hears many refusals with an offer that unusual.

contexts.subject: A traveller found Rock Tunnel dark and frightening and wishes for Flash.

DiglettsCave_NorthEntrance_RockTunnelPit.text: I went inside ROCK TUNNEL, but it's\npitch-black and scary in there.\pIf I could get a POKéMON to use\nFLASH and light it up…$

replies.text: A tunnel is much less inviting when the dark seems to have arrived before you.
Limited visibility makes navigation and identifying hazards substantially harder.
Get a reliable way to see before entering. No need to stumble through.
I understand feeling frightened when you cannot tell what the next sound belongs to.
Preparing for the darkness is better than hoping nerves will do the lighting.
The traveller has delivered an unusually persuasive review of inadequate illumination.
Darkness is quite capable of making an ordinary rock feel personally ominous.
A light source turns many frightening unknowns back into manageable terrain.
An unseen path asks too much trust from a tired pair of feet.
There is nothing embarrassing about wanting to see where you are going.
I wonder how far into the tunnel the traveller got before deciding to turn back.

contexts.subject: The sticker collector asks for a new achievement rather than hearing the same record again.

FourIsland_House2_Text_ComeBackWithBette.text: Hmm…\pCome back with a better story next\ntime, okay?$
Hmm…\pCome back with a better story next\ntime, okay?$
Hmm…\pCome back with a better story next\ntime, okay?$

replies.text: The sticker economy requires fresh bragging material. Repeats do not pass inspection.
The claimed achievement has not increased beyond the record already recognized.
Nothing new for him to reward. We can leave it there.
An old achievement still matters even when it no longer earns another sticker.
We need not turn every good memory into a fresh transaction.
The audience has requested new material before issuing another review sticker.
A familiar triumph has become yesterday's news in a remarkably tiny awards office.
A one-time reward system needs to distinguish a new record from a repeated claim.
Yesterday's bright thing does not dim because today's drawer stays shut.
He could ask for an update with a little less dismissal of what came before.
I wonder whether he enjoys the stories or handing out recognition more.

contexts.subject: The sticker collector calls the player a living legend and has no further stickers to offer.

FourIsland_House2_Text_LivingLegendEggs.text: Oh, no, no can do.\pYou're practically a living legend.\nI have no SITCKERS left to give.$

FourIsland_House2_Text_LivingLegendHoF.text: Oh, no, no can do.\pYou're practically a living legend.\nI have no SITCKERS left to give.$

FourIsland_House2_Text_LivingLegendLinkW.text: Oh, no, no can do.\pYou're practically a living legend.\nI have no SITCKERS left to give.$

replies.text: We have outgrown the available sticker supply. A very specific sort of fame.
The reward scheme has reached its upper limit; the achievement exceeds any remaining award.
No more prizes needed. The work still happened.
Living legend is a very large phrase to be handed in such a small room.
It is all right for a milestone to stand on its own without another prize.
The awards committee has exhausted its stationery and resorted to extravagant acclaim.
A career has become too large for its designated decorative label.
A reward system can end without making further achievements meaningless.
The small drawer is empty; the story has not become smaller to fit it.
There is something charming about running out of decoration before running out of admiration.
I wonder how many people have ever reached the end of his sticker collection.

contexts.subject: The sticker collector invites a future story about something the player has accomplished.

FourIsland_House2_Text_BragAboutSomethin.text: Brag about something for me.\nI'll give you a STICKER.$

FourIsland_House2_Text_GiveYouStickerIfY.text:
Oh, excellent!
You've come to the right place!\pLook, look! See? See?
These are my STICKERS!\lLook how many I got!\pI bet you want some.
I bet you do!\pI'll give a STICKER if you can tell
me something awesome about\lyourself.\pWhat will you brag about?$

replies.text: A man has built a tiny awards ceremony out of wanting to hear people boast.
The offer establishes a future reward, not an achievement already verified today.
We can come back with a real accomplishment. No need to invent one.
It is an unusual way of inviting someone to talk about what they are proud of.
A little recognition can make someone want to share a good story.
A willing audience and adhesive applause. The arrangement has a certain elegance.
Bragging has found a very modest patron of the arts.
We should understand what he counts before making the reward the goal.
A small bright square is waiting for a story worth carrying.
He clearly enjoys giving people a reason to talk about themselves.
I wonder which tale he would enjoy even if there were no sticker left to give.

contexts.subject: A reader is surprised that the newest Pokemon Journal has not reached Four Island.

FourIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_NewPoke.text: What's this?\pThe new POKéMON JOURNAL hasn't\narrived on this island?$

replies.text: The latest news has apparently decided to take a slower boat.
Distribution delays are more noticeable when a reader is expecting a regular arrival.
It will arrive when it arrives. No reason to blame the people here.
Waiting for the next issue can make a small delay feel strangely long.
There is a particular disappointment in looking for something familiar and finding an empty place.
The devoted audience has encountered an unscheduled gap in publication.
The island is being made to practise patience by the postal schedule.
Distance makes a regular delivery schedule harder to keep perfectly even.
News travels less quickly than the wish to read it.
The surprise tells me the journal is a real part of this reader's routine.
I wonder what feature they were most looking forward to reading.

contexts.subject: A defeated challenger explains that a powerful Fighting team was not enough against Agatha.

IndigoPlateau_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Agat.text:
AGATHA's GHOST-type POKéMON are
horrifically terrifying in toughness.\pI took my FIGHTING-type POKéMON
and raised them to the max.\pI went at AGATHA feeling pretty
confident, but she whupped us.\pThat old lady's also got a really
short fuse, too.\pIt doesn't take anything to get
that scary lady hollering.$

replies.text: All that muscle met a problem it could not solve by being more muscle.
The result illustrates why strength alone cannot replace attention to type interactions.
A hard lesson. Adjust the plan instead of only pushing the same team harder.
It sounds rough to arrive that confident and leave so shaken.
Preparation includes knowing what the team will struggle to handle.
A carefully trained cast has discovered that the script asks for a different approach.
Confidence had an unpleasant appointment with a mismatch.
Review the matchup before adding more effort to the same plan.
Force can meet a door that opens only to a different question.
Blaming Agatha's temper will not do much to repair the battle plan.
I wonder which moment made the challenger realize the expected advantage was not there.

contexts.subject: A visitor has heard that Lance has a cousin who leads a distant Gym.

IndigoPlateau_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Lanc.text: Maybe becoming an ELITE FOUR\nmember is in the blood.\pFrom what I've heard, LANCE has\na cousin who's a GYM LEADER\lsomewhere far away.$

replies.text: An impressive family anecdote, though I expect both cousins have done a fair bit of work.
A family connection does not establish that skill is inherited rather than developed.
A strong relative does not do the training for you.
I wonder whether they get to talk about ordinary things when they meet.
A family can share an interest without every accomplishment coming from the same place.
The rumour has supplied a distant relative and immediately drafted a theory of greatness.
A bloodline is a very tidy explanation for something that usually takes untidy effort.
Shared background could matter, but it would not tell us the whole story.
Two strong branches do not show us all the weather the tree endured.
I would rather hear about their work than reduce them both to a surname.
I wonder which of them first made the other interested in serious battling.

contexts.subject: A traveller sold a Nugget for five thousand because it had no practical use to them.

Route10_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_NuggetUsel.text: A NUGGET is totally useless.\nSo I sold it for ¥5000.$

replies.text: A useless thing that becomes five thousand coins has discovered a rather useful second career.
Utility depends on context. A valuable material need not have a direct travelling use.
Sold something unnecessary for money they could use. Sensible enough.
It is funny how a thing can mean nothing to one person and quite a lot to another.
That could buy a very respectable amount of travelling supplies.
The allegedly useless object has financed the next chapter admirably.
A little gold has declined employment as a burden and applied to become money instead.
Converting an unused resource into something practical is a sound choice.
Value sometimes lives in what a thing can become rather than what it does in your hand.
Knowing what you actually need is better than carrying something simply because it shines.
I wonder whether the traveller already knows what they want to spend it on.

contexts.subject: A trainer explains that Pokemon types have different matchup strengths and weaknesses.

Route10_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_EveryTypeS.text: The types of POKéMON match up\ndifferently with each other.\pEvery type is stronger than some\ntypes and weaker than others.$

replies.text: There is usually another side to the type chart waiting to spoil a confident grin.
Matchups depend on the specific types involved; no single broad advantage answers every situation.
Know the opponent before assuming the matchup favours us.
It helps to remember that a difficult match is not proof the team is bad.
A different approach can help more than insisting on the same advantage.
The strongest-looking entrance can still meet an awkwardly chosen opponent.
A useful reminder that superiority rarely remains universal for long.
Coverage and alternatives make a team less dependent on one favourable matchup.
Every familiar strength casts a shape that something else can step around.
Good advice, provided we keep room for the exceptions in an actual matchup.
I wonder which unexpected type interaction first made the lesson stick.

contexts.subject: A traveller repeats a rumour that ghosts haunt Lavender Town.

Route10_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_HeardGhost.text: I heard that ghosts haunt\nLAVENDER TOWN.$

replies.text: A town can collect a lot of spooky introductions before you have even reached its sign.
That is a report of a rumour, not direct evidence about what we will encounter.
We can see for ourselves and treat the people there respectfully.
I hope the rumour does not make visitors forget it is somebody's home.
A place deserves more than being treated as a frightening story over lunch.
The town's reputation has arrived ahead of the town itself.
A haunting is a very efficient way for a place to occupy people's imaginations.
We should distinguish what people have seen from what they have heard repeated.
Some places carry both grief and stories. Best not mistake one for entertainment.
Curiosity travels better when it brings decent manners with it.
I wonder who first told the story and what they were actually trying to describe.

contexts.subject: A gate visitor is surprised and impressed that the player found a way in.

replies.text: We have earned a small compliment for the sophisticated technique of getting here.
The surprise suggests the approach is less obvious than the destination makes it look.
We found the way. Nice that someone noticed.
It is a small thing, but being recognized for figuring it out feels good.
Sometimes arriving is an accomplishment before anything else happens.
The entrance has received a favourable review from its accidental audience.
A little recognition for the journey instead of only the destination.
An indirect route can reward a bit of practical problem-solving.
A threshold can mark more effort than the room beyond it suggests.
An honest, surprised compliment can be rather charming.
I wonder how many travellers miss the approach entirely.

contexts.subject: A local says strong Water teams gather here and that Misty trains in the area.

Route20_Text_MistyTrainsHere.text: Strong TRAINERS and WATER POKéMON\nare common sights in these parts.\pThey say that MISTY of the\nCERULEAN GYM trains here.$

replies.text: A good seaside training spot apparently has a reputation among people with very splashy teams.
Suitable habitats can attract both particular Pokemon and trainers specializing in them.
A useful warning about the sort of matches we may meet.
It is nice to imagine her having a familiar place to practise away from the Gym.
Worth preparing for Water teams before choosing challenges along this coast.
The stretch of sea has secured a distinguished professional endorsement.
A place can acquire character from the people who keep returning to it.
The terrain makes it sensible to anticipate Water specialists here.
A shoreline holds its regular visitors as well as its tides.
I like hearing about the work behind a Gym Leader's polished public role.
I wonder which part of the coast she finds best for training.

contexts.subject: A local describes the cape as a date spot and says Misty has hopes for it.

Route25_Text_MistyHighHopesAboutThisPlac.text: This cape is a famous date spot.\pMISTY, the GYM LEADER, has high\nhopes about this place.$

replies.text: The cape has a reputation for romance and apparently a very optimistic local supporter.
Its reputation tells us how people use the place, not what every visitor must want from it.
A pleasant view works fine without anyone arranging our plans.
It does seem like the sort of place people might remember visiting together.
A good place can give people a reason to linger after the walk.
The scenery has been confidently assigned a romantic genre.
A quiet view has somehow become responsible for several people's expectations.
A welcoming spot can serve plenty of purposes beyond its advertised one.
The water does not mind whether the people watching it arrived as a pair.
A little local hope can make a place feel fondly looked after.
I wonder which ordinary detail makes the cape memorable to the people who return.

contexts.subject: A man assumes the cape should only be visited as a couple.

Route25_Text_AreYouHereAlone.text: Hello, are you here alone?\pIf you're out at CERULEAN's cape…\nWell, it should be as a couple.$

replies.text: The cape has not asked us for a second ticket to enjoy the view.
A reputation as a date spot does not exclude other perfectly valid reasons to visit.
We can be here however we like. It is a view, not a requirement.
Sometimes a quiet walk is exactly the company a person wants.
There is nothing wrong with enjoying a pleasant place on your own terms.
The self-appointed curator has mistaken a popular genre for an admission rule.
A solitary visitor is not a failed couple. Remarkable that this needs saying.
A place can support more than one use without needing redesign.
The sea has no particular opinion about how many people arrive together.
A friendly question becomes less friendly when it tells us which answer is acceptable.
I would rather ask what someone likes about the cape than whether they came correctly.

contexts.subject: Bill invites the player to view his rare Pokemon collection on the PC.

Route25_SeaCottage_Text_CheckOutRareMons.text: BILL: Feel like checking out some\nof my rare POKéMON on my PC?\pGo on, check out my PC.$

replies.text: Bill has reached the delighted host stage of showing us his favourite things.
A collection can be especially informative when its curator explains what makes each entry notable.
A generous invitation. We can take a look when we like.
It is sweet how pleased he is to share the interest itself.
Somebody happily showing you a collection can make a short visit stretch pleasantly.
The curator has opened the private exhibition to a very small visiting audience.
Enthusiasm is often more interesting than the impressive thing it is pointing at.
I would enjoy comparing the details Bill considers unusual.
A person's favourite things make little windows into how they see the world.
The collection matters to him, and he trusts a visitor enough to share it.
I wonder which entry he would choose first if we asked him to explain just one.

contexts.subject: Bill prefers research to a party and invites the player to enjoy the S.S. Anne in his place.

Route25_SeaCottage_Text_SSAnnePartyYouGo.text:
That cruise ship S.S. ANNE is in
VERMILION CITY.\pI hear there are lots of TRAINERS
on board, too.\pThey invited me to their party, but
I can't stand fancy do's.\pWhy don't you go instead of me?
Go on and have a good time.$

replies.text: He has found the elegant solution of not attending the party he does not want to attend.
He recognizes his own preference and offers the opportunity to someone who may enjoy it more.
Fair arrangement. He can keep working while we decide about the ship.
I appreciate someone admitting a party is not where he would rather be.
A good invitation does not have to be enjoyed by the person who first received it.
The reluctant guest has delegated his society appearance with admirable efficiency.
A party avoided can be an excellent evening, from a certain point of view.
Different people can find the same opportunity useful in entirely different ways.
One person's unwanted crowd becomes another person's open doorway.
Knowing what suits you is rather more appealing than attending out of obligation.
I wonder whether Bill feels relieved the moment somebody else agrees to consider it.

contexts.subject: The Magikarp seller firmly refuses refunds after the sale.

Route4_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_IDontGiveRe.text: MAN: Well, I don't give refunds.\nYou knew what you were getting!$

replies.text: The salesman's friendliness has developed a very abrupt financial boundary.
The statement establishes his refund policy, not whether the purchase was good value.
The sale is done. The Pokemon still deserves proper care.
I hope any frustration stays with the seller rather than the Magikarp.
A living companion should not become the target of buyer's regret.
The promotional warmth has ended precisely where the money changed hands.
A remarkably brisk closing of the door behind the customer.
We can learn from the transaction without treating the Pokemon as a faulty component.
An awkward bargain has still brought a life within our care.
A clear policy would have looked better before the persuasive speech.
I wonder how differently he sounds when the next customer walks up.

contexts.subject: The Magikarp seller claims a declined sale was a special favour.

Route4_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_OnlyDoingTh.text: No? You say no? I'm only doing this\nas a favor to you!$

replies.text: A favour that comes with a price and protests when declined is doing some suspicious stretching.
Describing a transaction as a favour does not establish that it benefits the buyer.
We declined. His sales pitch does not get to turn that into a debt.
I dislike being asked to feel guilty for deciding not to buy something.
A real kindness should survive the other person not wanting it.
The merchant has dressed the invoice as generosity and demanded applause.
An unaccepted bargain has wounded a very commercial sort of benevolence.
We should judge the offer by its actual terms rather than the seller's chosen label.
A gift-shaped shadow does not make the coin in his hand disappear.
How tiresome to make refusing a purchase sound like rejecting someone's kindness.
I wonder how many travellers hear that same supposedly personal favour.

contexts.subject: A reader is troubled by reports of Rocket attacks on Cerulean residents.

Route4_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_TeamRocketA.text: TEAM ROCKET attacks CERULEAN\ncitizens…\pNot a day goes by without TEAM\nROCKET being in the news.$

replies.text: That is not the sort of familiar face anybody wants appearing in the news every day.
Repeated reports suggest a serious ongoing problem, though this reader is citing the news.
People should be able to live there without being threatened.
It must be tiring to keep seeing your town described through what is hurting it.
I hope the residents have people nearby they can rely on.
