A peaceful spot can make a visit feel like a proper break.
An obscure address may be a privacy preference or a personal challenge.
Some of us enjoy having neighbors at a geographically respectful distance.
Hard to find can mean fewer interruptions during a project.
A hidden place may simply give its owner room to breathe.
Privacy can be part of how someone chooses a place.
I would rather ask the owner than decide what the hiding means.

contexts.subject: A base owner enjoys favorite decorations, a favorite Pokemon and steady growth.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer4PreChampion.text: I found a spot I liked, and I did it up\nwith my favorite decorations.\pI raise my favorite POKéMON and grow\nstronger with it.\pEvery day is a great day.$

replies.text: Favorite place, favorite stuff, favorite friend. A very strong good-day recipe.
A pleasing environment and a valued partner make a consistent routine easier.
They built a life they like. Good for them.
That sounds lovely in a very ordinary, attainable way.
A comfortable room and a happy partner can make a whole day.
A remarkably satisfying life assembled from a few well chosen favorites.
They have solved daily happiness without requiring a very large building.
A personalized workspace and a shared goal. Excellent starting conditions.
Some days grow good through small things tended well.
A place that fits your taste can make everything else sit better.
I would enjoy hearing which part they look forward to each morning.

contexts.subject: A base owner prefers this location despite the many other places available.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer5PreChampion.text: There're a lot of places where you can\nmake a SECRET BASE.\pBut I like this spot best.\nDon't you think it's nice?$

replies.text: So many possibilities, and this one felt right. The spot has a fan.
A favorite need not be the only suitable option to be a good choice.
They like it here. That is enough reason.
I like how pleased they sound when they show it.
The best place is often the one you actually enjoy coming back to.
The search is over, and the winning location receives a glowing introduction.
An entirely biased review from someone with excellent grounds for enjoying it.
I would ask which feature matters most to them.
A place becomes special through being chosen and returned to.
Taste is personal. Their confidence makes the place feel welcoming.
I would look for the detail that made them choose it.

contexts.subject: A base owner welcomes the player to a secret laboratory for battle research.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer6PreChampion.text: Welcome to my POKéMON LAB.\pI carry out research on battling in\nsecrecy.$

replies.text: A secret lab with a welcome speech. The secrecy is feeling sociable today.
An informal research space can be useful, provided the observations are careful.
Keep the research safe for the partners involved.
I like a small quiet place to work on an idea.
Their partner should enjoy the routine as much as the researcher.
A confidential institution has issued an unexpectedly cordial press release.
The laboratory's secrecy has survived precisely until our arrival.
I would like to see what they record after each practice match.
A private place can give curiosity room to settle.
A laboratory with a very personal choice of surroundings.
I would ask which battle question they are working on now.

contexts.subject: A base owner equally enjoys shopping for decor and raising Pokemon.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer7PreChampion.text: I simply adore shopping for decorations\nand furniture.\pI also love raising POKéMON just\nas much.$

replies.text: Decorating the base and raising friends. Hopefully the friends approve of the cushions.
Two different interests can make a nicely balanced routine.
Make the place comfortable for the Pokemon too.
It sounds like they enjoy making a life around both.
A well loved partner and a welcoming room go together nicely.
A host equally devoted to the residents and the scenery around them.
They have found two hobbies that both demand a surprising amount of floor space.
Furnishing a place is more interesting when you know who will use it.
A room can grow kinder as we learn the habits of those sharing it.
Finally, someone who understands the joy of choosing a good chair.
I would ask which piece of furniture their Pokemon likes best.

contexts.subject: A base owner proposes a friendly race to acquire nicer decorations and furniture.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer8PreChampion.text: People have told me that you can get\ndecorations in several ways.\pWe should have a race to see who can\nget nicer decorations and furniture!$

replies.text: A furniture race! I hope the chairs are allowed to finish sitting down.
A friendly comparison could introduce us to different sources and styles.
Keep it friendly. A nicer chair is not worth a grudge.
I might prefer comparing the rooms after the rushing stops.
A good find is more fun when somebody else enjoys seeing it.
A domestic arms race has been declared, with cushions among the likely casualties.
Competition has found the last quiet corner and installed a display shelf.
We should define nicer before turning the shopping into a contest.
A room can please its owner without defeating another room.
A decor challenge sounds fun if personal taste still gets a vote.
I would like to see what each of us finds worth bringing home.

contexts.subject: A base owner says decor reveals peoples taste and teases a speechless visitor.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer9PreChampion.text: You can learn a lot about the taste\nand sense of people by the kinds of\ldecorations they have, and how they\ldisplay them.\pWhat do you think of my taste?\nAre you speechless?$

replies.text: I was observing! My opinion had not finished putting its little shoes on.
The arrangement does suggest preferences, though silence permits many interpretations.
Give us a moment to look before demanding a verdict.
I would rather offer a real thought than answer too quickly.
A room says a lot, especially about what makes someone comfortable.
Our thoughtful pause has been boldly mistaken for a standing ovation.
I am speechless in several possible directions. Let us be diplomatic.
I would look at how the objects work together, not just count them.
A chosen place can hold more of a person than they realize.
The display certainly starts a conversation. I would give it a proper look.
I would ask which piece they most wanted us to notice.

contexts.subject: The Day-Care lady confirms a deposit; this is final when both Day-Care places are occupied.

DayCare_Text_WellRaiseYourMon.text: Fine, we'll raise your {STR_VAR_1}\nfor a while.\pCome back for it later.$

replies.text: A little stay has been arranged, and somebody else is taking a turn at the daily looking-after.
The statement confirms the care arrangement without claiming a particular amount of growth.
They are in her care now. We can return and check how things are going.
It helps to hear the arrangement said plainly before we walk away.
A temporary stay can be part of caring well, too.
A supporting member of the journey is taking a short residence away from the road.
A brief goodbye need not be a dramatic one to feel like something.
We can plan the next visit without assuming a result before enough time has passed.
One small life rests beneath another roof for a while.
A clear handover makes the parting feel a little less uncertain.
I wonder what familiar detail will be the first thing we notice when we come back.

contexts.subject: A sleeping Snorlax lies comfortably across the route.

Route12_Text_MonSprawledOutInSlumber.text: A POKéMON is sprawled out in\na deep and comfortable slumber.$

Route16_Text_MonSprawledOutInSlumber.text: A POKéMON is sprawled out in\na deep and comfortable slumber.$

replies.text: A roadblock has achieved perfect comfort without consulting any of the road's users.
The Pokemon appears deeply asleep. The blocked path is inconvenient, but there is no immediate emergency.
No pushing it around. We need a sensible way to deal with the blocked route.
It looks very comfortable in a place that is making everyone else's day less comfortable.
A sleeping traveller should not be treated like a piece of luggage to drag aside.
The road has acquired an immovable lead actor with no intention of waking for the cue.
An impressively peaceful source of logistical difficulty.
We should work around the actual obstacle instead of trying force first.
The path has become somebody's entire afternoon bed.
Comfortable is an excellent choice of mood and a less excellent choice of location.
I wonder how long the path had been quiet before Snorlax decided it belonged to a nap.

contexts.subject: Snorlax calms down, yawns, and returns to the mountains after the encounter.

Text_SnorlaxReturnedToMountains.text: SNORLAX calmed down.\nIt gave a huge yawn…\lAnd returned to the mountains.$

replies.text: A huge yawn has put a very gentle full stop on a rather large interruption.
The immediate disturbance has ended, and Snorlax has left the route on its own.
Good. The path is clear and the Pokemon has moved on.
I am glad the last thing we see is it calm enough to yawn.
Everyone can get back to their day without another argument over the road.
The formidable obstacle has delivered a sleepy exit rather than a final threat.
A surprisingly soft ending for something that occupied so much space.
A clear route and a settled Pokemon are both useful outcomes.
The mountain has called its wandering sleeper back.
An enormous presence can leave a very peaceful absence behind it.
I wonder whether the next chosen sleeping spot will inconvenience fewer travellers.

contexts.subject: The sticker collector recognizes Hall of Fame achievement and offers the first award tier.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowHoFLowest.text: Oh, wow, you made it into the\nHALL OF FAME.\pThat's pretty good, yup!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: An enormous accomplishment has been met with a very small decorative celebration. I like the mismatch.
The sticker records recognition of the Hall of Fame achievement without adding to the achievement itself.
We earned the record. A little acknowledgment is welcome.
It is nice when somebody hears the story and is simply pleased for us.
A small keepsake can hold the memory of a much bigger day.
The grand triumph has found an endearingly modest commemorative edition.
A tiny bright square can be a perfectly respectable monument.
A visible marker makes the milestone easy to recognize later.
A large memory has been given a small place to rest.
I like recognition that is allowed to be cheerful rather than solemn.
I wonder which part of earning that record comes to mind when we look at the sticker.

contexts.subject: The collector admires repeated Hall of Fame entries and offers a higher award tier.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowHoFLow.text: Oh, wow, you've entered the\nHALL OF FAME often!\pThat's impressive, yup!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: Coming back and doing it again is a different sort of impressive from one wonderful afternoon.
Repeated success suggests consistency across attempts, not only one favourable result.
A strong record. The team has done a lot of work.
Returning to a hard challenge can take a quieter kind of courage.
There are a lot of preparations and recoveries hiding behind those entries.
The successful run has acquired enough sequels to impress the reviewer.
Familiar ground can still ask for real effort every time.
Consistency usually means several small processes are working reliably together.
The road has learned our footsteps through the number of times they returned.
It is good to see repeated effort recognized instead of treated as automatic.
I wonder which return visit felt most different from the first.

contexts.subject: The collector is astonished by the large Hall of Fame record and says the player owns the League.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowHoFHigh.text: Whoa! You've made it into the\nHALL OF FAME that often?\lThat's seriously incredible, yup!\pYou own the POKéMON LEAGUE!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: We apparently own the League now. I hope ownership does not include sweeping all those corridors.
His wording is enthusiastic exaggeration, but the record does reflect substantial repeated achievement.
An impressive history. We can enjoy the praise without believing the exaggeration.
He sounds so surprised that I almost want to check the record again.
That much effort deserves more than pretending it was easy.
The reviewer has promoted the visiting champion to proprietor of the entire venue.
A fine achievement has received an entertainingly oversized hat.
The underlying consistency is more interesting than the colourful description.
A familiar road can become deep with the weight of remembered journeys.
A little extravagant praise is charming when everyone knows it is affection talking.
I wonder how many different teams and decisions are folded into that record.

contexts.subject: The collector can scarcely believe the Hall of Fame total and offers his highest tier.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowHoFHighest.text: No way! You've gone into the\nHALL OF FAME that many times?\pYou're beyond incredible, yup!\nThat's it, I have to give you this.$

replies.text: We have reached the number that makes the sticker man briefly forget how numbers work.
The total has exceeded the scale his ordinary praise was prepared to describe.
A lot of hard-won victories. We do not need another one today to make them count.
I like that he still sounds capable of being surprised.
After that much returning, a quiet day would also be well earned.
The awards committee has reached the end of its adjective budget.
A little astonishment has made the familiar record feel strange again.
A long run of success represents many preparations, not simply a large final number.
The small room has been asked to hold a very long stretch of road.
His delight makes the last tier feel like a celebration rather than a formality.
I wonder what advice we would give the version of us making that first attempt.

contexts.subject: The sticker collector is surprised to learn about Pokemon Eggs.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowEggsLowest.text: Oh, wow, there are POKéMON EGGS?\nI didn't know that!\pThat's pretty good, yup!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: We came to brag and accidentally became a very small educational programme.
His surprise is a reminder that an ordinary fact to one traveller may be new to someone else.
He learned something. No need to make him feel foolish for not knowing.
I like seeing someone delighted by a thing that had become familiar to us.
A fresh discovery can make an old subject feel interesting again.
The intended boast has become an introductory lecture with a decorative honorarium.
The world has managed to be larger than he expected without leaving the room.
A new observation is a perfectly good reason to revise what he thought he knew.
Something ordinary has opened a new little window for him.
His lack of embarrassment makes the surprise rather charming.
I wonder what question he will think to ask after we have gone.

contexts.subject: The collector admires the number of Eggs hatched and assumes the player enjoys it.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowEggsLow.text: You've hatched that many EGGS?\nYou really must like them!\pThat's impressive, yup!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: A lot of tiny introductions have added up to a very convincing reputation.
The record establishes repeated hatching, though the motive need not be exactly what he assumes.
That took patience. Worth recognizing it.
Each one was its own little beginning, even if the total sounds like one big task.
A lot of careful ordinary days sit behind a number like that.
The collector has reviewed the quantity and inferred a favourite genre.
A heap of separate beginnings can look oddly tidy from a distance.
Repeated care is less flashy than the final number but much more important to the process.
Many closed little worlds have opened along the same stretch of road.
It is nice that he sees enthusiasm in the work instead of only a statistic.
I wonder which hatching we remember most vividly out of all those quiet waits.

contexts.subject: The collector calls the prolific hatcher an Egg-hatching machine.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowEggsHigh.text: Whoa! You've hatched a whole\nbunch of EGGS!\pYou're an EGG-hatching machine!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: An Egg-hatching machine still needs snacks, sleep, and somewhere to put its shoes.
A colourful description of persistence, though the work still depends on individual care.
A strong record. We are still allowed a break.
The number is impressive, but I like thinking of the separate little lives behind it.
No machine here. Just a lot of patient days and new mouths to welcome.
The enthusiastic reviewer has promoted the traveller to an entire specialist industry.
A human being has once again been mistaken for the sum of their busiest habit.
A repeated process can become efficient without making its results interchangeable.
Each new beginning remains singular, however many have come before it.
I would keep the compliment and quietly put the mechanical nickname aside.
I wonder whether the most memorable hatch was one we expected or one that startled us.

contexts.subject: The collector is overwhelmed by the highest Egg-hatching tier and asks what motivates it.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowEggsHighest.text: Wh… You hatched that many EGGS?\pWhat's behind your love of EGGS?\nIt's beyond incredible, yup!\pYou're too awesome, I tell you.\nThat's it, I have to give you this.$

replies.text: The total is so big that he has started asking about the person behind the Egg collection.
Motivation is a more interesting question than assuming a large record explains itself.
That much care takes commitment. No need to make the number larger right now.
I think the honest answer could be much smaller and warmer than the grand total.
A love of beginnings can turn into a remarkable amount of daily work.
At last, the interviewer has moved from the impressive statistic to the character question.
A very large habit can grow around a surprisingly small fondness.
It would be interesting to know which parts of the process kept it rewarding.
A hundred little dawns may all be loved for different reasons.
He sounds sincerely curious now, beneath the magnificent overstatement.
I wonder what story we would choose instead of answering with another number.

contexts.subject: The collector recognizes success in battles against other trainers.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowLinkWinsLowest.text: Oh, wow, you've had success\nlink battling?\pYou're pretty strong, yup!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: A few good matches have travelled all the way into this man's sticker collection.
Competition with other trainers tests decisions against someone else's changing plans.
A good record. Respect the people who helped make those matches worth having.
Winning feels nicer when the other person still wants to say hello afterward.
A friendly match can give both trainers something useful to take home.
The competitive record has received a modest but enthusiastic local review.
A victory is more pleasant when it leaves a conversation still possible.
Another person's decisions make a match more revealing than practising the same sequence.
Two roads have crossed often enough to leave a few bright marks.
Being a good opponent makes the achievement easier to celebrate.
I wonder which match taught us something we could not have learned alone.

contexts.subject: The collector admires repeated victories against friends.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowLinkWinsLow.text: You've beaten your friends a lot\nlink battling, huh?\pYou're impressively strong, yup!\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: Winning often is impressive. Having friends who still enjoy the matches is a very good extra part.
Repeated competition can be valuable when both trainers have opportunities to adapt.
Keep the matches fair and the friendships worth coming back to.
I hope there is room for laughing together after the difficult matches, too.
The best repeat opponents are people we actually like spending time with.
The successful rivalry has apparently secured a recurring cast.
A familiar opponent can teach entirely new lessons on an ordinary rematch.
Shared practice works best when both people can learn rather than one only collect wins.
A friendly road can cross itself many times without wearing thin.
A good winner makes it easy for someone to be glad the two of them played.
I wonder how many of those victories came after finally understanding an old friend's favourite tactic.

contexts.subject: The collector jokingly wonders whether so many victories have cost the player friendships.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowLinkWinsHigh.text: Whoa! You've beaten your friends\na frightful number of times.\pHave you lost friends over this?\nI'll give you one of these.$

replies.text: A win should not come with a compulsory friendship deduction. Good manners help.
The result alone does not determine whether people enjoy competing together. Conduct matters.
Win decently. A friend is worth more than another mark in the record.
It would be sad if being good at something made sharing it feel unpleasant.
A thoughtful winner leaves room for the other person to enjoy the afternoon, too.
The reviewer has identified the social cost the scorekeeper conveniently omits.
A victory can become very lonely if it insists on being the whole conversation.
We can keep the challenge interesting without treating friends as sources of points.
A bright record is a poor lantern if everybody else has stopped walking beside it.
A little graciousness can keep an impressive streak from becoming a tedious personality.
I wonder whether the friends remember those matches as fondly as the winner does.

contexts.subject: The collector extravagantly praises the highest victory tier as the stuff of nightmares.

FourIsland_House2_Text_WowLinkWinsHighes.text:
Wh… Wickedly whoa!
You've won mind-blowingly often!\pIt just knocks me out thinking
about how tough you are.\pYou're the stuff of nightmares!
That's it, I have to give you this.$

replies.text: Nightmare is a very dramatic title to receive from a man holding a sticker sheet.
His astonishment is understandable, though the theatrical wording exceeds the information in the record.
A formidable record. We can still make a match pleasant for the person across from us.
I would rather people be excited to see us than actually frightened to try.
A long winning record is worth enjoying without making it the whole meal.
A fearsome legend has been officially endorsed by a tiny decorative awards office.
A grand dark title attached to a remarkably cheerful form of stationery.
Such consistency is interesting; I would rather examine the decisions than cultivate the reputation.
Strength is kinder when it does not need somebody else's unease to feel real.
I would accept the extravagant praise and continue being pleasant company.
I wonder which match the collector would find most surprising if he could hear the actual story.

contexts.subject: The apprentice cries with happiness after the player selects a challenge level.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks0.text:
{STR_VAR_1}?
Waaaaah!\pOh! I'm so sorry!
You've made me happy by choosing\lthe level for me, and it's made me cry…\pSnivel…
Thank you so much!\lPlease talk with me again!$

replies.text: Happy tears over a level choice. We've apparently become a very efficient little fountain switch.
The relief seems genuine. We can acknowledge it without making the reaction embarrassing.
A choice helped. Give them a moment to settle.
I'm glad the tears meant happiness. I was worried I'd misunderstood.
A little patient help can matter much more than the task itself suggests.
Our modest piece of advice has received an unexpectedly enthusiastic weather report.
Joy has escaped containment. At least the cause is kind.
Now they have a starting format. The next step can be small and concrete.
Relief sometimes arrives in water before it finds words.
I'd rather let them be moved than hurry them into looking composed.
I'd ask later how the first attempt felt, once the happy surprise has settled.

contexts.subject: The apprentice accepts the selected level and eagerly asks for future teaching.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks1.text: {STR_VAR_1}, huh? That's true!\nI'll do my best there!\pIf we meet here again, please teach\nme something else, teacher!$

replies.text: They've found a starting line and already waved at us from the next lesson.
They accept the recommendation and remain interested in learning. Good momentum.
A clear start. They still need to do the work.
I like how quickly the question turned into wanting to try.
I'd be happy if the advice helps them discover what they enjoy doing.
One answer has successfully created a future appointment with more questions.
The lesson is finished. Curiosity has declined to leave with it.
We can review the choice after they have actual experience with the format.
A small answer can open the next door rather than close the conversation.
They make learning feel sociable instead of shameful. That's lovely.
I'd ask them to bring back one thing they noticed during their attempt.

contexts.subject: The apprentice confirms the selected level and plans to return with further questions.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks2.text: Oh, the {STR_VAR_1} challenge?\nUnderstood!\pIf I have another question, I'll come\nback here for your advice!$

replies.text: Understood, accepted, next question reserved for later. A wonderfully organized little visit.
They've retained a clear next step and a source for clarification. Practical approach.
Good. Try the format, then ask about anything unclear.
I like not needing to pretend one answer settles every question forever.
A useful lesson gives someone something to do, not just something to repeat.
A crisp acknowledgment, with future confusion sensibly booked into a later conversation.
The question has been answered without acquiring a dramatic afterlife.
Their next observations can help us decide whether the initial choice suited them.
A path is easier to begin when asking again remains allowed.
They sound comfortable enough to admit there may be more they don't know.
I'd ask what they hope to learn from the first round before they go.

contexts.subject: The apprentice doubts their chances but agrees to try the chosen level.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks3.text:
{STR_VAR_1}? Okay!
But do you really think someone like\lme would have a chance?\pI'll do my best, even though I don't
think it will work.\pThank you very much for spending
time with someone like me.$

replies.text: They're taking the first step while their doubt keeps trying to tie the shoes together.
Their prediction of failure isn't established. An attempt will provide actual information.
Try it first. They haven't lost the match in advance.
I recognize that habit of apologizing before anyone has been disappointed.
I'd like them to know the time wasn't wasted just because they're uncertain.
A perfectly ordinary lesson has been made to carry an unfair trial of the learner's worth.
The doubt arrived early and is pretending to be an official forecast.
We can set a small first goal that doesn't require immediate victory.
A trembling beginning is still a beginning.
They don't have to earn the right to be helped by sounding confident.
I'd ask them to notice one thing they learned, whatever the first result is.

contexts.subject: The apprentice accepts the level partly because blaming the player choice would soften a loss.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks4.text:
Okay, {STR_VAR_1} is suitable for me?
Thank you!\pKnowing that you made the decision,
{PLAYER}{KUN}, I won't be so upset if\lI lose.\pOkay, I'll look to you for advice again.
Bye!$

replies.text: We've recommended a level and accidentally been appointed the official cushion for disappointment.
Advice can inform a decision without taking ownership of every future result.
We'll help. They still own how they approach the challenge.
I'm glad it feels less frightening, though I don't want the choice to become a place to hide.
A loss can be handled without needing to hand it to someone else.
Our teaching appointment appears to include a complimentary blame-absorption service.
The responsibility has been quietly placed beside our name tag.
They should understand why the format was selected, not only who selected it.
A borrowed certainty won't hold every difficult feeling for long.
I'd rather help them feel able to choose than simply feel safe because we did it.
I'd explain the reason behind the recommendation before they rely on the name behind it.

contexts.subject: The busy apprentice accepts the level advice and hurries back to work.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks5.text: {STR_VAR_1}, huh? Okay, gotcha.\nI'll find time somehow and give it a go!\p…Whoops, I'd better go to work!\nThanks! See you around!$

replies.text: A battle plan squeezed between shifts. I hope their calendar leaves somewhere for breathing.
They need to fit practice into existing obligations. A realistic schedule will matter.
Work first if it needs them. The challenge can wait.
I hope they get to enjoy the attempt instead of making it one more thing they're late for.
I'd rather they try rested than carve the time out of every meal and break.
The grand training ambition has met the much more punctual demands of employment.
Adventure has been allocated a small gap in the schedule. Brave little gap.
We can keep future advice specific enough to use in limited practice time.
A wish can travel beside an ordinary working day, even if it has to walk slowly.
Their time matters. I'd make the next conversation useful rather than merely long.
I'd ask what part of battling makes the effort of finding time worthwhile.

contexts.subject: The delighted apprentice calls the level advice cool and ends the day visit.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks6.text:
Oh-oh-oh!
{STR_VAR_1}, you say!\lThank you for a totally cool reply!\pI guess that's about all I wanted
to ask you today.\pLet's meet here again, okay?
Thanks!$

replies.text: We've delivered a cool answer. I wasn't aware the level menu came with a temperature rating.
Their enthusiasm is encouraging, though the recommendation still needs experience behind it.
Enough for today. Let them try what they learned.
They sound happy to have one clear thing to take away.
I like ending a lesson while the learner still feels eager instead of exhausted.
An ordinary choice has received excellent reviews for style. I shall endeavor to remain humble.
The advice has been judged cool. Its practical assessment is scheduled for later.
They have a next step. Another question can wait until the choice has been tested.
A small lesson can leave a brighter mood than it found.
Their delight is infectious. I'd still want the decision to feel useful tomorrow.
I'd ask them next time whether the format matched what they expected.

contexts.subject: The apprentice politely thanks the player for choosing a level and promises effort.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks7.text: {STR_VAR_1} is your choice!\nI see. I will do my best!\pThank you, {PLAYER}.\nI hope I can count on you again.\lPlease take care!$

replies.text: A little thanks, a little determination, and a very kind goodbye. Nicely packed.
They distinguish the advice from the effort they must supply. A healthy response.
They'll do their best. That's the part in their hands.
I like the way they wished us well, too.
Help feels better when both people remember the other is a person.
A courteous lesson ending that has remembered to distribute goodwill in both directions.
No grand guarantee. Just effort and decent manners. An excellent combination.
They can test the recommendation and bring back observations later.
A little trust can be carried without becoming a heavy demand.
Their gratitude feels warm without making the relationship awkwardly grand.
I'd be glad to hear how their attempt goes when we next meet.

contexts.subject: The apprentice repeats understanding the level choice and expresses delighted gratitude.

gText_ApprenticeLevelModeThanks8.text: {STR_VAR_1}! Perfectly understood!\nI understand perfectly!\lI'm deliriously delighted!\pI hope you'll be willing to teach me\nsome more another time.$

replies.text: They understood it twice. That's a very generous margin of understanding.
The repetition signals excitement. I'd still check their practical interpretation when needed.
They've got the choice. Time to see how it works.
It's lovely hearing someone so pleased about a starting point.
I hope the excitement carries into patient practice, not just a quick rush.
The answer has been understood with enough enthusiasm to require a second confirmation.
Understanding has been achieved and then enthusiastically achieved again.
A short explanation of the choice would help turn delight into usable knowledge.
Relief can repeat itself when one set of words isn't quite enough.
They sound delighted by being helped as much as by the actual answer.

We should explain the lead's role clearly enough that they can evaluate it themselves.
A careful question can keep trust from being built on a misunderstanding.
I'd rather earn their confidence with a clear reason than ask them to suppress the doubt.
I'd ask what part of the choice surprised them most.

contexts.subject: The grateful apprentice accepts a victory saying, cries happily, and hopes to battle the player someday.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks0.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pAwesome! Wicked! Awoooh!
It's really cool!\pOh… I'm sorry…
I'm so happy, I'm crying…\pSnivel… {PLAYER}!
Thank you so much for everything!\pI will battle the best I can for
your sake, {PLAYER}!\p{PLAYER}…
Next time… We should battle!$

replies.text: They've packed a saying, several lessons, and enough happy tears to water the whole road ahead.
The teaching sequence is complete. A future battle remains an intention, not an arranged result.
They did the learning. They should take some credit with them.
I'm glad the goodbye includes something they want to try for themselves.
I'd like them to battle for their own enjoyment, not feel they owe us every result.
A final lesson has become a farewell with an unusually generous supply of emotion.
The pupil is departing. The tear supply seems determined to outlast the curriculum.
Now the useful test is adapting those lessons to unfamiliar opponents.
A little guidance has become something another person can carry beyond us.
I'd let the gratitude stay warm without letting it turn into a lifelong debt.
I'd love to hear what they discover before that hoped-for battle ever happens.

contexts.subject: The apprentice accepts the saying and leaves eager to improve and meet the player in battle.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks1.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pOh, wow! That is so cool!
Okay, I'll say that!\pThanks for teaching me all this time!
I'm going to do the best I can\lwherever I go from now on!\pWhen we meet again, it'll be for
a battle!$

replies.text: They've found their own road out of the classroom. I hope the new saying travels comfortably.
They intend to apply the instruction broadly. Experience will supply situations our lessons didn't cover.
Good. Go practice, think, and make the choices their own.
I like the change from asking what to do to sounding ready to try.
Doing their best can mean learning from a hard day as well as enjoying a good one.
The final answer has successfully produced a future opponent. An excellent educational complication.
The student has graduated to threatening us politely with a rematch. Progress.
They should keep observing rather than treat the completed lessons as finished knowledge.
A goodbye can be the first step of a new way to meet.
Their confidence sounds earned through trying, not borrowed only from our name.
I'd ask them to remember one surprise from the first battle they approach on their own.

contexts.subject: The apprentice accepts the saying and plans to seek battles widely, perhaps meeting the player again.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks2.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\p…Cool!
I will use that!\pI'm going out to battle all over
the place.\pWho knows, I may even get to battle
you one day, {PLAYER}.\pNext time, let's meet at a place
of battle!$

replies.text: The lessons have grown legs and a fairly ambitious itinerary.
Seeking varied opponents can test how well the learned principles transfer.
Different opponents will need different thinking. Keep learning on the road.
I like imagining a familiar face arriving later with stories we haven't heard yet.
I'd want the journey to include care and rest, not only a list of people to challenge.
The graduate has selected the wider world as the next classroom. Sensible choice of venue.
An educational departure with a possible future disagreement conducted through Pokemon.
They can compare what works across different teams rather than assume one plan fits all.
A path away from someone can still curve toward another meeting.
I'd hope they meet people worth listening to as well as people worth defeating.
I'd be curious where they choose to go first and what draws them there.

contexts.subject: The apprentice admires the saying but still doubts their worth and fears being forgotten after leaving.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks3.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pThat's inspired…\pUh… Is it okay for someone like me
to even say that?\pNo! I'll do my best!\p{PLAYER}, thank you so much for
putting up with me for so long…\pI promise to do my best from now on.\pI'm sure you'll quickly forget about
someone like me, but let's meet\lsomewhere again!$

replies.text: They've learned so much and still think they're the small forgettable part of the story.
Their self-dismissal isn't supported by the effort they've already shown.
They earned the progress. Say that plainly before they go.
That fear of being forgotten makes the goodbye feel much quieter than the words around it.
I'd want them to leave knowing they weren't merely being tolerated through the lessons.
A substantial amount of work has been completed by someone still apologizing for appearing in the room.
The lessons are finished. The old doubt has apparently missed the announcement.
We can point to specific decisions they've learned to make rather than offer vague reassurance.
A person can leave a mark without believing they had the weight to make one.
I'd tell them what I remember about their effort instead of demanding they stop feeling uncertain.
I'd ask them to tell us about their next journey if we meet again. Their story has room to grow.

contexts.subject: The apprentice accepts the final saying, apologizes for being pushy, and sets out with the lessons.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks4.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pNot bad!
Yup, that's what I'll go with!\pI'm going to hit the road and do what
I can with what you taught me in\lmy head and heart.\pI'm sorry that I've been so pushy
with you!\pNext time, we battle, okay?
See you!$

replies.text: They've noticed the elbows in their earlier questions. That's a useful extra lesson to pack.
Acknowledging the pressure they placed on us suggests reflection beyond merely following instructions.
Good apology. Now take responsibility for the next choices, too.
I appreciate hearing them recognize how the conversations felt from the other side.
The best thing they can carry forward may be learning to ask without making the answer a burden.
An unusually satisfying graduation: practical knowledge accompanied by an actual revision of one's manners.
The self-awareness has arrived before departure. Excellent timing.
They can apply the principles independently instead of carrying our exact choices unchanged.
A little roughness can soften before someone steps onto a new road.
The apology makes the farewell warmer. It feels like they see us as people, too.
I'd be interested to hear how their own way of asking and deciding changes after this.

contexts.subject: The busy apprentice accepts the saying and resolves to make time for battling beyond the lessons.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks5.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pOkay, gotcha.
I can find time to say that!\pHonestly, I'm glad I met a good mentor
like you.\pI'm going to make time somehow so
I can get into battling.\pThanks for everything, {PLAYER}{KUN}!
We have to battle, you and me, one day!$

replies.text: They can find time for a sentence. I hope the rest of the adventure gets a reasonable appointment, too.
A wish to continue is clear. A sustainable schedule will matter more than an enormous promise.
Make room for the battles without giving away every break.
I like hearing them choose something for themselves in such a busy life.
I'd want the hobby to add something good to the week instead of becoming another shift.
A graduation ceremony briefly delayed by the continuing logistical problem of having a job.
The adventure has received tentative space in the calendar. Guard that little square kindly.
They can begin with manageable practice periods rather than wait for an entirely empty day.
A road can begin in the small piece of time someone finally keeps for themselves.
I'd like their future effort to be a choice they enjoy, not another obligation to us.
I'd ask what kind of battle they most look forward to making time for.

contexts.subject: The apprentice accepts the saying, recognizes growing competence, and plans to challenge other trainers.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks6.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pThat… That's fabulous!
It's dignified and cool! I claim it!\p…Listen, I think I'm getting decent
at this, huh?\pSo, I'm thinking of challenging other
TRAINERS from now on.\p{PLAYER}, your advice really helped me.\pMaybe one day, there'll be a time when
we battle!\pThank you for everything!$

replies.text: They've finally heard their own progress speaking. That's an excellent sound to take on the road.
Their assessment now includes personal improvement, rather than only admiration for the adviser.
They're getting better. Good that they can say it themselves.
I like the small question about being decent. It sounds like confidence finding its own voice.
They've done the practice behind that feeling. They can keep a share of the credit.
The most important statement in the farewell is the discovery that they can do some of this themselves.
The pupil has detected competence in the vicinity. Correctly, for once.
New opponents will let them refine that competence rather than simply repeat familiar answers.
A borrowed light has helped someone notice the light they carry.
I'd celebrate that little bit of self-recognition more than the claim of a perfect saying.
I'd ask what they can do now that felt impossible when they first came to the desk.

contexts.subject: The apprentice finds the saying refreshing and formally leaves to battle many others.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks7.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pAh! That saying! It refreshes me
and makes me feel reborn!\pI must use that right away!\pAnd now, I must take my leave,
{PLAYER}…\pI will go out to battle many others,
but never will I forget your teachings.\pPerhaps one day…
Farewell!$

replies.text: A refreshed trainer with a whole road waiting. I hope the saying is easier to carry than all that gratitude.
They regard this as a transition to independent experience. The lessons can support rather than constrain it.
They can remember the teaching and still change the plan when needed.
The formal goodbye feels sincere. I'd want to answer it with equal care.
I'd rather they keep what helps than feel obliged to preserve every instruction forever.
A dignified departure, giving one short saying a remarkable amount of ceremonial work to do.
A new beginning has been declared. No actual rebirth paperwork seems necessary.
They can test the guidance against new situations and revise their understanding.
A farewell can clear a little space for the person who steps through it.
Their respect is lovely. I'd want it to leave them free to become different from the teacher.
I'd like to hear which lesson changes most once they've met a wider range of opponents.

contexts.subject: The overwhelmed apprentice thanks the player for everything and leaves to travel and battle.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks8.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pWaaaaah!
I'm going to say that?!\lI… I'm delirious with joy!\pTh-th-thank you!
I have nothing left to regret now!\pI'm going to travel now and battle
all sorts of people.\pEverything, I owe it to you, {PLAYER}.
Really, really, thank you!\pI've got to go now, but let's meet
in battle one day!$

replies.text: The joy has packed for the whole trip. I hope they leave a little room for giving themselves credit.
Our guidance contributed, but their participation and future effort belong to them.
They don't owe us everything. They did the learning.
It's moving hearing that much gratitude. I wouldn't want it to make them feel smaller.
I'd like them to leave feeling supported, not carrying a debt for every good thing ahead.
An ordinary mentor has been awarded a frankly implausible share of the credit for another person's life.
The gratitude is enormous. The invoice should remain nonexistent.
They should keep using their own observations as they meet unfamiliar teams.
A gift of guidance can help a person stand. It needn't become something tied around the ankles.
I'd answer the warmth while gently returning some of the achievement to its actual owner.
I'd ask what discovery they're eager to make that nobody has told them about yet.

contexts.subject: The apprentice enthusiastically accepts the saying and hopes for a future battle before departing.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks9.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pUh-huh, that's sweet!
Si, bueno!\lI'll try saying that, like, ham!\pAnd now, it's time to say good-bye!
Thanks for all sorts of things!\pGive me a battle one day, OK?
Adios!$

replies.text: A fast goodbye, a new line to try, and the promise of a very lively next hello.
The farewell expresses a future challenge without establishing when or whether it will occur.
Good. Go learn from other teams. We can meet again if our paths cross.
I think the energy will still be in this room a moment after they leave.
I'd want the journey to feel good for the partner beside all that excitement.
A thoroughly energetic graduation, concluding before the punctuation could request a rest.
Several syllables may arrive at the exit before their speaker.
They can use varied encounters to test their plan rather than rely on one confident impression.
Some goodbyes sound less like an ending than a door being flung open.
Their style is entirely their own. I'd like their future choices to become just as individual.
I'd ask for one surprising story if we meet after their travels.

contexts.subject: The joking apprentice accepts the final saying, recognizes learning, and leaves hoping to challenge the mentor.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks10.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pThat's what I should say, huh?
Then, I'll stay away from that!\pJust kidding!
I'll obey your teaching, master!\pThanks for teaching me all this time,
master!\pI'm finally understanding what being
a TRAINER is about.\pI'm going to go out and win battles
against any TRAINER.\pMaybe it'll be you one day, master!\pThat's all!
Farewell, my master!$

replies.text: One last tiny rebellion, then off to become a possible opponent. The lessons have grown an excellent sense of mischief.
They recognize growing understanding. That matters more than the repeated promise to obey.
Take the learning. Leave the need for a master behind.
I like that the farewell sounds ready to turn admiration into a fair challenge someday.
I'd rather they carry a thoughtful habit than a rule that our answer must always be followed.
The student has graduated from joking rebellion to the entirely legitimate prospect of defeating the teacher.
Obedience is promised. A future battle suggests the healthy possibility of ignoring us competently.
Independent decisions will test whether they understand the principles beneath the choices.
A good lesson can lead someone far enough away to meet us on level ground.
The title master can stay in the joke. Their actual judgment needs room to grow.
I'd ask them to bring their own plan if we ever meet as opponents.

contexts.subject: The rhyming apprentice accepts the saying, thanks the mentor, and cheerfully leaves the nest.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks11.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pPerfect! That's what I'll use.
I was right to make you choose!\pAnd now, I think it'd be best,
if I were to fly the nest!\pThanks for all you taught me.
I'll be off on a battle spree!\pB-O-N-V-O-Y-A-G-E!
And that spells bon voyage,\lto you this is my homage!$

replies.text: They've packed the farewell, rhymed the luggage, and spelled the departure for good measure. Thorough traveler.
The playful delivery accompanies a clear transition to independent practice.
Ready to leave the nest. Keep thinking when the first plan fails.
I like hearing the goodbye sound so much like them.
A good lesson should eventually make room for someone to go and try.
A final tribute with enough rhyme to require its own luggage allowance. Magnificent excess.
The nest has been vacated through a considerable quantity of verse.
They can take the useful ideas while adapting the actual methods to new conditions.
A bird leaves with more than the sound of the voice that called it forward.
The confidence is playful instead of polished. I'd hate to smooth that out of them.
I'd enjoy hearing which story their next rhyme decides to tell.

contexts.subject: The rhyming apprentice has no questions left, offers an affectionate farewell, and hopes to meet in battle.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks12.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pAll right, all right!
I'll use that because it's so tight!\pI'm out of things to ask you.
Waving bye is all that's left to do.\pBut maybe one day we'll meet, with one
destined to go down in defeat.\pBut, it really is time to say farewell.\pWell, {PLAYER}, I have to roam free,
but don't you forget about me!\pTake care, {PLAYER}!
Love ya!$

replies.text: No questions left, one rhyme overflowing, and a goodbye that seems reluctant to stop waving.
The teaching sequence ends, though future experience will certainly generate new questions.
Go try things. Being out of questions today doesn't mean finished learning.
The affectionate little ending caught me off guard. It feels very sincere.
I'd like them to carry the warmth without feeling they have to return it through victories.
A farewell performing several excellent attempts to end before discovering another line it wanted to say.
The goodbye has packed a possible rematch and forgotten how doors work for a moment.
They can develop their own judgments rather than treat the completed questions as a fixed recipe.
A fond thread can remain without keeping either person from walking away.
I'd remember the warmth more than the rhyme. That's what gives the words somewhere to land.
I'd be glad to hear how the world surprised them after this cheerful departure.

contexts.subject: The emotional apprentice accepts the saying, thanks the player, and declares a new rivalry.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks13.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\p… … …That's good.
No, it's awe inspiring!\lIt's bringing fresh tears to my eyes!\pBut in spite of my tears and runny
nose, I will use that saying!\pI'm plumb out of things to ask you,
{PLAYER}{KUN}.\pFrom now on, we're rivals!
Thanks for everything!$

replies.text: Tears, a runny nose, and a rival declaration. They have not let dignity delay the important part.
They are shifting from seeking instruction to proposing equal competition. A meaningful change.
A rival now. Good. They should trust some of their own work.
I like that the tears don't stop them saying what they want next.
I'd still wish them a quiet chance to recover before any grand new campaign.
The pupil has completed the course and issued a rival notice without waiting for the tissues to arrive.
The sniffle is temporary. The newly declared competitive relationship may last longer.
A future contest would let them test an independently chosen plan.
A shaking voice can still speak a new place for itself in the world.
They've found a way to stand beside the person they looked up to. That deserves recognition.
I'd ask them what they most want to try now that they're choosing for themselves.

contexts.subject: The nervous apprentice accepts the saying but doubts being able to deliver it before saying goodbye.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks14.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\pOh… Okay!
I'll try to say that!\lI might be too nervous to say it…\pThank you, {PLAYER}{KUN}.
I have to say good-bye now.\pI'll obey all that you've taught me,
{PLAYER}{KUN}, and do the best I can.$

replies.text: They can borrow the words without borrowing a louder voice. A quiet victory still counts.
Difficulty saying the phrase doesn't invalidate their progress as a trainer.
They don't have to perform the line perfectly. The battle comes first.
I understand having the words ready and still finding them difficult to let out.
I'd want the goodbye to leave them less pressured, not with one final test of sounding brave.
A useful education should not end by demanding a flawless public performance from its most nervous student.
The saying can survive being whispered. Remarkably durable thing, a sentence.
They can adapt their delivery instead of treating our wording as a compulsory performance.
A small voice needn't become large to carry something true.
I'd rather they feel like themselves than imitate an idea of the perfect confident trainer.
I'd ask them to remember one thing they accomplished despite feeling nervous.

contexts.subject: The skeptical apprentice carefully accepts the saying, thanks the mentor, and chooses independence.

gText_ApprenticeWinSpeechThanks15.text:
{STR_VAR_1}\p… … … … … …
When I win a match…\p{STR_VAR_1}\p…Are you serious?\pI see. If you are serious, that's fine.
I thank you for your time.\pI do hope even I will be able to
put that saying to good use.\pI seem to have run dry on what advice
I need.\pI do believe it's high time I bid you
farewell and strike out on my own.\pThank you, my mentor!
I apologize for my skepticism!$

replies.text: They've checked the final answer twice and then chosen their own road. That's a very respectable goodbye.
Their skepticism can become useful independent evaluation rather than simple reluctance.
They can stop asking permission to think. That's a good next step.
I like the quiet certainty in deciding it's time to go, even after all the questions.
No need to apologize for wanting advice that makes sense. I'd want them to keep that habit.
A carefully considered graduation, complete with a formal release of the mentor from further questioning.
The inquiry has concluded. Independent skepticism is now open for business.
They should retain the habit of checking whether a recommendation fits the actual situation.
A doorway opens differently when someone chooses it for themselves.
Their farewell feels earned because they haven't pretended every doubt vanished.
I'd like to hear which choice they first make differently once they're out on their own.

contexts.subject: A Journal says Brock seldom laughs but struggles to stop once he starts.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureBrock.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: PEWTER GYM\nLEADER BROCK!\pBROCK rarely laughs, but is said to\nbe unable to stop if he starts.$

replies.text: I want to hear the joke that gets through his defenses.
An infrequent laugh is not necessarily a small one.
Good. Everyone should have something that gets them laughing.
I like imagining the serious face finally giving up.
The quietest person at dinner can start the biggest laughing fit.
A stern exterior guarding an absolutely catastrophic giggle.
A stone face with a hidden structural weakness.
Now I want to know what reliably triggers it.
Even a mountain can discover it has an echo.
Somebody has definitely made him laugh at the worst possible moment.
That is a side of him I hope his friends get to see.

contexts.subject: A Journal says Misty deeply admires Lorelei.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureMisty.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: CERULEAN GYM\nLEADER MISTY!\pMISTY is said to worship LORELEI\nof the ELITE FOUR.$

replies.text: Even a Gym Leader can have someone she hopes to impress.
A respected example can give ambition a useful direction.
Nothing wrong with looking up to someone good.
I wonder if Lorelei knows what her example means to Misty.
It is nice to know even confident people started by admiring someone.
A formidable trainer with a formidable favorite.
A little admiration beneath all that confidence.
Studying someone skilled can help you set concrete goals.
Even a strong current began by finding somewhere to flow.
I hope she gets to tell Lorelei without a magazine doing it first.
I would ask which part of Lorelei's style first caught her attention.

contexts.subject: A Journal repeats a rumor that Surge piloted a plane powered by Pokemon electricity.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureLtSurg.text:
POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: VERMILION GYM
LEADER LT. SURGE!\pLT. SURGE is rumored to have been
a pilot while home in America.\pHe used the electricity generated
by POKéMON to power his plane.$

replies.text: A Pokemon-powered plane? I would spend the whole trip thanking the Pokemon.
I would need more than a rumor before assessing that power system.
Hope the Pokemon got a say in being the engine.
I wonder what that sounded like from the ground.
That is a story I would like to hear over a very long lunch.
An aviation story with an unusually lively power source.
A plane depending on a creature having a sufficiently good day.
I have questions about the regulator. Several questions.
If the story is true, those partners shared quite a sky.
He must get asked about that at every gathering.
I would love to see an actual photograph from that part of his life.

contexts.subject: A Journal repeats a rumor that Erika often naps in the Gym.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureErika.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: CELADON GYM\nLEADER ERIKA!\pRumor has it that if you peek into\nCELADON GYM, you can often\lsee ERIKA snoozing.$

replies.text: A little nap among plants sounds extremely easy to understand.
Rest is ordinary. Turning it into a feature is the stranger part.
Let her rest if nothing needs doing.
A quiet room full of leaves would make a lovely place to drift off.
A well-earned nap after lunch can improve everybody's afternoon.
An exclusive report: local woman occasionally becomes tired.
A flower garden with an excellent sleep endorsement.
Comfortable environment confirmed. Productivity conclusions unproven.
A little stillness among growing things is no great mystery.
Peeking at someone asleep is not a hobby I plan to encourage.
I hope people let her have the quiet the place was made for.

contexts.subject: A Journal describes Koga medical knowledge and medicines he prepares for his Pokemon.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureKoga.text:
POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: FUCHSIA GYM
LEADER KOGA!\pKOGA is said to have a thorough
knowledge of medicine.\pHe even concocts medicine to nurse
his POKéMON to health.$

replies.text: I like knowing those partners have someone who knows how to help them.
Knowing how to treat harm matters alongside knowing how to inflict it.
A strong trainer should know how to care for the team afterward.
That is a quieter kind of skill than the Gym shows off.
Making something that helps a partner recover takes patient care.
The poison specialist also knows the restorative chapter.
A useful reminder that dangerous knowledge can have gentle work to do.
I would ask how he checks the preparations are safe.
The same careful hands can tend what they know could be hurt.
That deserves as much attention as the intimidating reputation.
I would rather hear about a partner recovering than another frightening trick.

contexts.subject: A Journal says Sabrina can communicate with her Pokemon in battle without speaking.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureSabrin.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: SAFFRON GYM\nLEADER SABRINA!\pPeople say that SABRINA can\ncommunicate with her POKéMON\lduring battle without speaking.$

replies.text: I would still say thank you out loud. It feels nice to hear.
The report describes silent coordination. The mechanism remains worth asking about.
If the team understands, the orders do not need an audience.
I wonder whether it feels like a voice or something without words.
I hope there is still room for an ordinary comforting word afterward.
A commanding performance with no lines for the audience to quote.
An entire conversation the room is not invited to hear.
An unusually direct communication channel, if the account is accurate.
Some understanding may arrive before a word can put on its coat.
People already assume I should know what they mean. She might actually manage.
I would like to know what the Pokemon notice first when she reaches out.

contexts.subject: A Journal claims Blaine removes his shades when devising quiz questions.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureBlaine.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: CINNABAR GYM\nLEADER BLAINE!\pBLAINE is said to remove his dark\nshades only when he is thinking up\lnew quiz questions.$

replies.text: The glasses come off. Somewhere, a perfectly innocent question becomes a trap.
I doubt the eyewear is necessary, but rituals can help concentration.
The important part is whether the question makes sense.
Maybe that is how people know to leave him to his thoughts.
Everyone has a small habit when thinking through something difficult.
The shades are apparently the curtain between us and another quiz.
A warning signal for the approach of organized trivia.
I want to test whether he writes better questions without them.
A little uncovered gaze, searching for something else to ask.
Someone noticed that often enough to make it his public fact.
I wonder whether he knows people have identified his thinking face.

contexts.subject: A Journal praises Lorelei calculated battling and teases an unspecified surprising secret.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureLorele.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature:\nELITE FOUR's LORELEI!\pKnown for her logical, calculated,\nand cool battling style, LORELEI\lhas a surprising secret!$

replies.text: They cannot just say secret and leave the page looking that pleased.
The battle description is useful. The unspecified secret is a sales device.
If she wants to keep something private, let her.
I would rather hear what she enjoys when she chooses to tell us.
We know she can battle. We do not need every other part of her life.
A magnificent little hook with no fish attached.
An entire paragraph trying to sell us an unopened drawer.
Precise battling described precisely. Then the article gives up on precision.
Some doors belong to the person who closes them.
Being impressive in public does not make her private life a prize.
I would prefer a question she wants to answer to a secret someone wants to expose.

contexts.subject: A Journal attributes Bruno joining the Elite Four to his desire to battle the strongest trainers.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureBruno.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature:\nELITE FOUR's BRUNO!\pBRUNO apparently joined the ELITE\nFOUR out of his burning ambition to\lbattle the best TRAINERS.$

replies.text: He found a job where the difficult part is exactly what he wanted.
A demanding position aligned with a clear personal ambition.
He wanted strong opponents. He put himself where they would arrive.
It must feel good to reach a place you worked toward.
That kind of work takes more than wanting it on one determined morning.
An ambition with the courage to choose a very inconvenient workplace.
He built a life in the path of very formidable visitors.
Clear objective. Extremely demanding implementation.
A strong wish can become the place where someone stands.
I hope he has something he enjoys on the days nobody challenges him.
I would ask what the best battle taught him, rather than just who won.

contexts.subject: A Journal reports that Agatha and Oak were rival trainers when young.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureAgatha.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature:\nELITE FOUR's AGATHA!\pIn her youth, AGATHA and PROF.\nOAK were rivals who vied for\lsupremacy as TRAINERS.$

replies.text: Those two used to challenge each other? That must have been a lively route.
Their shared history predates the roles we know them for.
Old rivals tend to remember things no title can erase.
I wonder if either still remembers one particular match perfectly.
I can imagine a very competitive conversation over tea.
Two impressive careers with an old argument tucked into the roots.
A rivalry old enough to have collected its own ghosts.
Competition may have helped shape both of them.
Long years do not always quiet a familiar challenge.
She probably knows stories that would make his students sit very still.
I would love to see a photograph from a day they still thought everything was ahead.

contexts.subject: A Journal suggests Lance grandfather is an elder of a renowned dragon-master clan.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureLance.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature:\nELITE FOUR's LANCE!\pLANCE's grandfather is thought to\nbe the elder of a famous clan of\ldragon masters.$

replies.text: Imagine bringing home your first Pokemon when the family specializes in dragons.
A possible family tradition, though the article leaves the relationship tentative.
His family may have taught him plenty. He still had to do the work.
That sounds like a childhood with some very large expectations.
Family knowledge can be a gift. It can also arrive with instructions nobody asked for.
A family tree with an unusually high chance of breathing fire.
An impressive inheritance, with teeth attached.
I would ask what practical knowledge was passed down.
Some families carry their old stories on very large wings.
I hope he got to choose what part of the family story became his.
I wonder which small lesson from his grandfather he still uses.

contexts.subject: A Journal reports Oak lives with his grandchildren Daisy and the rival.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureProfOa.text: POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature: PROF. OAK,\nthe POKéMON Researcher!\pPROF. OAK reportedly lives with his\ngrandchildren DAISY and {RIVAL}.$

replies.text: A busy household, a busy lab. I hope someone reminds him to eat.
Living arrangements are a small part of a life. The article gives us only that part.
Being somebody's grandfather matters alongside the famous job.
It is strange to read a familiar family detail in a feature.
I wonder who notices first when everyone has missed lunch.
The celebrated professor also has ordinary household negotiations.
A grand public name, with a very ordinary front door.
I hope the household gets more quiet than the lab.
Even a well-known life has a place where the kettle needs filling.
Imagine your home situation becoming a magazine paragraph.
I would rather hear a family story they chose to share than keep inspecting the address.

contexts.subject: An old Journal names Daisy Oak as the Spring Contest Grand Champion.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureDaisyO.text:
This is a POKéMON JOURNAL from
years ago…\pPOKéMON JOURNAL
CONTEST Special!\pThe Spring POKéMON CONTEST's
Grand Champion is DAISY OAK of\lPALLET TOWN!$

replies.text: Daisy won the whole spring Contest? I hope someone cheered themselves hoarse.
That is a documented achievement, not simply a flattering description.
Good for her. That would have taken real preparation.
I wish we could have heard the room when her name was called.
I hope the celebration afterward was as warm as the victory.
A champion's chapter, quietly waiting on an old shelf.
A familiar name carrying a bright season behind it.
An award like that represents a lot of work people did not see.
A spring preserved between pages, with her name at its center.
I would absolutely ask about the outfit and then the entire performance.
I wonder which moment from that day she most likes remembering.

contexts.subject: A Journal notes Fuji declined an interview and describes the community respect for him.

PokemonJournal_Text_SpecialFeatureMrFuji.text:
POKéMON JOURNAL\pSpecial Feature:
MR. FUJI of POKéMON HOUSE!\pEditor: The shy MR. FUJI turned
down our interview requests.\pHe is a kindly man who is adored
and respected in LAVENDER TOWN.$

replies.text: He said no, and they still found something kind to print. Good.
Declining an interview does not diminish the care people observe in his work.
He does not owe a magazine his story.
I like that his kindness reached people without him having to explain it.
Some people show you who they are by what they do each day.
A man who declined the spotlight and remained visible through his kindness.
A quiet refusal, surrounded by a town's affection.
Observable care is a stronger account than a forced interview.
He can leave a page blank and still be known gently.
I am glad they printed the refusal without treating it like a scandal.
I would rather notice how the Pokemon settle near him than make him pose.

contexts.subject: The base owner accepts that the player cannot battle now.

replies.text: No battle today, and the ceiling has stayed up. A very successful refusal.
The owner accepts the present limitation without requiring an explanation.
Not now is enough. Good that they leave it there.
I like not having to turn a small no into a whole account of my day.
We can still enjoy visiting without making it another task for the team.
A proposed battle has quietly returned to being a perfectly ordinary visit.
The challenge has withdrawn without attempting to haunt the rest of the afternoon.
We can decide on a challenge later when the team is ready.
A welcoming room can keep its warmth after an invitation is declined.
They seem disappointed, but they haven't made us responsible for fixing that.
I'd be happy to ask about the base itself instead, if the owner feels like talking.

contexts.subject: The owner asks for an opinion of the base and invites a visit tomorrow.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer0PostBattle.text: What do you think of my SECRET BASE?\nCome visit me again tomorrow.$

replies.text: They've moved from battling to the very serious question of whether we like the room.
The invitation is for another visit. This message doesn't establish a particular battle result.
A friendly return invitation. We can look around properly now.
I'd find one small detail I genuinely liked rather than give a vague compliment.
It feels nice to be wanted back for more than a single match.
The combat report has been replaced by a request for an interior review. A pleasant change.
Tomorrow has received an invitation. It remains entitled to arrive at its own pace.
I'd ask which part of the arrangement took the most effort.
A little hidden room can become familiar through the promise of another hello.
I'd like to know which piece the owner most wanted visitors to notice.
I'd ask how the base has changed since the first day they moved in.

contexts.subject: The owner interprets refusing a battle as not wanting the desirable base location.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer1DeclineBattle.text: Hunh? Is that right?\nYou're not interested in this spot?$

replies.text: We declined a battle, not an entire opinion about the floor plan. Two separate little forms.
Interest in the location doesn't necessarily imply willingness to battle for it now.
A no to battling isn't a claim about wanting the spot.
I'd rather say what I meant than let the conversation quietly choose it for me.
We can admire a place without turning somebody's home into a prize.
A practical refusal has accidentally been entered into the property-interest questionnaire.
The room and the battle have become tangled. No need to let them stay that way.
We should distinguish appreciating the location from agreeing to the proposed contest.
A place can be worth seeing without needing to become ours.
They seem proud of the spot. We don't have to covet it to recognize that.
I'd ask what made them wait for this location, rather than argue about taking it.

contexts.subject: The owner promises the spot only if they move out one day.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer1PostBattle.text: Okay, when I move one day,\nthis place will be yours!$

replies.text: A future home with a very flexible moving date. I wouldn't start carrying boxes yet.
The statement is conditional on the owner's eventual move. No transfer has occurred.
They still live here. Don't treat the promise as a vacant room.
I'd rather they enjoy their place than feel we are waiting outside for it to empty.
A friendly promise doesn't mean either of us needs to plan a move today.
A generous offer whose timetable has been carefully delegated to some unspecified future day.
The lease is imaginary and the vacancy date has declined to introduce itself.
We should leave the arrangement conditional rather than assume any current ownership change.
A possible doorway in the future isn't a room we occupy now.
I'd appreciate the gesture without making their home feel like borrowed space.
I'd ask where they'd like to go if they ever did decide to move.

contexts.subject: The sociable base owner invites the player to ask for a battle when ready.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer2DeclineBattle.text: When you're ready, give me a shout!$

replies.text: The battle can wait for our shout. I may send a polite indoor voice instead.
The owner leaves initiation with us. A future attempt remains optional.
Good. We can ask when we're ready.
I like having time to look around without feeling the invitation is counting down.
No need to hurry the team just because someone else is eager.
A refreshingly clear arrangement: the host is available, and our readiness gets a vote.
The challenge has settled into a chair instead of following us around the room.
We can inspect the team's condition before taking up the offer.
A door left open doesn't need to pull anyone through it.
The invitation stays friendly because it isn't trying to become an obligation.
I'd ask about a favorite decoration while we decide what we want to do.

contexts.subject: The owner wants furniture and decorations that make the base enjoyable for visitors.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer2PostBattle.text: Well, anyway, I should go buy some\ndecorations and furniture.\pI want my SECRET BASE to be a place\nother people can enjoy.$

replies.text: A secret base with guest comfort in the budget. That's a very nice kind of secret.
The owner connects personal choices with other people's experience of the room. Considerate design.
Make it somewhere people can settle. Doesn't have to be expensive.
I'd like a small quiet place where a shy visitor doesn't feel stuck in the middle.
A comfortable seat and room for the partners could do more than an impressive display.
A battle host has remembered the excellent possibility of entertaining people without battling them.
An interior scheme containing the radical idea that guests have feet and need places to put them.
I'd ask what visitors actually do in the space before choosing the next pieces.
A little room changes when someone makes space for another person's ease.
I'd help choose one welcoming focal point instead of filling every spare tile.
I'd ask a returning visitor which detail made them feel most at home.

contexts.subject: The owner wonders whether finding the hidden base has left the player tired.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer3DeclineBattle.text: Oh… Are you maybe tired from searching\nfor this place?$

replies.text: They've considered that the journey might have used up our spare battling legs. Thoughtful host.
Fatigue is proposed as a possibility, not established by this question.
Could be tired. Either way, we don't need a battle now.
I like that the first guess is considerate instead of accusing us of being afraid.
A host who notices the trip can be part of the effort has the right idea.
The invitation has been replaced by the sensible suspicion that visitors also possess limited stamina.
At last, someone acknowledging that a hidden address creates an errand.
We can check the team's condition rather than simply accept or reject the guess.
Being found can be a welcome without becoming another demand.
They've made room for the visitor's day instead of only thinking about their own plans.
I'd ask how most people find the place. There may be several rather different arrival stories.

contexts.subject: The owner asks about the player base and expresses interest in visiting.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer3PostBattle.text: Where's your SECRET BASE?\nI should go visit you there.$

replies.text: A hidden-house visit has become a possible exchange of hidden-house directions. Very neighborly.
The owner proposes reciprocity without claiming a visit has already been arranged.
Nice offer. We can share directions if we want company.
I'd want a little time to make the place feel ready for someone else to see.
A visit can be nicer when both people get a turn being the host.
The secret-base community has discovered the complicated diplomatic business of returning a visit.
Two hidden addresses attempting to establish ordinary neighborly relations.
We should agree on the invitation and actual location before treating it as a plan.
One small doorway can make another one feel less far away.
I'd enjoy seeing what the owner notices in our choices after showing us their own.
I'd ask what kind of detail they most enjoy discovering in someone else's base.

contexts.subject: The owner accepts that people are not always in the mood to battle.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer4DeclineBattle.text: I guess there are times when you're not\ninto it.$

replies.text: An excellent discovery: even an enthusiastic trainer can have a not-today pocket.
The owner recognizes that interest varies with circumstances. A reasonable response.
Exactly. No need to turn a quiet day into a test.
I like hearing someone say that as though it is ordinary. Because it is.
Being fond of battling doesn't mean every visit has to become one.
A host has successfully distinguished an enduring interest from an endless obligation to demonstrate it.
The mood has been allowed to exist without submitting a written defense.
We can choose a better time rather than force a less prepared attempt.
An open hand can remain open while the person beside it rests.
That response makes me more comfortable accepting an invitation on another day.
I'd be happy simply talking about what they've been enjoying lately.

contexts.subject: The owner encourages mutual improvement after the battle.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer4PostBattle.text: We can both become stronger.\nLet's keep at it!$

replies.text: Both of us can get stronger. I like a conclusion with room for everybody's next try.
The response frames the encounter as shared development rather than a final ranking.
Good attitude. Take one useful lesson each and keep going.
It's nice when a battle ends without somebody needing the other person to feel small.
I'd rather leave with an idea to practice than only a number to defend.
A competitive meeting has produced a cooperative conclusion. An excellent use of opponents.
Two trainers have survived a comparison without becoming permanent categories.
We can identify a specific improvement instead of treating stronger as an undefined demand.
Two paths can sharpen each other without needing to become the same path.
I like the shared direction in that encouragement. It feels generous.
