I'd ask what they noticed changing during the match. That could give both sides something to work on.

contexts.subject: The base owner quietly accepts that a battle cannot happen now.

replies.text: The battle has been put away without making the whole visit feel canceled.
The present refusal is accepted. The message doesn't establish any loss of future access.
No fight now. We can still be courteous guests.
The small pause sounds disappointed, but not angry. I appreciate that.
A kind no can leave the rest of the afternoon perfectly usable.
An invitation has been declined with no attempt to turn the answer into a grand insult.
The challenge has receded peacefully into the furniture.
We can decide later whether this is a suitable time for a match.
A quiet answer can leave the room just as warm as before it.
I'd rather acknowledge the disappointment than pretend the offer never mattered.
I'd ask what the owner most likes about this particular place.

contexts.subject: The owner invites the player to visit again when passing through the area.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer5PostBattle.text: If you're in this area again,\nI hope you'll visit me.$

replies.text: A little place has become somewhere we might stop instead of merely somewhere we found once.
The invitation is conditional on a future journey through the area. No appointment is implied.
Good reason to remember the turn next time we're nearby.
I like the easy kind of invitation that doesn't make distance feel like neglect.
A friendly stop can give a long trip a different shape.
A home has quietly promoted itself to a welcome landmark on future journeys.
The hidden address has acquired a repeat visitor policy. Quite civilized.
We should remember the actual location if we want to take up the offer later.
A familiar greeting can wait along a road without asking the road to bend toward it.
The wording feels relaxed. It leaves us welcome without keeping count.
I'd ask whether the base changes much between visits. There may always be something new to notice.

contexts.subject: The private battle researcher accepts postponing the match.

replies.text: The research has been postponed. I hope the notebook has a box for visitor-not-in-the-mood.
No trial occurred, so there is no battle evidence to interpret from this visit.
Another time. Better than a reluctant test match.
I'm glad being curious about the lab doesn't make us responsible for supplying an experiment.
A good host leaves room for somebody to be a guest instead of a useful opponent.
The secret laboratory has accepted the regrettable temporary shortage of willing test subjects.
Science will have to endure a moment without making us its immediate problem.
The owner can use the time to refine the question they want a future battle to test.
A paused experiment needn't become an unwelcome room.
They accepted the answer neatly. That makes me more curious about talking again.
I'd ask what they most want to learn from their next match.

contexts.subject: The battle researcher thanks the player and invites another visit tomorrow.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer6PostBattle.text: Thanks for battling with me.\nPlease come back again tomorrow.$

replies.text: A thank-you from the secret lab. I hope our contribution is filed under helpful visitor rather than unusual specimen.
The completed match offers observations. A repeat visit could test a revised idea.
Good. Learn something from the match before asking for another.
I like that the thanks comes before the next invitation.
A useful practice partner should be appreciated as a person, too.
The experiment concludes with gratitude and a politely requested sequel. Sound academic manners.
Our participation has earned a thank-you and possible future employment as a difficult question.
The owner can review the match and choose one change to investigate next time.
A shared effort can leave something worth returning to, without making tomorrow a debt.
I'd hope the next visit includes a little of what they've discovered since this one.
I'd ask which result surprised them most before leaving.

contexts.subject: The decoration-loving owner openly expresses disappointment after a battle refusal.

replies.text: A little disappointment is allowed. It doesn't mean we have to buy it a battle.
The feeling is stated without a further demand. We can acknowledge it and keep our choice.
They're disappointed. Our answer can still stay no.
I feel the little sting in that pause, but I don't think a guilty yes would help.
I'd be kind without treating their mood as something we're obliged to repair.
The invitation has met an ordinary disappointment, mercifully without becoming a contract dispute.
A feeling has been announced. It has not thereby become an instruction.
A later match can be considered on its own merits, not as compensation.
A small cloud can cross a friendly room without becoming its whole sky.
I'd let the honest feeling exist instead of hurrying to make it look happier.
I'd ask about the room only if the owner still felt like sharing it.

contexts.subject: The owner treats the match as fun and turns toward shopping afterward.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer7PostBattle.text: That was all in good fun!\nI should go enjoy shopping now.$

replies.text: Battle finished, next adventure: a very dangerous encounter with a cushion display.
The owner can move between interests without making the battle define the entire day.
Enjoyed the match and ready to move on. Sensible.
I like that the afternoon can contain a serious effort and something light afterward.
A little ordinary pleasure can be a good way to leave a hard match behind.
The competitive appointment has concluded. Decorative acquisition is now accepting visitors.
The Pokemon can rest while the furniture experiences the pressure.
I'd suggest a clear idea of what the room needs before browsing everything at once.
A day can keep more than one kind of enjoyment without making them compete.
I'd ask what they feel is missing from the room before choosing another piece.
I'd love to hear which object they come home pleased to have found.

contexts.subject: The owner leaves the battle offer open for another time.

replies.text: A standing battle invitation. I hope it has comfortable shoes.
The statement leaves a later challenge possible, rather than establishing a current obligation.
Good. We'll ask if the time is right.
I like being welcome without having to decide immediately.
We can enjoy the visit and keep the team's readiness separate from the host's enthusiasm.
The challenge has adopted a flexible schedule, an excellent improvement in hospitality.
A battle offer willing to sit quietly until needed. Unusually considerate offer.
We can review our plans before deciding whether another match fits.
An invitation can remain present without standing in the doorway.
That kind of patience makes a return visit feel easier.
I'd ask what other parts of the base the owner enjoys showing visitors.

contexts.subject: The owner promises to remain competitive at collecting decorations and invites another visit.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer8PostBattle.text: I won't lose at collecting decorations.\nCome visit again!$

replies.text: The battle has ended, but the cushions have apparently entered a much longer tournament.
Decoration collecting is the owner's next competitive focus. No collection result is established here.
A room should still be useful, not just a score against someone else.
I hope they keep choosing things they like, even when nobody is comparing collections.
A favorite object can be worth more than the one bought only to beat a rival.
One contest has ended and another has immediately recruited the household furnishings.
The shelves have been informed that victory remains compulsory. Poor shelves.
We could ask which piece serves the room best instead of ranking sheer quantity.
A collected thing deserves a place beyond proving somebody else has less.
I'd want the base to show the owner's taste rather than the opponent they imagined while shopping.
I'd ask which decoration they'd keep if the competition vanished tomorrow.

contexts.subject: The style-conscious owner offers to demonstrate battle style another time.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer9DeclineBattle.text: I'll be happy to demonstrate my style\nanytime.$

replies.text: The demonstration has a flexible curtain time. I appreciate that in a person's living room.
The owner offers a future demonstration. We haven't seen a new battle from this refusal.
Another time can work. No need to perform for us now.
I like being allowed to look at the room without immediately joining the next event.
A style is easier to appreciate when the person leaves room for the visitor's mood.
A postponed display, with the owner's enthusiasm apparently sufficient to preserve it indefinitely.
The style remains available by appointment. Merciful arrangement.
We can decide whether a future match suits the team rather than answer under pressure.
Something worth showing can wait until another person is ready to look.
I'd enjoy asking about the choices themselves before judging the whole impression.
I'd ask what the owner most wants an opponent to notice about their approach.

contexts.subject: The owner asks about their battle style and intends to keep refining it.

SecretBase_Text_Trainer9PostBattle.text: What did you think of my style?\nI'll keep on polishing it!$

replies.text: They've asked for a review and already booked more polishing time. A productive little mirror.
Continued refinement suggests the owner treats style as something developed through feedback.
Give a useful observation. Flattery won't improve the next match.
I'd find one thing that felt distinctly theirs and say why it stayed with me.
A specific kind comment can help more than calling the whole thing perfect.
A performance has concluded with an unusually practical request for an opinion that might improve it.
The style has survived being tested and is reporting for further maintenance.
We can distinguish what worked from what simply looked impressive.
A chosen way of moving can become clearer each time it meets another person's answer.
I'd ask which part they most want to develop, then respond to that rather than redesign everything.
I'd describe one turning point clearly. It gives the owner something concrete to think about.

contexts.subject: A reporter praises the players bond with their Pokemon and promises an entertaining television story.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_ThatsA.text:
Wow…
That's an interesting account.\pYou really are tight with {STR_VAR_1},
aren't you?\pI get the feeling that your account
will make a great TV story.\pI promise that I'll turn this into
an entertaining show.\lKeep your eyes out for it.\pOkay, that's all.
Bye-bye!$

replies.text: They heard about our friend and found a whole show in it. That is lovely.
Our firsthand account has given the reporter something specific to work with.
Hope the show treats our partner fairly. Good conversation.
It is a little strange thinking our small story might be on TV.
A story about a cared-for partner sounds worth sharing.
Our ordinary affection has been offered an unexpectedly public audience.
Our Pokemon may become famous before it has formed an opinion on fame.
A clear account should help make the final story accurate.
Something personal has been met with warm curiosity.
I hope the finished story keeps the kindness they heard in it.
I would love to see which detail they choose to open with.

contexts.subject: A museum reporter finds the players story uplifting and plans a television version.

SlateportCity_OceanicMuseum_1F_Text_That.text: Oh, what an uplifting story!\pI'll be sure to get your story told\non television.\pIt should be aired sometime, I think,\nso please look forward to it.$

replies.text: An uplifting story is a good thing to send out into people's afternoons.
A positive account could be pleasant to share with a wider audience.
Glad they found something good in it. Hope they tell it straight.
I would be shy about watching the first time.
A good story can leave someone a little happier than it found them.
The conversation is complete, and the reporter has acquired a hopeful ending.
A small bright thing has apparently qualified for broadcast.
I would be interested in how they turn the account into a clear story.
A little hope can travel farther than the people who first felt it.
It is lovely hearing that the account meant something to its listener.
I would keep an eye out to see how the story comes across.

contexts.subject: A reporter thanks the player for an enlightening Pokemon conversation and mentions possible TV coverage.

SlateportCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_ThatsA.text:
I see!\pHmhm…\pOkay!
Thanks for helping me out.\pIt was fun and enlightening
chatting with you.\pIt's possible that our interview will
end up on TV. Tune in and check!\pOkay, that's all.
Bye-bye!$

replies.text: We had a nice talk and may accidentally become part of the television. Busy day.
An enjoyable interview can still produce useful observations.
Good talk. They got the answers they needed.
I appreciate being told the conversation was enjoyable.
Sharing what we notice about our partners can be a good afternoon.
Our conversation has ended with gratitude and the possibility of a second audience.
The interview was pleasant. The prospect of television can panic quietly later.
It is good when both sides leave a conversation with something useful.
Being listened to can make a familiar thought feel newly worth sharing.
A friendly exchange deserves a friendly ending like that.
I would enjoy comparing what we meant with what they put in the program.

contexts.subject: A reporter thanks the player for their interpretation of a contest concept and possible TV story ideas.

LilycoveCity_ContestLobby_Text_ThatsAllF.text:
I see!\pSo that's how you imagine the concept
of “{STR_VAR_2}” to be.\pThank you!
You've given me some good ideas.\pI think I can write a good story on
POKéMON CONTESTS now.\pMaybe, just maybe, this story will even
make it to television.\lI hope you'll look forward to it!$

replies.text: Our idea gave them another idea. Thoughts are very good at making little cousins.
Different interpretations can give a familiar subject a useful new angle.
Glad the answer helped. They can build from it.
It feels nice when an awkward explanation actually makes sense to someone.
A shared idea can become something neither person had alone.
Our brief interpretation has volunteered for a possible career in television.
The thought has left our head and acquired professional ambitions.
A fresh perspective can be more useful than repeating the usual description.
One person's impression can open a little space in another's thinking.
An interesting interpretation can change the whole look of a story.
I would be curious which part of our answer stays with them.

contexts.subject: Mr Briney thanks the player for rescuing Peeko, offers help and takes the bird home; field control returns after departure.

RusturfTunnel_Text_ThankYouLetsGoHomePee.text:
PEEKO owes her life to you!\pThey call me MR. BRINEY.
And, you are?\p… … … … … … … …
… … … … … … … …\pAh, so you are {PLAYER}{KUN}!
I sincerely thank you!\pNow, if there's anything that troubles
you, don't hesitate to tell me!\pYou can usually find me in my cottage
by the sea near PETALBURG WOODS.\pCome, PEEKO, we should make our way
home.\pPEEKO: Pihyoh!$

replies.text: Peeko is going home. That little chirp is the best part of the whole cave.
The rescue is complete, and the gratitude seems deeply sincere.
Glad Peeko is safe. They can get home now.
The way he calls her home is so gentle.
Someone getting their beloved friend back is worth the trouble.
A frightened little story has found a warm cottage to end in.
The cave has finally produced a thoroughly welcome goodbye.
Good to know the rescue ended with both of them able to leave safely.
One small life has made the whole tunnel feel lighter.
That is a lovely reunion to have helped bring about.
I would remember how his voice changed once Peeko was safe.

contexts.subject: Normal and Gold Card nurse farewells have byte-identical text and return to the map caller, which only waits and releases.

gText_WeHopeToSeeYouAgain.text: We hope to see you again!$

gText_WeHopeToSeeYouAgain2.text: We hope to see you again!$

replies.text: A friendly goodbye from somewhere our partners are welcome. Good place to remember.
It is reassuring to know this help remains available when needed.
Good people to have nearby. We can head on.
I like leaving a place that made us feel welcome.
Kind service can make a busy day feel a little gentler.
A familiar farewell from one of the most dependable stops on the road.
An invitation worth keeping for a day that goes less smoothly.
Reliable help is an excellent thing to know how to find.
A warm doorway can matter long after we walk through it.
Courtesy makes even a quick visit feel more comfortable.
I would remember the welcome as much as the building.

contexts.subject: A nurse explains a possible Pokerus infection and the limited knowledge of its microscopic life-forms and reported growth effect.

gText_PokerusExplanation.text:
Your POKéMON may be infected with
POKéRUS.\pLittle is known about the POKéRUS
except that they are microscopic life-\lforms that attach to POKéMON.\pWhile infected, POKéMON are said to
grow exceptionally well.$

replies.text: Tiny life-forms with a big effect. Our partner has become even more surprising.
A fascinating observation. I appreciate that the nurse stated what remains uncertain.
Good that she told us. Keep an eye on our partner.
That is unexpected. I would want to know how our friend is feeling.
I am glad someone knowledgeable explained what they noticed.
A very small discovery has made our familiar companion newly mysterious.
The microscopic world has made a rather conspicuous entrance.
Something we cannot see can still change a great deal. Remarkable.
There are lives within the little lives we already know.
A surprising detail does not change how carefully we should treat our partner.
I would ask what the nurse has observed in other Pokemon.

contexts.subject: A shopkeeper or service clerk politely ends the visit with an invitation to return.

replies.text: A cheerful goodbye. We can come back when the next little errand finds us.
A pleasant conclusion to the visit. The service remains available.
All done here. Thank them and move on.
It is nice leaving with a welcome for another day.
Friendly service makes an ordinary errand a little better.
Our business concludes with a courteous invitation for the sequel.
A tidy farewell, free of any obligation to keep browsing.
Useful place to remember if we need something later.
A small kindness can sit comfortably inside an ordinary goodbye.
Good manners are always a lovely final touch.
I would remember a place that made the visit feel easy.

contexts.subject: A shared gift refusal reports that Pokemon boxes are full and cannot receive another partner.

gText_NoMoreRoomForPokemon.text: There's no more room for POKéMON!\pThe POKéMON BOXES are full and\ncan't accept any more!$

replies.text: There is no proper space for a new friend yet. We should sort that first.
Available care space needs checking before another Pokemon can be accepted.
Make room before taking on another partner.
I would want a place ready before welcoming anyone new.
A new partner deserves more than being squeezed into the last gap.
Our hoped-for new arrival must wait for suitable accommodation.
The practical arrangements have caught up with our enthusiasm.
A capacity problem should be solved before repeating the handoff.
Make a little room with care for those already with us.
A proper welcome begins with an actual place to belong.
I would make the necessary space before asking to try again.

contexts.subject: A traveler explains using Secret Power at suitable trees or indented rock walls to make a personal base, then leaves.

Route111_Text_ExplainSecretPower.text:
Find a big tree that looks like it might
drop some vines.\pUse SECRET POWER in front of the tree.
Some vines should get free and drop\ldown, so you can climb the tree.\pYou'll find a lot of space for putting
your favorite things.\pIt'll be your own secret room…
A SECRET BASE!\pYou should make one, too.\pAnother thing, you don't always have
to make your SECRET BASE in a tree.\pTry using SECRET POWER on rock walls
that have small indents in them.\pI'm going to look for other places, too.
Okay, bye!$

replies.text: A secret room with room for favorite things. I would start with a very good chair.
The surroundings offer clues to suitable sites. An interesting use of the move.
Check the place before settling in. A safe spot comes first.
A little quiet room of our own sounds rather lovely.
A comfortable corner to share with a partner could be wonderful.
An ordinary tree has just acquired the possibility of a private address.
A hidden room is an excellent way to keep the outside at a polite distance.
I would like to compare what different sites let us arrange inside.
A chosen place can become familiar through the small things we bring.
A whole space for personal taste? That is a very convincing invitation.
I would enjoy seeing what makes each traveler choose their spot.

contexts.subject: The Record Corner attendant thanks a visitor after records have already been mixed and ends the conversation.

replies.text: A friendly thank-you after sharing. Nice to have a calm ending.
The exchange is complete. A courteous conclusion is welcome.
All finished. Thank them before heading out.
I like a simple goodbye after meeting people.
A visit can be worthwhile without needing to last longer.
Our shared session concludes with a refreshingly modest farewell.
The records have mixed; we may now stop being socially coordinated.
Everything for this visit seems to be settled.
A small thanks can let the whole encounter rest kindly.
A graceful ending makes the visit feel well received.
I would leave with a friendly word for the people who helped.

contexts.subject: A link attendant apologizes because the Wireless Club is undergoing adjustments.

gText_SorryWirelessClubAdjustments.text: I'm terribly sorry.\nThe POKéMON WIRELESS CLUB is\lundergoing adjustments now.$

replies.text: The club is still getting its bits in order. We can try another day.
Work is still underway, so the service is not available yet.
Not ready. We can come back later.
At least they explained why we cannot go in.
A little patience now may make a better visit later.
Our anticipated gathering has been postponed by necessary preparations.
The club has requested a little more time to become a club.
Better to finish the adjustments than invite people into a faulty setup.
The invitation can wait until the place is ready to welcome us.
An unfinished arrangement is best left to the people fixing it.
I would check back after they have had time to finish.

contexts.subject: A Colosseum attendant gives seating instructions and returns player control; battle is initiated separately at the seats.

BattleColosseum_2P_Text_TakePlaceStartBa.text: Please take your place and start\nyour battle.$

replies.text: We have our instructions. The seats are waiting more patiently than I am.
Taking the designated positions should let both participants begin together.
Get into position. Make sure the other trainer is ready.
A clear place to stand makes the start less awkward.
A fair start is easier when everyone knows where to go.
The competitors have been directed to their respective opening positions.
Our dramatic opening now requires the rather ordinary act of sitting down.
Clear positions help keep the start coordinated.
A little order gives both sides the same first moment.
We should take our places without crowding the other participant.
I would check that the other trainer heard the same instructions.

contexts.subject: A Trade Center attendant gives seating instructions and returns player control before a separate trade interaction.

TradeCenter_Text_TakeSeatStartTrade.text: Please take your seat and start\nyour trade.$

replies.text: A proper place to arrange the trade. Much better than juggling Pokeballs in a doorway.
Both participants should confirm the arrangement before starting.
Take the seats. Make sure the trade is understood.
I would want everyone comfortable with the choice first.
A careful exchange is worth taking a moment over.
The proposed exchange has acquired its own designated meeting place.
The paperwork of friendship apparently begins with a chair.
A clear setup should make the handoff easier to follow.
A new beginning deserves care from both sides.
A tidy arrangement helps everyone feel certain about the exchange.
I would make sure both trainers know what they are agreeing to.

contexts.subject: A Record Corner attendant asks visitors to take a seat and wait; field conversation ends before separate record-mixing input.

RecordCorner_Text_TakeSeatAndWait.text: Please take your seat and wait.$

replies.text: A seat and a little patience. Finally, instructions my feet can follow.
Waiting in the designated place should help the group coordinate.
Take a seat. Give everyone time to get ready.
I can manage a quiet wait much better with a clear place to be.
A small rest while everyone gathers sounds welcome.
Our gathering has entered the dignified sitting portion of proceedings.
A rare official instruction to sit quietly. I intend to excel.
A common waiting point makes the next step simpler for everyone.
A little pause can give a shared visit a gentler beginning.
Patience is easier to wear when there is somewhere comfortable to sit.
I would take the moment to see whether anyone else needs help.

contexts.subject: Mom's attached letter cheers the player on and sends Running Shoes for the journey.

PewterCity_Text_RunningShoesLetterFromMo.text: There's a letter attached…\pDear {PLAYER},\pHere is a pair of RUNNING SHOES\nfor my beloved challenger.\pRemember, I'll always cheer for\nyou! Don't ever give up!\pFrom Mom$

replies.text: Shoes and a cheering section small enough to fold up beside them. She packed both kinds of support.
The practical gift and the written encouragement address rather different needs. Both were thoughtfully chosen.
She wants us ready for the road, and to know somebody is on our side.
I would keep the letter somewhere dry, even after the shoes feel familiar.
A useful gift keeps helping all day. The note might help on the days the walking feels harder.
The expedition has received equipment and a beautifully unambiguous endorsement from home.
A small piece of paper can make the distance back home feel less absolute.
Good equipment matters. So does having someone who wants to see what you manage with it.
Her words can travel farther than her voice, tucked quietly into the journey.
She has put love into something we can actually wear out through living. That is a lovely gift.
I wonder what ordinary moment will make us unfold the letter and read it again.

contexts.subject: A convincing Pokemon doll is briefly mistaken for a rare Pokemon.

SaffronCity_CopycatsHouse_2F_Text_RareMo.text: This is a rare POKéMON!\nHuh? It's only a doll!$

replies.text: An exceptionally successful doll. It has completed a whole encounter without moving a stitch.
The resemblance was convincing enough to produce a mistaken first identification. Closer inspection helped.
A good imitation. Leave it where its owner put it.
The little surprise makes me appreciate how carefully somebody made it.
Only a doll seems a little unfair after it worked that hard to fool us.
A remarkably accomplished understudy has secured the audience's attention while remaining entirely stuffed.
A brief disappointment, followed by respect for a very persuasive piece of fabric.
The proportions and details must be doing their job. That is effective design.
A small made thing has borrowed the shape of wonder for a moment.
Only a doll? That is a rather good compliment to the person who designed it.
I would like to know which detail fooled us before we looked closely.

contexts.subject: Lorelei's house contains a large collection of stuffed Pokemon dolls.

replies.text: That is a magnificent amount of soft company. A difficult day would have trouble finding an empty chair.
A personal collection can reveal interests that a public role leaves little opportunity to show.
Her home. She is allowed somewhere comfortable to return to.
I like seeing a room that holds something its owner simply enjoys.
A home should have room for delights that do not have to earn their place.
The formidable public figure has a private supporting cast made almost entirely of stuffing.
An admirable refusal to make the living room uphold a severe reputation.
There must be interesting little differences between all the designs collected here.
A strong person's quiet room can still be full of soft things.
A collection this fondly kept says more than a carefully managed public image.
I wonder which doll started the collection, before it became a whole roomful of favourites.

contexts.subject: The museum displays a clear gold-coloured piece of amber.

PewterCity_Museum_1F_Text_BeautifulPiece.text: There is a beautiful piece of\nAMBER in a clear gold color.$

replies.text: It looks as though somebody persuaded a little sunlight to sit still for the museum.
Its clarity lets us appreciate the material itself, quite apart from anything it might contain.
Worth a quiet look. The display does not need us tapping on it.
I like the warmth of that colour against the stillness of the case.
A beautiful small thing can make a slow walk through a museum worthwhile.
A modest exhibit with an exceptionally accomplished lighting effect supplied by the object itself.
A little gold-coloured stillness. It need not contain a grand secret to be worth keeping.
The transparency is lovely. It would be interesting to see how the surface scatters light.
An old piece of the world has kept a warm-looking corner of itself.
A single clear colour can hold attention better than an overcrowded display.
I wonder how different it looks as the light shifts across the room.

contexts.subject: Lanette is embarrassed by research clutter and gives a doll while asking for discretion; success ends after ignored decoration receipt.

Route114_LanettesHouse_Text_EverythingCl.text: LANETTE: Oh! {PLAYER}{KUN}!\pI'm sorry everything is so cluttered…\nWhen I get engrossed in research,\lthings end up this way…\pThis is embarrassing… Please keep\nthis a secret in exchange for this.$

replies.text: Her research made a nest. The doll is lovely, but the secret was safe already.
A busy work area is hardly a scandal. No payment for discretion was necessary.
Her house, her business. We do not need a gift to keep quiet.
I would be embarrassed about my own clutter too. We can be kind.
A little mess happens when someone gets absorbed in work.
An earnest researcher has attempted to purchase our silence with a small doll.
The room contains evidence of thinking. A grave and entirely forgivable offense.
I recognize that particular arrangement of an unfinished project.
We need not carry an awkward moment farther than this room.
A cluttered workspace is no reason to make someone feel exposed.
I would thank her and put away any thought of making this a story.

contexts.subject: A receptionist congratulates the winning Pokemon and gives the pending prize; terminal on successful prize pickup.

LilycoveCity_ContestLobby_Text_PokemonWo.text: Congratulations! Your POKéMON is the\nCONTEST winner!\pWe have your prize right here.\nPlease, right this way!$

replies.text: Our partner won! I hope they know the congratulations are for them too.
A result worth enjoying, and a well organized way to collect the reward.
Good work from our partner. Give them some credit.
Hearing the official congratulations makes it feel real again.
A little celebration for the partner who worked so hard.
The victory has acquired both formal recognition and something to carry home.
Our partner's triumph has successfully completed its administrative phase.
The preparation paid off. It is nice to see that acknowledged.
A pleased little moment deserves time before the next challenge.
A prize is lovely, but that proud partner is the best part.
I would remember our Pokemon's reaction when the congratulations arrive.

contexts.subject: The treasure hunter confirms a completed shard trade; terminal when the player has no further shards.

Route124_DivingTreasureHuntersHouse_Text.text: It's a done deal!\nUse that wisely!$

replies.text: Our little shard has become something useful. A tidy treasure exchange.
The exchange is complete. We can consider how best to use the result.
Fair trade. Keep the new item safe.
I like leaving with the arrangement clearly settled.
A useful find feels even better when it leads to something we need.
The treasure's story has moved neatly into another pair of hands.
One little fragment has negotiated an impressively complete future.
Good to know exactly what we gained from the exchange.
Something found can become the beginning of another useful thing.
A well chosen exchange makes the search feel worthwhile.
I would ask what the hunter plans to do with the shard.

contexts.subject: A woman recognizes the Pokemons extraordinary effort with an Effort Ribbon; root whitelists both named success receipts afterward.

SlateportCity_Text_PleaseGiveItThisEffor.text: Went for it stupendously!\pAs its reward, please give it this\nEFFORT RIBBON.$

replies.text: A ribbon for working so hard. Our friend deserves a very proud little moment.
Recognition for sustained effort is a meaningful kind of reward.
They earned it. Make sure our partner gets the thanks.
I like a ribbon that notices the work behind the result.
All those little days of effort have become something they can wear.
The quiet accumulation of hard work has finally received a visible tribute.
A ribbon for persistence. I rather like that kind of ornament.
Consistent practice can be hard to see until someone recognizes it.
Effort leaves its marks. This one happens to be lovely.
That ribbon belongs with a proud partner and a proper compliment.
I would love to remember how our Pokemon looks wearing it.

contexts.subject: A shared NPC gift or purchase failure says the bag is full; reply applies only where no later conversation replaces it.

replies.text: The bag has reached its maximum amount of yes. Time to find one little space.
The immediate problem is capacity. A little sorting should resolve it.
Bag is full. Make room before trying again.
At least the reason is clear. We can sort it out quietly.
We can clear a little room before asking for anything else.
Our eager collecting has met the entirely reasonable limits of the bag.
The bag has declined further responsibility until we become more organized.
Check what we are carrying before repeating the same attempt.
A little empty space can make the next small kindness easier to receive.
An edit to the bag would improve the whole arrangement.
I would make room first, then return to finish what we started.

contexts.subject: An attendant explains the Union Room, Direct Corner, nearby connections and cable alternative, then ends the conversation.

CableClub_Text_ExplainWirelessClub.text:
Let me explain how the POKéMON
WIRELESS CLUB works.\pOn this, the top floor, there are
two rooms.\pFirst, the room on the left.
It's the UNION ROOM.\pYou may link up with TRAINERS
around you who have also entered\lthe UNION ROOM.\pWith them, you may do things like
chat, battle, and trade.\pSecond, the room on the right is
the DIRECT CORNER.\pYou may trade or battle POKéMON
with your friends in this room.\pSometimes, you may not be able to
find your friends in the UNION ROOM\lor the DIRECT CORNER.\pIn that case, please move closer
to your friends.\pIf the Wireless Adapter isn't
connected, you may still link up\lusing a GBA Game Link cable.\pIf that is the case, you must go
to the DIRECT CORNER.\pI hope you enjoy the Wireless 
Communication System.$

replies.text: Two rooms, several things to do, and one very patient explainer. We have directions now.
A clear distinction between the rooms and their connection requirements.
Pick what we want to do before choosing the room.
I appreciate being told how it works before having to try.
A little preparation will make meeting up much easier.
Our social expedition has acquired both a floor plan and some practical instructions.
An admirably thorough defense against wandering into the wrong room.
Clear room functions and a useful troubleshooting step. Good explanation.
Knowing how to meet can leave more room to enjoy the company.
A well explained arrangement makes a new place feel less awkward.
I would check where our friends plan to go before choosing a room.

contexts.subject: An attendant accepts declining the explanation and wishes an enjoyable visit.

CableClub_Text_HopeYouEnjoyWirelessSyste.text: I hope you enjoy the Wireless\nCommunication System.$

replies.text: We can skip the explanation and keep the friendly send-off. Nice.
The information remains available if we discover we need it.
We know enough for now. Good to know we can ask.
I like not being made to listen when I am already ready.
A warm welcome can be brief and still feel thoughtful.
The optional lecture has gracefully become an uncomplicated good wish.
Our existing knowledge has been permitted to survive without another introduction.
We can try it and return with specific questions if needed.
A kind wish is a pleasant thing to carry into a gathering.
A gracious response that leaves us comfortable choosing for ourselves.
I hope everyone gets the chance to enjoy meeting their friends here.

contexts.subject: The Union Room attendant says the Wireless Adapter is not properly connected and invites a return.

CableClub_Text_UnionRoomAdapterNotConnec.text: This is the POKéMON WIRELESS CLUB\nUNION ROOM.\pUnfortunately, your Wireless\nAdapter is not connected properly.\pPlease do come again.$

replies.text: The room is ready, but our connection is not. Time to check the little attachment.
The adapter connection is the stated problem. We should inspect that first.
Check the adapter. This attempt is finished.
At least they were kind about pointing out the problem.
We can fix the setup before asking to try again.
Our arrival has encountered one small but essential missing connection.
The invitation is open. The hardware is being considerably less sociable.
A clear fault to investigate is better than guessing at the whole system.
A small adjustment may let a postponed meeting begin.
An inconvenient detail, delivered with decent manners.
I would make sure the adapter is fitted properly before we return.

contexts.subject: A rooftop sign makes the extravagant claim that its owner knows everything.

replies.text: Everything? I have several questions about socks that could make this a very long afternoon.
A confident assertion with a rather impossible burden of proof attached.
A sign can say anything. We can judge the advice separately.
I would be more comfortable asking questions if the sign left room for not knowing.
An expert in everything should be useful when dinner refuses to behave.
The shortest autobiography ever written, and possibly the least reliable.
An admirably compact way to leave no room for growth.
Knowing the limits of your knowledge is a much more useful skill.
A very full cup has announced that it contains the entire sea.
A modest sign would apparently have been too large a sacrifice.
I wonder which question its owner most enjoys being challenged with.

contexts.subject: A Silph pamphlet describes TMs and repeatedly usable HMs.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_RoofRoom_Text_P.text: It's a pamphlet on TMs.\p… …\pThere are fifty TMs in all.\pThere are also seven HMs that\ncan be used repeatedly.\pSILPH CO.$

replies.text: A little reading material for people who like their new techniques to come with instructions.
The pamphlet describes its catalogue and usage rules. We should still check the item we actually have.
Useful to read the instructions before relying on a tool.
I like when something unfamiliar comes with a quiet explanation instead of a test.
A quick look at the instructions can save a very avoidable disappointment later.
The manufacturer has supplied a brief practical preface to a shelf of possibilities.
A small pamphlet is preferable to learning every limitation through regret.
Clear instructions make useful equipment much easier to put to work properly.
A few printed words can steady the hand that carries an unfamiliar thing.
The useful part is knowing what something does before choosing it.
I wonder which question made the writer realize that explanation needed to be included.

contexts.subject: A sports game on display seems like something Dad would enjoy.

replies.text: A shop display has turned into a very specific gift idea. That is dangerous for the budget.
Recognizing someone else's tastes is a thoughtful starting point for choosing a gift.
Nice to spot something with another person in mind.
It is sweet when a small familiar detail makes somebody come to mind.
A good gift begins with remembering what the other person enjoys.
The browsing expedition has unexpectedly acquired a warmly personal subplot.
A shelf can briefly make an absent person feel close.
We could check what kind of sports game it is before deciding it would suit him.
A little box has tugged on a thread that runs back home.
Thinking of the person matters more than simply choosing the most expensive thing.
I wonder what ordinary evening together makes that game feel like his kind of thing.

contexts.subject: A fighting game on display looks challenging.

replies.text: Another kind of battling, apparently designed for people whose fingers also need an adventure.
An intimidating appearance does not tell us how approachable the game actually is.
We can look without having to prove anything to a display.
Learning something difficult can be fun when there is room to be clumsy first.
A challenge is easier to enjoy when it is allowed to start as play.
The shelf has offered an alternative venue for being dramatically outmatched.
A small box has managed to look rather more confrontational than necessary.
I would like to see how well it teaches the basics before judging the difficulty.
A make-believe contest can still ask a real little leap of courage.
Looking difficult is one thing. Making people want to try is the more interesting trick.
I wonder whether the players who love it most began by losing rather spectacularly.

contexts.subject: The display offers Red and Green Pokemon games side by side.

replies.text: Two colourful invitations to spend far too long deciding which colourful invitation to take.
The two editions invite comparison. Their packaging alone would not establish every difference.
We can read what each offers before choosing.
I like how two small boxes can suggest different beginnings to the same kind of afternoon.
It is a good excuse to compare interests with a friend before buying anything.
The same premise has dressed for two separate opening nights.
A choice becomes strangely large when both little boxes look inviting.
I would compare the actual contents rather than choose solely by the colour.
Two doors can invite the same curiosity in slightly different coats.
A paired display knows exactly how to make browsing last longer.
I wonder which small difference people end up caring about most after they start playing.

contexts.subject: A Game Corner machine is marked out of order.

replies.text: A machine whose current game is not taking anybody's money. Quite a restful design.
The sign clearly states that the machine is unavailable. No attempt to operate it is warranted.
Leave the broken machine alone. Plenty else to do.
A clear little notice saves an awkward disappointment.
We can spend the time somewhere that does not need a repair first.
The attraction has wisely cancelled its performance rather than improvise a malfunction.
An inactive machine can be remarkably good company in a loud room.
A useful failure notice. Testing it ourselves would not make it more fixed.
This little corner of chance has gone quiet for the day.
It is better to say clearly that something is broken than let people discover it at their expense.
I wonder what the room sounds like when all the machines finally stop for the night.

contexts.subject: A Game Corner seat is reserved while its user is out to lunch.

replies.text: A gaming session has left a note explaining that lunch briefly won the argument.
The sign communicates a temporary absence rather than an abandoned place.
Reserved. Leave it for the person coming back.
I hope the break feels like a proper pause instead of an anxious dash back.
At least somebody has remembered that an afternoon needs lunch in it.
The player has announced an intermission and retained the seat for the next act.
A small note has been asked to sit patiently in somebody else's place.
The message makes the intended use clear without us needing to guess.
An empty chair is holding a little promise of return.
A reservation deserves the same courtesy whether its owner is watching or eating.
I wonder whether the person notices the room differently after stepping outside for a while.

contexts.subject: Keys left by a Game Corner machine indicate that its user plans to return.

replies.text: The keys have been promoted to a tiny and rather important seat-saving assistant.
Personal belongings indicate somebody intends to return. They are not an invitation to investigate.
Leave the keys where their owner expects them.
I would hate to come back and find the one thing I needed to get home had moved.
We can respect the place without touching the owner's belongings.
The absent player has left a surprisingly consequential stand-in.
A small object is doing the important work of being exactly where it was left.
Changing their position would add an unnecessary problem for somebody else.
A little ring of metal is keeping a person's next doorway within reach.
There is no need to make a stranger's afternoon harder just because they stepped away.
I wonder whether they remembered where they left those the moment they reached the door.

contexts.subject: A hidden switch is discovered behind the Game Corner poster and activated.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_SwitchBehind.text: Hey!\pA switch behind the poster!?\nLet's push it!$

replies.text: The poster was doing considerably more work than looking decorative.
The concealed switch confirms that the display was also hiding an access mechanism.
A secret entrance in a public room. Stay alert.
The familiar-looking wall feels different now that we know something was hidden there.
We should think about where the passage leads before hurrying into it.
An innocent piece of scenery has disclosed its second profession.
A very thin layer of normality was covering something less ordinary.
A concealed control is easier to understand now that we can see what it operates.
A flat bright picture has acquired a dark little depth.
The deliberate concealment is more interesting than the poster's sales pitch.
I wonder how many people looked straight at that wall without noticing what it was protecting.

contexts.subject: The Pokemon printer completes a print on the player's Trainer Card.

CeladonCity_GameCorner_Text_PrintIsReady.text: Your POKéMON print is ready!\nCheck your TRAINER CARD.$

replies.text: Our card has acquired a little more company without getting any harder to carry.
The printer reports completion. We can check the resulting image directly on the card.
Done. Have a look before putting the card away.
A small familiar image can make an ordinary card feel much more personal.
A nice little keepsake does not have to be elaborate.
The travelling cast has received its official pocket-sized promotional portrait.
A whole companion reduced to a little image, without losing the reason we like seeing it.
A compact print on an existing card is a neat practical format.
A small likeness has found a place among the ordinary things we carry.
A personal detail makes the card feel more like its owner's.
I like pictures that stay close through ordinary days instead of only appearing for an occasion.

contexts.subject: The Pokemon printer cannot be used because the player lacks the fee.

replies.text: The little photo opportunity has reached the practical end of our pockets.
The payment condition is unmet, so the print has not been produced.
No print today. We can leave it for later.
A disappointing little pause, but the picture does not have to happen right now.
Keep the money for what we need before chasing a keepsake.
The promotional portrait has been delayed by a very small production budget.
A missing fee is allowed to remain a reason to do something else.
The printer needs the payment before its process can begin.
A wanted little image can wait without losing the life it would have shown.
No need to make a small extra feel like an urgent omission.
We still have the real company beside us, even without a new picture on the card.

contexts.subject: Pokemon magazines line a shelf at the volunteer Pokemon house.

LavenderTown_VolunteerPokemonHouse_Text_.text: POKéMON magazines line the shelf.\pPOKéMON INSIDER…\pPOKéMON FAN…$

replies.text: A whole shelf of reading for people whose favourite subject is already wandering around the room.
A collection of specialist magazines can preserve a wider range of interests than one reference book.
A good way to spend a quiet few minutes here.
I like a room with things to read while familiar lives carry on nearby.
A comfortable place needs small pleasures as well as the practical care.
The residents have acquired an admirably enthusiastic periodical section.
A shelf of old magazines can make waiting feel like somewhere to be.
Different issues could show how information and interests changed over time.
Small printed worlds have gathered beside the living ones.
The shelf makes the room feel used rather than merely furnished.
I wonder which issue people keep picking up even after they have read it before.

contexts.subject: A personal note lists Copycat's mimicry, doll collecting, and fondness for Clefairy.

SaffronCity_CopycatsHouse_2F_Text_MySecr.text: …\pMy Secrets!\pSkill: Mimicry!\nHobby: Collecting dolls!\lFavorite POKéMON: CLEFAIRY!$

replies.text: A very small set of secrets, most of which the dolls were already cheerfully giving away.
The note offers a selected self-description. It does not claim to explain the whole person.
We have read enough. No need to rummage for anything more personal.
It is sweet to see the ordinary favourite things behind all that confident imitation.
A few things someone enjoys can make an unfamiliar room feel like theirs.
The self-authored character sketch is brief, clear, and rather well supported by the scenery.
The alleged secrets have left a remarkably visible trail of soft evidence.
The interests are specific enough to remember without needing to turn them into a theory.
A little list has given the room's scattered things a familiar centre.
Her own choices say more than someone else deciding she is merely a clever trick.
I wonder which of those favourites she would spend longest talking about if we asked her.

contexts.subject: A game on display features Mario wearing a bucket on his head.

SaffronCity_CopycatsHouse_2F_Text_MarioW.text: A game with MARIO wearing a bucket\non his head!$

replies.text: The hero has apparently solved a hat shortage in the most resourceful possible way.
An unusual silhouette is certainly an effective way to make a game memorable.
A ridiculous little detail can be a perfectly good reason to enjoy something.
I like that somebody kept a game with such a specific silly image.
The bucket was probably not expecting a career in heroic headwear.
The leading man has made a bold and highly practical costume choice.
Dignity has stepped out while the bucket handles the scene.
Improvised equipment is entertaining when it works in a world built for it.
A very ordinary object has wandered into a much less ordinary story.
An accessory with unmistakable confidence and absolutely no restraint.
I wonder how long it takes before the strange little design starts feeling entirely normal.

contexts.subject: The captain is reading a book about conquering seasickness.

SSAnne_CaptainsOffice_Text_HowToConquerS.text: How to Conquer Seasickness…\nThe CAPTAIN's reading this!$

replies.text: Even the captain has a problem the captain's hat cannot fix on its own.
Seeking information about a difficulty is sensible, regardless of professional experience.
No shame in looking for help with something that keeps troubling him.
It must be tiring to struggle with the very place people expect him to feel most at home.
An ordinary bit of help can matter more than trying to look unbothered.
The seasoned captain's reading list has revealed a thoroughly human complication.
Expertise does not come with a guarantee of comfort. An inconvenient omission.
A reference book is a practical response to a recurring problem.
A person can know the sea well and still find its movement unkind.
Being accomplished should not mean having to hide every difficulty.
I wonder whether he feels more relieved by useful advice or simply knowing other sailors struggle too.

contexts.subject: Looking into the captain's bin proves unpleasant.

replies.text: My curiosity has filed an immediate apology to my nose.
An avoidable investigation has produced an entirely unsurprising reason to stop investigating.
Enough looking. Step back and leave the bin alone.
Some discoveries really do work better as things we never found out.
Fresh air seems like a much better next activity.
The investigation has received a decisive and deeply unappealing closing argument.
A private little abyss has answered the question nobody needed to ask.
Observation complete. No further sampling is remotely necessary.
Some lids are kind enough to hide precisely what they ought to.
A valuable lesson in resisting the impulse to look at absolutely everything.
I would be content to remember the room through any other detail.

contexts.subject: A Three Island house displays rare rocks and gems.

ThreeIsland_House1_Text_RareRocksGemsDis.text: Rare rocks and gems are displayed.$

replies.text: Somebody has brought home a very sparkly selection of things the ground was keeping.
A mineral collection can reward close observation of differences in colour and structure.
Look carefully without touching. Those pieces matter to their owner.
I like seeing a room arranged around something a person simply enjoys noticing.
A collection gives ordinary days a reason to keep looking closely at the world.
The house has lent part of itself to a small exhibition of the earth's better flourishes.
A handful of quiet stones can make a surprisingly personal room.
The shapes and surfaces would be interesting to compare under the same light.
Small old pieces of the world have been gathered into one person's care.
The display makes each piece feel chosen rather than merely expensive.
I wonder whether the owner remembers where each one was found.

contexts.subject: A letter hopes for a reunion, worries about Rocket trouble in Saffron, and reports safety in Vermilion.

VermilionCity_House3_Text_DearPippiLette.text: Dear PIPPI,\nI hope to see you soon.\pI heard SAFFRON has problems with\nTEAM ROCKET.\pVERMILION appears to be safe.$

replies.text: A small hello from far away has made room for worry and a little reassurance.
The letter distinguishes a report about Saffron from the writer's impression of safety in Vermilion.
People keeping each other informed matters when a place is in trouble.
The hope of seeing someone soon feels especially tender beside the worry.
An ordinary message can mean a lot when someone is wondering whether a friend is safe.
A brief personal letter has carried the wider trouble directly into an otherwise quiet room.
Distance makes even a plain assurance of safety feel worth writing down.
We should remember this is the writer's report, not a guarantee about every place mentioned.
A few words are trying to make the space between two people feel less uncertain.
The personal greeting makes the news feel much closer than a public notice would.
I wonder how many times the recipient reads the part about seeing each other again.

contexts.subject: A Fan Club notice asks members to listen politely to other trainers.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Listen.text: Let's all listen politely to other\nTRAINERS!$

replies.text: A club full of favourite stories needs a few people remembering to leave room for the next one.
Reciprocal attention makes a shared-interest conversation more informative and enjoyable.
Let other people finish. Simple enough.
It is easier to share something you love when someone actually lets you say it.
A good gathering has room for more than the person with the loudest story.
The house rules have sensibly protected the audience from becoming a permanent occupation.
Listening is a useful contribution for people with no story prepared.
Taking turns keeps one enthusiastic participant from occupying the whole conversation.
A room grows warmer when every small voice has somewhere to land.
Good manners make enthusiasm much easier to enjoy.
I wonder what lovely little story gets missed whenever the loudest admirer keeps talking.

contexts.subject: A Fan Club notice recommends answering another person's bragging with some of one's own.

VermilionCity_PokemonFanClub_Text_Someon.text: If someone brags, brag right back!$

replies.text: The club has installed a competitive boasting system. I hope the chairs are sturdy.
That may keep a conversation energetic, though it could also become a competition for attention.
A little pride is fine. Do not drown out the other person.
I would rather people enjoy sharing than worry about having a better story.
A friendly bit of showing off can be fun if everyone still feels welcome.
An official invitation to escalate the anecdote. The club knows its audience.
Mutually assured exaggeration has apparently become a social policy.
It works best if both people are enjoying the exchange, not defending their place in it.
Two bright stories need not burn each other out to fill the room.
A little playful rivalry is charming when nobody mistakes it for a ranking of people.
I wonder how quickly two ordinary favourite-Pokemon stories turn into something magnificent here.

contexts.subject: A Silph report records that some Pokemon evolve through trading.

SilphCo_5F_Text_SomeMonsEvolveWhenTraded.text: It's a POKéMON REPORT!\pSome POKéMON have been confirmed\nto evolve when they are traded.$

replies.text: An exchange can contain a rather bigger surprise than the two trainers first bargained for.
The report identifies trading as an evolutionary condition for some species, not all of them.
Worth understanding before agreeing to a trade.
It must feel extraordinary to watch a familiar companion change during that handover.
A thoughtful exchange should make room for what happens to the Pokemon afterward.
The research report has found a way for a handover to become a transformation scene.
A change of company can apparently arrive with a change of shape.
Interesting trigger. Comparing affected species could tell researchers more about the process.
A threshold between two hands can also become a threshold between forms.
It is important information for somebody choosing whether to trade a companion.
I wonder how surprised the first trainers to see that happen must have been.

contexts.subject: A Silph report lists more than three hundred and fifty confirmed Pokemon techniques.

SilphCo_5F_Text_Over350TechniquesConfirm.text: It's a POKéMON REPORT!\pOver 350 POKéMON techniques have\nbeen confirmed.$

replies.text: That is a very large list of things a Pokemon might do while we are still deciding what to expect.
A confirmed catalogue represents substantial observation; its size is not a reason to stop revising it.
Plenty to learn. Start with what our own team needs.
A number that large makes me grateful nobody expects us to learn it all this afternoon.
The world has enough variety to keep a curious person busy for a long time.
The repertoire has grown beyond any sensible one-evening performance.
A reassuring amount of the world remains too busy to fit neatly in my head.
Organizing that many observations into something usable is a significant job in itself.
A long list can still be only the edge of what living things know how to do.
The impressive part is all the patient confirmation behind the number.
I wonder which discovery made the researchers realize the catalogue was much bigger than they expected.

contexts.subject: A research report credits Pokemon Lab with creating Porygon, a virtual-reality Pokemon.

SilphCo_5F_Text_PorygonFirstVRMon.text: It's a POKéMON REPORT!\pPOKéMON LAB created PORYGON,\nthe first virtual-reality POKéMON.$

replies.text: Somebody's research became a whole Pokemon. That is considerably more exciting than finishing a report.
A created Pokemon raises fascinating questions beyond the technical achievement of making it.
Creating a life means taking responsibility for what happens to it.
I would like to know what the people who made it noticed when it first responded.
An extraordinary beginning still needs ordinary care afterward.
The laboratory has crossed the impressive distance between describing a character and introducing a life.
A manufactured beginning does not make the being that follows less worth knowing.
That is an astonishing piece of engineering. I would have a notebook full of questions.
A life can begin in an unfamiliar place and still belong fully to itself.
I would rather meet Porygon than only admire the people taking credit for it.
I wonder which small moment first made the researchers see a companion instead of a project.

contexts.subject: An empty chart has spaces intended for recording measurements.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_BlankCha.text: It's a blank chart of some sort.\pIt has spaces for writing in\nrecords of some kind.$

replies.text: A chart patiently waiting for somebody to introduce a suitably impressive bug.
A prepared record sheet turns future observations into something that can be compared consistently.
Blank for now. No need to fill it with guesses.
I like seeing the little space people leave for things they have not found yet.
An empty page can make a hobby feel like it has somewhere to grow.
The record has built its stage and is awaiting the first extraordinary contestant.
An absence of numbers is occasionally the most honest set of numbers available.
A consistent format is a good start. Measurements still need a clear method.
A few empty boxes have made room for an unknown future.
It is nice to see enthusiasm given a tidy place to keep track of itself.
I wonder what the first entry will look like beside the last one somebody eventually adds.

contexts.subject: A chart records the largest Heracross measured so far.

SixIsland_WaterPath_House1_Text_BiggestH.text: The biggest HERACROSS that I have\never seen measured so far is:\p{STR_VAR_3}!$

replies.text: A bug has earned itself a place on the wall without having to climb the wall.
The wording correctly limits the record to what has been observed so far. That distinction matters.
A useful record. It does not need to make every smaller Heracross feel like a disappointment.
I like imagining the excited little moment when somebody wrote that measurement down.
A hobby can give an otherwise ordinary day something specific to remember.
The reigning champion has been preserved in the surprisingly modest form of a measurement.
A number on a chart is a very small monument to a rather particular enthusiasm.
Keeping the record makes later comparisons possible instead of relying on an excited memory.
One encountered life has left a careful little mark among the numbers.
A record is charming when it stays a shared delight rather than a judgment of everything else.
I wonder what the room sounded like when that record was first broken.

contexts.subject: A slight breeze can be felt around a box in the Seven Island house.

SevenIsland_House_Room1_Text_SlightBreez.text: There is a slight breeze blowing\naround the box.$

replies.text: An ordinary box has developed a rather interesting relationship with the air.
The airflow is observable. Its source is not established by noticing it alone.
Notice it without pulling the house apart. We are guests.
A tiny unexpected detail can make an otherwise familiar room feel different.
We can mention it to the person who lives here rather than start moving their things.
The unassuming prop has supplied a very quiet suggestion of something beyond it.
An excellent small mystery to avoid solving with somebody else's furniture.
Airflow could indicate a gap. That does not authorize an improvised inspection of the wall.
A little breath of elsewhere has found the edge of the room.
Curiosity can remain polite even when it notices something tempting.
I wonder whether the owner stopped noticing that breeze long ago.

contexts.subject: One warehouse password is entered, but a second is still required.

FiveIsland_Meadow_Text_EnteredPasswordAn.text: {PLAYER} entered a password.\p“GOLDEEN need log.”\p… …  … …  … …\pAnother password is needed to\nopen the door…$

replies.text: Half a secret is apparently not enough to persuade the whole door.
The first credential has been supplied, but the second required condition remains unmet.
Still locked. We need the other password.
It is a little frustrating to be closer without being through.
We can keep the known part without trying to force the missing one.
The entrance has accepted the opening line and declined to begin the scene without the second.
A door has found an impressively literal way to demand more information.
Two-part access checks need both parts. Repeating the first will not add the second.
One small tooth of the key has found its place; the rest is still absent.
A partial success is useful information, even when it is not yet a welcome.
I wonder how much confidence the guards place in people never learning the two pieces together.

contexts.subject: The warehouse door is already open.

replies.text: The warehouse has run out of door-related objections. We should still watch what is past it.
The entrance state is clear. An open door does not establish the safety of the interior.
Open. Stay alert when we enter.
A barrier being gone can make the next part feel more real.
Worth checking our readiness before turning an opening into a rushed entrance.
The obstacle has retired from its role, leaving the rest of the scene unresolved.
An open threshold is not necessarily a friendly one.
Access and safety are separate questions. We have answered only the first.
A shut place has given up its boundary, not all its secrets.
We can appreciate progress without behaving as though the whole problem is finished.
I would pay as much attention to what lies beyond as we did to what kept us outside.

contexts.subject: The ancient door in Ruin Valley is open.

replies.text: The old doorway has finally stopped answering every question with a wall.
The opening provides access, but it does not by itself explain the structure beyond.
Take a careful look before moving farther in.
A place feels different once its entrance is no longer only something to stare at.
A slow first step is sensible in an unfamiliar ruin.
The setting has finally granted the visitor more than a view of its exterior.
A threshold has changed its mind after a very long silence.
We can learn more by observing the entrance than by rushing through it.
The dark little space beyond has become somewhere we can approach.
It is satisfying to see an obstacle become an invitation.
I wonder which detail inside will make the most sense of what we saw on the door.

contexts.subject: The player decides not to investigate the strange door further.

replies.text: The door can keep its quiet mystery for a little longer. We have other footsteps available.
Deferring an inspection is reasonable when we are not ready to interpret what we find.
Leave it for now. Curiosity does not set the schedule.
I like knowing we can be interested without having to press farther immediately.
There is time to return with a clearer head and a better plan.
The suspense has been left intact by the perfectly legitimate decision to walk away.
An unanswered question can survive being given the afternoon off.
A pause avoids making an irreversible guess just to satisfy the urge to act.
Some thresholds are kind enough to wait where we found them.
Walking away can be a deliberate choice rather than a failure of nerve.
I wonder what we will notice differently if we come back after thinking about it.

contexts.subject: The Card Key successfully opens a Silph security door.

Text_CardKeyOpenedDoor.text: Bingo!\nThe CARD KEY opened the door!$

replies.text: A little card has settled an argument that the whole door was winning.
The key has satisfied the access control and the door has opened.
Through this one. Keep an eye on the next room.
It is a small relief when the thing you found fits the problem in front of you.
A useful tool is a good reason to remember where we put it.
The imposing barrier has accepted a rather understated credential.
A very small rectangle has out-argued a very large panel of metal.
The access system has responded as expected. Useful to confirm.
A little carried thing has made a wall remember it was a doorway.
A clean solution has its own quiet satisfaction.
I wonder how ordinary that little success feels to the people who used to work here every day.

contexts.subject: A Silph security door remains locked without a Card Key.

replies.text: The door has a very particular opinion about which flat little object counts as a greeting.
The required credential is absent. Force is not a substitute for identifying the access method.
We need the key. Keep looking carefully.
It helps to know what the barrier actually needs instead of guessing at it.
We can work out the next step without making this one into a wrestling match.
The gatekeeper has no lines beyond its inflexible request for proper identification.
A locked door has made its demands admirably specific.
Look for the intended credential rather than testing the strength of the mechanism.
A thin piece of absence is keeping a thick door closed.
At least the problem is clearer than simply being told we cannot go through.
I wonder who last carried the key that should fit this part of the building.

contexts.subject: The inspected security door is already open.

replies.text: One less door trying to become a separate chapter of our afternoon.
The access barrier is already resolved. We can focus on the route beyond it.
Clear passage. Keep moving carefully.
It is nice when checking something confirms there is no new problem waiting.
A clear route is useful, especially when the team needs a simple way back.
The scenery has courteously declined to supply another obstacle.
An ordinary open door can be surprisingly reassuring after enough locked ones.
Worth noting the route while it is unobstructed.
A space has remained open long enough to feel like a little kindness.
There is no need to make an easy part harder just because we expected trouble.
I wonder how different the building will feel when open doors are ordinary again.

contexts.subject: The Network Machine display reports that adjustment work is still in progress.

OneIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_MachineU.text: Network Machine\nLink Level 0\p…POKéMON Storage System under\nadjustment…$

replies.text: The machine has announced that it is having a work-in-progress sort of day.
The display reports an incomplete adjustment state. It does not claim normal operation.
Leave the work to the person handling it. No reason to hurry the equipment.
I appreciate a plain message that admits the job is not done yet.
A careful finish is worth more than pretending something is ready.
The impressive apparatus has issued a modest request for more time backstage.
A machine has found an honest way to say not yet.
A visible status helps people understand what is happening without interfering with the work.
The lights have not quite settled into their finished pattern.
Work in progress is a respectable state to acknowledge instead of hiding it.
I wonder which small adjustment will make the operator finally step back looking satisfied.

contexts.subject: The Network Machine display reports its first established connection.

OneIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_MachineL.text: Network Machine\nLink Level 1\pLink established with the KANTO\nregion.$

replies.text: A very plain status message with a considerable amount of work hiding behind it.
The display now confirms a connection rather than merely describing an adjustment in progress.
Good. The work has a clear result to show.
I like the little relief in seeing something complicated finally say it is working.
Somebody has earned the chance to stop watching the equipment anxiously for a moment.
The grand technical effort has chosen a remarkably restrained announcement of success.
A difficult little triumph has arrived wearing an ordinary status line.
A confirmed state is useful. It gives the operator something definite to test from.
A patient effort has found one clear answer among its lights.
It is satisfying when a result does not need a complicated explanation to be noticed.
I wonder how many earlier attempts the operator remembers while looking at that same message.

contexts.subject: The Network Machine display reports an additional established connection.

OneIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_MachineL.text: Network Machine\nLink Level 2\pLink established with the KANTO\nand HOENN regions.$

replies.text: Another successful line on the display. Complicated work can look wonderfully small once it succeeds.
The status indicates that an additional part of the planned connection is now established.
More progress, properly confirmed. Good work by the people doing it.
It feels good to see a long effort become something the display can state so calmly.
I hope the people behind that result give themselves time to enjoy finishing it.
The technical epic has concluded another chapter in the least dramatic typeface available.
A second quiet confirmation can carry a surprising amount of relief.
An additional working connection means another clear result to verify, not just a hopeful plan.
A careful labour has gathered another little light into its finished shape.
The modest display makes the achievement feel rather sincere.
I wonder which person first noticed the confirmation and called the others over to see.

contexts.subject: A Dojo slogan warns of enemies on every side.

replies.text: A very energetic way to make standing in the middle of a room feel complicated.
As a training slogan, it encourages awareness. Taken literally all the time, it would be exhausting.
Stay aware. No need to turn every stranger into an enemy.
I would rather leave the room more attentive than more afraid of people.
A useful lesson should leave some room for a peaceful meal afterward.
The training hall has declined to give the protagonist a single convenient direction to face.
An excellent slogan for ensuring the shoulders never get a day off.
Awareness is useful when it helps distinguish actual threats from ordinary surroundings.
A person can watch the path without teaching every shadow to wear a hostile face.
Alertness looks better when it leaves room for good judgment.
I wonder whether the instructor explains the difference between readiness and suspicion.

contexts.subject: A Dojo slogan says that what goes around comes around.

replies.text: A slogan with enough room for consequences, kindness, and the occasional badly aimed kick.
Actions often affect future interactions, though the phrase is not a guarantee of perfect fairness.
Treat people decently even when nobody promises a reward for it.
I like the idea of giving the next person something kind to carry onward.
A small good turn can travel farther than the person who began it notices.
The hall has supplied a compact theory of consequences with a nicely circular structure.
A comforting thought, provided we do not mistake every misfortune for something deserved.
Feedback matters. So does remembering that real situations are more complicated than a slogan.
What we set loose in the day may find another doorway than the one we expect.
A good reminder to think beyond the instant of getting what we want.
I wonder which experience made that phrase worth putting where students would see it every day.

contexts.subject: A Trainer Tips sign recommends Guard Spec and advertises the Department Store.

CeladonCity_Text_GuardSpecProtectsFromSt.text: TRAINER TIPS\pGUARD SPEC. protects POKéMON\nfrom status-reduction moves during\lbattle.\pGet your items at the\nCELADON DEPT. STORE!$

replies.text: A helpful battle tip has brought a tiny shop advertisement along as its travelling companion.
Preventing a problem can be useful. The purchase still needs to fit our actual plan.
Read the item properly before relying on it.
I like the useful part better than the assumption that reading means we should buy something.
A little preparation can help, provided we do not fill the Bag with every advertised answer.
The educational notice has remembered which merchant paid for its closing line.
A piece of advice can be useful and still have something to sell.
Match the tool to the problem rather than collect tools without a plan.
A shield is most useful when we know which small doors it can close.
Practical advice benefits from a little thought about the sales pitch attached.
I wonder which situation first made someone wish they had packed that item.

contexts.subject: A posted tip advertises items intended to improve accuracy or critical-hit chances.

CeladonCity_Text_ExplainXAccuracyDireHit.text:
TRAINER TIPS\pX ACCURACY boosts the accuracy of
techniques.\pDIRE HIT jacks up the likelihood
of critical hits.\pGet your items at the CELADON
DEPT. STORE!$

replies.text: Two little promises to make a battle less wobbly, both conveniently sold just over there.
Improving a probability and guaranteeing an outcome are different claims. Useful to keep them distinct.
Helpful options. They do not replace paying attention to the fight.
I would rather plan calmly than reach for something because one missed move made us panic.
Choose what helps the team instead of buying every promise on a sign.
The store has offered the traveller two kinds of dramatic improvement in portable form.
Chance has been invited to behave itself, not forced to sign a contract.
We can compare the effect with the situation before deciding it earns a place in the Bag.
A little help can steady the hand without writing the ending.
The distinction between more likely and certain deserves larger lettering.
I wonder how many shoppers remember the useful explanation after the colourful promise.

contexts.subject: A Trainer Tips sign explains that Pokemon can carry useful items.

CeruleanCity_Text_TrainerTipsHeldItems.text: TRAINER TIPS\pA POKéMON can be made to hold\nan item.\pSome items can even be used by\nthe holding POKéMON in battle.$

replies.text: A little equipment for the companion instead of another thing for us to drop in the Bag.
A held item can support a particular role when its effect suits the Pokemon's actual needs.
Choose something useful and check who is carrying what.
