contexts.subject: A Game Boy Advance is connected to a Nintendo GameCube as its controller.

PlayersHouse_2F_Text_ItsAGameCube.text: It's a Nintendo GameCube.\pA Game Boy Advance is connected to\nserve as the Controller.$

replies.text: A little game machine helping a bigger game machine! Very cooperative electronics.
The handheld doubles as an input device. An interesting reuse of existing hardware.
Useful setup. One device gets another job.
That looks like a comfortable way to spend a quiet afternoon at home.
Everything connected and ready. That's how a short break becomes a long afternoon.
Two machines have negotiated a partnership beneath one television.
A controller with its own ambitions. I respect the versatility.
I love seeing a portable device take on a second role in a larger system.
The little machine stays connected to something it could usually leave behind.
A clever arrangement, provided the cable doesn't take over the entire floor.
I'd ask what games someone picks when they've finally got an afternoon free.

contexts.subject: The Space Center sign calls it the closest place to space.

MossdeepCity_Text_SpaceCenterSign.text: MOSSDEEP SPACE CENTER\n“The closest place to space.”$

replies.text: Closest to space! I suppose the roof gets a very small head start.
The claim is more aspirational than geographical. An effective invitation, though.
Good sign. Tells you what they're aiming for.
It makes a huge distance feel a little less unreachable.
A place where very far away becomes someone's daily work. I like that.
An excellent promise for a building that remains firmly attached to the ground.
A reassuringly short journey to an unsettlingly large distance.
Inside are the plans and equipment that make that slogan more than a nice thought.
One door away from people who spend their days thinking beyond the sky.
Short, clear, and full of ambition. That's a sign people will remember.
I'd ask someone here what first made space feel like a place they could actually reach.

contexts.subject: A sign points down Jagged Path toward Lavaridge Town.

replies.text: Jagged Path, then Lavaridge. The name seems to be doing some responsible warning.
The sign provides the descent and destination. We'll still need to judge the footing.
Downhill doesn't mean easy. Keep an eye on the path.
It's nice knowing where the descent leads before starting it.
A rough path with a town at the end. Enough reason to take our time getting there.
A concise itinerary: uneven ground, followed by civilization.
A path honest enough to advertise its own sharp edges.
I'd check the way down before committing to a ledge. The destination can wait.
The mountain gives us a downward road and a name to follow.
Practical directions. Sensible shoes remain our department.
A destination sign feels particularly welcome when the road starts dropping away.

contexts.subject: The Meteorite has been removed from the mountain machine and successfully received.

MtChimney_Text_PlayerRemovedMeteorite.text: {PLAYER} removed the METEORITE from\nthe mysterious machine.$

replies.text: One space rock, freed from a very suspicious job. A better career move already.
Removing the Meteorite separates it from the machine's energy arrangement.
Keep it secure. That machine has had enough access to it.
I'm glad it's out of there. It feels easier to breathe around the machine now.
A valuable object is better packed safely than left in that contraption.
The Meteorite has resigned from a disastrous position. Effective immediately.
A rock with fewer alarming responsibilities. An improvement.
Now the machine can't keep using that component. That's a concrete change.
The fallen stone is separate from the thing that wanted to use it.
Safely put away is a much better look for that Meteorite.
I'd remember where it came from. The rock has already had a complicated journey.

contexts.subject: A Ranking Hall sign identifies Dome, Pike and Factory records.

BattleFrontier_RankingHall_Text_DomePike.text: BATTLE DOME, BATTLE PIKE,\nand BATTLE FACTORY Records$

replies.text: Three facilities' records in one place. A concentrated supply of impressive numbers.
The heading distinguishes these facilities' records from the other displays.
Dome, Pike, Factory. Good to know which results we're comparing.
A clear label makes it easier to take time with each set of results.
Three different challenges, and room to remember the people who did well.
A small sign announcing a rather large collection of hard-earned bragging rights.
An index to other people's exceptional afternoons.
Keeping the facility names visible prevents very misleading comparisons.
Different paths have left their numbers together here.
A clear heading gives a busy display some order.
I'd be interested in which of the three draws the longest look from visitors.

contexts.subject: A Ranking Hall sign identifies Palace, Arena and Pyramid records.

BattleFrontier_RankingHall_Text_PalaceAr.text: BATTLE PALACE, BATTLE ARENA,\nand BATTLE PYRAMID Records$

replies.text: Palace, Arena, Pyramid. Those names make a records board sound like an enormous holiday.
Another group of facility-specific results. The distinctions matter when reading the records.
Three challenges with their own records. Treat each on its own terms.
It's easier to appreciate the numbers when you know which challenge produced them.
Different kinds of effort all get their own place on the board.
Three grand names sheltering some very determined competitors' results.
Palace, Arena, Pyramid. An unusually architectural collection of accomplishments.
The grouping gives the record display a sensible structure. Now we can inspect the details.
Each place leaves a different mark on the people who pass through it.
Matching headings make the hall feel considered rather than crowded.
I'd ask a visitor which facility name means the most to them, and why.

contexts.subject: A Safari Zone sign directs tired visitors to the Rest House.

replies.text: A sign that understands feet. Finally, representation for the bottom of the expedition.
A rest stop is most useful when visitors can find it before they're exhausted.
Good place to stop before tired feet turn into a bad decision.
It's reassuring when a place gives you permission to slow down.
Rest first. Exploring is much more enjoyable when every step isn't an argument.
The invitation lacks grandeur but possesses excellent timing.
A building advertised through fatigue. An audience I understand.
Putting the rest sign where people are walking is a small but useful choice.
Even an exciting place needs somewhere to be still.
A welcome that starts with people's comfort. That's good hospitality.
A rest stop is also where people finally have time to tell you what they've seen.

contexts.subject: Verdanturf Battle Tent sign invites visitors to enjoy watching battles.

VerdanturfTown_Text_BattleTentSign.text: BATTLE TENT VERDANTURF SITE\n“Feast Your Eyes on Battles!”$

replies.text: A feast for the eyes. Mine were expecting sandwiches, but they'll adjust.
The sign emphasizes the spectacle of the battles rather than their particular rules.
An invitation to look around. We'll learn the rules before joining anything.
Watching first might make the place feel less overwhelming.
A feast for the eyes is fine. I'll still want an actual meal afterward.
The sign offers spectacle with the confidence of someone who knows their audience.
A feast requiring no plates. Convenient cleanup.
It gets attention. The practical details will need a separate look inside.
A canvas building holding many people's brief, fierce moments.
It's a vivid promise for a small sign. A little excitement suits the tent.
I'd ask spectators which moment made them glad they stopped to watch.

contexts.subject: A sign records the cancelled tunnel project between Rustboro and Verdanturf.

VerdanturfTown_Text_RusturfTunnelSign.text: RUSTURF TUNNEL\n“Linking RUSTBORO and VERDANTURF\p“The tunnel project has been\ncanceled.”$

replies.text: A sign for a road that didn't turn out as planned. Even signs can have awkward histories.
The cancellation notice records the project's status, not necessarily everything that happened afterward.
Plans on a sign can fall behind what people actually do. Check the way itself.
A cancelled project still leaves something behind. Even if it's only a sign.
A promised shortcut matters to the people at both ends. I'd want to hear their side.
The sign preserves the official ending. Roads are less tidy than official endings.
A monument to a plan encountering reality. A familiar architectural genre.
I'd want to know what stopped the project before judging the people who worked on it.
Two town names remain linked here, even in a notice of cancellation.
The wording tells us what was decided. It doesn't tell us how everyone felt about it.
I'd ask a local what they remember about the project. A notice can only hold so much.

contexts.subject: A sign displays the recorded Cycling Road collision count and elapsed time.

Route110_Text_BestRecord.text: THE BEST RECORD TO DATE…\pNo. of collisions: {STR_VAR_1}\pElapsed time: {STR_VAR_2}$

replies.text: Speed and collisions on the same board. A useful reminder that fences count too.
Time and collision count measure different aspects of a ride. Both deserve attention.
Fast is good. Fast without hitting things is better.
I like that it remembers more than the clock. A smooth ride matters too.
A little care around the turns belongs beside the speed.
The record includes both the sprint and its less graceful punctuation.
A public collision count. The road refuses to let dignity obscure the data.
Two measurements give us a clearer target than time alone.
The ride is gone, but its haste and bumps have left a small trace.
A good result should look smooth as well as quick.
I'd ask the rider which stretch cost them the most concentration.

contexts.subject: The Cycling Road board has no recorded challenge result.

Route110_Text_ThereIsNoRecord.text: THE BEST RECORD TO DATE…\pNo one seems to have taken the\nchallenge. There is no record…$

replies.text: No record yet! The board is having a very patient first day.
An empty record offers no baseline for comparison. The first completed result would establish one.
No result to beat yet. Still worth riding carefully.
An empty board feels less intimidating. It hasn't started comparing anyone yet.
Someone has to be first. They might as well enjoy the ride.
A vacant place in local sporting history. Currently accepting applicants.
No record, no embarrassing collision count. An unusually peaceful scoreboard.
The first result will give future riders something concrete to compare against.
A space is waiting for a journey to leave its numbers.
A blank display needs one clear result before it can tell much of a story.
It would be interesting to hear from whoever first decides to put a result here.

contexts.subject: The player leaves the Meteorite in the machine after declining removal.

replies.text: The rock stays put. It has not, however, become any less suspicious-looking.
Leaving the component in place preserves the current arrangement. We can reconsider later.
Left it alone for now. Keep track of where it is.
I don't quite trust that machine, even when we're only looking at it.
No need to pretend we've packed something that's still sitting right there.
The Meteorite retains its questionable accommodation for another visit.
An ominous object left exactly where we found it. At least the inventory is simple.
We haven't changed the machine's components. I'd remember that distinction.
The stone waits where someone fitted it. The choice remains beside it.
Leaving it in place is easy to see. Understanding the machine is another matter.
I'd remember this spot if we decide to come back for a closer look.

contexts.subject: The mysterious mountain machine gives no response.

MtChimney_Text_MachineMakesNoResponse.text: This mysterious machine…\nIt makes no response whatsoever.$

replies.text: No response. A pleasant change from mysterious machines doing far too much.
Lack of response tells us its current behavior, not the full state of every component.
Quiet is good. Let's leave it that way.
I prefer it silent. This is one mystery I don't need to hear humming.
A machine that isn't asking anything of us. Fine place to stop investigating.
The contraption declines to provide a dramatic development. Thank you, contraption.
Unresponsive machinery. For once, that feels like a favorable report.
No output to observe. I'd avoid treating that as an invitation to start pressing things.
Whatever stirred in it isn't answering now.
The absence of a response is enough information for this visit.
An inactive machine can still have a history. We don't need to restart it to acknowledge that.

contexts.subject: A mysterious machine appears to store energy in its fitted Meteorite.

MtChimney_Text_MeteoriteFittedOnMachine.text: A METEORITE is fitted on a mysterious\nmachine…\pThe machine seems to be storing\nenergy in the METEORITE.$

replies.text: A space rock attached to a mountain machine. Someone has very alarming hobbies.
The visible description suggests energy storage, though it doesn't explain the mechanism.
Leave the controls alone. We don't know what they're connected to.
That doesn't look like a harmless display. I'd keep a little distance.
Something storing energy on a volcano deserves more caution than curiosity.
A mysterious machine and a Meteorite. The arrangement hardly inspires domestic confidence.
A rock has been given a position of alarming technical importance.
I'd want a diagram and a safe way to measure it before making any claims about that system.
A fallen thing is being asked to hold something that isn't still.
Whatever the design is meant to do, it hasn't made its purpose welcoming.
I'd ask who built it before trusting anyone's account of what it can safely do.

contexts.subject: The player closes Lanette research notebook without continuing to its next page.

replies.text: Notebook closed. The next page will have to keep its clever thoughts to itself for now.
We've stopped reading here. The remaining notes shouldn't be mistaken for something we've reviewed.
Leave the notes tidy. They're still someone else's work.
We can close it without pretending we've understood everything in it.
Back where it belongs. Research notes are easy enough to lose under ordinary clutter.
A brief reading ends with a neatly closed cover. Perfectly respectable pacing.
The notebook has returned to being mysterious on the outside.
Stopping here leaves the rest available for a more focused look another time.
The unwritten part of our visit stays between its closed pages.
A clean place to pause. No need to leave somebody's notebook sprawled open.
If a question comes up later, we'll know where the notes are.

contexts.subject: Lanette notes explain sending stored Pokemon to the last inspected Box or the next available one.

Route114_LanettesHouse_Text_ResearchNote.text:
When storing a POKéMON, it should be
sent to the BOX inspected last.\pIf that BOX is full, the received
POKéMON is stored in the next BOX.\pIn other words, when a BOX is examined,
it is automatically selected as the BOX\lto which POKéMON are sent.$

replies.text: The last Box you looked at gets the next arrival. A surprisingly attentive little filing system.
The system uses the last inspected Box as the current destination, with overflow to the next.
Check the Box you want first. Saves searching for the arrival afterward.
That explains why looking at a Box matters even without moving anything.
A chosen place first, then the next if it's full. Easy enough to remember.
A quiet administrative decision happens the moment someone looks inside a Box.
Inspection counts as selection. A detail with excellent potential to confuse the unwarned.
Using the last inspected Box as a default saves an extra selection. Good to document it.
The place you last considered becomes the next place something arrives.
A useful default becomes much friendlier when someone explains it clearly.
I'd point this out to anyone who keeps wondering where a newly stored Pokemon went.

contexts.subject: The ship corridor sign identifies Cabin 1.

replies.text: Cabin one. An excellent number to start the cabin collection with.
A simple number is sufficient identification when the corridor follows a clear order.
Cabin one. Easy enough to remember if we need the way back.
A little number makes an unfamiliar corridor less confusing.
Useful sign. No wandering into the wrong doorway to ask where we are.
The first cabin receives a suitably economical introduction.
One. A door label refreshingly free of nautical riddles.
Clear numbering is one of those small details a busy corridor needs.
A small marker divides this stretch of ship from the next.
Plain lettering is right for a cabin sign. Finding the door comes first.
I'd remember the number before getting distracted by everything else aboard.

contexts.subject: The ship corridor sign identifies Cabin 2.

replies.text: Cabin two! The numbering system remains reassuringly undefeated.
The next numbered cabin. Consistency makes navigation easier on an unfamiliar ship.
Cabin two. Mark the number before choosing a door.
The corridor feels easier to follow once you notice the numbers.
A number worth remembering. Much easier than describing which identical door we meant.
Cabin two makes its presence known without demanding a speech.
Two. The sign has resisted the temptation to overcomplicate things.
Repeating the same clear format keeps the whole corridor readable.
Another small address traveling across a very large sea.
The right number in the right place. Sometimes design should be this straightforward.
I'd check the sign twice before confidently knocking on the wrong cabin.

contexts.subject: The ship corridor sign identifies Cabin 3.

replies.text: Cabin three. I'm glad the ship isn't making us solve a puzzle to find the doors.
Numbered doors provide stable references even while the vessel itself is moving.
Third cabin. Now we've got another landmark in the corridor.
It's a small sign, but it gives you somewhere definite to be.
Remember the number and nobody needs to hear a long story about which door.
Cabin three, announced with the confidence of a place that knows its own address.
Three. An entire identity delivered in one very manageable number.
A clear local reference is useful when the outside view doesn't stay put.
The number stays steady while the water passes outside.
No flourish needed. A door number has a practical job.
I'd use this sign as a reference if someone needed directions through the ship.

contexts.subject: The ship corridor sign identifies Cabin 4.

replies.text: Cabin four. Four useful numbers, and I haven't had to name a single door myself.
The label completes another clear reference point in the cabin corridor.
Cabin four. Good, we've kept our bearings.
A familiar number is enough to make the corridor feel less anonymous.
Now if anyone says cabin four, we won't have to open every door to find it.
The fourth cabin preserves the corridor's admirably restrained naming policy.
Four. I appreciate a sign that finishes before I lose my place.
Consistent door labels make giving directions much simpler.
One little numeral holds a place apart from all the others.
A readable sign earns its space without needing to decorate the whole door.
It's worth noticing these signs before the conversation aboard gets distracting.

contexts.subject: The Weather Institute bed interaction provides a completed party rest.

Route119_WeatherInstitute_1F_Text_TakeRe.text: There's a bed…\nLet's take a rest.$

replies.text: A proper rest indoors. Rain may continue its performance without us for a bit.
A recovery stop here is practical, especially with the long wet route outside.
Good stop. Better to continue rested than prove we can stay tired.
A quiet bed feels especially welcome with all that weather outside.
Rested up. Even a busy institute has room for a sensible pause.
A short intermission beneath a reliably dry roof. Excellent accommodation.
A bed at a weather institute. Research has finally produced something immediately restful.
Keeping a rest space beside the working rooms makes this a very useful stop.
For a little while, the rain belongs to the other side of the wall.
Dry shelter and a chance to recover. Nothing needs improving on that combination.
A rest stop changes how the next stretch feels. We can notice more when we're less tired.

contexts.subject: Lilycove Harbor sign advertises S.S. Tidal cruises.

LilycoveCity_Text_HarborSign.text: LILYCOVE CITY HARBOR\p“Enjoy a delightful cruise on\nthe ferry S.S. TIDAL.”$

replies.text: A delightful cruise, says the sign. I'm choosing to believe the sea signed off on that.
The harbor sign identifies the ferry service. Sailing details will require a separate check.
There's our harbor. Worth asking where the ferry's headed before boarding.
A cruise sounds peaceful from here, with both feet still on the ground.
A seat, a sea breeze, and time to enjoy the crossing. That is an appealing promise.
The harbor has compressed the romance of travel into one cheerful invitation.
Delightful is doing some optimistic work on behalf of the ocean.
A ferry turns a long stretch of water into a practical connection between places.
The sign invites us to leave land behind for a little while.
A pleasant promise belongs at a harbor. So do clear boarding directions.
I'd ask returning passengers which part of the crossing they enjoyed most.

contexts.subject: Lilycove Museum sign advertises its Pokemon masterpiece collection.

replies.text: A whole collection of masterpieces! The ordinary pictures must feel very outnumbered.
The sign identifies both the collection's subject and its artistic emphasis.
Good place to slow down and look at something properly.
I'd like to see which pictures make people stop for a little longer.
A quiet look around sounds good. There's no need to hurry past someone's work.
Masterpieces await inside. The sign has sensibly delegated the evidence to the paintings.
A building full of pictures is a reasonable excuse to avoid a crowded afternoon.
I'd enjoy comparing how different artists approach the same kind of subject.
Many ways of seeing Pokemon have found shelter in one place.
I'd like to look at how the collection is arranged as well as the individual works.
I'd ask a regular visitor which piece keeps bringing them back.

contexts.subject: The sign identifies the player home by name.

replies.text: Your name on a house. Very official. The doormat must be proud.
A simple name makes the house easy for visitors to identify.
Home. Nice to see a sign that doesn't need further directions.
Seeing your name there makes the place feel more settled.
A house is easier to find when the welcome starts outside.
A modest plaque granting you a starring role in local postal geography.
A useful sign for anyone whose directions end with asking a stranger.
Clear identification. The smallest useful piece of a town's navigation system.
A name gives the doorway a particular kind of belonging.
Personal without being elaborate. A house sign doesn't need much more.
It must feel different reading your own name there than anyone else's.

contexts.subject: A sign identifies Professor Birch home.

replies.text: Professor Birch's house. Useful distinction from wherever he has wandered off to study something.
The house is clearly identified. A researcher's home and workplace needn't be the same address.
Birch's home. Worth remembering before going to the wrong building to find him.
A plain house sign makes a professor seem a little less distant.
Even a busy professor has somewhere to come home at the end of the day.
An academic title attached to an ordinary front door. A pleasantly grounded introduction.
The professor has a house. Evidence that fieldwork occasionally pauses.
A clear sign prevents visitors from mistaking the home for the lab.
The name outside belongs to someone with a life inside.
A proper nameplate is helpful when half a town seems to know the same person.
I'd ask a local which building they mean before assuming every Birch errand leads here.

contexts.subject: The Running Shoes booklet explains holding B to run in them.

PlayersHouse_1F_Text_RunningShoesManual.text:
It's the instruction booklet for the
RUNNING SHOES.\p“Press the B Button to run while
wearing your RUNNING SHOES.\p“Lace up your RUNNING SHOES and hit
the road running!”$

replies.text: Shoes with instructions! Mine usually settle for suggesting which end the toes go in.
A short manual for a frequently used action. It sensibly avoids unnecessary complication.
Lace them properly before trying the fast part.
It's nice having the instructions nearby. Asking again can feel awkward.
Good laces first, running second. Saves an embarrassing argument with the ground.
The booklet introduces running with the enthusiasm of a shoe salesman late for lunch.
A manual short enough to read before the urge to sit down wins.
One clear instruction and the basic safety of lacing up. Efficient documentation.
A pair of shoes can make the road feel a little more inviting.
Useful shoes still need a proper fit. Speed won't improve a loose lace.
I'd want to try a short stretch first, just to get used to the difference.

contexts.subject: An email from Pokemon Trainer School explains the four-move limit and choosing movesets.

gText_PokemonTrainerSchoolEmail.text: There's an e-mail from POKéMON TRAINER\nSCHOOL.\p… … … … … …\pA POKéMON may learn up to four moves.\pA TRAINER's expertise is tested on the\nmove sets chosen for POKéMON.\p… … … … … …$

replies.text: Four moves! That makes choosing harder than remembering which pocket has my snacks.
A four-move limit makes selection a problem of coverage, specialization, and trade-offs.
Choose moves that work together. Four strong choices can still leave a gap.
Leaving something out can be harder than choosing what to keep.
Four places on the menu. Each one should have a reason to be there.
The limit gives every choice weight. Even the omitted move gets a little influence.
Only four moves. A useful defense against decisions becoming literally endless.
I'd check what each move contributes before replacing anything. Overlap can hide a missing option.
A few chosen actions can take a Pokemon in many directions.
A coherent set often does more than four impressive pieces thrown together.
I'd ask a trainer which move they kept changing their mind about, and why.

contexts.subject: A Game Corner machine cannot be played without a Coin Case.

MauvilleCity_GameCorner_Text_CantPlayWit.text: You can't play if you don't have\na COIN CASE.$

replies.text: No Coin Case, no game. The machine has very specific ideas about pockets.
The required container is missing. The machine can't be used in this state.
Need the case first. No point feeding the machine hopeful looks.
At least it tells us what's missing instead of leaving us guessing.
A clear answer. We can leave this machine alone for now.
Entry has been denied on a technicality involving personal storage.
The machine demands a particular sort of preparedness. We do not possess it.
A requirement stated plainly saves a lot of fruitless button pressing.
The bright machine has one quiet condition we haven't met.
Useful to learn that before settling in front of it.
I'd ask about the case rather than keep trying the same machine.

contexts.subject: The Trick House entrance object is simply described as a scroll in this state.

replies.text: A scroll. In this house, that feels like a suspiciously short explanation.
The visible description establishes only that it's a scroll. No further mechanism is revealed here.
Just a scroll for now. Don't assume every object is ready to do something.
It's strange how an ordinary scroll can feel less ordinary in this house.
A scroll isn't much to go on. We can leave it at that for the moment.
A scroll with an admirably restrained introduction, considering its surroundings.
The scroll refuses to elaborate. I understand the impulse.
No additional function is apparent in this state. Observation before experimentation.
Rolled paper can keep a great deal out of sight.
Simple description. The setting supplies quite enough extra speculation.
I'd remember how it looks now before deciding later that it has changed.

contexts.subject: The Trick Master note says he has left on a journey and asks not to be sought.

Route110_TrickHouseEntrance_Text_Leaving.text: There is a note affixed to the scroll…\p“I am leaving on a journey.\nDon't look for me. TRICK MASTER”$

replies.text: He's gone on a journey and left us a note instead of a puzzle. A surprisingly direct trick.
The note states his departure but gives no destination. We shouldn't infer one.
He asked not to be followed. Fair enough.
Leaving a note is kind. It saves someone waiting without knowing.
Everyone gets to head out sometimes. Even the person who builds reasons for others to visit.
An exit note with no riddle attached. Perhaps that's his final surprise for the room.
A request not to search. Remarkably clear for this particular household.
No destination or return date supplied. The only clear instruction is to leave him to it.
Someone who made paths for visitors has taken one of his own.
A plain note can say enough. He seems quite definite about this.
I'd be curious about his journey, but curiosity doesn't require following him.

contexts.subject: A formerly occupied Shoal Salt spot is empty.

ShoalCave_Text_WasShoalSaltNowNothing.text: There was some SHOAL SALT here.\nBut, there's nothing here now.$

replies.text: Salt was here, salt is not here. The cave has delivered a very concise report.
The source is empty at present. That observation doesn't establish its future availability.
Nothing left at this spot. Move on rather than keep searching it.
An empty patch still tells you what used to be there.
No salt to collect here now. At least we checked before promising any.
A former salt deposit has become a short lesson in absence.
The salt has left no forwarding address.
Empty location confirmed. Rechecking it immediately won't add useful information.
A little place remembers what the tide once left there.
The empty space is the important detail this time.
I'd note that it's empty now rather than assume we missed something obvious.

contexts.subject: A formerly occupied Shoal Shell spot is empty.

ShoalCave_Text_WasShoallShellNowNothing.text: There was a SHOAL SHELL here.\nBut, there's nothing here now.$

replies.text: A shell used to be here. Now it's a very small exhibition of no shell.
The spot is currently empty. We have no shell to identify or collect from it.
No shell here now. Keep an eye on the footing as we move on.
It feels odd knowing exactly what an empty place is missing.
Nothing to pack from this spot. That keeps the count honest.
The shell's former location has outlasted its appearance in the scene.
An absent shell. Less attractive than a shell, but considerably lighter to carry.
One empty collection point. Better to record that clearly than search it in circles.
The shape of a place can remain after its small occupant leaves.
No shell to admire here at the moment. The cave has other details to look at.
I'd compare what this spot looks like another time before drawing any conclusions.

contexts.subject: Slateport Harbor sign advertises S.S. Tidal cruises.

SlateportCity_Text_HarborSign.text: SLATEPORT HARBOR\p“Enjoy a delightful cruise on\nthe ferry S.S. TIDAL.”$

replies.text: The S.S. Tidal has a proper invitation here. Very polite for such a large boat.
A harbor notice for the ferry service. It doesn't specify the current sailing conditions.
Harbor's here. Next step is checking the actual route.
The invitation makes the water feel like a way somewhere, rather than an edge.
A cruise sounds like a pleasant change from walking every mile ourselves.
The sign sells a delightful crossing while the harbor handles the practical business.
A cheerful invitation to trust a very large quantity of water.
A regular ferry gives a busy port another useful connection.
A name on the sign turns the sea into a possible road.
Clear harbor identification first, a little charm second. Sensible order.
I'd ask someone arriving here how different Slateport looks from the water.

contexts.subject: The shipyard notice says S.S. Tidal construction is nearly complete for the two ports.

SlateportCity_Text_SternsShipyardNearsCo.text: STERN'S SHIPYARD\p“The ferry S.S. TIDAL nears\ncompletion for serving the ports of\lSLATEPORT and LILYCOVE.”$

replies.text: Nearly a ferry! That's a lot of work hiding inside one small word.
The notice describes the project as nearing completion, not already operating.
Nearly finished still means work left. Let the builders do it properly.
It must be exciting to see something this big getting close to ready.
Almost done is when you check the details, even if everyone is eager to begin.
The shipyard announces an approaching debut while wisely leaving the curtain down.
Nearly complete. A phrase that can contain several extremely important bolts.
I'd love to see which finishing tasks remain before a ferry is ready for passengers.
Two ports are waiting for a road that still has to be built.
A clear progress notice gives people a reason to look forward without promising too much.
I'd ask a worker which part of seeing the finished ship they're most looking forward to.

contexts.subject: The shipyard directs S.S. Tidal passengers to board at the harbor.

SlateportCity_Text_SternsShipyardFerryCo.text: STERN'S SHIPYARD\p“Boarding of the SLATEPORT-LILYCOVE\nferry S.S. TIDAL is handled at the\lHARBOR.”$

replies.text: The shipyard builds it; the harbor lets us on. Good to sort that out before waving at cranes.
The notice distinguishes construction facilities from the passenger boarding location.
Board at the harbor. Saves asking the shipwrights for a seat.
I'm glad the sign says where to go. It's easy to feel in the way at a working yard.
Useful directions. Passengers can find the boat without interrupting everyone building things.
The shipyard politely redirects anyone who mistakes the workshop for the departure lounge.
Boarding elsewhere. The workers have escaped becoming an information desk by accident.
A simple routing notice prevents pedestrians from wandering through a working site.
The place where a journey is built isn't always where it begins.
Practical signs spare both visitors and staff a repeated awkward conversation.
I'd pass that direction along if we saw anyone else waiting at the wrong entrance.

contexts.subject: BELDUM gives a small, satisfied hum. Its travel arrangements appear to be settled.

KantoRare_BELDUM_CaughtText.text: BELDUM gives a small, satisfied\nhum. Its travel arrangements\lappear to be settled.$

replies.text: Our new friend has finally found an itinerary. I hope it allows snack stops.
A willing new partner, with a remarkably decisive way of settling introductions.
We'll make sure it knows where we're going. Most of the time.
That little hum sounded rather like relief.
I wonder what counts as a good travel meal for a Beldum.
A floating metal traveler has selected us as its navigation department.
Its search for direction has ended with people who also read signs twice.
A magnetic new colleague. I should check which pocket contains my tools.
A small hum can make a road feel less lonely.
Travel arrangements settled. Now we can get acquainted properly.
I'd remember the first time it turns toward us instead of the crossroads.

contexts.subject: SHINX gives you one final stern look, then relaxes. You appear to have passed inspection.

KantoRare_SHINX_CaughtText.text: SHINX gives you one final stern\nlook, then relaxes. You appear to\lhave passed inspection.$

replies.text: We passed the tiny thunder inspector. I was trying very hard to look qualified.
Its ambition has found someone willing to help it practice.
A good start. We can work on the rest together.
I'm glad it can stop looking fierce for a little while.
That much determination deserves patient care between the big moments.
We have been approved by a critic with excellent little paws.
The glare was formidable. The paws somewhat betrayed it.
Confidence is useful. Safe practice will make it sturdier.
Even a small spark can choose a long road.
I hope it knows we liked it before it finished trying to look impressive.
I'd like to remember that stern little face before it grows into it.

contexts.subject: RIOLU bows again. The class now has a traveling instructor, or possibly a traveling student.

KantoRare_RIOLU_CaughtText.text: RIOLU bows again. The class now\nhas a traveling instructor, or\lpossibly a traveling student.$

replies.text: I have always wanted to join a class with this little paperwork.
It seems interested in practicing with us, rather than merely winning once.
We'll train properly. No pretending the hard part is already done.
That bow felt like a rather kind beginning.
A good practice partner also notices when it is time to rest.
The pebble academy has approved our application for a field placement.
We have joined a school whose previous students were exceptionally grounded.
A thoughtful little training setup. We can build on that.
A quiet bow has opened another path.
I like that the invitation came with manners as well as determination.
I'd ask which pebble had been its most difficult opponent.

contexts.subject: MAREEP settles down with a contented bleat. The expedition has acquired a little more wool.

KantoRare_MAREEP_CaughtText.text: MAREEP settles down with a\ncontented bleat. The expedition\lhas acquired a little more wool.$

replies.text: Excellent. Our journey is now significantly fluffier and slightly more conductive.
We should learn what helps it relax when its wool builds up charge.
Give it space until that crackling settles.
That sounded like a very comfortable little decision.
A rest, a meal, and somewhere dry would make a good welcome.
The expedition has recruited both a companion and a caution about enthusiastic hugs.
A portable cloud with opinions about personal space.
I have several interesting questions and absolutely no intention of testing them with my hair.
A warm little cloud has chosen to follow the road.
We can admire the wool without immediately trying to pat it.
I like the way its whole posture softened once the match ended.

contexts.subject: BUNEARY gives the twig one last triumphant hop. The next obstacle course will be wherever you go.

KantoRare_BUNEARY_CaughtText.text: BUNEARY gives the twig one last\ntriumphant hop. The next obstacle\lcourse will be wherever you go.$

replies.text: I award it full marks for making that twig look important.
A small challenge can still build confidence when someone takes it seriously.
We'll find it a better course. And a proper rest between runs.
It looked so pleased that somebody stayed to watch.
That much hopping must work up a very respectable appetite.
The reigning champion has agreed to take its twig-based talents on tour.
A heroic final leap over an obstacle the wind could defeat.
We could arrange a little course without making every practice a competition.
A small hurdle has become the beginning of a much longer path.
That was a victory lap, and I will respect it as such.
I'd love to remember how proudly it landed that last hop.

contexts.subject: ESPEON takes a leisurely stretch. It appears satisfied with the direction this afternoon has taken.

KantoRare_ESPEON_CaughtText.text: ESPEON takes a leisurely stretch.\nIt appears satisfied with the\ldirection this afternoon has\ltaken.$

replies.text: I hope it likes our direction even when the direction is back to the shop.
Its posture seems relaxed. We can let a new partnership develop at that pace.
It chose us. We don't have to make a grand prediction out of it.
That stretch made the whole introduction feel less hurried.
I hope our rest stops offer a decent sunny patch.
Our newest companion has reviewed the itinerary and declined to reveal the ending.
A reassuring endorsement from someone who looked disappointed in everybody else's route.
I'd ask what it notices before assuming it can solve all our planning.
A little sunlight seems willing to travel with us.
It has perfected looking entirely certain without explaining a single thing.
I'd notice which direction its ears turn before the rest of us hear anything.

contexts.subject: UMBREON gives a quiet nod and lets its rings dim. It seems comfortable enough to stop making an announcement.

KantoRare_UMBREON_CaughtText.text: UMBREON gives a quiet nod and\nlets its rings dim. It seems\lcomfortable enough to stop making\lan announcement.$

replies.text: I like an introduction that ends with everybody being allowed to relax.
It seems more comfortable now. We should keep noticing what helps it feel secure.
No rushing it. It has already made its choice.
It is nice being trusted enough for the bright signals to become unnecessary.
A shaded rest stop should remain part of our plans.
A remarkably effective entrance, followed by the confidence to become quiet.
At last, somebody who understands the practical appeal of a dark corner.
Clear signals, carefully used. We can learn to read the subtler ones too.
A little night has found people it can be quiet beside.
We can enjoy its company without demanding it glow on command.
I'd remember the moment its posture changed from watchful to comfortable.

contexts.subject: LARVITAR gives its favorite pebble a farewell nibble. Its geological education is becoming a field trip.

KantoRare_LARVITAR_CaughtText.text: LARVITAR gives its favorite\npebble a farewell nibble. Its\lgeological education is becoming\la field trip.$

replies.text: I hope it knows that saying we know a good place to eat was not a geological recommendation.
We should learn what is suitable food before making assumptions about that appetite.
Ask before packing its stones away. Some of those might be lunch.
That last little nibble looked almost sentimental.
I have finally met a traveler whose packed lunch can weigh more than the luggage.
A very discerning restaurant critic has expanded its definition of restaurant.
The mountain has received a mixed review and a small bite.
We should label samples clearly if we carry any actual research equipment.
A favorite stone can make a surprisingly personal goodbye.
I refuse to judge a farewell snack. It clearly meant something.
I'd like to see what makes it choose one stone over another.

contexts.subject: HERACROSS nudges the branch neatly out of the way before turning back to you. The roadworks are complete.

KantoRare_HERACROSS_CaughtText.text: HERACROSS nudges the branch\nneatly out of the way before\lturning back to you. The\lroadworks are complete.$

replies.text: It finished the job before leaving. That is a very good reference.
Strength and consideration are a useful combination in a traveling partner.
Good worker. Knows when somebody smaller needs the path.
I liked how it kept making room for the others.
Somebody that considerate deserves a proper break afterward.
The strongest member of the road crew has also supplied its best manners.
Public service, performed without a clipboard. An alarming precedent.
It considered how the finished work would affect other travelers. Excellent instinct.
A clear path left behind is a kind farewell.
That last tidy nudge told us quite a lot about it.
I'd remember the little pauses it took for the smaller Pokemon.

contexts.subject: DRATINI watches one last circle spread across the water. Then its attention turns toward the road.

KantoRare_DRATINI_CaughtText.text: DRATINI watches one last circle\nspread across the water. Then its\lattention turns toward the road.$

replies.text: We can stop at the next interesting puddle. That is a perfectly good travel plan.
Curiosity can be a useful reason to begin a partnership.
We'll show it where the road goes. No need to rush the quiet stops.
It looked ready, but still wanted a little time to say goodbye.
A trip can make room for familiar comforts as well as new places.
A contemplative traveler has agreed to join a rather less organized expedition.
It has left the water's circles for our occasionally circular navigation.
I would like to know which details of new places interest it first.
One circle fades, and another kind of journey begins.
A small goodbye deserves time even when there are no words for it.
I'd remember that final glance across the ripples.

contexts.subject: MISDREAVUS circles you once, then makes an entrance from exactly where you already knew it was. A promising rehearsal.

KantoRare_MISDREAVUS_CaughtText.text: MISDREAVUS circles you once, then\nmakes an entrance from exactly\lwhere you already knew it was. A\lpromising rehearsal.$

replies.text: I was extremely startled by the ghost I had been looking directly at. I hope that helped.
It seems interested in play, and able to notice when somebody is not enjoying it.
A joke needs the other person to be having a good time too.
I like that it stopped when somebody needed quiet.
It can have a little audience without having to keep everybody on edge.
An ambitious entrance with a critically compromised element of surprise.
A considerate little haunting. I am almost professionally jealous.
We can agree on suitable times for surprises. Preferably after I put down the tools.
A playful shadow can learn where another person's quiet begins.
It seems to care whether the joke lands kindly. That matters.
I'd like to remember the exact face it makes while pretending we cannot see it.

contexts.subject: ABSOL checks the path once more before turning to you. It seems ready to leave the next traveler a safer road.

KantoRare_ABSOL_CaughtText.text: ABSOL checks the path once more\nbefore turning to you. It seems\lready to leave the next traveler\la safer road.$

replies.text: A serious face can belong to somebody doing a very kind thing.
Its actions gave us a better account than the first impression might have.
It was helping. Glad we paid attention.
I hope being understood makes the next part feel a little easier.
A partner that notices little hazards deserves someone who notices its effort.
A forbidding silhouette, undermined by a conspicuously considerate work ethic.
Misunderstood, yet still tidying up everyone else's problems. Distressingly relatable.
Removing a hazard is more useful than merely announcing it.
A dark shape can leave a kinder road behind it.
It should not have to look cheerful for the kindness to count.
I'd remember the careful way it moved each loose stone.

contexts.subject: FEEBAS completes one final circuit, then swims back toward you. Its longer journey appears to be approved.

KantoRare_FEEBAS_CaughtText.text: FEEBAS completes one final\ncircuit, then swims back toward\lyou. Its longer journey appears\lto be approved.$

replies.text: It has approved the long route. I hope we can live up to the committee of one fish.
Its persistence is worth noticing without comparing it to any future form.
Good partner as it is. We can work out the rest together.
It looked so quietly determined about coming back to us.
A proper welcome does not depend on looking impressive.
Our newest traveler has demonstrated a very persuasive commitment to finishing the lap.
An ordinary-looking fish has considerably better follow-through than several grand adventurers.
Steady effort is a useful strength even when it does not look spectacular.
A small circuit has opened into a much wider journey.
I like it now. That is not a compliment I am saving for later.
I'd remember the determined little turn that brought it back toward us.

contexts.subject: ROTOM gives the silent machine one last hopeful buzz. Apparently your team offers a more responsive audience.

KantoRare_ROTOM_CaughtText.text: ROTOM gives the silent machine\none last hopeful buzz. Apparently\lyour team offers a more\lresponsive audience.$

replies.text: At last, an audience capable of answering something besides electrical silence.
Its attempts at interaction have found a more responsive partner.
No moving into somebody's equipment without asking. We'll establish that early.
It sounded so pleased when the introduction finally got an answer.
Let us agree that kitchen appliances are not an open invitation.
The machine has lost its most determined interviewer to a better conversation.
A cheerful haunting with an electrical engineering problem.
I have questions. It probably has access to my entire toolkit. We need boundaries.
A little spark has found somebody willing to answer.
Its enthusiasm is lovely. My belongings would also appreciate a brief discussion.
I'd remember the difference between its patient little buzz and that delighted crackle.

contexts.subject: GIBLE abandons the pedal in favor of following you. The bicycle industry has been granted a temporary reprieve.

KantoRare_GIBLE_CaughtText.text: GIBLE abandons the pedal in favor\nof following you. The bicycle\lindustry has been granted a\ltemporary reprieve.$

replies.text: I hope its research does not require a representative sample of our shoes.
We should establish which materials are safe to chew before it expands the experiment.
Good choice. The pedal was not a sensible lunch.
I am glad the introduction ended with the bicycle remaining in one piece.
We will find food that was made to be food.
A promising young critic has spared an entire industry by accepting a travel invitation.
The first rule of our expedition will concern the difference between luggage and lunch.
I would like my tools to remain tools. We should discuss that gently but clearly.
A little curiosity is good company when somebody helps it find safe questions.
We can admire the enthusiasm while rescuing the footwear.
I'd remember the thoughtful look it gave a completely unsuitable snack.

contexts.subject: BAGON watches one last bird cross the sky, then turns proudly toward you. The next part of its training will have company.

KantoRare_BAGON_CaughtText.text: BAGON watches one last bird cross\nthe sky, then turns proudly\ltoward you. The next part of its\ltraining will have company.$

replies.text: We can believe in the dream and still suggest a safer place to practice hopping.
A long-term ambition deserves patient, practical support.
We'll help it train. Nobody needs to prove anything by getting hurt.
I hope having company makes the waiting part a little less lonely.
Dreams go better with proper rest and somebody remembering dinner.
An ambitious future has acquired a supporting cast and, ideally, sensible landing arrangements.
We have joined a very small campaign against the concept of being grounded.
Good training can turn enthusiasm into progress without skipping safety.
A piece of sky can stay with somebody long before they can reach it.
That proud little turn was a very good way to begin.
I'd like to remember this stage of the dream, before the sky becomes familiar.
